Y’a beaucoup de choses à dire sur cette pépite incroyable. J’ai 383h dessus sur trois plateformes (oui je l’ai acheté 3 fois laissez-moi tranquille). Même sa réputation de jeu buggé j’ai eu la chance de ne pas l’avoir subie : j’ai pas eu de bug à la première run mais les problèmes sont venus avec les MaJ (jsp comment).

Déjà de un pour moi un truc beaucoup trop souvent pris pour acquis : La VF d’une qualité folle, et le sound design général. Les multiples bruits des armes, tirs, voitures, les bruits de portes, les voix synthétiques la qualité des doublages sont juste fous et pour moi qui suis particulièrement fan de VF, les personnages sont superbement bien choisis : Ils ont quasiment tous la voix de leur tête quoi tu t’attends à ça c’est très satisfaisant. Ce genre de niveau de soins et surtout en français c’est la pépite d’immersion par rapport à une VO qui t’oblige à lire. Et je parle même pas des musiques parce que pourquoi parler de l’éléphant dans la pièce. (I’m a Netrunner, Never Looking Back, The Rebel Path) tous des bangers.

Cyberpunk parle vrai, les thèmes sont parfois lourds, il est bien plus froid au niveau de sa satire qu’un GTA par exemple mais l’immersion est totale ça c’est pas un scoop, on a une pépite d’écriture de choix et de conséquences avec un contenu vraiment dense. J’ai vraiment été marqué par le DLC qui est juste, beaucoup trop court finalement et c’est peu dire parce que y’a beaucoup de choses à voir. Le jeu de base nous ancre dans Night City, le DLC nous ancre dans LE LORE de Cyberpunk, il nous donne une situation nationale des enjeux beaucoup plus grands et ça agrandit l’univers énormément ce qui permet de nous rendre encore plus compte à quel point nous sommes éphémères même dans un monde qui n’existe pas.

Sans même vous parler des quêtes qui restent sacrément mieux écrites que 90% des jeux qui sortent, le Gameplay est juste super ! Quand tu passes ton temps à t’optimiser pour caler des tirs improbables ou la satisfaction de voir ton couteau prendre la trajectoire d’une tête à 30 mètres pendant que tu ralentis le temps en sandevistan, que tu pirates comme un acharné....quel effet

Tes builds optimisés peu importe lesquels sont dévastateurs mais tu ne sens pas que ce sont des features qui te sont injustement enlevées pour te les débloquer après. En clair : Tu ne débloques pas la compétence “s’accroupir” comme si c’était logique qu’à 30 ans tu saches pas faire DE BASE. Et la QUASI-TOTALITÉ des missions sont vraiment faites pour être rejouées sous différentes formes, rien que ce genre de choses prouve que le monde ouvert est un choix de design avant d’être un choix de marketing, tu prends un contrat de merc, chaque bâtiment est faisable peu importe ta spécialité, gros bourrin, ninja, hacker, tueur de l’ombre ou non létal. Tu auras toujours des moyens de voir une entrée moins gardée, une grille qui se défait, un panneau à pirater, une plateforme accessible en double saut...

Pour nuancer : À mon sens, contrairement à The Witcher 3 le jeu a plus besoin de mods pour briller. Pas pour l’immersion ni la densité de choses mais plus pour l’exploitation et le plaisir de jouer de ça. Un petit mod FOV étendu pour la conduite à moto et ça change tout, vraiment j’ai pas utilisé UNE SEULE FOIS les fast travel parce qu’en moto à 180° c’est juste trop bien de bombarder en centre-ville entre les voitures. Pareil pour la physique de la conduite ou le custom des véhicules (surtout esthétique ne vous attendez pas à LS Customs qui est déjà rudimentaire)

L’IA est pas super intelligente mais ça c’est pas nouveau, les appels de la NCPD par centaines me donnent envie de me défenestrer (regarde ta map tu vas comprendre), y’a vraiment des trucs qui manquent quand même comme : de quoi custom ton player home, un garage, un peu plus d’interactivité avec ton monde mais ça reste quand même UN PEU du chipotage.

Il y a aussi des pans du jeu que j’ai laissés un peu à l’abandon comme les cosmétiques, là où voir une belle armure de Geralt (l’armure de la vipère est juste trop belle) ça fait plaisir eh bien là avoir une doudoune rose et un legging léopard chaussure à talon rose on s’en fout on le voit pas.

Pour conclure, il veut en faire parfois trop mais les mods aident pas mal pour certaines choses, je ne sais pas si c’est une bonne ou une mauvaise chose en tous cas ils ont relancé mon intérêt après 3 runs parce que refaire le jeu dans les conditions qu’on aime c’est parfait. Même en dehors du jeu, ça reste un univers vraiment plein de mystères où j’adore m’y perdre. FF 06 B5.

Je lui mets un solide 9.5/10 pour l’animation, les détails des visages et évidemment l’écriture de l’histoire. Si vous n’avez pas fait Phantom Liberty vous ratez vraiment quelque chose.

Cyberpunk 2077 feels like my favorite '90s movies came to life — Blade Runner's neon-noir streets, RoboCop's corporate dystopia, Johnny Mnemonic's data-in-the-skull paranoia, Total Recall's untrustworthy memories. There's Alita's cyborg heart, The Sixth Day's cloning anxiety, Minority Report's surveillance-state advertising, even Stallone's Judge Dredd in the city's brutalist sprawl. The characters feel alive, and the whole thing plays less like a game and more like a prestige TV series — Sons of Anarchy, Breaking Bad. Most games don't touch storytelling on this level. Історія гри Cyberpunk 2077 є дуже цікавою. Я пам'ятаю шалений ажіотаж 2020 року. Він був настільки шалений, що викладач на одній з наших пар відпустив нас раніше, щоб встигнути пограти в передзамовлення. Проте, гра вийшла "сирою", недопрацьованою, що призвело до критики та розчарування. Саме ця критика звернула мою увагу. Через летсплеї, побачивши цю гру, я став її палким прихильником. Сюжет 1000000000/10. Це найсильніша як на мене сторона гри. Розробникам вдалося повністю втілити всесвіт, а доповнення Phantom Liberty дійсно доповнило, й закінчило цю логічну історію. Найсильнішою стороною сюжету є його відомі кінцівки. Їх декілька, я б навіть сказав - багато. Далі спойлер: Кінцівки часто критикують за відсутність хепіенду, немов відсутній розв'язок проблеми котрий задовольний би всіх. Як вдало зазначили розробники в самій грі вустами персонажа Джонні Сільвергенда: "Гарний кінець для всіх? Для таких як ми? Ти помилився містом". Але, насправді в кожній кінцівкі присутня також, надія, що не дозволяє категорично висловитися про них. Сюжет бомбезний, часто пронизаний містицизмом, езотерикою. Для кращого розуміння необхідно мати й певний філософський та літературний бекграунд. Марксизм, екзистенціалізм, абсурдизм - все це, й навіть більше. Для короткого ознайомлення рекомендую український переклад Н. Кетрін Хейлз "Як ми стали постлюдством". Геймплей 9/10. Він на висоті, але видно, що гра планувалася більш амбіційною, й помічаєш мимоволі ці моменти та думаєш: "Ну ось тут можна було б таке додати; можна було б деталізувати й т. д.". Але це в принципі для багатьох ігор такого штибу притаманно. Персонажі 10/10. Дуже гарно показані, прописані, їх внутрішні моменти, мотивація, страхи, проблеми. Графіка 8/10. Моє обладнання не дозволяє насолодитися повно цією грою, але знову ж таки, через масштабність помічаєш певні недопрацювання. Вони не критичні, але через баги (котрі стають невід'ємною частиною сучасних ігор), трохи псується враження. Музика 10000000/10. Прекрасний музичний супровід, атмосфера 80-х, в яких цей всесвіт й створювався. Оптимізація 7/10. Дійсно, багів стало набагато менше, проте все ще залишаються деякі. Гру хочеться проходити й перепроходити. Гідний наступник Відьмака як на мене. Гра 10/10. Всім рекомендую абсолютно. Одна з моїх найулюбленіших відеоігор. Окрема, велика подяка за підтримку України

🔴 THE SPOILER REVIEW
Do yourself a favor: [b] play the main game first, enjoy all the base game endings first, then play the DLC. [/b] It hits so much harder that way. 

I played the main game first, then the DLC came out a few years after.
In the main game, I tried so hard thinking if I played my cards right, I would get to save V. But there is no perfect choice. You only get a bad ending or a semi-bad ending. There is no easy way out. 

A few years later, the Phantom Liberty DLC dropped. I went in completely blind, only knowing there might finally be a cure to save V. It gave me real hope. But this DLC really drove home the theme that there are [u] absolutely no happy endings in Night City.[/u] 
Reality hits you like a truck and shuts you down. 

Like the game says: [b] "You play grown-up games, you face grown-up consequences." [/b]


At the end, what did V have to lose to stay alive? What did you have to destroy to get there? Are you really ready for those consequences? Can you live with your conscience? When it's over, you will just sit there, watch the credit rolls, and listen to the music in total silence. BTW that music hits you strong!!

Once you complete the DLC and experience all of its endings, go back and play the base game endings again. You'll go into them knowing there is truly no real cure for V at all—or V gets to be saved, but at what cost? It changes everything. You aren't playing to find a cure anymore—you are playing to choose what is truly best for V.
If you want a game that stays with you long after it ends, play this.

游戏叙事策略可以理解为一种 “伪反抗”，这不是革命 。系统允许甚至鼓励一定程度的反抗姿态，因为它知道，只要反抗不触及生产资料的所有制形式，它就永远无法构成真正的威胁。游戏通过其机制本身强化了这一主题：无论V多努力，变得多强，最终都只是在系统的牢笼里进行一场华丽而绝望的表演。
有趣的是赛博朋克概念本身确实有批判基因。它揭示的不是反抗不存在，而是反抗如何被收编、商品化、消费化。强尼的摇滚、V的义体、来生酒吧的传奇，都是反抗被包装成商品的例子。这本身是对资本主义文化工业的尖锐讽刺。问题不在于悲剧结局，而在于把“不可能改变”自然化。终于在叙事中找到了一个深层的矛盾：它构建了一个技术资本主义吞噬一切的世界，但其中上演的所有反抗，从形式到逻辑，最终都未能逃出这个系统本身。其深刻之处，不在于它描绘了一个多么可怕的未来，而在于它诚实地指出了：当资本主义发展到极致，它最强大的力量不是镇压反抗，而是让反抗本身也成为一种可以被系统消化、消费甚至鼓励的商品。
然而，“无法改变夜之城，夜之城只会吞噬你”不是客观规律，而是资本主义文化生产中的政治无意识。
这不是事实，而是意识形态。因为它的叙事被三重桎梏锁死：一.资本主义范畴下的现实主义：公司统治被自然化，仿佛无法想象替代方案。二.3A 游戏工业逻辑：需要续作、IP、夜之城作为永恒舞台，不能真正改变世界。三.个人主义类型惯例：主角必须是个人英雄，革命必须是背景板。于是游戏只能提供个人结局：成为传奇、逃离城市、交出身体、死去。
它展示了牢笼，却把牢笼说成世界本身。

武器载具都有非常多的种类，其中最喜欢的载具是石中剑的武装载具版本。可惜的是武装载具在游戏内容中的使用条件比较苛刻，一般都没办法使其大放异彩。
游戏内容也很多，比如我这次通关了游戏，完整体验大概在70-80个小时，十分满足。目前为止只打了一个结局，后续估计还会再开其他结局，但考虑到单周目都已经花了这么长时间，估计以后很难再有机会有这么大把的时间去品鉴了十分可惜。
个人对于这款游戏的整体评分是9.8/10，扣分点主要在于人物模型上（特别是女v）过于政治正确了，其他都非常好。

**10/10 — Absolutely worth it.**

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those games that gets better the more time you spend with it. Night City is incredible to explore, the story is genuinely engaging, and the characters, especially Johnny Silverhand, are unforgettable.

The amount of freedom you have with builds, weapons, cyberware, and dialogue choices makes every playthrough feel different. The atmosphere is probably the game's biggest strength; Night City feels like a place with its own identity rather than just a backdrop.

The game definitely had a rough launch, but after all the updates and improvements, it’s hard to believe how far it has come. Phantom Liberty makes the experience even better.

If you skipped Cyberpunk because of its launch problems, give it another chance. Night City is absolutely worth visiting.

The moment I stepped foot into Night City, it somehow managed to steal my attention for 6 months straight.

The beautiful, yet depressing dystopian world as well as the memorable characters and great story engaged me enough to not only play through the entire game twice in a row, but also actively made want to play the DLC and chase after all the endings when most other games make me lose my interest after the credits. Some moments in the game genuinely left me speechless due to how eerily close we are to making the exaggerated setting of this game's world into a reality. Social Media algorithms irresponsibly dictating our perception of the world? Vulnerable teenagers who delete their facebook selfies out of shame receive targeted advertisements for beauty products? Mass surveillance laws are disguised as ineffective child protection measures? Ex-Disney stars monetize your grief with AI deepfakes of your dead relatives?

I believe that this game is not just a phenomenal immersive experience, but also an important reminder for us to reflect on the relationship we have with the technology we rely on.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a story rich RPG featuring a beautiful open world, with the best character writing I've seen. The game covers themes such as freedom, identity, greed, and social inequality. It's an unforgettable experience worth playing. Jackie Welles & Johnny Silverhand are [b] GOATED [/b] support characters!

Story: You play as V, a lone merc in Night City, a futuristic violent dystopia dictated by greedy capitalist mega-corporations. You take on the most dangerous jobs trying to stay alive and make a name for yourself. There are 3 life paths to choose from: Nomad, Streetkid, and Corpo. They don't make much of a difference gameplay-wise, aside from unique dialogue options and shaping V's perspective on the world. After your biggest high stakes job goes FUBAR, the story truly begins as you race against time for your life! 

Gameplay: This game feels like a mixture of GTA and Borderlands because of the interactivity, stores, looting, class building, and the leeway to play however you like. Unfortunately, some elements are not well polished, but its not that bad because they can be fixed with mods. Majority of the cars handle terribly! I got around the map 90% of the time using motorcycles because they're really fast and consistently handle well. Another thing I did not enjoy too much was the early game. Enemies scale heavily to your level at all times, so the beginning is kind of rough because your guns aren't strong and targets feel tanky. Shotguns, revolvers, and snipers became my go to weapons. You'll be fine if your aim and positioning is really good. Mid to late game is when you can really start going crazy. 

Environment: Along with the story, this is another great aspect because of its visual storytelling. It shows you how bad things are, instead of telling you. The city is plagued with advertisements, some even reaching the sky! Gangs rule certain city districts, crime thrives more often in some places, and you can really see the poverty and flourishment of areas. What I truly did love were the small mentions of the 2076 Edgerunners crew. You can find iconic items left behind by a few members which is very cool, it makes the city's history feel more connected on a deeper level.

Side Quests: There are many to do and they give you really good rewards, but they aren't special because they follow a repetitive format. The only good quests are the character story missions, these deepen your bond with key characters, allowing you to learn their history and help them out with personal troubles. 

TL;DR Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best story rich RPG games you can ever play. It has some issues gameplay wise, but they're relatively minor and won't hurt your overall experience. Never stop fighting, my chooms!

Cyberpunk 2077, para mim, possui de longe uma das melhores histórias que já presenciei em um jogo nesta década. O roteiro é extremamente bem construído, envolvente e consistente, e os personagens são cativantes e muito bem desenvolvidos. No geral, considero a experiência narrativa uma verdadeira obra de arte.

Porém, apesar de todos esses méritos, sinto que o jogo possui alguns problemas que acabam prejudicando bastante a experiência.

Ainda existem inúmeros bugs que atrapalham a jogatina, além de animações que poderiam ser muito melhores e algumas funcionalidades básicas que simplesmente não estão presentes na versão vanilla, sendo muitas vezes a comunidade modder responsável por corrigir ou adicionar coisas que deveriam fazer parte do jogo.

Outro ponto é que, apesar de Night City ser enorme e muito bem construída, depois de certo tempo o mundo pode começar a parecer repetitivo e limitado em termos de atividades e interações. E, para mim, o maior problema está justamente na falta de profundidade na vida pessoal do V.

Depois de concluir toda a história de personagens como a Panam, por exemplo, seria muito interessante poder construir uma rotina com ela. Poder convidá-la para sair, tomar um café, passear pela cidade ou simplesmente passar mais tempo juntos de maneiras diferentes. Mesmo dentro do apartamento do V, as interações são bastante limitadas: sentar no sofá, algumas poucas cenas e pouco mais.

Sinto que faltou justamente essa sensação de continuidade. Depois de terminar a história principal e as missões dos personagens, parece que boa parte daquele mundo perde a vida que tinha antes. Seria incrível poder acompanhar mais de perto o cotidiano do V e aprofundar suas relações, criando uma rotina e momentos mais espontâneos com os personagens que aprendemos a gostar.

No fim, minha crítica não vem de falta de carinho pelo jogo — muito pelo contrário. Cyberpunk 2077 tem uma narrativa fantástica, personagens memoráveis e um mundo incrível. Justamente por isso, acredito que ele poderia ser ainda mais especial se tivesse maior profundidade nas pequenas coisas: mais interações, mais vida cotidiana, mais atividades e uma sensação maior de que a vida do V continua existindo mesmo depois de encerrarmos as grandes histórias.

É um jogo que chegou muito perto de ser algo extraordinário em todos os aspectos, e talvez por isso essas pequenas ausências sejam tão perceptíveis.

[h3] 我心如火 [/h3]

  早上好，夜之城！那是2022年10月的一个周六，伴随着《I Really Want to Stay At Your House》大卫被亚当重锤爆头露西孤身一人登上月球，看着剧中无敌的重锤和草菅人命的荒坂深深感到无力。那是我第一次想买这游戏，亲自打爆重锤核爆荒坂塔但只恨财力不足下载了学习版（电脑都是借的）在马上打到结局时电脑被要了回去留下遗憾。现在打工买了新电脑趁着促销买了本体后在秋促补全DLC打了全成就一切完满，我想也该留下些纪念了。

[h3]高级动物 [/h3]

  游戏的主线就是v不断奋斗的过程—从无名小卒到扬名立万，再到命不久矣余下六个月。眼看他/她起朱楼，眼看他/她宴宾客，眼看他/她楼塌了。置身于夜之城中，以v的视角见证了形形色色的人和事。见证了强尼银手放荡、糟糕、自以为是的一生，见证了帕南对改善家族的努力又或是骗了所有人只是想保命的百灵鸟...在高塔结局里v活了下来但再也回不去了。看着身边人一个个都过上了新生活，v最后走入人群成为那一个个无名小卒时我沉默了，v经历了这么多事最后回归平常生活那句“你是想要扬名立万还是当个无名小卒”仿佛像一个回旋镖打了回来。从山巅一下滑落到谷底到底还是认了命或许这才是v真正的归宿吧。

[h3] 死城[/h3]

  回到游戏，游戏最大优点就是美术和题材，赛博朋克这个题材确实很新鲜吸引人并且市面上也没什么同类型的大型游戏作代餐。当然大家应该都知道CDPR的另一ip巫师是靠剧情起家但这次的赛博朋克真的太短了，剧情推到华子在等待竟然就结束了然后花大把时间去通支线但支线质量对比巫师却差点意思，好在DLC剧情回归正常水平。除此之外，什么车辆手感像块肥皂、v卡入虚空、ncpd重复无聊等缺点就不一一列举了

[h3] 以我残躯化烈火[/h3]

  虽然你首发就是个半成品，bug满天飞、主线剧情短、支线留不下太多印象。先端半成品再修的行为很伤玩家的心，但我还是希望能出赛博朋克2在吸取第一部的教训后好好打磨游戏品质吧CDPR！

Title: Never Fade Away...

A lot of time has passed since launch, and only now can I truly say it: this game is a masterpiece. The work CD Projekt Red put into turning this around is fantastic.

The plot tackles real, massive issues reflecting our own world. This isn't just a brief main quest that feels like a small add-on to a massive map—it’s a deeply human story filled with heroes, villains, and losers. It asks what it really takes for a "nobody" to become a legend, and more importantly, what price you pay for that success. This is pure, authentic Cyberpunk. To be honest, I wasn't sure CDPR could pull it off, but the voice acting and performances are fabulous. They brought Night City to life so convincingly that you instantly buy into its ruthless rules and struggles.

Gameplay at launch was okay, but weak. Today? It’s phenomenal. The world is packed with hidden details, easter eggs, and its own urban legends. As for bugs, I rarely ran into anything major—just the occasional floating car or clipping geometry. For where the game stands today, it plays great. It just needs a few tiny polish tweaks, but nothing that ruins the experience.

The map is huge, and the DLC filled in every empty space seamlessly. There are countless small stories to uncover and interesting places to explore. The level design and world-building deserve serious praise.

Summary:
Without spoiling anything: trust me, you won't regret playing this. It’s far from a typical video game story—it’s something much deeper. Accept the rules of Night City, jump in, and experience it. The writing and acting ensure this world never feels like a hollow cardboard set; the city is cruel, and you will feel every bit of it.

Score: 9/10 (Play it, and you’ll understand why).

[h1] Final feliz pra gente como a gente? Cidade errada, povo errado. [/h1]

    Cyberpunk 2077 é um jogo em que você passa por toda uma cidade e percebe que ninguém tem um final feliz. Todos, sem exceção, são jogados de lado e tratados como se fossem meros números para as grandes corporações, de modo que morrer de velhice é constantemente retratado como inalcançável, servindo de piada em alguns momentos.

    Apesar de ter um lançamento desastroso, esse jogo é um exemplo de como o amor por um projeto pode reerguê-lo se não desistir dele. Atualmente, com quase nenhum bug (os principais que encontrei foram colisões que te mandam para baixo do mapa e alguns bosses travarem no ar), o jogo conta com muitas opções de build é bem otimizado, sendo uma das melhores coisas a capacidade de só explorar a cidade e ir para onde quiser.

所以各位，当你玩高等数学玩不下去时，没必要死磕，可以试试赛博朋克，毕竟，人最重要的，还是快乐。

A Gentle Dystopia

Ah yes, the promised land is finally here. After a botched release and years of updates improving, expanding, and stabilizing the game along with the release of the massive Phantom Liberty expansion. All is forgiven, Polish devs. But is it? As much as there is about Cyberpunk 2077 that I like and as much as I respect the support CD Projekt Red continued to put into it. We need to talk about the massive elephant in the room that never actually left. Borrowed time.

Majora's Mask is probably one of the most famous examples of making time itself part of the gameplay. Even though its three day loop, that doomsday clock is always ticking. The player constantly understands that time has value. For more modern examples, look at games like The Blood of Dawnwalker or Kingdom Come Deliverance II. Neither necessarily hangs one giant doomsday clock over the player in the same way. Instead, time becomes part of the player's agency. Dawnwalker gives you a limited amount of time before the endgame, with quests and major actions advancing that clock. Deliverance II takes a more situational approach, where certain quests and events will move forward without you if you wait too long. Personally, I think Deliverance II takes this idea a little too literally. Persona 5 is another great example. You have a limited calendar and have to decide how to spend it. Do you improve a relationship? Work on yourself? Explore the palace? Prepare for the next major confrontation? All of these systems are asking the player some variation of the same question. What are you going to do with the time you have? And Cyberpunk presents one of the strongest possible versions of that question. When you're dying, what do you do with your time?

Apparently nothing. Get up samurai, we're going drag racing. Get up samurai, we're clearing every gig and side mission on the entire map. Get up samurai, we're going bowling. This is the massive elephant that I don't think gets criticized nearly enough. The story presents V with a very simple and horrifying problem. You are dying. Your life is disintegrating in front of you. The writing becomes emotional. Relationships start forming. People begin attaching themselves to V. Johnny is slowly taking over. Every lead toward a possible cure should feel increasingly desperate. Your entire story is supposedly happening on borrowed time. And then Cyberpunk almost immediately throws that idea out the window. The clock doesn't actually exist. Take as long as you want. Do every gig. Help every fixer. Buy every car. Make every friend. Finish every companion storyline. Explore every corner of Night City. Eventually, whenever you finally feel like it, go choose your ending.

That's not meaningful agency. That's a story telling you that your time is valuable while the game design simultaneously tells you that your time is infinite. And that creates a massive disconnect. Your relationships with people begin to lose weight. Desperately taking gigs because you need money to upgrade your cyberware stops meaning anything because... why not just do everything? Eventually you'll be swimming in money anyway. The writing constantly asks for an emotional response from the people around V. Meanwhile, V suppresses the biggest problem in their life, another identity is literally eating away at their mind, their body, and eventually their entire existence. That should hang over everything. Every relationship. Every choice. Every job. Every conversation with Johnny. Instead, the uncertainty loses its weight. The confrontations with Johnny lose some of their urgency because, at the end of the day, who cares? Johnny, you and me are going bowling, again.

As always modders enter the scene. Modders add an actual doomsday clock, progressing V's deterioration according to the in-game passage of time. Other mods add life sim elements like eating, drinking, sleeping and generally maintaining yourself. The most baffling thing about all of this is that the foundations for these systems are already sitting inside the game. There are food vendors everywhere. Vending machines everywhere. You have a bed. You have showers. You can buy multiple apartments and living spaces. These places are presented like somewhere V can return to, decompress, sleep, shower, eat, and temporarily escape Night City. But for what? The game has all these little pieces suggesting that V is supposed to be living in Night City while simultaneously dying inside it, yet almost none of them carry any real mechanical consequence. And that becomes even stranger when you consider how heavily the writing emphasizes borrowed time. Every new person V grows attached to is potentially someone they're going to lose. Every relationship V builds is happening under the shadow of an approaching death. Every lead toward a cure should matter because another day wasted is another day gone. But without any meaningful passage of time, that shadow never really moves. And that's why, even after all the updates, all the fixes, Phantom Liberty, and everything CD Projekt Red poured into this game, part of Cyberpunk 2077 still feels half cooked to this day.

One of the biggest contradictions is still sitting there at the heart of V's story. Untouched. Unfixed. They wrote about a person discovering that their life suddenly has an expiration date, but never implemented the one element that could have made that premise truly meaningful. Your life is supposed to be on borrowed time. The grim story of a dystopian hell where one person is desperately trying to find some meaning in the trash heap around them loses much of its weight when the game refuses to make time matter. For all the work CD Projekt Red has done rebuilding Cyberpunk 2077, this contradiction has been sitting there since the beginning.

The elephant never left the room.

[b] 《赛博朋克2077》：当物化成为日常，孤独便是唯一的真实 [/b]
如果要给《赛博朋克2077》一个精炼的判断，那就是：当前无可撼动的赛博朋克游戏。这不是说它没有缺陷——本体的赶工痕迹至今可见，主线与支线之间的叙事裂缝从未完全弥合。但在“赛博朋克”这个命题上，没有任何一款游戏比它走得更远、挖得更深。

[b] IP改编的叙事诡计：蠢驴滤镜下的强尼 [/b]
这是个IP改游戏，原作是1988年桌游《赛博朋克2020》及后续。其设定超前，世界观核心不是科技多炫酷，而是“人被科技拆解后还剩什么”。CDPR改编时刻意制造叙事诡计：玩家看到的强尼·银手回忆——英勇就义的摇滚传奇——在桌游正史中不成立。正史里，2023年荒坂塔事件中强尼只是救人，奥特被抓与他无关；他被亚当·重锤炸成两半，蜘蛛墨菲插芯片才保住意识；核爆主力是摩根·黑手和罗格。强尼在记忆里把自己美化成了主角。CDPR同步推出的新版桌游才是正史，游戏中的强尼因此是不可靠叙述者，自我美化、自恋自大，符合人设。这不是编剧失误，是设计。强尼在Relic里五十年后仍坚信自己的版本，这种顽固的自我中心，比完美英雄更像真实的人。

[b] 物化到极致，孤独到骨髓 [/b]
对我来说，这个IP真正的赛博朋克特色，在于把人的身心和体验物化、量化到极致，以及由此衍生出的生活随时可能脱离自我掌控的孤独感。
物化的第一层是身体。义体把感知替换为功能性输入：走路像按键，视角像滑动鼠标，斯安威斯坦等同开风灵月影。赛博精神病并非玄学，而是把现实当键鼠游戏——其心态接近endgame玩家。
物化的第二层是体验。超梦将意识体验变成可剪辑、贩卖、消费的商品；忏悔刑罚型超梦更强制罪犯以受害者视角反复体验痛苦，摧毁意志、植入服从，使共情成为武器。
物化的第三层是意识。RELIC与神舆将人格数字化、复制、转移；“灵魂杀手”即复制大脑的AI。V的Relic存有强尼人格并逐渐覆盖宿主，共享身体即缓慢人格分裂，意识可复制性动摇了“我”的定义。
所有这些物化最终指向孤独。夜之城的黑帮火并、公司竞争、流窜AI与网监对抗、赛博精神病随机爆发，让生活随时脱离掌控。公司取代国家，帮派是白手套，NCPD与六街帮交易。你永远不知明天会不会被裁员、被波及、被入侵义体，或义体过载变成赛博精神病。这种无处不在的无力感，才是赛博朋克最根本的恐怖。

[b] 狗镇与本体：两种任务设计，两种沉浸感受 [/b]
游戏内容方面，狗镇的通马桶任务比本体的通马桶任务制作得更加上心，这几乎是玩家社区的共识。
本体的中间人委托，用大家的话说就是：接电话、偷或杀、收短信，细节埋在芯片、邮件与路边文本中。这种碎片化叙事补充世界观，但需玩家主动挖掘串联；对未能沉浸者，易沦为不知所云的文本，令人疲惫。大量剧情散落支线甚至路边芯片，线索需自行琢磨，不知是刻意为之还是未完成。
狗镇的委托则是另一种体验。狗镇委托在设计上更加完善，大多拥有专属地图与完整起承转合，包含配音NPC互动、实质性抉择和后日谈，并以多分支结局让选择影响NPC乃至整个区域。玩家能真切感受到时间在向前走，狗镇在随剧情变化。
两者的差异本质上是叙事责任分配的不同。本体把理解世界的责任交给了玩家，它信任玩家的主动性和沉浸意愿；狗镇则把叙事责任更多地交还给了设计者，用更密集的演出和更直接的反馈来确保每一个委托都被体验到，而不仅仅是被完成。

[b] 结语 [/b]
即使在2026年，《赛博朋克2077》仍然是同类作品中的佼佼者。它不完美，本体的框架至今能看到赶工的裂痕，主线与支线之间的节奏断裂从未真正修复。但它做到了其他赛博朋克游戏没有做到的事：它让物化不再是主题，而是机制；让孤独不再是背景，而是体验。 当你操控着高度义体化的V在夜之城的霓虹下穿行，用超梦消费别人的记忆，用Relic和另一个人格共享大脑，在狗镇的道德困境里反复权衡——你不再是在玩一个赛博朋克游戏，你就是“赛博朋克”本身。

Прям погружаешься в этот мир, когда видишь эти мегабашни, рекламные баннеры на каждом углу, разборки персонажей или целых банд, фискерские тёрки. Персонажи очень проработанные, приятные и живые. Озвучка просто нереальная, CD Projekt Red умеют передавать всю энергию и эмоции в озвучке персонажей. Геймплей шикарный, так и хочется собрать себе какой-нибудь смертоносный билд и с огромным удовольствием нарезать врагов. Лично я для себя отметил билд через силу и дробовик Реббеки. Реиграбельность тоже высокая, ведь разных выборов в диалогах очень много, почти во всех квестах можно поступить по-разному и получить совершенно новый результат. Phantom Liberty - могу назвать самым лучшим длс для игр, которое я когда-либо видел, в каких-то моментах даже лучше основной игры. Сюжет длс просто шедевр, персонажи... боже, персонажи просто неописуемые. Проходя длс, иногда в голове всплывала мысль: "А я сейчас точно в игре?". Я рад, что приобрел эту игру и столько потратил времени на неё, пройдя 4 раза. Помните, в Найт-Сити нет хороших концовок.

游戏刚发售那会儿就已经游玩并通关了太阳结局，早期的版本与现在有较大区别，回想2020年的时候我还在读大学，一台游戏本、宿舍里的三个小伙伴每当闲暇之余就开启电脑“早上好！夜之城！”一听到这就开始背着“铁哥们”斯丹利的台词，有时间就坐下来玩一会儿。没想到一晃这么多年过去，版本已经换了很多代，今天终于趁着空闲，通关了所有本体+DLC结局，也算是给自己在夜之城的旅程画上了一个完整的句号。
从最初那个被各种Bug和优化问题包围的《赛博朋克2077》，到后来经历一次又一次更新，再到《往日之影》的加入，这款游戏已经和刚发售时完全不是一个样子了。作为我接触的第一款真正意义上的3A开放世界RPG，它也许并不完美，但无论是世界观、美术、音乐、角色塑造还是剧情氛围，都给我留下了非常深的印象。
通关之后回头看，我觉得这个游戏最让我难忘的，其实不是枪械、义体或者夜之城本身，而是那些人物，以及每一个结局背后的代价。建议做完所有的任务、主线、委托后把除了高塔结局其他所有的结局任务全部通关一遍，因为通关后你还可以回到见华子前并获得相对应的通关奖励，高塔结局通过后就回不去了就是真正的大结局了，然后有条件的配一台高配置的电脑买个好屏幕，可以在没事的时候打开游戏慢慢欣赏里面的风景，游走在大街小巷里，会慢慢的沉浸其中，发现更多的彩蛋，有时候，甚至幻想自己就是生活在夜之城这个未来都市里。

1.恶魔结局【梦安眠于九霄】
和荒坂合作，用自己的方式换取活下去的机会。这个结局给我的感觉最压抑。一路走到最后，你会发现很多东西已经不再掌握在自己手里。V和强尼之间的关系也走向了最彻底的割裂。即便最终还有所谓的“选择”，那种无力感依然挥之不去。
这是我最不喜欢的结局，也是最让我觉得冰冷的一个结局。

2.自杀结局【夜曲】
这是最简单，同时也是最沉重的一个结局。V选择结束这一切，不再让任何人为自己付出代价。
从某个角度来看，这确实避免了更多牺牲，但当看到那些朋友留下的留言之后，还是会发现，这从来都不是一个只属于V自己的决定。
这是一个很悲伤的结局。

3.星星结局【沿着瞭望塔】
和帕南以及阿德卡多一起离开夜之城。虽然V依然只剩下有限的时间，但至少这一次，他不再是一个人。相比夜之城那些宏大的野心、公司和传奇，这个结局反而显得格外真实。
有时候人生未必一定要赢到最后，能够和真正关心自己的人一起走完剩下的路，也许已经足够了。

4.太阳结局【城市之王】
成为夜之城真正意义上的传奇。V终于站到了这座城市最顶端的位置，拥有了曾经想要的一切，但身体的倒计时依旧没有停止。
这是一个很“赛博朋克”的结局：你赢得了名声、地位和传奇，却依然无法战胜死亡。至少在夜之城，人们会记得曾经有一个叫V的佣兵。

5.节制结局【镜子中】
把身体留给强尼。这个结局很特别，也很复杂。一路走下来，V和强尼从最开始互相排斥，到后来逐渐理解彼此，最后甚至愿意把最重要的东西交给对方。
从某种意义上说，这是两个人真正完成和解的结局。只是代价同样巨大——最终必须有一个人留下，有一个人离开。

6.高塔结局【只身打马】——《往日之影》
DLC新增的结局，也是我感触最深的一个。V最终活了下来，却失去了曾经赖以生存的一切。强尼消失，义体无法继续使用，朋友们也有了各自的新生活。
曾经那个在夜之城里横冲直撞、想成为传奇的V，最后变成了茫茫人海中的一个普通人。
但仔细想想，这未必是最坏的结局。
至少，他真的活下来了。
不用继续和荒坂、Relic、死亡倒计时抗争，也不用为了成为传奇不断赌上自己的命。也许从此以后，他只是一个普通人，但普通人的生活同样可以重新开始。

如果一定要按照我个人的喜好给这些结局排个顺序，我大概会排：
高塔＞节制＞太阳＞星星＞自杀＞恶魔
当然，每个人对这些结局的理解都会不一样。

回头再看，《赛博朋克2077》对我来说已经不单纯是一款游戏了。它更像是一部我断断续续看了很多年的电影，也像是人生某个阶段留下来的记忆。
从大学宿舍里的那台游戏本，到今天终于把所有结局全部走完，现实中的几年过去了，游戏里的夜之城却一直停在那里。
很多人来到夜之城，都想成为传奇。
但走到最后才会发现，也许真正重要的，从来不是你有没有成为传奇，而是一路上遇见了谁、失去了什么，又做出了怎样的选择。
这游戏有缺点，也经历过众多批判，也许有些细节没有做到尽善尽美，但它最终还是成为了一款让我愿意多年以后重新回来，并认真把故事走到最后的作品。
我们都将回归现实，不得不去面对更大的困难和挑战。

Cyberpunk 2077 is a great game, and the story is amazing. Personally, I really liked playing as male V.
It is sad because this game had so much potential, but CD Projekt Red did not develop many parts of the world enough. For example, driving could be better, there could have been flying cars, more stores you can actually enter, and more NPCs with different voices and animations.

I think Cyberpunk 2077 could have been one of the greatest games of all time if it had received another five or six years of development, but CD Projekt Red made the choice to release it when they did.
The game is still worth playing and finishing, especially for the main story. The Dogtown/Phantom Liberty storyline is also very good. But if you like exploring the open world and paying attention to small details, you will notice many of the game's weaknesses.
I finished the game, experienced all the endings, and completed all the achievements. My favorite ending is “(Don't Fear) The Reaper.” I really enjoyed the idea of V and Johnny deciding to attack Arasaka Tower alone instead of risking the lives of their friends.
Even with all its problems, I recommend Cyberpunk 2077

从争议半成品到赛博史诗的五年救赎
 
历经五年数十次版本迭代、2.0体系大革新与《往日之影》高质量DLC补全，《赛博朋克2077》早已摆脱首发阶段“虚假宣传、半成品bug大作”的负面标签。在2026年的当下，这款游戏完成了彻底的自我救赎，成为开放世界、叙事艺术与赛博朋克美学的标杆级作品。它不再是一款徒有噱头的流量游戏，而是一部兼具极致视觉沉浸、深度玩法体系、残酷人文内核的完整杰作，也是目前市面上最纯粹、最立体的赛博朋克题材单机大作。
 
一、世界观与画面：无可替代的夜之城，顶级氛围封神
 
如果要用一个词定义《赛博朋克2077》的场景设计，那就是真实且鲜活的赛博乌托邦。不同于多数开放世界“空有地图、毫无灵魂”的流水线设计，夜之城是游戏行业为数不多真正实现垂直分层、地域割裂、阶级分明的活体都市。
 
整座城市六大区域风格迥异，沃森区的霓虹贫民窟、市中心的资本摩天大楼、海伍德的混乱市井、太平洲的荒芜废土，每一片区域的光影、音效、建筑细节、路人生态都高度差异化。雨夜潮湿的柏油马路倒映全息霓虹广告、悬浮车流穿梭在楼宇之间、街头义体改造者、流浪汉、企业精英各行其是，没有刻意的剧情堆砌，却处处充斥着高科技、低生活的核心赛博朋克内核。
 
2026年最新画质更新进一步拉高了画面上限，适配次世代设备的光线追踪模式全面优化，车漆、玻璃、全息投影的反射效果极致逼真，全局阴影动态渲染让昼夜、雨雾场景的层次感拉满。同时新增的性能模式可实现高刷屏90帧稳定运行，兼顾画质与流畅度。
 
即便上线五年，夜之城的细节依旧吊打多数新晋开放世界游戏：老旧巷道的锈迹、广告牌的斑驳裂纹、义体过载的电光特效、城市喧嚣的立体音效，构建出独一份的压抑、繁华、荒诞交织的沉浸感。唯一短板在于场景交互依旧有限，多数商铺、建筑无法进入，保留了早期版本的地图结构性遗憾。
 
二、玩法体系：2.0重构新生，自由构筑极致流派
 
首发版本单调、固化的玩法体系，在2.0大更新中被彻底推翻重构，义体、天赋、战斗、潜行全部重做，让游戏从“流水线射击游戏”蜕变为高自由度的RPG构筑大作，不同流派体验差异堪称两款游戏。
 
游戏核心的义体系统全面升级，全身骨骼、神经系统、皮下、手部义体可自由搭配，螳螂刀、蓄力跳、光学迷彩、义体过载等经典机制手感大幅优化。天赋树彻底分层重构，衍生出三大核心极致流派，可玩性拉满：
 
1. 网络黑客流 2. 肉体狂战流 3. 潜行狙击流
武器系统同样形成完整体系，智能武器、动能武器、科技武器各有专属机制，配件改装、词条刷新体系成熟，没有绝对的最强武器，只有适配流派的最优搭配。
 
相较于传统开放世界，本作摒弃了“刷等级、堆数值”的无聊套路，构筑思路决定战力上限，每一套搭配都能带来全新的战斗体验。全程无氪金、无内购，纯单机买断制的玩法体验，在当下的3A大作中尤为良心。
 
美中不足的是，游戏底层代码顽疾尚未彻底根除，2026年版本依旧存在少量瑕疵：偶尔出现NPC抽搐、轻微穿模、楼梯卡位、加载微卡顿等小bug，极少数场景会出现闪退问题，虽不影响主线通关，但偶尔会打破沉浸感，也是这款游戏始终无法完美的核心硬伤。同时UI界面交互逻辑依旧繁琐，菜单操作、物品筛选不够便捷，长期游玩略有违和感。
 
三、剧情与人物：残酷的成人寓言，单机叙事天花板
 
玩法可以迭代优化，但顶级的叙事与人物塑造，是《赛博朋克2077》最核心、无法复刻的内核优势。本作没有传统3A游戏的英雄主义、圆满结局，只有一场关于资本碾压、命运无常、生命尊严的残酷成人寓言。
 
主线围绕主角V与传奇佣兵强尼·银手的共生羁绊展开，不再是简单的“拯救世界”套路，而是普通人在资本垄断、义体泛滥、人性异化的夜之城，对抗命运、挣扎求生、寻找自我的卑微抗争。剧情节奏张弛有度，伏笔贯穿全程，从最初的街头混混，到卷入企业阴谋、背负生死诅咒，主角的每一次抉择都贴合人物成长，真实到令人共情。
 
人物塑造堪称封神，桀骜叛逆、憎恨资本的摇滚佣兵强尼·银手，温柔坚韧、身不由己的朱迪，隐忍孤勇的帕南，每一个配角都立体鲜活，没有工具人角色。海量支线任务质量远超多数游戏主线剧情，街头的悲欢离合、资本的冷漠残酷、普通人的无奈妥协，每一条支线都在补整夜之城的世界观，细节满满、后劲十足。
 
而《往日之影》DLC作为官方终章内容，直接将游戏叙事拉高至顶级水准。谍战悬疑的剧情框架、跌宕起伏的抉择、影帝级的角色演绎，搭配完整的结局闭环，彻底弥补了原版主线的结局短板，让整个故事逻辑完整、立意深刻。
 
整款游戏没有绝对的善恶对错，所有抉择都伴随代价，没有完美结局，只有不同的遗憾，这种贴近现实的残酷叙事，也是赛博朋克美学的终极表达。唯一争议点在于主线抉择自由度有限，核心剧情走向相对固定，玩家无法彻底改写命运，存在一定的剧情局限性。
 
四、时长与性价比：买断制良心之作
 
截至2026年，游戏内容体量完全匹配3A定价，纯主线通关时长约20-25小时，主线+核心支线流程可达40-50小时，全收集、全结局、流派毕业的完美通关时长突破100小时。
 
五年持续免费更新、画质迭代、玩法重构，外加一次顶级质量的付费DLC，无任何内购、氪金、抽卡要素，相较于逐年涨价、半成品首发、后续割韭菜的主流3A游戏，《赛博朋克2077》的诚意肉眼可见。

Найди себя в отражении неоновых огней: Почему Cyberpunk 2077 — это больше, чем просто игра
Когда мы впервые ступили на улицы Найт-Сити в декабре 2020 года, мир замер. Мы ожидали увидеть идеальный симулятор будущего, а получили разбитое зеркало, осколки которого до сих пор режут нам сердце. Но если отбросить технические шероховатости первых дней и посмотреть на эту игру спустя годы, сквозь призму патчей, дополнения Phantom Liberty и собственного опыта, открывается нечто удивительное.
Cyberpunk 2077 — это не про кибернетику. Это не про хакерство или перестрелки. Это трагическая, пронзительная ода человечности в мире, который пытается её стереть.
Город, который дышит (и задыхается)
Найт-Сити — это третий главный герой этой истории. Он великолепен и отвратителен одновременно. Здесь кислотный дождь смывает кровь с асфальта, чтобы через минуту снова забрызгать его новыми жертвами корпоративных войн. Неоновые вывески кричат о счастье, которое можно купить, пока внизу, в тени небоскребов, люди продают последние воспоминания, чтобы купить еду.
Каждый уголок этого города рассказывает историю. Заброшенная квартира с недопитым кофе, граффити на стене под мостом, случайный диалог в баре — всё это ткёт полотно мира, который чувствует себя пугающе живым. Вы не просто наблюдатель; вы — часть его пульса.
Ви и Джонни: Танец двух душ
В центре всего этого хаоса — Ви. Неважно, какого происхождения ваш персонаж, его путь — это путь поиска себя. Но самое трогательное в игре — это отношения Ви и Джонни Сильверхенда.
Поначалу Кeanu Reeves в роли рок-легенды кажется просто камео, раздражающим призраком в голове. Но по мере прохождения игры происходит чудо. Вражда перерастает в понимание, понимание — в уважение, а уважение — в самую необычную дружбу, которую когда-либо показывали в видеоиграх.
Вы спорите с ним о музыке, о жизни, о смерти. Вы видите его уязвимость за маской цинизма. И когда приходит время финального выбора, ваши руки дрожат не от напряжения геймплея, а от эмоциональной тяжести решения. Кто из вас двоих достоин жить? И что значит "жить" вообще?
Фантомная свобода и цена предательства
Дополнение Phantom Liberty добавило новый слой глубины. История Соломона Рида и Сонг Ми — это шпионский триллер уровня лучших фильмов, но с душой Киберпанка. Здесь нет хороших или плохих. Есть только люди, загнанные в угол системой, которые пытаются выжить, ломая других.
Моменты, когда вам приходится выбирать между долгом и совестью, между другом и идеей, оставляют шрамы на душе игрока. Игра не судит вас. Она просто показывает последствия. И эта честность восхищает.
Почему это восхитительно?
Саундтрек: От агрессивного индастриала до меланхоличного синти-попа. Музыка здесь — не фон, а эмоция. Песня "I Really Want to Stay At Your House" становится гимном упущенных возможностей и тихой грусти.
Визуальный язык: Закаты над Пустошами, отражение неона в лужах после дождя, интерфейс, который является частью нарратива. Это один из самых красивых миров, созданных человеком.
Философия: Игра задаёт вопросы, на которые нет правильных ответов. Что делает нас людьми? Тело? Память? Душа? Или наши связи с другими?
Послесловие
Cyberpunk 2077 — это игра-исповедь. Она начиналась как амбициозный провал, но превратилась в триумф искусства. Она учит нас, что даже в самом тёмном, самом технологичном и бездушном будущем главное — это способность любить, дружить и оставаться собой.
Когда экран гаснет после финальных титров, вы не просто выключаете консоль. Вы выходите из Найт-Сити с тяжестью в груди и светом в глазах. Вы понимаете, что этот город изменил вас.
Идите в Найт-Сити. Не за экшеном. Идите туда, чтобы найти себя.

Пройдя игру на все концовки, закрыв все побочные квесты, пройдя все возможные романы и фактически «вылизав» Cyberpunk 2077 до последней мелочи, я могу сказать: я эту игру люблю. Правда люблю. Но есть нюансы, которые из раза в раз портят впечатление.
Начну с самого раздражающего — баги. Я уже коллекционирую их в скриншотах. И каждое новое прохождение приносит свежую порцию. Они не просто встречаются — они бесят. Конкретно и системно.
Теперь о сюжете и о Джонни Сильверхенде. Я его ненавижу. Искренне. Человек, который полностью просрал свою жизнь, относился к друзьям и любимой женщине как к мусору, а игра упорно заставляет нас с ним сближаться. Более того — существует концовка, в которой ты просто отдаёшь ему своё тело. Он своё уже уничтожил, а мы, оказывается, должны предоставить ему новое. Нет. Просто нет.
Если говорить о концовках в целом — единственная по-настоящему живая и человечная для меня та, что с Панам. Во всех остальных вариантах либо ты не выживаешь, либо выживаешь, но жизнь после этого превращается в унылое существование. Да, я прекрасно понимаю задумку авторов: в Найт-Сити нет «хорошего конца», твоя свеча должна гореть ярко и быстро погаснуть. Красивая метафора. Но от этого не становится менее обидно, что нет хотя бы одной концовки, в которой Ви лечит свою «кибер-рак» и получает шанс на нормальную жизнь.
Геймплей же — сплошное удовольствие. Каждый билд приносит свой особый кайф. Я даже собрал собственный «билд Ведьмака»: взламываешь мозги, рубишь мечом и добиваешь ракетницей. Работает отлично. Единственное, чего я категорически не рекомендую — умное оружие. Оно слишком казуальное: самонаводка + хороший урон. Разве что для тех, кто играет на консоли и не любит целиться.
В итоге Cyberpunk 2077 — это игра, которую я искренне люблю, несмотря на всё. Но любовь эта получается довольно сложной.

It's been a long time since a single-player game pulled me in the way Cyberpunk 2077 did. This is what the writers at CD Projekt Red do best: they create characters you genuinely care about and tell a story that emotionally engaging.

This story is a personal one. You're not here to save the world, you're trying to save yourself. And the game keeps asking how far you're willing to go for that. Do you go out in a blaze of glory and become a legend, or do you choose a quiet, long life?

Night City is the perfect stage for it. The city is loud, beautiful and completely indifferent to you. It promises everything and takes whatever it can get. Against that backdrop, the game raises some surprisingly philosophical questions: What is soul? What is consciousness? And what is left of a person once everything is taken from them?

Gameplay-wise, it's a fairly lightweight RPG in an open world. There are no fixed classes; instead you shape your playstyle through attributes, perks and cyberware. A netrunner, for example, is a hacker, basically this world's version of a mage, who attacks with quickhacks instead of spells. A solo is a sturdy tank who goes in with heavy guns or melee weapons. That gives the gameplay real variety: netrunners can sneak around, shut down cameras or trigger traps that quietly take out enemies, while solos charge straight into the fight and smash everything to pieces. You can mix and match, of course. Cyberware, meaning body implants, plays a big part here and supports whatever playstyle you go for.

You create your own character: one of three backstories, plus body, appearance and voice. Since the protagonist is fully voiced, V does come with a fixed name and a predefined personality. Still, the dialogue options leave room for role-playing, because you decide how to react in a given situation, and those choices affect how things turn out with some NPCs.

The setting is Night City, a city full of traffic, side missions and activities. Beyond the city limits lie the Badlands, wide open and sparsely populated, but still the location for a number of jobs. I'm someone who tries to see as much as possible in games, and it took me more than 200 hours to get through everything Cyberpunk 2077 has to offer.

But let me address a few negatives that need to be said. Most people will remember the disastrous launch, and it has left its mark. By now the worst bugs have been fixed and some missing features have been patched in, but it still isn't the game CDPR promised back then, because certain core features never made it in. Night City was sold as a living, interactive city. It isn't one today. It's a static, scripted backdrop that loses immersion around every corner. As a backdrop it works well, and if CDPR hadn't promised more, nobody would have a problem with it. But expectations were very different, and many fans were disappointed. That doesn't make it a bad game, but you should know what you're getting: not a reactive, simulated open world, but a static stage for a scripted story, where many of your choices are about flavour and role-playing rather than visible consequences.

The main story and many of the side jobs are very well written, but a large share of the smaller missions, such as gigs, feel like busywork: similar jobs that all play out the same way. Every now and then there's a small twist or you learn a bit more about the lore, but mostly all you get out of them is more loot and XP. At some point you don't even know what to do with it all, because money stops mattering. The world follows the Ubisoft formula: lots of "interesting" places to tick off, but little substance behind them. Early on you're also flooded with jobs that pull you away from the main story, which can get pretty annoying.

None of this makes the game bad, quite the opposite. Once you accept Night City as a backdrop, it's a beautiful and incredibly detailed one. With ray tracing or even path tracing, the neon lights really shine at night. CDPR had to think not only horizontally but also vertically, and you can see how well the high-rises fit into the cityscape. And if it all gets too much, you can simply skip the optional stuff. Just be careful with the side jobs of the main characters: skip those and you may lose options later, because you never got to know the people involved.

So Cyberpunk 2077 is far from a perfect game, but it's absolutely one you should have played, especially if you're interested in philosophical questions about what it means to exist, or if you simply love cyberpunk works like Blade Runner or Akira.

Holy, what a game. Fully enables you to live out your cyberpunk fantasies. Want to be a hulking, impenetrable machine of a man with tons of cyberware enhancing your strength, endurance, and reflexes? You can. Want to be more of a stealthy ninja with tactical camo(invisibility) and speed to bypass or rush your enemies? You can. Want to be a netrunner, spamming foes with quickhacks, applying effects ranging from various debuffs and DoTs up to making them attack their allies or straight-up one-shot them? You can. You can even do all that from distance via a camera you hacked. Want to combine any of these playstyles and more? You can. There's also a wide variety of weapons from katanas and clubs to pistols, rifles, SMGs, sniper rifles, shotguns, etc. All of them feel different and satisfying to use.

And that's just systems and mechanics. The game offers an excellent cinematic story with likes of Keanu Reeves and Idris Elba(if you get Phantom Liberty, too). I don't want to get into too much of a detail here, as I think it is worth playing through by yourself, but there is plenty of iconic characters and twists and turns to keep you entertained for dozens of hours, even if you barely do any side quests. And man, many of those are pretty good, too, and serve to flesh out the world.

I heard that the game was full of bugs on release, but I only played it after the release of Phantom Liberty and the big patch that fixed those issues, so aside from a very few visual glitches, I never experienced any performance issues nor bugs. I would honestly recommend Cyberpunk 2077 to anyone who enjoys a great action gameplay with an awesome story.

As a pre-order and day 1 player, and now after 100%ing it and the new DLC, I think this game is significantly better, and great in some respects, but still rough around the edges, and straight up bad in some respects. I did a ~90 hour playthrough on release (pain and suffering), and I just finished my 2.0 + DLC fresh playthrough which took ~40 hours. I still have a lot of complaints but I think it's at least a worthwhile experience now.

[hr][/hr]

[h2][The Bad/The Mid][/h2]
- I have a hard time with calling games like this a role-playing game, the only choices that ACTUALLY matter are the last few relating to your ending. Nearly every single quest and event in the world is linear,  barring a few rare exceptions you really don't have a say in the end result. For a world with this potential, I want to be able to explore around, be immersed, and be able to make my own decisions and see how they impact the world around me, to me that is what a good rpg is and I don't think this is one. 
- Tying in to that, the world is pretty much uninteractive, you can't talk to anyone that's not a key npc, you can't go in a random building, you can't really do much of anything if there isn't a map waypoint there. So the majority of the game is just running from waypoint to waypoint, a lá Ubisoft, which I'm not a fan of. 
- The vast majority of the world's jobs/gigs are repetitive and uninteresting, which is annoying because there are a few good ones scattered throughout so you kinda have to do all the mid/bad to get the good
- The base game's story is just bland to me, the characters are mostly uninteresting, maybe I'm just a heartless animal, I don't think enough time was spent with Jackie to really care about him. All you get is a 30 second montage at the start of the game to build your 'relationship' and everyone talks about how close you were but I don't really buy it, and I feel similarly about others.
- The romance system felt half-baked, buggy, and unnecessary to me
- The new component/crafting system is... fine? It sort of clogs up the loot and feels tact-on and not useful to me
- This may be a personal one, but I think the game balance isn't great. Which can not necessarily be a bad thing in a singleplayer game, but when there's a few extremely strong strategies that dominate gameplay, its easy to just play through large chunks of the game with your brain off playing like that. 
- With the amount of build variety now, I wish it was easier to swap between different builds. The game is artificially restrictive in that you have to choose between netrunning/sandestivan/berserk key cyberware and there's no way to swap on the fly. Also I can't fathom why they would only allow 1 respec per run.

[hr][/hr]

[h2][The Good/The Improved][/h2]
- First of all, the gameplay and gameplay progression is massively improved, the builds are much more interesting and perk tree actually relevant and interesting. I also think the cyberware system is significantly better and more thematic, and clothing not being tied to armor value is a no brainer good change. The variety of builds now are really great, special props to the new throwing knives because they are not only usable now, but actually really cool, maybe my favorite new build. Maybe this is preference, but I only found the Tech/Body trees to be uninteresting, the rest are great. 
- Phantom Liberty (PL): oh do I have so much to say about it. Its like they hired all new writers that know how to write an interesting spy thriller with good character motivations all of a sudden and makes me even sadder when thinking about the base game. Songbird and Reed are both extremely compelling for different reasons, without going too crazy into spoilers, f*ck Reed. There are fantastic themes and symbolism throughout the story and its really a very well written tragedy sort of unfolded non-linearly.
- PL: The new Dogtown area is leaps better than any base game district. First of all, this is what the density of events/gigs/stuff to do that should be going on in all of Night City, the base game feels ridiculously sparse after all this. The random airdrop events give you something interesting to do in between gigs, and even if you don't do them (which you should bc their loot is crazy) they are great world-building and and an example of interactivity with the world which I really like. The gigs are hit or miss for me in Dogtown, maybe 50/50 between good/bad ones (excluding the sleeper vehicle deliveries those suck), but is wayyyy better than the base game which is maybe more 10/90
- PL: The story and levels, actually change in Act 3, depending on a key decision you make. Which is still far from the RPG I crave but a step in the right direction. The paths are significantly different, I HIGHLY recommend doing the 'bad' path even if you reload later, even though I knew I was doing So Mi wrong, the set pieces afterwards were insanely unique and cool, you just [b]have[/b] to do this path at least once. - Quick PL spoilers and thematic discussion: [spoiler] Songbird literally lives up to her name, she's just a bird that has been caged her whole life that wants to escape, so while Reed has her best intentions, he is so headstrong he can't see he is harming her by putting her back in that cage. So the unveiling of Reed being the 'bad guy' in the Songbird story is extremely well done. The idea to make So Mi a betrayed and cornered animal if you betray her, is insanely compelling given her story and your relationship, and then to make the ultimate level a horror level as retribution is just... perfect. Super unique and unlike anything else in the game period. Great storytelling, great decisions affect the characters and world moment, no notes, just good sh*t. [/spoiler] 
- I have to give props on level designs, even in the base game, since my first run I was just a blade maniac running straight at people I didn't engage much with the levels, but my second run I did a stealthier netrunner build and enjoyed the variety of ways to approach the encounters, especially early on. 
- The police system is night and day from when I played. If you shot a civilian on day 1 you would turn around and there would be cops and drones that spawned behind you and it would just be and endless onslaught of them, completely un-interactive and immersion-breaking. Now the star system, while not really original, makes more sense, and then having Max-Tac finally existing in the world and being called on you is absolutely perfect for this game.
- On a technical level, between bugginess and performance, the game is much improved.

[hr][/hr]

My overall verdict, Phantom Liberty absolutely mogs the rest of the game, it carries my positive review on its back, heavily. The gameplay is very solid and diverse now and its way more fun to dispatch groups of enemies in different ways than before, but the game hasn't improved much in terms of the RPG elements, immersiveness, and world since launch. If you're more into traditional RPGs and not just 'only perk-tree' RPGs, you probably won't like it much like me, its comparable to Skyrim. If you're in it for the story/writing, the DLC is a highlight, the base game is lackluster in that aspect imo. If you like the newer Bethesda games, or like Ubisoft open world games, I think you'd love this game. While the game isn't [i]bad[/i], I just expected it to be a more interactive and compelling world, and a better RPG to accompany it, so I felt pretty underwhelmed by the experience (except for the DLC). On a meta level, it is a bit absurd I needed to wait for a several years and a DLC release for the game they advertised to even somewhat resemble the actual product, I'm exhausted of studios releasing overambitious projects with not enough development time. I'd rather have a smaller city/world that is a tighter, more curated experience than a giant Ubisoft-slop world. But maybe das just me :p

[h2]後期資本主義の地獄へようこそ[/h2]
近未来のディストピアを描いた作品。全てが消費される世界。
子供がいるような空間でもお構いなしに性的な広告が流れ、化学合成による食品ばかりが流通する。
消費されるのは人も例外ではない。例えば、コーポレートは企業の歯車として使い捨てられる。
心身を犠牲にして働いても、欺きと競争の中で生活そのものを失う。
例えば、インパクトのある事件を起こした傭兵は「伝説」として消費される。
[spoiler]主人公とて、結局、その枠組みで消費される一人に過ぎない。[/spoiler]

徹底されたサイバーパンクの世界観がそこにある。

[h2]選択と代償[/h2]
エンディングに分岐する選択はそう多くはないが、細かい分岐が沢山。
欺き、欺かれ、戦いの中で世界観の理解が深まっていく。

エンディングに関しても上述のような世界観なので、
[spoiler]何かを得るには何かを失わないといけない。物語冒頭のフィクサーの問いがエンディングで答えとして帰ってくる。細く長くか、太く短くか、の２択しかない。もっとも主人公にとっては後者の一択しかない[/spoiler]

個人的なお気に入りは[spoiler]「塔」エンド。唯一命は助かるし、関係者が助かる望みも残ってはいる。代償に生き方を失い、自分の行動が徒労だったことも判明する(アラサカ社は手を下さずとも撤退に追い込まれる)。[/spoiler]
ぐっと現実に引き戻されるエンディングで、一番心に残った。
ただし、このエンディングを選んでしまうとそのセーブデータが使い物にならなくなる(エンディング分岐地点まで戻れない)ので、その点だけどうにかしてほしかった。

GTA, but it's in a messed up and punked up version of the future, and it's also an RPG. 

Bought it on release, waited for a few years before playing it. Still has more bugs than I would like, but none of them have been game breaking. Glad I waited, and glad I decided to actually play it and not refund it.

WORLD AND ATMOSPHERE
Incredible world and atmosphere. I have not experienced anything like it. It's best explained by this example: In the middle of a mission, it was raining at night and I was supposed to go inside some store to interrogate a guy. I simply ended up sitting in the car for a while, stepping outside and just taking in the scenery, trying try pretend I was actually there. Never been able to do this so well in any other game. Honestly brilliantly done, it says a lot about how much effort they put into the atmosphere.

Some open world games fail to make the world come alive. Especially the ones that are in big cities. This game manages to make the world come alive and feel interactive on the same level as a GTA game, and that is a huge compliment. It is more buggy, and the vehicle variety isn't as good as GTA, but the game makes up for that in other ways, like with the character customization (build paths and so on). It also has loads of all the "life stuff" that GTA games are famous for, and it does them well.

CHARACTERS AND CHOICES
The characters, the premise and thickening plot are also selling the game hard. Deep and multi-dimensional characters, similar to how they function in The Witcher, but belonging to this world ofc. Over the top, but still believable scenarios where you have make difficult and often very ambiguous choices. It also shows you and forces you to consider what your stance is on a lot of ethical dilemmas linked to a highly technological world where humans, AI and robotic implants mix together in an incredibly corrupt city where the environmental concerns of today where never dealt with. 

Haven't finished the story yet, but at 100 hours, I can safely recommend it. Does require a beast of a PC though, that's also part of why I waited a long time to play it.

TLDR: GTA, but it's in a messed up and punked up version of the future, and it's also an RPG. Bit buggy, and requires a strong PC, otherwise super good.

Запустил игру просто посмотреть Найт-Сити. Через несколько часов уже гоняю на тачке, стреляю по бандитам и веду философские разговоры с людьми, у которых больше имплантов, чем у меня здравого смысла.

Город — просто космос. Вечно куда-то спешишь, но постоянно отвлекаешься: «О, интересная точка на карте». Через минуту ты уже взрываешь склад и совершенно забыл, куда вообще ехал.

Стрельба бодрая, прокачка затягивает, оружия столько, что можно открыть небольшой оружейный магазин. А машины иногда ведут себя так, будто водитель получил права в GTA.

Правда, иногда Найт-Сити живёт по своим законам: NPC могут внезапно начать разговаривать с невидимым человеком, машина может решить, что физика — это рекомендация, а прохожий способен материализоваться прямо из стены, будто у него срочный вызов из другого измерения.

Итог: отличная игра. Если увидите меня в Найт-Сити — не зовите. Я занят. Мне ещё 36 побочных квестов пройти.

I don't really write reviews for games unless it's a joke, because I don't really care to. However I feel like I should write one for this game, as it holds an interesting place in my heart. This game is not a masterpiece, not even close, and everyone who tells you it is is lying. This game is unfortunately a shell of what it SHOULD have been, and does not deliver on many fronts. The RPG is shallow, the gunplay is fun but repetitive, and the story is all over the place. So why am I giving it a good review? Because despite all that, I really do love this game, in all of its sloppiness. The atmosphere is awesome and beautiful, it FEELS like a cyberpunk world, the music is great and I listen to some of the tracks regularly. The combat has its moments where I feel like a TRUE edgerunner and can be genuinely fun. The story may not have the best pacing and sometimes just doesn't hit, but when it DOES hit, it hits good. There are so many scenes and story beats that I love and have made me FEEL emotional. I also just love customizing my character and messing around with the awesome photo mode. So is this game a 10/10 masterpiece that should be praised for everything it's done. God no. Not even close. CDPR still screwed us and gave us a game that doesn't even begin to reflect what they promised, but goddammit do I love it. This game is slop, but it's MY slop. I would give it an 8/10 and I still plan to keep playing till I can't anymore. Now the game isn't COMPLETELY bad, and I think some people are FAR too harsh on it, looking at it from a less biased lens, I think it's a fine game, and I think a lot of people can find things to enjoy about it, just maybe get it on sale. And for the people who REALLY love this game, this is not an attack. I LOVE this game, but I'm not going to mindlessly glaze it and praise CDPR for what they have done (though I do really appreciate what they have done with the game and think they made something pretty solid). ALL I ask is that no one EVER forgets how this game was released and how the developers and consumers were treated. Do not forget what CDPR did, hold them accountable. Cyberpunk 2077 is a fine game and does somethings really well. But it is NOT a masterpeice at ALL.

Cyberpunk’s generational comeback needs to be studied. From a horrible launch to a game whose polish allows you to see it for the absolute gem of an experience that it is. Night City is an absolutely gorgeous city. When first beginning my playthrough, I would just get lost in the city. I’d drive, travel by NCART (Night City’s public metro system), or even walk through the streets. There is also a desert area outside Night City called the Badlands that breathes even more life into the game, reminding you that it isn’t just a city you’re exploring, but an entirely different world lush with its own lore and backstory. The only flaw of the open-world setup is that there isn’t much to do in the world (outside of missions) compared to games like GTA. But Cyberpunk has a large number of story-heavy interactive missions that will have you doing a variety of things, and the game gives you the freedom to accomplish many missions in whatever way you like (stealth or guns blazing). The dialogue you pick on these missions can also dictate how the mission ends. I personally found myself repeating the missions over and over because I hated one outcome and wanted to get another one. However, you’ll learn quickly that many missions don’t have a “perfect” outcome, and the outcome YOU like will depend largely on YOUR morals and personal values. The main plot of the base game is pretty good, but if you pick up the DLC, you’ll realize Phantom Liberty’s story is S-tier. The characters themselves are also pretty good (and the PL characters are especially good). The combat of the game is also a big selling point. You can customize your character in a variety of different ways. You can play like a “samurai” with a katana, a regular merc with a gun, etc. You can choose many different abilities according to the cyberware you equip. Equip a sandy? Now you’re moving like the Flash and murdering enemies before they even see you coming. Equip a cyberdeck? You are effectively the closest thing Night City has to a god because you can hack other people’s cyberware and it can go from basic stuff like overheating their cyberware to forcing people to kill each other. If you play Phantom Liberty, you can gain access to a netrunning ability that is so powerful, it's unspeakable in this review. There are many other cool abilities in this game as well, and I’d heavily encourage experimenting. As for the soundtrack, A-tier. The game has many awesome radio songs and battle themes, including one song that you may recognize if you watch the Cyberpunk anime. Overall, this game is absolutely worth checking out as it has so many amazing things going for it - setting, soundtrack, gameplay, characters, and plot. You will find yourself sucked into this huge city of hopes and dreams, and carving your name in history as a legend.

Ama hem sürekli gelen güncellemeler, yeni içerikler ve cillop gibi hazırlanmış yeni hikaye Phantom Liberty dahil, CD Projekt Red oyunu çok güzel toplayıp derlemiş. Evet, maalesef verdikleri sözlerin çoğunu tutamadılar, ancak oyunu olduğu gibi değerlendirmeye başlayınca elimizdeki ürün aşırı sağlam. 57 başarımın 45'ini alıp oyunu istediğim sonla bitirdikten sonra ''keşke biraz daha sürseydi'' dedim. Ki ben oyunu güncel haliyle, yani yeni içeriklerle desteklenmiş haliyle, üstüne Phantom Liberty DLC'siyle birliklte oynadım. Tüm yan görevleri bitirdim, sibersaykoları yakaladım, hiç az olmayan NCPD görevlerini yaptım, istediğim tüm araçları aldım, şehri tavaf ettim. Oyunun bana sunabileceği ne varsa deneyimledim, ve buna rağmen daha fazlasını istedim. Geldiğim en son raddede build'im Sandevistan + Katana + Malorian Arms 3516 üzerineydi. Hem Johnny Silverhand'in tabancasıyla yargı dağıtıp millete The Rebel Path şarkısıyla terör estiriyor, sonra Sandevistan'ı aktif edip milleti kılıç manyağı ettikten sonra etrafa saçılan vücut parçalarını izliyordum. Bazen ise hiç görev yapasım yoksa Porsche 911 Turbo (930) arabama atlıyor, şehirde caka satıp SAMURAI şarkıları eşliğinde sokaklara esas stil nasıl olur onu gösteriyordum. Sokakta bana iş olan çeteleri karım yapıyor, esas karım Panam'ı eve atıyor, pompadan sonra bir kadeh viski ve sigaramı yakıyordum. Cyberpunk ben bu satırları yazarken sağlam bir comeback atıyor. Edgerunners 2, diğer oyunlarla işbirlikleri, yeni merchler derken, tekrardan sağlam bir popülarite yakalıyor. Deneyimleyebiliyorsanız, kesinlikle Night City sokaklarına bir göz atın derim.

Its ok. Story was interesting at first but towards the end I was just rushing through to get it over with. Gameplay was whatever. I mostly played with Katanas, maybe that was a bad idea but it was just fine. AI provides no challenge. I recall defeating one boss by circling around a pillar repeatedly while blasting it with headshots each time it froze to T-pose. Enough said there I think. Almost never engaged with the quickhack mechanics, it was easy enough just running up and slicing enemies with my katana. Tried to do a stealth build but I got bored because of the unintelligent AI so I switched to melee/shotguns, which made it less boring.

The world is very pretty and interesting to look at. I never felt particularly interested or encouraged to explore so I never did except to finish quests. I think the only optional content I finished was the Delamaine quest and part of the cyberpycho quests. Very forgettable.

I never felt like my dialogue choices made much difference, especially the skill checks. I don't think those options affected dialogue even a single time. Most irritating example was succeeding a "cool" check to ask a merchant for a discount. They immediately tell me to fuck off. Why even waste my time?

 I did enjoy dressing up my character quite a bit. It was the only thing I ever spent my money on since the game throws guns at you and I never felt the need to buy a car. It was annoying though because I had to keep driving around to different clothing stores to find clothes I liked.

I expected a lot more from this game. It was all kind of forgettable and never particularly interesting. None of the characters made much of an impression on me except for the arasaka bodyguard (cant remember his name) but I didn't know I could save him so he just died. Modern games have trained me to assume I cant do anything that isn't explicitly told to me by the game, so good on them for having a hidden outcome, but it ended up removing the only character I cared about so R.I.P. I think I got the "good" ending (the aldecaldo ending), but it didn't leave me satisfied (partly because I screwed up hooking up with Panam, my fault). I'd say this game was about as enjoyable as Fallout 4, with a better story and much better character customization.

Є ігри, які виходять один раз за весь час існування ігродева   які не хочеться проходити... Не тому, що вони погані, а тому, що таких більше не буде.

Настільки глибоко зачепила історія Ві, Джонні та світ Cyberpunk, його опрацьованість, хоч і не без технічних та геймплейних огріхів, що довго відкладав фінал гри... Щоб якомога довше не покидати цей наповнений неоном та атмосферою жорстокого, але технічно розвиненого майбутнього з імплантами, що дають нереальні можливості у вигляді уповільнення часу або автоприцілювання зброї, скриптами, що змушують палати ворога на відстані, або того гірше.

Але всьому приходить кінець, і морально, і технічно гра стала надто відставати від новинок, тому прийняв рішення пройти її після розтягування майже на 3 роки.

Якщо забути, що являла собою гра на релізі, то очікування її фіксу перед покупкою того вартувало.

Розробники непогано попихтіли над технічною стороною, і до неї особливо немає питань. На 4070 при ультра налаштуваннях  (усіх, що можна виставити) в 2К, видає стабільні 100+ FPS і навіть без генерації.

Графіка... Тут навіть у 2026-му році цю гру використовують для тестування нових відеокарт, тому можна сказати, що вона більш ніж гідна, щоб передати атмосферу майбутнього та світу Cyberpunk на всі 100%.

Квести. Кожен квест має в собі задатки окремого унікального мінісюжету. Немає банальних «Подай, принеси». Навіть найпростіші квести, на кшталт поліцейських запитів або замовлень фіксера, несуть у собі окрему мініісторію. Не кажучи вже про додаткові квести, які самі викликають не тільки моральне задоволення від проходження, а й здивування зі словами: "Та ладно!?"   від несподіваних поворотів сюжету. Все це робить Cyberpunk, на відміну від більшості конвеєрних проєктів із відкритим світом, не просто гріндилкою заради ачивки в штучно розтягнутій копіпасті на 100500 кв. км карти, а неповторним, наповненим захопливими пригодами світом.

Світ Кіберпанку в цілому... Що тут сказати... Це, напевно, єдина гра з відкритим світом, у якій практично не використовував фаст тревел. Тільки вже під кінець гри та в рідкісних моментах проходження.
Гра дає задоволення просто їхати на машині неоновим містом майбутнього під шикарні саундтреки радіо (а зокрема, напевно, варто відзначити саундтрек "I Really Want to Stay at Your House", який став гімном цієї гри, прослуховування якого навіть на YouTube подумки переносить у гру). Заслуговує на увагу той факт, що місто та всі технічні фішки/особливості розкриваються саме вночі. Власне, і назва міста саме що Нічне Місто.

Персонажі, що, знову таки, рідкість у наш толерантний час, запам'ятовуються і мають не просто базову історію/сюжет, але і в якомусь роді вони представляються глибокими та травмованими, кожен по своєму індивідуальними, яких намагаєшся зрозуміти. Мало в яких іграх тобі буде цікава передісторія або особистість простого NPC. Діалоги з персонажами побудовані так, ніби ти спілкуєшся як у житті   розслаблено, легко та невимушено, без відчуття якоїсь награності чи офіціозу, що робить гру живою.

Кінцівка залишила після себе гіркий післясмак, але в хорошому сенсі. Давно не було таких емоцій. Особливо суму.   не тільки через прощання з персонажами та з Ві, а й від того, яку ціну потрібно заплатити наприкінці.

Яку кінцівку обрав, розкривати не буду, але вона своєю складністю вибору ідеально відобразила цей жорстокий світ майбутнього. Коли, начебто, технології, здатні давати безсмертя та лікувати всі хвороби, в руках людства перетворюються на інструмент контролю та збагачення. Цей контраст між досягненнями людства та реальністю на вулицях Найт Сіті переслідуватиме всю гру, щоб в кінці підтвердити очікуване, а саме, що за все треба платити, і платити дуже дорого.

Підсумувати можна з того, з чого почав. Важко залишати цю гру, так як мало проєктів допомагають відволіктися від більш жорстокої реальності, яку, на жаль, доводиться щодня спостерігати та чути за вікном. Але цій грі це вдалося, за що вдячний розробникам.

[h3] 在夜之城的中心呼唤爱 [/h3]决定要打全成就到实现磕磕绊绊用了一年多，也算是打完了。从打开2077开始算的话，应该有两年多了。一开始玩的时候还什么都不知道，最爱玩潜行的任务，这游戏玩困难模式也不会有太大压力。CDPR游戏后期的数值膨胀是人尽皆知。
后来为了打成就方便，重开的档都是黑客流了。玩游戏本体的时候，其实打到结局，已经有很大感触了。帕南有着笨拙但是就是爱你的坚定信念，才愿意离开家族陪v。包括月亮结局，我做的都心里难受。强尼身上带有一种只有少数人能读懂的个性意义，而很遗憾我觉得我没有和他灵魂共鸣。
因为开的是旧的档打dlc，卡了好几次bug，最后都拿不到成就。这次补丁更新完后，就决定重新打。我觉得应该本体是男v代入感强一些，dlc女v更好。我个人比较喜欢的是本体的的太阳结局和dlc的钱币国王高塔结局。玩的时候感觉亚历克斯立了这么多flag，按照压抑的故事走线来看，应该是活不长了。但是最后死的时候还是感觉很痛。而且背叛百灵鸟这条线实在是太完整了。CDPR做恐怖小玩法做的一直很好。巫师三那个闹鬼高塔和百灵鸟追逐战氛围感都给足了，有力气。
可能我本人觉得新的高塔结局还挺不错的，可是社区里好像都不太喜欢，我记得原来是v做思维复健的那个任务的，现在改成联系其他角色了。不知怎么我觉得看到每个人都有自己的生活，其实感觉还挺安心。但是v的配音给我一种拘谨又怕打扰别人生活的被抛弃味道，听的我心好难受。其实游戏里我那么长时间都在路上自己做任务和跑图，他们联系我的次数还没中间人多，玩这游戏孤独就是底色，所以我觉得这结局也比较映射玩家吧。感觉最后看到米斯蒂，回想起这一路上实在是没绷住的泪目了。其实我一直不明白v为什么不愿离开夜之城。我想可能对他来说，心性如此，无论去哪都是夜之城。
而我完成的最后一个成就是狗镇五星通缉。感觉自己颇有一种经历了无数次结局之后得了赛博精神病的荒诞感，在越来越多的暴恐机动队面前无力招架，结束了罪恶的一生。之后一套丝滑的卸载加存档清理，这就是我见2077的最后一面了。
无论怎样，我都诚挚的感谢CDPR愿意无偿的一直对游戏优化和维护，作为后人，才能玩到这样一款游戏。从世界观到略有遗憾的故事过程，到十分完整的结局。现在我回忆着太阳结局，然后感慨卧槽v，你可真是个传奇。而我则要去另一个世界线体验公司狗开局了。

Sinceramente, cuando empecé Cyberpunk 2077 ya esperaba que fuera un juegazo, pero aun así me ha sorprendido muchísimo.

Las primeras 5-6 horas iba un poco perdido y pensaba que el juego iba a ser bastante más complejo de lo que realmente es. Pero una vez te metes de lleno en Night City, todo empieza a encajar y es un juego que he disfrutado muchísimo de principio a fin.

Una de las cosas que más me ha gustado es el gameplay. Las posibilidades que tienes, las armas, las habilidades y, en general, la forma de jugar hacen que sea muy divertido. Pero si hay algo que para mí destaca especialmente es la historia y, sobre todo, sus personajes.

Los personajes se sienten muy reales. No solo por cómo están hechos físicamente, sus caras, expresiones o movimientos, sino por todo lo que hay detrás de ellos. Sus historias, sus problemas, sus vivencias, sus relaciones... consiguen que realmente te importe lo que les pasa. Y aquí tengo que mencionar especialmente a Johnny Silverhand, porque su historia y la relación que vas construyendo con él me han parecido impresionantes. Es uno de esos personajes que acabas entendiendo y viviendo durante el juego.

Y luego está Night City. El mundo es simplemente increíble. Tienes una ciudad enorme, con zonas completamente diferentes entre sí, y todo el territorio que la rodea, con la zona desértica y los Badlands. Recorrerlo es una pasada y da la sensación de estar realmente dentro de ese mundo.

¿Hay cosas mejorables? Sí. Por ejemplo, creo que los NPC podrían tener algo más de profundidad y resultar más naturales, porque en algunos momentos recuerdan bastante a los de otros mundos abiertos como GTA V. Pero sinceramente, es algo que no llega ni de lejos a estropear la experiencia.

También me ha sorprendido muchísimo el doblaje al castellano. Hay personajes que hablan con acento español, otros con acento latinoamericano, personajes que hablan japonés... y todo está muy bien integrado. No se siente como el típico diálogo genérico de un videojuego. Cuando los personajes hablan, realmente parece que están teniendo una conversación de verdad.

Y tengo que mencionar los vehículos, porque me encantan en este tipo de juegos. Hay auténticas preciosidades y conducir por Night City, especialmente de noche, es una maravilla. Si además le sumas el modo foto, puedes acabar simplemente dando vueltas por la ciudad con un coche que te encanta y haciendo fotos, y sorprendentemente es algo que me ha divertido muchísimo.

En definitiva, Cyberpunk 2077 me ha parecido un juegazo. He disfrutado muchísimo de la historia, los personajes, el mundo, el gameplay y simplemente de perderme por Night City.

Muy recomendable. De esos juegos que terminas y te quedas pensando en todo lo que has vivido.

The game's greatest achievement is arguably its world-building. Night City functions not simply as a setting, but as a living cultural phenomenon. Its juxtaposition of immense technological advancement with social inequality creates a fascinating dystopian paradox: humanity possesses unprecedented technological capabilities while remaining fundamentally flawed. 🤖🏢💰

Narratively, the game demonstrates remarkable thematic ambition. Questions concerning consciousness, identity, mortality, corporate power, and technological determinism are integrated into the experience with surprising sophistication. Characters such as Johnny Silverhand provide particularly compelling examinations of ego, legacy, rebellion, and existential uncertainty. 🎸💀🧠

Mechanically, the sheer variety of possible playstyles is equally impressive. Players can specialize in firearms, stealth, hacking, cyberware, melee combat, or combinations thereof. 🔫🥷💻⚔️ This flexibility transforms Night City into a remarkably expressive playground where experimentation is consistently rewarded.

Visually, *Cyberpunk 2077* is nothing short of spectacular. Its architecture, lighting, character design, environmental detail, and vibrant neon aesthetic combine to produce an almost absurdly cinematic experience. 🎨🌃✨ The soundtrack further enhances this atmosphere, transforming routine journeys through the city into strangely profound audiovisual experiences. 🎵🚗🌌

Ultimately, *Cyberpunk 2077* represents an ambitious synthesis of narrative, technology, art, and interactive design. It is simultaneously a science-fiction epic, philosophical meditation, urban simulation, and spectacular action RPG. 🤯🎮

El título alcanza una cota de inmersión en virtud de la cual, más que jugar, vives una experiencia. No me pararé a detallar el apartado técnico: es una joya de neón. ¿La jugabilidad? Espectacular.

Los personajes son carismáticos y profundos al grado de cogerles un cariño que repercute en que nos importen, genuinamente, sus posibles desenlaces.

Sin duda, una maravilla técnica y narrativa que, te guste el género o no, disfrutarás. J'écris cette review après la fin d'un 3e playthrough : 3 départs différents (nomade, corpo, gamin des rues), 3 styles de jeu différents (stealth netrunner, sandevistan, et ninja/katana/lancer de couteaux). J'y reviendrai. 

   Cyberpunk est l'un des meilleurs jeux auxquels j'ai joué ces dernières années. Grand fan de l'esthétique cyberpunk, cette branche de l'anticipation/dystopie me fascine au plus haut point et cette pépite du jeu vidéo n'a fait qu'augmenter ce sentiment. Le climat oppressant d'un monde ultracapitaliste, tombé aux mains de giga corporations aux pratiques inhumaines... la ville, l'une des plus belles du jeu vidéo, et ses rues, dans lesquelles j'ai passé des heures à conduire sans but, la nuit, de la musique dans les oreilles... les personnages, attachants au possible, dont les destins tragiques m'ont trop souvent arraché des larmes. Cyberpunk crée avec une grande virtuosité un monde cohérent, et les personnages qui l'arpentent le sont tout autant. Chacun d'entre eux a son histoire, ses quêtes, des relations, etc. Sérieusement, c'est un des rares jeux qui a réussi à altérer mon vocabulaire pendant aussi longtemps, tant les références et le lexique sont riches et bien écrits. Ca participe vraiment à créer une histoire qui tient debout, et un environnement très réaliste où les personnages habitent véritablement le monde. Les trois départs possibles sont intéressants, et sont surtout importants pour ceux qui aiment le roleplay : c'est d'ailleurs le premier jeu où j'ai pris plaisir à me créer une identité, un style de jeu précis. Je roulais dans des voitures particulières pour coller à ce style, je portais des fringues différentes, etc... 

   Parlons des styles de jeu. C'est une facette de Cyberpunk qui ne m'a pas sauté aux yeux immédiatement, mais le jeu offre une vraie variété d'équipements, d'armes, de skills, et d'implants pour que vous puissez aborder tous les combats avec le plus de liberté possible. Vous pouvez nettoyer un immeuble entier sans être vu, ou sans jamais y entrer, avec un des gameplay "hacker" les plus poussés et fluides du genre. Vous pouvez au contraire incarner un psycho ultra violent et découper tout le monde en 7 en l'espace de 2 secondes. C'est jouissif d'avoir autant de choix, et chaque style de combat est satisfaisant à sa manière. 

  Foncez sur le jeu, sans hésiter, et achetez le DLC, qui vraiment exceptionnel à mon avis. Je pense que c'est une expérience à vivre au moins une fois dans sa vie : l'histoire vous marquera, le gameplay vous manquera, et si, comme moi, vous relancez le jeu de temps en temps pour faire des tours dans la ville, je pense que le jeu aura réussi sa mission.
