I had never written a game review before because I thought it was unnecessary. However, after playing Cyberpunk 2077, I felt a huge desire to share my thoughts. Honestly, I still find it hard to find the right words to describe everything I felt while playing.

At first, my expectations were around 7/10. I have always liked cyberpunk and dystopian worlds, so the concept immediately interested me. I had also heard that Cyberpunk 2077 was unfinished, full of problems, and far from a masterpiece. Still, I hoped I would like it.

But after a few hours, I realized that I was going to love this game.

Cyberpunk 2077 captivated me with its atmosphere, story, characters, gameplay, huge world and, especially, its music. The more I played, the more I realized that it wasn't just another open-world game. It was a world I wanted to stay in.

[h1] Story [/h1]

The story of Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best I have ever experienced in a game. From the very beginning, it was hard to imagine where it would lead and what would happen next.

The game stays with you even after you finish it. You keep thinking about what happened, the characters, their decisions, and the choices you made.

Cyberpunk 2077 explores many important topics: life and death, friendship, loss, loneliness, memory, the fear of being forgotten, and what it means to be yourself.

The idea of fighting for your own life isn't new, but the way CD Projekt Red used it is incredible. [spoiler] You literally end up with a person in your head who was once your enemy and the biggest threat to your life. However, they gradually become your friend and even try to save you.

The relationship between V and Johnny is one of the emotional cores of the game. Their relationship changes from hate and mutual distrust to real friendship. [/spoiler]

The side quests also feel meaningful. Many tell their own stories, develop the characters and world, and sometimes even add to the main story. Because of this, Night City gradually starts to feel alive.

[h1] Night City [/h1]

Night City is another reason to love this game.

At first, it seems incredible: neon signs, skyscrapers, implants, cars, advertisements, technology, gangs and corporations. You look at it and think, "This is the future".

But behind the neon signs are poverty, violence, addiction, exploitation and people simply trying to survive.

This contrast makes the atmosphere so strong. Even in a world where people can change almost any part of their bodies, human problems remain. People still fall in love, lose loved ones, fear death, feel lonely and search for the meaning of life.

[h1] Phantom Liberty [/h1]

[spoiler] It is worth mentioning Phantom Liberty. In my opinion, it is even stronger than the main story.

Song So Mi, or Songbird, and Reed are, for me, two sides of the same coin. Songbird tries to survive at any cost, just like V. Reed wants to save her, but he is also controlled by the president and the system he serves.

The best thing is that you can understand both of them. There is no simple "right" choice. Everyone has their own reasons, fears and beliefs.

That is why I found the main choice in Phantom Liberty so difficult.

The DLC's main musical theme makes the ending even more powerful. There is no simple answer where everyone ends up happy, and that leaves you with a very heavy feeling. [/spoiler]

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

The gameplay offers a lot of variety. You can play as a pure netrunner, a stealth character with silenced weapons, a monowire fighter, or use smart guns from behind cover.

And that's just one example.

I like that the game lets you create your own playstyle. Your V can be a netrunner, stealth killer, katana fighter, gunslinger, or someone who simply rushes into a room with a shotgun. Most importantly, these styles really feel different.

[h1] Music [/h1]

The soundtrack is truly incredible.

The tracks fit the situations perfectly and make you feel even more immersed in the world. Cyberpunk 2077 combines many styles, from loud and energetic tracks to slow, melancholic and tense ones.

Energetic music makes you feel like a cool mercenary with cyberimplants who can do almost anything. But when something quiet and melancholic starts playing, you see another side of this world. Behind the neon signs is a harsh reality, and V becomes an ordinary person who fears death, experiences loss, falls in love and searches for the meaning of life.

Each track creates its own mood or captures a particular situation.

When I listen to this music, the whole atmosphere of the game comes back. That's why I added almost every track to my playlist, and I still listen to them regularly.

It would be an insult to the composers not to add the Cyberpunk 2077 soundtrack to my playlist.

The only thing I regret is that some tracks were never released on digital platforms and remained available only in the game.

[h1] Flaws [/h1]

Of course, Cyberpunk 2077 isn't perfect.

The biggest problem becomes noticeable when trying to complete the game 100%. At first, additional activities help you explore Night City, but many eventually become repetitive. Gigs and interesting side quests are great, but some smaller activities turn into simply "clearing" areas.

There is also a contrast between how alive Night City seems and how much you can actually interact with it. The city is incredibly detailed, but outside quests, many NPCs and elements are mostly decoration. I wish there were more ways to simply live in this world.

Some characters could also have been developed further. Some left a strong impression on me, while others appeared, played their role and disappeared quickly. This is especially noticeable in Phantom Liberty, where the characters receive much more attention.

[spoiler] There is also a problem with the sense of urgency. The game constantly reminds you that V has limited time and needs to save their life quickly. At the same time, nothing stops you from putting this problem off for dozens of hours, driving around the city, completing gigs, buying cars and doing whatever you want. From a gameplay perspective, this is understandable, but sometimes it contradicts the story. [/spoiler]

However, these flaws are minor for me. When I think about Cyberpunk 2077, I don't remember repetitive activities or imperfect AI. I remember Johnny, Panam, Judy, Song So Mi, Reed, Night City, the music, my decisions, and the emotions the game made me feel.

[h1] Afterthoughts [/h1]

After about 20 hours, I realized that simply finishing the main story wouldn't be enough. I wanted to complete the game 100%.

I rarely want to explore all of a game's content, but in Cyberpunk 2077 I wanted to do everything: complete side quests, experience characters' stories, try different builds, make different choices, and explore Night City.

Even after finishing the game, you are left with the feeling that you have just stepped out of another life. That's why it was so hard to close the game and move on to something else.

[h1] Finally [/h1]

Even on my not very powerful laptop, I was able to fully enjoy this game. I especially appreciate the developers for making such a huge and beautiful world accessible even on relatively weak hardware.

Cyberpunk 2077 is the kind of game that makes it difficult to immediately start something new.

Maybe I couldn't describe everything I wanted to. Maybe some things are simply impossible to describe properly in words. However, I know one thing for sure:

Cyberpunk 2077 is a game I won't forget for a very long time.

Zerei Cyberpunk 2077 no lançamento e, naquela época, não recomendaria. Rejoguei diversas vezes ao longo dos anos, acompanhei a evolução e comprei até no Xbox. Hoje eu digo com tranquilidade: esse jogo É FODA. E Phantom Liberty é, pra mim, uma das melhores DLCs já feitas para qualquer jogo.

Essa mudança de opinião importa. Eu estava lá quando saiu, joguei até o fim e sei o quanto a recomendação mudou pra mim. Os problemas do lançamento continuam fazendo parte da história. Só que também seria injusto ignorar tudo que veio depois, principalmente tendo voltado tantas vezes a Night City.

A cidade continua sendo um dos grandes motivos pra entrar nesse mundo. Prédios empilhados, propaganda invadindo cada espaço e luxo dividindo a rua com miséria. A arquitetura conta muita coisa antes de alguém abrir a boca: quem tem dinheiro ocupa o espaço de um jeito, quem precisa sobreviver se aperta onde dá. Até o teu corpo entra nessa lógica de comprar uma versão melhor de si mesmo.

A história de V dá uma dimensão pessoal a esse cenário. Tem ambição, identidade, medo de morrer e aquela convivência com Johnny Silverhand, que consegue transformar um minuto de silêncio numa discussão. Os personagens ajudam a dar peso ao que está acontecendo. É muito mais fácil se importar com uma cidade quando tu se importa com quem vive nela.

E o combate tem liberdade pra sustentar as voltas. Armas, lâminas, furtividade e invasões rápidas mudam a maneira de abordar uma situação. Controlar câmeras e atacar pela rede exige uma preparação diferente de entrar cortando todo mundo. Montar a combinação de habilidades e implantes faz parte da graça, porque ela aparece na maneira como o personagem se movimenta e resolve os confrontos.

A atualização gratuita 2.0 reformulou vantagens, implantes e polícia. A armadura passou a depender principalmente dos implantes, com uma capacidade que limita o que tu consegue instalar. Essas mudanças são do jogo base. Phantom Liberty acrescenta sua própria campanha, Dogtown e a árvore Relic, entre outras novidades. Vale separar as duas coisas pra entender o tamanho da evolução.

Phantom Liberty merece espaço de verdade nesta análise. Dogtown tem uma identidade própria dentro de Night City, com estruturas arruinadas e uma milícia controlando o território. A trama de espionagem coloca V no meio de interesses políticos e lealdades difíceis de decifrar. Reed e Songbird fazem parte desse jogo em que confiar em alguém pode custar caro. A busca por uma saída continua pessoal, mesmo quando tem gente muito poderosa puxando os fios.

É uma expansão que eu coloco entre as melhores de qualquer jogo, sem precisar diminuir esse elogio. A história e os conflitos ampliam o que Cyberpunk tem de mais interessante: pessoas tentando conservar alguma liberdade num mundo que trata todo mundo como recurso. Pra quem gostou do jogo base, recomendo muito incluir Phantom Liberty na experiência.

Ainda existem limites. As origens de V poderiam influenciar mais a campanha, há atividades repetitivas e nem toda a cidade permite a interação que o cenário sugere. Isso não mudou o quanto gosto do conjunto hoje. Minha recomendação vem dessa relação de anos com a obra, passando pelo lançamento, pelas rejogadas e pela expansão.

9/10. Recomendo muito.

Comecei sem conseguir recomendar e terminei comprando de novo em outra plataforma. Night City levou meu dinheiro duas vezes, e eu ainda estou aqui elogiando.

**Cyberpunk 2077 — це моє ігрове кохання ❤️**

Пройшов Cyberpunk 2077 і можу сміливо сказати, що це одна з найкращих ігор, у які я коли-небудь грав. На мою думку, в неї точно повинен пограти кожен.

Ми граємо за Ві — найманця з Найт-Сіті, який робить усе можливе, щоб потрапити у вищу лігу та вижити. Історія дуже добре написана й тримає в напрузі практично до самого кінця. У грі є кілька фіналів, а твої рішення та дії протягом проходження впливають на те, чим у підсумку закінчиться історія Ві. Сам фінал залишає сильні емоції й точно не залишить байдужим.

Окремо хочеться відзначити світ гри. Найт-Сіті та Пустоші неймовірно красиві, деталізовані й наповнені життям. Місто дійсно відчувається живим і неповторним. Тут постійно знаходиш щось нове, а чудова музика ще більше доповнює атмосферу.

Окрім основного сюжету, у грі величезна кількість додаткових місій. І що найважливіше — це не просто завдання заради кількості. Багато з них мають власні історії, унікальних персонажів і цікаві ситуації. Саме завдяки цьому досліджувати світ було неймовірно цікаво.

Найбільше мені запам'яталася сюжетна лінія з Панам і місія з Василіском. А ще окремо хочу згадати битву з Ода — особисто для мене це був найскладніший бос у грі.

Персонажі взагалі одна з найсильніших сторін Cyberpunk 2077. Тут дуже багато героїв, з якими дійсно хочеться взаємодіяти, дізнаватися їхні історії та проводити час. Через це до деяких персонажів по-справжньому прив'язуєшся.

Бойова система також дуже різноманітна. Гру можна проходити практично так, як тобі хочеться. Можна грати за нетранера, який тихо й непомітно знищує ворогів своїми скриптами, а можна перетворитися на справжню бойову машину, яка в стані берсерку з катаною розносить усе навколо. Варіантів розвитку персонажа багато, а в прокачці досить легко розібратися.

Активностей у грі теж вистачає: замовлення найманця, гонки, бої, завдання поліції, додаткові місії та багато іншого. При цьому гра не створює відчуття, що тебе змушують робити одне й те саме по колу. Особисто я взагалі рекомендую проходити Cyberpunk 2077, намагаючись зачистити карту максимально — так можна побачити величезну кількість цікавого контенту.

Щодо платини — вона досить легка. Особисто я витратив на гру близько **220 годин**, але знаю гравців, які вибивали платину приблизно за **120 годин**. Багато залежить від того, наскільки детально ти досліджуєш Найт-Сіті та скільки додаткового контенту проходиш.

Звичайно, без багів не обійшлося. У мене траплялися моменти, коли я провалювався під землю або автомобіль раптово починав поводитися дуже дивно. Але це настільки рідкісні випадки, що особисто я перестав на них звертати увагу. Якість і масштаб самого світу настільки високі, що подібні дрібниці просто губляться на його фоні.

**Cyberpunk 2077 — це неймовірна гра.** Якісний сюжет, живий світ, чудові персонажі, величезна кількість цікавих місій, різноманітний геймплей і атмосфера, у яку дуже легко зануритися.

Для мене це тепер одне з тих ігрових проходжень, які надовго залишаються в пам'яті.

**10/10. Однозначно рекомендую кожному.**

The most immersive, fun game I've played in years. 

Someone I saw a review from described it as 'doing missions and then riding home with your buddies in the car after', and I'd agree with that general synopsis of the gameplay loop. 

It's funny that the ride after probably became my favourite part. The voice acting, the lines, the fact you can look out the car window at Night City rolling by while you think of your reply to a question... I've never played a more immersive RPG from a look and feel perspective. 

Yes, I am utterly blessed to have a high end PC. So that helps. But after playing some on Steam Deck, I'd say that even on lesser hardware the immersion from this game comes mostly from the atmosphere CDPR built so carefully and the characters that are really hard to pick from as you make your end game choices. If you're a Bladerunner / Altered Carbon sci-fi junky, the questions asked by this game of the human psyche are nothing short of riveting as you explore a world shattered by corruption and the evisceration of what it means to be human. 

Another thing - I think people don't like RPGs that 'end'. They want you to beat the final boss and then roam forever free with the god-killing character you've created. But to me, Cyber Punk having an 'ending' (I don't think that's a spoiler - the game has been out long enough) meant that I valued my last few hours with V all the more. I was more emotionally invested knowing I was reaching a conclusion. I think the last time I sat down to finish a game with this much anticipation was Bioshock: Infinite. 

I probably could have spent more time in this world, but these days with a job and responsibilities, 50hrs felt about right. It has only left me eager to replay it all again in a few months with the Phantom Liberty DLC this time around. 

Thanks for reading!

Cyberpunk 2077 is the only game where you can go from having a casual conversation with a vending machine to fist‑fighting a cyber‑enhanced gorilla man in a back alley, all before breakfast. It’s a neon‑soaked fever dream, a tech‑dystopia vacation package, and a glitchy circus that somehow became one of the best RPGs out there.

Night City: The World’s Most Dangerous All‑Inclusive Resort
Night City is gorgeous. It’s vibrant. It’s alive. It’s also trying to kill you every five minutes.

You’ll be walking down the street admiring the neon skyline and—boom—someone’s car explodes. Not because of crime. Not because of gang violence. Just because Night City is built like it was coded by interns on Red Bull.

And yet… you love it.
It’s like visiting Las Vegas if Vegas had cybernetic arms, megacorporations, and existential dread baked into the architecture.

The Story: Existential Crisis, But Make It Stylish
You play as V, a mercenary who accidentally installs a brain‑haunting rockstar terrorist into their skull. Johnny Silverhand is equal parts mentor, menace, and malfunctioning Alexa. He pops up to give advice, insult you, or remind you that you’re dying. Very supportive.

The story is legitimately fantastic—emotional, intense, and full of characters who feel real enough that you’ll miss them when they’re gone.
Even the side quests slap harder than a malfunctioning cyber‑arm.

Combat: Guns, Blades, Hacking, and Occasionally Throwing Furniture
Cyberpunk lets you fight however you want:

Sneak around like a cyber‑ninja

Hack people’s brains until they catch fire

Run in with a shotgun and zero life insurance

Punch enemies so hard they forget physics

It’s chaotic, stylish, and extremely satisfying—especially once you realize you can hack someone’s cyber‑legs so they forget how to stand.

The Glitches: Comedy Gold (Mostly Fixed, But Never Forgotten)
Cyberpunk launched with bugs so legendary they deserve their own museum wing. NPCs T‑posing in the street, cars spawning from the sky, and police teleporting behind you like cyber‑ninjas who skipped the tutorial.

Most of that’s fixed now, but the memories live on.
Cyberpunk’s glitches were the closest thing gaming had to slapstick comedy.

The City Feels Alive… Even When It’s Actively Trying to Mug You
Night City is packed with detail—ads, crowds, conversations, weird robots, questionable food vendors, and people who look like they haven’t slept since 2041. It’s immersive in a way few games manage.

You don’t just play Cyberpunk.
You exist in it.
You suffer in it.
You thrive in it.
You get run over by a taxi in it.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a chaotic masterpiece.  
It’s stylish, emotional, hilarious, occasionally broken, and absolutely unforgettable. It’s the kind of game where you finish a mission, stare at the skyline, and think, “Wow… I should probably go do another mission instead of fixing my real‑life problems.”

If you want a game that’s equal parts brilliance and absurdity, Cyberpunk 2077 delivers.

If you want a game that never glitches… well, Night City has a message for you:
“We don’t do that here.”

[h1]CDPR Redeemed[/h1]

[h2]The Hype Train[/h2]
As a major Witcher 3 fan, I was well and truly on the hype train prior to Cyberpunk's release. I remember when the first teaser for the game came out and getting increasingly excited with each subsequent trailer. Then, after multiple delays, the game finally came out, and you all know the rest.

I felt not just let down by CDPR, but also misled. Honestly, if it wasn't for Steam's refund policy, I would have said that releasing the game in that state was downright anti-consumer.

Like many others, I closed the game and only came back every six months or so to check up on it. Eventually, I stopped coming back altogether. By this point, CDPR was dead to me. I didn't intend to buy another game from them again.

[h2]The Redemption[/h2]
When Phantom Liberty released, every headline in my feed was saying Cyberpunk was fixed, so reluctantly, I reinstalled the game and decided to give it one more try.

For once, the internet did not lie.

The game is fixed. It's exactly what it should have been in 2020. I'm still not happy about how everything went down, but I have to hand it to them. CDPR could have cut and run, but they didn't. They produced exactly what they promised, just three years later than they should have.

[h2]Gameplay Loop[/h2]
It's a big fuck-off RPG with futuristic guns, swords, and shit. It's all tied together with that excellent CDPR writing and outstanding visuals.

Not much more I can say than that. Everything about this game has already been said.

[h2]Stutter Struggle?[/h2]
Nope. In fact, it has some of the best CPU multicore scaling I've come across.

It will utilise your whole CPU, which helps prevent you from getting bogged down by the same sort of CPU, shader, and traversal stutter that plagues so many games today.

The one thing I would say is that, as much as you'll be tempted to crank the visuals and turn on all the fancy ray-tracing settings, the game still looks great at Medium. The extra smoothness just makes the gunplay feel that much better.

I do know that the game received a lot of criticism for a widespread of bugs and such on release. However, as someone who played the game for the first time just recently and just completed it, I can say that I found it amazing.

I'm a big fan of The Witcher series so I did have quite high expectations and honestly, I believe they were met well. I'm not gonna say that the game is completely free from bugs and issues even now because it's not but I can say that I thoroughly enjoyed playing it.

The main storyline and, I'll call them "main side quests", are very well-made, intriguing, enjoyable and not to forget, emotional. The reason I call them main side quests are because there are a few side quests that aren't necessarily needed to finish the game but are deeply relevant to the story and missing out on them effectively means you are missing out on big parts of the story. As far as stories go, I would say that Cyberpunk was something I wouldn't want to miss out on. As a completionist I could also add that the side content other than the "main side quests" quickly grow boring and is a bit too much, such as the NCPD Scanner Hustles and gigs which are MANY and aren't especially fun or interesting after you've done a few.

Gameplay-wise, I think the combat varies from effortless to slightly difficult. I played the game on normal difficulty and only ever thought the enemies posed a threat at early levels but as soon as you started getting better gear and improved your build, it almost became too simple. The combat is still fun and since you can play stealthy, straight-forward combat or with quickhacks as a netrunner you have a few choices on how you approach combat in this game. I also really enjoyed exploring the open world with a series of different vehicles at my disposal, except when my car broke down for unkown reasons... (you'll know it when it happens).

I do want to mention the customization opportunities, where you can create and customize your character however you like aswell as use fancy clothes and all but the reason why I'm bringing this up is actually because I find it useless. You will barely see your character at all throughout your gameplay (except for a few specific situations) which makes the customization kind of pointless in my opinion. The only thing that really matters is whether your character is male or female for some interactions with certain characters.

As a separate part here, I'll mention the DLC, PL (Phantom Liberty). I very much enjoyed it and it feels like the developers put more time into the side content here because most gigs in Dogtown actually has more of a "story" and isn't just the same thing over and over. The main story line in PL is also very fun and comes with a handful of difficult decisions. Trust me when I say that you'll have a hard time choosing the "right" decision in this DLC.

To summarize, I really enjoyed Cyberpunk 2077 even if it is somewhat expensive. I would still say it is worth the price especially since you can sink a lot of hours into it. 

I hope this review helped you decide if this is a game for you or if you'd rather keep looking. Good luck and have fun gaming!

关于赛博朋克2077的游玩体验及感受
 
      当问起出圈的3A游戏，毋庸置疑，必定是这部正宗的美式RPG作品，《赛博朋克2077》。它的爆火，一部分因为其打出的宣传：开放世界，赛博朋友，未来科技，这些标签无论出现在何时何款游戏上都是十分吸睛的存在，另一部分则是系列衍生番《赛博朋友边缘行者》的播出（现在来看，可能更多的应为后者）本人也是在25年暑假看完番后抱着对大卫故事的遗憾与对夜之城的憧憬，在steam秋促买下了它，但那时刚玩完艾尔登法环的几十h主线，并未对所谓的3A祛魅，想着3A的游戏时，流程一定很长，再者临近开学，于是便只好暂时放下对夜之城的向往，游戏也在库中吃灰。
      中途虽曾几次拾起，却望着周末那挤不到一天的时间，却又好望而却步。今年暑假末，当我抱着闲着也是闲着的心态，打开这款游戏，我便有了新的感受。流程并不长，若只推主线的一个结局大致20h便能落户（但我是一个喜欢打开一款游戏，便想解锁全结局、全成就的收集控，所以花了大概60h左右，我观看了全部结局。）
       接下来便是对这次体验的一点总结，希望对各位盒友有帮助。
关于剧情，我认为主线做的过于潦草，回顾整个主线就像是在喂你吃一份预制菜，即通过强尼的往事与杰克的死来让你强行流泪，在强尼刚出场后，我原本预想的是后续主线会以V的故事与强尼的回忆两条线并行，在V的故事中穿插补完强尼的背景故事，但直到结局，关于强尼的剧情也仅存在于主线部分与克里支线的一部分，这也直接导致了人物塑造的扁平化。我对强尼角色的印象正如剧情中所言“满嘴脏话鼓吹反抗的愤青”（虽然我懂制作组肯定想法并非这样）。但有一点值得肯定的是，核心剧情紧紧围绕着“无名小卒还是扬名天下‘’，而各个结局也确实能使人深刻意识到“夜之城没有活着的传奇”的主旨，而支线任务也并没有给人很深的印象，且不说帮居民找东西，解决赛博精神病这种千篇一律的重复性任务，连解锁结局的重要支线中，我能有兴趣玩下去的也只有赛车任务与帕南支线（别的不说，家族人真义气，有事是真上啊）以及罪与罚能排的上号了。
      关于游戏性设计：有些网上有部分玩家所称道的路人的台词设计使人很有沉浸感，让人感觉他们似真的置身于街头，但我个人认为，这种说法是根本站不住脚的，首先，台词的设计有两个目的，一是增加沉浸感，营造为剧情服务的环境，二是增加了游戏交互性，使故事更加有趣。但其实2077中的台词设计，只能算是平平无奇。初入游戏时，听一听路人的对话觉得饶有趣味，但随着游玩时间被拉长，重复的模式磨平了新鲜感。行走于大街上，你所能体会到的只有那充满屏幕的聒噪，或是抱怨，或是脏话，可能制作组的本意是想体现在夜之城这种资本主义高度发展的社会背景下底层人民饱受剥削的压迫，但此种设计似乎并没有达到这种效果，也并没有增强其给玩家带来的沉浸感。
       关于玩法：在搜攻略时，便见有人这么评价：这款游戏更类似于一个半成品。游玩下来后，也确实有点这样的感觉，但我觉得更贴切的来说，它并没有找到一个核心的玩法，虽然玩法众多，但总能找到一款平替。如驾驶系统，毫无疑问，在夜之城这款赛博朋克风未来都市，你马路上风起，车不真实令人心神惆怅，我在清支线时，甚至更喜欢不用快速移动，而是开车前往，然后也是我最想吐槽的便是这个游戏的车底盘和抹了肥皂一样难控制。拐弯开到人行道后撞到行人会被NCPD通缉，这时候要么进入任务对话要么开往其它区域甩开NCPD，不然只能重新回到上个存档点，（或者直接找出武士刀大杀四方直到引来警察暴力部队将你打死（GTA乱入）再因为其他大大小小的问题，这部作品中驾驶的体验是远不如地平线这种竞速大作的。又如游戏中获得物品的方式是满屋子找亮光拾取，玩久真的会让我感到在玩辐射，（而且第一人称视角转动不灵活，玩到后面有点头晕）。就再说地图设计方面，宣传时的开放交互令人惊喜而实际上手发现有的方面的确有些敷衍，如大部分门无法打开，等电梯时间过长，以及商店的重复性（666演都不演了，同种类型的商店卖的东西都大差不差）。
      最后要提到的便是审美设计角度，地图中每个区域似乎并没有各自的鲜明的特点（至少并没有让几十小时游玩下来的我有很深的印象）并且大街上随处可见的性偶店及情色产业广告与脏话，真的有些令人感到低俗，厌恶。其次就是人物的建模，不多说了，LGBT懂的都懂。
      从结果上说，有《边缘行者》的加持，这部作品在知名度上称得上成功，但就其作品本身与其游玩体验来说，并不让人满意，或者说与它的荣誉相比，差之甚多了。
My Game‑play Experience and Reflections on Cyberpunk 2077
 
When it comes to well‑known AAA games, Cyberpunk 2077, a genuine American‑style RPG, undoubtedly springs to mind. Part of its massive popularity stems from its promotional selling points: an open world, cyber‑punk aesthetics and futuristic technology — labels that draw huge attention in any video game. Another major factor, arguably the more important one, is the release of its spin‑off anime Cyberpunk: Edgerunners.
 
I bought the game on Steam’s Autumn Sale after watching the anime in the summer of 2025. Deeply moved by David’s story and fascinated by Night City, I was eager to step into this world. At that time, I had just finished dozens of hours of main‑story gameplay in Elden Ring, and I was still excited about AAA‑title experiences. Assuming the campaign would be extremely long and facing the approaching new semester, I set the game aside, and it sat untouched in my game library.
 
I tried to get into it several times later, yet I hesitated, since I barely had a full free day on weekends. Toward the end of this summer vacation, I decided to play it just to kill time, and it gave me brand‑new impressions.
The main story itself is fairly short. You can finish one single ending in roughly 20 hours. As a completionist who loves unlocking every ending and achievement whenever I start a new game, I spent around 60 hours to see all of its endings.
 
Below are my thoughts on this playthrough, hoping they will be helpful to other players.
 
In terms of storytelling, the main campaign feels rather underdeveloped. The whole narrative is like serving players pre‑cooked food: it tries to force emotional reactions through Johnny Silverhand’s past and Jackie’s death. Right after Johnny first appears, I expected the main plot to alternate between V’s personal journey and Johnny’s memories, with Johnny’s backstory gradually revealed in V’s timeline. Instead, Johnny’s character development is confined mostly to the main questline and a small portion of Kerry’s side missions, which results in a flat characterization. To me, Johnny comes across exactly as described in‑game: “a foul‑mouthed rebel ranting about resistance”, though I understand this was hardly the developers’ full intention.
 
To its credit, the core theme revolves around the dilemma: to remain a nobody or chase fame and glory. Every ending powerfully drives home the central message that “In Night City, no legend lives.”
 
Still, most side missions fail to leave a lasting impression. Putting aside repetitive filler tasks such as fetching items for civilians or hunting down cyberpsychos, even major side content tied to unlockable endings offers limited appeal. Only the racing missions, Panam’s questline (her clan is genuinely loyal and reliable when trouble strikes), and Crimes and Punishments stand out as memorable.
 
Moving on to game mechanics. Some players praise NPC dialogue for building immersion, making you feel as if real people fill city streets. Personally, I find this argument unconvincing. NPC dialogue serves two purposes: to build atmospheric immersion for the setting, and to boost interactivity to enrich storytelling. Dialogue design in Cyberpunk 2077 is merely mediocre. Early‑game NPC conversations feel interesting, yet repetition quickly wears away that novelty. Roaming city streets, players are constantly flooded with noisy complaints and vulgar lines. The writers presumably intended to depict the oppression of the underclass under highly‑developed capitalism in Night City, yet this design choice rarely achieves that goal and does little to strengthen immersion.
 
Regarding gameplay itself, some reviewers comment that the game feels like an unfinished product. Having played through it, I can see where this opinion comes from. More accurately, the game lacks a solid core gameplay loop despite its wide variety of mechanics, nearly all of which have better alternatives in other titles.
 
Take the driving system. Night City is built as a futuristic cyber‑punk metropolis, yet vehicle handling feels unnatural and awkward. I often skipped fast‑travel and drove across the city for side quests, but vehicle controls are slippery and frustrating. Hitting pedestrians on sidewalks triggers NCPD police pursuit. You must either enter a mission cutscene or drive far enough to shake off cops; otherwise you have to reload an earlier save. (Or you can grab a katana and fight until heavily‑armed police units gun you down — a very GTA‑style scenario.) Overall, driving mechanics cannot compare with dedicated racing franchises such as Forza Horizon.
 
Looting is another point of criticism: you hunt for glowing highlights scattered all over rooms to collect items, which quickly gives off Fallout‑vibes. Furthermore, the first‑person camera handles poorly and can cause motion‑sickness after extended play.
 
As for map design, the promised interactive open world falls short in multiple practical aspects. Many doors cannot be opened, elevator waiting times are unreasonably long, and shops suffer from obvious repetition: stores of the same type sell nearly identical merchandise.
 
From an aesthetic perspective, few city districts have truly distinct identities, at least not for someone who has poured dozens of hours into the game. The streets are saturated with advertisements for sex‑work establishments and non‑stop profanity, which often comes across as vulgar and distasteful. Character model design also leaves much to be desired, and the handling of LGBTQ‑related content speaks for itself.
 
Thanks to Edgerunners, Cyberpunk 2077 has achieved great fame and public recognition. Nevertheless, judged by its own gameplay experience, the game is far from satisfying, and it fails to live up to its widespread reputation.

Literalmente el futuro que nos espera.

Megacorporaciones con el control de casi todo, haciendo lo que les da la gana por el dinero y poder que tienen, mientras unos pocos mandan y el resto intenta sobrevivir como puede. Y lo peor es que viendo cómo funciona el mundo actualmente, cada vez parece menos ciencia ficción.

Me he jugado el juego entero, he desbloqueado todo y me he sacado todos los logros de Steam, incluyendo todo el contenido del DLC, y puedo decir que es una auténtica barbaridad de juego.

La historia me ha parecido increíble. Hay un montón de misiones principales, otras secundarias, encargos y pequeñas aventuras que te vas encontrando mientras simplemente vas por ahí haciendo el cabra.

Además, dependiendo del género que elijas para tu personaje, tienes diferentes escenas, conversaciones y pequeñas partes de la historia. No cambia completamente el juego, pero son detalles que hacen que cada partida tenga un poco más de personalidad.

Eso sí, hay tantísimo contenido que en algunos momentos puede llegar a ser un poco agobiante. Tienes misiones por todas partes, encargos, eventos, vehículos, tiendas, mejoras... Pero personalmente creo que es de esos juegos donde ir completando cosas poco a poco acaba siendo muy gratificante.

Las posibilidades de personalización también son enormes. Puedes cambiar prácticamente todo físicamente: ropa, pelo, modificaciones, armas, implantes... Y luego está toda la parte de habilidades y mejoras del personaje, donde puedes crear auténticas barbaridades.

Puedes ser un tirador super poderoso, darte de hostias con una katana o convertirte en el mejor hacker de Night City.

Yo personalmente lo de hackear no lo utilicé prácticamente nada. Soy más de darme de hostias y pegar tiros en la cabeza con el revólver.

Y hablando de armas, hay una cantidad absurda de ellas. Escopetas, pistolas, revólveres, metralletas, subfusiles, francotiradores... además de diferentes modificaciones, mejoras y rarezas.

Yo prácticamente hice todo el juego con un revólver y un francotirador que creo que era casi un antitanque porque pegaba una barbaridad. Luego iba con cuchillas o espadas en los brazos para el cuerpo a cuerpo y la verdad es que molaba muchísimo.

El mapa es gigantesco y está lleno de cosas. Hay un montón de puntos de teletransporte, tiendas de ropa, armas, comida, vehículos, enemigos, policías y todo tipo de interacciones.

Pero lo que más me ha gustado es que Night City se siente viva.

Puedes ir andando tranquilamente por la calle y de repente encontrarte con algo que te llama la atención. Enemigos, policías, una pelea, una misión o cualquier situación que no estabas buscando. Se nota que han intentado que no sea simplemente un mapa enorme lleno de iconos y ya está, sino que realmente estén pasando cosas a tu alrededor.

Tengo entendido que el juego salió bastante mal y que tuvieron que ir arreglando y mejorando muchísimas cosas mediante actualizaciones. Y no me quedo corto diciendo que hicieron un trabajo excelente.

Actualmente el juego está increíble.

Sí que es cierto que siguen habiendo bugs y alguna vez el juego incluso me ha crasheado porque le ha dado la gana, pero sinceramente no es algo que me haya molestado demasiado y se puede disfrutar perfectamente. Además, muchos de los bugs que me he encontrado han sido más graciosos que otra cosa.

Hay muchísimos vehículos, tanto coches como motos. Quizás la conducción no es lo que mejor se siente del juego, aunque por lo que tengo entendido al salir era bastante peor, así que también se nota que la han mejorado.

También hay diferentes finales y bastantes variaciones dependiendo de las decisiones que hayas tomado y de las misiones secundarias que hayas hecho. Si haces los saves en los momentos oportunos puedes sacar prácticamente todos sin tener que rejugarte el juego entero, que es básicamente lo que hice yo para conseguir todos los logros.

Y luego está el DLC que es una pasada.

Casi me ha gustado más que la historia principal. La historia, las cinemáticas, los personajes y todo lo que ocurre me parecieron una barbaridad. Me encantó y creo que es de esos DLC que realmente merecen la pena.

Después de haberlo jugado todo y haber conseguido el 100%, puedo decir que es un juegazo que creo que deberíais jugar o al menos darle una oportunidad.

Además, creo que es un juego que te hace pensar en el mundo que vivimos actualmente...

Te presenta un mundo donde las megacorporaciones tienen un poder enorme, donde el dinero está por encima de prácticamente todo y donde unos pocos pueden hacer lo que quieran porque tienen suficiente poder como para no tener consecuencias.

Y viendo cómo funciona el mundo real y hacia dónde parece que vamos, algunas partes dan un poco de miedo porque cada vez se parecen menos a ciencia ficción.

Al menos en el juego podemos pararles los pies... o unirnos a ellos.

Yo personalmente soy más rebelde, así que les doy plomo.

Nota: 9,5/10

それだけゲームの世界やキャラクターに愛着を持って、夢中になってプレイできたんだと思います。
グラフィック、音楽、キャラクター、世界観、ゲーム性など、どれを取っても本当に素晴らしく、文句なしでおすすめできるゲームです。

Résultat, tu percutes d'autres voitures, des obstacles sur la route et il en devient vraiment dur de finir un trajet sans que la voiture soit dans un piteux états à l'arrivée. C'est une partie qui, à mon sens, est très importante pour un jeu. Cela dit, ce n'est pas un gameplay de jeu de voiture, donc on peut très aisément passer outre, c'est frustrant mais sans plus. En revanche, et ce n'est peut-être que moi, mais je n'arrive pas à suivre l'histoire... Je veux dire, j'arrive à accomplir les missions, c'est relativement simple, mais tout les éléments arrivent tellement rapidement que je n'arrive pas à m'immerger dans l'univers du jeu. Une autre critique assez importante, pour les joueurs français, il vous faudra passez votre clavier en QWERTY, car le jeu n'est pas prévu les clavier AZERTY, ce que je trouve vraiment dommage. Aussi, un dernier point sur le clavier, sûrement que sur manette, c'est bien plus simple, en tout cas sur clavier, j'ai personnellement trouvé les commandes assez compliquées. Il se pourrait que ce ne soit que moi mais la prise en main des commandes n'a pas vraiment été aisé. Et pourtant je prends généralement rapidement la main quand il s'agit d'apprendre de nouvelles commandes.

Outre ces points, dont ma difficultés à suivre l'histoire du jeu, en partie à cause des multiples quêtes qui s'accumulent relativement vite, le jeu est excellent, les graphismes sont bons c'est un bonus (je ne suis pas tant que ça attaché au graphisme, mais c'est une plus), l'histoire extrêmement développée et vraiment entraînante, on sent que nos choix ont des conséquences (par moment), et le jeu ne manque pas d'action !!!

Pour moi je note le jeu à 3.5 sur 5.

Vamos lá !
93 horas.
93 horas vivendo uma vida que, de certa forma, parecia mais real do que eu esperava.

Comecei Cyberpunk 2077 querendo jogar um RPG. Terminei sentindo que tinha me despedido de pessoas que nunca existiram.

A história de V me pegou de um jeito que eu não esperava. Cada escolha, cada conversa, cada relacionamento e, principalmente, cada final foi me deixando com aquela sensação de que não existia uma escolha realmente feliz. Você pode lutar, pode tentar mudar seu destino, pode se sacrificar, pode escolher viver… mas Night City sempre cobra alguma coisa.

E os finais foram o que mais me destruiu.

Depois de conhecer todos aqueles personagens, acompanhar suas histórias e passar tantas horas ao lado deles, chegar ao fim e perceber que, independentemente do caminho escolhido, existe uma perda… é difícil explicar. Alguns finais me deram esperança. Outros me deixaram completamente vazio. E teve aquele sentimento de ficar olhando para a tela depois dos créditos pensando:

"É isso?"

A Phantom Liberty conseguiu deixar tudo ainda mais pesado. É uma expansão que não parece apenas conteúdo extra; parece mais uma camada daquela mesma pergunta que o jogo inteiro faz: até onde você iria para ter uma chance de viver?

E talvez seja isso que mais ficou comigo.

Não foi a ação.
Não foram as armas.
Não foi o dinheiro ou o nível.

Foram as pessoas.

Judy, Panam, Johnny, Kerry, River, Misty… todos aqueles momentos pequenos que, quando você percebe, já fazem parte da sua jornada. E então você termina o jogo e volta para a vida real.

Night City continua lá.

Mas você não.

Depois de 93 horas, eu senti um vazio enorme no coração. Aquele tipo de vazio que aparece quando você termina uma história que te marcou e percebe que não vai mais descobrir algo novo com aqueles personagens pela primeira vez.

Eu sabia que o jogo precisava acabar.

Só não estava preparado para sentir falta dele.

Cyberpunk 2077 não me deu um final feliz. Me deu uma história que eu vou lembrar.

E, sinceramente?

Talvez isso seja muito melhor.

10/10. Eu só queria poder esquecer tudo e jogar novamente pela primeira vez.

Cyberpunk 2077 started with a pretty bad launch. There were bugs, performance problems, missing features and a lot of things that clearly weren't ready. Even now, some bugs still exist, but after finally playing through the game and Phantom Liberty, I can honestly say that underneath all of that is one of the best RPG experiences I've had.

Night City is incredible. The atmosphere, music, characters, quests and the sheer amount of things you can discover made me want to keep exploring even when I wasn't following the main story. The combat and build variety are also fantastic, and I loved being able to shape my male V into the kind of character I wanted.

But the characters are what really made this game memorable for me.

Johnny Silverhand is easily one of those gaming characters I don't think I'll ever forget. Keanu Reeves absolutely put his own personality into the role, and Johnny never felt like just another NPC following me around. I didn't always agree with him and I definitely wouldn't call him a great guy, but that's exactly what made his character interesting. Saying goodbye to Johnny when I chose the Star ending was genuinely sad.

And speaking of the Star ending, I went with Panam and the Aldecaldos. Out of all the choices I had, that was the ending I wanted for my male V. It was emotional and bittersweet, but it felt right. After everything V goes through, having people who are actually willing to stand beside him and leave Night City together gave the ending a feeling of hope that I really appreciated.

Saul's death hit me harder than I expected too. Saul was a great character, and losing him genuinely hurt. I still miss the guy.

Phantom Liberty was another highlight. Dogtown felt completely different from the rest of Night City, and the expansion brought a much more focused and darker story. Solomon Reed was interesting, but personally, I never really felt that Reed was a great guy. I chose not to kill him, but I also didn't completely trust him.

Songbird was another difficult choice. I didn't want to side with her because I didn't feel that was the right thing to do, so I ultimately chose to disconnect her and free her from everything instead. Phantom Liberty constantly put me in situations where there wasn't an obvious good choice, and I loved that about it.

Judy and Panam also deserve a special mention because both of them became some of my favorite characters in the entire game. Judy's story had this emotional weight to it that I really wasn't expecting, especially seeing everything she goes through and how much she genuinely cares about the people around her. Her questline is one of those parts of Cyberpunk that sticks with you long after you're done with it.

And then there's Panam. Panam quickly became one of the characters I cared about the most. She's stubborn, reckless, aggressive and sometimes an absolute pain in the ass, but that's exactly what made her feel real. Her relationship with V develops naturally through the story, and the Aldecaldos genuinely felt like a family by the end. That's why choosing the Star ending with Panam felt so satisfying to me. After everything V had been through, leaving Night City with Panam and the Aldecaldos felt like the closest thing to a happy ending V could realistically get.

Judy and Panam aren't just romance options or side characters. They're two of the people who make V's journey feel personal, and I'm glad Cyberpunk gave them the amount of attention and development they deserved.

After finishing everything, what stands out to me isn't the bugs, the technical problems or even the insane amount of content. It's the characters. V, Johnny, Panam, Saul, Songbird, Reed and everyone else made Night City feel like a place I actually spent time in rather than just another open world.

Cyberpunk 2077 may have started badly, but what CD Projekt Red eventually turned it into is something special.

I came for Night City.

I stayed for the people.

And honestly, saying goodbye was harder than I expected.

Why I love this game:

Night City Vibe & Atmosphere: You can stumble across anything in this city. Every area is packed with interesting loot, weapons, and armor.

Great Controller Optimization: The game plays exceptionally well on a controller, making movement and combat feel smooth and natural.

Incredible Replayability: Every time I start a new playthrough, I spend hours testing different playstyles. Whether you go stealthy, run in guns blazing, or hack from the sidelines, every build completely changes how you complete quests.

Expanded Skill Trees: The updated skill tree gives you way more options to customize your character than before.

Respects Your Time: Earning money and getting gear is straightforward. You never have to spend hours grinding for money or upgrade materials, which makes starting new runs fast and fun.

This is a game where you either love it or you don't—and personally, I absolutely love it. After 500 total hours across both platforms, I can’t wait for the next Cyberpunk title!

Note: Possible spoilers ahead, but I tried to keep it pretty vague. Still, read at your own risk.



Having just finished getting all achievements during my first playthrough of this game (and doing all the side quests, gigs, NCPD scanners, etc. that I had available to me), all I can say is that this might genuinely be one of the best games that I have ever played. For the longest time, I swore I would never play this game after I had heard how bad the launch was for it, with the game being unplayable for many people, even with decent computers. With that being said, after Edgerunners released, I heard people picked up the game again and I was hearing nothing but praise, especially following the 2.0 update they put out later on. I personally found the Edgerunners anime to be really awesome, and even recently did a rewatch of it since I had started playing the game. I'd say it was the anime, which was followed by people's good words towards it that made me rethink my outlook on this game, and lead me to give it a shot just recently when I was able to get both the game and DLC for cheap during the Steam Summer Sale.

With that being said, I want to get into what I loved about this game. For starters, the Night City seen in-game genuinely feels alive. It's almost ironic, a game where there are multiple sentient and conscious AIs that are capable of thinking for themselves somehow also manages to almost make you think the same about the people you interact with in the game. I myself found several different interactions just randomly, either from looking at a certain location for a couple seconds or by bringing up certain dialogue options. Additionally, the characters are all very well-written and do a phenomenal job of fleshing out the world just by existing. Characters like Jackie, Johnny, Panam, Judy, River, Rogue, and so many others do such a great job breathing life into this world through their questlines and interactions. It's clear that the game really wants you to become attached to these characters, and they want you to feel happy when they're happy or sad when they're sad.  I found myself on numerous occasions becoming attached to characters, especially the ones that I interacted with the most. And of course, if I'm talking about characters I cannot forget to bring up the most important one, V. V is such a great character, even though they are the player character. I personally chose to play as Male Streetkid V, and I found myself loving the way he interacted with those around him, especially his typical banter between him and Johnny. The freedom that this game gives you with the world, allowing you to go basically wherever you want and do almost anything you could want to do in Night City, really helps V feel like a real person. Additionally, the choice to also have Keanu Reeves be the depiction for Johnny was really good, and he played the role absolutely amazingly to the point where it might be my favorite role I've seen him do (For reference, I have watched the Matrix trilogy plus the new one, John Wick 1-4, and Speed). To tie it all up, these well-written characters were used in such a phenomenal story about struggle, with a desire to become something important and leave a mark on the world. The fact that this game also has multiple endings helps solidify the freedom it gives you, allowing you to side with several different people to tackle your problems based on choices you have made throughout the story. There is even a "secret" ending that I was unable to get since I failed to pick the correct dialogue options during a certain part of the story, but the fact that such an ending even exists is what makes this game so special.

To wrap this up, I also want to briefly discuss the DLC since I had played that as well, and to be blunt, it might be the best DLC I have played for any game ever (so far). I have played many DLCs for many games that add on to the original story in a meaningful manner, while also not feeling mandatory, and I consider those to be good DLCs. With that being said, I can almost not imagine playing Cyberpunk 2077 without the Phantom Liberty DLC because it alone is simply that good. The DLC is essentially a whole other main plotline, which even supplies the game with an additional ending upon the completion of the DLC (depending on choices made). The DLC unlocks access to an otherwise restricted part of Night City known as Dogtown and revolves around a situation that occurs there. The DLC on its own is decently long (I'd wager 15-30 hours depending on your method of interacting with it), and even has around 4 different ways that things can turn out. I found myself being constantly posed moral questions for which I had no answer to in this DLC, questions that felt like I would lose with either choice I make. I am not often mentally challenged by a game in such a way, so I often found myself sitting and thinking about what to do at these times. While the main game has some of these kinds of choices as well, I felt that it was much more difficult to discern the "correct" choice to make in the quests and gigs in the DLC. Phantom Liberty also introduces some amazing characters as well, such as Songbird and Solomon Reed (who is portrayed by Idris Elba) and once again they just improve this DLC so much. The conflicts, breakdowns, resolutions, and so much more that are posed in the main questline really make the characters feel human and make Night City seem so much more real.

Now to be clear, I won't say the game is without problems. I found there to still be some bugs here and there, plus I had my fair share of crashes or technical difficulties, but I think I can look past those. Overall, I truly had a one-of-a-kind experience playing Cyberpunk 2077 with the Phantom Liberty DLC, experiencing something that I don't think can be equally supplied by any other game. Because of this, I want to extend my deepest gratitude to CD Projekt Red and Mike Pondsmith (the creator of the tabletop game that this game is based on) for creating such a beautiful world for the people to immerse themselves in. Anyhow chooms, I thank you for reading my extremely long love-letter to this game, and I'll see you all for Cyberpunk 2.

Я закончил Cyberpunk 2077 и до сих пор не понимаю, кто кого прошёл: я игру или она меня.
Найт-Сити сначала улыбается тебе неоном. Мол, заходи, детка, тут можно стать кем угодно. Легендой. Убийцей. Богом с хромом в костях. А потом этот город закрывает дверь, гасит свет и начинает медленно, сука, объяснять, что мечты здесь продаются по частям. Сначала ты отдаёшь время. Потом совесть. Потом друзей. Потом себя.

Моя V начинала на улице: грязь, татуировки, взгляд “пошли все нахер, я выживу”. А закончила где-то в стерильном белом свете, будто её разобрали, промыли, перепрошили и спросили: “Ну что, теперь ты счастлива?”
И самый страшный прикол в том, что ответа нет.
Эта игра не про пушки. Не про тачки. Не про сиськи, импланты и красивые вывески, хотя всё это тут есть и выглядит охрененно. Она про то, как человек цепляется за жизнь, когда жизнь уже держит его за горло. Про то, как хочется стать легендой, а в итоге молишься просто остаться собой.
“Wake the fuck up, samurai.” Сначала звучит круто. Потом звучит как диагноз.

Джонни, этот говнюк с голосом в голове, который бесит, ломает, режет правду прямо по живому. Они не ощущаются как набор квестов. Они остаются. Как шрамы. Как старые сообщения, которые не удаляешь, потому что рука не поднимается.

И вот ты сидишь после финала. В комнате тихо. Экран уже почти ничего не значит. А внутри будто кто-то прошёлся наждачкой. Потому что Cyberpunk 2077 делает мерзкую, прекрасную вещь: заставляет думать не о том, как ты играл, а как ты живёшь.
Не исчезай. Не растворяйся. Не дай этому миру сожрать тебя без остатка.
Это не идеальная игра. К чёрту идеальность. Идеальные вещи мёртвые. А Cyberpunk живой. Грязный, злой, красивый, больной. Такой, что после него другие игры кажутся пластиковыми.
Если вы ещё не играли, сыграйте. Не потому что “надо”. А потому что однажды Найт-Сити посмотрит на вас своими неоновыми глазами и спросит:
“Ну что, кем ты хочешь быть перед тем, как всё закончится?”
И, мать вашу, этот вопрос останется с вами надолго.

“Never fade away.”

它是游戏史上极具争议的作品：首发口碑崩盘，经多年更新+2.0大版本+DLC《往日之影》完成口碑逆袭。
优点
1. 美术与世界观顶级：夜之城氛围感独一档，霓虹高楼、贫富割裂的街区，完美诠释赛博朋克；光追画面视觉冲击力强，中文配音质量很高。

2. 剧情人物出彩：支线任务质量极高，小人物故事饱满；强尼·银手塑造经典，本体多结局，内核探讨资本、人性、自我存在；DLC《往日之影》是谍战神作，叙事、抉择、演出达到3A第一梯队水准。

3. 玩法自由度高（2.0版本后）：重做技能树，黑客、潜行、螳螂刀近战、枪械硬刚多种流派；义体改装系统丰富，build搭配空间大。

4. 沉浸感强：第一人称视角，城市氛围渲染到位，代入感强。
 
缺点
1. 开放世界短板：城市看着庞大，但大量建筑无法进入；NPC交互有限，缺少传统开放世界丰富休闲玩法，属于“剧情驱动型开放世界”。

2. 本体主线偏短仓促，部分宣传内容没有实装；车辆驾驶手感一直偏笨重。

3. 第一人称强制，部分玩家会眩晕；仍残留少量小BUG；对电脑硬件有一定要求。

4. DLC《往日之影》需要单独购买，完整体验建议本体+DLC一起玩 。
 
整体总结
不算传统意义上的完美开放世界，更像一款可以自由逛城市的RPG电影。优先推荐给喜欢故事剧情、赛博朋克题材的玩家；追求高自由度沙盒玩法的玩家会觉得内容单薄。
Несмотря на то, что иногда игра все равно выдает баги - она не перестает быть лучшей для меня. Единственная игра, которая у меня вызвала желание пройти на 100%. И вот наконец-то я это сделал

Cyberpunk 2077 — A Game That Proved Redemption Is Possible

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best examples of a game that completely changed the way I look at developers and their commitment to their players.

When Cyberpunk 2077 launched, it was a disaster. It was buggy, unstable, poorly optimized, and nowhere near the experience that many players expected. CD Projekt Red deserved the criticism they received. They made enormous promises, and at launch, they failed to deliver on them.

But what happened afterward is what makes Cyberpunk 2077 special.

CD Projekt Red didn't simply move on. They kept working.

Year after year, they continued improving the game, fixing bugs, rebuilding systems, listening to criticism, and eventually delivering the massive Phantom Liberty expansion and the 2.0 update. They didn't just patch a few crashes and call it a day—they fundamentally improved the game.

And that is where Cyberpunk 2077 stands apart from many other games.

It demonstrates something that is becoming increasingly rare in the AAA industry: developers who genuinely care about making their game better after launch.

The irony is that Cyberpunk 2077's redemption makes Bethesda's approach increasingly difficult to defend.

Bethesda has built an entire identity around its games being ambitious, expansive, and sometimes buggy. And perhaps the most infamous phrase associated with the company is Todd Howard's "It just works."

The problem is that sometimes it clearly doesn't.

Bethesda's games have historically shipped with bugs, technical problems, dated systems, and questionable design decisions, yet there has often been an attitude of this is simply how Bethesda games are. Players are expected to accept the quirks because the games are huge and ambitious.

Cyberpunk 2077 initially fell into the same trap—but CD Projekt Red eventually chose a different path.

They essentially said:

"We screwed up. Now we're going to fix it."

And they actually did.

Today, Cyberpunk 2077 feels like a completely different game from the one that launched in 2020. The combat, police system, skill trees, vehicle gameplay, cyberware, AI, UI, progression, and countless other systems have been improved or rebuilt. Phantom Liberty demonstrated that CD Projekt Red wasn't interested in simply maintaining the status quo—they wanted to prove what the game could have been.

That's what I respect most.

Cyberpunk 2077 isn't impressive because it launched perfectly. It is impressive because the developers refused to let their failure define the game.

There is something admirable about seeing developers acknowledge their mistakes and spend years rebuilding the trust they lost.

Meanwhile, Bethesda's reputation increasingly feels like it relies on the same old formula: release an ambitious game, accept the bugs as part of the experience, and tell players that eventually everything will work.

"It just works."

Well, CD Projekt Red showed us something better:

"It didn't work. So we fixed it."

That's the difference between defending a product and being passionate about improving it.

Cyberpunk 2077 ultimately became more than just a great RPG. It became a lesson in accountability, perseverance, and what a developer can accomplish when it genuinely commits to its promises.

I won't forget how terrible the launch was.

But I also won't forget what CD Projekt Red did afterward.

Cyberpunk 2077 didn't just redeem itself. It earned its second chance.

El Gran Secreto del Líquido Dorado: Cómo la Orina Construyó Imperios y Descubrió ElementosCuando compramos un videojuego, solemos pensar en códigos, algoritmos y píxeles. Pero si miramos la historia de la humanidad, las cosas que mueven al mundo suelen ser mucho más terrenales, extrañas y, en este caso, líquidas. Hoy vas a conocer la historia de la orina humana, el desecho biológico que se convirtió en una de las mercancías más valiosas del mundo antiguo y que, por puro accidente, dio origen a la química moderna.Parte 1: El Impuesto que Dividió a RomaPara entender el valor de este desecho, debemos viajar al Imperio Romano en el siglo I d.C. En aquella época, la orina no se desperdiciaba; se recolectaba en vasijas gigantes puestas en las esquinas de las calles. ¿Por qué? Porque la orina contiene altas concentraciones de amoníaco, un excelente agente limpiador y blanqueador natural. Los tintoreros y lavanderos (conocidos como fullones) pagaban grandes sumas de dinero por ella para usarla en la limpieza de las togas de lana y en el proceso de fijación de tintes en las telas.El emperador Nerón, siempre necesitado de dinero para sus excesos, vio una oportunidad de oro y creó la vectigal urinae (el impuesto a la orina). Su sucesor, el emperador Vespasiano, decidió mantener y aumentar este impuesto. Cuenta el historiador Suetonio que Tito, el hijo de Vespasiano, criticó duramente a su padre por cobrar un impuesto sobre algo tan asqueroso. En respuesta, Vespasiano tomó una moneda de oro ganada gracias a este impuesto, se la acercó a la nariz a su hijo y le preguntó si olía mal. Al responder Tito que no, el emperador pronunció una frase que quedó para la posteridad: "Pecunia non olet" (El dinero no huele). Hasta el día de hoy, en países como Italia y Francia, los urinarios públicos callejeros se conocen informalmente como vespasiani o vespasiennes.Parte 2: El Alquimista que Buscaba Oro en el BañoDamos un salto temporal de más de 1,500 años hacia adelante, hasta la ciudad de Hamburgo, Alemania, en el año 1669. Aquí encontramos a Hennig Brand, un comerciante y alquimista aficionado que, como muchos en su época, estaba obsesionado con encontrar la Piedra Filosofal: la sustancia mítica capaz de transmutar metales comunes en oro puro para alcanzar la riqueza infinita.Brand tenía una teoría muy peculiar. Observó que la orina humana tenía un color amarillento y dorado muy similar al del oro. Convencido de que el cuerpo humano concentraba la esencia del preciado metal en sus fluidos corporales, ideó un plan tan ambicioso como desagradable. Decidió recolectar miles de litros de orina. Las malas lenguas de la época decían que prefería la orina de los monjes cerveceros de la zona, asumiendo que su dieta le daba propiedades especiales al líquido.El proceso que llevó a cabo en su laboratorio casero fue una auténtica pesadilla olfativa:Dejó reposar la orina durante días en barriles hasta que se pudrió y crió gusanos.Hirvió el líquido putrefacto hasta reducirlo a un jarabe espeso y pastoso.Calentó esa pasta a temperaturas extremas en una retorta de barro sellada durante horas.Lo que Hennig Brand no sabía era que estaba realizando una destilación destructiva en ausencia de oxígeno. De repente, algo mágico sucedió en la penumbra de su laboratorio. Un vapor blanco y denso comenzó a llenar el recipiente y, al condensarse, se transformó en un sólido ceroso que brillaba intensamente en la oscuridad con una luz verde pálida e irreal. Además, al entrar en contacto con el aire, este material se encendía espontáneamente en una llama blanca y cegadora.Brand no había descubierto el oro, pero había logrado algo mucho más importante: aisló por primera vez en la historia un elemento químico puro utilizando el método científico primitivo. Lo llamó Fósforo, que en griego significa "portador de luz". Este fue el elemento número 15 de la tabla periódica.Parte 3: El Impacto Global de un Descubrimiento AsquerosoEl descubrimiento del fósforo cambió el rumbo de la humanidad. Brand intentó mantener el secreto para hacerse rico vendiéndolo a príncipes y reyes como un truco de magia, pero eventualmente el secreto se filtró. Sigles más tarde, el fósforo se convertiría en un componente vital para:La agricultura masiva: Los fertilizantes a base de fosfatos son los responsables de que la Tierra pueda producir suficiente alimento para sostener a miles de millones de personas hoy en día.La tecnología militar: Se utilizó para crear cerillas, bengalas de señales y, lamentablemente, armas incendiarias devastadoras.La biología molecular: Eventualmente descubrimos que el fósforo es un bloque fundamental de nuestro propio ADN y del ATP, la molécula que usan nuestras células para almacenar y transportar energía.Conclusión: Una Lección para los Videojuegos y la VidaLa próxima vez que estés jugando un RPG y recolectes ingredientes extraños del suelo, o cuando estés en un juego de supervivencia crafteando pólvora o pociones con materiales ridículos, recuerda a Hennig Brand. La historia humana demuestra que la curiosidad más absurda, combinada con los materiales más desagradables, puede dar paso a los avances más brillantes de la civilización. La ciencia y la riqueza literalmente nacieron del inodoro.

顺便个人评价一下剧情[spoiler] 虽然知道认识杰克的剧情没做完，但是与杰克认识这么长时间你就给一个幻灯片。确实是很拉，还有艾芙琳的剧情，给人的感觉就像莫名的介入了一群人乱七八糟的生活里，而且还与自己无关，OK那也无所谓，但是差不多这条线都是救你，你艾芙琳凭什么就直接下线啊是活是死总得给个选择吧？总之让人非常无语。
虽然都能自己选择剧情，给人的感觉还是差了点，我觉得如果剧情选择都像取货那个剧情去选择的话那给人的感觉就很不一样了。你所有的结局都是对应塔罗牌，还是太过于死板了，对于我来说，要是剧情选择还是得稍微开放一些才对的上开放世界。
再评价一下往日之影DLC的剧情，这个剧情也是非常的难评，我觉得所有人物里最无辜的就是亚历克斯，完全毫不知情的被卷进来，还有一个就是汉森，被百灵鸟骗完就被V震天除了，真要是够恶的话在宝石青发现了两个间谍为什么要放走？剩下的三个人就简直是全员恶人...反正剧情这方面做的真的是太牵强了。 [/spoiler]
总之，让人惋惜的是你能发现这个游戏的潜力，但却无力回天。明明能坐稳必玩榜却还只是半成品。或许在另一个平行时空，赛博朋克2077会是一个完美发售的完全体，也期待一下蠢驴的下一个2077是什么样子。

[h1]Cyberpunk 2077[/h1] Is one of those games you can honestly call one of the best things you can experience in life. Not just a “good game”, but something that really sticks with you.

The gameplay is top-tier: shooting, progression, implants — everything works and feels satisfying. The locations are highly detailed, every district has its own vibe. Night City actually feels alive — not just a backdrop, but a real world you want to spend time in.

The characters are alive, charismatic, and memorable.

Also, the music is amazing and fits the atmosphere perfectly. I often caught myself just driving around the city listening to the tracks.

The game is packed with easter eggs, and it’s genuinely fun to find them. There are references to a lot of other games and pop culture: The Witcher, Fallout, Portal, Death Stranding, Dark Souls, Doom, GTA San Andreas, Half-Life, Contra, System Shock, and many more. There are also references to movies, anime, and even real people like Hideo Kojima. And a nice bonus — easter eggs related to Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, which is great if you’ve watched the anime.

There are also many different endings, which is a big plus. They’re all interesting and have their own tone — there’s no single “right” choice.

The DLC is fine, but I’m not a big fan. It’s not bad, but the main game hit way harder for me.

Cyberpunk 2077 to jedna z tych gier, przy których po skończeniu człowiek chciałby wymazać sobie pamięć i przeżyć to wszystko jeszcze raz.

Fabuła jest naprawdę zajebista. Historia V, relacja z Johnnym, wybory, które faktycznie potrafią mieć znaczenie, i masa świetnie napisanych postaci sprawiają, że ciężko się oderwać. Do tego dochodzą zadania poboczne, które nie są tylko zapychaczami — wiele z nich ma własne historie, klimaty i momenty, które zostają w głowie.

No i oczywiście Panam. Wątek z Panam i Aldecaldos to dla mnie zdecydowanie najlepsza część gry. Pustynia, cała ekipa, wspólne akcje i ten zupełnie inny klimat niż w samym Night City. Każda misja z Panam była dla mnie czymś, na co naprawdę czekałem. Jeśli ktoś pyta mnie o najlepszy wątek w Cyberpunku, odpowiedź jest prosta — Panam bez dwóch zdań.

Samo Night City też robi ogromne wrażenie. Miasto jest wielkie, pełne neonów, reklam, ludzi i różnych dzielnic, a jeżdżenie po nim nocą z muzyką w tle ma swój własny klimat. Do tego mamy mnóstwo możliwości rozwoju V — bronie, cyberwszczepy, różne buildy i style gry. Można być praktycznie niewidzialnym netrunnerem, chodzić z kataną albo wejść z bronią i zrobić kompletny rozpierdol XD

Muzyka również robi robotę. Są momenty, w których samo siedzenie w samochodzie i jeżdżenie po Night City jest przyjemnością.

Ogólnie Cyberpunk 2077 ma świetną fabułę, genialne postacie, niesamowity klimat i ogromny świat, w którym można spędzić masę czasu. A jeśli dodatkowo trafisz na wątek Panam, to już w ogóle pozamiatane.

[h1]A City Worth Burning For[/h1]

Background: I played this game to completion on launch when it was a mess (or at least within its first 6 months of release) and returned to do another 100% run with Phantom Liberty now. What CDPR have managed to achieve by slowly revamping this game is nothing short of incredible. 

[h2]Graphics[/h2]

The graphical fidelity of this game is well documented so I won't spend too much time here, but the game is gorgeous - the part I find [b]really[/b] impressive graphically is how rich and dense the environment is. Unless you're actively looking for it by going to the edge of places you're not really supposed to be (or you experience a glitch here or there - and you will!) - you're unlikely to come across even so much as an ugly texture in this game. It also all feels very cohesive. Just make sure you calibrate your brightness settings - particularly gamma if you've got an HDR screen.

[h2]Gameplay[/h2]

Do you like Deus Ex Human Revolution/ Mankind Divided? If so, this game has that on crack. As well as a lot more for you to dig your teeth into. I thoroughly enjoyed my recent return to NC - I ran a stealth/ netrunner/ melee build and had so much fun running around the city, "ghost"ing missions and taking out hoards of "gangoons" without anyone knowing what had happened. The game also has many options for pure action if that's your thing.

Getting from place to place is a pleasure, particularly when you've unlocked some movement speed upgrades and - I cannot recommend this enough - get the double jump leg implants as soon as you can. They improve the walking traversal so so much. I also enjoyed using motorbikes almost exclusively during this run, they're a lot easier to navigate with. The driving in general I think has been improved, or at least that's what it felt like. I found myself frequently choosing to drive from place to place to take in the sights rather than making use of the fast travel.

This is a personal nitpick, but I loathe sandbox games that don't allow you to fast travel from the map. Having to walk to a fast travel point to fast travel to another point feels dumb, but many games have this design decision for one reason or another. I just find it really annoying not being able to click on a map point and teleport to it when so many other games do this.

[h2]Music[/h2]

Fantastic, particularly in the Phantom Liberty expansion. The game is full of bangers that absolutely fit the style and tone of the "era" and the vibe of Night City - I can't fault it. I do wish there was a little more variation in the radio stations - there are lots of them, but the genre doesn't seem to shift too much between them.

[h2]Story[/h2]

I'd probably rate the story as excellent, or at least very [i]very[/i] good. Like any game with mass amounts of content and an open environment, it's easy to introduce your own pacing issues depending on your approach to side content. The magical thing about this game's side content is that so much of it is rich and steeped in impressive variability. You can do one random Gig for a fixer and become immersed in the story of that single situation by reading emails, overhearing conversations while you're infiltrating an area, or just speaking to the characters.

The main plot I liked - I won't go into detail to avoid spoilers, but I found it thought provoking, touching at times, ridiculous (in a good way) at others, and even disturbing. That's kind of the point.

I mentioned variability in the side content, but that variation in the scenes/ lines/ reactions in main story missions is honestly extremely impressive. I'm a big fan of RPG's with choices and consequences, and it definitely does this aspect very well. I just finished up achievement hunting which required the different endings - and the variability not just in the endings themselves, but the missions leading up to those, was an insane surprise.

[h2]Stability[/h2]

In spite of the game being in an exponentially better state than it was when it initially released, I still encountered somewhat frequent crashes and bugs. Sometimes these were graphical - a texture shooting to the moon (massive triangles), the ocean straight up not loading - sometimes these were progression related (example: I couldn't interact with an object to progress a quest, but saving/ reloading on the spot fixed it). 

The worst offender is probably the random crashing though. I'd turn a corner on the way to a mission and it would just freeze up and crash out of the game completely, resulting in me troubleshooting quite a few times. I'd reload the game, restart my PC, change settings, and sometimes it'd be fine, others it wouldn't. It sucks, but the game is absolutely worth persevering with.

Excellent game. I feel like now CDPR have mastered this game, I really do hope they make a sequel in future. I'll wait to see how stable it is before buying though!

Cyberpunk 2077 foi um jogo que me surpreendeu muito. Eu já esperava encontrar um mundo aberto bonito, cheio de tecnologia, carros, armas e possibilidades, mas o que mais me prendeu acabou sendo a história e, principalmente, os personagens.

Uma das coisas que mais gostei foram as cutscenes e os diálogos. O jogo consegue fazer muitas conversas parecerem naturais, sem aquela sensação de estar apenas esperando o personagem terminar de falar para voltar a jogar. Muitas vezes eu realmente queria continuar ouvindo, entender melhor aquele personagem e descobrir o que aconteceria depois.

Também gostei muito da forma como Cyberpunk cria conexão com os personagens. Judy, Panam, Johnny, River, Kerry e vários outros têm personalidade própria, histórias e problemas que fazem eles parecerem parte daquele mundo de verdade. Algumas missões começam parecendo apenas mais um trabalho e acabam se transformando em histórias muito mais pessoais.

Night City também é um dos grandes pontos fortes do jogo. A cidade é enorme, bonita e cheia de detalhes. Mesmo quando eu não estava fazendo uma missão principal, gostava de simplesmente dirigir pela cidade, observar os lugares e sentir o clima daquele universo.

O jogo também consegue misturar muito bem momentos de ação com momentos mais calmos. Existem missões cheias de tiroteios e perseguições, mas algumas das partes que mais ficaram na minha cabeça foram justamente conversas, encontros e escolhas feitas durante a história.

Claro que Cyberpunk não é perfeito. Algumas atividades do mundo aberto acabam ficando repetitivas e ainda existem algumas situações estranhas na inteligência artificial e no comportamento dos NPCs. Mesmo assim, para mim, esses problemas ficaram pequenos perto da experiência geral.

No final, o que mais gostei em Cyberpunk 2077 não foi simplesmente o combate ou o tamanho do mapa, mas a sensação de estar vivendo uma história dentro daquele mundo. As cutscenes, os diálogos, os personagens e as escolhas fizeram eu realmente me importar com o que estava acontecendo.

Foi um daqueles jogos que, quando a história começa a chegar perto do fim, dá até vontade de jogar mais devagar para não terminar tão rápido.

If your here looking at this you probably know what it's about, it's hardly an obscure game. 
Cyberpunk 2077 is fantastic and well worth your time. If you're interested in a story set in a techno-future, dystopian, nightmare this is the one to buy.
Combat is good, a little on the easy side.
Story is good.
Setting is good.
I Love/Hate Johnny

The bad:
I never played the original release, which apparently was quite bad. I purchased the game about a year after release during a Steam sale. So I can't really speak from experience what it was like then. I can tell you with certainty that the game is good now.
The only issues I find are with exploration. It's a little pointless. You have this big map, you explore some area and most of the time get nothing much for it. Which is a shame, because someone worked very hard at every location to make it seem authentic.
There are some odd choices when the developers were deciding what the city should have in it. For example, there are multiple s*x shops but no sports stadium. Lot's of cars of all types, but no car dealerships/showrooms. Things missing that a normal city would have. This isn't a deal breaker, but it kind of breaks immersion a little. These buildings form part of the wider culture of the city. I like to explore and look around, I notice these things and it seems not quite right. Still the game is mostly set around violence, militant corporations and gangs. Those things are definitely present. 
I put it down to narrative choice, that the story is told through V's eyes and he/she isn't a completely 100% reliable narrator. This is simply how V sees Night City.

tldr; if you like exploration then you might be a little disappointed. 

All that said, the map is nice aesthetically. As I said before, they worked very hard to make each area seem authentic to the narrative.
