[h1] Cyberpunk 2077: [/h1]
[h3] Introduction: [/h3]
I definitely over-complicated my review. This game is just so incredibly good I wanted to pour my heart out about it in text. I originally wrote 47 paragraphs, over 3500 words and 20k+ characters, most of which explain stuff which is practically irrelevant to a game review. I even analysed Cyberpunk against other games I’ve played recently with similar plot points / themes. I’ve spent a while reducing this as much as possible. But it’s pretty clear I had a lot to say. My full review sadly cannot fit on steam so I've removed the VAST majority of it.
[h3] Gameplay overall: [/h3]
To start off with the actual gameplay, I’d say it was overwhelmingly entertaining. I very much gained an un-ignorable hyper-fixation regarding Cyberpunk. The combat is really fun, the multitude of options available for combat, whether being stealth, quickhack, armed or melee is really enjoyable overall. I really enjoy the variety of choices. It's very freeing regarding the fact that it’s an open-world story game. The boss-fights were pretty fun, though pretty easily beatable. I also very much appreciated the driving mechanics and how it approached transportation overall, cars were decently fun in this, it was a bit difficult to get used to at first, but after a while, you’d work out the control sensitivity.
[h3] Bugs, optimisation: [/h3]
As everyone knows, this game was HEAVILY glitched when it released. One of my main worries about this was from the reputation of its bugs, though I will say, upon playing 220 hours of the game, I’ve encountered little to none. The ones I did encounter, however, weren’t even that impactful on the gameplay, they were just more so, like little hindrances more than an actual bother. The most common bug I got was when an NPC would rarely get stuck inside a wall or floor during combat, which was easily beatable as they’d still be hittable using melees. I also had a few situations where the car would get stuck in the road, teleport a few meters away or just not drive correctly (while an NPC is driving, with me in the passenger seat), but all of those were easily fixed via leaving the area and coming back. It’s clear the devs have put a lot of effort into optimising the game, fixing the majority of glitches since the launch version. The bugs I encountered I’d just consider usual for a game this big. Overall, very well fixed and practically almost entirely smooth gameplay with no hindrances. 
[h3] Replayability, Duration + Completion: [/h3]
The game is decently good regarding duration and re-playability. As mentioned before, it does offer multiple lifestyles as well as a large multitude of play-styles available to choose from, meaning it’s very replayable as well as durable. The main story offers around 20-ish hours of gameplay, meanwhile side missions can go to 60+ hours, it’s VERY durable. It unfortunately does not feature a New game+, but that’s due to it being so attuned to the slow progression process during gameplay.
I eventually 100%ed the game. The vast majority of which was through casual gameplay and completing the story naturally. Regarding achievements I hadn’t unlocked upon finishing – the tasks needed to complete them were pretty easy. Most were basic repetitive tasks which could be easily grinded upon and the few others were done completed pretty easily after going through guides on steam. It’s a pretty easy game to gain all achievements on, it mostly just depends on how willing you are to sacrifice a lot of your time playing through it.
[h3] Immersion: [/h3]
Cyberpunk’s interface is not only visually pleasing, but also a very well crafted immersive experience within the game. The UI, including the menu, title screen, pause menu and overall layout are all well thought of and well executed, being just an extra step towards the immersiveness in Cyberpunk. The loading screens are also very satisfactory, having news broadcasts about the recent events the player has played through, being a fun Easter egg to listen to in between play sessions. As for the atmosphere and actual videography of the game, it’s visually beautiful. The graphics are mind-blowing and the game's map has so much detail put towards it. It's genuinely stunning. Cyberpunk franchises are usually pretty similar, but this one is quite distinctive visually. From the mega-building flat blocks to the lonely motels in the badlands, all the buildings are so well-designed. The game is also optimised really well, my gameplay felt very smooth, and it was overall just really nice to have a wonder around the world and just feel the attention to detail presented to you. The soundtrack, as in songs during missions, credits, radio and even just background, is really well done, clearly with a lot of dedication towards it. I’ve even saved a few of the songs from the game into my own playlists. I really admire the ‘Samurai’ metal music, it genuinely goes so hard.
[h3] Spoilers 4 story [/h3]
[spoiler] I would definitely say that Cyberpunk's story is a masterpiece. The narrative is so well thought of and I was genuinely hooked on the plot. It's such an incredibly cool concept. All the missions in the game contribute so well, as well as the side missions giving more insight, end-game options and just genuine entertainment overall. The whole point of the Relic being a criticism of the rich corporate world is a really cool concept. The fact the game advertises it as if to promote it to consumers is also a very nice touch. The whole plot is so cool. I really like how V was made to be someone just trying to get their way in the world, get rich and famous in the criminal space but then went onto fighting for their life with Silverhand in their head. It's so incredibly cool. I really truly do like the critique cyberpunk gives us. It's so anti-capitalistic, corporate and overall greed. The greed of the corporations, the rich and civilians dominates the world, everyone out for themselves on a continuous self-destructive path. The same path V was on themselves, until the Relic. That sudden turn in the direction of motivation was executed really well. The emotional toll it also took on V, but also the player, was really well handled. I truly do admire the whole becoming someone else trope. It was executed very well in this game, the slow transition showing changes in V, as well as the gradually increasing interactions with Johnny overtime. It was very well done. [/spoiler]
[h2] Conclusion:[/h2]
I unfortunately had to cut a lot of my review to make it fit on steam but I’d definitely say that Cyberpunk 2077 is one of my favourite games of all time, it just can’t not be on that podium. It’s literally perfect in almost all aspects it presents; there are barely any negatives. I’m so impressed with it and I had so much fun playing through it. I loved every second. You literally couldn’t get me away from my PC during this phase of my life. I COMPLETELY recommend this game for ANYONE even slightly interested in the genre. Its immersiveness, story, graphics, gameplay system and overall tone is just breath-taking. It’s not just a game but a gateway into this extensive creative universe Pondsmith created. Open world story games are definitely my favourite genre. I honestly wasn’t expecting this to be as good as it was, but I’m glad that it’s this way, literally the best game in its genre. I stand on that. I am so incredibly excited for the upcoming sequel. This universe is so cool, and I’m very glad it’s being explored. Overall, I’d absolutely rate this a 9.8/10 – I COMPLETELY recommend it.

Cyberpunk 2077... you probably don't need my review to tell you that this is one of the best games ever made.

For years, I was extremely apprehensive about playing it. In fact, when it first released in 2020, I actively disliked the hype surrounding it and pretty much wrote the game off completely.

Six years later, I saw it on sale on Steam and thought, *you know what? Fine. Let me finally try it.*

And oh boy.

I had absolutely no idea what I had been missing.

Night City draws you in unlike almost any game world I've experienced before. At first, it's the obvious things that impress you: the visuals, the scale of the city, the combat, the action, the sheer atmosphere of walking beneath enormous buildings glowing with neon.

But those aren't really what make Cyberpunk 2077 special.

It's the stories. The characters. And the strange, gradual way you begin shaping V's fate until, somewhere along the way, an invisible line gets crossed.

At some point, playing V stopped feeling like controlling a character in a video game and started feeling like I was actually there.

I found myself genuinely thinking about my choices. About who I trusted. About what I wanted V to become. About what my next move would be on the road toward becoming a Night City legend.

And the characters around you slowly stop feeling like NPCs, too. Everyone seems to carry some history with them, some regret, ambition, trauma, dream, or mistake that shaped the person they became. Even many of the people doing terrible things don't feel like cartoon villains. Night City is simply a ruthless place filled with people desperately trying to survive, succeed, matter, or leave something behind before the city swallows them.

Some of the stories I encountered genuinely broke my heart. Several times.

And that's probably the highest compliment I can give this game: it lingers.

When I finally reached my first ending and the credits began to roll, with the people I'd met along the way appearing one by one to say their final words, I think I just sat there staring at the screen for twenty minutes afterward, trying to process what I had just experienced.

Not many games do that to me.

So, should you play Cyberpunk 2077?

Absolutely.

Just be warned: you may enter Night City thinking you're going to play a cool cyberpunk RPG for a few dozen hours...

...and leave feeling strangely nostalgic for a place that never existed.

Night City somehow becomes part of your memories as though you actually lived there.

And I think that's something very few games ever manage to achieve.

在艾芙琳·帕克的墓碑上，刻着这么一句话：[b]“她对抗体制，她英勇就义。”[/b]这句话，通关后再看，感慨万千。

最早是因为丹尼斯·维伦纽瓦的《银翼杀手2049》超绝摄影迷上了赛博朋克美学，而这款游戏则让我置身画中，看清了赛博朋克世界下的黑暗体制。

我做很多任务都会犹豫。很多任务都在逼问同一个问题：你究竟是拿钱办事的雇佣兵，还是心里还揣着一点火苗的活人？艾芙琳·帕克想靠绀碧大厦一票挣脱风尘，最后受尽折磨，自己了断；宋昭美一路奔赴月球，背着一身黑墙的伤痕，仓皇逃离，而李德守着理想与原则，最终成了被随手丢弃的弃子，众叛亲离。心照不宣任务中，汉兹在电话里轻描淡写地说：[b]“如果伤害到你的正义感，那么我很抱歉。”[/b]那一刻隔着屏幕，也能感受到另一个世界的无奈与冰冷。

就算把一座吃人的工厂连根拔起，又怎样呢？九头蛇砍掉一个头，还会长出三个。大环境如此，过分地感性、固执地坚守道德底线，反倒背弃了雇佣兵的本分。可若要两全——既要活下去，拿报酬，又不踏破底线——宋昭美那句“有没有什么办法，谁都不连累？”便是整个游戏最残忍的冷笑话。没有。李德和强尼便是现例。在乎太多的人，最后两头落空，[b]辜负的比拯救的多，害死的比保护的少[/b]。

这就是体制：无论你选哪条路，尽头都是一堵墙。活人被资本与利益一口口吞没，个体的反抗在集体面前微不足道，而更多的个体则变成集体的齿轮，日复一日地麻木转动，日复一日地互相啃噬，弱肉强食，将社会达尔文主义奉为教条。如竹村五郎所言：“这个城市的根已经烂了。”

那么，到底该怎么选？其实没有完美结局，没有皆大欢喜的选项。[b]你搞错了城市，也搞错了人。[/b]但正因如此，才更要忠于自己的心。选定一个方向，然后义无反顾地走下去——自反而缩，虽千万人，吾往矣。这是孔子所谈的对义的坚守：反省自己，如果觉得道理确实在我这边（理直气壮），那么纵然面对千万人，我也勇往直前。我不愿为几把压箱底吃灰的不朽武器，出卖心里那点烫手的真实。现实里活得窝囊，游戏里总要活得潇洒。百灵鸟一路为己，愧疚一直缠绕着她，可当她奄奄一息，却选择告诉V真相。[b]那一刻的坦然，比飞上月球更为珍贵。[/b]那是真正的自由——无关结局，只关乎交付。

无须在岔路口过度盘桓，试图寻找两全之道；不如顺从内心，无论踏出哪一步，都能收获宋昭美结尾那一份安然。那份安然，胜于任何不朽武器，胜于迈尔斯结尾递来的那枚奖章。精神的丰盈，永远无法用物质来丈量。

“回头看看，这一路经历了许多啊。”每一个任务都有不同的感受。直到大厦崩塌让我觉得恐怖，猎杀让我觉得诡异，美梦继续则细思极恐，布兰登支线让我意识到AI伦理问题，罪与罚则充满宗教意味，当你凝视深渊时带来的是战争创伤的思考……CDPR无疑是善于刻画人物、叙写剧情的，往日之影DLC的质量更是超越了本体，可惜当年本可为一代神作，终究成了遗憾的半成品。

如果你五年前年玩这款游戏，我会说你有钱；如果你现在玩这款游戏，我会说你有品。[b]但无论如何，我们永不消逝[/b] 。

[b]无论如何，都不要忘记奋斗。无论如何，为自己而活，不要为了他人而改变自己。[/b]这是强尼临别的嘱托。带着这些话，我也更有底气，推开现实的门，走进那一场场真实的风雨。

仅此纪念第一款通关的3A大作，也敬我最喜欢的游戏。

## Minha avaliação de Cyberpunk 2077

Eu nunca escrevi uma avaliação para nenhum jogo na Steam. Nunca senti que precisava. Mas depois de 141 horas em Cyberpunk 2077, acho que esse jogo merece.

Halo 3 sempre foi, para mim, **o jogo da minha vida**. É um jogo que marcou minha infância e tem uma importância que provavelmente nenhum outro vai conseguir substituir. Só que, depois que conheci Cyberpunk 2077, pela primeira vez encontrei um jogo capaz de ficar lado a lado com ele.

E isso diz muita coisa.

Cyberpunk 2077 é simplesmente **um dos melhores jogos que já joguei na vida.**

Não dá para falar de Cyberpunk sem lembrar de como foi seu lançamento. Em 2020, o jogo chegou em um estado extremamente problemático, cheio de bugs, problemas de desempenho e diversos outros problemas que fizeram muita gente perder completamente a confiança no projeto.

Mas o que a CD PROJEKT RED fez depois disso merece reconhecimento.

Com anos de atualizações, correções, melhorias e muito trabalho, Cyberpunk 2077 foi transformado em um jogo completamente diferente daquele que chegou ao mercado. Hoje, na minha opinião, é um jogo excepcional.

E o mais impressionante é que, depois de todas essas horas, o que mais me prende não é apenas a história ou a gameplay.

**É Night City.**

Para mim, Cyberpunk 2077 tem uma das melhores — talvez **a melhor** — ambientações que já experimentei em um jogo.

Night City não parece simplesmente um mapa gigante colocado ali para você atravessar. Ela parece uma cidade que existia antes de você chegar e que vai continuar existindo depois que você sair.

Você anda pelas ruas e vê pessoas conversando, comendo, trabalhando, bebendo, discutindo, se divertindo. Você encontra pequenos grupos reunidos em determinados lugares, pessoas perto de uma fogueira, um sofá velho, comida espalhada, lixo perto do mar, bares, becos, lojas, prédios e centenas de pequenos detalhes que, individualmente, parecem insignificantes, mas juntos fazem a cidade parecer viva.

E muitas dessas pequenas interações ainda têm diálogos dublados em português.

É uma coisa que talvez seja difícil explicar para quem nunca jogou, mas em determinados momentos você simplesmente esquece que está fazendo uma missão.

Você está só... **vivendo em Night City.**

Já aconteceu comigo de terminar uma sessão de jogo e simplesmente pegar meu carro ou minha moto e sair andando pela cidade sem objetivo nenhum. Às vezes de madrugada, sem missão, sem precisar fazer absolutamente nada. Só dirigindo, andando a pé, olhando os prédios, as luzes, as pessoas e os detalhes da cidade.

E isso, para mim, é uma das maiores qualidades do jogo.

Se eu comparar com outros mundos abertos, como GTA V, por exemplo, existe uma diferença que eu sinto muito forte. GTA V tem uma cidade enorme e cheia de NPCs, mas em Cyberpunk eu sinto muito mais que estou **dentro daquele lugar**.

Night City tem identidade.

Você começa a reconhecer lugares. Começa a lembrar de determinadas ruas. Começa a perceber pequenos detalhes. E quando você conhece a história daquele mundo, a cidade fica ainda mais interessante.

E falando da história...

**10/10.**

A narrativa de Cyberpunk 2077 é absurda. Os personagens, as escolhas, os relacionamentos, as missões secundárias e a própria construção do mundo fazem com que você realmente se importe com o que está acontecendo.

E uma das coisas que eu mais gosto é que o jogo não trata o futuro simplesmente como algo bonito e tecnológico.

A tecnologia evoluiu.

A humanidade também.

Mas não necessariamente para melhor.

Você vê desigualdade, pobreza, violência, exploração, corporações controlando praticamente tudo, pessoas tentando sobreviver enquanto outras vivem em um nível completamente diferente. Você vê como comida, tecnologia, dinheiro, implantes e até o próprio corpo humano podem virar mercadoria.

É exatamente esse tipo de futuro distópico que eu gosto na temática cyberpunk.

Não é apenas neon, carros voadores e prédios gigantes.

É a ideia de uma humanidade que conseguiu avançar tecnologicamente enquanto continuou carregando praticamente todos os problemas que já tinha — e talvez tenha criado alguns novos.

Para quem gosta de cyberpunk de verdade, seja por jogos, quadrinhos, mangás, filmes ou simplesmente pela temática, acho que esse jogo entrega uma experiência absurda.

E ainda existem aquelas pequenas referências e conexões que tornam o universo ainda melhor.

Para quem assistiu **Cyberpunk: Edgerunners**, por exemplo, encontrar personagens, locais e referências ao David, à Lucy e à antiga equipe é simplesmente muito legal. Você pode até usar a jaqueta do David e carregar um pedaço daquela história com você enquanto explora Night City.

E preciso falar de uma coisa que, para mim, representa perfeitamente essa ligação entre o anime e o jogo: **“I Really Want to Stay at Your House”.**

Essa música já é praticamente uma marca registrada de David e Lucy. Depois de assistir ao anime, você nunca mais escuta essa música da mesma maneira.

E então você está jogando Cyberpunk 2077, dirigindo pela cidade, completamente imerso em Night City, e de repente ela começa a tocar no rádio.

**É um negócio diferente.**

Por alguns minutos, parece que o jogo, o anime e a cidade se juntam em uma coisa só.

Você reconhece a música, lembra do David e da Lucy, lembra de tudo que aconteceu, olha para Night City pela janela do carro e sente aquele pequeno “tchan” que é difícil explicar.

É como se aquela música pertencesse à cidade.

E é justamente esse tipo de detalhe que faz Cyberpunk 2077 ser tão especial para mim. Não é apenas a música estar na trilha sonora. É ela carregar uma história, memórias e sentimentos de outro lugar e, quando toca no rádio enquanto você está dentro de Night City, transformar completamente aquele momento.

É uma das melhores sensações que esse jogo consegue proporcionar.

E a gameplay?

**Muito divertida.**

Você pode jogar de várias maneiras, experimentar diferentes builds, armas, implantes, habilidades e estilos de combate. E conforme você vai ficando mais forte, o próprio jeito de se movimentar pela cidade muda. Quando você começa a usar habilidades de movimento, dash e todas aquelas possibilidades do sistema de habilidades, atravessar Night City fica ainda mais divertido.

Os gráficos nem precisam de muita explicação.

Até hoje eu paro para olhar determinadas paisagens e penso: **“caralho, que jogo bonito.”**

E talvez a maior prova de que esse jogo realmente me marcou seja o fato de que eu já terminei praticamente tudo o que queria fazer nele e, mesmo assim, ainda pretendo fazer outra run.

Porque Cyberpunk 2077 é um daqueles jogos que eu não sinto vontade de simplesmente “zerar e desinstalar”.

Eu sinto vontade de voltar.

Voltar para Night City.

Voltar para aquele mundo.

Criar outro personagem, tomar outras decisões, experimentar outra build e viver aquela história novamente.

E deixo uma recomendação para quem estiver lendo isso:

**Quando terminar Cyberpunk 2077, não tenha pressa para sair de Night City.**

Depois de zerar, ou até mesmo durante a campanha, pegue seu carro, sua moto ou simplesmente vá andando.

Escolha uma noite.

Desligue um pouco a pressa de fazer missão.

Ande pelas ruas.

Olhe os prédios.

Observe as pessoas.

Passe pelo litoral.

Entre nos becos.

Dirija sem destino.

Explore a cidade.

Porque é nesses momentos que você percebe uma das maiores qualidades desse jogo: **Night City não é apenas o lugar onde a história acontece. Night City é parte da própria história.**

No fim das contas, não sei se essa avaliação vai convencer alguém a jogar Cyberpunk 2077.

Mas, se convencer pelo menos uma pessoa a dar uma chance ao jogo, já valeu.

Eu entrei em Night City esperando jogar um RPG futurista.

Saí de lá sentindo que tinha vivido em uma cidade.

**Cyberpunk 2077 é excepcional.**

**10/10.**

E, para mim, é um dos poucos jogos que conseguiu chegar ao lado de Halo 3 no lugar mais especial da minha lista.

Fast forward a couple of years and we're in 2025, I'm spiralling from the most painful combination of not only being dumped by a woman I thought was the love of my life but also from my online friend group because I just happened to piss off the wrong person. Главными плюсами являются сюжет и вариативность во всём. В игре очень много концовок, а большинство квестов можно пройти различными способами. Порадовала прокачка, которая отчётливо показывает каждое изменение на практике. Дополнительно в игре очень достойный визуальный стиль, который никак не портит слегка мыльная графика. Музыка в Cyberpunk 2077 — одна из лучших во всей индустрии, она нередко связана напрямую с историей Ви. Помимо сюжета, имеется очень интересный и глубокий лор, который выходит за рамки игры, побуждая окунуться в мир настольной игры, ставшей основой для этого хита.

Минусов мало. Наверное, можно выделить лишь небольшой процент мусорного контента. В качестве примера приведу постоянные преступления, с которыми приходится разбираться нам, а не полиции. Ну и некоторые заказы фиксеров скучнее остальных. Да, в игре остались проблемы с оптимизацией, но теперь они минимальны. Кстати, меня бесит Джуди Альварес, а Панам Палмер является одной из лучших героинь в играх за всё время.

Я рекомендую эту игру. Несмотря на ранние проблемы, она смогла стать классикой на одном уровне с Red Dead Redemption 2 и Grand Theft Auto V. Cyberpunk 2077 очень сильно выделяется на фоне большого количества шлака, выходившего в последние годы, и имеет крайне привлекательную цену. По скидке брать обязательно!

[h1] 绝对推荐（90/100） [/h1]

《赛博朋克2077》+《往日之影》是一个让我非常矛盾的游戏。以2026年的眼光来看，我认为现在的2077已经是一款相当优秀，甚至在某些方面可以称得上顶尖的开放世界RPG；但如果让我评价整个《赛博朋克2077》项目，我依然无法原谅它2020年的首发灾难。因为我始终认为，一款游戏应该在正式发售的时候就已经准备好，而不是先通过预购和首发玩家获得收入，再靠数年的更新、修补和扩展内容把它慢慢变成一个完整的作品。

我当然承认CDPR后来做的一切值得肯定，《往日之影》以及2.0更新确实把2077从一个问题非常严重的游戏拉回了优秀作品的行列。但我反而希望这件事情不要成为行业值得效仿的“成功案例”。如果以后越来越多厂商认为“首发先捞一波，游戏的问题以后慢慢修”，那对于玩家来说绝对不是什么好事。《无人深空》同样经历过类似的翻身过程，而且后续表现确实值得鼓励，但这种事情本来就不应该成为一种商业模式。后来做得好，可以得到肯定，但不能因此抹掉首发时对玩家造成的问题。

这也是为什么即使现在的2077已经完全配得上“优秀游戏”的评价，我依然不会因为它后来的成功，就把当年的问题一笔勾销。

不过抛开这些历史问题，单纯讨论现在的《赛博朋克2077》，它最令人惊艳的地方依然是夜之城。CDPR对于视觉、氛围和世界观的塑造能力非常强，这座城市有着非常鲜明的赛博朋克气质。霓虹灯、广告、贫富差距、帮派、企业、义体、街头文化共同构成了一个非常完整的视觉世界。它并不是一个单纯“地图很大”的开放世界，而是一个拥有非常强烈个性的城市。你甚至可以把夜之城本身看成2077最重要的角色之一。

但这里也存在一个非常明显的矛盾：夜之城看起来比实际玩起来更加丰富。你可以看到无数建筑、广告、NPC和街道，但真正能够深度互动的东西并没有视觉上那么多。它更像是一座非常优秀的“被观看的城市”，而不是一座真正意义上可以被玩家自由改变和深度参与的城市。2077给人的第一印象很容易让人产生一种“这里什么都能做”的错觉，但实际游玩之后会发现，它本质上还是一款剧情驱动型开放世界RPG。

而我认为2077最成功的部分之一，就是剧情和角色。

V、银手、竹村、帕南、朱迪等角色都有相当鲜明的特点，很多支线甚至比主线还要精彩。CDPR对于中小规模剧情的掌控力确实非常强，这一点从《巫师3》的大量支线，到《石之心》《血与酒》，再到《往日之影》，其实一直都非常明显。尤其是《往日之影》，它几乎把2077的问题重新梳理了一遍，也再次证明了CDPR非常擅长制作这种中等体量、人物集中、氛围明确的剧情作品。

但当CDPR试图把这种能力扩张到一个巨大的开放世界时，问题也开始暴露出来。
我最明显的感受就是：2077的主线剧情和开放世界之间存在一种非常严重的割裂。

V的生命倒计时本应该让整个故事拥有一种非常强烈的紧迫感，主线实际上也是在相当短的时间里发生的。可与此同时，玩家完全可以放下这件事情，先去夜之城各处探索，接几十个支线任务，完成大量重复性的委托，甚至花很长时间去做一些和主线完全没有关系的事情。
于是就出现了一个非常奇怪的情况：
V刚刚知道自己命不久矣，剧情告诉你现在必须争分夺秒；下一秒玩家却可以骑着摩托车跑到城市另一边，花几个小时帮陌生人处理各种“通马桶”任务。
这种开放世界结构不可避免地削弱了主线剧情的紧张感。
当然，2077的支线里有很多非常优秀的作品，问题恰恰在于这些支线太优秀了。它们本身值得体验，却又不断把玩家从主线的情绪里拽出来。开放世界的自由和线性叙事的紧迫感，本身就是一对很难完全调和的矛盾。

还有一个我认为非常可惜的地方，就是杰克。
V和杰克从认识、熟悉，到最后成为可以托付生命的挚友，这一段在最终游戏中处理得实在太仓促了。甚至很容易让人怀疑这里存在明显的删减。
我一直觉得，如果2077能够把游戏开头的这段时间真正展开，让玩家作为一个刚来到夜之城的新人，和杰克一起生活、接任务、认识城市、认识一些人，再逐渐建立起真正的友情，那么后面进入主线的紧张剧情时，玩家的代入感一定会强得多。
现在的处理方式更像是：
“你们两个是最好的朋友。”
然后游戏告诉你：
“相信我，你们确实是最好的朋友。”
而不是让玩家自己经历这段关系的形成。
这其实是非常可惜的，因为杰克本来完全可以成为玩家认识夜之城的第一扇窗户。

2077还有一个很有意思的叙事特点，就是它选择了第一人称视角。第一人称并不是游戏史上独一无二的设计，但放在这样一款高度强调角色扮演和沉浸感的作品里，它确实产生了非常特殊的效果。玩家几乎一直是以V的视角观察夜之城、和角色交流、经历剧情，这让一些场景拥有非常直接的临场感。尤其是当游戏把第一人称、表演、配音和环境结合起来时，它会让你感觉自己不是在“观看V的故事”，而是在经历V的故事。

但另一方面，这也会带来角色扮演上的矛盾：V虽然是玩家的角色，但V本身又拥有固定的过去、性格、价值观和人生经历。玩家可以决定V说什么、做什么，却无法完全决定V究竟是谁。这也是开放世界RPG长期存在的问题之一。

至于战斗、义体和技能系统，2.0之后确实已经有了非常明显的提升。现在的2077在Build构筑、义体、武器和技能组合方面已经相当成熟，不同流派也确实能够形成不同的游玩方式。它仍然不是一款完美的沉浸式模拟游戏，但至少已经足够成为一套有趣而且能够长期研究的RPG系统。

真正让我对2077又爱又恨的，还是CDPR本身。
波兰蠢驴对于中小体量剧情的掌控能力，我认为在这个行业里确实非常强。《巫师3》大量优秀支线、《石之心》《血与酒》，再到《往日之影》，都证明了他们非常擅长把一个有限规模的故事做得完整、有氛围、有角色、有情绪。
但当这个故事被放进一个巨大的开放世界以后，CDPR对于整体结构的控制能力就明显下降了。
《巫师3》因为本身的剧情结构、任务设计以及玩家对开放世界的预期等因素，这个问题没有那么明显，反而让很多优秀支线成为了游戏最受欢迎的部分。而到了2077，这个缺点几乎被彻底暴露出来：他们非常会讲一个故事，但不一定非常会管理一个巨大的游戏世界。
《往日之影》反而证明了这一点。
它没有试图无限扩大夜之城，而是把故事集中在一个相对明确的区域，用更有限的规模讲一个完整的故事。结果反而非常出色。
所以我认为《往日之影》真正“救回”2077的地方，并不仅仅是修复了Bug或者增加了内容，而是让人再次看到了CDPR最擅长的东西：集中资源，把一个中等规模的故事做到极致。
而这也让我重新审视了2077。
它不是一款失败的游戏，更不是一款应该因为首发灾难就永远钉死在耻辱柱上的游戏。到了现在，它已经是一款非常优秀的作品；但与此同时，我也不认为后来的优秀就能够证明当初的营销没有问题。

因为当年的宣传本身就是一次非常彻底的失败。
CDPR当年把2077包装成了一款几乎能够重新定义开放世界RPG的作品，给玩家制造了极高的期待，而最终发售的产品不仅没有兑现其中大量承诺，甚至连基本的稳定性都没有达到应有水平。
所以对我来说，2077最终留下的最大遗憾不是“它没有成为神作”。
而是：它明明有成为神作的潜力，却在最应该兑现承诺的时候出了问题。
我依然非常喜欢夜之城，也依然喜欢这里的人物、音乐、视觉风格和剧情，更承认2.0和《往日之影》把这款游戏拉到了一个相当高的水平。但我不会因为CDPR后来把它修好了，就忘记首发玩家经历过什么。

这是一款我现在依然愿意推荐的优秀RPG，也是一个非常典型的“亡羊补牢成功案例”。但我希望以后真正被记住的不是“CDPR竟然把2077救回来了”，而是游戏公司应该从一开始就把自己的作品做到足够完整。

Una pena que aquest joc sortís en un estat horrible i que l'empresa preferís mentir per llançar-lo quan encara no estava acabat, perquè és un molt bon joc.

Primer de tot, vull destacar el món obert i l'ambientació. La ciutat de Night City és un indret on fa gust conduir i caminar; sempre hi ha alguna cosa a explorar o observar, i mai et canses de veure-la.

Després, el que és per a mi el millor del joc és el combat. Se t'ofereixen diverses opcions perquè puguis personalitzar-lo a la teva manera: pots ser un pistoler que dispara bales amb una precisió mil·limètrica amb el temps alentit; una bèstia amb braços que poden destrossar els teus enemics en diversos trossos, o pots no tocar cap arma i transformar-te en un hacker que fregeix la tecnologia que els enemics tenen implantada al cos i, fins i tot, fer que es matin ells mateixos. També vull fer una menció especial a les armes; crec que no havia jugat mai a un joc en què les armes se sentissin tan diferents entre elles i presentessin una varietat que vagi més enllà de simples millores de percentatge.

La història és bona i compleix, però trobo que l'expansió Phantom Liberty fa una molt millor feina en aquest apartat. El lore és mol interessant i fa que t'interessis per petits detalls i mencions que en el meu cas han fet que vulgui saber més d'aquest món.

Recomano molt aquest joc en la edició completa amb Phantom Liberty, i no puc esperar a veure Projecte Orion.

Ambientazione: 9/10
Night City è semplicemente stratosferica. Ogni distretto, dalle luci al neon di Westbrook alle baraccopoli di Pacifica, trasuda atmosfera cyberpunk. L'attenzione al dettaglio nell'architettura, nelle insegne, nei veicoli e negli interni è senza precedenti: ti senti davvero immerso in una metropoli distopica del 2077.

Storia: 8/10
La trama principale è solida, con un'ottima caratterizzazione dei personaggi e scelte morali ambigue che danno peso alle tue decisioni. Le missioni secondarie presentano storie autonome spesso più memorabili della campagna principale.

AI dei nemici: 5/10
Qui il gioco mostra il fianco. L'intelligenza artificiale dei nemici è limitata: si nascondono e sparano, ma bastano azioni semplici (come chiudere una porta o salire le scale) per confonderli completamente. Lo stealth diventa quasi inutile perché evadere la detection è troppo facile, e anche a difficoltà elevate i nemici restano poco reattivi e prevedibili.

Voto complessivo: 7.5/10
Un'esperienza visivamente mozzafiato con una narrativa coinvolgente, ma frenata da un'AI datata che riduce la sfida e l'immersione nei combattimenti.

CP77'yi çıktığı sene aldım ama gündemdeki sonsuz şikayet nedeniyle oynamamaya, güncelleme beklemeye karar verdim. 2026'da ilk kez baştan sonra oynadım ve 103 saatlik maceramın sonunda hâlâ şikayet edeceğim tonla şey var.

Öncelikle hakkını verelim, CP77; birçok stüdyonun altından kalkamayacağı, hatta hayal dahi edemeyeceği kadar kompleks bir yapıya sahip. Başlangıçtaki path seçiminin sembolik olmaması ve tüm oyuna etki etmesi, verilen kararların gerçekten hikayeyi şekillendirmesi ve hikayeyi onlarca farklı noktaya evirmesi tam delilik. Oynarken "bu kadar işi nasıl yapmışlar" diye düşünmekten yoruldum, yapanların nasıl manyaklar olduğunu hayal bile edemiyorum.

Çıkışının üstünden altı yıl geçmiş olmasına rağmen CP77'de ekrana yumruk atma isteği uyandıran şeyler:

-Arabaların BOK gibi spawnlanması. Witcher 3'te de Roche dağın başında falan spawnlanıyodu ama ıslıkla kolayca yerini değiştirebiliyorduk. CP77'de bunun üstüne hiçbir şey koymamışlar. Arabalar havada spawnlanıyor ve yere düşüyor, bu da zaman zaman hasarlı gelmelerine sebep oluyor. Hatta kaç kere olduğunu sayamadığım kadar arabanın yarısı yerin altında kaldı ve zaten yakında olduğu için tekrar çağıramadım. Biraz yürüyüp uzaklaştıktan sonra bu sefer düzgün gelmesini ümit ederek tekrar çağırmak zorunda kaldım.

-NPC'ler APTAL. 22 senelik GTA SA'da bile NPC'ler arabalardan kaçmayı başarıyordu. Bunlar üstüne sürmememe rağmen arabanın önüne atlıyorlar. Defalarca bu gerizekalılar yüzünden peşime polis takıldı ve göreve girmek için dakikalarca bekledim.

-Arabaların otopilotu çalışmıyor. A noktasından B noktasına otomatik gitmenin tek yolu teleport kullanmak. Arabayla şehrin içinde otopilotun biraz keyfini çıkarayım, etrafa bakayım deme şansınız yok çünkü on saniye içinde kaza yapıyor. Önce ucuz arabaların otopilotları kötü, daha iyi arabalar aldıkça düzelecek mi diye düşündüm, çok detay unsurlar düşünen bir oyun şirketi bunu da düşünmüş olabilirdi. Ama yok, en iyi arabalar bile otopilotta gitmeyi beceremiyor.

-Nesneler etkileşime geçtiğinizde kayboluyor. Örneğin bir kadeh viski içeceksiniz, masada duruyor, "iç" seçeneğine tıklayınca kadeh yok oluyor ve V elini ağzına götürüyor sadece. Her seferinde olmuyor ama bu bir RPG, ben bu gibi saçma hatalarla deneyimimin bölünmesini istemiyorum.

-Işınlanma, araçtan çıkma, sinematiklerden çıkma gibi noktalarda ışık patlamaları oluyor. Üç saniye içinde yavaşça eski haline dönen ama en başta anlık olarak ekranı bembeyaz yapan bir hata var. Başka hiçbir oyunda görmedim ve ne olduğunu asla anlamadım. Gece oynarken sinematiklerden çıkarken gözümü kısıyordum önlem olarak.

-Diyaloga geçtiğimiz yan karakterler sinir krizi geçirtecek derecede yavaş hareket ediyor. Asansöre biniyoruz mesela, tuşa o karakter mi basacak, geçmiş olsun on dakika bekle babam bekle. Yürüyecek de asansöre gelecek de diyalogunu bitirecek de tuşa basacak da. Tüm saydıklarım arasında en çok bu delirtti beni. Neden tüm karakterler benden daha yavaş yürüyor anlamak mümkün değil, koşmak değil yürüme hızında bile benden en az %50 daha yavaşlar.

Tüm bu şikayetlerime rağmen birkaç yıl sonra CP77'yi inanılmaz atmosferi ve en ince ayrıntısına kadar düşünülmüş dünyası sayesinde corporate olarak tekrar oynayacağımı biliyorum.

Peace out.

Where to begin....

God I had such high hopes for this game..

Ok act one. Holy shit what a world CD project ReD created!
You're dropped into this MASSIVE world that feels so alive your mind just experience a complete overload.
On top of that their path-tracing technology and general visual effects are so beyond anything else thats out there you can almost smell the humidity as it rains on the asphalt! 

Technologically speaking this game is surreal!

Then you start exploring, doing all the side gigs
Getting to know all the NPC and what they stand for.
It doesn't take long to realize that the science fiction aspect of this game is really mostly related to the medical implant aspect. It does not take long to realize this game pulls no punches when it comes to some of the ugliest things that humanity, or lake-thereof, has to offer.
Drugs, abuse, coercion, exploitation, murder, torture, suicide, mental illness, black-mail, violation of ones autonomy... this game doesn't just "NOT" shy away from it, it flat out embraces these topics.

By the time you reach the end of act 1 you are neck deep in corporate conspiracies, loss of any autonomy, and you find yourself in a landfill, thrown out discarded like trash, WITH trash, fully betrayed by the very city you've come to love.

Act one Cyberpunk 2077 is a 10/10... top shelve, nothing better out there, no doubt...



then comes act 2...

And all of a sudden the writers mediocrity becomes very clear VERY quickly..
The entire act 1 was designed to give you the chance to shape what kind of V you wanted to be.
-Stealthy
-honorable
-mass murdering fuckhead
Take your pick!! it was all in your own hands.

Act 2 in contrast to that forcefully funnels your character, and all the side characters, down a very narrow trajectory that quit frankly is so poorly written it would make a cheap porno feel like an Oscar nominee by comparison!!! And that's NOT hyperbole!!!

Lets start with the obvious.
Almost nothing you do produces the degree of narrative consequence Act 1 taught me to expect.

Your choices have very little meaningful impact on the characters if at all.
What was a starting point for massive potential quickly comes crashing down hard as no one in this game learns anything, adapts, grows, or evolves. The only growth is your talent tree, and your arsenal of weapons/appartments/cars
But as far as actual emotional depth is concerned. NADA!


Relationships...
If you are the type of person who wants to solicit work from Joytoys and one night stands... then sure there is some material in this game that can tickle your fancy. But once again try to have anything of meaning and you will be horrible disappointed ESPECIALLY if you're playing a Male-lead protagonist and you're choosing to have straight orientation... because your ONLY option is Panam...
An alcoholic, impulsive, short-tempered, foulmouthed, nomad with the body of a porn-star, who only gets excited when she's committing mass-murder followed by socializing with you over the bottom of a fucking bottle. 
To add insult to injury, the only time you can be intimate with this bloodthirsty phsycho, is when you're driving a billion dollar tank called a baselisk, blowing everything to shit, and getting electrically high with her like its a rave-lazer show...
It's fucking pathetic. 


And then... there is Evelyn... 
Evelyn is very real. If you've ever worked in trauma departments anywhere you will recognize Evelyn immediately! And not just in act 1, but harrowingly enough you will recognize her in act 2!
Evelyn is a over-confident attractive woman who's intellect is above average. She's not a genius, but she's ok. She is also wildly attractive and has learned to survive by utilizing her sexuality.
Like any woman in such an industry she desperately wants to get out, and tries to use her connections, her charm, and her smarts to organize a heist that would be her ticket to a better life.
This goes horrible wrong, which is unfortunately also a very real-world parallel.
After having been brutally violated for an entire week by several parties, you manage to safe her in the worst state possible... but she is alive...
Anyone who has worked with people like Evelyne recoil during this scene, and her respons to being saved is what you would expect from someone in her shoes. 
So now comes the very interesting question.: How do we help Evelyn recover, how do we get her back on her feet?

Cyberpunk 2077 repeatedly mistakes provocation for profundity.

It raises fascinating questions about trauma, consciousness, autonomy, sexuality, religion and identity—

Rating: ★★★★★ (5/5) — Absolute Masterpiece — blew my brains out

Despite the heavy initial refunds back at launch, this 2020 game turned massive profits, easily recouped its huge $300M+ budget, and reached 40 million copies sold worldwide—making it one of the best-selling RPGs of all time.

When a game's world-building, writing, and gameplay loop line up this well, I can completely see why. The game is so fantastic—it hits that sweet spot where you just want to wander around soaking in the atmosphere, explore Night City's side stories or side quests, or just to test out new iconic weapon builds on some NCPD targets. It makes every penny spent feel completely justified and keeps you coming back for "one more gig."

Iconic weapon? How does a shotgun that fires 8 target-seeking mini-explosive missiles—complete with screen-filling explosions—sound to you? Or how about a chatty AI pistol, or a machine gun spewing abusive remarks?

Even if there are still a few very minor bugs, they don't take away from the experience at all.

Nothing—no game—matches the rush of storming Dogtown's Barghest stronghold as V and causing absolute chaos: downing 50+ Barghest militias, pummeling those red-and-black heavy enforcers with the crazy AF Sasquatch’s Hammer alongside MaxTac AV drops, and rampaging through MaxTac until the latter calls in a second anti-cyberpsycho squad and you, V—that freak-of-nature cyberpsycho alpha maniac—are forced to scramble for cover.

With so many branching endings, almost every path leaves you with a lingering sense of loss, quiet existential dread, or bittersweet acceptance. It's a staple of the cyberpunk genre: there's no such thing as a 100% happy ending — you just can't win it all.

And one of the best parts? It still works on an old ROG GL753VE with a GTX 1050 Ti mobile from 2017, hitting 70 FPS on medium settings!

Prós:
Conteúdo e Exploração: Mundo aberto verdadeiramente livre, com poucas ou nenhuma limitação de navegação e uma quantidade enorme de coisas para fazer.

Gameplay e Comandos: Jogabilidade divertida que prende a atenção do início ao fim, acompanhada de controles precisos e de ótima resposta.

História e Evolução: Narrativa excepcional combinada com uma progressão de personagem muito bem construída e gratificante.

Contras:
Organização das Informações: Uma certa bagunça de informações no começo do jogo, o que pode poluir e dificultar a experiência inicial.

Sistema de Talentos Rígido: A limitação de reiniciar a árvore de habilidades apenas uma única vez durante toda a campanha é um ponto bem negativo. No meio para o final do jogo (especialmente na dificuldade Muito Difícil), a escolha das técnicas certas se torna indispensável para sobreviver e causar dano real.

Pequenos Bugs: Existem alguns deslizes técnicos pontuais, mas nada que comprometa a experiência geral.

Veredito: Recomendo a compra apenas se estiver em promoção. No preço cheio, pense duas vezes; mas com desconto é uma excelente pedida!

Cyberpunk 2077 to gra, która potrzebowała czasu, ale dzisiaj – jako kompletnie poprawiony, dopracowany produkt – jest absolutnym mistrzostwem świata. Warto było czekać od samego dnia premiery, aby ograć tę grę w jej ostatecznej, idealnej formie.Fabuła i konstrukcja historii to rzadko spotykany w grach poziom geniuszu. Dialogi są napisane po prostu po mistrzowsku – każda rozmowa z Johnnym, Panam czy Takemurą ma niesamowitą głębię, naturalność i ładunek emocjonalny. Teksty rzucane przez bohaterów zapadają w pamięć na długo po wyłączeniu komputera.To pierwsza gra w moim życiu, która aż do samego końca, do ukończenia dosłownie wszystkich możliwych zakończeń, nie znudziła mnie nawet na sekundę. Ani przez chwilę nie czułem, że "cisnę ją na siłę" czy gram dla samych osiągnięć. Każdą minutę w Night City spędziłem z gigantyczną ciekawością i czystą przyjemnością, chcąc zobaczyć, jak potoczą się losy V w innych scenariuszach.Dodatkowo gameplay w niczym nie ustępuje fabule. Mój build oparty na maksymalnej mobilności, dynamicznym wpadaniu w środek walki (rush) i szatkowaniu wrogów kataną dodał tej grze niesamowitego tempa. Walka mieczem daje tak potężną satysfakcję i niezapomniane wrażenia, że człowiek czuje się jak prawdziwy, cyberpunkowy cyberpunk.Jeśli jeszcze się wahasz – nie czekaj. W obecnym stanie Cyberpunk 2077 to jedna z najlepszych gier w historii elektronicznej rozrywki. 10/10.

Firstly, this game is a visual treat on a high end PC. Even without ray tracing on its a beautiful game when you're roaming the city at night. I was planning on upgrading to a RTX 3080 specifically for this game, but for now with all the supply issues I have to play it with a GTX 1080 Ti (still a beast of a card). The way the neon lights flood the streets, the visual details found both on characters and the world are stellar. CDPR still is top notch when it comes to visuals. I've also seen the videos with ray tracing on max, and while that seems to tank framerate, its next-gen looking.

Voice acting, music and sounds are all stellar. The sheer size of the soundtrack is great, even if the type of music isn't my favorite genre. But it all fits the world and futuristic setting. The voice actors are great, they really emote very well and get you into the scene.

The world design is excellent. Night City itself is easily the best part of the game. I adore the setting, and the world designers need to be given major props. Never have we seen an open world this vertically layered, dense and filled with visually unique touches.

The story - This is highly subjective of course, some have said its great while others find it lacking. For me the story is above average. I love the themes it deals with, from corporations becoming the true ruling power in the future to transhumanism. But even in the story it can feel like CDPR cut corners with a chainsaw. The part where V and Jacky are supposed to bond and where you become established is entirely a brief montage video, suddenly jumping months ahead instead of actually letting you start from the bottom. There's bizzare oversights everywhere, I killed a character in one mission (The Dollhouse) only to have him return in another mission later on down the road, no explanation why he's still alive. Depending on which quest you take first, plot will suddenly fall out of order and there is no check condition that checks whether you've already played another quest and adjusts the dialogue to it. Then in the cutscenes there is the constant weird bugs like this that really make it difficult to take the entire thing seriously.

Night City is the game's real triumph. Every district has its own visual identity, sound design, and social texture — you can tell Kabuki from Westbrook from Pacifica without checking a map. The vertical density (skyscrapers, alleys, rooftops) makes exploration feel purposeful rather than padded.

Combat and build variety hold up well after multiple playthroughs. Whether you lean stealth-hacker, melee brawler, or gunslinger, the perk trees and cyberware let you specialize meaningfully rather than just picking cosmetically different flavors of the same build.

The writing and voice acting for companions and side characters is consistently strong — the side gigs often have more texture and moral ambiguity than the main missions of most open-world games.

Post-2.0 (with Phantom Liberty), the core systems — police AI, vehicle combat, cyberware/perk trees — got a real overhaul rather than surface patches, which fixed a lot of what made the game feel unfinished at launch.

The rough edges:

Mod installation is genuinely more finicky than it should be — REDmod, load order conflicts, and version-breaking updates make it less plug-and-play than something like a Bethesda title.
Bugs persist, even years post-launch — NPCs occasionally going invisible, T-posing, or clipping through geometry. Rare enough not to break immersion for long, but frequent enough that you'll hit one eventually.

Overall: a game that turned a rough launch into one of the better redemption arcs in gaming, held back only by some jank that CDPR never fully stamped out.

I put off playing this game until 6 years after its release, I saw several of my friends play parts of the game over those 6 years, I never looked up any spoilers online, so while I have partially seen some of the characters; I didn't have a frame of reference for how any of them interacted within the narrative. I can admit, when it comes to stories in video games, for me personally, stories get sidelined in favor of gameplay; despite this, Cyberpunk 2077 has done a decent job creating an engaging story with interesting characters on top of familiar but unique, FPS-RPG gameplay.
The game is very story heavy, thus if you cannot sit through "long" portions of dialogue in between stretches of gameplay, you may not enjoy this game, though having now put 20+ hours into the game, I would recommend it for the gameplay alone. the core mechanics of the game are pretty solid. The character-building systems won't be anything unfamiliar to anyone who has played an RPG with first person camera perspective in the last 15 years, you level up, you get attribute points and perk points. Thankfully, there's decent build variety available to make your character's playstyle however you'd like to play, Whether that be Stealth with guns/melee, sharp/blunt melee brute, technomancer hacker, cyber-ninja, etc.
The narrative of the game's dialogue choices branch enough that they allow several playthroughs with decently varied outcomes at key plot points. while managing to create numerous characters who generally don't overstay their welcome and are enjoyable, which is fairly rare in the modern day for triple-A game writers. It isn't the most amazing writing in video game history, but the story takes itself seriously and isn't seeped in Whedon-esque self-deprecating characters buried under multiple layers of irony.
My only complaint is, despite having been out for 6 years now, There are still some bugs I've encountered, usually minor ones like a visual glitch or NPC abruptly t-posing for a brief moment, but the worst one I've seen thus far was a softlock which forced me to reload to a previous save. At release I can see why people were disappointed with Cyberpunk but in its current state I am having an enjoyable time and give the game a recomendation.

After 6 years from the game release i manage to save enough money to buy myself  a pc and saw how cheap the game was + DLC so i immediately bought it plus hearing how good the game actually is after all these years. 

  My first impression of the game is how funny the character customize was cause you can make a female character with a male genital (weird ahh impression). After that was the best 160+ hours of my life when playing a video game.

*Review:
- Positive:
 + Graphics: I haven't played that much of AAA game with open world but this game was beautiful in my opinion, even without ray tracing the game still look incredible. Maybe if you compare this game to Wukong this game might be a bit worse but for me the game still looks insane. If you a bit more nitpick then you probably hate the water physics in this game since is pretty bad for a 2020 game compare to HL2 but you won't be step foot in a single water molecule for like 99% of the game except for a few mission.
  + Sounds/OST: Sounds/OST probably the strongest point of the game beside the gameplay since you have so many iconic OST, for example: Like A Supreme, Rebel Path, Who's Ready For Tomorrow?, Phantom Liberty,... And all the sounds of Sandevistan, weapons, cars,... 
  + Gameplay: Strongest point of the game since you can build your character however you want. You want to be a cool hacker? Play Netrunner, you want to be a cool anime dude? play Sandevistan with any weapon you want, or you just want to be Hulk and destroy everything if so play berserker + Gorilla Arms, there's so many build for you to choose and the game want you to play whatever you want instead of forcing you to play like a robot.
  + Story: I'm not a lore guy but the story in the game is easy enough for a monkey like me to understand but so deep that you had to become Sherlock Holmes to know all the tiny details. I also like how the game have so much ending even though 99% of it lead you to death or just delay it but the other just straight up turn you into a NPC if you want to live, this shown how you never going to be a good ending in the game. (Don't Fear The Reaper in my opinion is the best ending and the coolest you can't change my mind)
  + Character/NPC: I really love how CD PROJEKT RED design all of their characters, each characters have their own charms, their own personality that made players adore them. My favorite is either Jackie Welles or Ozob Bozo cause of how funny they are especially Ozob Bozo since he's literally had a grenade as a nose and you can accidently kill him if you punch him repeatedly in the nose when doing a boxing mission against him.
  + Environment: CD PROJEKT RED really nailed it when comes to building an impressive world in the future where you have a flashy city of Night City filled with skyscraper, mega corps,... and it really made you think this is how the future going to look like. But there's still a shit tons of flaws in this so called futuristic city. Even though the city center seems futuristic but the outskirt are just filled with mountains of trash, gangs fighting each other, corrupted system, mega corps control most of the city, rich people get treated like kings where poor people are treated worse than trash. All of this made the game felt so deep when you go and explore the city.
  + Weapon: The game have a tons of weapon split in 3 category for both range weapon and melee. Such as power/tech/smart and for melee is blade/blunt/throwable, each have their own gimmick for example: power weapon can ricochet against wall to hit enemy behind wall, tech weapon can charge to dealt a shit load of damage or to penetrate cover and smart weapon just free aimbot. This make the player can use whatever they want, whenever they want depends on their situation/playstyle.
  + Side content: The games have quite a lot of content for people to explore and items you can miss when to focusing on mission until youtube/tik tok just randomly pop up a vid where they said 90% of players missed this OP weapon when first playing the game. This kinda encourage player to play slow on their first playthrough and go try to explore the game. And i also love how there are so many easter eggs in the game, my favorite is how they add Hideo Kojima to the game.

- Negative:
  + Cars and travelling system: I feel like cars in this game felt pretty bad when compare to games like GTA 5 cause of how bouncy some car is and some car felt so slippery when driving .Quick travel are good but the placement are pretty bad that they force me to download mod for me to TP to anywhere on my fourth playthrough. 
  + Dialogue: A lot of Dialogue in this game is pretty funny but when doing all these sidequest and listening to all the NPC yapping for 5 minutes in an unskippable dialogue and proceed to walk to the mission for another 3 minutes force me to download mod to speed up all of this.
  + NPC/Environment?: I don't know how to categorize this but i really hate how there isn't much happening around  the character for example in GTA 5 you can easily face situation where there's gang fight happening, traffic accident, or interaction with between player and NPC. This made the game feel both deep and bland at the same time when traveling though the city.
  + Weapon: Even though the weapon system was goated but there's still things i hate when using some type of weapon. Mostly power weapon, even though power weapon had the highest raw damage compare to other weapon but the ricochet gimmick are so ahh since you had to line up perfectly with the angle just to kill a enemy hiding behind a wall where a tech weapon can just penetrate his ahh behind a wall. This lead to ricochet gimmick rarely gets used, I'm doubt anyone use this mechanic unless you really try hard just to use this thing.
  + Minimap: I hate how they just add a low ahh poly minimap that's make finding item on the minimap incredibly difficult, would much rather they add a detailed map to the base game instead of making the players downloading mod.
  + Bugs: Most of the bugs i faced all related to vehicle so i won't really count this as a negative thing.

* Overall this game is a 9/10 for me, even though there's some flaws in the game but the positive outweigh the negative and i suggested everyone finish this game once whether they love it or not they still definitely like some part of the game.

首先，这是一个中评。直至今天，游戏依然有数不清的bug，且游戏经常不定时崩溃，令我烦不胜烦。

1.如果你是奔着游戏性来的，我并不是很推荐这款游戏。这个游戏优秀的地方是剧情，而不是游戏性。游戏往往是战斗五分钟，剧情两小时。同时，游戏系统的深度并不深，流派比较固定，各个流派的打法也都相对固定，最高难度下，流派成型前各种坐牢，成型后又无双割草，很容易腻。且游戏全程只有一次洗点机会，意味着你只能换一次流派。

拿我玩的纯黑客流举例，成型前只能清一清地图上比较简单的ncpd事件(说白了就是清问号)，挨几枪就死。成型后就靠着ram配平的bug乱杀，所有人都是固定的一套技能组合打死，一次打不死就再来一次，碰到群怪就是关机流，消耗极少的蓝量把一群怪集体哄睡着，没有任何挑战性。

2.如果你是个完美主义者，我先浇一盆冷水：这个游戏不可能全收集。打个比方：一个任务分为A，B两条线，你走A线，B线的收集就不可能拿到，反之亦然。或者是三个特殊配件都需要某个boss的掉落物，但掉落物只有一个，你只能三选一制作。

3.游戏的战斗系统虽然不深，但道具之类的东西有很多。这些东西大部分都是时尚小垃圾。每个餐馆都会卖一大堆没卵用的食物，每个酒保都卖一大堆没卵用的酒...一方面，增加了游戏的沉浸感，但另一方面，这一大堆洋垃圾让新手看得眼花。新手根本不知道哪些是垃圾，哪些东西真正有用。

总之，这个游戏仅推荐给个喜欢体验游戏剧情，对游戏性没有太高要求的玩家，不是每个人都适合这个游戏

26 Horas em Night City: Como o Prólogo de Cyberpunk 2077 me Quebrou

Eu não sabia absolutamente nada sobre a história de Cyberpunk 2077 quando dei os meus primeiros passos em Watson. Claro que sei do lançamento desastroso cheio de bugs, e da volta por cima do jogo. Claro que vi diversos vídeos de gameplay e que o Keanu Reeves interpreta um dos personagens principais, como também sei que jogo vendeu mais de 30 milhões de unidades. Mas da história e dos acontecimentos relevantes não sabia nada, porque não costumo conhecer antes a história de um jogo que pretendo jogar.

E foi justamente essa total inocência que tornou o tombo tão brutal. Eu passei até aqui 26 horas jogando. Vinte e seis horas antes mesmo do título principal do jogo subir na tela. Eu me perdi completamente na imersão daquela cidade; fui engolido por sua arquitetura opressiva, pelas luzes de neon, pela sujeira dos becos, e pela falsa sensação de que eu estava no controle. Cada esquina me puxava para uma nova história, um novo contrato. Eu demorei de propósito. Eu queria respirar Night City. Me relacionei e 
 me apeguei a diversos personagens. 

Mas então, o assalto ao Kompeki Plaza acontece junto com impactantes reviravoltas na historia. A imersão das primeiras 26 horas me fez achar que eu já estava no profundo do jogo, mas ainda era o prólogo e este fez eu ter umas das maiores experiências pessoais da minha vida com jogos. 

Se o prólogo conseguiu me marcar desse jeito, não faço ideia do que me espera no resto da cidade. Isso é só o começo da jornada, mas já estou completamente rendido. Quando eu finalmente zerar, volto aqui para contar o resto dessa jornada.

[h1] CYBERPUNK 2077 [/h1]
[h2] ЛЮБОВЬ, СМЕРТЬ И ИМПЛАНТЫ [/h2]

Ну вот и дошли руки до самого кажется для меня важного события, пишу обзор (по моему мнению) лучшую игру всего времени, которая есть сейчас в доступе. Почему такое громкое заявление? Попробую уложиться в этот обзор, потому что тут есть что обсуждать с начала выхода игры в 2020 по сегодня (2026).

[h2] ВПЕЧАТЛЕНИЯ [/h2]
Польской студия [b] CD Projekt RED [/b] в очередной раз представляет проект, который выводит историю и подачу игры на новый уровень, даже если закрывать глаза на тот ужас, который ждал игроков на релизе. Нас погружают в мрачное будущее [b] Найт-Сити [/b] и глубокий нелинейный сюжетом. Визуальный стиль Найт-Сити выглядит потрясающе! Его неоновыми вывески, грязные переулки, летающие автомобили и огромными корпоративными башнями выглядит так, будто сошёл с обложек киберпанк-журналов 80-х, или какого-нибудь футористичного аниме. Уже в прологе, который зависит от выбранного жизненного пути, игра знакомит с миром через разные точки зрения. Меня цепляла всегда оригинальная история, поэтому я выбрал "Дитя улиц" и продолжил свой путь. Знакомство с персонажами и при этом грамотная подача способностей и оружия, не нагружает геймплей игры. Кат-сцены сделаны настолько с осторожностью, что финальная миссия пролога ощущается с тревогой. Всё равно, каждый путь даёт уникальные диалоговые опции и по-разному вводит в мир. Например, Корпорат начинает в роскошном офисе, а затем оказывается на дне, что создаёт сильный контраст. Выбор пути влияет на некоторые побочные квесты и реплики, но не меняет глобальный сюжет — это, скорее, ролевой инструмент для отыгрыша. Теперь переходим к интересному:
[hr][/hr]

[h2] СЮЖЕТ [/h2]
Сюжет. Музыка. Герои. Я склоняю голову разработчикам и сценаристам. Но начну по порядку: Главный герой (или героиня) [b] V (Ви) [/b] — наёмник, мечтающий стать легендой Найт-Сити. После серии событий, связанных с кражей биочипа у корпорации [b] Arasaka [/b], Ви получает в голову цифровую копию сознания [b] Джонни Сильверхенда [/b] (в исполнении [b] Киану Ривза [/b]) — легендарного рокера и террориста, погибшего полвека назад. Чип постепенно перезаписывает личность V, и у героя остаётся не так много времени, чтобы найти способ спастись. Джонни Сильверхенд не просто пассивный спутник, он постоянно комментирует происходящее, спорит с V, делится воспоминаниями и постепенно из врага превращается в друга (или наоборот, в зависимости от выбора игрока). Отношения между V и Джонни — эмоциональное ядро игры. Диалоги между ними полны сарказма, философских размышлений о свободе и идентичности. Киану Ривз, несмотря на критику в этой роли, отыграл легендарно, чего только стоит фраза "Еб*ть Арасаку" или "Еб*ть мой лысый х*й". Сюжет разбит на несколько веток в которым Ви и ищет своё спасение, но перед этим хочется упомянуть [b] Джеки [/b], яркого персонажа с тяжелой судьбой. Друга Ви, который стал для него братом (как мне показалось). Каждая ветка приводит к одному из финальных заданий. Концовки сильно различаются, поэтому выбор и помощь персонажам игры является неотъемлемым событием, которое стоит проходить. Возможность пройти игру на разную концовку позволяет конечно ощущать историю и игру живой, настолько реалистичной, что в концовке самопожертвования, можно пустить слезу. Стоит пройти серию заданий от любимой фиксерши [b] Джуди, Ривера и Джонни [/b], который знакомит нас с его ярким другом - [b] Кери [/b]. Остальные побочки интересны, но не так шокируют как эти. В целом, сюжет Cyberpunk 2077 — это смесь нуара, готики и мрака в неоновом ночном или дневном роскошном мире.

[h2] ОПТИМИЗАЦИЯ[/h2]
[b] (Ryzen 5 5600, RX 5700 XT, 16 GB Kingston FURY) - Мои настройки [/b]
Теперь чуть о грустном. Как игра работает на моей конфигурации: на версии игры 2.0/2.1 (после всех патчей), без трассировки лучей, в разрешении 1080p. Для достижения стабильных 60+ FPS в большинстве сцен рекомендую балансировать между выскоми и средними настройками, почему? В открытом городе, плотные районы (Уотсон, центр) FPS колеблется от 50 до 75 в зависимости от времени суток и количества NPC, а вот в помещениях и сюжетных сценах: стабильные 70-90 FPS. В перестрелках с большим количеством эффектов просадки достигали до 45-50 FPS, но кратковременные, а на мимо Догтауна было и вообще ниже, однако после 2.1, исправили - стабильные 50-55 FPS есть.  Вывод, хорошая конфигурация, но не хватает чуть до 1440p. Задумываюсь о карточке новой и оперативной памяти.

[h2] СТОИТ В НЕЁ ИГРАТЬ СЕГОДНЯ? [/h2]
Да, но в ней есть но и расскажу почему. Сегодня Cyberpunk 2077 — это совершенно другая игра по сравнению с релизом. Большинство критических багов исправлено, производительность игру улучшена, но структура игра всё такая же и вот немногие её минусы: — враги часто тупят, не используют укрытия грамотно и просто бегают по карте. Могут наносить хороший урон, если играть на высоком уровне. Полиция раньше появлялась из ниоткуда (исправлено в 2.0, но всё ещё не идеально). Пешеходы и трафик живут по примитивным скриптам, нет ощущения цельности мира, но потом привык и это не бросалось больше в глаза. Открытый мир — красивый, но как по мне не хватило креатива в роде азартных игр или настройки жилья. Однако на фоне этого всего, в игре обилие оружия, мечей, хорошо прописанных побочных героев с Скиппи, который поразил многий фандом.

Für mich eines dieser Spiele, bei denen einfach alles zusammenpasst. 
Besonders begeistert hat mich die Gestaltung der Welt in Kombination mit der Story und dieser einzigartigen Atmosphäre. Es fühlt sich unglaublich besonders an.

Die gesamte Gestaltung des Spiels gefällt mir unglaublich gut. Die Stadt, die verschiedenen Bezirke, die Lichter, die Musik und diese teilweise düstere, aber gleichzeitig wunderschöne Atmosphäre sorgen dafür, dass man richtig in die Welt eintauchen kann.

Glücklicherweise wurde ich von den vielen Bugs verschont, über die man zum Release so viel gehört hat. Da ich Cyberpunk erst Jahre nach der Veröffentlichung gespielt habe, konnte ich das Spiel direkt so genießen, wie es für mich sein sollte. Dadurch wurde meine Erfahrung zum Glück nicht durch technische Probleme oder andere Fehler kaputtgemacht.

Auch die Story hat mich sehr gepackt. Es gibt viele Momente, die einem im Gedächtnis bleiben, und besonders die Beziehungen zwischen den Charakteren sind meiner Meinung nach sehr gut gelungen. Die Freundschaft zu Jackie hat mir beispielsweise richtig gut gefallen. Gerade weil man ihn am Anfang begleitet und gemeinsam einiges erlebt, fühlt sich diese Verbindung für mich sehr natürlich an.

Auch die Liebesgeschichte mit Panam finde ich unglaublich gelungen. Solche Momente sorgen dafür, dass die Charaktere nicht einfach nur irgendwelche NPCs sind, sondern dass man tatsächlich eine Verbindung zu ihnen aufbaut.

Für mich passt bei Cyberpunk einfach alles zusammen. Man merkt, wie viel Arbeit in Night City und die vielen Geschichten gesteckt wurde.

Deshalb ist es für mich ein Spiel, das man nicht einfach nur durchspielt und danach vergisst. Die Welt und ihre Charaktere bleiben im Kopf.

Definitiv eines meiner Lieblings Rollenspiele.

最开始接触这部作品的时候，是看着他能退款让我白嫖了有钱之后再补票。但实际上，这是我在24以后肝完鸣潮到现在唯一玩进去了的开放世界游戏，我便在游历了大约25小时后便立刻补票。这部作品凭借他独特的美术风格及其吸引人的剧情让我在期末月的时候沉醉不已，以至于我迟迟不愿意为这部来自夜之城的冒险画上句号，近来无聊，我便翻出这部作品将其通关。
实话实说，这部作品到今日对我而言依然算是并不完善的半成品。虽然距离首发灾难已经过去了很久。但是他依然存在着部分影响游戏的bug，后面几次对武器的平衡性调整也很莫名其妙，游玩过程中能看到很多别的系统的废案，战斗系统的手感一言难尽。但这些始终都无法改变他是一部剧情优秀，内容丰富的开放世界赛博朋克游戏，也是目前上独一无二毫无代餐的赛博朋克游戏。整体而言瑕不掩瑜，值得一试。

Story:
Felt well written and had a lot of still relevant comparisons to the current times. Bitter sweet ending no matter what choices are made.

Gameplay:
Really liked the power system and abilities, but lacked any sort of enemy scaling other than the 'final' boss. so the last 30~ hours of gameplay feels very steam rollie on the normal difficulty

Issues:
SOO MANY VISUAL BUGS even after 5+ years from release. Feels like only the really well known/viral bugs were addressed :/ ran into bugs where NPC vehicles would just disappear mid mission while driving near them, and some NPC's were just always aggressive even though a mission would suggest otherwise.

Positives:
give this game a solid 4/10. Graphics were nice, lack of loading screens were cool from a technical perspective, but the massive visual bugs, and mediocre writing made those accomplishments moot.

Game just does not feel finished. There are still tons of bugs and I will list a couple of the most common/memorable at the end of my review. 

My three general complaints are: 
1. You level up way to fast to the point where it feels punishing to play the hacker playstyle. Every mission you can kill everybody no matter what by only clicking a few buttons. I do think this is a general game issue because the game feels very easy even on the highest difficulty. The only real challenge is when I tell myself "I will only use [x] weapon for this mission." Some enemies have "resistances" to certain forms of combat, but attaching that to the ram system negates it due to the many ways to regen ram or overcharge mode, which allows you to sacrifice hp to hack increasing your ram pool near infinitely. 
2. I don't know if this is just me, but the main story fails to entertain me. This is okay because the side missions are honestly more fun than the busywork the main missions provide. Too much dialogue, too much following frustratingly slow NPCs, and too many tasks and decisions that feel unimportant. 
3. Lastly I know its hard to make games look good while flying; but having flying cars around, millions of dollars in the bank, and being unable to buy one feels kinda bad for a futuristic game. 

All that being said: The world has amazing atmosphere. Driving around, especially in the rain or at night, feels just amazing. The music, the views, and just something I cant explain gives me a amazing feeling of being small... of peace. I do wish there were driving sounds though. 

Here is a list of bugs I have experienced so far. 
1. Picking up items or opening a chest frequently causes things to go flying.
2. NPCs t-posing while driving their cars.
3. Story NPCs get hit by cars during cutscenes causing their dead bodies to drag on the floor while talking to me until they start a different animation and get revived.
4. Enemies glitching into walls and floors.
5. Enemies seeing you through walls and floors.
6. Once a enemy I killed glitched so hard his body was shot into the sky while his head was stuck on a railing causing his entire model to be a massive tapestry spanning over a block and crashing my FPS till it unloaded.
7. Cyberpsycho missions, while being some of the most fun, are also insanely buggy with their triggers. Three times I have had to fast travel, skip 48 hours in time, and then go back just to have things spawn or trigger.
8. Constant floating items, occasional floating NPCs, and briefly floating cars before they crash down. 

The bugs are the main reason I just cannot recommend this game. They break immersion more than anything else.

Die Story ist (Stand Anfang Akt 2)… irgendwo vorhanden. Ich weiß zwar nicht wo, aber es gibt sie. Ok.“ Man bekommt NIEMANDEN dezidiert vorgestellt oder entwickelt eine emotionale Tiefe mit ihm oder ihr. Die Leute sind halt da. Ich hoffe DRINGEND, dass sie besser wird, denn dafür spielt man Story Spiele doch? Aktuell QUÄLE ich mich durch das Spiel, um es abzuschließen.

---{ Preis }---

---{ Gesamtwertung }---
Ein Spiel, dessen Story mich nicht fesselt, in einer Welt, die absolut tot wirkt, weil man mit niemandem Zufallsgespräche führen kann und so auch mal explizit auf der Karte herumstrohmert um Sachen und Zufallsbegegnungen zu finden. Alle Örtlichkeiten, bei denen man  Missionen und Begegnungen hat, sind auf der Map markiert, damit auch der letzte Vollpfosten sie findet. Wenn man einfach so durch die Stadt latscht, findet man mal Loot. Mehr nicht. Kein Typ, der einen auf dem Weg zur Mission an der Jacke packt und ins Dunkel einer Gasse zieht, weil er „dringend Hilfe“ braucht. Einfach stumpf den Markern hinterher und ihr habt alles gesehen.

四年前，我还是一名初三学生。
那时我在暑假看了动漫《边缘行者》，真是一把鼻涕一把泪，诸多心酸。多么动人的情节，多么令人震撼的世界观。听说还有同名游戏？还真有啊，我迫不及待地想着去游玩游戏《赛博朋克2077》，但设备的缘故，我不得不将它放在旁边，说到底还是因为贫穷，大卫，我同情早期的你呀。便只好暂且不去想它。
我明白，有一天我会去打开它的。
到了今年，是要上大学了。
这时的笔记本行情并不乐观，各大品牌的价格水涨船高，是某种不可抗力导致么，听起来算是让高价购买笔记本的学生好受一些。在众多平台蹲守多日，总算看到了一款价格还能接受的笔记本，七彩虹的。先前我还看不起它呢，现在看来，我多么幼稚。5050足够我畅玩《赛博朋克2077》了。3倍帧生成与DLSS是个不可多得的好技术。其实在录取学校与专业出来之前，我在网吧就几乎快将它的剧情玩了一遍，只不过像是蜻蜓点水般，或说是焦急的“速通”，完全不能体会该游戏的魅力嘛。不久前我建了一个新存档，而今估计也有五六十小时了，剧情刚到中期，一切可以慢慢来。
说到动漫，动漫与游戏的氛围实在是各不相同。大卫是一个悲剧角色，露西则是一个可怜的未亡人。赛博世界的剥削多么残酷啊！可游戏却不能体会到残酷的氛围，V是一个近乎无敌的角色，对于玩家来说。存档读档，风灵月影……啊，玩家总是强大，而赛博朋克的残酷并不永恒。到现在为止，对于游戏内容我有些许失望，我想进入的是大卫与露西的世界，体会那种身不由己的向前。V的存在粉饰了赛博朋克世界的黑暗，让人误解其中仍有光明。但大多数人只是普普通通的大多数，与他们相比，V像是凌驾于赛博法则之上，relic的使用者，多么理想化的主角……
总的来说，《赛博朋克2077》是一个好的作品，怎么也算佳作，但并不是一个深刻的作品。作为赛博朋克风格的里程碑，它的综合素质足以替它抵挡风雨。玩家迫切想要看到赛博世界的黑暗。我持久期待，期待着《赛博朋克猎户座》的诞生！

Yo fui uno de los que compró Cyberpunk 2077 prácticamente de salida. De hecho, tenía una edición coleccionista para PS4 y terminé devolviéndola por el estado en el que salió el juego. Fue una decepción enorme.

Tiempo después intenté volver a jugarlo en un portátil. La experiencia había mejorado y el juego empezaba a gustarme, pero no consiguió engancharme del todo.

Ahora, años después, he podido jugarlo en un equipo capaz de mostrar realmente todo lo que Cyberpunk 2077 puede ofrecer. Y la diferencia ha sido brutal.

Me ha parecido una auténtica pasada.

Lo que más destacaría es lo fácil que resulta entrar en su historia y acabar involucrándote emocionalmente con sus personajes. No parecen simples NPC colocados ahí para darte una misión. Tienen miedos, problemas, relaciones, objetivos y una personalidad propia que consigue que algunos terminen importándote de verdad.

Y esto no se limita únicamente a la historia principal. Muchas misiones secundarias podrían formar parte perfectamente de la trama principal por la calidad con la que están escritas. Incluso encargos aparentemente menores consiguen contar pequeñas historias y aportar algo al mundo.

Ese ha sido uno de los aspectos que más me han gustado: tienes constantemente la sensación de que Night City continúa existiendo aunque tú no estés mirando.

La ciudad, además, es espectacular. No solamente por su apartado gráfico, que jugando al máximo puede llegar a ser impresionante, sino por todo lo que transmite. Publicidad por todas partes, desigualdad, tecnología, decadencia, exceso, violencia... Está llena de pequeños detalles que ayudan muchísimo a creerte el mundo en el que estás.

También me ha sorprendido lo bien que trata determinados temas relacionados con la tecnología y con un futuro que quizá no esté tan lejos como parece. La identidad, la conciencia, hasta dónde seguimos siendo nosotros mismos cuando la tecnología empieza a formar parte de nuestro cuerpo o qué significa realmente dejar algo de nosotros cuando morimos.

Y consigue plantear muchas de esas cuestiones sin necesidad de convertir el juego en una explicación filosófica constante. Están integradas dentro de la propia historia, los personajes y el mundo.

Incluso algunas historias aparentemente absurdas o secundarias terminan planteando preguntas interesantes. Desde inteligencias artificiales hasta situaciones completamente surrealistas que, dentro de Night City, terminan pareciendo perfectamente normales.

La jugabilidad también me ha parecido muchísimo mejor de lo que recordaba. Puedes afrontar muchas situaciones de maneras diferentes dependiendo de cómo hayas construido a V: utilizando armas, sigilo, hackeo, implantes o una combinación de todo ello. Hay suficiente variedad como para encontrar una forma de jugar que realmente encaje contigo.

En mi caso, el principal punto negativo ha sido la conducción. No porque esté mal diseñada, sino porque nunca terminé de conectar con las físicas de los vehículos. A veces tenía la sensación de que los coches pesaban menos de lo que deberían, como si flotaran ligeramente sobre el asfalto. Te terminas acostumbrando, pero probablemente sea el apartado que menos me ha convencido.

También he encontrado algún bug y algún crasheo ocasional, aunque nada comparable con el estado en el que salió originalmente.

Y quizá lo mejor que puedo decir de Cyberpunk 2077 es que ha sido uno de esos juegos a los que no entraba simplemente porque estaba aburrido.

Entraba porque quería seguir jugando.

Quería saber qué ocurría con V, continuar las historias de determinados personajes, descubrir otra zona de Night City o simplemente ver qué nueva situación absurda iba a encontrarme.

La historia principal me ha encantado y además ofrece diferentes desenlaces, lo que hace todavía más interesante pensar en las decisiones que has ido tomando durante la partida.

Después de haber sido uno de los jugadores que salió profundamente decepcionado con su lanzamiento, me alegra muchísimo haberle dado otra oportunidad.

Si todavía tienes dudas por todo lo que ocurrió cuando salió, mi recomendación es sencilla: olvídate de aquello y juega al juego que existe ahora.

Disfruta de Night City y, sobre todo, disfruta de la historia de V.

Totalmente recomendado.

Cyberpunk 2077 is not simply one of the best games I have played. It is my favorite game, full stop.

I know the history of this game. I know how it launched, the controversy, the bugs and all the promises that were discussed for years. None of that should be forgotten. But judging Cyberpunk 2077 as it exists today, especially together with Phantom Liberty, I think CD Projekt RED created something extraordinary.

What makes it special to me is not just Night City, although Night City is probably the most impressive open world I have ever experienced. It feels oppressive, beautiful, decadent and alive at the same time. The neon, the megabuildings, the dirty backstreets, the corporate districts, the Badlands, the rain at night, the advertisements everywhere... there are moments when I stop playing and just look around. Few games have ever given me such a strong sense of place.

But a beautiful city means nothing without characters worth caring about, and this is where Cyberpunk really becomes something else. Johnny Silverhand, Panam, Judy, Viktor, Jackie and so many others are not just quest dispensers. They have personality, contradictions, flaws and memorable conversations. Johnny in particular is one of my favorite characters in gaming. The relationship between V and Johnny changes naturally over the course of the story and gives the game much of its emotional weight.

The writing is also a huge reason why I prefer Cyberpunk even to other great open-world games. The main story is excellent, but some of the side quests are just as memorable. The game constantly moves between huge moments and very personal stories without feeling like a checklist. It can be violent and spectacular one minute and unexpectedly intimate or depressing the next. Its best moments stay with you long after you stop playing.

I also love that the gameplay gives me freedom without turning the game into a slow sandbox. You can go in shooting, use stealth, build around blades, pistols or heavy weapons, become a walking cybernetic tank, or destroy an entire group through quickhacks before they even know where you are. The progression actually changes how you play. Experimenting with cyberware and builds is part of the fun, and combat remains fast and satisfying instead of becoming secondary to the story.

Then there is Phantom Liberty. For me, it is not just extra content; it completes the game. Dogtown has its own identity, the espionage tone works perfectly, and the story involving Songbird and Reed is some of CDPR's best writing. Songbird is an especially memorable character because the game never gives you an easy, comfortable answer about her. The expansion forces you to make decisions where every option has a cost, and that is exactly the kind of storytelling I want from an RPG.

Visually, Cyberpunk 2077 is still one of the games I use as a reference for what a high-end PC can do. With the settings pushed to the limit, ray tracing/path tracing and all the modern rendering technology enabled, Night City can look almost absurdly good. But the art direction is more important than the technology. Even when you strip away the technical effects, the city has a visual identity that is instantly recognizable.

The soundtrack and sound design deserve their own mention. The radio, the combat music, the ambient tracks and the quieter pieces all contribute to the atmosphere. There are scenes where the combination of music, dialogue and Night City in the background creates something genuinely cinematic without taking away the feeling that you are still playing a game.

Is it perfect? No. Some systems could still be deeper, the open world can occasionally reveal the limits of its simulation, and anyone who experienced the original launch has every right to remember how unacceptable parts of it were. But the game that exists now is vastly different from the game people argued about in 2020.

What matters most to me is that Cyberpunk 2077 has something many technically excellent games never achieve: identity. I remember its characters. I remember specific conversations. I remember driving through Night City at 2 a.m. with the radio playing. I remember the decisions I made and the endings that genuinely hurt. I remember the atmosphere.

There are games I admire, games I enjoy, and games I consider masterpieces. Cyberpunk 2077 is the rare one that goes beyond that for me. It is the game I compare other narrative open-world games to, and very few come close.

Night City is a living, vibrant city: crowded sidewalks, bustling markets, and constant traffic. There is a surprise around every corner.

The other side of the coin is a sense of underlying decay and social despair. As you explore, you realize the profound social disparity between the various neighborhoods and classes as you move from the city center toward the outskirts: gleaming buildings give way to crumbling neighborhoods and filth everywhere.
All this leads to rampant crime; you will see scenes of senseless violence and gangs simply by walking the streets.
At night, the city is at its best: the neon lights and crowded venues will make you want to be there and join the party!
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3772848420

You decide how to approach missions and assignments: Do you want to go in guns blazing? Do you want to handle everything stealthily without being detected?
Do you want to fry your opponents' brains? It’s all in your hands!
The skill system and the wide variety of weapons available will truly let your imagination run wild =D

Reignited my love for open world games.

Night City is a city that never sleeps. Sometimes you are up there and sometimes down there, or rather, from my V's perspective: Sometimes you are solving a humanitarian crisis in Europe from the comfort of a luxurious office on the 30th floor of Arasaka Tower with a fat bank account and health insurance, only to find yourself practically on the streets the next day. Without influential friends, without an ambulance, with a few small euros in your pockets.

The corporate start is one of three possible ones that you choose at the beginning. They do not have any bonuses to your statistics, but apart from the opening lesson, they have a great influence on the story background of the main character or heroine. Raised by a corporate person, V does not let herself be bullied because she knows how things work in the world of big animals, so she does not hesitate to rub her nose in their lies.
In my case, it was the acquaintances from Arasaka that played a crucial role in the story, and I can only guess how it would have all played out if I had chosen to play as a nomad or a street child.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a world of its own, where power and money are concentrated in the hands of the successful one percent. The poor majority have long since stopped believing that the key to success is hard work. However, your goal this time is not to change or dominate the world, and that is actually quite refreshing in terms of gaming. You will not change Night City, it will change you. It is difficult to write your name in a long and turbulent futuristic history, but you have a free hand in how you become a legend. You will soon find out that the hardest thing will be to survive the whole merry-go-round leading to fame, so that you can at least enjoy the desired fame for a while. [b] 95% [/b]
