no que ele se propõe, entrega igual poucos jogos entregam. night city é visceral, agressiva, viva de um jeito que poucos mundos abertos conseguem chegar perto. e é uma crítica pesada a uma sociedade "do futuro" que na real é só um espelho distorcido do que a gente já vive hoje... corporações substituindo governo, gente vendendo pedaço do próprio corpo pra sobreviver, desumanização em escala industrial disfarçada de progresso. tem até aquela pergunta que o jogo faz sem precisar dizer em voz alta, o que sobra de "você" quando seu corpo, sua memória e sua identidade viram produto que pode ser comprado, trocado, melhorado? v carrega isso o jogo inteiro, literalmente com johnny dividindo espaço na própria cabeça dele.

e a construção de night city como espaço físico é genuinamente impressionante. a cidade é tão viva e tão bem desenhada que mesmo sem olhar o mapa você sabe exatamente onde você tá. você sente quando entrou numa parte pobre, você sente quando tá no berço das megacorporações, dá pra diferenciar o distrito só pela vibe, pela arquitetura, pelo tipo de gente andando na rua. isso é MUITO foda e é o tipo de trabalho de world design que poucos jogos conseguem acertar desse jeito.

e o jogo é brutal em uma coisa específica: fazer a "coisa certa" não te garante final feliz. isso não é só na main quest, tá espalhado em TUDO... nos serviços de fixer pela cidade, nos assaltos, nas side quests mais bobinhas. cada personagem parece ter problemas reais, vida própria, motivos reais pras próprias escolhas. ninguém ali é só um NPC de missão, todo mundo parece genuinamente vivo, e isso é o que faz night city pulsar do jeito que pulsa. dá pra sentir que o jogo não acredita em final feliz fácil porque a sociedade que ele retrata também não acredita nisso, e é exatamente por isso que funciona tanto.

os personagens em sua grande maioria são todos bem escritos, cada arco bem construído o suficiente pra você se importar de verdade com o que acontece com eles.

e nem a jogabilidade fica devendo. cada playthrough eu jogo uma build completamente diferente e sinto a diferença de verdade, não é só reskin de número. netrunner hackeando tudo à distância, build de samurai parecendo que está num jogo de matrix, build stealth andando pelas sombras, build de armas inteligentes, e por aí vai... cada uma muda completamente como você joga night city e todas são genuinamente divertidas do jeito delas.

cyberpunk 2077 foi um jogo que começou devendo muito no seu lançamento, com certeza foi a grande decepção de um monte de gente que aguardava esse jogo na época. hoje, depois de inúmeros patchs e da excelente DLC phantom liberty, é com certeza um grande jogo.

[h1] Мой любимый Cyberpunk 2077 [/h1]
Сотни часов проведенные в этой игре до ее покупки и последние мои 100 часов уже в купленной версии Cyberpunk2077 позволяют мне написать максимально честный обзор с моей стороны.
CD Project RED создатели моих любимых игр не подвели и в этот раз. Я помню CP2077 на запуске, как было куча гневных обзоров и отзывов на его релизе. Я не отнесся к игре с каким то предостережением после всего что я видел, я все равно скачал и не пожалел.
[h3] Сюжет [/h3]
Сюжет довольно прост, но в то же время игра и не ставит на него, побочные ветки - вот на чем Реды сконцентрировались. Сюжетные линии Панам, Джуди и Керри - что то с чем-то. Жалко что Ривера по моему мнению не сильно раскрыли. Каждый квест въелся мне в сердце и оставил свой след. Я помню как плакал вместе с Джуди , [spoiler] после того как Эвелин решила роскомнадзорнуться[/spoiler] , как бухал вместе с Панам, [spoiler] после убийства стиллетов[/spoiler]. Их истории я прожил будто я не простой игрок, а человек который был с ними там, в Найт-Сити. 
[h3] Открытый мир [/h3]
Открытый мир это главная боль игры. Найт-Сити невероятно красивый, но внутри пустой. Всё, что можно делать на улицах это стрелять в банды и собирать хлам. Нельзя просто посидеть в баре или купить нормальную еду, если это не квест. Похоже, разработчики просто не успели добавить жизнь в этот город, поэтому я все 100 часов телепортировался из одного места в другое, не осматривая сам город.
В то же время сюжетные локации выполнены просто на высшем уровне, чего стоит пентхаус Арасаки или Бар Кайот. Я готов был бы находится в них вечно и осматривать их все свое время.
[h3] Отношения [/h3]
В игру завезли отношения, но они не сильно проработаны. Да , за муж. Ви вы можете романсить Панам или Керри, а за жен. Ви Джуди или Ривера, но здесь кроется одна проблема - отношения вовсе не прописаны. Да у вас будет любовная сцена и вы сможете их приглашать к себе домой. Но на этом все, нет никакого интерактива. И что дальше? А дальше тишина. Они приходят в твою квартиру и просто стоят. Не реагируют, не разговаривают, не предлагают куда-то пойти. Вы даже поесть вместе не можете.
Как и весь Найт-Сити - красиво снаружи, но пусто внутри. Отношения есть, а настоящей жизни в них нет. 
[h2] Итог [/h2]
Cyberpunk 2077 это игра великих противоречий. Она дарит тебе незабываемые истории и персонажей, за которых переживаешь как за реальных людей. Но при этом она запихивает их в самую красивую, но самую пустую коробку, которую я видел в играх.
Если вы ищете глубокий сюжет и эмоции - берите, не раздумывая. Если вам нужна живая песочница, где можно зависнуть на сотни часов просто исследуя мир - здесь вы этого не найдете.
Я люблю эту игру. Люблю за Джуди, Панам, за этот неон под дождем. Но я ненавижу ее за нереализованный потенциал. CD Projekt RED создали шедевр, который мог стать величайшей игрой всех времен, но остановились на полпути.
Ставлю твердую 9/10 - за сюжет, за атмосферу, за сердце. Но эта девятка с горьким осадком. Еще немного, и было бы 10.

Purchases this at launch and like many others - was disgusted. Almost every aspect of the game seemed unfinished at best.  

For whatever reason - I decided to boot it up last week for the first time since then after hearing from many friends over the years that it was finally worth playing and actually is a great game now. 

I spent the first hour tweaking with graphics settings (as i usually do with AAA games), noticing almost every setting had noticeable impacts on performance - namely DLSS and ray tracing. I finally found a sequence of enabled and disabled settings that I felt equaled flawless performance with elite tier graphics. This alone makes this game a 7/10 for me. To be clear, this game is so beautiful and is now (6 years after launch) so optimized, that there could be literally no story, missions, etc. and I would still consider it a very very good game. 

As for the other stuff - movement and gunplay still is (and probably always will be) a bit clunky for my taste. I believe this is the nature of this game holding on to the RPG genre. That being said, its still fun and I enjoy it for what it is. 

While the map is beautiful at a macro scale, at a micro level, its unfortunately at its core just a massive copy of the same street vendor, vending machine, store front, etc. There are some buildings that are accessible but that seems to be the exception and not the norm. 

Story and characters so far (only 7 hours in) is elite. Movie-like. Only gripe is it seems like it feigns ways for you to change the story massively with dialog decisions, only to map seemingly opposite decisions back to the same ultimate path. 

Overall - it looks like this game has arrived, finally. Its still not perfect - and tbh, I don’t think its at a level set by Rockstar for open world games such as RDR2, but its close.

Wow!
Once of a decade game, a real masterpiece. It has very good writing and Story telling, a lot of appealing characters and a believable world and setting. CD Projekt really took the Cyberpunk setting very serious. They were able to deliver a world where you can feel the corporate dominance over people and government, how Augmentation tear society apart and what conflicts that brings to human beings. They also put a lot of effort into displaying many different aspects of it, like people almost being robot, how healtcare wokrs (Trauma Team) what AI is capable of doing, what happens if augmentations are not integrated well and in general how technology advances (Mechs, Surveillance, flying AVs). It´s a blast to immerse yourself into it.
A lot of character are written very well and with some depth that they are not only fitting a certian stereotype but going beyond that and deliver a sense of authenitc beings in that world. Ofc there are some relief characters, but I found them all to be in the right place. Sure, some were fooling around, but at a rate that its brightens up the cast and setting. 
Writing is at a so high note, that all the endings of the main game are fitting into the setiing and always leave me back jaw opening.

The major missions and major side missions are made with a lot of effort and are all worth playing. Most of the minor side missions (gigs) are also intriguing, especially if you dont mind reading. Even these gigs have some interesting level build ups and may later lead to major side missions with new characters to get to know. Overall the game had a great variety of missions to offer

Gameplay is smooth and fun. You can combine several styles (Melee, hacking, stealth, shooting). I often started a level with stealth, failed at it doing some shooting, and then went back to stealth. Besides the usual RPG exp points that you invest in really worthy perks, because they add new gameplay mechanics, you can also upgrade your body by adding cyberware and becoming more and more augmented.

Visuals are stunning! I took so many screenshots, and often just stopped to stare at whatever unfolds in front of me. Buildings, cars, weapons, everything is so well designed. Even the people on the streets look so stunning and fancy with all their futuristic looks, it all blends in well to immerse yourself into this setting.

The Phantom Liberty DLC falls a bit behind all that in my opinion and is not really a must have if you enjoy the main game. Certainly its made with high value, but I did not like the military touch of the new are and factions. Also the new characters were not that interesting to me (but are still written with effort).
So I would rate the base game as a must have with a score of 93 %
The DLC is maybe a 83%

Un peu déçu de ce jeu après la claque intersidérale qu'était The Witcher 3. Mais autant le dire, la barre était peut-être trop haute pour l'atteindre à nouveau.

C'est un bon jeu mais avec des défauts assez notable. Déjà la quête principale, assez courte en comparaison des jeux précédents de CDPR. Ce qui me gênerait pas si y'avait un buildup autour. Car au stade où ça arrive dans l'histoire, on s'y attend pas. La dernière mission arrive de manière abrupte. Sans trop de préparation. Alors y'a un message qui nous le fait comprendre mais j'étais vraiment surpris que la fin arrive aussi tôt. Ceci-dit le scénario est très bien. Les personnages aussi. CDPR sait faire. Toutes les fins possibles sont banger. Mais une meilleure construction narrative en amont aurait renforcé leur impact à mes yeux.

Autre défaut: la taille de la map. C'est pas énorme. Et les activités annexes sont très vites répétitives. Un défaut partagé avec The Witcher 3. Clairement, les quêtes secondaires sont beaucoup plus intéressantes. Même si de qualité variable.

En parlant de répétitivité, les combats le sont pas mal à force. Ca fonctionne. Mais le gamefeel est pas incroyable non plus. Ceci-dit, y'a quand même une bonne variété de build et spécialisations possibles. Peut-être que jouer full corps à corps est plus divertissants. J'ai eu ouïe dire qu'un build hacker peut permettre de clean des zones entières sans tirer un coup de feu donc ça c'est bien.

Niveau qualité, le jeu en a quand même sous le capot. Déjà visuellement. La DA est incroyable. L'univers de Cyberpunk est très bien retranscrit et immersif. La conduite est vraiment bien. C'est peut-être le seul jeu qui m'a fait aimer ça parce qu'autrement ça a vite fait de m'ennuyer. Mais là non. Foncer à toute allure sur une moto à travers Night City sur du gros Chrome Rock c'est d'un kiff ! Limite j'évitais les voyages rapides juste pour faire ça :))) D'ailleurs l'OST du jeu est vraiment top. Que ce soit les musiques originales ou toute la sélection écoutables dans les radios. Y'en a pour tout les goûts. En tant que métalleux, j'étais AUX ANGES que y'en ai une qui passe du gros Black Métal, du Death et du Hardcore. Sans compter toute la quête autour de Johnny Silverhand où on rassemble son ancien groupe Samuraï pour faire une dernière perf. C'est pour ce genre de moment que je kiffe CDPR.

Puis y'a ce sens délicat de l'écriture. Qui sait alterner entre le pathos et l'humour avec une précision constante. Ca humanise TELLEMENT les personnages (décidasse à la quête du distributeur, les vrais savent). Ce qui rend l'impact de nos choix d'autant plus fort parce qu'on s'attache à eux. Et si ils meurent alors...la tristesse est d'autant plus réelle.

En résumé: bon jeu qui vous retiendra plus pour sa DA, son ambiance et son écriture que son gameplay.

优秀的游戏剧本，会改变现实的剧本，没有一个真正意义上的好结局，却是最真实的表现，没经历过bug连篇的早版本，所以我的体验非常的棒，我一直都是冷科幻的发烧友，22年边缘行者的惊艳，让我一直不敢在网络平台了解和2077相关的内容，痒了几年，终于通了这部rpj神作。
首先这游戏缺点真的不少，稀烂的车辆驾驶手感、等电话或信息的设定让体验有点割裂、通关后大世界的可玩性不高等等，2.0后的现在也会有些bug，但由于优秀的部分过于超群，所以真的瑕不掩瑜。第一人称、身份选择、对话选择都让带入感强于市面大部分rpj游戏（当然一直跳对话肯定进不去），波兰蠢驴的优势叙事和道德选项，有些选择会让你获得大量奖励，但代价是一个家庭家破人亡，而你就是其中的变量，把愧疚感带到现实，大量的支线都有类似逻辑。主线自然是主菜，紧凑又刺激，让你快速了解所有人，然后再失去，偷货的007式路程体验然后再给你当头一棒，让你失去你的挚友，再引入新的人物，卷入公司斗争，然后一切从零开始，可以说是我个人主线中最喜欢的一章，那种感觉就连终章也稍逊一点。强尼这一角色，毫无疑问是一大亮点，谁会拒绝一个幽默嘴臭的活宝在任务途中和你唰唰嘴贫吐槽现状呢，他那叛逆又实干强大的摇滚青年形象，很难让人不爱。结局是你和强尼分离的时候，让玩家自己建造和强尼的感情桥梁，然后再亲自创造遗憾，只能说编剧真的很毒。dlc往日之影是一部剧情好过本体主线的紧张谍战故事，v身陷国家和公司的绞肉机，是像弥补大卫的遗憾选择救出和你情况类似的百灵鸟，把这个欺骗所有人但又本质什么都没错的姑娘送上太空，还是选择一生献身于祖国但本质是国家弃子的李德，无论如何都让玩家陷入道德困境，无情的把遗憾和满满的讽刺打在玩家的脸上，整体无疑是这部游戏锦上添花的一笔。
天我简直太爱这游戏了，10分满分，强烈安利！！！

[h1]Cyberpunk 2077 — I wasn't ready for the ending I chose.[/h1]

[b]⚠️ MAJOR SPOILERS for Cyberpunk 2077 and Phantom Liberty below.
Do not read past this line if you haven't finished the story.[/b]

I almost never write Steam reviews.

But after finishing Cyberpunk 2077, I feel like simply leaving a thumbs-up doesn't do it justice.

I started this game as a female V with a pretty clear idea of who I wanted to be: a powerful netrunner, a wealthy and experienced merc, someone who would approach Night City with a plan and eventually become a cybernetic monster who could hack anything standing in her way.

Then Johnny Silverhand happened.

At first, I hated him. Then I understood him. Then, somehow, I started becoming a little like him.

My playstyle changed completely. I stopped caring so much about having the perfect plan and started enjoying the chaos. I wanted the adrenaline. I wanted to get into fights, pull out my weapons, go loud, and just live. I started appreciating the music, the streets, the neon, the people, the little moments between missions.

Johnny didn't just become a character accompanying V.

[b]He changed V.[/b]

Then came Phantom Liberty.

Songbird's story hit differently after everything V had already been through. When I finally chose to respect her wish to live, even knowing where it could lead, something about it stuck with me.

And then I returned to V's own story.

I unlocked the secret ending.

Went into Arasaka Tower alone.

No army. No backup.

Just V.

I went in like a legend, went absolutely boom boom through the place, and eventually took down Adam Smasher.

For a moment, it felt like I'd finally become the V I had been building toward.

And then the game reminded me of the truth:

[b]It was too late.[/b]

My body was rejecting me.

I had fought through everything. I had become incredibly powerful. I had survived things that should have killed me.

And I still couldn't save myself.

I initially chose to live.

But after sitting with Johnny and talking to him, I realized something: maybe surviving wasn't necessarily the ending I wanted for V anymore.

Johnny had changed.

And so had I.

Then came that final conversation.

V and Johnny, sitting together.

Two people who started this journey wanting completely different things, somehow ending up understanding each other.

I stood up.

Johnny tried to stop me.

We talked.

And eventually, we shook hands.
No hatred. No anger. No grand speech.

Just two friends who finally understood that it was time to say goodbye.

I gave Johnny the body.
And then I watched the ending.

It broke me.
Not because it was some perfect happy ending. It wasn't.

But because it felt right.

V didn't “win.”
Johnny didn't “win.”
There wasn't some magical cure that erased everything we'd been through.

Instead, there was acceptance.
Johnny got the chance to live differently because of V.
And V got to leave behind something that mattered.

I started Cyberpunk wanting to create the strongest V possible.
I ended it realizing that strength wasn't really the point.

[b]It was about living. Loving. Changing. Letting go. And deciding what your life means when you know it won't last forever.[/b]

I don't think I could have written a better ending for my V.
I don't even want to reload and change it.
I finished everything I wanted to finish. I built the V I wanted to play. I experienced Night City. I fought like a maniac, hacked like a ghost, became a legend, met incredible characters, laughed, got angry, got attached, and eventually had to say goodbye.

When the credits rolled, I just sat there thinking:

[b]“Damn. That was a story that I played.”[/b]

Not watched.
Not read.

[b]Played.[/b]

Cyberpunk 2077 isn't just a game I'll remember for its combat, builds, graphics, or Night City.
I'll remember it because, for a little while, V felt like someone I knew.
10/10.

1) Одним из первых впечатлений от игры является её впечатляющая графика. Детально проработанный мир Найт-Сити с его неоновыми вывесками, голографическими рекламными щитами и технологическими новшествами создаёт уникальную атмосферу. Дизайн персонажей и окружения выполнен в стиле, который идеально вписывается в жанр киберпанк.

2) Сюжет игры вращается вокруг Ви, персонажа, который стремится достичь успеха в Найт-Сити. Игрокам предстоит выбирать между различными заданиями и квестами, влияющими на развитие сюжета. Персонажи проработаны до мелочей, каждый из них имеет свою уникальную историю и мотивацию. Диалоги и взаимодействия с неигровыми персонажами также на высоте.

3) Cyberpunk 2077 предлагает открытый мир, который можно исследовать по своему усмотрению. 4) Cyberpunk 2077 — это не просто игра, это погружение в уникальный мир, полный деталей и возможностей. After around 100 hours, Cyberpunk 2077 ended up becoming my second favorite game of all time and probably the best playing game I’ve ever experienced.

Night City is incredibly immersive, the characters feel like actual adults, and the writing handles some surprisingly mature themes without ever making me feel like I was being lectured. I became genuinely attached to characters like Judy and Panam, and by the end I cared enough about my V that the final decisions were legitimately difficult.

The combat was probably my favorite part. I built V into a Sandevistan katana swordswoman, and I don’t think another game has ever made me feel this good playing a sword-based character. Starting as a capable merc and eventually becoming an absolute monster who could tear through some of the strongest enemies in the setting felt incredible.

Phantom Liberty was also fantastic. Great spy-thriller story, difficult choices, excellent characters, and Dogtown was a great addition to the world.

It’s not flawless. There are occasional bugs, some missed opportunities in the story, and Somewhat Damaged suddenly turning my action RPG into hide-and-seek with an invincible janitor robot was probably my least favorite part of the entire 100 hours. 😂

But none of that comes close to outweighing everything Cyberpunk does right. I finished the game completely satisfied with my V, my choices, my romance with Judy, and the ending I received.

I don’t think I’ll immediately replay it because this playthrough feels complete. Maybe years from now. For now, I’m happy leaving Night City with one hell of a gaming experience.

Anyways, to preface this, I wanna say that I never was a fan of Sci-Fi, but I was especially never a fan of open-world urban-style environments in games (such as the GTA series). Color me surprised when I launched Cyberpunk 2077 for the first time and... got hooked immediately. And somehow I never even got bored with this game, which I usually end up doing after anywhere between 50-100 hours even if the game is very good. Many of the bad points I'm going to present here are very nitpicky, so take that into account.

Something that not everyone would do is probably playing modded on their first playthrough. I've wanted to do this with a game for some time and since Cyberpunk is a "moddable game" (not really, you have to rewrite game files), I decided to watch a video on some mods and downloaded them. I've not spoiled myself anything nor did I download any immersion breaking or completely gameplay altering mods, mainly just cosmetic and gameplay enhancing. One thing I would definitely suggest are better loot markers and especially the ability to be able to respec multiple times. The game only allows you to respec once which imo is beyond stupid - as a first time player you're bound to make a bad build and if your second build doesn't work out or end up being fun, you can... restart on a new playthrough? Yeah.

If there is one thing to fault Cyberpunk for, it has to be that the main story (base game and especially the DLC) is too short. You can spend up to 150 hours doing side content (most of which doesn't even come close to the charm of the main story) but the main story is only about 25-35 hours long for both the main game and DLC combined. There's a lot of depressing elements in the game (as usual in the cyberpunk genre) and there's also an incredible amount of morally gray areas displayed in throughout the story that you often don't know who the good guy is or what the correct option is - you often just end up picking the lesser evil or what you feel is the more correct option. The story is just so good that I'm sad for it to end so soon. I would also prefer more build options because it feels like there's not too much to pick from in the trees other than "I like this weapon and/or playstyle" - but that's the ARPG player in me speaking. Other than that, no real gripes - graphics are some of the best we've ever seen in any game period, writing is great, gameplay is awesome (even for someone that doesn't like this kind of game!) and the setting? Just perfect.

This game/the Cyberpunk TTRPG was also adapted into an anime series and the adaptation is so good and accurate I genuinely couldn't believe it on my first watch. Definitely can recommend watching before starting the game.

On a side note: Johnny Silverhand might be my new favorite character out of any series. He's incredibly well written and makes my day every single time he shows up.

All in all, if someone tells me Cyberpunk is their favorite game of all time, I wouldn't even try to argue even though it probably isn't my number 1, but it's up there alright - even as someone that shouldn't like anything about this game according to my taste. The effort that was put into this game is visible at first sight and its quality shows within minutes of play. I will wholeheartedly be recommending this game to anyone who hasn't played it, even if they're not a fan of the genre or themes just like myself, as Cyberpunk 2077 is an experience that everyone should go through in their lives.

Cyberpunk 2077 был пройден мной ещё на самом его релизе в 2020 году со всеми его техническими проблемами и с минимальными настройками графики, ведь тогда мой старый компьютер не мог нормально потянуть эту игру. Но даже несмотря на это, игра запала в душу: перед глазами предстала невероятная история с живыми и запоминающимися персонажами, стильный и технологичный мир с разнообразными активностями. И вот, стоило мне вернуться в 2026 году в уже доработанную игру, как она не просто вернула те прежние чувства, но и сумела подарить совершенно новые. Cyberpunk 2077 вновь удивила.

[h1]Долгожданное будущее. Или же нет?[/h1]
В этот раз CD Projekt Red адаптировали не серию книг, как это было с «Ведьмаком», а настольную ролевую игру, предложив свой взгляд на вселенную Cyberpunk. Разработчики сделали всё под стать своему фирменному стилю: масштаб, безрадостный реализм, глубокие истории, сложные моральные выборы. И на этот раз нас встречает мрачная антиутопия будущего, где мегакорпорации сопоставимы с целыми государствами, технологии ушли далеко вперёд, импланты стали частью повседневности, а тема утраты личности выходит на первый план.

В таком мире и строится история наёмника Ви — главного героя, который мечтал попасть в высшую лигу и прославиться, но волею судеб оказывается на грани смерти, и теперь он вынужден бороться за свою жизнь. За развитием сюжета весьма интересно наблюдать, он богат на различного рода события, в нём достаточно много сильных моментов (чего только стоит развитие отношений Ви и Джонни), и их по-настоящему проживаешь. А в конце остаётся горькое послевкусие, ведь в игре есть несколько концовок, каждая из которых со своими хорошими и не очень последствиями.  Помимо этого, в игре достаточно много разнообразных побочных заданий, некоторые из них оказываются даже интереснее основного сюжета.

И, конечно же, нельзя не отметить персонажей — они живые, каждый со своей историей, со своими проблемами. К ним привязываешься, за них переживаешь. С некоторыми из них можно завязать роман и впоследствии проводить время вместе. Сюжет и персонажи — это, вероятно, лучшая часть игры.

Атмосфера здесь выдержана отлично и построена на смеси технологичности и социального упадка. Эта двойственность во многом достигается за счёт самого города Найт-Сити, где богатые кварталы соседствуют с трущобами. И город, наравне с сюжетом, прекрасно передаёт гнетущую атмосферу безнадёги с редкими проблесками надежды. Мир, кстати, наполнен различной необязательной информацией, изучая которую можно чуточку лучше узнать его историю.

Игра обладает и глубокой философской основой, затрагивая множество тем: потеря человечности, утрата личности, расслоение общества, превращение человека в расходный материал, бессмысленность борьбы с системой и бессмысленность погони за славой. И это не просто выдуманные проблемы, многие из них уже проявляются в нашей реальности. А потому игра проводит через всё это, затрагивая каждую из них и ещё глубже погружая в свою атмосферу.

Кроме этого в игре повсеместно прослеживается серая мораль: здесь каждый руководствуется своими личными целями, а игроку приходится делать выбор без однозначно правильного ответа.  В игре нет деления на абсолютное добро или зло — каждый выбор имеет как достоинства, так и недостатки — а потому можно отыгрывать Ви по-разному, исходя из собственных моральных принципов.

Саундтрек игры заслуживает отдельного внимания — он, без преувеличения сказать, шикарен. Он отлично подходит к каждой ситуации, будь то экшен-сцены или драматические моменты. И музыка здесь не просто фон, она усиливает эмоции, делая игру ещё более живой и запоминающейся. Некоторые композиции однозначно останутся в памяти.
[h2]Phantom Liberty[/h2]
В 2023 году вышло крупное дополнение к игре, и оно приятно удивило: лор игры был немного расширен, появился новый район города, новые задания, персонажи и полноценная сюжетная линия, наполненная политическими дрязгами. Помимо различных исходов расширения, DLC привносит новую концовку для оригинальной истории.
Дополнение ничуть не уступает оригинальной игре: в нём также хватает внезапных поворотов, трогательных моментов, исследований и интересных заданий. И оно ещё больше пронизано серой моралью — это даже добралось до простых необязательных заказов. А потому дополнение вновь вынуждает принимать не самые однозначные решения.

[h2]А что по недостаткам?[/h2]
Ох уж эти баги… На релизе игра была технической катастрофой — багов и прочих проблем было предостаточно: одни были безобидными и даже забавными, другие же могли помешать прохождению игры, а то и вовсе испортить впечатление от игры. Эта тема была настолько острой, что игровые баги стали отдельным элементом мем-фольклора. Но игра преобразилась, а вместе с тем были исправлены многие её проблемы. И всё же баги по-прежнему встречаются, это стоит иметь в виду.
Но помимо очевидного можно отметить слабый искусственный интеллект, ограниченный в плане интерактивности открытый мир, редкие сюжетные дыры, а также иллюзорность выбора. Хотя это скорее придирки, ведь сила игры прежде всего в её истории.
[h2]Never Fade Away[/h2]
Cyberpunk 2077 — это отличная игра. Она прошла долгий путь от неудачного запуска до своего искупления. И хоть игра даже сейчас далеко не идеальна в техническом плане, в плане нарратива, визуала, атмосферы и погружения здесь почти всё прекрасно. А вариативный геймплей позволяет проходить игру в любом стиле и в своё удовольствие. И игра действительно захватывает с головой, её проживаешь, пропуская через себя все эти эмоции. В неё хочется играть снова и снова, а после финала внутри остаётся пустота, ведь с ней не хочется расставаться. Cyberpunk 2077 — та самая игра, которая никогда не исчезнет из памяти.

Cyberpunk é um jogo difícil de se avaliar. Pra mim, é praticamente impossível não o comparar a The WItcher 3, então acho melhor arrancar o band-aid e começar por isso.
Enquanto The Witcher 3 deixou sua marca na indústria pela sua revolução como jogo de mundo aberto, Cyberpunk 2077 (inicialmente) deixou sua marca como uma das maiores decepções da década. Falar da catástrofe que foi esse jogo no seu lançamento é chover no molhado, então eu vou focar nos defeitos e problemas que eu ainda encontrei 6 anos após o jogo ser lançado, e um ano após ser finalizado. 

- Primeiro ponto: Otimização. Apesar do meu computador não ter um processador tão bom quanto o recomendado, o meu hardware sobra com folga dos requisitos mínimos. Logicamente, eu deveria ser capaz de rodar tudo no médio e pegar 60+ FPS, certo? Nem tanto. Colocando tudo no baixo (a ponto de não conseguir ver meu personagem no espelho), em algumas regiões do jogo eu mal chegava a 50 FPS. Além disso o jogo crashou várias vezes, e tiveram bugs ocasionais bem chatos também. 
- Segundo ponto: O fator "Role-Playing". Cyberpunk é baseado em um TTRPG já existente, enquanto The Witcher é uma continuação de uma saga de livros. Mesmo assim, The Witcher consegue ser um RPG muito melhor do que Cyberpunk, e isso pra mim é uma baita infelicidade. O impacto que o seu personagem tem em Night City é bem pobre em comparação a The Witcher, visto que em Cyberpunk tomar diferentes decisões não muda muita coisa na história principal (com exceção do final). 

Minha crítica se encerra dizendo que toda review negativa de Cyberpunk é compreensível e justificável, visto que a primeira impressão que esse jogo causou é algo difícil de se desvincular, e que ele não possui todas as ferramentas necessárias pra provar que deixou 100% de ser essa catástrofe.

Agora, por que eu estou recomendando um jogo que eu acabei de descer a lenha por 3 parágrafos? Porque apesar do que eu pontuei, minha experiência com Cyberpunk foi EXTREMAMENTE positiva, e eu me sentiria mal de fazer uma review totalmente enviesada. A gameplay é extremamente divertida, as missões são incrivelmente interessantes e profundas, e a história principal é uma obra-prima; na minha opinião. Todos os personagens que eu encontrei foram marcantes de alguma forma, e a DLC (apesar de mal-otimizada) é a melhor já feita pela CDPR. Cyberpunk me proporcionou uma das experiências mais marcantes que eu tive com um mundo fictício de videogame. Mesmo com 100 horas, e praticamente 100% das conquistas, ainda tem muita coisa que eu posso fazer, que eu perdi, e que eu nunca descobri em Night City. Cyberpunk está longe de ser um jogo perfeito, mas a experiência que eu tive com ele foi quase que isso. Uma pena que esse jogo pode proporcionar experiências individuais tão divergentes por causa da cagada que a CDPR fez quando lançou. Pelo menos eles sabem da besteira que fizeram e demonstram ter aprendido com ela. 

Analisando friamente,  eu acho o jogo um 7,5/10 ou 8/10. Minha experiência, no entanto, foi um 10 redondo. E ah, menção honrosa ao anime Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, que resgatou essa IP pra CDPR de maneiras inimagináveis.

如果让我用一个词形容《赛博朋克2077》，那一定是“矛盾的美”。它像夜之城的霓虹灯——表面炫目到刺眼，深处却藏着锈迹斑斑的钢筋与潮湿的眼泪。而正是这种撕裂感，让我彻底沉迷其中。
从踏入夜之城的第一秒起，CDPR就用细节堆砌出一个令人窒息的未来。全息广告在雨中扭曲，义体医生的工作台沾着血渍，街角的流浪汉和公司精英共享同一片肮脏的空气。这不是“干净”的未来，而是一个充满人性挣扎的活体城市。光追加持下，每一帧都像电影截图，但真正震撼的是那些不经意的瞬间：垃圾堆旁抽烟的NPC，小巷里突然爆发的械斗，甚至风掠过高楼时金属的呜咽声——世界不是背景，而是角色本身。
主线关于“生存与自我”的探讨足够深刻，但真正让我破防的是支线。帕南的流浪者家族、朱迪的底层反抗、强尼·银手刻在记忆里的愤怒…每个角色都像一把钥匙，打开夜之城的另一面黑暗。尤其是与强尼的共生关系，从对抗到共情，到最后模糊了“谁才是这具身体的主人”——这种叙事张力，是近年RPG中少见的灵魂拷问。
黑客、近战、枪械、潜行…Build自由度极高。你可以用病毒瘫痪整栋大楼的安保，也能靠螳螂刀在血雾中杀出重围。虽然初期战斗手感略有生涩，但技能树成型后的爽快感无与伦比。更惊喜的是，你的选择真的在改变世界：一句对话可能让任务走向截然不同的结局，一个不经意的善举或许在几十小时后以意想不到的方式回响。
我承认，首发时的灾难让人心碎。但2023年的2.0更新+《往日之影》DLC，让这部作品真正涅槃。优化大幅改善，警察系统、义体重做、车辆战斗…几乎每个痛点都被打磨成亮点。现在的它，配得上“完成品”三个字。
它或许仍有小Bug，驾驶手感依然飘，但当你站在来生酒吧的屋顶，看着全息鲸鱼游过摩天楼，听着《I Really Want to Stay at Your House》的旋律响起——你会明白，这不是一款游戏，而是一场关于人类如何在科技洪流中寻找自我的寓言。如果你愿意给夜之城一次机会，它会把你的心踩碎，再亲手用霓虹线缝起来。
推荐给爱深度叙事的RPG玩家、赛博朋克文化爱好者、愿意为沉浸感牺牲“完美体验”的冒险家。

アニメ「エッジランナーズ」を視聴してドはまりしたのでゲームもプレイ
公式引用あらすじ
巨大企業とギャングが支配する、暴力とネオンに満ちた近未来の巨大都市ナイトシティ。主人公Ｖは生死をかけた仕事の最中、50年前に死亡したテロリスト、ジョニー・シルヴァーハンドの精神を脳に移植されてしまうが...

[h2] いいところ [/h2]
■圧倒的な作りこみ
ナイトシティの煌びやかな摩天楼と退廃的なスラムが混在するカオスな雰囲気、アウトランズの荒廃した砂漠、そこに息づく人々、すべてが作りこまれすぎて本当にその世界にいるように感じられる
そこら辺を走り回っているだけでかなり楽しい。ファストトラベルあまり使わずバイクで爆走してた
サブクエストも一つ一つしっかりストーリーがあって世界を深堀っている。ただのお使いのような無駄なサブクエスト全くないの本当にすごい

■キャラクター
登場人物は基本悪い奴ばっかりだけど、どこか憎めなくて、それぞれに考え方が異なっていて人間臭くてよかった。みんな命より大事なものがあって、それを守るために手段を選ばない感じがカッコイイ
あと和訳も全く違和感なく、吹き替え映画を見てるような感覚で楽しめた。海外特有の言い回し好き
主要キャラに関しては、本当に友人や恋人ができたような没入感があった

■ストーリー
DLC含め息をつかせないストーリー。海外ドラマのようなクリフハンガーが多くあり続きが気になるし、世界観も相まって緊張感と迫力がすごい。複数あるエンディングもハッピーエンドではなく、何かを得て何かを捨てるような感じになっているもの好み
全体的に言えることだけど、一人称であることで没入感や緊張感が増していると思う

■ビルド幅
アニメ勢なのでデイビッドよろしく近接サンデヴィスタンビルドで超気持ちよくプレイ
ネットランナーや射撃特化、武器も色々幅があってよい◎

[h2] わるいところ [/h2]
■バグ
進行不能バグなどはなかったが、ホロコールが使えない（セーブ＆ロードで解決）、車に乗ったときにバグる（急発進して追突、Vが車の上に立って運転）などちょいちょいバグがあった
この規模のオープンワールドにしては全然許容範囲かなと思いますが

■クラッシュ
セーブデータのロードのタイミングでちょくちょくクラッシュした。プレイ中にはない
仮にプレイ中に発生してもファイルを分けたオートセーブがマメに入るので問題ないと思う

■取り返しのつかない要素
良くも悪くも自分で選択し物語を決めるPRGなので、選択次第で人が死ぬ、アイテムが手に入らなくなるなど気になる人は気になる要素かなと思う。悪魔エンドの条件以外はトロフィーには影響しない

■右側通行
海外なので右側通行なんだよな～～～～ゲーム内では全然慣れたけど、現実で日本歩くと違和感あってやばい

[h2] まとめ [/h2]
まごうことなき神ゲー
自分はすべてのアプデが終わってからプレイしたので、不満はほとんどなく快適にプレイできた
洋ゲーやオープンワールド敬遠してる人にもおすすめのPRG

Played it once. Played it twice. Now I’ve played it three times.

And honestly? Cyberpunk 2077 just keeps getting better.

The graphics are absolutely amazing, but what really stands out to me is the weather system. Night City looks incredible when it rains, especially at night—the whole city just pops. Then you have the sandstorms, which are genuinely blinding and add another layer of atmosphere to the world. It makes Night City feel alive.

My third playthrough, playing as Female V — Streetkid, has been my favourite so far, especially alongside Phantom Liberty. The combat and cyberware have always been some of the best parts of the game for me. There are so many different builds you can make, and experimenting with them never really gets old.

And then there's the story.

What an emotional rollercoaster.

Even after three playthroughs, the story still manages to hit. The characters, the choices, the highs and the lows—it’s one of those games where you can know what's coming and still feel it when it happens.

Now I can only hope the second game gives us more.

And by more, I mean MORE.

Give me more flying cars. Let us actually use them properly. Give us the possibility of becoming a cyberpsycho if we push our cyberware too far. More futuristic weapon technology. More insane outfits and cyberware customisation.

And honestly, why stop at Night City?

Give us more than one playable city.

I'd love to see different futuristic cities with their own cultures, gangs, architecture and dangers. And while we're dreaming, I'd absolutely love to see Braindance assassinations or missions built around them.

Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way, and after playing it three times, I'm still finding reasons to come back.

CD Projekt Red, give us more cyberpunk.

10/10 — Would chrome myself again.

[h2] Beautiful, but hollow [/h2]

I really wish Steam would let you leave mixed reviews.

Cyberpunk is a game I wish I could love more than I did, truly. And I wish the the things barring me from loving it more weren't so fundamental and glaring.
This game has had a notoriously rough development, with a lot of content and mechanics being changed,  cut, or otherwise altered, and boy, it shows.

To start from afar, visually, the game is absolutely stunning, Night City is beautiful in a gritty, back-alley beauty sort of way. The neon, the graffiti, the ads blasting everywhere, the oppressive feeling of being caged in by the towering megabuildings, it all works wonderfully. From a graphical standpoint, the game is masterfully done. And yet all this beauty feels strangely empty. The world is densely populated by NPCs, and yet sometimes you feel completely alone in this massive bustling city, seeing as most of those NPCs feel like soulless set pieces and the city itself, despite being sprawling and huge in size, lacks interactivity with most of it. Environmental story-telling moments are few and far between, and as a result the world ends up feeling extremely hollow despite its beauty. 

Gameplay-wise the game is [i] fine [/i]. The shooting, melee combat and hacking all work and perform about as well as one'd expect, with very few issues that I experienced personally. The driving though, oh THE DRIVING. You get sorta used to it after a while, but most vehicles (cars being the worst offenders) feel like you're driving on an oily kitchen floor if you so much as tap your finger a second too long on the A or D keys. It's clunky, uncomfortable and can and WILL fuck you over in some situations, even going so far as forcing you to reload. The police's AI in this game is abysmally bad, to the point one might even call it utterly braindead. They either shoot at you to submission or lose interest within a minute, that is if they even bother chasing you to begin with. That, or they fire off at you for inching a foot too close to their personal space, taking it as a monumental personal offence worthy of killing a man over. Oh and there are bugs. Lots. Less than on release, that's for sure, but do expect to have to reload saves because something broke to an unfixable degree. It'll happen sooner or later.

The story is where the game both shines and completely falls flat on occasion. Let me preface by saying that the RPG elements in this game are limited to none-existent. You choice of lifepath will warrant you the occasional dialogue option or, rarely, an alternative path to completing a quest objective (note: I have played with the Corpo lifepath, so I can't attest to how much the Streetkid or Nomad lifepaths affect gameplay. It is my assumption that they're mostly the same), but not much more. V isn't an avatar you create to project yourself onto, he's much more of Geralt in that regard - he has a story and a personality and your inputs into that story will affect your actual character very, very little. Just the main story (disregarding side content for a second) is fine for the most part (if a little rushed in the intro, the Jackie montage could've been a whole series of quests giving us a  reason as to why we actually care for him, instead of just being told that), if it wasn't for one huge, glaring Samurai in your soup (and no, I do not mean Takemura. He's alright, actually).

Johnny Silverhand has got to be one of the most unlikable videogame characters I've ever had the displeasure of experiencing. Now, I get it. He's an asshole, stays and asshole and you're meant to slowly understand where he's coming from and sympathize with him or at least his cause. I found those moments of clarity where he isn't actively being a nuisance, brat or outright asshole very few and far between and not nearly enough to make me want to [spoiler] give my body up to him. He had his life, he screwed up. V isn't responsible for letting him have a second chance to fix those screw-ups, when he himself barely had a chance to live his own life. [/spoiler]. The Relic being a ticking time bomb that supposedly gives you very little time to solve that little problem before you're dead creates an extreme narrative dissonance where the forced sense of urgency really doesn't hold any water considering we have this huge world to explore and a whole map worth of stuff to do and clear out, who cares that we'll be dead in two weeks?

Now where the game really, really shines: the side quests. This game has some of the most interesting, creative and tightly scripted side content, which seems to be something CDPR truly excels at. Every single one of the 4 potential love interests are immaculately written (I will accept no River slander) and you truly feel like the hardships they face together with V bring them closer, and the love lines between them don't feel forced. Beyond that, the world is chock full of interesting side stories that on occasion are leagues better than even the main story. These kept me invested and are one of the main reasons I don't regret having experienced this game. Kerry Eurodyne has got to be one of my absolute favourite characters in gaming and has become a ray of sunshine in this bleak, depressing world from the very first moment he appeared. Best boyfriend ever, no one even comes close.
The side content involving gigs, cyberpsychos and NCPD missions however felt extremely repetitive and, after a while, very boring. It's only so fun killing the same 3-10 goons for so long. Sure, you can do it with different cyberware and weapons, but ultimately it still feel mind-numbing.

Overall, Cyberpunk is a game I desperately wanted to love more. It's beautiful, atmospheric, and at its best genuinely brilliant, especially when it comes to its characters and side stories. But beneath all the neon and chrome, there's a hollowness that I couldn't ignore. Too much of the game feels like a glimpse of what could have been rather than what it ended up being. I don't regret playing it, and I certainly don't think it's a bad game by any margin, but I can't help feeling that it falls painfully short of its own potential.

tl;dr: 7/10, good, but could've been so much better

I first played Cyberpunk 2077 when the COVID lockdowns began in March 2020. My second playthrough was around three and a half years ago, and now I've returned for a third run, this time with Phantom Liberty. After more than 60 hours, I'm close to finishing the DLC, and it's interesting to see how much the game has changed.

The gameplay is far easier than I remember. You can now reach 20/20/20/15/5 in your attributes, skill progression is no longer heavily restricted by attribute levels, and some builds are absurdly overpowered. My Netrunner build with Overclock and Legendary Synapse Burnout effectively gives me unlimited RAM, allowing me to chain quickhacks almost indefinitely. Even on the highest difficulty, I was able to survive MaxTac for several minutes after reaching a five-star wanted level. Once your build comes together, very little in the game can challenge you.

The biggest problem, however, isn't the balance—although I don't think it should be possible to nearly max out every attribute—it's the structure. The game constantly tells you that V is dying and has very little time left to live, yet it expects you to spend dozens of hours completing side jobs, gigs, races, and other activities. The urgency of the main story clashes with the open-world design, hurting both immersion and pacing.

CD Projekt Red promised an RPG but ultimately delivered something much closer to GTA with skills and light RPG mechanics. I believe the game would have been stronger if it had fully embraced replayability instead of trying to let players experience almost everything in a single playthrough.

Imagine spending the first ten hours actually living through V's memories instead of watching them in a short montage. You would build a real relationship with Jackie, making the events at Konpeki Plaza far more emotional. After that, the story could branch into distinct paths focused on Takemura, Panam, Judy, Songbird, or another lead. Some paths could end in failure and V's death, while only one would reveal the true ending. Instead of encouraging players to ignore Hanako at Embers for dozens of hours, the game should push you to commit to a path and accept the consequences. The objective should be discovering the "true" ending through multiple playthroughs—perhaps one where V and Johnny find a genuine way to coexist instead of one inevitably replacing the other.

Only after surviving should the world fully open up. At that point, spending time on side quests, gigs, cyberpsycho contracts, and other optional activities would feel natural instead of undermining the story's urgency. The open world would become an epilogue, allowing V to build a reputation after escaping death rather than while supposedly having only weeks left to live.

This is exactly why Phantom Liberty works so well. Rather than trying to complete everything before advancing the story, you pursue one lead and see where it takes you, naturally encouraging you to explore Dogtown, complete gigs, and take on side quests. It is, in my opinion, the game design Cyberpunk 2077 should have embraced from the beginning.

Phantom Liberty is easily the strongest part of the game. Idris Elba delivers an excellent performance as Solomon Reed, and the writing is consistently stronger than in the base game. Even the optional blue side quests feel meaningful. One of my favorite missions was choosing Hansen's successor. If the main game had maintained this level of storytelling and pacing throughout, it would have been significantly better.

Another major missed opportunity is cyberware. The world constantly talks about the dangers of replacing your body with machines and descending into cyberpsychosis, yet the player never truly experiences that. You can become almost as heavily augmented as Adam Smasher, but your appearance barely changes. Looking in a mirror still shows a mostly ordinary human. You can even remove Gorilla Arms at will, despite having replaced your biological limbs. Cyberware should be be visually reflected on your body, removing major implants should have meaningful consequences, and excessive augmentation should eventually trigger its own storyline or gameplay mechanics related to cyberpsychosis.

Cyberpunk 2077 has improved enormously since launch. It now offers excellent visuals, memorable characters, and an outstanding expansion. At the same time, many of its biggest weaknesses were never technical. They stem from fundamental design decisions that patches could never fully solve. It is a very good game, but it still falls short of being the deep role-playing experience it once promised.

One of the best games I have ever played

I really enjoyed Cyberpunk 2077. The first thing that impressed me was the graphics — Night City looks absolutely amazing, especially on high settings. The world is incredibly atmospheric, and it's actually fun to just drive around and explore the city.

The story is also fantastic. The characters, missions, and overall plot are very engaging, and some moments are genuinely memorable.

I also have to mention **Phantom Liberty**. For me, it's one of the best expansions that could have been made for this game. The new story, characters, and atmosphere made the game even better.

Of course, I can't ignore the fact that the game had a lot of bugs and technical problems when it was first released. However, the developers didn't abandon the game and continued improving it. Nowadays, most of the major problems have been fixed, and the game is much more stable and enjoyable.

The developers really did a great job. They managed to turn the game into something that can now be considered one of the best games of its generation. Despite the problems at launch, the final result is absolutely amazing.

The only major downside is that the game is quite demanding on hardware, especially if you want to play on high settings with all the fancy effects.

Other than that, everything is awesome. The graphics are amazing, the story is amazing, and Phantom Liberty is on another level.

Wasn't able to turn off all the swearing so if that's something you're not into, might want to give this one a pass.

[b]Story[/b]
The relationship between V and Johnny is the backbone of the whole game, and it earns that place. Two guarded, difficult people forced to share headspace against their will slowly become something closer to reflections of each other, and watching my own choices start drifting toward his worldview as the game went on was one of the more rewarding character arcs I've experienced in an RPG. Where the story lands depends heavily on the path you choose, and the ending I landed on had real emotional weight, enough that I'm still turning it over. Phantom Liberty adds another wrinkle to that decision, offering a very different flavor of resolution that changes what "winning" even means for V. I won't get into specifics, but be ready for the tone to shift from triumphant to bittersweet depending on what you choose.

[b]Romance and character writing[/b]
Every major character arc is well written, but the romance system has one structural problem: V can juggle multiple relationships at once with no consequence, and there's no clean way to end one you've started. I don't regret the relationship I pursued, but it eventually stopped fitting the version of V I'd been playing, and there's no graceful exit once you're in. The system needed a forced choice between competing love interests, the way most games with romance options handle it. Letting V run every option in parallel undercuts the writing invested in any single one of them.

[b]Themes and world[/b]
Night City doesn't feel like science fiction so much as a preview. Strip away the chrome and the setting's corporate overreach and erosion of privacy already track with things happening in the real world right now. That's what makes the dystopia land: it's not abstract.

Where the world falls short is scale. Night City needed to be bigger, with more districts and side content, and more importantly, the choices you make in those side quests needed to ripple outward further than they do. One good example: an aggressive choice early on can permanently lock you out of a useful vendor down the line, and choices with the major cast can derail entire storylines if you push too hard. But the smaller fixer gigs feel weightless by comparison, no real way to screw them up or steer them differently, so they end up feeling like filler next to the character-driven content.

[b]Presentation[/b]
Visually and sonically this is a genuinely impressive game. The one oddity: certain characters occasionally sound like their lines were re-recorded in a different session, a noticeably different mic or room tone mid-conversation. Minor, but noticeable once you catch it.

[b]Combat and builds[/b]
I ran a Ninja Guerrilla Netrunner build with smart weapons, mostly because precision aiming on a controller isn't much fun, and smart weapons essentially give you soft auto-aim. Late game, popping Overclock and chaining high-cost quickhacks across five or six enemies before needing to fall back and recharge was some of the most satisfying combat in the game. Once Overclock drops, though, smart weapons don't hit hard enough to carry you, so it becomes a rhythm of burst and retreat rather than sustained firefighting.

[b]Progression[/b]
The perk and cyberware systems are well tuned. Nothing felt like a dead pick, just a mix of strong choices for your build and traps to avoid for someone else's. Leveling up never turned into a chore, which is a real accomplishment for a game this deep into its systems.

[b]Performance[/b]
Most people probably won't run into this, but worth flagging: after extended play sessions the game can start to stutter and lag on my end (Ryzen 7 3700X, RX 6600XT), even on the Steam Deck preset. I haven't dug into whether it's thermal, memory-related, or something else, but a quick restart clears it up for another few hours. Not a dealbreaker, just something to know if it happens to you.

[b]Phantom Liberty[/b]
Phantom Liberty's story stands with the best writing in the whole game. It pushes the base game's corporate greed theme all the way up into the highest levels of government, making clear the rot in Night City was never limited to corpo boardrooms. Dogtown feels like a natural extension of the city rather than a bolted-on expansion, the same power struggles wearing a different uniform. The new mechanics, especially the relic skill tree, give late-game builds the capstone abilities the base game was missing, the finishing layer the core game needed.

The ending choices genuinely reshape what winning looks like for V, and unlike most DLC epilogues, they don't feel like a footnote to the base game's story, they feel load-bearing. I won't spoil what those choices are, but expect to sit with them for a while after the credits roll.

[b]Final verdict[/b]
Recommended without hesitation. The base game and Phantom Liberty together tell one of the more thoughtful stories about power, identity, and compromise that I've played in years, backed by combat and progression systems that stayed fun for over a hundred hours straight. The world could stand to be bigger and some of the side content needed sharper teeth, but that's a minor complaint next to everything this game gets right.

Bought this game a few years ago, while it was still buggy and didn't expect much, except the graphics. So I ran a few benchmarks, tried starting the game and wasn't impressed by the first hour or two. 
But got some free time to play some games this year and decided to try it again. And wow what a wonderful game it is! Not gonna lie, first ~5-10 hours was still boring because of the amount of the tutorials, talking (without understanding anything about the world yet), mid fights (before you figure out the perks and invest some points into one of the trees) and pretty sluggish driving. 
But after you get thru the early game, everything starts to feel much more engaging - fights becomes cool after you learn enough perks for a style you prefer, quests feel well-written and often give you a choice and multiple endings (esp. in the Phantom Liberty), you even can get used to the driving. 
Atmosphere and the attention to details are pretty high, but not rockstar-level. Yet in some aspects I like this one more. 
Played 172 hours so far and still not finished the main quest (do not want to rush it). Overall very rich experience, a lot of things to do, very interesting perk and weapon systems, some quests are amazing (some are just okay, but still rewarding), graphics and mocap animations are top quality (except transitions between some animations). 
Ofc there are some downsides too: there are still some bugs, esp. visual, but very rarely game-breaking, enemies ain't always smart, so you can abuse them to win (so if you do, try playing on Very Hard), not all of your actions are ack. by quest-givers, immersion tends to break by visual bugs, distant objects rendering, NPC/cars pops (in and out), floating objects and enemies, etc... which means the game is not perfect, don't expect it to be and you'll be enjoying it! 
P.S. Phantom Liberty is a side-DLC, which means you can buy it at any point of your main quest (I bought it in the middle), it unlocks DogTown for you and lots of its quests, which are wonderful and focused on the gray-moral all-in, including the main quest of the DLC. Best DLC I've ever seen - definitely worth its cost maybe even 2 times over.

Just finished platinum it.

Best experience I've ever had, not even exaggerating.

IMMERSION
I don't think I could've gotten as immersed as I got if it weren't for path tracing, I loved every moment of it, everything was a cinematic experience, from free roaming the city, to being in quests with hand made scenarios planned to look a certain way. City felt alive most of the game, if I wasn't grinding it, it could've stayed that way from start to finish.

I don't know if I would've played this game if I couldn't run it in max graphics, it was a deal breaker in the experience for me.

CHARACTERS
Awesome personalities, stories, depth, interactions, secrets. Expressions, voices, and body language was worth of an Oscar for each one.

WORLD
Big, full of mini stories, some repetitive (like NPCD scanners) but they are there to just do them on the go, by stumbling upon them, if you go grinding them they become repetitive quite fast, still there where some interesting ones with cool rewards. City is beautiful at day and at night it's just visual candy everywhere, neon lights reflecting in the pavement while you take a ride to some shady biz, having the radio on and hearing the muffled city outside your car is something GTA could never replicate, those twisted highways, weird streets, digital crosswalks and all of that are great.
The story of the world as it became to be is also interesting, but I didn't read all about it, but it was awesome seeing the world develop from your actions, I stood a lot of minutes hearing the news channel on the elevator back to my apartment, and seeing the multiple ad planted everywhere, on signs, machines, etc.

GAMEPLAY
I've never been a singleplayer shooter guy, the most close of an experience I've had is Borderlands 2 and I could never get into it, I just grew bored. This though, was entertaining, I don't know if for the immersion, for the cyberware and skill tree, or because it was satisfying shooting enemies, but I just had a good time.
Didn't like katana builds, gameplay felt stiff, didn't like hacking builds neither monowire because it wasn't satisfying, also didn't go assault rifle or shotgun route, I liked gunslinger because I always liked heads popping and precise shooting (killing floor made me that way), but I gave shootguns a try, and they are quite funny too.

Cyberware is another game completely, I like sandevistan and camo, playing with stealth was fun, but I just resorted to seeing a build online, didn't wanted to risk committing to something I wouldn't like, and it was a good call, though stressing because I had to spoil myself a little in advance because I was scared ot miss some important weapon, or messing my attributes and that limits experimentation, if a lot of things weren't locked, they wouldn't feel so special, but also makes your build quite linear and can't change more than 1 time, and there not being a new game + there's not much motivation to start a new run to test another build, unless you mod the game to revive it.

One thing I hated the most is fall damage, I feel there was a point where I should be able to fall from a rooftop and the floor will break instead of me, but maybe I had the wrong Cyberware.

Ah, and the other thing I hated the most, is that when a NPC from a quest is talking to you, and walking you to somewhere, your walking speed is faster than them, and if you walk behind them, that's another walking speed, that's still faster than them, but if you enable walking, you're too slow, so that did break immersion at some points where I could be walking slowly, hearing them and admiring the scenery whilst lore was dropped, but I just kept orbiting the NPCS to make up for the speed.

STORY
Good story, good messages, a lot of endings, an awesome DLC that adds content like if it where a new game. I couldn't sympathize with every character or situation, but V was an awesome protagonist, and the variety of decisions you can make and the impact they have really keeps you thinking like if you where taking decisions in real life. Each ending taking half an hour, up to an hour and a half to complete demonstrates just how much the developers cared for this game, each ending has such an unique closure and gives you so many different emotions.]

Without spoiling too much, the one that kept me thinking the most is when you have a talk with misty in the staircase in The Tower ending.



10/10 experience overall. I had 3 or 4 crashes, saved scummed like crazy (510 manual saves), looted most of the iconic items I could, drive through all the city, tried every interaction that gave me curiosity and I'm satisfied, I started seeing the stitches of the game more closely to the end, but even in that moment I had a good time every moment. Didn't planned to leave a review this long neither to fragment it, don't even gonna read it again and correct it or whatever, just wanted to give this game a good review, it deserves it, truly happy to see a game come back from the ashes like No Mans Sky.

No cyberpunk, tu é MORALMENTE OBRIGADO pegar um carro e ir até o seu objetivo, mesmo estando a 5KM de você. Tu dirige olhando para a cidade, para os prédios, estabelecimentos... e fica pensando, "como estão as coisas ali dentro? As pessoas dos prédios estão olhando para mim? O que elas estão fazendo?" -- sem parar na cidade de tirar o fôlego, é gostoso e prazeroso atravessar o mapa com um veículo.

Nesse jogo, assim como em The Witcher, as escolhas finais que você decide para os personagens secundários dão PESO. Tu, pode deixar um político totalmente paranoico, pode quebrar o coração de uma mulher, ou pode somente deixar os dois se f* e pronto. Total liberdade. 

Atrelado com uma EXPANSÃO FENOMENAL, a história é enriquecida. Um pequeno spoiler, vá pelo caminho do Reed, não porquê é moral ou superior, mas por conta do tamanho do conteúdo das missões que serão apresentadas -- tu saí de uma porradaria braba, para uma missão Alien-Style no final (que é uma puta missão e tem uma PUTA LORE). 

100/10, gostaria de mais uma expansão e estou ansioso para o Cyberpunk 2.

[i] Alright, so I think it's worth mentioning that I actually have 200+ hours, but I migrated to steam to cut down on the amount of launchers I need to use. [/i]

Overall, cyberpunk is in my top 5 (in no particular order). The world - I don't think I fast travelled once on my first playthrough, the map, the music, the visuals, the voice acting - all are absolutely top notch, and there is only an extreme few games that can compete with it in these aspects. Also, going with the first-person perspective exclusively made the sense of scale and immersion so much better. 

It's definitely a unique experience, and you could easily end up with 60+ hours of high-quality content by the end of a playthrough.

However, there are some aspects where this game shows rare and eyebrow-raising cracks:
The story is phenomenal for 95% of it, but CDPR leaned too heavily into the [spoiler] "there are no happy endings" [/spoiler] part, even if it goes against common sense, which means that there are a few moments in one or two endings that make you question the writing, in a "Huh? But why?" way (the expansion is the biggest offender here, though). It can also be a bit too on the rails to keep the story going. The main story is also oddly short if you count its hours separately, I have a feeling that they turned some of its parts into side quests, which doesn't really impact you if you play it mindfully and not just blindly rushing, but it's worth keeping in mind anyway.
Same with a few characters - consistently great until they briefly aren't - but this is an even smaller problem. Except Claire, fuck that guy overall, [spoiler] asks to do one thing to make you interested then changes mind near the end, and you have to see that complaining mug every time you visit Afterlife. [/spoiler]
By RPG standards, the gameplay is amazing: fast paced, diverse, fluid. Since 2.0 skills actually unlock different abilities, instead of being mostly +15%, yet they tried too hard to balance it, making every progression path yield roughly the same effectiveness in combat (unless you straight up pick random stuff).

For me the biggest problem in the whole game is probably just one specific change that they made after release: 
Since 2.0 (or 1.6 I can't recall) enemy auto scaling was introduced. No it cannot be turned off like in The Witcher 3. Which results in absurd situations where a bum in some back alley of a starter area deals roughly the same % of damage (relatively to your HP) both at level 5 and 50; or that you can go to the "dangerous" areas of the city where people are armed to the teeth and have a stupid amount of implants, and put up a fight even when [i] you [/i] are the bum in question. Thus, making the skill selection matter even less, with implants providing the vast majority of the combat potential.

2077称不上是我体验过的最好一批开放世界游戏， [b]游戏赛博朋克+开放世界的结合能看出遇到了不少挑战，但它确实在我脑海里留下了难忘的余韵，是一部我很喜欢的作品 [/b]——它呈现给我一个喧哗浮躁、光怪陆离的新奇世界，这里充满不公、糜烂腐朽、醉生梦死，却又歌颂反抗精神，它为我带来了数个印象深刻的人物，尤其是强尼·银手。

我们先聊聊“问题”吧。

 [b]其实2077在游戏开始的最初是相当令人震撼的 [/b]：以前我接触的开放世界或者欧美RPG游戏，较多是以西方奇幻为题材（代表如上古卷轴、巫师3），即使是科幻题材，末日（如辐射4）和太空（如质量效应）也更常见。 [b]赛博朋克+开放世界的组合是我第一次见，那种高科技低生活、看似绚烂实则糜烂、大公司掌控一切的世界，从小说、动画、独立游戏中猛然鲜活起来 [/b]。至少最开始的几个小时，我是非常兴奋的。我认为从这个意义来说，2077可谓是“无代餐”的。

 [b]但接下来，2077又多少令我有些失望 [/b]：（1）整个主线偏短，尤其是开篇杰克之死的铺垫并不充分，以佣兵身份展开故事，对大公司迫害底层的描写也相对同类作品偏薄弱。主角本人比起真的被迫害，更像是自己主动卷入了公司战争之中。（2）城市看起来庞大，但大部分建筑都无法拜访，世界生态做得比较单薄，几个帮派区域之间没有明显的差异，同质化较强，中间人给的“清单列表”任务大多无趣，只有一部分人物支线（比如讲述将杀人赎罪者包装为“基督式死亡”变成超梦娱乐的罪与罚等）和阅读物还算可圈可点。

不过，回过头来，我实质上能明白本作出现这种情况的部分原因： [b]赛博朋克和开放世界结合，其实是有很多困难的。 [/b]

 [b]首先，从人物来说，大部分赛博朋克的作品，它的主视角往往是一位无能为力的小人物 [/b]——或许是被压迫的普通人，也可能是体制内的基层执行者——通过这个人物的悲欢离合，去观察、讽喻这个高科技低生活的社会，最终，在个体与高压体制的对抗中，主角其实通常是改变不了这个糟糕的世界太多的，而这正是讽刺的精髓所在。 [b]但作为开放世界游戏，无法设定一个无能为力或者不自由的人作为主角 [/b]，主角不能只跟着既定的剧情走，他必然要“开疆拓土”（开拓这个自由的世界），是个“传奇人物备选”。 [b]而主角在自由探索中，于各个城市区块大杀特杀、营救NPC、漫游收集、轻松潜入大公司、摆平各大帮派、成长为城里风光传奇的存在，这实际上是略微消解了游戏的赛博朋克感的 [/b]，因为给人的感觉是面对公司或者说社会整体的黑暗，我这个超级佣兵个体并非无能为力，我甚至是一个很自由自在、无法无天的存在（只有在恶魔结局，我能比较明确地感知到V身上的赛博朋克隐喻，被荒坂利用、一切努力竟然反而加固了大公司的统治，是非常讽刺的；而其他剧情给我的感觉大多是荒坂也并非不可打败，V能成为“传奇”）。

 [b]第二，赛博朋克题材比起奇幻或者传统科幻，是更不容易做出差异感较大的区域与种族的 [/b]。某种意义上，巨型企业垄断整个社会的现状与开放世界需求多元体验是略有冲突的，因为赛博朋克的世界已经规定了整个世界的社会样态——贫富差距极大、虚假繁荣却精神空虚，整个城市的每一处几乎都是如此，因为假设有部分区域不是这样的，赛博朋克就不成立了。而这使得不论是夜之城还是狗镇，人们遇到的问题、街道给你的感觉、混混们说话的方式，差异性都不大，很难做出对某个特定区域或者组织令人意外的揭示。作为小说、动漫、独立游戏，这没有问题，不如说这种同质化是加强了社会现状无法扭转的感觉，但作为开放世界，这可能会给人以单调的感受（尤其是在清理那些如列表一般的支线任务时）。而奇幻、科幻题材，则可以通过丰富的种族、地貌、政治体制（如王国、帝国、部落）提供多样化的异域探索感。

 [b]第三，制作垂直维度多层次的赛博朋克未来都市，在技术上比普通的水平延伸的开放世界要难更多。 [/b]奇幻题材或者末日题材游戏，只需要模拟一些近似当代村庄小镇级别的世界样貌；太空题材，往往也只需要模拟自然星球+少量定居点/空间站。而一个赛博朋克都市，人们往往期待这个都市能像是真实的都市一样，丰富多样，甚至还要搭配上更多的科技互动——而这的制作难度是几何倍上升的。很容易因为大部分内容只是贴图而产生虚假感。

坦率说，我能从游戏里感到，制作组是在尽力规避这些问题的（比如我能感受到几个帮派的设计已经是在希望做差异化的，但最终呈现起来并不那么明显；在阅读物里埋下了特别多小人物的悲剧故事，支线也尽量用多元的方式去陈述），但很多时候还是难以完全避免上述的情况。这或许也是以2077世界观为基底的《边缘行者》动画能够取得比游戏更好的评价的原因之一。

 [b]但即便如此，我还是很喜欢《赛博朋克2077》这部作品，它的世界观和人物确实很出色，剧本对话的撰写水平也很好，很多台词直击人心 [/b]。我自己打通了太阳（单刷）、节制（单刷）、高塔结局，又云了恶魔、星星、罗格线的太阳。每个结局都很有余韵。哪怕是我看攻略时觉得不太能接受的结局，最后其实都写得挺动人的——坦率说，我起初完全没有想到，最打动我的结局竟然会是单刷+节制（我在游戏初期就有看过攻略，当时觉得身体留给强尼是最不太能接受的结局）。 [b]而在这些塑造出色的点之中，让我印象最深的还是我们的“脑内伙伴”强尼·银手。 [/b]

固然，强尼占据了一个非常有利于塑造角色的位置（主角的“随身同伴”位置，这个位置的角色可以在游戏过程中大量积累陪伴感，往往是最容易直入人心的角色，也是游戏叙事特殊的优势）， [b]但强尼的塑造在这类型的角色中也是挺特别的 [/b]：他和主角的关系的演变非常有趣，甚至和这类角色通常的塑造是反着来的。大部分“陪伴者”的剧情是开头作为主角的友善同伴，随着剧情进展会揭示TA特别的身份，主角会短暂失去和陪伴者的同行关系，意识到这段关系的重要性，并最终再次夺回它；而强尼的剧情恰好相反，开头他与V其实是被迫同行的，关系紧张甚至有一些敌对，而最终在经历了风风雨雨后，二人走向和解以及无奈的分别。

 [b]在最初，强尼给我的印象并不那么好 [/b]：他过于个人英雄主义，性格暴躁固执，像是一个叛逆的标签化人物、一种不管不顾的耍酷，他和主角V还时不时唱反调，实在是“要找办法去除的危险存在”（这也就是为什么我最初看攻略的时候，对节制结局最为不接受）。但随着剧情的进展，我们揭开了强尼的记忆，也帮他找到了几个老朋友，解决了这些老朋友们面临的问题，在主线中也算是一起经历了几场风风雨雨， [b]我们会发现他（当然也是在V的改变下）逐渐展露了自己重情重义、甚至颇有对社会思考的一面 [/b]。可以说，他和V从一开始的敌对，逐渐变成了互相影响的朋友，乃至彼此重要的存在。

 [b]而几个结局里，强尼的所言所行是挺令我挺感动的。命运让他和V成了跨越时代的战友，但也让他和V必定不得共存 [/b]。在绝大部分结局里，他都尊重我们的选择，哪怕是自杀或者用手术做掉他。如果我们选择在抗争后把身体留给自己（太阳，星星），强尼会在道别时说“再见了，V，永远不要放弃战斗”。而如果我们选择苟且偷生、用手术做掉强尼（高塔），强尼其实也没有生气，他会说V一路走到这里，还是可以为自己骄傲，我们与他也还是朋友，“时候差不多了，孩子。答应我一件事——以后别老钻牛角尖，有些事后有些事该放就放。不要为了任何人改变自己，好吗？晚安，瓦莱莉，今天是个好日子。”（注：瓦莱莉是女V的真名）。

 [b]而最打动我的其实是“节制”结局的剧情 [/b]，也就是如果我们选择把自己的身体让给强尼——讲真，其实到结尾那里，得知如果V占有身体只剩下几个月能活，而强尼则可以长久地活下去时，与最开始不同，我是真的认真考虑了让强尼活的选项。毕竟，事已至此，毕竟，最初去荒坂偷窃我们就是冒着死亡的风险去“干一票大的”，这个结局也并非不可接受。而选择这个选项后，强尼的所作所为也让我觉得是值得的：节制结局用一个小人物做引子，让我们看到了新生的强尼，改变了自己过去不好的部分（比如戒了烟，不再花天酒地也不再空喊口号），但仍然是那个能够指引众人反抗的旗帜（虽然只是短暂的交集，但他为一个孩子指明了用音乐表达自我、反抗原生家庭的前路，坦率说我开始完全没想到他买吉他是要送给那个孩子的，直到他直接坐上大巴车，孩子追着说“你忘了吉他”，我才意识到一切，也很感动），他在V的坟墓前说“反正我想忘也忘不掉你了，一照镜子就是你的脸”的时候，我觉得好像这样也不错，我相信强尼未来一定还会掀起反叛的风潮，而这也同样会是V所作所为更长远的延伸。

而对V自己呢？哪个结局最好？坦率说这是争论不断的问题。很多人说是太阳或者星星，但这两个结局其实看到最后，我仍然无法拔除心中的虚无——尽管都多少有一些“可能找到解药”的暗示，但毕竟生命只剩下六个月。而饱受诟病的“高塔”结局，在我看来倒也没有那么糟糕，V成了普通人，未来或许无法再成为传奇，但活着就总会有新的希望与出路（比如投奔李德当个公务员，或者和米丝蒂一样去别的地方寻求自我，甚至可以出个自传写写去荒坂偷出了强尼银手的“传奇故事”……）。“高塔”结尾的那些朋友们的“冷淡”对话在我看来是有些刻意的，或者说，是游戏不可能将“高塔”结局定位为好结局导致的。游戏的其他结局，结尾语音留言都大概是V离开1-2个月的样子，而仔细考虑，其实其他结局的两年后，大概率也是如此物是人非（除非某个结局V真的可以活下来，还能拯救朋友们）。高塔虽然两年后也同样如此，但未来还有机会慢慢修补关系，至少朋友们都还活着，三郎也没有复活，这已经不算是太坏了。但对我如此（毕竟我只是个普通人），对V可能又是不同的答案吧。

 [b]带着这样的思考，我完成了2077的游戏，尽管它有这样那样的不足，但它也确实塑造了一个令人印象深刻的赛博朋克世界，并带给人以感动和沉思，总的来说还是很值得推荐的一款游戏。 [/b]

12/10! Що ж. Не вважаю сумніви щодо купівлі доречними. Раджу всім, і якщо ви прийшли по сильний сюжет, і якщо по гарний геймплей. Пишу відгук бо це одна з небагатьох дій як я можу висловити величезну шану геніям з CD Project Red. Але Аврору я їм не забуду. Одразу скажу, що весь текст в грі є українською. Варто також одразу написати, що доповнення "Phantom Liberty" це найкраще DLC, в яке я грав. Не знаю у кого може вистачити слів, щоб описати наскільки воно неймовірне. Чіпляє за живе сильніше ніж жуйка за волосся. А це мені ще треба було постійно натискати на паузу, щоб гра провантажилася. В грі дуже багато маленьких деталей, що потребують потужного заліза, тож обличчя були мильними, а дороги ставали прозорими без цього. Але під час боїв проблем майже не було, стрілянина не гірше "Call of Duty", як на мене. Сюжетне проходження ця мильність не зачіпала, там все було нормально. Ну це в мене залізо просто слабке. Не знаю хто придумав, що під час їзди на машині саме провантаження хмарочосів, а не дороги в пріоритеті. Майте на увазі, що DLC потребує ще потужнішого заліза ніж основна гра, але без нього гра як борщ без м'яса. Сама гра дуже влучно обирає налаштування, копатися в них немає сенсу. 
Тут ви впливаєте на все, це не “Bethesda”. Особисто я грав так само як би в реальному житті і гра це дозволяє. Але напевно через власний двигун гри дуже мало тактильної взаємодії, що іноді прям сильно відчувається. І це не Dishonored, де ваші вбивства впливають на кінцівку. Хоч у тебе 1000 трупів за спиною, як у мене, хоч лише 100, це рольова гра, де саме вибір діалогів впливає на розв'язку. Сенсу проявляти милість до бандюків і рабів корпорацій не бачу. Я навіть не відмовляв собі в задоволенні уважно перевіряти чи всіх було вбито. Механіка із залишенням в живих треба для деяких квестів, зокрема. Звісно, мені прикро, що єдині способи тихого вбивства це злам шиї та удари об ящики чи багажники. Я все ж таки прихильник ножа в горло.
Про наступний пункт, гадаю, знають майже всі. Варіативність бойовки. Так-так, ти можеш бути різним. Утім ніщо не може бути потужніше за деку зі скриптами в голові. Мене вже від слова "Сандевістан" нудить. Ну біжить на мене ваша представниця погано проробленого "Макс-таку" з клинками богомола і найкращим, не буду повторювати це противне слово, і що? Надсилаєш скрипт “Порушення моторики” і ріжеш як беззахисну антилопу, поки не прибіжать її друзяки. А про босів у яких немає допомоги я взагалі мовчу. Так само. Бій який у "сандевістаніка" займає хвилин зо 10 у мене займає 3. Дека ультимативна! 10/10! На її тлі все інше має вигляд наче Audi з Rolls-Royce поруч поставили. Від "Макс-таку" я очікував значно більшого чи то може у мене ноутбук поганий не дозволяє розігратися на повну їхньому ШІ, не знаю точно. Так-так, о великий патч 2.0 з кращою поліцією. Щодо нього, я за всю гру пару разів перекриття вулиць копами побачив, а шипи?  Їх немає. Побачення пророблені жахливо, певно, бо їх додали вже в патчі.Така "дешева" пародія на GTA, яке я хоч і не люблю. Поліціє діє як в "PayDay 2", просто лізе м’ясом. Не можу не вшанувати клинки богомола, вони класні. Також абсолютно не враховані ані твій рівень репутації, ані гаманець, я в кінці мав чотири з чимось мільйонів євродолларів, всі квартири, всі автівки. А почуття наче твій геймплей і сюжет не пов'язані взагалі. Бабло подіти справді нікуди. Всім раджу придбати "Рейфілд Калібурн", на якому я проїздив більшу частину гри, на ньому максималка більше 311 км/год, а Арондит "Гвінера" це одна з найгірших автівок в грі. На діалоги і ставлення майже нічого не впливає взагалі, хоч рівень навичок впливає, це дуже гарна ідея. Але після 2.0 всякі двері стали вимагати 20/20 техніки в розкачці персонажа. Мені як прихильнику TES V: Skyrim було неочікуванно побачити, що максимальний рівень обмежується числом 60, що не дозволяє вкачати всі перки на 20. А 50 для репутації це ж смішно. Для прикладу у мене було: 20/20 реакції, 16 з 15 сили, а решти по 15. Сумно, що реакція для бойовки найкорисніший напрям, а дає за гру дуже мало додаткових реплік, а інтелект з силою чи не в кожному діалозі є. Утім ви можете скасувати перк і повернути очко чи скинути характеристики будь-коли. Кепкування Геральта щодо ворогів: "Може у мене з обличчям щось не так?" актуальне і тут. Зовнішність за бажанням можна змінити. Музика якісна, особливо від групи "SAMURAI". Є радіо зі станціями на будь-який смак. Їх можна слухати пішки та під час стелсу, але не в боях. Дуже багато тексту на накопичувачах в усій грі, а кожна синя точка зі злочином це міні-історія. Але за кількістю тексту "Bethesda" ніхто не переплюне, ну і не варто. Я весь текст, який бачив прочитав, окрім, звісно деяких нісенітних історій, але! Кожен клятий раз щоб щось прочитати або обрати перк чи спорядження треба знімати навушники, бо фонить дивний звук в голову, від якого вона болить. Мапа зачищається в мить ока, за відчуттями — погляд — пів мапи ще в точках, наступний — вся зачищена. Я пишу цей відгук вже півтори години, а мені не набридає, а це про дещо каже, гадаю. Те що я переслуховую пісні з гри постійно, гадаю, очевидно. Але можна було зробити більше активних пісень-бенгерів на кшталт найпопулярнішого “The Rebel Path”, “V”, “You Shall Never Have to Forgive Me again”, “Never Fade Away” та “Chippin` In”. Загалом кількість прослуховувань говорить сама за себе. Сумно, що “Phantom Liberty” не мав таких активних бенгерів, як на мене. 
Якщо вам раптом набридли Far Cry, TES та інші ігри, де ти стаєш богом з німбом на голові в найбілішому пальто Cyberpunk 2077 й тим паче DLC “Phantom Liberty” вам обов’язково сподобається. Тут не можна не вимазатися в чомусь. Ти можеш бути справді непереможним, але найкращі імпланти, гроші, репутація і зброя не врятують близьку людину. CDPR обожнює спускати з небес на землю. Є фоторежим з купою параметрів. Звісно, я поважаю, що зробили телеетери й, авжеж, багато реклами, а також різні сайти, які я теж, певно, всі подивився, але хоч я і не люблю “GTA”, тут воно перемагає, можна було зробити більше етерів, щоб про термінове повідомлення мені не казали чверть гри. “Брейнданси” це окремий біль. Гадаю, мала бути змога їх переглядати і поза сюжетом, але щось не пішло. Тому вони є лише сміттям. 
Варто підбити підсумок. Це неймовірна гра, якій немає рівних, з ще кращим DLC. Я з честю тисну руку всім причетним і бажаю успіхів у розробці в Бостоні і щиро сподіваюся, що нова гра буде ще кращою і зачепить навіть більше за “Phantom Liberty”. Переконаний, що інвестори, які так підганяли творців не забули -75% ціни акцій, коли гру сиру випустили і новий Cyberpunk буде випущений лише при повній готовності. Я вважаю, що його дії будуть відбуватися в Нью-Йорку або Чикаго, а головним конфліктом буде вибір між загадковим ШІ і звичайними моральними виродками. Всім бажаю якнайкращого досвіду у “Місті мрії”! І побачимося на тій стороні.

说实话，我不是很喜欢玩所谓3A大作，太过庞大的世界观让我恐慌——在游戏中到底要干什么？杀了这个人会不会有什么影响？没有好好搜索这个房间会不会漏掉什么重要的线索？做错哪一步会不会导致接下来哪个任务不会触发？玩到最后，疲劳总是大过快乐

刚开始玩的时候有一个地下拳赛的任务，和我对打的是一个赌上了所有资产和爱车的男人，而他的孩子即将出生。看着他没什么肌肉的身体，我轻而易举的打败了他，他瘫坐在一边，而我要开始决定他的命运了：拿走一切还是放他一马？

我做了好长时间的心理斗争，看着他苦瓜般的脸和站他旁边大肚子的妻子，我最终还是选择拿走了钱和车，这笔钱在当时对我是巨款，我可以升级好几件义体装备，而那辆车呢更不用说，金光闪闪，夺人眼球

后来，随便做一个任务打个架，光搜地上的尸体卖枪就够赚大几万，我甚至懒得去捡了。当时那些升级的义体也早就被淘汰，至于那辆车呢，华而不实，也就拿到手的那一刻开过两条街，后来我就再没开过。那个男人？我没有他的一点消息

所以现在我开始思考，我当时为什么那么纠结？也许，让我恐慌的不是庞大的世界本身，而是它让我误以为“每一个选择都重要”——把一扇门做成金色，暗示我只有一次机会，可等我推开门走进去才发现，那只是一扇普通的门，后面还有几十扇在等着我

3A大作最擅长的，就是用庞大的体量来伪装出“意义”。那个输掉一切的男人，他瘫坐在那里的表情，他身后站着的妻子和即将出生的孩子——我当时以为我在决定一个人的命运。后来我才知道，我什么都没决定。他只是游戏设计者在我面前摆好的一件道具，他的穷途末路是编排好的，而我的纠结，也是被计算在内的

所以现在我不恐慌了，我终于明白——在这个世界里，真正需要我做的不是选择，是走过去。该开枪就开枪，该搜刮就搜刮，该无视就无视。因为说到底，我才是那个真正重要的人。这个故事不是关于夜之城的，是关于我的

我做出的一切选择都构成了只属于我自己的故事，也许正是从玩完赛博朋克开始，我不会再“害怕”玩这种大体量游戏了

Bought this game on launch on CDPR's GOG, played through all the bugs (Like police spawning in a backroom of a shop with no backdoor) and to me, it was still a good enough experience. Played for about 37 hours before reaching the final level.

No idea, why but I couldn't bring myself to finish the game then so I stopped playing. Years later, I bought this game on steam when it arrived and gone on sale. Just kept it in my backlog. Then, phantom liberty came out, I bought it too. Even got the physical PS5 game disc just because I love this IP and the characters.

Yesterday, I somehow found myself having some free time so I decided to finally fire CP2077 up again to finish what I started 6 years ago in 2020. I'm extremely glad CDPR has the cloud save function which ported my save over on steam so I could seamlessly continue my session from there. Also, the major bugs are gone. I have yet to encounter any so far.

In the next 8 hours where I would finally reach my ending for this game- I was reminded of the reason to why I fell in love with the game in the first place. The writing, casts, animations and characters. Truly felt alive. Bad people gave you a reason to hate them and the good makes you want to help them etc.

Anyway, I went on finishing a number of mini story side quests to tie off some loose ends (No spoilers but they are really good) before starting the final mission and boy, the only thing I can say is that it'll make you think about your life. When a game can do that to a person, make one think about their life's choices? I think it has achieved something special.

There are multiple endings btw so don't look it up first till you beat the game. More fun this way imo.

So yes, this is a good game that is definitely worth playing. I was never really a cyberpunk person till I was reeled into it by CP2077. Glad I got into it.

That said, I'm gonna be firing up the game again to experience phantom liberty soon. Heard good things so I know I won't be disappointed. If you are going to be coming to Night City as well? Good luck!

我不是什么专业的评测者，甚至大多数时间都在玩cs或者战雷等网游，但是2077真的非常吸引我。
2077刚出的时候，它赛博朋克的题材就深深吸引了我，我梦想着那个霓虹灯管的光盖过太阳的未来城市。但是在当时我只觉得首发爆雷的2077是个乐子。而且自己的电脑肯定带不动。
后来有了5070，在这个暑假我得知它史低打折，也是火速购入。说真的，这款游戏真的给了我身临其境的体验感。独特的第一人称视角与hud设计让我觉得我已经来到了夜之城。公司狗开局，坐上浮空车穿行与钢铁丛林之中，自己只能是巨大树干间的一只蜉蝣，我已经被震撼了。剧情也是没得说，每一个抉择都要让我思考很久，不同选择带来的剧情差别也很大。
它独特的战斗系统也是一个吸引我的点，不同于枪械设计与刀枪棍棒的纯粹设计，它独特的包含黑客的战斗系统让我有了更多选择，当我通过不断的骇入与潜行最终逃出荒坂大厦时，我感觉自己已经成为了传奇，这种成就感是无与伦比的。
总结一下，我个人是赛博朋克题材的狂热爱好者，所以我会给他五星。如果你是想抱着试一试的态度，我认为也能给到四颗星，因为本土化做的太好了，你能在其中听到正宗的ctmd。不足之处在于开放世界的内容太少了，城市中的餐厅与服装店同质化非常严重，根本没有存在的意义。还有载具系统完全是莫名其妙，前期买不了（没钱没声望），后期没意义（都有任务给的石中剑了）。
