Cyberpunk 2077 : une renaissance qui mérite le respect… et une nouvelle raison de retourner à Night City !

Je fais partie des joueurs qui ont connu Cyberpunk 2077 à sa sortie, avec tous ses défauts et les nombreuses critiques qu’il a reçues. Mais aujourd’hui, force est de reconnaître que CD Projekt RED a réalisé un travail exceptionnel pour redonner au jeu la place qu’il mérite.

Night City est, selon moi, l’une des villes les plus impressionnantes jamais créées dans un jeu vidéo. Chaque quartier possède sa propre identité, l’ambiance est incroyable, les éclairages sont magnifiques et les graphismes sont tout simplement époustouflants. On peut passer des heures à simplement se promener dans la ville sans jamais s’en lasser.

L’histoire est excellente, les personnages sont mémorables, les quêtes secondaires sont souvent aussi travaillées que la quête principale, et l’immersion est totale. On s’attache aux personnages, on réfléchit à nos choix, et chaque mission donne envie de découvrir la suivante.

Sur PC, avec une bonne configuration, le jeu devient encore plus impressionnant. Les graphismes poussés au maximum, le ray tracing, les mods et toutes les possibilités offertes rendent l’expérience encore plus immersive.

L’extension Phantom Liberty est une véritable réussite. Elle apporte une nouvelle zone, une histoire captivante et montre à quel point le jeu a évolué depuis son lancement.

Et comme si cela ne suffisait pas, CD Projekt RED nous offre une nouvelle excellente raison de retourner à Night City avec la sortie de la mise à jour 2.5, baptisée Edgerunners 2, qui accompagne l’arrivée de la deuxième saison de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners sur Netflix.

Cette mise à jour gratuite apporte son lot de nouveautés particulièrement intéressantes :

* Une nouvelle quête secondaire inspirée de l’univers d’Edgerunners 2, avec un équipement exclusif de cinq pièces à récupérer.
* Une nouvelle station de radio, HKGN 102.0 FM, avec plusieurs musiques issues de l’univers de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners.
* De nouvelles tenues, coiffures et possibilités de personnalisation pour V.
* Cinq nouveaux cosmédocs permettant de personnaliser visuellement ses implants cybernétiques : lames Mantis, bras gorilles, monocâble et lance-projectiles.
* Une nouvelle possibilité de combat à deux armes, permettant de manier simultanément un pistolet ou un revolver dans chaque main.
* Le support des mods multiplateformes grâce à mod.io, permettant de découvrir et d’installer une sélection de créations communautaires directement depuis le jeu.
* Une nouvelle quête de visite guidée de Night City racontée par Richard Night.
* Douze nouvelles cartes de tarot à découvrir à travers la ville.
* De nouvelles fonctionnalités pour le mode photo, notamment des cadres inspirés du jeu de cartes Cyberpunk.

Et ce n’est pas tout : la mise à jour apporte également des améliorations techniques, notamment la prise en charge du DLSS 4.5, des optimisations du ray tracing et différentes améliorations de performances.

Autant dire que les joueurs qui n’ont pas remis les pieds à Night City depuis longtemps ont désormais de belles raisons de s’y replonger !

Après plus de deux mille heures passées à explorer Night City, je prends toujours autant de plaisir à y retourner. Peu de jeux parviennent à créer un univers aussi vivant, aussi crédible et aussi fascinant.

Cyberpunk 2077 est la preuve qu’un studio peut écouter sa communauté, corriger ses erreurs et transformer un lancement difficile en une réussite remarquable.

Aujourd’hui, entre le jeu de base, Phantom Liberty, les nombreuses améliorations apportées au fil des années et désormais cette nouvelle mise à jour Edgerunners 2, Cyberpunk 2077 est bien plus qu’un simple RPG : c’est une expérience incontournable.

Merci à CD Projekt RED pour ne pas avoir abandonné ce projet, pour avoir continué à faire évoluer Night City et pour nous donner encore aujourd’hui de nouvelles raisons d’y retourner.

Alors, que vous soyez un ancien joueur ou que vous hésitiez encore à découvrir cet univers, c’est peut-être le meilleur moment pour vous lancer ou relancer une partie.

Un chef-d’œuvre qui mérite amplement une seconde chance… ou une première, pour ceux qui hésitent encore.

[h1]I couldn't rate this game out of 10 if I tried.[/h1]
Not because it's just [i]that[/i] good or anything. If you're into FPS's or stealth games, you'll get a lot of enjoyment out of this one. However, if you're not into those genres, I don't think the RPG mechanics and other elements would save it for you.
[hr][/hr]
[h2]Crushing it in Combat[/h2]
Combat and stealth are so integral to this game that there are very few missions that don't have you doing at least some. You're going to be taking down thousands and thousands of baddies and there's an alright variety to be had, what with the different factions and different classes of weapons they use. There's a dozen different "capstone" abilities you can mix and match across the different skill paths that all play differently, and you're free to combine a few of them across your playthrough to see what works the best for you. Similar to Skyrim, however, "stealth archer" is always what I find myself drawn to. Fortunately Cyberpunk makes that a ton of fun.

You'll find yourself in a lot of situations where the game wants or even requires you to do it quietly and never be spotted. This means you'll need to carefully manage enemies, take over the cameras to scout ahead before shutting them off, jack into security systems to shut off traps, and carefully take down and dispose of enemies one at a time so you don't raise an alarm. This feels awesome every single time, and nothing was better than clearing a mission without being seen. Even if you go in guns ablazing, the actual combat feels very satisfying with it's wide variety of punchy guns. However, the game's not perfect enough to facilitate that experience 100% of the time.

[h2]It's Glitchy (to rock your mind)[/h2]
There's no denying that this game is about on the level of Bethesda games in terms of bugs, and that's coming from someone who typically never notices glitches. Menus misbehaving, UI elements disappearing or displaying wrong information, lighting and texture glitches, framerate hiccups, and untimely crashes, the list goes on and on. Granted, I was in the habit of quicksaving, so I never lost hours of progress, but this game just straight up isn't stable enough to maintain anything close to pristine. The worst of the bunch were when enemies glitched out before/during combat, either becoming aggressive unusually fast or seeing me through walls or just have botched animations, it was always a toss-up if something was going to work right or not.

This couples with the minor gripes I have about all the menus and equipment in this game that are horrible to sort through and manage. You'll be hitting your inventory limit all the time and the game will grind to a halt every half hour or so for five minutes while you fumble with the lack of usable sorting options and clunky interface, with unintuitive dives through the nested menus. Eventually I felt like I had a handle on it, but that was 80 hours in, which I don't know if that reflects worse on me or the game. This isn't helped by the notification for picking anything up being so small and quick that I never saw what I was picking up unless I studied it beforehand, which with there being anywhere from 15 to 100 things to pick up in any one area, I quickly abandoned the practice.

[h2]Smiting the Writing[/h2]
I think that the writing is alright. It gets the job done. A few lines made me chuckle, some of them were deeply cringe, but what game at this scale doesn't have that mix of dialogue? A lot of, if not basically all but a handful of the side quests are incredibly forgettable. They all boil down to one-sentence descriptors, typically involving one person who's bad and you need to go stop them. To put it into perspective, I thought they were randomly generated at first because a lot of them felt so generic. Granted, when the game wants to, it'll put on a show for you, but I found myself skipping over the voice actor's decent to excellent delivery of lines just to get through some of it faster.
The worst writing comes with a lot of the romanceable characters. They're gender-locked, which while realistic, should've impacted their writing more. All of them will act as though you boned down and that you're the love of their life even if you reject them or, even worse, aren't their preferred gender of partner. It's even more awkward when they are actively seducing you, you go to do a sexy dialogue option, and they put up their hands and say "WOAH I'm not gay bro" (I paraphrased) before then letting you "spend the night" where you wake up in their bed. Coming off of a game such as Baldur's Gate 3, where they're down to let anyone be with anyone, coming into this one was probably gave more whiplash than your typical player as I played heterosexual whack-a-mole trying to avoid the painfully awkward and sometimes even unskippable sex scenes.

The main storyline also doesn't feel as sprawling as games like CDPR's other headliner the Witcher is. I could actively see how my choices were being acknowledged 99% of the time, sure, but insofar as to just let me know that I did indeed decide something. Often I'd have V, the player character, say something, and realize that based on the response of the NPC that regardless of what I said, they'd've said the same thing. Some games hide it better, but this one certainly doesn't. It helps that the voice actor for V (at least the male one) is phenomenal.

[h2]But hey, 100 hours is a 100 hours.[/h2]
I won't deny that there's a lot of stuff to do in this one. I could write a whole multi-hour video essay over all the aspects to this game that are done well, like the combat, the driving, the [i]shockingly[/i] good photo mode and clothing options, the main quest line, the characters, and on and on. And the city, good lord Night City is one of the most well-executed cities I've ever seen in a video game. I just loved existing in it, and it pains me to keep the praise on it brief, because honestly the asking price (especially on sale) is worth it just to walk around and take in the incredible work that's been done.

But just as many words can be said about the awkward and sluggish menus that take up way more hours of the game time than they should or all the glitches and edge cases that weren't accounted for. But, obviously, I recommend this one. There's a lot to hate on when it comes to Cyberpunk 2077, but there's also a whole lot of preem stuff in there.

I played and completed this game on release. It was exceedingly mid. This has been a labor of love by CDPR to fix it and make it closer to the game we had envisioned. It's still missing some of the promised features and most of the choices you make don't matter. It's odd that in a futuristic world where transhumanism is a thing that our companions are sex locked when people can easily modify their body to change their sex, but if we like a certain companion we are locked out if we are playing as the incorrect sex. It's a bit of a nitpick, but it really feels out of place in this world. The main story itself is not particularly special in my opinion. I found it interesting that you could approach missions with quite a few different methods depending on your own creativity. 

The side stories are where a lot of the interesting lore and the best stories are told. Even the really good Phantom Liberty DLC (despite loving it) where the characters felt solid, the endings felt quite shoe-horned and forced. Spoiler free but it feels like it changes a lot of characters' personalities or is just forcibly melancholy.

The RPG elements and systems feel more interesting and fun after the reworked systems. Gunplay is solid. You get some interesting builds with melee, netrunner/hacker, and several gun types. 

My main problems in the game are that the game still feels like there's a [i]lot[/i] of missed opportunity, particularly that the choices don't matter 99% of the time, and the 1% that do you don't know how or why without looking up a guide. I think that's lame storytelling. You should [i]feel[/i] as though your choices matter and actually impact the world. For example, Witcher 3 I found to be a much better game despite in terms of storytelling despite, in my opinion, the combat being significantly worse than it is in this game.

I'm torn between if I thought this game was a solid 8 (8.5?) or a 9 so I think I'll give game an enjoyable 8.5/10 and Phantom Liberty a 9/10.

[h2]This game is a literal masterpiece, and a candidate for best RPG of all times.[/h2]

[h3]Overview[/h3]
I actually bought this game on release day, purely on the strength of the demo they'd released and my desire to vote with my wallet for the kind of game I want to see made. I know it had issues at release but I didn't get around to seriously playing it until 2025 so my opinion is based on only experiencing the current ("fixed") state of the game.

It is a complex game with a lot of subtlety that is all kind of stuff thrown at you at once when you first play and I recommend just shutting off your brain, going with it and see what happens. You'll figure it out. My first run was somewhat typical for me in RPGs...he was a kind of stealthy corpo assassin who tried to use a cyberdeck but wasn't great at it. It wasn't until late in my first run that enough of the quickhack stuff clicked and I finally "got it." So I played again explicitly going full-on netrunner and it was almost a different game. Massively fun and I got emotionally invested in the entire story in ways that surprised me. Just finishing my fourth run and I'm still discovering new things, hidden references or rewards, character interactions I'd never seen, different romance stories, etc.

[h3]The Game[/h3]
An expansive Cyberpunk role-playing game based heavily on Mike Pondsmith's Cyberpunk tabletop RPG. And no screwing around it is a very faithful adaptation. It's a computer game so some stuff will get streamlined, some stuff ignored, but having experience with both I can say that it's clearly an adaptation of the TTRPG. The setting, characters and world are all consistent. And all horrible. There are no happy endings in Night City and that's another aspect of storytelling I can enjoy here. Characters are so well fleshed out that you can really start to hate them, or want to protect them. But more often than not they'll die. And you'll be at fault. If you insist on exclusively goody-twoshoeing your way through RPGs you'll find Night City a great wake-up call. Sometimes you have to make choices and it's rare for everyone to have a good outcome.

Combat is engaging and varied. You can set yourself up to rely on your cyberdeck to hack your environment and enemies, be a stealthy assassin that was never there, or enable a kind of bullet-time mode where time is slowed for your opponents but not for you while you apply shotgun or katana, or become an invulnerable baseball bat-wielding psychopath who drops on her opponents superman style smashing everything around them.

[h3]TL;DR[/h3]
Story is awesome. The actors are uniformely great and I got very attached to them. Missions are excellent and varied with some reaching the pinacle of cool design. I would consider the Project Liberty content mandatory. It is top notch, and slots into the existing story very well. Combat is amazing. Modding it can be fun, particularly for clothing.

The only thing I'd note is that "storyline missions" can feel quite "on-rails" at times, and it's a very different feeling from general side jobs or other activities. A minor compaint for a game that offers so much.

Combat is AMAZING....not matter how you want to approach it. 

The world is huge and always ALIVE. The builds ranges paired with Iconic weapons, the upgrade system, the methods of  executing a mission, the itemization, the cosmetics, the cars.....there is just so much to rave about; especially the graphics! QoL like fast travel and vehicle call allow you to move at your own preferred speed...I sometimes just drive to the next stop to appreciate the vehicles, scenery, and what I may stumble across on the way. 

Since this one is safely in the highly recommended category, this does not need to be a long review. 

Buy it....I cannot think of any gamer that would disagree.

Instead of repeating praises over and over, let me give you some cons. None of them deal-breaking, but something to consider.

The biggest con for me personally is the character writing / relationships. Being open world, you are bound to do some missions / world interactions in "wrong" order, resulting in weird "mood swings" of some characters. Some relationship building (and even missions!) also comes in form of texts/calls from the characters, which sometimes come way too late to be useful world building. 

Finally, as is often the case, your dialogue choices not only rarely matter, but have a very specific personality. I'd understand that in a Witcher game, where Geralt is his own thing, but I see no reason for V to be written like that, after we got one of the better character creation screens out there. Would've loved to have more freedom to develop V's personality & relationships more for that proper RPG experience, where it's not just skill trees and leveling with a customized face but also choices that matter.

I'm usually late to the party. I rarely jump head first into newly released triple a titles that cost a fortune and have yet to be fully optimized. In the case of Cyberpunk 2077 this was undoubtedly a boon, given its supposedly disastrous launch state. The Cyberpunk 2077 I played ran like a dream on both my desktop and LegionGo (Steam OS on Linux). But at this point, the technical aspects feel largely beside the point. Cyberpunk is more than the sum of its technical accomplishments. It's a pulsating, neon gut punch of sex, violence and moral ambiguity. It's everything I've always wanted from GTA but that GTA has never been able to give me. It's the general direction the Fallout series should have been aiming for after New Vegas. The characters, the acting. All the different ways you can approach the same mission, the builds, the city. Most of all Night City. Alongside Witcher 3 Cyberpunk surely establishes CD Projekt Red as  the best in the business when it comes to creating teeming environments that truly feel alive. Just driving around the various neighborhoods is a blast. Plus, if you go for Phantom Liberty, which you absolutely should, you get to spend some time with Stringer bell, which is never a bad thing. I played out every possible ending to the main scenario and each moved me in a different way, leaving me with a sense of loss and sadness and incredible beauty against the odds. I see this frequently on sale for about $30. That's an absolute steal. It sucks the devs won't be making any more DLCs.

只打了相对能接受的三个结局，分别是自杀、单挑荒坂塔的太阳结局、节制结局，相对最喜欢的是节制。
自杀虽然可以说是放弃抵抗了，但这确实是“最干净、死人最少”的方法，只是很遗憾什么都没有改变，只能寄希望赖宣。而米丝蒂在楼下注定等不到v了，J+V大小事情吵架拌嘴那么久，竟就这样平和地一起躺在天台的躺椅上，镜头在夜里的Night City变换很久，像是在生命尽头终于能够纯粹地欣赏这里的风景，然后在城市夜晚的喧闹里，砰地一声枪响。
但重走一万次我都会选择单挑荒坂塔，“以我残躯化烈火”，我太喜欢这个中文改译了，正如v说：“如果我要去死，那我希望最好一边开枪一边挖坑下葬，而且不拉任何人垫背”。然后强尼站起来，把v从躺椅上拉起来，一个转场，v在ai机械的“欢迎来到荒坂塔”声中、在强尼“2023，昨日重现吧”的开场白中，游戏程序自动掏出玩家背包里的枪，搭配上《The Rebel Path》bgm真的有种不顾一切无畏失去的感觉，以一己之力发起奇袭。
能接受太阳是因为v成为了传奇、荒坂受挫、强尼也希望v活下来，但实际上强尼的死还是很难受，像是一个银v关系更平和的高塔结局一样。v坠回自己的身体的时候，他说，再见，v，永远不要放弃抗争。在太阳结局里v登上水晶宫，仍然没有放弃，徒留一个在太空里义无反顾地飞向水晶宫的身影。
最后是节制，这结局给我一种“谁的生命都没有浪费”之感。没有任何一个朋友死去，强尼也获得了第二次生命，离开了Night City，网上有看法说这是强尼最终放弃了反抗公司，但我更认可另一个解释。荒坂赖宣固然可以利用手上的资源一次性给荒坂带来重创，然而治标不治本，还会有军用科技一家独大，还会有荒坂的东山再起。他内部的革命是暗中缓慢发展的，这是他有策略的“节制”。而强尼终于意识到他2023炸荒坂塔是个人的叛逆，一种无谓的牺牲，并不是真的因为心怀“解救被公司压迫的民众”的愿望而战的。这一次，强尼只是从v身上学会了“节制”。
强尼离开Night City的任务名就叫“镜子中”。他操纵v的身体给v买了一个骨灰龛，里面是v的挂坠，他在赛博空间里告别的时候第一次带上哭腔，第一次害怕，最后一句话是“我只是很害怕，我只是放心不下你”，在人间的骨灰龛前说：“你知道，不能再这样下去了，沉湎于过去不好，人不能总活在回忆里。反正我想忘也忘不掉你了，一照镜子就是你的脸。”

Honestamente uma das melhores experiencias da minha vida, realmente eu levei muito tempo para jogar este titulo, embora acredito que tudo tem um propósito e um tempo certo para que as coisas aconteçam. 
E jogar este jogo em 2025/2026 foi o momento exato. 
O Enredo é excepcional, uma obra prima, dialogos bem amarrados, a lore então nossa, cada "caco" que você pega pelo caminho conta sobre o mundo, sobre uma Night city que respira, que é viva, cheia de segredos, que sobrevive ao tempo e a ela mesma.

Nada, absolutamente nada passa despercebido, e você sente isso até mesmo quando cruza por um NPC e ele fala para outro que ja lhe viu por ai, que vc é quase uma lenda, um mito.
Todas as missões secundárias são elaboradas, embora pareçam com objetivo repetido, o cerne da missão é unico e nenhuma se repete na sua história.
V é sem duvida um personagem cheio de histórias, mas, nada se compara a complexidade de Johnny Silverhand, o cara é literalmente um ser profundo e muito mas muito complexo, com varios problemas internos, e questões que não foram resolvidas, o que torna cada dialogo com ele imprevisivel e muito peculiar. 
Embora ele seja um c***** em muitos momentos, é inegável que a atuação do Keanu trouxe a alma do que é Cyberpunk. Como ele mesmo diria " sinto cheiro de merda" em cada momento em que você toma uma atitude questionavel e até mesmo burra em termos de história, até por que cada decisão tomada aqui tem sérias consequencias no futuro, e sim, elas vão moldando um dos seus possiveis finais.

Recomendo que ao invés de sair focado na história principal, façam as missões secundárias e complete os arcos de cada personagem, que sim, é inicio, meio e fim. O jogo foi tão bem elaborado que realmente você vê toda a dinamica e evolução de cada um dos personagens mesmo os secundários, todos possuem sua história sendo contada diante dos teus olhos, enquanto a cidade que nunca dorme segue firme dia após dia, entre sonhos, ambições e derrotas.
Acho que nunca vou esquecer deste game e do que ele me ensinou enquanto pessoa. 
E na boa, que trilha sonora, olha Never Fade Away é uma musica que tu vai lembrar para o resto da vida, e a versão na voz da Olga Jankowska é sensacional.

Viktor, Jackie, Rogue, Panam, Judy, Takemura, River, Kerry Eurodyne e tantos outros que você sente quase como se fossem reais, como se você os pudesse ver nas próprias pessoas que você cruza durante a vida, amigos que surgem, amigos que vão, histórias que se cruzam, e nem todos permanecem em nossa vida.

Essa é uma grande lição de Cyberpunk, ou seja, um grande soco de realidade, quando você para e pensa poxa a vida é assim, a cidade grande é assim, nunca dorme, quantos sonhos despedaçados em cada amanhecer, quantos sonhos de quem chega buscando um novo recomeço, e quanto a brutalidade do dia a dia nos molda, nos muda, nos transforma em personagens que nunca imaginamos ser, e é esse o ponto, o que você é capaz de fazer para alcançar teus objetivos, sonhos e como você lida com traições, é possivel confiar em alguém de verdade?

Obs: Faça saves regulares manuais antes de cada grande decisão, isso lhe poupara um certo tempo em replay de gameplay para alcançar outros finais, a não ser que você decida começar do zero, pois, até mesmo na criação do personagem o jogo lhe da caminhos distintos.

Portanto e encerrando, aproveite cada momento deste jogo, vasculhe os segredos da cidade, mergulhe na história, jogue sem compromisso com o final, faça as escolhas da forma como você viveria, pelos teus principios, isso sim, considero como experiência verdadeira, e depois de terminar o jogo, se ainda não viu, veja o anime edgerunners, o que vai expandir ainda mais sua mente.

Cyberpunk 2077, gerçekten distopik bir geleceğin nasıl olması gerektiğini iliklerinize kadar hissettiren eşsiz bir yapım. Şirketlerin dünyayı ele geçirdiği, insanların yaşamlarının birkaç mega şirketin iki dudağı arasında olduğu bu karanlık gelecekte, Night City sokaklarında bir efsane olmaya çalışan paralı asker V'nin hikâyesine ortak oluyoruz. Ancak bu yolculuk sırasında kaderimiz, Night City'nin en unutulmaz isimlerinden biri olan Johnny Silverhand ile kesişiyor. Üstelik yalnızca yollarımız değil, ruhlarımız da aynı bedeni paylaşmaya başlıyor.

Hikâye, başından sonuna kadar merak uyandırmayı ve oyuncuyu sürekli içinde tutmayı başarıyor. V'nin yaşam mücadelesi, hayalleri ve verdiği zor kararlar; Cyberpunk evreninin acımasız, yozlaşmış ve umutsuz atmosferiyle birleşince ortaya gerçekten nefes kesen bir deneyim çıkıyor.

Oynanış tarafında ise oyun, oyuncuya ciddi anlamda özgürlük tanıyor. İsterseniz hançer ve katana kullanan, gölgelerde hareket eden gizlilik odaklı bir samuray olabilir; isterseniz ağır silahlarla önüne çıkan her şeyi yerle bir eden agresif bir savaş makinesi ya da zekâsına ve hack yeteneklerine güvenen ölümcül bir Ağgezer (Netrunner) olarak ilerleyebilirsiniz. Hatta bunların hiçbirine bağlı kalmak zorunda değilsiniz; farklı oynanış tarzlarını bir araya getirerek görevin yapısına, bulunduğunuz ortama ve karşınızdaki düşmana göre sürekli değişen hibrit bir karakter oluşturmanız mümkün.

Bütün bunları destekleyen siber implant (Cyberware) sistemi ise oynanışın en güçlü taraflarından biri. Karakterinizi yalnızca sayısal olarak güçlendirmiyor; kullandığınız yetenekleri, çatışmalara yaklaşımınızı ve oyunu oynayış biçiminizi doğrudan değiştiriyor. Her yeni implant, karakterinizi biraz daha size ait hissettiriyor ve gelişim hissini oyun boyunca canlı tutmayı başarıyor.

Night City ise başlı başına oyunun en büyük yıldızlarından biri. Neon ışıklarıyla süslenmiş caddeleri, birbirinden farklı semtleri, sokaklarında dolaşan insanlar, çeteler ve her köşeye gizlenmiş küçük detaylarıyla yalnızca görev yaptığınız bir harita değil; gerçekten yaşayan bir şehir hissi veriyor. Bazen hiçbir görev yapmadan motosikletinize atlayıp radyoyu açarak şehrin sokaklarında dolaşmak bile başlı başına keyifli bir deneyime dönüşüyor.

Yan görevler ise çoğu açık dünya oyununda olduğu gibi haritadaki işaretleri temizlemekten ibaret değil. Büyük bir kısmı ana görev kalitesinde yazılmış; yeni karakterlerle tanışmanızı sağlayan, bazen sizi güldüren bazen de duygusal anlamda etkileyen hikâyeler sunuyor. Bu yüzden Cyberpunk 2077'de yan görev yapmak hiçbir zaman zorunluluk gibi hissettirmiyor, aksine Night City'yi tanımanın en güzel yollarından biri oluyor.

Karakterler konusunda ise CD Projekt RED yine ne kadar başarılı bir hikâye anlatıcısı olduğunu kanıtlıyor. Johnny Silverhand'in yanında Panam, Judy, Takemura, Rogue, Viktor, Jackie, Kerry ve River gibi karakterlerin her biri kendine has kişilikleri, geçmişleri ve amaçlarıyla oyuna büyük katkı sağlıyor. Hiçbiri yalnızca görev veren sıradan NPC'ler gibi hissettirmiyor; onlarla zaman geçirdikçe bağ kuruyor, hikâyelerini merak ediyor ve oyun sona erdiğinde bazılarına gerçekten veda etmek istemiyorsunuz.

Son olarak Phantom Liberty DLC'si de ana oyunun yakaladığı kaliteyi başarıyla sürdürüyor. Yaklaşık 15-20 saatlik yepyeni hikâyesi, merak uyandıran senaryosu, güçlü atmosferi ve unutulmaz karakterleriyle Night City'ye geri dönmek için fazlasıyla geçerli bir sebep sunuyor. Sadece bir ek paket olmanın ötesine geçerek oyunun evrenini genişletiyor, sunduğu yeni deneyimle Cyberpunk 2077'yi taze tutmayı başarıyor ve bu dünyadan kopmanızı istemeyecek kadar etkileyici bir macera yaşatıyor.

Few games capture the imagination quite like Cyberpunk 2077. Set in the sprawling metropolis of Night City, CD Projekt Red delivers a world that feels alive with towering skyscrapers, neon-lit streets, and unforgettable characters. Blending a compelling narrative with deep role-playing mechanics and breathtaking visual design, the game immerses players in a futuristic society where ambition, technology, and humanity constantly collide. Following years of improvements and updates, Cyberpunk 2077 has evolved into the experience many hoped for at launch, standing as one of the most immersive and visually impressive RPGs of its generation.

This game developed by CD Projekt Red shows that a great open-world RPG is not only about its main story but also about its side missions. The optional quests make the game more interesting, meaningful and lengthen your whole run in this game. Even though the game has some bugs, its exciting missions and emotional moments more than make up for it.

In the game, you play as V, a mercenary living in Night City. After getting shot in the head early on in the story, V was implanted with a special bioship called the “Relic”. The chip contains the digital personality of Johnny Silverhand, a famous rock star and rebel played by Keanu Reeves. As the Relic started taking over V's mind, Johnny began appearing in V's head, which allowed him to start appearing in front of him  and to talk to him in his head. At first, Johnny and V do not get along, but over time they build a stronger relationship. Their journey together is one of the most important parts of the story.

The structure of this game is different from many other RPGs. After only a short time in the main story, you already have many side missions and gigs (from various fixers) to choose from. In the future, people often call you on your phone to offer new jobs, so you do not always need to search for quests yourself. This means the game gives you many choices early on. While your progress may not always feel bigger over time, there is always something interesting to do.

One important thing to mention is that, if you make use of the Fast Travel option, there is the possibility of certain questlines bugging, which means that you will not receive an important phone call for the next mission. This happened to me during the Panam and Judy questlines on an older save. Because of this, I recommend driving around the city and completing short activities such as NCPD missions while waiting for important calls instead of using Fast Travel too often.

Night City rewards careful exploration. If you move too fast, you will miss many interesting details. You can shape your character through your skills and dialogue choices. Your decisions affect both V's story and the lives of other characters, making every playthrough feel unique.

The combat in Cyberpunk 2077 becomes more enjoyable as you play. At first, the enemies can feel too strong, but as you unlock new skills, weapons, and cybernetic upgrades, combat becomes much easier and more fun. You can use powerful weapons, slow down time, double jump, or fight with Mantis Blades or an Electric Baton, which lets you pick up an enemy and toss them through the air or against a wall, which is extremely violent. These abilities let you choose your own fighting style and make every battle more exciting.

One of the best parts of the game is its unique Iconic weapons. These special weapons have different abilities and can be upgraded, so they stay useful throughout the game. Some weapons have special effects, while others are simply fun to use. This system lets players keep their favorite weapons instead of replacing them all the time, making combat more enjoyable and rewarding.

As you become stronger, the game lets you choose how to complete missions. You can fight enemies directly or use stealth to avoid them. Many areas have hidden paths, useful items, and computers that can help you by opening doors or turning off security cameras. Even though the stealth system is simple, it is fun to plan your route and use Quickhacks to distract or stop enemies.

Quickhacking is one of the most interesting features in Cyberpunk 2077. It lets you hack enemies by overheating them, causing them to detonate a grenade, making them suffer from cyberpsychosis, or temporarily blinding them. This makes both stealth and combat more exciting. By using Quickhacks and hidden paths, you can complete some missions without fighting anyone, giving players many different ways to play the game.

Unfortunately, the amount of bugs I experienced really does need to be mentioned. Sometimes characters move in strange ways, objects do not appear correctly, dialogues overlap, and certain questlines can get stuck. I also experienced visual glitches, such as missing hair on my character or V being stuck in a T-pose inside a car. Although I had to reload my saves a couple times, these problems never stopped me from enjoying what is probably the most content-rich single-player game I have ever played. The game's strong characters, huge variety of content, and well-written missions made these issues quite easy to overlook.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is an outstanding open-world RPG with a beautiful and highly detailed world to explore. The story is exciting, emotional, and full of memorable moments. Although the main story is shorter than expected, you can turn the game into a very long experience by exploring everything it has to offer, listening to every dialogue, completing every side mission and gig, and unlocking all possible endings. I highly recommend completing every available mission before entering Embers to meet Hanako, because after that the story does not continue. Instead, the game returns you to the point right before the final mission through the "Sure, just one more gig" option, allowing you to finish any remaining content, but it just wouldn’t feel the same after having already completed the story beforehand. If you own Phantom Liberty, you should also complete it before the final mission, as it unlocks an additional ending that becomes available during the game's final choice.

Cyberbug 2077 is a good game overall, and I'd give it an 8.5/10. The graphics are really good, the main story is solid, and the shooting feels satisfying, even if it's nothing special. Most of the side content isn't very interesting. Character skills and talents mostly feel unnecessary, as it has little impact on the overall experience.

The game also involves a lot of walking and watching cutscenes. At times, I'd almost categorize it as a walking simulator rather than an action RPG. In most cases, the dialogue options don't meaningfully affect the story and instead provide only the illusion of choice, with the different responses leading to largely the same outcome.

Additionally, I encountered around 50 bugs during my playthrough, most minor, few times the game crashed. Considering the game is now about six years old, I found it surprisingly buggy, especially given the amount of post-launch updates it has received.

Após algumas horas de jogo, quando as informações começam a se assentar na sua cabeça (entender o que são as megacorps, pessoas, implantes cibernéticos e afins) você sente que as infos começam a vir de forma mais natural e a imersão se torna outra.

Você lida com diversos personagens no decorrer do jogo, mas cada um inevitavelmente te marca de forma distinta, sendo muito fácil se apegar a eles e desejar pelo bem de cada um. Cada escolha torna a história diferente da última, o apego aos personagens também.

Night City parece sempre viva, você anda, explora, completa trabalhos e ainda assim sente como se a imensidão daquela cidade nunca fosse ter fim.

O gráfico do jogo é lindo, várias vezes há o sentimento de se pausar e olhar para a cidade, principalmente em alguns pontos específicos.

A trilha sonora do jogo te acerta de forma absurda (quem viu a animação sabe o sentimento de estar dirigindo e a rádio começar a tocar "I really wanna stay at your house"), músicas boas e boas risadas quando a rádio começa a tocar.

Um ótimo jogo, está entre meus preferidos.

Ох, «Киберпанк 2077»... Это та игра, в которой я успел прожить три жизни, получить пару нервных срывов и влюбиться в цифрового призрака с чипом в голове. Прошёл я её на релизе на ПК и перепрошёл спустя год так же на ПК с патчами. Так что отзыв будет честным, как исповедь перед Виктором Вектором.

Вот мои субъективные, но максимально объективные плюсы и минусы.

🥰 Плюсы (за что прощаю всё)
Атмосфера и мир - это просто наркотик. Ночной Город - это не локация, это живой персонаж. Он воняет, гудит, переливается неоном и давит на психику. Если вы любите киберпанк, то вы будете просто стоять и пялиться на небоскрёбы, слушать радио и ловить кайф. Это лучший открытый мир по вайбу со времён Ведьмака 3.

Сюжет и персонажи. История с Джеки, Джуди, Панам и, конечно, Джонни Сильверхендом (Киану Ривз - красавчик, хоть и ворчун) цепляет за живое. Концовки в этой игре - это эмоциональный нокдаун. После титров я сидел в тишине минут 10, переваривая, что только что произошло. Игра реально заставляет задуматься о смерти, памяти и о том, что значит «быть человеком».

Геймплейный песочница. Да, стрельба не уровня DOOM, но билдов тут море. Хочешь - бегай с самурайскими катанами и руби всех в стиле «Призрак в доспехах», хочешь - взламывай камеры и заставляй врагов кончать жизнь самоубийством через хакерство, хочешь - просто разноси всё из дробовика. Скучно не будет.

Саундтрек. Это просто отдельный вид искусства. Саундтрек от Marcin Przybyłowicz и треки на радио (особенно I Really Want to Stay at Your House) - это база. В машине я слушал радио чаще, чем ездил по квестам. (+ Добавил несколько треков группы SAMURAI себе в плейлист)

🤬 Минусы (за что хочется закидать клавиатурой)
Техническое состояние (даже сейчас). Да, багов стало меньше, но они есть. Иногда Т-поза у NPC, машина вылетает в космос от столкновения с бордюром, а в диалогах персонажи могут смотреть не друг на друга, а сквозь твою душу. Починили? Да. Идеально? Нет. Это как чип Реликвия - вроде работает, но знаешь, что подвох есть.

Пустой открытый мир. Вот ты стоишь на площади, вокруг куча NPC, а поговорить с ними нельзя, поесть в забегаловке - просто анимация, и нет возможности просто посидеть на скамейке полюбоваться закатом (если только через фоторежим). Полиция спавнится за спиной буквально из воздуха. Это разрушает иммерсию. Ты чувствуешь себя не частью города, а главным героем, который бегает по декорациям.

Система лута - АД. В начале игры я подбирал ВСЁ. В итоге у меня в инвентаре было 300 единиц оружия с разными циферками, и я тратил больше времени на сравнение статов «+2% к урону огнём», чем на стрельбу. К 30-му уровню ты просто перестаёшь смотреть на хлам, потому что на прокачку нужны компоненты, которых вечно не хватает.

Обещанного три года ждали, а не дождались. Нет, игра хорошая. Но она НЕ ТА, которую нам показывали на E3 2018. Метро не работает, коптеры не летают, система разветвлённых квестов (где каждый выбор меняет мир) - это миф. В сравнении с тем, что обещали, это «Ведьмак 3», а получили «Ведьмак 2» - круто, но масштаб не тот.

ТАК ЖЕ:
В этой игре я понял, что если встретил человека с жёлтым восклицательным знаком над головой, то будь добр - отложи спасение мира, потому что «Срочный заказ!».

Такси Деламейн - лучший психотерапевт в Найт-Сити. Если бы у меня была такая же навигация в Яндекс.Картах, я бы давно уже разбил машину об столб, как это делают местные водители.

Прокачка взлома: сначала ты чувствуешь себя хакером-некромантом. Потом ты просто нажимаешь «Контролировать» и смотришь, как враги убивают друг друга, попивая колу. Боже, какая же это сила.

Итог (Премия «Самая честная оценка»)
9/10 (с патчами) и 6/10 за то, что было на релизе.

Если вы ждали «Жизнь и приключения в Найт-Сити» - возьмите, играйте и получайте удовольствие. Это крутая драма с отличным сюжетом. Но если вы ждали симулятор жизни будущего с полной свободой - вы будете разочарованы.

Совет: Не гонитесь за 100% прохождением, делайте сюжетку и побочки любимых персонажей (Панам, Джуди, Риверу). Потом уж можно и на 100% закрыть)

Теперь Phantom Liberty... Это не просто DLC, это «Cyberpunk 2.0 в миниатюре». Честно говоря, после него стыдно вспоминать, во что мы играли на релизе. Краткий отрыв башки:

Плюсы (Иммерсивный восторг)
Сюжет - это триллер уровня «Самолёт президента». Ты не просто бегаешь по поручениям, а спасаешь президента НСША в сетях и расследуешь шпионский заговор. Идрис Эльба (Соломон Рид) - это вам не Киану с гитарой. Здесь ставки выше, а моральный выбор - больнее. Концовки этого DLC заставят плакать...

Новый район - Догтаун. Это не просто ещё одни улочки. Это вертикальный, плотный, грязный и опасный город в городе. Там каждая подворотня дышит атмосферой «Бегущего по лезвию», а чёрный рынок крафта - просто подарок для задротов.


Минусы (Есть ложка дёгтя)
Коротковато. За 15–20 часов ты проходишь всю основную ветку. Платить за 20 часов (почти как за новую игру) - местами дороговато, хотя и очень качественно.

Тяжело морально. Это не весёлая прогулка по городу. Это шпионский психотриллер. После одного из выборов я просто выключил игру. Тут нет хэппи-энда, есть только «меньшее из зол».

ТАК ЖЕ:
Phantom Liberty - это как «Догтаун» в реальной жизни: ты думал, что Найт-Сити уже достаточно жёсток, а тут тебя заставляют выбирать между предательством и предательством. Спасаешь президента - получаешь по шапке. Сдаёшь Сола - плачешь в подушку. И всё время слышишь голос Рида: «Это ради великой цели, Ви».

Вердикт: 10/10 по атмосфере, 9/10 по геймплею, 10/10 за Идриса Эльбу. Берите, не пожалеете, но готовьте носовые платки - эмоционально будет тяжело, как после просмотра «Секретных материалов» в дозе старых советских детективов.

Настоящий киберпанк начинается здесь. А старый Найт-Сити теперь выглядит как дворовая песочница. хаха

centrist cyberpunk is kind of a non-starter for me. i was really hoping this game had anything interesting to say about our world (given it has cyberpunk in its title), but it's so much about its characters that society isn't allowed to exist. quests have dynamic combat encounters that provide quite a bit of flexibility with how you complete them, that allow for a lot of player expression, but they're connected by a story in which the momentum inevitably grinds to a halt every other mission.

if you're inclined to actively seek out side content, to do literally everything possible in games before completing the main quest, then you'll probably have a lot more fun with this than i did. frankly, the late game missions are designed around having done a whole bunch of side quests, upgrading gear, getting new passive abilities, etc. so the game is much more for you. personally, i think this game's big issue is that it's too difficult to discover side quests, to stumble into the fun; if the main quest is going to force you to wait potentially multiple in-game days before you're allowed to continue, you shouldn't be able to drive for five minutes without something catching your eye. i only really like doing side content if it seems immediately interesting, but since the interesting parts of side content are only in their twists, i spend 90% of the quest line waiting for the cool stuff and then the quest is over before i get to do anything interesting or unique.

在体验了一段时间本作之后 我决定为它写一点东西。首先我认为2077是一款确实出色的游戏，在推出六七年之后依然非常值得品鉴。事先需要说明的是我入手本作的时间点已经比较靠后，所以可能并没有遇到任何在2021年左右的玩家描述的痛苦问题和质疑，而且作为我体验的比较早的3A，不排除有我个人对科幻题材的偏好带来的影响。
  一个游戏最重要的部分，我觉得就是它想和玩家讲好一个什么样的故事，包括剧情和游戏整体的氛围和基调。只从本体主线看，对于一个这么庞大的世界观20个小时可能确实太短了，叙事是比较松散的，从第一章杰克死了之后就变得自由度比较大，和后续各种人物比如帕南和竹村等的感情可能更加深入一些，但我觉得这挺有意思，毕竟2077的叙事本来就有一个V几乎肯定要死的残酷前提，玩家的选择就是串联各种支线的骨架。2077的所有剧情基本上编织的就是一种精密的无力感，因为无论你怎么选都没有一个最漂亮的合家欢结局，所以我在选择剧情分叉的时候一般会选择更悲壮一点的——固有一死嘛。如果算上狗镇的话对剧情的评价还可以更高，政治谍战很有意思，而且比起本体奋力反抗超级资本主义这种大家喜闻乐见的主题摆出了更多道德上的两难困境，我认为表现的情感密度和张力都非常精彩。最后活成普通人也好，成为传奇也罢（虽然我觉得2077的本意不是个人英雄主义叙事），2077的很多剧情确实可以让我在通关的时候怅然若失。
  在战斗方面我体验了除了纯粹的黑客以外的基本上所有玩法，因为一开始就点智力太坐牢了。其他流派给我的体验都很好，技能树也算非常便于理解和好入手的，专长可以重复选给了你玩不同武器的自由度，但是我不太喜欢加点只能洗一次这点，这导致我还是不能在一两个周目里玩到所有武器和战斗方式。总体而言在不点特别高难度下，你可以随心所欲地混搭各种好玩的义体和娱乐武器，而且这些小玩具做的都很炫，狗镇的未来武器设计得尤其漂亮，这个战斗系统还是值得好评的。
  从美术和音乐等等表现设计上也挺有意思，城市设计和电影布景一样很漂亮，给我的感觉是“棱角分明”，而且服务于剧情，有很明显的富人区规整，秩序井然和穷人区拥挤混乱，郊区则沙尘遍布，荒凉一些的分别。在我的电脑上开启中等画质已经可以享受到很漂亮的城市细节，比如雨后的霓虹灯倒影等等。音效上对于夜之城这样一个多文化的城市来讲也起到了一个烘托的作用，我觉得对于本来不熟悉嘻哈，街头，电子这些音乐流派的玩家会觉得很有趣，配音也是少有的双语配音都很顺耳的作品。
  我个人对电脑配置不太精通，但是至少在这部设备上我没有遇到这款游戏的老玩家反馈的严重性能问题，可能归功于后续的优化吧，我没有遇到过卡顿而且在约200小时游玩里我只遇到了两次闪退。
  如果让我谈一谈遗憾的地方，可能就是它半成品的痕迹，尤其是本体依然有点严重，不可否认的是极大部分建筑都不能进入，大部分路人是背景板，开放世界的深度我认为不太够。这也导致了另一个我不喜欢的问题，这会导致玩家在不做任务的时候几乎没有事情做，何况这是一个没有多周目的游戏，如果我通关了游戏，就只能对着进不去的房子逛街。我真心希望这游戏能有个二周目，至少我不会厌烦把打过的任务再玩一遍，反正给我的剧情选项够多，而且我也可以试试大后期才能拿到的武器比如骄傲和弃子。骄傲这枪让我火很大，谁想出来的毕业级武器真的毕业才能拿的？还有一些小问题，比如通缉系统比任何其他有类似机制的游戏都敷衍，开车的手感像黄油，当然我觉得这些老问题应该也得不到什么修复了。
  如果你希望要一部和gta一样的城市漫游，你可能会失望，但我还是认为2077是一款好玩而且有风格的好游戏，有深刻的主题，优质的视听感受和世界观构筑，对于喜欢漂亮的武器和城市设计，独特文化氛围的玩家来讲有着和对我一样的吸引力，狗镇这种颠覆了曾经的游戏评价的高质量，代表制作的巅峰水准的dlc也可以无脑入。说到最后，我依旧很感谢CDPR经历了各种颠簸之后，最后还是为我带来了许多大学里能够打开电脑享受游戏的小小快乐时光。

roll forward to 2024 and I finally had a 4 slot toaster that could run the game, and hearing tales of things being fixed and turned around got me curious, so I dipped a pinky toe in,

the sheer depth of the story, and the connections you make along the way, the friendships, Jackie <3 Rogue, River, Judy, Panam, even to a smaller degree, Johnny,

Se eu tivesse que definir Cyberpunk 2077 em uma palavra, com certeza escolheria: Anarquia Ⓐ (obviamente). Porém existem dois tipos de conceitos dessa palavra: 

🔹 Filosófica (como era proposta pra ser): Viva a sua vida conforme você achar melhor, de forma responsável, podendo fazer o que bem entender, contanto que não prejudique ninguém. Tendo sempre em mente que: “Toda a decisão e ação tem consequências (independente se são boas ou ruins), e cabe a você assumir a responsabilidade pelos seus atos.”

🔹Coloquial (Desordem): Na linguagem comum, a palavra é frequentemente utilizada como sinônimo de confusão, descontrole, desorganização ou ausência de regras em uma instituição ou situação. Refere-se a um estado onde o comando ou a liderança falhou, gerando um ambiente de desordem.

O conceito predominante apresentado no Game é o Coloquial (obviamente). O Corpo deixou de se tornar um Templo onde você deveria se autopreservar, para se tornar uma casca banal, sem importância e modificável. Pecados como: Luxuria, Materialismo, Egocentrismo e Escravos de seus Próprios Prazeres, Fatores como: Problemas Sócias, Desigualdade Social e Falta de Empatia, fazem dos cidadãos de Night City levarem uma vida bastante Infeliz, Ansiosa e na maioria das vezes: Solitária.

Quem vive na “ralé” tem que lutar dia após dia há sua maneira para sobreviver, e quem é “nobre” vive para ser manipulado por seus próprios prazeres. Trazendo a ideologia fictícia desse Jogo para o mundo real, é demonstrado que quando você não segue os princípios Bíblicos de Deus, as consequências são bem severas e o peso de suas ações cobram muito caro.

I originally played Cyberpunk a little while after it released. If you're unaware, the game had an incredibly rocky launch, being in an unacceptable state. At best, it was an average RPG with a good story, and at worst, it was an unfinished and unpolished experience. I shelved it thinking I would never return, until about five years later when I bought the Phantom Liberty DLC. Now, I regard Cyberpunk as one of the finest RPGs, though not quite the greatest.

The game especially shines with how much player interaction there is. The ways missions reacted to my previous actions, such as decisions or completion of certain quests, is astonishing. Almost everything I did felt like it will be acknowledged down the line, whether that be through modified quest-lines, objectives, or dialogue. Each one of those moments, of which is present throughout the entire game, added greatly to my experience, no matter how small nor insignificant those acknowledgements turned out to be. The variety of these experiences is vast as well. Aside from the major story beats, my two playthroughs of this game felt incredibly different. 

Beyond missions, Cyberpunk does a great job at feeling [i]alive[/i]. I love how I can walk into any shop and chat with the owner, especially bars. I love how I'm able to text or call characters after missions to debrief them or seek a second opinion. And more broadly, I love how much unmarked content there is. There are so many things in this game that I would have never encountered if I lacked explorative drive. From things as minor as dialogue or texts, to as major as really powerful items and entire side-quests. Amazingly, despite my recent ~100 hour playthrough, there's definitely still a portion of the game I have yet to experience. The abundance of content makes the game feel fresh and like it's a world at my fingertips.

In a similar vein, I greatly appreciate how much variety there is. There are tons of different builds you can pursue, each being very flexible in how you design it. For instance, fast-paced blades, heavy-hitting weaponry, stealthy glass canons, and any combination thereof. Within missions, there's always several ways to go about them and a plethora of optional objectives that can improve (or hinder) your primary goal.

However, as much as I regard Cyberpunk as one of the finest RPGs, I hesitate praising it too highly. While a strong entry in its category, it sits [i]just[/i] beneath the best. Most overtly, there's a strange absence of trans-humanism. In a world where one can modify any part of the body with cybernetic enhancements, and enter most stores to change one's phenotype on a whim, you would expect themes of identity, alienation, individuality, and the human condition to be present. At best, the extent of trans-humanism's presence is cyberpsychosis, quite literally psychosis induced by cybernetic abuse, and interaction with a few characters who hardly view themselves as human. How can a game based on a genre whose defining trait is trans-humanism completely omit it? Even something as minor as the occasional human with elf ears or otherwise unnatural traits would have satisfied this niche.

Another criticism is a small, yet significant, portion of writing for the protagonist, V. I appreciate that you have a great deal in customizing V, including their identity and backstory, as well as their behavior. However, I dislike that V has one constant underlying motivation: to make a big name for themselves. This made perfect sense for certain backstories, especially my first playthrough as a Streetkid, but made little sense for my playthrough as a former Corpo. Why do I have to always role-play as someone who ultimately desires fame and glory? What about something as simple as living comfortably or returning to a former lost life? While I concede that I am ultimately role-playing as V and not a self-insert, I dislike how Cyberpunk offers so much variety to customize V's character, only for their driving force kickstarting the story to always be exactly the same. Isn't this antithetical to the customization of V?

Despite these two, I still regard Cyberpunk among the greatest RPGs. The story is one of the better video game stories. Frequently, RPGs suffer from the exponential writing needed to make it work, and I think Cyberpunk nailed both the execution of the main story beats, as well as flexibility in responding to my play-style. Проходил игру как до релиза 2.0 патча (или что там было), так и после+дополнение.

Честно говоря, не особо заметил какие там серьёзные изменения все эти патчи и обновления привнесли. Игра как была кривой, так и осталась (вспоминаем кулачные бои). Вряд ли ключевые механики можно пофиксить просто патчами.

Есть ли баги? Да, есть. Не особо много, конечно, но попадались такие, что портили/мешали прохождению.
Игра местами очень жёстко заскриптована. Доходило до того, что проходя по стелсу, дойдя до определённого триггера, срабатывает тревога и на тебя все агрятся. И нет, это не ты что-то делаешь неправильно. Это просто скрипт срабатывает, но делает он это очень криво.

Производительность всё ещё хромает. Опустим Ray Tracing, у меня всё же не Нвидиа, но даже без него, на разрешении 3440х1440 фпс часто может падать до 60 и даже ниже. А ПК у меня явно не слабый.

Мир игры, по сути, пустой. Город ничем непримечательный. Ну он есть и есть. Вообще, в игре про киберпанк, очень мало киберпанка. Он ощущается только когда ты проходишь сюжетные миссии, где есть хоть какая-то постановка, кинематографичность и прочее.
Стоит только отойти от сюжета (который сам по себе очень короткий), начинается самый обыкновенный гринд и самые примитивные побочные квесты. И дух киберпанка просто улетучивается. Вот вроде город есть, будущее есть, технологии есть, а киберпанка нет.
Чёрт, даже в Deus Ex Human Revolution киберпанка больше чем тут.

Персонажи? Ну да, они есть, но мне было на большинство откровенно плевать. Игра часто пытается выжать драму или слезинку, но ты с персонажами от силы побегал пару игровых дней или пару часов в реальной жизни. Особенно это касается Джеки. После похорон игра практически забывает про него, как и ты сам.

За Джонни особо сказать нечего. Всю игру он ведёт себя как мудила и лишь в конце ты немного начинаешь проявлять к нему симпатию. В DLC с этим намного лучше, он там больше раскрывается как персонаж и меньше тебя раздражает.

Сам V, как минимум, в агнл.озвучке, очень часто срывается на эмоции или начинает говорить странным голосом, когда причин для этого нет. Намеренная драма? Кто знает.

Все секции с Джонни и роком вообще оставили меня равнодушным. Как вяжутся рокер, ядерная бомба, бунт против корпораций—хз. Да, Джонни пару раз говорит какие корпорации плохие, как страдают люди, но на этом всё. Мотивация есть, но как по мне, она очень слабенькая чтобы пойти взрывать ядерку (что, кстати, непонятно что дало и вообще мув очень сомнительный).
Рокерная составляющая местами романтизирована и непонятно, зачем всю эту музыку приплетать к игре и в сюжет.

Сам геймплей, по большей части, приятный. Именно стрельба, взломы и т.д. Но больше сказать особо и нечего.
Важно отметить то, что в игре очень много чего происходит просто потому что сценаристам там захотелось, а не по какой-то логике или законам мира.
И из-за этого, геймплейная (игровая) составляющая очень часто идёт в разрез с тем, что показывают сценаристы.
А печально то, что люди это поддерживают, аргументируя в духе "да просто наслаждайся сюжетом что дают" или "не пытайся всё сравнивать с игровым V, вот каноничный V сделал бы..." и так далее. Звучит как полный бред, но да, такие люди среди нас существуют.
Во-первых, сюжет в игре не то чтобы какой-то шедевр, чтобы им наслаждаться.
Во-вторых, сюжет так-то очень короткий.
В-третьих, зачем тогда мы играем в игру, если можно было сделать аниме/фильм/сериал и рассказать свою историю?
Это относится и к самим концовкам. Они все "плохие" ну просто потому что сценаристам там захотелось. 
Где-то внезапные комы, где-то стандартное оправдание про "нанитов/нанотехнологии" и т.д. Надо строго придерживаться мантры "В Night City хэппиэнда нет"

Отдельно стоит упомянуть и секретную концовку. Оставим сам геймплей. Чтобы выйти на неё, тебе во второстепенной миссии надо выбрать специальные варианты ответа, а потом ещё и подождать какое-то время. Люди на неё выходили чисто случайно, уйдя в туалет или заваривая чай, пока V сидит на крыше. Я понимаю, секретная концовка и всё такое, но можно же было сделать выход на неё более адекватным? В том же третьем Ведьмаке варианты выхода на хорошую концовку были намного более очевидными и логичными.

Также важно отметить, что возможно, кто-то захочет проходить с минимум имплантов. Так вот, игра так-то не предлагает каких-то особых возможностей для этого. Да, есть дерево скиллов, там есть полезные скиллы в начале и середине, но финальные уровни бесполезны.
Поэтому, играя на максимальной сложности и на секретную концовку, битва со Смэшером может быть напряжной.

Когда речь заходит о лоре, у тебя возникает очень много вопросов. Игра (как и персонажи) очень редко удосуживаются дать ответы, а когда лезешь искать их на вики, вопросов становится ещё больше. Может для этого надо настолки штрудировать, но я как-то рвения не испытываю.

В общем, пропустив эту игру, вы не потеряете толком ничего. По скидке можно взять, да, а можно и не брать и поиграть во что-то другое.

Вроде как команда, отвечающая за вторую часть, переехала в США, да ещё и перешла на UE.
Если это правда, стоит ли ожидать от второй части какого-то прорыва или откровений? Я думаю, нет. Скорее, навалят ещё больше контента для modern audiences.

Visuellement, il y a peu à redire : Night City claque sévèrement. L'ambiance futuriste, la verticalité et la densité de la ville marchent du tonnerre pour l'immersion, c'est un régal à explorer de fond en comble pour chopper tous les recoins.

Côté écriture, l'aventure principale et les quêtes annexes assurent, vraiment un des rares jeux ou les quêtes secondaires méritent d'être faites et on un sens réels car on rentre dans les détails des personnages secondaires et ce n'est pas des quêtes ou il faut juste aller d'un point A vers un point B pour déposer une lettre. La vraie bonne surprise vient du ton : le jeu sait se montrer étonnamment drôle et cynique par moments, surtout grâce aux interventions permanentes de Johnny qui dans notre tête qui apportent une vraie dynamique au duo. Ça casse le côté ultra-sombre juste ce qu'il faut. L'extension Phantom Liberty rajoute une couche d'espionnage bien ficelée qui élève encore le niveau global.

Mention spéciale aux différentes fins du jeu qui sont vraiment génialissimes. Chacune propose une conclusion percutante, des choix qui ont du poids et une écriture qui marque les esprits bien après avoir lâché le jeu. Viser le 100 % des succès demande de s'y investir un minimum en temps, mais ça permet de profiter de tout ce que le titre a dans le ventre sans aucune frustration. Bref, j'ai tout kiffé du début à la fin, un très gros morceau à faire.

Full blown reality junkie, getting gigs done, no matter the fixer. From zeroing gangers and corpos, klepping shards or rides, and cracking ICE for prime detes. For real though, thanks to CD for bringing this world to life and most of all thank you Mike Pondsmith for making such an immersive world. the nitty gritty gray area of Night City is so good, a dystopia clad in neon facades. beautiful on the surface, but horrifying in it's reality. Such a well written story, with so many possible endings, all of which, while not "good", are incredibly satisfying. It's like a choose your own adventure novel, and the outcome reflects the choices you make. I've played so many different V's, but in the end they're all *ME*. I can sympathize with all of their paths in some way. I still have more paths to walk and more secrets to find, even 250+ hours in.

Лучшая игра, которую я проходил.
Несмотря на плохой старт (меня он не касался, тогда еще не заинтересовала игра), игра спустя год-два стала тем, чем должна была стать до. На данный момент - шедевр, который мы узрим, взглянув на нынешний геймдев, предпоследний раз в данном десятилетии. Такой проработки лора, звука (саундтреков), визуала и мира не везде встретишь. Да, это РПГ, где для секретной концовки надо неплохо себя подготовить, в ином случае ожидай порванную жопу в фойе Арасаки или вентиляцию в голове от Смэшера. 
Кстати, о героях. Каждый персонаж имеет свой характер и взгляды, ты понимаешь их ценности, а иногда  - ценишь их. Вспомнить только момент, когда при тебе погибает товарищ - Джеки Уэллс. Здесь только больной человек не почувствует потерю, хоть это и "просто пиксели". Так-то таких моментов в геймдеве не особо много: подобное я запечатлел в Metro: Исход.
О предысториях: имхо, но корпорат - канон. Как и Сильверхенд, тебя поимела гигантская контора, а теперь тебе надо её уничтожить. Больше сказать нечего на сей счёт.
Хотелось бы коснуться и DLC. Как по мне, это отлично пройденное время. Если докопаться, то как-будто резко нам всех героев дали. Какая-то Сойка, Рид, Майерс... Однако DLC меня очень заинтересовало другим: это не просто миссии "принеси-подай"/"убей"/"сделай", а целая серия заданий, содержащая шпионаж, вопросы жизни и смерти. По локациям удивил бункер. Объективно, с натяжкой, но повеяло Resident Evil 2: дается бункер, карта и робот, пытающийся "пощекотать" голову или брюхо (на деле проткнёт твою тушу). В общем дополнение имеет скорее мрачный стиль: темные локации (Привет тем, кто играет днём), гробовую тишину.
Подытожу: Cyberpunk 2077 - замечательный продукт, заслуживший внимание КАЖДОГО геймера. Это не копия/альтернатива GTA или Deus Ex (хотя дх и кп (как игра) имеют общий источник идеи), а реально качественная AAA-игра, которую почему-то практически проигнорировали на игровых премиях, относительно других проектов.
不推荐。虽然说是现在和发售时已经一个天上一个地下了，但是这和我期待的完全不一样。帮派内容单调，游戏内容少，连浮空车都不能驾驶。本体主线大概50小时，剧情跳脱，明显删除了很多东西。个人主观打分65

Hablar de Cyberpunk 2077 no es hablar solo de gráficos increíbles o de mecánicas de disparos impecables es hablar de Night City, una metrópoli de neón, lluvia y asfalto que se siente tan viva, vibrante y desalmada como fascinante. Night City feels genuinely lived-in, the lore and history behind the world is deep without being overwhelming, and it rewards players who like piecing together a dystopian future through environmental detail, shards, and side conversations.

The story and characters carry the experience. V's arc and the supporting cast are well written, with enough weight to keep you invested from start to finish. Visually the city is a standout, dense, varied, and atmospheric block to block. The soundtrack and in-world radio stations round it out nicely, adding a lot of personality to just driving or walking around.

It's not a flawless game, but the core experience (world, story, atmosphere) is strong enough to make it an easy recommend, especially if you're into dystopian sci-fi.

[b]One of the Greatest Comeback Stories in Video Game History[/b]

I had started this when it first came out way back in 2020 on the Series X. Dropped off a few times as I was studying exams and lost track of the narrative and it remained benched.

Enter 2026! Cyberpunk 2077 is a triumph! What an insane experience to engage with this after the incredible amount of overhauling CDPR have done over the years. This, arguably is now the only way it should be played and I am SO GLAD I inadvertently waiting this long to play it.

CDPR have managed to turn something that was one of the most horrific openings of all time for a video game into something that is now in many circle regarded as a masterpiece.

The world is gorgeous and running on a suped up PC rig with path tracing is a true sight to behold. I'm over 100 hours in and still stop to admire the eye candy. More importantly is the story being told. Here we have a bleak view of the future where corporate giants rule the world crushing the environment with dangerous AI and other nefarious groups running amok. Sounds familiar right?

Cyberpunk is probably more relevant today than it ever has been. Listening to Johnny Silverhand, the incredibly cast Keanu Reeves, rant about tech giants obliterating farmland is somewhat scary as we are watching that very same thing happen in 2026 with these new large data centres.

The game pulls on so many sci-fi influences, the love it have for Neuromancer and Gibsons work is evident and there are so many little awesome easter eggs if you are already initiated. The musical score is equally evocative and does so much heavy lifting in the games dramatic and emotional moments. Moments that will be seared into your meat sponge for a long time.

Ultimately this is a story about what it means to be human, dealing with loss and time running out. By the end I was genuinely a bit broken and this stands as clear evidence that video games are art. No piece of media has been able to drag me along the same dystopian journey that this game has. 

Buckle up choom. If you haven't played this, now is the time.

I'm not much of a guy for story games, but this is genuinely one of the greatest games I have ever played.
[hr][/hr]
[h1]GENERAL RATINGS: [/h1]
[h2]Story: [/h2]
Incredibly well-written. The story is genuinely so interesting that even side missions, gigs, or those random data chips with archived conversations are worth looking into. In fact, even though I'm a guy who usually spams the skip button, I like to occasionally take the time to learn about Cyberpunk, it's lore, and even some of the more nitty-gritty details with things like Maximum Mike, the Cyberpunk 2020 TTRPG, etc.

[i] - Side note: You should 100% check out the anime/show Cyberpunk Edgerunners. In game, I also recommend setting your radio to 107.3 Morro Rock Radio, as it's basically a podcast of theories by "Maximum Mike," voiced by Mike Pondsmith, the original creator of the Cyberpunk Series. [/i]

[h2]Graphics: [/h2]
Top-tier with an amazing environment to simply roam around in, but slightly rig dependent if you want something truly amazing. Still, it can look amazing even on the lowest settings.

[h2]Gameplay Loop and Upgrades: [/h2]
Pre-2.0 I heard that the gameplay loop wasn't the greatest, with a stale upgrade system that never gave anything meaningful. Now, it has been fleshed out so that almost every single major module makes it feel like you didn't waste time grinding for a higher level.

[h2]DLC: [/h2]
Genuinely amazing. I consider this one of the best DLC/Expansions made for a game. It's a true expansion with a new part of the map that flips the experience of Night City on its head while still keeping the dark cyberpunk vibe. Ending was open-ended, which some people consider bad. Personally, I think it was one of the better endings.
[hr][/hr]
[h1]MISC. RATINGS: [/h1]
[h2]Complaints: [/h2]
The only thing that is truly missing here is maybe some depth with a few fixers around the map, as I would have loved to see more from fixers like El Capitán. Gigs were awesome overall though (however, some of the NCPD scanner missions did get stale after a little bit). Still though, the game only feels like a grind if YOU choose to grind.

[h2]My Experience in a Nutshell: [/h2]
Currently, I have around 90 hours on it and I have almost 100% finished the game aside from 2 of the DLC endings, of which I plan to complete on my new second playthrough. This game is able to perfectly balance a linear story that you can quickly complete, as well as an immersive open-world that you can spend tens if not hundreds of hours in if you choose to.

[h1]Final Remarks: [/h1]
This game may not be perfect, but no matter what people say, I can confidently say that this game will not be a waste of your time if you simply give it a try (and that includes the absolutely amazing DLC that is Phantom Liberty).

Bom, o que dizer sobre Cyberpunk?

Primeiramente: é um excelente jogo! Em segundo lugar: possui uma narrativa e uma jogabilidade fantásticas. O que mais me atraiu a jogar foi, sem dúvida, a história, um aspecto em que a produtora sempre se destaca. Consegui evitar muitos spoilers desde o lançamento, e foram 120 horas que passaram rapidamente — assim como a vida em Night City.

Quanto à história, achei-a incrível. Os personagens são extremamente memoráveis, como Jackie, Viktor, River, Judy, Panam, Takemura e, especialmente, Johnny. Apreciei todas as missões secundárias e a DLC, que foi uma adição monumental à trama, trazendo ainda mais profundidade com Dogtown.

O tempo que passei explorando Night City sem um destino certo, ouvindo as músicas tema de Cyberpunk: Edgerunners nas rádios junto com Kartel Sonoro na 98.7 e 106.9, foi simplesmente maravilhoso.

E sobre o final... não há muito o que dizer. Experimentei todos os finais, mas só posso afirmar uma coisa: NÃO HÁ FINAL FELIZ EM NIGHT CITY.

Entretanto, eu amei e ainda amo essa cidade. Dito isso: Boa noite, Night City

When I first played the game, the bugs utterly killed any interest I could have had for it. A crafting error wiped my entire nine hour save and I had no interest in playing it again.
Then Phantom Liberty dropped a few years ago, and people were calling it one of the best games of the decade; I remained unconvinced, because I’m a stubborn bastard.
Then, recently, I reinstalled it on a whim when there was a lull in my backlog. I figured if they fixed all the major bugs, there’s no harm in giving it another shot, right? I don’t lose another sixty dollars.

That turned out to be one of the best decisions I’ve made in my entire life.
I say this to you, dear reader, with no hyperbole, no sensationalist overhyping or overselling of facts: Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the greatest games I have ever had the pleasure of playing. 

Mike Pondsmith’s gritty, dark and morally-corrupt neon-concrete playground comes truly alive.
It’s simply one of those games that you can completely lose yourself in; I spent about a five hour stretch just walking through Night City, no car, just strolling one end of town down the other and back, walking down the street and taking in the sights and vibes. I didn’t even realize I did it at first until I heard birds chirping outside my window, and my first thought wasn’t “holy crap, it’s morning now”, it was “wait a minute, there’s no birds in Corpo Plaza”. 

It isn’t just the visuals or themes that completely sell me, the narrative is utterly gripping. Even the most unassuming side quest will suddenly grab you by the throat and make you question your ideals in a city that thrives on grinding them into paste. I went from disassociating after dealing with a vile serial killer, to playing laser tag with my friend’s kids at a cookout, and the very next day I talked a sentient car off a ledge after disposing of some corpo’s body for the Japanese mob. Take your time and do all the side content you can, because all of them have little nuggets of gold in them. You will completely regret it if you just do the main story. When you do work at the main story, I strongly suggest you get to know Johnny Silverhand; he’s a remarkably deep lake of insight and character development where I initially saw a jerkass puddle of self-importance. He steals the show in literally every scene he is in - which is a lot, considering he can jump into them at any time he feels like.

You do yourself a disservice if you don’t dedicate a portion of your time to this game. I’m not ashamed to admit it’s life-altering, and the kind of person that comes out of the other end of NC is based solely on your choices, which is refreshing in an industry seemingly built on the illusion of choice. 
Welcome to the City of Dreams. You won’t regret it.

Le jeu de base a connu un lancement catastrophique. Je l'avais rushé et j'étais plutôt déçu, moi qui l'attendais comme un nouveau GTA... Je l'ai refait récemment et les dévs l'ont quand même amélioré.

Je vais commencer par citer les points positifs, puis les négatifs.

Le plus gros point positif du jeu est tout simplement son ambiance qui est, selon moi, la meilleure à ce jour de tous les jeux vidéo. Night City est juste magnifique, surtout de nuit, on est en totale immersion.

Ensuite, le gameplay. Pour un RPG, il est varié : on peut jouer de plein de façons différentes (katana, couteau, armes à feu, hacker netrunner, etc.). On prend plaisir à améliorer son perso avec toutes les upgrades et on ressent la montée en puissance au fur et à mesure.

L'histoire est bien écrite et plaisante à suivre, on dirait un film, surtout avec l'ajout du DLC qui finit en beauté le scénario du jeu principal.

Le contenu est également très bon : il y a une multitude de missions annexes intéressantes, plein d'activités sympas et d'objets à trouver. Tout ça renforce la durée de vie du jeu.

Malheureusement, tous ces points positifs sont entachés par de nombreux défauts, à commencer par les bugs. Et je ne parle pas de petits bugs comme on a l'habitude d'en voir dans les jeux. Non, là, il y a carrément des bugs qui plombent l'immersion et qui obligent à relancer la mission (j'ai déjà vu des persos censés être morts qui se sont volatilisés, des objectifs qui disparaissent de la map et deviennent donc impossibles à récupérer, des flics qui font du surf sur leurs bécanes... J'en passe et des meilleures).

Deuxième point négatif, et pas des moindres : l'IA catastrophique. Les ennemis sont archi cons, les flics ne représentent aucune menace. Plusieurs fois pendant les fights, on assiste à des comportements débiles qui cassent le rythme du jeu. On a l'impression de jouer à un jeu fait par des amateurs par moments.

La verticalité est également un gros défaut : aucun hélico, aucune voiture volante dans un jeu comme ça, et surtout dans cette ville si bien faite. C'est un crime de ne pas avoir la liberté de se déplacer où l'on veut. On peut certes nager, mais les fonds marins ont des textures de Nintendo 64. Aucune vie maritime, pas de bateau ni de jet-ski, vraiment naze pour un monde ouvert.

Autre problème : la vue FPS imposée. C'est bien beau de pouvoir customiser son perso avec un milliard de cosmétiques, mais si c'est pour ne le voir qu'en voiture ou à moto, ce n'est pas la peine. Ils auraient dû mettre l'option de choisir entre la troisième et la première personne, comme dans Skyrim, par exemple.

La conduite est tout simplement l'une des pires de l'histoire des jeux vidéo.

Enfin, dernier défaut selon moi : le manque de multi. Même si, au vu de la qualité du jeu solo, ce n'est pas plus mal qu'il n'y en ait pas. Les dévs galèrent déjà à nous pondre un jeu solo de qualité, je pense qu'ils n'ont pas le niveau pour le online, ça aurait été merdique à souhait aussi.

Les radios du jeu sont parmi les pires, ce qui est dommage, car quelques musiques d'ambiance ainsi que celle de l'outro de Phantom Liberty sont tout simplement exceptionnelles.

Sachant tout ça, si je devais mettre une note, ce serait 14/20 dans son état actuel (à sa sortie, on était plutôt sur un 9/20).

If someone ask me what is my most favorite game, I say Cyperpunk 2077. Isn't that enough?

I spent the first hour admiring my character in every mirror, accidentally punched a random civilian trying to open a door, got flattened by a car while crossing the street, and somehow still felt like the coolest person alive.
Night City has a funny way of making you feel unstoppable one minute and completely insignificant the next.
One mission has you blasting through enemies with an arsenal that would make an army jealous. The next has you sitting on a rooftop, talking to someone about life, regret, and the choices that brought them there.
And that's when the game quietly sneaks up on you.
I came for the explosions, the cyberware, the fast cars, and the overpowered builds.

I stayed because of the people.

Every character feels like they have a life outside of your story. Some make you laugh, some frustrate you, and some leave a mark that stays with you long after the credits roll. Even the smallest side gigs often tell stories that are more emotional than entire games.

Then there's Johnny Silverhand.

At first, he's the last person you'd want living in your head. Sarcastic, arrogant, constantly reminding you that your life isn't exactly going according to plan.
But somewhere along the way, without even realizing it, the arguments become conversations, the conversations become understanding, and the understanding becomes friendship.
I never expected to care so much about someone who technically shouldn't even exist.

Night City itself deserves its own award.

It's beautiful, chaotic, cruel, loud, vibrant, and strangely comforting all at once. Every alley has a story. Every neon sign hides another tragedy. Every district feels alive, whether you're racing through it at full speed or simply walking with the radio playing in the background.

For all its violence and chaos, Cyberpunk 2077 constantly asks one simple question:

**"What kind of person do you want to be when the world is trying to turn you into something else?"**
Very few games have made me laugh as much as this one.
Very few games have made me stop moving just to listen to a conversation.
And very, very few games have left me staring at the credits, not because I was waiting for a post-credit scene... but because I wasn't ready to say goodbye.

Cyberpunk 2077 isn't just about saving Night City.

It's about finding pieces of yourself in a city that never stops taking from people.
I thought I was buying an open-world RPG.
I ended up with memories I'll probably carry for years.

Aliás, os personagens em geral são um dos pontos mais fortes do jogo: cada um tem personalidade, motivações e desenvolvimento muito bem construídos.

A jogabilidade também merece destaque. Há uma enorme variedade de armas, implantes cibernéticos, árvores de habilidades e estilos de combate. Você pode montar uma build focada em hacking, furtividade, katanas, armas pesadas ou misturar tudo isso, o que deixa cada gameplay única. A exploração também é extremamente recompensadora, sempre há algo interessante para descobrir em Night City.

Quanto aos bugs, durante toda a minha campanha encontrei apenas alguns problemas menores, nada que comprometesse a experiência ou atrapalhasse a diversão. É impressionante ver o quanto o jogo evoluiu desde 2020.

Durante vários momentos da minha jornada senti a mesma empolgação que tinha quando era criança e ganhava um jogo novo. Eu queria explorar cada lugar, completar todas as missões, descobrir todos os segredos e simplesmente passar mais tempo naquele mundo. Fazia tempo que um jogo não despertava essa sensação em mim.

No fim das contas, Cyberpunk 2077 entrou facilmente para a lista dos meus jogos favoritos. É um jogo que merece uma segunda chance de quem desistiu dele no lançamento. Se você ainda não jogou por causa da má fama inicial, dê uma oportunidade. Hoje ele é um dos melhores RPGs de mundo aberto disponíveis e, na minha opinião, vale muito a pena.

Falando sobre **Cyberpunk**:

Eu achei um jogo muito foda, com muitas side quests que, infelizmente, não importam para a história, mas que levam um bom peso narrativo. Ver pessoas que você ajudou simplesmente se morrendo é meio foda, porque você, aos poucos, entende que o melhor que pode fazer em Night City é sair de lá, deixar tudo que pensou sobre ser o maior de lá e fugir para um lugar de verdade, um lugar onde, quando você morrer, alguém fique triste e você não seja só mais um corpo jogado no lixão, igual às lendas do próprio game, como o Johnny e o Rache Bartmoss. Fala sério, na lore os caras eram monstros, mas, no final, um deles está em uma geladeira e o outro está jogado em um terreno baldio. E, no final, você achou que ia fugir da espiral e virou só mais um no sistema.

Mas, após ver o anime, eu senti falta daquela loucura mostrada. Pô, é mais perigoso andar em SÃO PAULO do que em um mundo dito como o inferno na Terra, onde dizem que tem insanos por todo lado e você pode morrer a qualquer momento.

Sobre a gameplay:

Muito boa, não tem como negar. Minha única visão de falha foi: **PQ KCT SÓ POSSO RESETAR ATRIBUTOS 1 VEZ? PUTA QUE PARIU!** Se eu quiser fazer uma nova build, tenho que jogar tudo de novo, vai se foder. Mas o game é bom, completo e muito foda. Eu joguei com hacks, uma sniper, além da escopeta, então gostei muito de jogar metralhando tudo e, ao mesmo tempo, me escondendo e pegando os caras por trás (ain). Ou seja, realmente vale a pena. É um jogo que, na minha visão, vale 80 reais, vale um valor desses. Claro, não peguei o hype nem as promessas, então, para mim, o jogo está bem completo, com muitas habilidades e estilos de jogo. As únicas reclamações seriam sobre o sistema de upgrade, onde eu não posso upar tudo ao máximo e não posso ficar mudando de build. Mesmo que fosse necessário só pegar um item, eu faria isso muito fácil.

**Nota final: 8/10.** Ótima história, ótimos personagens, péssimo mundo (isso é um elogio, tá? Morra, Night City).
