Night City is a dystopian masterpiece
The city isn't just a map it is a living character that suffocates you with its vibe.
The scale is overwhelming you look up and see massive megabuildings casting shadows over neon drenched alleys packed with vendors, cyberpunks, and garbage.
Kabuki and Japantown feel claustrophobic and alive with bright neon signs and dense crowds.
Pacifica feels like a warzone completely isolated from corporate control. 
The Badlands offer a massive, dust choked contrast where you can just throttle willy nilly on a bike. The environmental storytelling is everywhere with much more to find  then you think if you look around for stuff. 
these are just a few of many places i listed.

as for the gameplay The gameplay hits a super satisfying rhythm because it stops playing like a standard shooter and lets you become an absolute monster. The gunplay is heavy and punchy, especially when using tech weapons that punch through solid concrete walls or smart guns that track targets around corners.
The build variety is where the game actually excels

The Sandevistan build lets you activate a neural implant to slow down time, letting you run circles around enemies and slice them to pieces with a katana before they can even draw their weapons.
Mantis Blades and Gorilla Arms turn your own body into a lethal weapon, making close-quarters combat incredibly brutal.
Quickhack builds turn you into a ghost, allowing you to wipe out an entire building of guards without firing a shot by forcing their cyberware to self detonate or burn them alive from the inside out. or even kill themself 
theres many more builds out there these are just a few

The side quests aren't just filler either major storylines involving characters like Judy, Panam, or River feel just as fleshed out and emotional as the main plot. Vehicle handling takes some getting used to, and some of the minor fixer gigs can feel a bit repetitive, which is why the gameplay is an 8/10 for me. But when you are fully kitted out with cyberware and sliding through a firefight, the power trip is unmatched.

One thing you notice pretty quickly is that the clothing options are totally unbalanced. If you play as a guy, the male fashion choices feel lowkey mid and kinda trash. Meanwhile, the female clothing options get all the drip everything looks amazing, stylish, and actually fits the futuristic cyberpunk aesthetic perfectly. It wasn't an issue for me at all because I always prefer playing as a girl in most games anyway, but if you’re a dude who wants to play as a male V and look cool, the lack of good male drip is definitely going to annoy you.


The absolute best part of the game imo is Johnny Silverhand.
At first, I lowkey thought he was just a loud annoying terrorist.
I hated having this toxic digital ghost constantly trash talk me and all my choices i made (even if you drive to fast) most interactions force you to choose to follow with or against his radical philosophy that could cost you your life.
He felt like a nuisance stuck in V's head. He pops up as a hologram out of nowhere to talk shit on all the people you talk to. (they cant see or hear him)
But the writing is and gets so deep that your relationship actually evolves.
The more I played, the more I actually started to understand him.
His tragic backstory and cynical worldview completely won me over. not to mention his amazingly curated personality 
Hes an ego driven rockstar who masks his massive regrets with arrogance and dark humor and he holds up a mirror to the darkest parts of Night City, making you question who the real villains are.
but the friction slowly turns into understanding. You watch this deeply flawed, egoist slowly lower his guard and show real humanity. The transition happens so naturally that you don't even realize how close you've become until it all hits you. He goes from a parasite wanting you dead to someone who genuinely puts his own existence on the line just to save your life. By the end, they share an unbreakable bond out of shared trauma and mutual respect. Their banter, their quiet moments of vulnerability, and that shift from bitter enemies to true brothers-in-arms (i played as a girl) is easily one of my favorite story arcs in video game history. Keanu Reeves and the writing team absolutely cooked. 
Johnny Silverhand is now my favorite side character of all time and Honestly, calling him a "side character" feels like an insult. He is literally the co-protagonist. His dynamic with V is the beating heart of the whole story. Keanu Reeves fucking cooked with this performance.

bug，这方面还真是没招，在刚开始的bug77时代我并没有入坑但已经早有耳闻，后来财力颇丰拿下游戏，bug已经修了90%往上了感觉，至少大多数时候我不会遇到。但跑图的时候还是会不经意遇到一些小惊喜，这点倒是无伤大雅，但是我有一个掉落物卡地下了一直亮橙X但是捡不到，我本来以为大退那玩意会刷新结果还是在那里(๑⁼̴̀д⁼̴́๑)可恶。
剧情，这一点没什么好说的，没什么大问题。你是一个雇佣兵，一个杀手，一个求生的将死之人，剧情里含有大量的的暴力桥段，如果与你三观不合那还是劳烦你还是移架别处吧。剧情中遇到的小boss如果没杀或者某些特殊NPC的对话选错了会丢失一些获得不朽级武器的机会，如果你买了DLC，狗镇里会有一个商人卖这些武器，没买就只能遗憾了。
现在这个游戏的优化和剧情已经可以评为优异了，DLC的确成为了这个游戏的很大一个卖点，不过本体给你的体验也不会差劲，不用担心现在的财力不足让你在赛博都市不得安生。(≖‿≖)✧

Não joguei Cyberpunk 2077 no lançamento, já peguei ele junto com a adição de Phantom Liberty e posso dizer que a minha experiência foi INCRÍVEL!

Destaque especial para a história, tanto da campanha principal quanto a expansão. A ambientação é outro patamar, Night City é uma verdadeira metrópole distópica perfeitamente cativante e opressiva. Você também possui bastante liberdade para escolher como vai fazer as missões por meio de uma build totalmente personalizável.

Sobre pontos negativos, acredito que os bugs remanescentes e crashes sejam ainda os que mais incomodam. E apesar do mundo aberto ser impecável na parte da ambientação, os NPCs deixam a desejar. Suas rotinas são muito artificiais, todos são limitados e faltam detalhes para deixar o mundo realmente vivo nesse aspecto.

Dito isso, o restante do game é absurdamente bom, um dos poucos que eu realmente fui atrás de fazer todos os conteúdos extras, já que NADA é repetitivo. Vale a pena.

Cyberpunk 2077 é, sem dúvida, meu jogo favorito.

O que mais me impressiona nele não é apenas a estética futurista, a violência de Night City ou a liberdade de exploração, mas a forma como o jogo consegue criar vínculos reais entre o jogador e seus personagens. É surpreendente o quanto nos apegamos a pessoas que, tecnicamente, são apenas parte de uma narrativa digital, mas que parecem ter peso, história, falhas, desejos e contradições muito humanas.

Night City é um cenário que parece simples à primeira vista: uma cidade caótica, dominada por corporações, violência, ambição e sobrevivência. Mas, quanto mais você joga, mais percebe que existe uma complexidade enorme por trás de cada escolha, cada missão e cada relação. O mundo é cruel, exagerado e estilizado, mas ao mesmo tempo parece assustadoramente real. Existe uma sensação constante de que suas ações importam, mesmo quando o próprio jogo deixa claro que você não tem controle sobre tudo.

Eu nunca fui muito apegada a histórias excessivamente dramáticas, muito menos a narrativas em que a tristeza parece inevitável. Normalmente, finais melancólicos ou tragédias não são o tipo de coisa que me atrai. Mas Cyberpunk foi uma exceção. Talvez porque o jogo não use o sofrimento apenas para chocar; ele usa para construir significado. A dor dos personagens, as perdas, os dilemas e até os finais amargos parecem fazer parte da identidade da obra.

Mesmo que Night City não seja um lugar de finais felizes, Cyberpunk 2077 conseguiu me marcar profundamente. É uma história sobre sobrevivência, identidade, amor, memória, liberdade e sobre o quanto uma pessoa ainda pode tentar deixar uma marca em um mundo que insiste em apagá-la. E talvez seja exatamente isso que torna o jogo tão especial: ele não promete conforto, mas entrega intensidade. Não promete salvação, mas entrega humanidade.

Брат подарил мне эту игру вместе с дополнением Phantom Liberty, и это определенно лучшее, во что я играл за всё время. Кто же знал, что Найт-Сити так намертво затянет и заставит сидеть с тяжелым экзистенциальным кризисом после финала.
Коротко о главном:
Джонни Сильверхенд — этот цифровой террорист в моей голове комментировал каждый мой шаг и постоянно ворчал, но черт возьми, он просто самый трушный, харизматичный и невероятно крутой мужик во всей игре. Киану выдал абсолютную базу.
Phantom Liberty — дополнение вышло монументальным, это мрачный шпионский триллер с кучей интриг, предательств и крутой новой локацией. А француженка Аврора Кассель — это вообще отдельный вид искусства, харизма и эстетика в чистом виде, она моментально крадет всё внимание на экране.
Джуди Альварес — играл за женскую версию Ви, и это было лучшее решение. Джуди — абсолютное сокровище, ради её улыбки стоило пройти через весь этот ад.
Основной сюжет и его финалы — тяжелые концовки основной игры заслуживают отдельного упоминания. CD Projekt RED создали невероятно сильную драму, где нет однозначного «хэппи-энда». Каждый финал оставляет глубокий след, заставляя по-настоящему страдать и переживать за судьбу Ви.
Огромное спасибо брату за такой крутой подарок.
После прохождения Phantom Liberty я сразу побежал моддить игру, наставил кучу всего, и теперь мне хочется возвращаться в этот мир снова и снова — игра вообще не надоедает. Хоть концовки и оставляют мощное, щемящее чувство опустошения, это было чертовски сильное и эмоциональное приключение.
10 выплаканных электронных слез из 10. Пойду обниму Джуди ;3 (в своих мыслях).

Comprei Cyberpunk 2077 no lançamento, em dezembro de 2020. Na época, o jogo estava longe do estado ideal: havia diversos bugs, glitches, problemas de desempenho e várias mecânicas que não funcionavam como o esperado. Mesmo assim, eu conseguia me divertir explorando Night City e acompanhando a história principal.

Decidi jogar novamente este ano e a diferença é impressionante. Após anos de atualizações, correções e melhorias feitas pela CD Projekt Red, o jogo se transformou completamente. Hoje, Cyberpunk 2077 é uma experiência muito mais polida, estável e imersiva do que era no lançamento.

O que mais me marcou foi a qualidade da narrativa. Os personagens são extremamente bem escritos, cada um com sua própria personalidade, motivações e conflitos. Ao longo da jornada, acabei me envolvendo emocionalmente com várias histórias secundárias, algo que poucos jogos conseguem fazer tão bem. Completei todos os finais disponíveis e cada um deles trouxe reflexões diferentes sobre os temas centrais do jogo, como identidade, humanidade, ambição e mortalidade.

Outro aspecto que gostei muito foi a evolução do personagem. O sistema de progressão oferece diversas formas de construir o seu V, seja focando em combate direto, furtividade, hackeamento ou uma mistura de estilos. Os implantes cibernéticos também são um dos pontos altos da experiência, permitindo modificar o corpo do personagem com novas habilidades e tecnologias que realmente impactam a jogabilidade.

Além disso, a ambientação futurista de Night City é simplesmente incrível. A cidade é vibrante, cheia de detalhes e transmite perfeitamente a sensação de viver em um mundo dominado pela tecnologia, pelas megacorporações e pelas desigualdades sociais. A direção de arte, a trilha sonora e a atmosfera contribuem para tornar o universo de Cyberpunk extremamente imersivo.

E o mais impressionante é que ainda nem joguei a expansão Phantom Liberty. Pelo que vi da comunidade e das análises, ela é considerada uma das melhores expansões já lançadas para um RPG moderno, trazendo uma nova região para explorar, personagens marcantes e uma história de altíssima qualidade. Se a campanha principal já me proporcionou uma experiência tão positiva, minhas expectativas para a expansão são ainda maiores.

Na minha opinião, Cyberpunk 2077 representa um dos maiores retornos da história dos videogames. A CD Projekt Red conseguiu recuperar a confiança de muitos jogadores após um lançamento extremamente conturbado e entregou um RPG memorável. Recomendo fortemente para qualquer pessoa que goste de jogos de RPG, progressão de personagem, liberdade de construção, ficção científica e histórias marcantes. Foi uma experiência que me surpreendeu positivamente e que certamente ficará entre os melhores jogos que já joguei. 🤠

*Cyberpunk 2077* is one of those games that stayed with me long after I closed it.

At first, Night City feels exciting. The lights, the cars, the clubs, the implants, the advertisements, the gangs, the weapons, everything looks loud and alive. But the longer I stayed there, the more I felt that the city was not alive in a beautiful way. It was alive like a machine that keeps eating people. Everyone in Night City wants something: money, fame, power, revenge, survival, a way out. But almost nobody gets out clean.

V’s story hit me because it starts with such a simple dream. V and Jackie do not want to save the world. They just want to become legends. They want their names remembered at the Afterlife. That dream sounds cool at first, especially when Jackie is there laughing, talking big, and making the city feel less lonely. Jackie gives the early game its heart. He makes V’s ambition feel human. So when the Konpeki Plaza heist goes wrong, it does not just feel like a mission failure. It feels like Night City taking payment for a dream that was too big.

Jackie’s death is one of the moments that changed the whole game for me. After that, the city feels different. The neon is still bright, but it feels colder. V gets the Relic, Johnny Silverhand appears in their head, and suddenly the story is no longer about becoming famous. It becomes about time running out. Every mission after that has this shadow over it: V is alive, but not completely. V is fighting for a future that may already be disappearing.

Johnny is the best part of the game for me. At first, he is unbearable. He is arrogant, angry, selfish, and constantly insulting V. But the more time he spends with V, the more human he becomes. He is not just a rockstar terrorist ghost. He is a man full of regret, ego, rage, and unfinished pain. His hatred for Arasaka is real, but so is his fear of being forgotten. What makes his relationship with V powerful is that they begin as enemies sharing one body, then slowly become the only people who truly understand each other.

The side characters are what make Night City feel painful instead of just stylish. Judy’s story with Evelyn is tragic because it shows how the city destroys people who are already vulnerable. Evelyn tries to climb out, tries to use the system before it uses her, but Night City crushes her anyway. Judy’s anger and sadness feel real because she is not just fighting enemies; she is grieving someone the world treated like disposable flesh.

Panam’s story feels different. With the Aldecaldos, the game finally lets V breathe. The desert is still dangerous, but it feels honest compared to the city. Panam is stubborn, emotional, loyal, and sometimes difficult, but that is why she feels real. Her missions made me feel like V was not just chasing survival, but maybe finding a place where people actually cared if they lived or died. The Aldecaldos ending is so powerful because it gives V something Night City almost never gives anyone: a family and a road forward.

Takemura is also a character I ended up liking more than I expected. He believes in order, loyalty, and Arasaka, even after being betrayed by the system he served. There is something sad about him. He is honorable in his own way, but also trapped by the world that shaped him. His bond with V is not warm like Jackie’s or Panam’s, but it has respect. He feels like someone who could have been a friend in another life.

What I love about *Cyberpunk 2077* is that almost every major character is trying to survive their own version of Night City. River wants justice in a place where justice barely exists. Kerry is famous but still lost inside his own history. Rogue has power, but it came with compromise. Johnny wanted to burn the system down, but even he became a memory trapped inside technology. Nobody really wins here. They just choose what they are willing to lose.

The endings are what make the game unforgettable. None of them feel completely happy, and I love that. The Devil ending feels cold and terrifying because V puts their fate into the hands of the same machine that ruined so many lives. The Sun ending feels legendary, but also empty, like V finally becomes the myth they wanted to be while still running from death. The Star ending feels the most human because V leaves the city with people who care. The Temperance ending hurts because Johnny gets a second chance, but only by living in the space V leaves behind. Even the suicide ending is devastating because it shows how tired V can become when every road feels cruel.

*Phantom Liberty* makes the game even stronger. Dogtown feels like Night City with the mask ripped off. Songbird, Reed, Myers, and Alex all live inside a world where loyalty is never clean. Songbird is desperate for freedom, but she lies and uses people because she has been used her whole life. Reed is loyal, but his loyalty feels like a prison. The choices there are painful because nobody is innocent, but nobody is completely wrong either. The new ending where V survives but loses their old life is one of the saddest in the whole game. It asks whether survival is still victory if the person who survives is no longer the person who fought so hard to live.

That is why *Cyberpunk 2077* means so much to me. It is not just about guns, cars, cyberware, or neon streets. It is about people trying to matter in a city designed to erase them. V wants to live. Jackie wants to be remembered. Johnny wants revenge and meaning. Judy wants justice. Panam wants freedom. Songbird wants escape. Almost everyone is reaching for something, and Night City keeps asking for a price.

The gameplay is also incredibly satisfying now. Driving through the city at night, walking into a gig, hacking cameras, using mantis blades, sniping from a rooftop, or clearing a building without being seen all feels amazing. But the reason I love the game is not only because it feels cool. I love it because the coolness always has sadness behind it. The city looks beautiful, but it is built on broken people.

When I think of *Cyberpunk 2077*, I think of Jackie’s drink at the Afterlife. I think of Johnny sitting beside V, quieter than usual. I think of Judy staring at a world that keeps taking from her. I think of Panam driving into the desert. I think of Songbird looking at the sky like freedom is almost close enough to touch. And I think of V, still fighting, still afraid, still trying to leave some kind of mark before the lights go out.

Night City is beautiful, cruel, unforgettable, and impossible to trust.

That is why I love this game so much.

Le tuve que dar una segunda oportunidad para que realmente me atrape porque lo abandoné en las primeras horas de mi primer gameplay. 

Para mí lo más destacable es la dinámica entre Johnny y V y la evolución de su relación. Sin embargo, nunca llegué a empatizar con V porque todo el tiempo lo sentía más como un “avatar” que como un personaje en sí. La primera persona tampoco ayudó a generar esa conexión con él por lo que viví su historia desde cierta distancia. Parecía más un “instrumento para cumplir misiones” que una verdadera presencia en el juego. Me gustaría jugar como Valerie un un futuro para ver si el vínculo cambia de alguna forma.

Hablando de historia, la respeto mucho. Tiene varios momentos emotivos (sobre todo hacia el final), personajes que se quedan en tu cabeza y aborda temas más que interesantes, sobre todo esto de la identidad y la consciencia. Se sintió súper “Black Mirror meets Soma” por momentos. Pero no terminó de golpearme como esperaba que lo hiciera. Tampoco había decisiones significativas que cambien radicalmente su rumbo, solo en momentos muy particulares. Night City es enorme y creo que justamente esa vastedad fue la que me desconcentró de la emocionalidad de lo que me estaban contando (terrible trabalenguas, pero creo que me expliqué). Está repleta de facciones, corporaciones, conflictos políticos, cultura; visualmente es una locura, también. Es de no creer todo el desarrollo que tiene pero (y soy consciente de que es algo personal y no relacionado a la calidad) había tanta información por asimilar que nunca terminaba de ubicarme del todo y a veces terminaba un poco saturado. Podríamos resumirlo en que la riqueza de Night City fue una barrera más que una virtud [b]en mi experiencia y en cómo yo disfruto de los videojuegos.[/b]

En cuanto a gameplay me conflictuó el hecho de sentir que no estaba aprovechando las mecánicas lo suficiente. Todo este tema de los matasanos y los ciberimplantes, los hackeos, los atributos, el abanico inmenso de armas y sus mods, y no sigo para no hacerla larga. El juego me pone un montón de cartas sobre la mesa para modificar mi gameplay pero rara vez me dio motivos para involucrarme con ellas. De hecho te lo podrías pasar con un arma que dropea un NPC random. Y acá sí creo que no soy yo el problema sino que es el diseño del juego. Todo esto que nombré se sintió… prescindible. Dicho esto, no es que no me haya divertido. Me la pasé a los tiros porque el sigilo no es lo mío, probé armas nuevas, contribuí a la inseguridad de Night City decapitando a gente por la calle a katanazos un lunes cualquiera por la mañana. Intenté hacer uso de varias de estas mecánicas pero, repito, mi problema es que son opciones que fácilmente podés pasar por alto.

Para terminar, y acá sí lo presento como un defecto: gran parte de sus misiones secundarias son relleno puro y duro. Me pusе a hacer bastantes a lo loco antes de reunirme con Hanako en el Embers para exprimir un poco más el juego solo para descubrir que el propio juego fue el que exprimió su duración. Con [b]obvias[/b] excepciones como las de Johnny, Kerry, Panam y Judy (si es que no se me escapa alguna otra) que están excelentemente escritas. Más allá de eso hay un volumen inmenso de encargos, actividades y contenido opcional que no suma absolutamente nada.

Pese a que parece que lo estoy defenestrando de arriba abajo quiero dejar en claro que para mí valió la pena la experiencia. Tiene sus defectos pero definitivamente es un juego que disfruté y se va a quedar en mi cabeza por un tiempo, al igual que Johnny…

全成就很久之后才记起来写评论。

2077刚发行的时候，作为赛博朋克粉+CDPR粉，自然是第一时间打开PS上，预备花上一星期没日没夜沉浸式地游玩，但没想到主线不到30小时就结束了。

当时自然是一片怅然，甚至有一点愤怒，总觉得期待了很久却被辜负了。故事似乎完全没有触及赛博世界的核心，无论选择哪一条路，爱恨都不尽兴，于是我大多数时间只是在街头开车漫游、欣赏着美丽但空洞的城市，期望在不知名的街道和建筑物里面寻找一点彩蛋，来填补对它的遗憾。

几年后，是DLC出来，在一片好评之后，在PC上重玩，才感到DLC才是游戏缺失那一部分的补完，是游戏的核心精神所在。

赛博科幻世界是一个庞大到每个人都以为自己能做的梦，一个极致的幻象。我们渴望一个俯瞰的视角，想象自己透过云层遥想地球，或者在天际徘徊，殊不知我们只能常常在地面仰望。

高耸入天际的广告牌、无处不在的霓虹灯和全息投影填满了夜空，那些虚假的承诺、对未来的构想，似乎拉近了地表遗民和外星的距离，我们只能幻想被需要、爬到顶端，得到那一张去月球的门票。

但百灵鸟的命运才是一次真正的警示，我们永远无法打破属于自己身份和阶级的天花板，假如连天才黑客都只能命至于此，一介平民又能如何？无论去厮杀、去抢掠、去欺骗、把灵魂出卖给公司，或者走上反叛的路线，去抵抗，像强尼一样最后一次登上制高点，最终都是同样的命运。

出路似乎只有沉溺，潜入水底，追求你遗失在童年的梦；住在垃圾场边，当一个尽职尽责的边缘化的警察；成为市长，走到人上人，将你的意识转交给机器……你可以一步一步登上台阶，可以抵达任何高度，但永远无法让你触及天际。

赛博世界的底色似乎就是悲剧，是资本世界一路上升和达成极权之后、阶级更加固化的现实；所以你要么尽早习惯那些酒精、广告、洗脑歌曲，得过且过，活在当下，笑着死去，似乎是最好的结局。

但有反叛才有故事——V的故事没有完结，强尼的故事没有写完，百灵鸟却实现了玩家的悲悯、激发了玩家真正的反叛。

你们写DLC的编剧，真的把我对CDPR的失望彻底打消，又扳回一城。

Has not Cyberpunk been one of the most prescient genres of this Information age? Not because it has the language of technology we use today but that it shows us the very real and probable future of technologically accelerated hyper-capitalism. So where does Cyberpunk 2077 stand lay in the halls of Bladerunner and Neuromancer? And more importantly, is it a good fcking game?

CP2077 starts off strong by blasting you with a world that feels viscerally alive. The news reels blaring from nearby screens, the idle chatter that is more detailed and contextual than your usual npc lines done ad-infinitum, the cohesive and yet real and chaotic aesthetic narratives present in the architecture, clothes and minutiae of life. This not so distant future pops like a pungent tart thrown at your face. In the best way possible, the sensory overload mirrors ours, the trails of thought apparent in the many vivid lines to follow in the game’s immersion.  Yet this overloading of the senses does not stop the cheer joy and beauty of this supposed capitalist hellhole. The mega-structures are incredibly animated and the level design lets you explore the nooks and crannies of the various different sections of the city more openly than other GTA-style games.

In fact CB2077 is primarily a GTA-style sim that vastly improves on the formula and one of the major reasons is that the third person perspective is eschewed for the first. I can see up close the hyper-reality and the guts of my enemies fly into the ether. Whilst the side missions of GTA 5 felt like chores for the most part (playing weak mini-games to maintain relationships, taxing yourself or others) here they are much more fun because the shooting, hacking and stealth gameplay loop is superb. Some of the side quests are also indelible in their presentation and the leaving of notes and recordings trying to explain or give some semblance of story carries them better than the bare-bone fetch quests of games like Witcher 3. The guided meditation by the monk was a personal favourite as well as the braindance of the prisoner’s crucifixion.

Gunplay is the best facet in the loop with each weapon handling differently with the customisation and crafting components adding further variability and fun to the mess. Every shot and number popping out of the gonks head feels damn good and collecting rare guns is addictive. Stealthing around and backstabbing people is also satisfactory but not to the same extent as the AI feels stupid enough that the victory feels hollow. Hacking can be though of as spells in other games but more adaptable and malleable to the environment than the usual ‘do damage to bad guys’. You can disable CCTV or hijack them, distract enemies using household tech, make things blow up or cause psychosis again adding to the multiplicity of accomplishing missions. The driving parts are not very smooth and I would have rather ridden in the auto taxi service in the game than drive those monstrously weightless cars which is a damn shame as the scenery along the way can be truly stunning.

The rpg mechanics of the game are well realised with stat points and perk trees that are fun to explore and mess around with and the different specialisation can lead to markedly different playstyles. I did use a mod to enable unlimited respeccing that let me try them all out. One criticism is that the perks and special abilities are often automatic when a certain different action is done and that can make it too easy or dull depending on your tastes. The melee combat is not to the calibre of the gunplay but the fact it is added on and has some viability in what most other games would keep to ranged weapons only is commendable.

Where the GTA 5 comparison hurts CB2077 is that the writing and satire and commentary of the former is much better written than the later. While the world of CB2077 is really well historically documented and fleshed out, the actual content and exploration of the themes doesn’t hold a mirror to society like GTA did or the other masterpieces of the Cyberpunk genre. Those sparkling skylines and cybernetic enhancements are more welcoming than ominous and the freedom and rush of becoming a mercantile mastermind envelops any sense of the dystopia inherent in such a world. The uglier parts of the city are there but they lack the emotional wallop that comes with intelligent and poignant storytelling that hammers home the corpo-feudalism. Not that these themes aren’t hinted at in the story of V and his surrounds but it is undercooked and digest it long enough you will get salmonella. There is no inspection of the commodified sexuality of women and others, no dive into the racialised Haitian netrunner experience, the backlash against the Japanese super corporation and the role of poverty that underpins all class consciousness. 

The initial personal pathos of V’s path, in contrast to both the latter part of this game and GTA, is much more realised mainly because of the character of Jackie and his wholesome buffoon act. But V himself is a dull placeholder. Some of this is part of the genre of the RPG but the way he talks in any of the options is quite generic to say the least and reads like a throwaway Italian American gangster wannabee in some 80’s paperback. The male V has the accent to match too, this buttrock voice that got grating very soon.

This leaves the emotional hit to be carried by the characters around V and unfortunately Keanu Reeves, as perhaps the most overrated actor of his generation, cannot do it justice. He speaks in a monotone and sounds like hes locked in the cupboard. He cannot take all the blame though as the character he inhabits is the most infantile rockstar stereotype I have seen in a while. Johnny Silverhand actually says he isn’t talking about a summer anarchist camp but those anarchist teens would wipe the floor with him on any level of serious analysis and thought on his world. He’s seen as some lovable ruffian when he’s just arguably racist zealot focused on one corporation. The true curse of the central plot’s time device is being stuck with this dymbfck. Panam and Takemura save the game’s plunge into complete odious writing though and strong vocal performances bring these character’s relative arcs to life.

While Cyberpunk 2077 may fail as, well, cyberpunk, as a gorgeous video game that ensconces in a world perhaps too beautiful for its own sake, it is an undeniable winner. Every fluid shot of your gun and sly takedown is invigorating that carries you through the passable yet ultimately disappointing story of V’s foray into the cyber wilderness of Night City.

[h1]Cyberpunk 2077 — A Masterpiece Worth Every Hour[/h1]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Visuals & Art Direction[/h2]

Night City is the most visually stunning open world ever put into a video game. The neon-drenched streets, jaw-dropping character design, rain on every surface — every corner looks like concept art brought to life. [b]The word "beautiful" gets thrown around a lot in gaming, but this game has genuinely earned it more than any other.[/b]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Story & Narrative[/h2]

This is my [b]all-time favorite story-driven game[/b] and my [b]second favorite game overall[/b]. What makes it extraordinary isn't just the main quest — it's that every single side story feels completely alive and purposeful. No throwaway missions. Every character has depth. Every decision carries real weight.

The endings are something else entirely:
[spoiler]The Hanako path and the conclusion involving the stars left me completely speechless. I couldn't have imagined better endings if I'd written them myself. Both were truly amazing in ways I never saw coming.[/spoiler]

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Voice Acting & Performances[/h2]

V's voice actors — [i]both of them[/i] — give performances so natural and committed that the illusion never breaks, not for a single line. You would never be able to tell it wasn't a real person speaking at every waking moment. Johnny Silverhand is equally extraordinary — magnetic, complicated, and impossible to look away from.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Soundtrack & Audio[/h2]

[b]One of the best soundtracks in modern gaming, full stop.[/b] From the pounding synth during firefights to the melancholy ambience of V's apartment, to the radio stations you catch while cruising the highways — every audio choice feels deliberate and perfectly tuned to Night City's soul.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Vehicles & Combat[/h2]

The vehicles aren't built for realism purists — and honestly, [i]that's exactly right.[/i] Cranking a car to top speed, launching off an overpass, and landing in the middle of a cyberpsycho takedown is one of the most purely fun things you can do in any game ever made.

Weapons follow the same smart philosophy: [b]no cleaning kits, no durability meters to babysit[/b] — but enough mechanical variety and feel to make your loadout matter, especially on higher difficulties. It hits the sweet spot between accessible and genuinely tactical.

[hr][/hr]

[h2]Modding Community[/h2]

The modding scene is [b]extraordinary.[/b] Community creators have built [u]fully flyable helicopters and aircraft[/u] from scratch — something not in the base game at all. There are tactical gear and weapon mods that slot seamlessly into the existing balance without breaking immersion or difficulty. And if you [i]want[/i] the power fantasy, those mods exist too. The ecosystem is massive, creative, and still growing.

[hr][/hr]

[h2] Final Thoughts[/h2]

I haven't finished the game after [b]4 years[/b] — and that is [u]not[/u] a criticism. That's because I'm doing every side quest, every gig, every achievement before I let myself reach the end. [b]This game rewards that kind of attention completely.[/b]

[strike]Just one more side quest...[/strike] okay maybe two.

[hr][/hr]

[h1] Verdict: 10 / 10[/h1]
[b]Buy it. Mod it. Get completely lost in it.[/b]

If you haven't played this game before, or want to play it again, I highly, highly, highly suggest going to nexusmods and playing with the Welcome To Night City modpack. It's wicked easy to do, and you can't tell what's a mod and what's the vanilla game. And then, once I learned what it actually does for the game, I was like... yeah I can't live without those things! It's a sublime experience.

So, that's my only experience with the game, besides when it first-first came out. Grab WTNC and go for it.

The only problem I really have with the game is I hate V, the person you play as. She's really rude, and acts like a real jerk to people for no reason. Half the time I choose a dialog option, I do not like what I end up saying. It makes it hard to connect with the story sometimes.

Ultimately, I like to play this more like an arcade sandbox Deus Ex. All the beats of the missions and story are great, but I don't find myself emotionally invested in the overall plot. And that makes me want to play Crimson Desert, because that sandbox feels more expansive. But I guess those are 2026 problems for 2077, lol.

Anyway, it's fun, but I don't feel motivated to complete the story right now.

10/10.

Cyberpunk 2077 это шедевр. Всё в этой игре наполнено смысл, каждый квест и каждый персонаж прописан. Мир буквально ощущается живым. Многие квесты можно даже не найти, если не исследовать мир, тот же Бартмасс (или как его там) и чел с горящим хером. Игра дает свободу игроку, он может делать, что хочет, отложив сюжет на второй план, так как в игре очень много интересных второстепенных квестов и событий. И наоборот, можно идти по сюжету, забив на сайд квесты. 

Сюжетные линии различных персонажей это отдельная тема, как же там всё охеренно прописано, заметно, что персонажи становятся добрее к Ви по мере его/её помощи им. Атмосфера в самом Найт-Сити на высшем уровне. Заметны старания разработчиков над ней и городом в целом. В игровом мире присутствует много отсылок, а также можно узнать судьбы некоторых персонажей, которые появлялись в 
сюжете (та же Сандра Дорсетт).

Немного разочаровали фиксеры, потому что большинство заказов сводится к иди убей, сходи принеси, вот тебе награда. Но порадовал Мистер Хэндс, каждый его заказ имеет два пути завершения, и игрок имеет полную свободу в выборе. 

Вообще всё ДЛС Призрачная свобода это полный пик, можно узнать историю Сойки, которая явно не оставит равнодушным. Отдельно хочется описать персонажей, какие же они интересные, Рид, Сойка, да даже Президент Майерс интересно прописана. Все концовки ДЛС отлично прописаны и наполнены смыслом, после прохождения которых задумываешься, а так ли всё должно кончиться. 

Все концовки основной игры также сделаны отлично, что хочется увидеть их каждую, в каждой концовке Ви предстает по-разному. Отдельно хочется выделить Киану Ривза в роли Джонни, как же он сделан охеренно. Все его речи, поступки и то, как меняются его отношения с Ви. Как он осознает новый мир спустя 50 лет сна. Встреча ос старыми друзьями, которые сейчас уже влиятельные люди.

Я наиграл 104 часа и явно на этом не остановлюсь. Эта игра стала моей любимой из-за ее прописанности, атмосферы и чувства свободы выбора в ходе ее прохождения.

If you asked me at launch, I would’ve told you to run away from this game. But man, the developers absolutely redeemed themselves. Night City is easily one of the most jaw dropping, dense, and alive urban cities ever built. Walking out of V’s apartment at night with the neon reflecting off the wet pavement is pure cyberpunk eye candy. The first-person combat is incredibly slick , chopping through Scavs with Mantis Blades or quick hacking an entire room from the shadows feels amazing. The story hits heavy emotional notes too with great romance options, and Keanu Reeves as Johnny Silverhand is brilliant. It’s not a perfect 10 because the AI can still act completely braindead sometimes, but it’s a masterpiece now.

The Score:

Gameplay: 9/10 (Gunplay is GREAT, cyberware upgrades feel incredibly impactful, and build variety is wild)

Story: 9/10 (Beautiful, unique, emotional, and handles the corporate dystopia vibe perfectly)

Graphics: 10/10 (If you have the hardware to max it out, it's genuinely unmatched)

Sound: 10/10 (The radio stations are packed with bangers and songs that give you ptsd after watching edge runners)

Immersiveness: 8/10 (The city itself pulls you in completely, though the Npc´s are genuinely shit)

Overall 9/10

Cyberpunk 2077 — A Modern Masterpiece

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those rare games that feels less like a product and more like a fully realized artistic vision. Night City is not just a setting — it is a living, breathing organism, filled with ambition, decay, beauty, violence, and humanity. From the moment you step into its neon-soaked streets, the game pulls you into a world that feels both terrifyingly dystopian and strangely believable.

What impressed me most is how well Cyberpunk 2077 combines atmosphere, storytelling, character writing, exploration, and player choice. The main story is emotional, stylish, and deeply personal, but the side quests are often just as memorable. Many of them feel handcrafted, meaningful, and written with the kind of detail you rarely see in open-world games. The characters are outstanding, the dialogue is sharp, and the world constantly gives you reasons to care.

The gameplay has also become excellent. Combat is fast, flexible, and satisfying, whether you prefer hacking enemies from the shadows, going in with blades, using firearms, or building your own hybrid playstyle. The RPG systems, cyberware, weapons, and progression all make the experience feel rewarding from start to finish.

The DLC content only makes the game stronger. It adds more depth, more emotional weight, more style, and more reasons to return to Night City. Everything feels like it expands the world naturally rather than simply adding extra content for the sake of it.

Yes, the game had issues at launch. That is impossible to ignore. But judging Cyberpunk 2077 as it stands today, those early technical problems do not define the experience anymore. What remains is an incredible open-world RPG with unforgettable atmosphere, powerful storytelling, and one of the most immersive cities ever created in gaming.

For me, Cyberpunk 2077 is not just a great game. It is a masterpiece. A bold, emotional, visually stunning, and unforgettable experience that deserves to be remembered as one of the defining games of its generation.

From the beginning, Night City chews you up and spits you out, then insults your corpse while you're lying there, broken. You set out to become a legend, but just find you're hanging on, trying to keep your head above water, and so many promising starts lead to dead ends. Telling the truth or making what seems like a "morally good" choice may get you killed, or ruin someone's life. You'll shoot up the "criminals", only to remember they were criminals because a heartless corporation branded them as such, for what would usually (mostly) be minor offenses. You're not a hero, you're a rat in a neon maze. A maze of insanity, corruption, violence, pollution. Slathered with screaming ads and the stench of human suffering and vice at every level. Yet you can't stop coming back to it. The streets call to you. The city calls to you. The few friends you have (if they are truly friends at all), call to you. Each personality is so well written, they feel like living breathing beings, even as they disappoint you, use you, leave you, or stab you in the back. (Perhaps those traits in particular are what make them feel so humanly real.) Night City chews you up and spits you out, but you're an Edgerunner. That is the life you've chosen Choom, and whatever end awaits you, you'll light the motherfucker on fire on your way out, just to remind it you were there. See you in the Afterlife.

Well this was somethin, but not what I was expecting. Cyberpunk was a very VERY ok game, but I just cant recommend it. I will point out things i liked and the ones i didnt:

PROS:
- Graphics. Night city looked phenomenal. City is very well planned out and feels alive. 
- Character outfits and looks. They are very detailed and look awesome
- There are a lot of ways to upgrade your character abilities, skills etc
- A few characters (like Johnny) are nice
- Loading screens are a bit unique
- A lot of ways to customize your character looks.

CONS:
- Gameplay is very mediocre, could even say its just bad, not very fun to play, which is the biggest minus for me
- Whole game feels more like just a movie. 
- There is a lot of DEI things in the game (which makes sense its cyberpunk afterall). But still at sometimes these things are too much shoved into your face.
- Some characters are just put in the game for the case of DEI it feels like, which makes them unnecessary, not needed, not fittin.
- There is a LOT of bloated dialogue in the game. At some moments there is just too much talkin and made me almost fall asleep at times.
- Npcs and object keep on bugging, glitching, destroying them selfes even after all this patches the game got.
- Enemies AI is on brainded level. They just standin sometimes waiting for you to shot them. 
- Bosses are a complete joke. First one I encountered was like a DEI final boss and almost made me vomit. Their mechanics were also underwhelming.
- Driving mechanics are not too bad, but could have been much better.
- Sometimes some cutscenes during them missions just hit you out of the rythm of the game. Characters randomly start talking about their feelings while sitting next to each other in between some heavy action focused segments. Just pacing could have been better.
- Story was decent, good enough at times. But still it felt like it was missing something.
- You dont earn much in game money from the main story missions, all that money is hidden behind side missions, objectives, which is kinda annoying because you want to upgrade your character and cant because it needs money.
- Feels like the game is so much automated that at times it can play itself. You just need to hold W key and hold your left mouse button and you occasionally press space.
- Difficulty scalling is pretty bad. At highier difficulty than normal enemies become a big bullet sponges and at lower difficulty they just die too quickly.

Overall I was expecting much more and got dissapointed. I can only recommend this game for "movie games" enthusiasts.  It was ok but not good enough for my gaming taste.

I waited through the horrors of the initial rushed launch in 2020, I waited through the following years of patching, until the Phantom Liberty DLC, then some more years of patching and only then I finally got the game in 2026 ([i]with 65% discount, mind you[/i]), expecting it to for sure be done by now and ready to play.

But it is not, it is still not. Even after 6 years since the release it still feels rushed and rather abruptly done - like on that meme of drawing a horse. I don't mean bugs or crashes - there is almost none of those, from technical point it is quite stable and polished ([i]nha![/i]). I mean the actual game, the story - it is all "artificial", dumbed down, with a plastic taste and just empty - a ([i]very beautiful[/i]) husk that does not have a life inside. What it does have and a lot of is generic conversations with meaningless options in dialogues, pointless grinding, insufferable female V ([i]male V is probably the same[/i]), vastly annoying characters ([i]with a few exceptions[/i]), SJW vibes and loads of "[i]choom[/i]", "[i]sitch[/i]", "[i]deets[/i]", "[i]prolly[/i]", "[i]delta[/i]", "[i]preem[/i]", "[i]nova[/i]", "[i]saka[/i]" and other cringe crap.

By the way, even NVIDIA's Ultimate tier can barely handle 60 FPS at maximum graphics level in 4K, and that is already with upscaling, so don't expect miracles there. This game is all over the place. In some instances it's fantastic, then it rips your heart out with how undercooked it is in other places and your immersion is quickly broken.

[h2]Story and narrative[/h2]
The premise of the world is simple - megacorpos run most of the world in a world where governments inexplicably bent over to them nearly everywhere regardless of the system, yet it fails to deliver that feeling in the most corpo-driven city. For some odd reason, their presence is visible everywhere, yet felt nearly nowhere throughout the story, even in quests where you are screwing with the corporations, and I blame the writing and pacing here. Edgerunner immediately pulls you into a world run by corpos, whereas the game tries it in so many ways, and still falls flat. This corpo narrative began and ended with Meredith Stout. That was a fantastic introduction to what corpos can and would do, and then it just fizzles out. They quickly became a background noise even though your whole main quest is related to dealing with them. Gangs became the focal point and the pacing prioritized them and the result is tangible.

Narrative is also suffering from pacing and writing. Just like in Fallout, you need to fulfill your mission before time runs out. Here however, it does not run out, because the world is filled with side quests and we wouldn't want to miss out on that. A terrible mistake. Cake-and-eat-it-too kind of a mistake. On top of that, you are bombarded with endless phonecalls in the very first hour of gameplay, to the point you begin to lose track of what certain quests or side characters are about and you do not know what to do first. How this wasn't ever patched or why it was introduced in the first place is beyond me.

The first mission is the best example of this dissonance. It's an endless stream of information and cutscenes that attempt to pull you into the story but they instead leave you dazed and confused. You're meeting over a dozen characters within your first hour, which is filled with cutscenes that inform you about three subsequent missions. Incomparable to the pacing of Witcher 3's beginning. Absurdly terrible but am I glad I stuck through it, as I knew what they were attempting to do.

[h2]World and immersion[/h2]
I don't think I've ever played a game so immersive and yet so shallow at the same time. Citizens are immersion-breaking, but then you get to live a second life within this world as long as you're not done with much of the story, but as you finish quests, immersing in it becomes less and less interesting to you. Why? Because CD Projekt Red is not Rockstar nor Valve. They've created a static world that tries to simulate a dynamic one. Compare the world to GTA's where the world is an actual, reactive sandbox. Everything is designed to react to a trigger - from the world, from the characters, from the physics. In Cyberpunk, you are the sole trigger, and the game reminds you of it every so often. In GTA5 you can't drink, car interiors are awful, apartments are lackluster and staticky, the interaction with the world objects is undercooked, CP77 builds on that in so many ways, but it just didn't have the funding, time and tech know-how to build a living world, and one feels and sees it.

The city itself is beautiful to look at. The more you explore though, the more you see the seams unfortunately, but it's well detailed. Not many interiors to enter, some interiors are only a one-time occurrence, some are notably undercooked.

[h2]Characters' reactivity[/h2]
It's a heavily narrative-driven game, relatively loose where it can afford to be, but otherwise you are shoehorned into a particular V every single time no matter your background. However, your choices do matter when it comes to characters you come across - their fate, and the reaction to your actions, are a direct consequence of your doing. They act in juxtaposition to certain choices you make throughout quests or stories, which allows you to really ponder on the eventual outcomes, though some outcomes will certainly leave you confused as to why X happened, and will feel forced as a consequence. Again, writing isn't the strongest suit of this game, pacing exacerbates it, but the characters are well fleshed out and they thankfully salvage the entire game. They suffer from a few things though - terribly animated vehicle cutscenes where they're the ones driving, mistimed voice lines and sound EQ being all over the place. The loud and annoying ads sometimes cut through very emotional lines so awfully, it left me extremely annoyed.

[h2]The technical slavjank nightmare[/h2]
No wonder why they decided to go for Unreal Engine 5. The accumulated tech debt became too great. They're not a large corporation yet still they built an amazing looking engine that does things it's set out to do relatively well. But it is indeed a pig with a lipstick in every way imaginable and you get reminded of it while playing quite often. I will not list them here.

[h2]Phantom Liberty DLC[/h2]
Very happy they eventually fixed most of the issues plaguing the game and even released a fantastic DLC. They doubled down on a game they worked their asses off for nearly a decade. The writing and pacing there is immeasurably better and it shows what CP77 could've been had they simplified the whole premise and focused on building a reactive world. Instead, they branched the main story out and the further you strayed from the beginning the more it suffered. This is a non-issue in the DLC. It's a relatively simple and arguably much more linear approach to an immersive and atmospheric story with memorable characters and, finally, very few side characters you're supposed to remember after a dozen or so quests. I still remember Paco and his friend I smuggled out of Dogtown, the chippery merchant who kept spamming me with tidbits about events that happened a week ago in game for some reason.

[h2]Modding![/h2]
Hell yeah. So many great mods that we will not get to use once the new installment is launched on UE5. Plenty of mods brought back cut content and fix bugs that are still present. Imho they are vital for those who really want a great experience, doubly so for replays.

This is a really, really good game.  I remember first downloading GOG over 10 years ago and that's all they would advertise:  "Cyberpunk 2077!"  I was like, "Great, another future title is being over-advertised and over-hyped.  It will probably end up sucking."  Well, I was half-right, because it did suck initially when it was released.  I figured I wouldn't even give it a chance because have little faith in developers with investors who rush and over-hype everything, like No Man's Sky, for example, but I was talking to a friend about Cyberpunk 2077 a year or so ago and he said the game has improved significantly.  So, I decided to get it.

No regrets.  I had a ton of fun playing and re-playing this game.  There are so many main quests and side quests that intermingle with the main quests and side quests that don't intermingle with the main quest, but intermingle with other side quests and independent side quests and gigs and crimes to resolve and races, etc.  There's so much content it was almost overwhelming, but in a good "I am getting my money's worth out of this game" way.

The story is pretty dystopian and bleak.  I'm pretty sure the developers don't really believe in "winners" as we do in a lot of games.  Decisions can be very difficult to make, unless your ambition is to get the most gain out of it.  However, if you're trying to be a "good" person, this game makes it difficult to do, because most story-driven choices have good and bad sides to them.  I won't spoil anything, but you'll see when you experience it.  And it's not just the main quest, there are side quests that have this same dynamic.  It was morally challenging.  My only problem was that, with each ending I discovered, I felt like I was finally making the right choice, but then the writers throw a random wrench into the ending that kind of ruins it for me.  I got a little tired of that, but like I said, this game wasn't meant to be good vs bad.

Ok, potential spoiler ahead, but I can't resist.  I recognized Keanu Reeves the moment I saw him.  I hadn't realized he was in this game, but he did a marvelous job in his role and he's a great actor.  I think a big part of this game's success is because of him.  I won't lie, though, I hated his character my first playthrough, and I wanted nothing to do with him.  However, the game slowly and surely makes him seem decent and enables you to understand things from his point of view.  He's still a bit of a jerk, but as I mentioned before, this game doesn't cater to your whim.

Oh yeah, I almost forgot, developers are finally recognizing and representing straight-edge and sexually-abstaining persons.  I was getting so tired of games ruining characters for me by having them get drunk, do a bunch of drugs and sleep around like degenerates without giving me the option to avoid it.  I was glad to finally have the choice to graciously decline alcohol, cigarettes, drugs, promiscuity, etc. if I wanted.  Speaking of such, you can turn off any and all nudity in this game.  Female characters will have a black, bra-like texture over their bosoms if they're "naked" and they'll be wearing panties.  Male characters will always have boxers on at least.  However, if you want the nudity, you can even change the size of your ding-dong or rack.  Aside from the cosmetic viewpoint, I don't think this mechanic adds anything else to the game.

So, weapons, cybernetic implants, clothing and outfits and consumables are numerous.  I found myself always discovering something new or better than what I had.  There's also a huge amount of "written" dialogue, in the form of data shards.  This can also be a little annoying, because I could either be sneaking around, fighting enemies and looting stashes and corpses, etc. and I'd pick up like 18 different data shards that I'd have to go to my journal to read.  Normally, that's not so bad if you can ignore it, but each data shard shows up as a bolded item under an extensive list of categories.  The "other" category being the biggest culprit because I'd have like 75 unread data shards in there because I'm not going to pause my game every 5 seconds to read shard number 54 of the 87 that I somehow got from the 5 gangsters I just hollowed out, neither am I going to analyze every stash I search for every little thing I want to pick up or not.  It got a little ridiculous by the end.

Anyway, I'm happy to say that this game turned out great.  If you're looking for a new first-person action adventure, definitely play this.

I first bought this game on release. It was a terrible, broken mess. 

I tried the game again after 5 years, and it was a totally new game. Great job from CDPR to fix it. 

Some criticisms:

The game still has quite a few bugs, but most are harmless and sometimes funny. Not to be unexpected for a game this complex and big. However, considering the game's tone is serious, I do think it would be great to iron them out for the sake of preventing immersion breaks. 

Personally, I didn't like the English voice acting for male V nor female V. Perhaps just me, but it just felt a bit goofy, lacking in emotion, etc. They also reused quite a few voice lines and at times it is noticeable.

The game's pacing is also very awkward. There is quite a lot to do, except the game feels like it rushes you to complete the main storyline as you are dying in a matter of weeks. It seems like it was a big mistake to make that such a prominent part of the story so early on. It is also very difficult to care about Jackie, as you basically experience none of their previous relationship. I almost wonder if it was cut content. 

I won't get into the details, but the pacing of the main game was not good, and it also felt quite short. It would have been great to have some time being a regular merc with Jackie before everything begins to go downhill.

There are a ton of details that have not been attended to, and are only partially fixed by mods (reflection in mirrors, for example).

I think player customization is also quite limited, accessible building interiors are limited as well. As you get more cyberware, your character does not reflect it. A shame. 

Some random things that really came to bother me are how CDPR approached buildings that don't have accessible interiors. Instead of designing a model for the player to view from the window, they simply emplaced a 3D drawing that looks terrible if you look at it for longer than a second. And it is standardized, so you seem the same pattern everywhere, and it is quite immersion breaking. I wonder if they did it procedurally, because there are several spots on the map that you CAN actually go inside, but when viewing it from the outside window, it is just painted over with the same 3D drawing. This creates impossible physical dimensions and mismatched interiors/exteriors, etc.

Same thing with NPCs. Play long enough (just 10 hours was enough to notice), and you will realize that there are a limited number of base NPC models, of which all other NPCs are just variations of. Incredibly immersion breaking.

Your decisions in the game, as well as the life path you take in the game, basically do not matter except for the very end. That was quite frustrating. I also felt it was very limiting. If I wanted to roleplay as a diehard corpo, even after getting discarded, it is impossible to do so as your dialogue locks you into a certain philosophy and playstyle. 

The romantic options are generally all terrible. I didn't like any of the characters that you had an option to romance. Only Kerry was fine, and it just feels wrong to romance him while being half-Johnny. 

A lot of times, the dialogue prompts are completely different to what is actually said by V. Not just semantically different, directionally different. Very frustrating and a confusing design choice.

There is still a lot more to complain about, but those are the things that immediately come to mind.

Some compliments:

The graphics are generally great for a 2020 release. It is a visually stunning game. The atmosphere, overall story, and execution are well done. 

What really saves this game, in my opinion, is the Phantom Liberty DLC. What a fantastic addition. I think it is better than the base game by far. The story is dynamic, morally grey, your decisions have profound consequences, it just does everything you would like it to. The characters are well fleshed out, flawed, and make the story incredibly captivating. As much as I like Keanu Reeves, I think not having the DLC be as focused on Johnny allowed CDPR to make something really special. It's a spy thriller meeting the Cyberpunk world. It was truly awesome.

Replayability is also pretty decent. Combat is fun. The cyberware is fun. For the most part, especially if you are able to ignore details (I struggle a bit), the game is very immersive. 

I am really looking forward to Cyberpunk 2 (Orion), and I hope that not having to focus on Johnny will allow them to really flesh out a great story.

The game offers a brilliant mix of compelling storytelling, unforgettable characters, and fast-paced combat that lets you play exactly how you want - you can even go full cyberpunk samurai and slice through enemies using just a katana. To be fair, it's still not perfect, and you will definitely run into some annoying bugs and glitches from time to time. But despite these flaws, the incredible atmosphere and emotional story make it completely worth your time. It’s a solid 8/10 that you shouldn't miss.

新档，60小时全DLC成就，本体基本只做了把妹剧情，DLC任务审判日的时候注意下楼找百灵鸟前存档就能简单体验全结局。
2077当年首发本体怕bug学习的，补票之后DLC一直放着没玩，这次鸣潮联动把《边缘行者》看了，一下又勾起玩2077的瘾了，直奔《往日之影》。

进入狗镇后的前中期主线说实话是有点闷的，一眼骗的百灵鸟典型谜语人，李德也是半天憋不出一个屁来，不如通几个狗镇马桶来的有趣，马桶里还能看看2077背景下的少年运动员、试图洗心革面的假拳拳击手最后还是烂在桥洞、抽象超梦2人组……让人时而忍俊不禁、时而想炸荒坂塔。

不过在审判日剧情后，主线一扫之前的疲软，直接开始魔法攻击我脆弱的心灵。宝剑国王、权杖国王、钱币国王、圣杯国王加高塔，一共4.5个结局，每打完一个都更添一份惆怅。

[u]先打的支持[b]百灵鸟线[/b][/u]：
[spoiler]尾关守塔+跑酷、战斗压力不大，跟百灵鸟联机后还能体验黑墙也是爽起来了。

航空港剧情彻底撕碎了迈尔斯的伪装，候机平民被无差别屠杀也让人再次唏嘘赛博朋克背景下普通人就是纯纯消耗品。
百灵鸟就是一个不纯粹的坏人，她一路上一直在骗V，但也一路上在问是不是真的没有谁都不连累的办法；她想活下去，也因为7年前的良心债想就这样睡着不再醒来。百灵鸟的这种矛盾的恶，也让人不能简单的对报复她还是成全她做出选择。最后不论是把百灵鸟交给李德的“回家”（毕竟百灵鸟在李德线亲口认证的联情局和黑墙一样都是人间地狱），还是送上月球（月球大概率不过是另一个夜之城），在我看来身怀黑墙核弹技能的百灵鸟是否能真正获得自由都是存疑的（当然月球结局还是有一丝可能性，虽然间接引发公司5战）。而月球线作为唯一一条李德爆装备的线（“弃子”，很李德的装备名了），百灵鸟是否值得V为她杀掉李德+李德是活着比死了更惨的类型，也让我最终没有选择这条线作为通关后继续本体的存档。[/spoiler]

[u]支持[b]李德线[/b][/u]：
[spoiler]剧情量比百灵鸟线感觉多了不少，百灵鸟和李德的人物刻画更上一层楼，把这两个一辈子不说开就再也没机会说开的如父女如师徒的两人间的纠葛描写的更为深入，加上关底潜行解密和杀人蜘蛛即死的压迫感，个人觉得审判日选择支持李德的线路综合来说体验更为完整。

开局审判日百灵鸟选择被侵蚀刀掉亚历克斯，达成试图刀李德、试图刀迈尔斯以及刀了亚历克斯的成就，可以说是100%参团，也能看出百灵鸟和V虽然确实都面临相同的困境，却终究不是一类人。从被李德带进联情局后，不难猜出一边被迈尔斯的黑墙实验掏空、一边接受联情局教育的百灵鸟最终会成为一个完全无法信任他人的人，只能顾及小我，但在2077世界观下也不能苛责。“一片雪花落在手套上，我可以计算出它的分型结构...但自己妈妈的声音却不记得了”，如此可悲。被黑墙侵蚀的她最终也只是想再回到布鲁克林的家，那个她被带走时说不会回头望的地方（但这个谎言也只是被大人一眼看穿的程度），在家里一边回忆过去，一边悔恨过去。好在最终V也为这个小骗子的结局带来了一丝温暖：“我会把这一刻记在心里：回家了，还有个朋友在身边...一切消失前...最后那个瞬间，知道了自己并不孤独。”

李德，结局不是死亡、就是悔恨，某结局强尼锐评“这人算完了，没奔头了”的含金量。守着信仰一直想把小宋带回联情局，但是看不清现实，看不清迈尔斯、新美国，最后只是一次又一次把小宋送到恶魔身边，然后不断怀疑自己是否是对的，但又无法否认自己过去的选择，属于是无能的大人加上悲剧的盲信者，每条线的结局都是给人感觉瞬老30岁的余生活在悔恨里，使人发笑、使人悲叹。

圣杯国王线满足了百灵鸟的请求，V杀死了被黑墙侵蚀的百灵鸟，阻断了她作为武器的悲惨结局（虽然尸体也被迈尔斯解刨烂了），给她自由、给她离开；替李德做出了这个他做不到的选择，让他在尾声也终于能和自己和解，顺便粉碎了迈尔斯的阴谋，在我看来是最接近现实的结局。但即使理智让我选择了圣杯国王作为继续游玩的存档，这4条都很难说是完美的结局，也让我始终会回想起百灵鸟线最后，她在列车上说着“想活下去”的画面。

4条线各有各的遗憾，也互相补足了剧情，而百灵鸟、李德、亚历克斯等人的命运也不过是狗镇的一瞬罢了，话事人照旧选举、马桶照旧通、太阳照旧升起。[/spoiler]

全部体验后又一次感受到了好游戏后必备的空虚惆怅感......好在我还有通狗镇马桶时没有珍惜的偷车点，结局后为了《来得容易去的快》成就无能狂刷偷车点，偷了又偷、每偷要运那手感垃圾的破车2、3km，配着车载电台时不时刷到的《I really want to stay at your house》，一切都会好起来的。正好本体剧情也忘得差不多了，我来了！

Alright I admit that I'm six years late but bear with me; I don't usually write reviews for anything really but I had to make an exception here. I finally played Cyberpunk 2077, and I can confidently say it's the closest I'll ever get to living in the future. Night City is absolutely gorgeous. Every street looks like a neon-soaked fever dream designed by someone who drank six energy drinks and said, "What if Blade Runner had even more advertisements?" I spent half my playtime admiring the scenery and the other half accidentally running over pedestrians while trying to figure out the controls. The story is fantastic, the characters are memorable, and Keanu Reeves somehow manages to be cooler than every other person in a city full of cybernetic ninjas. That's not fair, but it's impressive. As for the bugs: I played long after launch, so most of them are gone. Instead of game-breaking glitches, I mostly encountered minor weirdness, like NPCs staring into the void or physics deciding that gravity is merely a suggestion.

Combat is fun, hacking makes you feel like a futuristic wizard, and customization lets you create a character that looks either incredibly intimidating or like they lost a fight with a glow-stick factory.

Overall: 9/10. Cyberpunk 2077 delivers an amazing sci-fi adventure, and after all the updates, it's finally become the game we were promised. Also, it taught me an important lesson: if the future is anything like Night City, I'm staying indoors.

Проходил игру множество раз, сначала на PS 4, потом GOG-версию, после этого решил приобрести в Steam. С момента последнего прохождения игра сильно изменилась, переработали боевую систему, добавили новые ветки скиллов, новые квесты, локации и транспорт. Особенно нравятся бои с Макс-Так. Игра оставляет сильное впечатление, особенно сюжетом, интереснейшими глубокими персонажами, история которых запоминается надолго и общей атмосферой. Музыкальное сопровождение к игре стоит отдельных похвал - практически все треки, так или иначе, погружают в гущу событий, происходящих на данный момент в игре. Красивые локации и пейзажи города тоже заслуживают отдельного внимания (я давно не делал столько скринов, как в этой игре). Боёвка, не скажу что самая простая (на ультра харде), вышла очень динамичной и адреналиновой, но сбалансированной - ты убиваешь за пару ударов или выстрелов, и тебя точно так же могут убить, особенно если играть от дробовиков, пистолетов и клинков, приправляя всё это Сандевистаном. Физика езды на транспорте неплохая, просто неплохая. Но сами автомобили очень красивые и, по-своему, колоритные. Особенно заметно внимание к несущественным деталям, что, по-моему, свидетельствует о том, что игру делали с любовью. К сожалению, баги в этой игре тоже есть, но они незначительные и порой смешные, геймплею они никак не мешают.

Cyberpunk é um jogo com uma ambientação incrivelmente bem feita, eu joguei o prólogo e só percebi que era o prólogo quando o jogo me falou que acabou o prólogo e começava o Cap. 1 do jogo. Eu sou mecânico e consequentemente gosto muito de carros, quando comecei como Nômade e eu precisei consertar um carro, entrei naquele carro e ele tinha um ronquinho legal, fiquei MUITO hypado, porém.........a física de dirigir no Cyberpunk 2077, pra mim, é a PIOR coisa desse jogo, realmente ela decepciona MUITO. 
Com intuíto de comparação, Saints Row 3 que é um jogo que tem a direção um pouco travada, é um jogo onde eu sinto o mesmo nível de satisfação/frustração com a Física, chegou um ponto no jogo onde eu literalmente deixei de usar completamente veículos e passei usar as mecânicas de locomoção por implantes. 

Minha build do meu único playtrought (Sim é isso mesmo, foram 50 horas em 1 só save e eu nem cheguei a zerar o jogo) é uma build de arremessáveis, com perks e implantes que me dão diversas opções de desacelerar o tempo. Eu recomendaria esse jogo de olhos fechados, nessas 50 horas os únicos Bugs que eu realmente encontrei foram relacionados aos veículos, a gameplay é fluída, a progressão é satisfatória, os personagens mais frequentes são bem escritos, os personagens com romance disponível em sua maioria são extremamente bem escritos.

[h1]ШТОШ![/h1]

[h3] Немного предыстории данного проекта:[/h3] 
[b]Май 2012 года - Анонс игры CYBERPUNK 2077.
Январь 2013 года - Первый кинематографический тизер-трейлер игры, в котором показали мрачный мир будущего. Далее последовал долгий период разработки игры. 
Май 2016 года - после завершения основных работ над дополнением для "ВЕДЬМАК 3", команда из около 500 человек перешла к полноценной активной разработке проекта. 
Июнь 2018 года - Первый геймплейный тизер на выставке E3. 
Август 2018 года - Второй геймплейный показ аж на 48 минут. И вот тогда то и был фурор "КиберПанка". CD Projekt Red задрали планку достаточно высоко. Июнь 2019 года - объявлена первая официальная дата релиза игры (16 апреля 2020 года) и представлен новый трейлер с Киану Ривзом в роли Джонни Сильверхенда. 
Январь - Октябрь 2020 года - череда масштабных переносов. Релиз трижды откладывали для полировки игры и исправления ошибок перед выходом. 
10 декабря 2020 года - состоялся глобальный релиз игры на всех площадках, или же глобальный 0БСЁР года и компании в целом... Игра сопровождалась масштабными техническими проблемами, что привело к скандалу, возвратам средств и падению акций компании. 
Март 2021 года - выпущен масштабный патч 1.2, заложивший фундамент для исправления технического состояния игры на старых консолях. 
Февраль 2022 года - состоялся полноценный релиз для консолей нового поколения. 
В марте 2022 года студия объявила о приостановке продаж всех своих игр в России и Беларуси в ответ на начало боевых действий в Украине. 
Сентябрь 2022 года - анонсировано масштабное сюжетное дополнение "Phantom Liberty". 
Сентябрь 2023 года - выход глобального патча 2.0, сильно изменившего кор-механики игры и релиз дополнения. И в целом, игра "полируется" до сих пор...[/b]

[h3] А теперь к сути))):[/h3]  Об этой игре я мечтал долго, но понимал, что не смогу себе позволить поиграть в нее на своем старом железе. Умудрившись замутить апгрейд в момент разгара пандемии и дождавшись патча, я наконец-то погрузился в этот мир. Этот опыт - словно первые детские ощущения от новых игр в начале 2000-х.
Итак, [h3] Cyberpunk 2077 - это грандиозный научно-фантастический экшен-RPG, прошедший путь от проблемного релиза до эталона жанра. Благодаря колоссальным проделанным работам и обновлениям, игра предлагает глубокую ролевую систему, первоклассную постановку, захватывающий открытый мир и отличную оптимизацию, Исключительно для одиночного прохождения.[/h3]  
[u]Я не гуру обзоров по играм, НОООО, вот чем я хотел бы поделиться за время моего игрового опыта:[/u]

[b]Описывать по всем пунктам можно очень много, а обзор и без того получится большим, поэтому пройдемся лишь по ключевым элементам основных критериев[/b]

[h3] 1) Геймплей. [/h3] 
- Боевая система - Динамичные бои с использованием огромного арсенала ближнего и дальнего боя, уникального оружия с использованием "умных пуль с самонаведением" и т.д., с обеих сторон, что заставляет подбирать индивидуальную тактику при стычках с врагом;
- Киберпространство и взлом - Взлом окружения (камер, турелей), боевые скрипты (перегрев или взлом киберимплантов), взлом протоколов для получения доступа к корпоративным сетям;
- Развитие персонажа - Прокачка главных характеристик, улучшение умений, установка имплантов кибернетического оружия;
- Исследование мира - Огромный, детализированный город Найт-Сити и окружающие его Пустоши с различными локациями и секретами;
- Транспорт - Огромный выбор автомобилей и мотоциклов с управлением от первого или третьего лица; 
- Заказы - Выполнение миссий наемника, устранение целей и помощь местным бандам ради репутации;
[h3] 2) Сюжет[/h3] - История наемника по имени Ви в мрачном Найт-Сити - это глубокая драма о выживании и поиске себя. Сюжет мастерски сочетает экшен, политические интриги и глубокие личные переживания и драммы.
[h3] 3) Атмосфера.[/h3] 
- Проработка персонажей - Напарники и второстепенные лица прописаны феноменально. Они имеют собственные мотивы, характеры и уникальные цепочки заданий;
- Джонни Сильверхэнд - Блестяще сыгранный Киану Ривзом, этот оцифрованный рокер-террорист становится вашим постоянным спутником и двигателем сюжета;
- Вариативность - Выбор жизненного пути меняет пролог и варианты ответов в диалогах. Разветвленные разговоры с множеством выборов, влияющих на исход заданий. Последствия ваших действий, которые могут изменить судьбы ключевых персонажей, предлагая несколько кардинально разных финалов;
- Разнообразие районов - От неоновых трущоб Уотсона и корпоративных высоток Сити-центра до опасных Пустошей за городом, пугающий и прекрасный мир будущего...;
- Побочные квесты - Они не уступают основному сюжету. Вы будете расследовать заговоры, участвовать в гонках, решать судьбы целых корпораций или помогать бандам;
- Саунд-дизайн - Электронная музыка, эмбиент и радиостанции дополняют стиль, каждый выстрел звучит максимально сочно и разнообразно на каждом типе оружия, а озвучка заставляет удивляться своей проработе спустя даже сотню часов.
[h3] 4) Графика и оптимизация[/h3]  - Движок REDengine отлично отлажен, обеспечивая стабильную частоту кадров даже в самых густонаселенных районах. Картинка на протяжении всей игры остается красочной, насыщенной, четкой и интересной (особенно на фоне контраста локаций). Все эти моменты можно прочувствовать даже на слабом железе, но с ограничениями и жертвами (Баги в игре - как отдельный вид искуства). Игра идет стабильно, вылетов не наблюдалось.
[h3] 5) Локализация[/h3]  - Полная русская озвучка, включая мат и диалекты, а также текстовый перевод выполнены на высочайшем уровне.
[h3] 6) Продолжительность[/h3]  - Прохождение основной сюжетной кампании занимает около 20–25 часов. Полное изучение всех побочных историй, займет у вас 80–120+ часов увлекательного геймплея.
[h3] 7) DLC[/h3]  - Имеется сюжетное ДЛС "Phantom Liberty", которое рекомендуют проходить после основного сюжета.

Primeiro Contato

Bom, esse foi um jogo que eu tinha vontade de jogar desde o lançamento, mas nunca tive um PC ideal, e nem chegava perto de ter. Porém, eu tinha baixado ele por uns métodos diferentes e ficou meio de lado. Joguei a missão inicial onde tudo começa, mas não me apeguei tanto por diversos fatores. Porém, pouco depois disso, passei por uma fase realmente conturbada na minha vida e a única coisa que eu tinha pra me "distrair" disso tudo era o jogo, e eu terminei a história principal em um final de semana direto. Eu não tinha visto spoilers sobre o jogo nem os finais, e como eu tava completamente imerso no jogo durante 3 dias, acabei fazendo muitas escolhas como se realmente fosse eu dentro da história. E, por mais curioso que possa ter sido, o final que eu escolhi foi aquele em que V acaba se suicidando. Depois disso, eu já não tava tão empolgado pra continuar fazendo os outros finais e uma nova semana ia começar, então eu não podia ficar parado no tempo e eu tinha que aceitar as coisas que aconteceram.

Segunda Chance

Exatamente um ano depois, eu consegui fazer um upgrade no meu PC e, agora sendo capaz de jogar jogos mais "potentes", eu pensei em vários, mas tinha um que mesmo depois de zerar ainda passava às vezes na minha cabeça, com um ponto de exclamação dizendo "ainda falta alguma coisa". E realmente faltava. Quando eu baixei de jeitos "ilícitos", eu baixei junto com a DLC Phantom Liberty, porém eu não instalei KKKKKKKK. Então, fora missões secundárias e outros finais, ainda faltava a DLC, que em todo lugar diziam ser incrível, ter até mesmo mais conteúdo que o jogo original. Então, dessa vez, eu comprei o jogo na Steam, com a DLC, e demorei uns meses pra ter coragem de abrir e jogar. Mas enfim fiz isso. Instalei MUITOS mods que, sinceramente, agregaram absurdamente à experiência do jogo, principalmente na parte de customização, mas sem mexer no core do jogo, nada de voar ou armas completamente quebradas.

Quebra de Expectativas

Eu sempre pensei que refazer algo que eu já fiz eu não iria conseguir. Por exemplo, assistir a uma série que eu já assisti, zerar um jogo que eu já zerei, esse tipo de coisa. Só que dessa vez foi completamente diferente. Eu realmente tive uma quebra de expectativa, mas de um jeito fora do padrão. Eu tinha expectativas de que eu iria jogar no máximo a DLC e depois iria desistir, porque eu tô acostumado a fazer isso, porém dessa vez foi diferente. E tudo o que eu ouvi falarem sobre a DLC, etc., era verdade. A DLC num certo momento parece ser um jogo completamente diferente, do início ao fim só foi me prendendo cada vez mais. Imagino que na escolha que precede o final, todos tenham escolhido ajudar a Songbird, e comigo não foi diferente. Porém, dessa vez, em vez de largar completamente o jogo após fazer um final, eu decidi que dessa vez eu iria completar 100%, e foi a melhor escolha que eu poderia ter feito.

Johnny Silverhand

Não existe Cyberpunk sem ele, e não existe Johnny sem Cyberpunk. Toda a trajetória da relação do Johnny com o nosso personagem... no início ele sendo aquele cara irritante, difícil de se gostar, em toda escolha ele sempre julgando ou querendo fazer o contrário. Mas, conforme o tempo passa, ele muda, mas ao mesmo tempo V também muda. E, sem você perceber, os dois são como um só, cada um com sua personalidade forte. Mas, como a própria Rogue percebeu, V conseguiu mudá-lo e ele conseguiu mudar V, e dá nitidamente pra perceber no que a relação deles se tornou. Johnny, que antes era um completo egoísta, agora mesmo tendo total controle do corpo no final "Temperance", ainda assim escolhe devolver para V.

V: No Johnny we won't. We're outta options. And I don't have the strength to keep fighting. Just promise me one thing asshole... you won't forget me.

DLC

Sim, ela realmente é tudo isso e ainda mais. Se você decide ajudar a Songbird e trair o Reed, é sim um final absurdo de bom, mas querendo ou não, você tem uma bomba nuclear te ajudando nesse final. Mas a história da Songbird com o Reed é incrível e vale a pena sim fazer essa "rota". Agora, se você escolhe a segunda opção, trair a Songbird... a partir dali o jogo se torna qualquer coisa, menos o que você tá acostumado. As cinematics, as missões de ir atrás da Songbird... você deixa de ser um mercenário que sempre se sobressai por cima dos outros pra ser apenas um ratinho dentro de um laboratório com um leão atrás de você. Eu nunca achei que iria ver algo assim dentro desse jogo e teve cenas que realmente me deixavam agoniado e cada vez mais sedento de jogar. A DLC é simplesmente impecável.

Completionist

Eu demorei mais que o necessário pra finalmente completar 100% do jogo, mas não me arrependo nem um pouco disso. Os mods de veículos e de personalização que eu coloquei ajudaram muito nisso. Ficar andando com uma Lamborghini pela cidade indo atrás das GIGS pra completar cada parte, me aventurar por lugares a que eu não dei tanta atenção e descobrir alguns easter eggs... e às vezes parei um pouco de fazer algumas missões como as de denúncia policial pra dar atenção a outras missões que não são necessárias para o 100%, e foi uma experiência incrível.

O Fim

Foi o primeiro jogo que eu realmente parei pra fazer o 100% e não tinha como ter sido outro. Quando eu comecei lá na primeira vez, com o jogo pirateado, eu nunca soube o que esperar, não tinha visto gameplays, meus gráficos rodando no mínimo possível a 30 fps... e dar uma segunda chance pra esse jogo foi a melhor decisão que eu tomei. Mesmo que tenha sido cansativo fazer algumas missões para completar o jogo 100%, as histórias e missões secundárias fizeram valer mais que a pena, e principalmente os finais. E a frase que eu diria que define esse jogo e a DLC é:

"Não existe final feliz em Night City"

Но за такой невероятно открытый и насыщенный мир можно простить, пусть уже и прошло 6 лет с момента релиза.
   Сюжет понравился, пусть и понесло в моменте, что с пеной у рта хотелось закрыть абсолютно все квесты и получить всякое сильное оружие и крутые машины. Но потом от этого аж начало подташнивать, что забросил игру на полтора месяца, хотя до финала оставалось 2.5 часа от силы.

Иногда невероятно тяжелые выборы дает игра, а иногда и тупые, что ты не можешь их изменить, только откатывать сейв, как было с Даламейном. С каждым из них ты чувствовал связь от начала и до конца. Кроме телефонных звонков, как будто можно было сделать их с более расширенным функционалом и больше вариаций ответов и вопросов с каждым разом — это очень сильно бьет по вовлечению в сюжет. И как раз после этого вообще отпадает желание звонить кому-либо в игре и как-то взаимодействовать по телефону.

И вот, спустя 170 часов, спустя получения всех концовок, спустя "платину", хочется сказать только одно, Cyberpunk 2077 - одна из лучших игр за последние 10 лет, если не лучшая(лично для меня), особенно спустя 5 с лишним лет после релиза, а так же нового DLC, и вот почему. Доброе утрой Нааайт-Сити!
