[b][i]СЮЖЕТ:[/i][/b]
Сюжет - одна из сильнейших сторон игры, однако, я проходил игру 2 раза, на релизе и сейчас, в 2026 году, в своем первом прохождении я совершил огромную ошибку, а именно решил не проходить побочные задания, а они здесь совсем не хуже основного сюжета, но дело даже не в этом, самое главное, что в этих заданиях скрыт большой кусок основного сюжета, без них ты не узнаешь прошлое Джонни Сильверхенда, Бестии, Керри Евродина, не сможешь почувствовать себя детективом вместе с Ривером Уордом, не решишь проблемы с Вудуистыми, Шельмами, Сетевым дозором вместе с Джуди, да в конце концов не покатаешься на Василиске с Панам(лучший персонаж игры, после Джонни конечно) и не станешь Частью Альдекальдо, к тому же все эти действия открывают множество концовок + 1 секретную, так что сам по себе основной сюжет хорош, но смотреть на него в отрыве от сайд-квестов - ошибка.
[b][i]ГЕЙМПЛЕЙ:[/i][/b]
Геймплей - огромная вариативность в билдостроении, хочешь быть нетраннером - никто не мешает вкачаться в взлом, хочешь быть "современным самураем" - да пожалуйста, или может быть хитменом на минималках - почему нет, ну или самый простой вариант, взять автомат и вперед - всегда рабочий вариант, вождение машин также давольно приятное, есть множество красивых машин(Porche 911 - моя любовь), а за такое время после релиза почти все баги уже были исправленны(однако они все еще есть).
[b][i]ГРАФИКА:[/i][/b]
Графика - по всей видимости Cyberpunk 2077 так и останется тестовым полигоном для нового железа, с каждым годом в него все добавляют и добавляют новые графические технологии, так что не смотря на то, что игре уже 5+ лет, по-моему мнению это все еще одна из самых красивейших игр на данный момент.
[b][i]СЛОЖНОСТЬ:[/i][/b]
Сложность - одна из спорных частей игры, ведь при хорошем билде даже Макс-Так на максимальном уровне сложности не является угрозой, скорее ты для них - угроза, а финальный бой с Адамом Смешером больше похож на избиение беспомощного, чем на битву с легендарным наемником.
[b][i]ГРИНД:[/i][/b]
Гринд - он совершенно необязательный, однако пока я проходил игру на 100%, в любом случаи получил максимальный 60 уровень и максимальный 50 уровень репутации наемника. Да и поверьте, вам захочется так же пройти игру, поэтому скорее всего вы так и так получите максимальный уровень прокачки и репутации.
[b][i]ВРЕМЯ ПРОХОЖДЕНИЯ:[/i][/b]
Полное прохождение игры займет у вас около 100-150 часов, конечно можно и быстрей, если бежать по гайдам, но так не интересно) Однако простое прохождение займет коло 30-40 часвов, если просто бежать по главным квестам, но... зачем?

I've played through the game several times, and every time I complete the game I like it a little less. I've played more hours on another account, I have completed the game three or four times. I will be concise.

It is scripted to all hell, cutscenes galore, actual roleplaying opportunities are few and far between without impactful consequences. I cannot in good faith call this game a good RPG, this is just Skyrim with a different setting. I found it very hard to care about any of the characters - everyone was just a different brand of weird asshole. I had no attachments to any of the characters when I reached the end of the game. I would have rather had them all killed.

The best part of the game by far is combat, specifically melee combat. Again, the CD Project Red has laid another dung pie that scales with player level with level equipment. Maybe there are people who enjoy the life of a homeless person with a horde of garbage in a shopping cart, but I certainly don't. I have no tolerance for having to sift through all the corpses to find an item that is 5% better. And there is crafting for some reason? Yes, pick up even more shit and turn it into other shit. It's just busywork. The game is at its best when you get a legendary weapon so you don't have to look for another one and just start cutting people into pieces after acquiring the necessary skills and cyberware. The game is much better if you completely ignore the meager RPG components and just play it as an action game.

So, in conclusion, it's a very bad RPG. If you are looking for a true RPG experience, don't play it. The plot is okay, the combat is okay. You will get some enjoyment out of playing this game, but it's not worth it.

Cyberpunk 2077 en 2026, c'est nova !

Tout le monde se souvient de la débâcle de sa sortie en 2020, autant dire que le jeu a bien remonté depuis, il se paye même le luxe d'être sûrement l'un des meilleurs jeux de son époque.

Dans son genre, Cyberpunk excelle en tout ou presque : le gameplay, le scénario, l'open world, franchement, mis à part que les véhicules soient des caisses à savon, j'ai du mal à lui trouver un vrai défaut. Merci Jackie, Misty, Vick, Judy, Rogue, Panam, Takemura, Sol, Alex, So Mi. Merci David et Lucy pour m'avoir donné envie de venir à Night City. 
Merci Johnny.

Merci CDPR de m'avoir fait vivre à une époque fantasmée, remplie d'intrigues et de rebondissements que je ne vivrai probablement jamais. C'est pour ça que je joue aux jeux vidéo.

Bref, si votre config tient la route (à vérifier avant quand même), y'a pas d'hésitation à avoir. Si The Witcher 3 est le jeu de sa décennie, c'est pareil pour CP 2077. En attendant, je ferme le livre Cyberpunk 2077, mais une chose est déjà certaine, je l'ouvrirai de nouveau, un jour ou l'autre.

被dlc与动画拯救的本体

2077的本体说实话我是不满意的：缩水的主线、注水的支线、大量的马桶、刻板的色情暴力、低智的敌人AI、看似立体的地图构造实际上仅有外壳、看似有所选择的委托却仅仅是粗暴与千篇一律的冲突、看似繁多的流派BD最终强力且直观的只有几种、还要在找医生换义体与部分刷子内容上有所限制、等等等等。甚至在绝大多数时候把赛博朋克四个字换成看门狗都没有违和感，很大程度上让我想起了幽灵线东京或是消光这类缺乏内核的空洞沙盒。除去第一章最开始的具有复杂脚本树的高质量任务之外，竟然在最终任务前都找不到任何重大主线剧情差分，加之空有外表却缺乏生气与互动反馈的夜之城，实际上如果没有动画和dlc的加成，本体的水准在开放世界里也只能勉强排到中游，尽管夜之城确实有着它五光十色与赛博朋克风味的独特魅力。

然后我来到了狗镇。
毫不夸张的说，往日之影dlc从演出到剧情、从场景搭建到地图密度、从新增玩法到玩具武器，包括十个手工感与设计感极强的委托任务，在第一人称RPG这个范畴下都是当之无愧的一流水平。跨越让大多数编剧现原形的政治与复仇戏码，V仅仅以一个佣兵的视角见证并经历了一场隐秘又壮丽的谍战故事。往日之影并未过多拷问我的立场、更没有强行输出价值观，它只是把四位塑造丰满的角色摆在了我的眼前，无奈、悔恨、坚持、矛盾，每个在当下能做出的最好选择都不可避免地通向一出出悲剧，仿佛罗生门一般的群像剧、搭配强大的音画表现与演出效果，使我在四个结局怅然若失之余，也不禁慨叹CDPR明明有能力做出好游戏，却倾斜了过多资源在本体无意义的大世界与画饼上。在最终行动前与alex在吧台跳着全世界最笨拙最愚蠢的舞蹈，却让我窥见了笼中鸟对自由最热烈最真挚的向往，是我整部游戏中最喜欢的桥段。原来在这个世界观下，像帕南、像alex这般敢爱敢恨的角色，在CDPR笔下是这般可贵、又是这般富有魅力。

其他想说的也没有太多。在多年的修修补补与dlc后，2077毫无疑问是它这一类别中不可错过的一款。你能看见夜之城的霓虹美学、看见阶级差距下的众生百态、看见主要角色们的人格魅力、看见双主角的成长弧光、看见歪掉的赛博朋克科技树、看见并未细说的巨大阴谋、看见梦想、看见绝望、看见一段佳话与一段传奇。

+++ 传奇的往日之影dlc
++ 丰富的世界观、丰满的人物塑造、优秀的主线文本
++ 强大的赛博朋克视觉美学
+ 拓展性足够的流派式战斗玩法
- 当年的大饼噱头仍未实现
- 各式各样的小bug
- 建筑群缺乏立体与内部探索
-- 本体的大量马桶支线与委托
-- 低智且无反馈的AI，平庸罐头的开放世界

A epic open world first person game with many different factions and political elites. A great story that'll have you either laughing or emotional at times. There's a skill tree mechanic in which you can unlock new abilities that'll either help you in combat, survive or learn skills to help you progress by means of learning how to hack systems, open doors and ventilation shafts.

The character animations are nicely done and life-like. The quests or missions are super long compared to other games. You literally feel like you're hanging out with someone for 2-3 hours. With lengthy dialogues and animations. Also, whether you are picking someone up, driving to a location to gather supplies, checking out or gathering intel on an enemy base before entering, driving to a location to pick up your reward. And even after everything, sometimes dropping that person back off.

To make the missions faster and easier to navigate, you can either fast travel to your objectives or allow AI to drive you to your objective markers with auto-drive. You can also skip forward in time, which skips dialogue and animations for those who have to reload a save and don't want to go through it all over again.

The Phantom Liberty DLC is well worth the price as I thought it would never end. But in a good way. With much more content, such as additional missions, skill tree, tech, cyberware, vehicles and weapons. A new cast of characters and actors. Not only does the base game alone have multiple different endings based on the decisions you make in the game, but the Phantom Liberty DLC also has many different endings.

The only downside to the game for me is there's no vehicle garage or aircraft hangars where you can customize your vehicles. You can at least purchase many different types of vehicles and give them a custom paint job.

I recommend making a manual save for each mission you play as there are some missable achievements and you also may have not liked the choices you have made that will change the overall experience and ending.

我觉得2077真得目前整体上是一款优秀的RPG。但是，不推荐它的原因在于，整体的支线故事和叙事设计相当一般，也不太符合个人的调性。如果说巫师系列的故事是传统的涉及爱恨情仇，爱情、亲情、家庭纠纷、村民困扰、妖魔与人的冲突、战争带来的动乱，他们其实有许多现实的“源头“，容易形成精神共鸣（其实我感觉很难简单总结）。

2077的很多故事就是纯粹的当雇佣兵在街头巷尾杀人，处理一些有的没的纷争、有的一部分故事充分折射了新时代新技术下的伦理危机，比如影响人的大脑从而改变一个人、有的一部分是解决某些NPC的心事。你会发现，这些故事其实并没有那种明显的联结感，尤其是前两部分，而后者，我们许多朋友，更像是V一直在提供情绪价值，听他们的心事，巴拉巴拉自己以前怎么样现在怎么样，就很”宏观“，站在一个很高的维度去谈，但完事了，一堆烂摊子还要我们自己去奔波，当然，我并不是是奢求游戏角色解决我们主角的生命危机，而是希望支线的故事更有温度。游戏中想透过”高屋建瓴“的人生对话深刻共鸣，我感觉很难，效果很差，不如透过具体的一段具有普遍共鸣性的故事来塑造一个人的性格，反映其性格的变迁。我们很多时候接的任务就很纯粹，A挟持了B，或者C绑架了D，解决完了感谢一顿，然后对方说下自己怎么怎么，差不多就这种闭环。问题就在后半段，有时候单单只是述说自己现在什么感受之后什么感受，不够具有冲击力，人通过看对方的动作、丰富的表情才能更具体的了解这个人。在叙事上，我在想通过侧面描写，让玩家自己拼凑对方的人生可能效果也更好，更能引发人的共鸣，因为侧面描写所提供的物，可能更可感，让一个人的人生更可信，我们才更愿意”打开心扉”（比如一封表白信，可以通过信纸选择，内容的体裁、文字的书法，文字内容诸多蛛丝马迹反映一个人的性格，我们自己推理出的，也更值得信任），以及物本身就承载许多难以简单言语的信息（比如一个人的审美）。

其实个人所玩到的有的支线本身的设计是不错的，故事意蕴也很有意思，尤其那种深入挖掘和展开新时代危机的任务。（当然平心而论，毕竟本身背景就是赛博朋克，每个支线多少都会展现新时代的问题，所以这里强调的是深入挖掘和展开，具有比较“有意思”的丰富的曲折性的任务。）但许多打打杀杀的任务，一些”高屋建瓴“的人生对话故事都让整个支线显得乏善可陈，尤其这些支线分布在大地图上，你需要满地图的跑来跑去，传送来传送去，会让人感觉本就不算特别有趣的故事上再加之乏味的前置步骤。        

此外，以上总总所反映的那种非常的混街头性质的游戏氛围也不太符合个人口味。（这里值得提醒一下，我个人按照游戏体验，本作尽管也是打打杀杀之类的，但完全不能把氛围和黑手党、荒野大镖客2、GTA5对标。因此不能轻率得认为可以接受后者，就必然可以接受2077。当然这只是我一点主观臆断，仅供参考。）

以上只是初略对2077任务设计上的感慨。不符合个人口味的雇佣兵故事调性+乏味的叙事（当然，我们也可以看出CDPR全配音+游戏内短信+游戏内视频+尽量不掉主角控制权的角色间的互动，还是为任务设计付出了努力，说乏味并不是否定这一方面的努力），让我个人的游戏体验不算特别好。如果你比较喜欢雇佣兵打打杀杀任务，其实我玩到的那些支线设计的还是不错的，因此本作任务还值得尝试全完成的。

除了以上内容，还有游戏本身的开放世界搭建也存在问题，可以继续参考别的玩家的评论。总之，从2077，其实让我个人更担忧的CDPR的叙事逻辑是否彻底转变了，我不像在任何游戏都看到一个像V一样的“憨子”雇佣兵，也不想继续玩到2077下的这种支线氛围和叙事设计......

İlk çıktığı dönemde ortalığı karıştıran, hatalarıyla ve kötü yorumlarıyla gündeme oturan Cyberpunk 2077, yıllar içerisinde aldığı güncellemelerle kendini oldukça toparladı. Çıkış dönemindeki haliyle şu anki hali arasında ciddi fark var ve bunu oyuna birkaç saat ayırınca hemen hissediyorsunuz.

Oyunun atmosferi gerçekten başarılı. Night City'nin sokaklarında dolaşırken yaşayan bir dünyadaymış hissini alıyorsunuz. Şehir tasarımı, karakterler ve genel sanat tasarımı oldukça etkileyici. Bu konuda yapımın hakkını vermek lazım.

Ancak oyunun bazı pürüzleri yok değil. Özellikle hikâye tarafında oyuncuya seçim özgürlüğü sunuyormuş gibi görünse de başlangıçta seçtiğiniz yaşam yolu ilk birkaç saat dışında çok büyük fark yaratmıyor. Nomad, Street Kid ya da Corpo olarak başlasanız da bir noktadan sonra hikâye sizi aynı ana yola bağlıyor. Bu durum rol yapma tarafında biraz daha fazla çeşitlilik bekleyenleri hayal kırıklığına uğratabilir.

Bir diğer konu ise savaş sistemi. Belki ben çözemedim, belki de gerçekten bana hitap etmedi bilmiyorum ama oyunu bitirmeme rağmen çatışmaların büyük kısmı beni çok fazla içine çekemedi. Boss savaşları genellikle daha eğlenceli ve akılda kalıcı olsa da sıradan çatışmalarda aynı hissi alamadım. Oyunu oynayan başka arkadaşlarla konuştuğumda onların da benzer şeyler söylediğini gördüm. Savaş mekaniği garip bir şekilde hem akıcı hem de bir o kadar tuhaf hissettiriyor.

Bunun dışında oyun gayet keyifli. Atmosferi, karakterleri ve dünyası sayesinde insanı ekran başında tutmayı başarıyor. Özellikle güncel haliyle oynandığında kesinlikle şans verilmesi gereken bir yapım.

Çıkışındaki kaotik dönemi geride bırakıp kendini toparlamayı başaran, kusurları olsa da oyuncuya unutulmaz bir bilim kurgu deneyimi sunan bir oyun. Aynı klasmanda çok fazla rakibi de olmadığı için türü sevenlerin kesinlikle denemesi gereken yapımlardan biri.

This game takes place in Night City, one of the most beautiful and detailed cities I have seen in a video game. The city looks especially amazing during the night, with all the lights, signs, and atmosphere making it feel alive.

You play as V and explore the city while upgrading different parts of your body to unlock new abilities and combat options. The gameplay gives you a lot of freedom in how you want to fight and build your character.

Everybody knows how rough the launch of this game was. It was a complete mess for many players. However, after multiple updates and the release of Phantom Liberty, the game has become much better and is now a great experience.

The story is excellent, and the characters are one of the strongest parts of the game. Johnny Silverhand, played by Keanu Reeves, is an amazing character. His dialogues, personality, and role in the story made him one of my favorite characters in the game.

Your choices also matter throughout the story. The people you talk to, the decisions you make, and the way you handle certain situations can affect future missions and events, so it is worth paying attention to what is happening.

The soundtrack is fantastic and always feels right for the moment. Whether you are exploring Night City or taking part in a mission, the music fits perfectly.

Phantom Liberty is also worth playing. It adds a new area called Dogtown along with new missions and characters. I enjoyed it just as much as the main game.

There are still some bugs and sometimes they can affect gameplay. They are not as bad as they were at launch, but you will probably run into a few issues during your playthrough.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is a fantastic game with a great story, memorable characters, fun combat, and one of the best open worlds I have explored in a game.

This is GTA for the cyberware age, and if you haven’t bought it yet, you’re missing out.

Night City is what happens when capitalism runs with no brakes. Corporations like Arasaka own everything, including the cops, the politicians, and basically the air you breathe. To this city you’re a number, a bank balance, and a body that’s worth more for parts than as a person. Compared to Night City, our version of capitalism looks like a charity.

The point of the game is to flip the bird to all of that and make a name for yourself anyway. You start as a nobody merc. Then you chrome the living hell out of yourself: mantis blades, a Sandevistan that slows time to a crawl, optics, reinforced tendons, whatever you can afford and your body can take. By the end you’re stronger than Night City’s legends, Adam Smasher included. (Fuck that guy, by the way. Putting him down is one of the most satisfying moments I’ve had in a game.)

You do what you want, when you want. Go in loud with a shotgun, ghost through a building by hacking every camera and turret, or talk your way past the fight completely. Side gigs and random encounters fill the whole map, and many of them are just as good as the main story. The city looks incredible, especially at night, all neon, rain, and a little sleaze.

Then there’s Johnny Silverhand, a dead rockerboy living in your head who has opinions about everything. The story goes places I didn’t expect, and the endings stuck with me long after the credits.

Yes, the launch was rough. That was years ago. The game you can buy today is the one they promised, and it’s one of the best open worlds out there. Pick it up, chrome up, and go make Night City remember your name.

Cyberpunk 2077 is the game I hoped it would be when it was first announced.

Night City is one of the most immersive open worlds ever created. Every district has its own atmosphere, architecture, and culture, making exploration rewarding even when you're not following a quest. The visual design remains outstanding, and the city feels alive at every hour of the day.

The gameplay offers a great deal of freedom. Whether you prefer stealth, hacking, precision gunplay, or charging into combat with cybernetic enhancements and a katana, the game supports a wide variety of playstyles. Character progression feels meaningful, and experimenting with different builds is genuinely enjoyable.

The writing is another highlight. The main story is compelling, but many of the side quests are just as memorable. The characters feel believable, and their stories often leave a lasting impression long after the credits roll.

The Phantom Liberty expansion elevates the experience even further with excellent missions, strong performances, and some of the best content in the game.

Cyberpunk 2077 isn't perfect, but after years of updates and improvements, it has become a polished and engaging RPG that delivers dozens of hours of entertainment.

Although you do need to do some research on graphics settings to make sure its dialed in. After playing couple hours I looked up some videos about the graphics and made some adjustments and my mind was completely blown away. I haven't dipped into the ray tracing just yet as i really like the DLAA settings, its super clear and very sharp. 

The progression could feel a little bit overwhelming as there's a bit of depth there with cyberware, but you will get the hang of it pretty quickly. The skill tree is also pretty straight forward.

Only thing that it lacks for me is gun customization.  Its a bit shallow and lacks the depth I would expect from a triple A rpg. Other than that at the moment I dont really have any other complaints.

So for a little bit of context, I did not like Cyberpunk at first cause my first impression of it was at launch on the PS4. I will forever regard this as my lesson to never pre-order anything ever again.

And with that out of the way, this game's pretty damn good now. Only real gripe I'd have with it is the combat feels a bit clunky no matter the playstyle (weapons kinda feel like they lack oomph) but it's not something too jarring.

The vibe of Night City really makes it feel like it's a living city with some people doing various weird/freaky things. The story is really memorable between some stupid little side objective and a high-stakes main mission, all with a side of allowing to approach it whatever way you want: wanna go full social engineering on your foes? Maybe sneaking by? Blowing their heads of with your mind? Or maybe just the good ol' big iron? The game really promotes getting creative with it and that's commendable. Weapons are mostly fun, especially the unique ones that can get a little wacky with their effects.

Safe for me to say, CDPR redeemed themselves. I'll be back for Phantom Liberty sometime (and the rumored second DLC).

One of the best if not the best story games i have every touched.

The Graphics id give a  10/10, they are gorgeous even tho i am running it on mid level graphics and it still has at least 70 fpsat the lowest. The map building is also awesome, each part of the map is deeply in touch with the certain organization running it shown not only by the Architecture, but also by the people and the language they speak.
TL;DR nice graphics even on mid settings

The fighting aspect gets a 7/10 from me, the fighting in itself is most of the time the same thing, you either shoot or slash through the enemies until you either fight a boss or get to a mission objective. The thing that makes the fightign better for me though is the variaty, you can basically be like a ninja and play to only do kills stealthy which 8 times out of 10 works perfectly fine, of course you still have to do bosses normaly. You could also go for a quickhack kind of style and make it your objective to never even enter the area your target is in.
TL;DR the combat is pretty much the same unless you change your way of playing, but you have a lot of options on how you fight.

The missions get a 8,5/10 from me. If you just stick to the main mission then ofc you will see a certain pattern being repeated here and there, but if you actually look around and do side missions either from certain fixers or just random gigs you find, you will most of the time be rewarded with either good loot for your current level or sometimes even a iconic weapon or piece of equipment. The good thing about cyberpunk side missions is that most missions are kind of unique and some even offer different outcomes to other missions, ofc there will be some that are nearly identical to other ones, but cyberpunk is one of the first games where i actually played the side quests because they were something new everytime. Sure doing them one after another is annoying and kind of boring, but sprinkling some side quests here and there has a nice touch.
TL;DR the game has nice missions which make it even more enjoyable as long as you dont just ruch the main mission

Now one of the most important things, the difficulty, i can only speak out of the perspective of someone who played the game only on the second hardest difficulty.

One thing is for sure, if you just started dont, and i mean DONT play on Very Hard if you want to actually experience the game in a way where you will have fond memories of this game. Now onto the gear, for me the gear gets a 6/10

The iconic weapons are like seeing a legendary item in fortnite, either it is the one and only legendary scar one of the best if not the best weapons in game or its a chug jug, in non gaming terms iconic weapons are just a hit or a miss with them being more often a miss. The worst part about this ICONIC weapon system is that some "classes"/builds feel like they are getting more then others, like the smart weapons for example, there are some that are incredible and not even hard to get, the problem you ask? You have maybe 3-4 that are acutally useable and that is not very much compared to other classes, especially if you have to do certain missions which you dont have access to in the first act and are more in the mid game areas.
TL;DR Normal weapons are nice but the iconic weapons are like 65% trash and only those 35% are good/better then normal weapons with mods 

TL;DR and this time its the last one. 
This game is incredible, Graphic wise but also the missions and the combat can be pretty nice. The main story is well done and the DLC is probably my favourite in all of gaming. The weapons are unique with most iconics being kind of useless but still cool, the skill tree is nice and gives niche play styles also some options to become even better, the loot is at some times even too much and game runs smoothly even when not on the highest settings.
The last few things i have to say is, dont just run down the main mission without doing at least some side mission, whether it is killing a couple of goons here and there or actually doing mission from panam or padre for example. This game is beautiful and if you just fly through it you will not only miss rewards that are good but also the experience this game has to offer.

And try mods lol they make the already good game even better.

Overall a solid 9/10 for me (with the dlc)

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the strangest gaming experiences I've had.

I bought the game at launch and, like many people, experienced some of the issues that surrounded the release. Despite that, I still gave it a fair chance and put around 11 hours into it before moving on. Some time later I came back and tried again, putting another 10 or so hours into a new save, but for whatever reason the game still wasn't clicking with me.

Then recently I decided to give it one more chance.

This time something changed.

Not only did the game finally click, but I couldn't stop playing it. I became so invested that after finishing the game I immediately started a second playthrough and completed the entire thing again while working towards 100% achievements.

Once you get a grasp of the mechanics, skill trees and general systems, everything starts to fall into place. The game does a lot and can feel overwhelming at first, but once it clicks it becomes incredibly rewarding.

The main story is outstanding.

The characters, writing, setting and atmosphere are some of the best I've experienced in gaming. Night City feels alive in a way very few open worlds manage to achieve. There is always something happening, whether it's a serious story moment, a side quest, random humour, or simply exploring the city itself.

The game also offers a huge amount of freedom in how you approach combat and progression. Different builds can completely change how the game feels, making multiple playthroughs genuinely worthwhile rather than simply replaying the same experience.

As a fan of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, I also loved the references and connections throughout the game. They never felt forced and added another layer of enjoyment to an already fantastic world.

Phantom Liberty deserves special praise.

The expansion is exceptional from start to finish. The new area is fantastic, the story is brilliant and the new characters are some of the best in the entire game. Solomon Reed, played by Idris Elba, and Song So Mi quickly became two of my favourite characters in Cyberpunk 2077. Their performances and the choices surrounding them create some of the strongest moments in the entire game.

If you enjoy Cyberpunk 2077, Phantom Liberty is not optional in my opinion. It is a must-buy expansion and one of the best DLCs I have played.

Achievement-wise, I found the list very respectful of the player's time. There are a few achievements that benefit from planning ahead, multiple playthroughs or smart save points, but I never felt forced into repetitive grinding. During my first playthrough I did experience a few issues with achievements not unlocking correctly, which ultimately contributed to my second run, but thankfully I enjoyed the game enough that this never felt like a chore.

After 223 hours and 100% achievement completion, Cyberpunk 2077 isn't just one of my favourite games, it's my game of the decade.

It took several attempts to finally click with me, but once it did, I couldn't put it down.

Спустя 5 лет, два из которых я провел в состоянии полной прокрастинации, я наконец-то закончил эту замечательную работу. В прошлом месяце я закончил основную кампанию, и, вау, насколько сложной оказалась ситуация. Множество выборов и, соответственно, несколько последствий. В начале у игры было много проблем, этого нельзя отрицать; она была почти неиграбельной, но со временем и с обновлениями многие серьезные проблемы были решены (баги все еще есть, но уже не так, как раньше).

Что сказать о персонажах? Ну, они очень хорошо прописаны, каждый из них раскрывает свою личность через интонацию, мимику и, самое главное, визуальную составляющую, каждый детальнее предыдущего.

И как можно не любить Джонни Сильверхэнда? Помимо того, что изначально он пытался предстать угрозой жизни главного героя, он оказался многогранным персонажем: от эгоцентричного безумца до очень близкого друга, с философскими идеями, подкрепленными моральными ценностями, и с точкой зрения, защищающей жизнь игрока (в зависимости от уровня близости с ним). Я не могу сказать больше, так как это будет считаться спойлером относительно тех больших перемен, которые с ним происходят.

НайтСити — если не самый важный персонаж в этой истории, то, по крайней мере, самый главный, вовлеченный в конфликты с самого начала: коррупция, бандитские войны и, наконец, война корпораций, в разгар которой город пришел в упадок.

[b]Phantom Liberty:[/b] это DLC для меня особенное; персонажи сумели удержать мое внимание на основном сюжете. Здесь моральные ценности доведены до абсурда. Вы очень легко сочувствуете представленным персонажам, лжи и еще раз лжи; Вы не знаете, кому можно доверять. Обещание лекарства затягивает вас в эту интригу. [spoiler](Я не могу упоминать здесь никаких персонажей, потому что это связано с цепочкой событий, и говорить даже об одном было бы неправильно)[/spoiler]
[url=https://youtu.be/u15tEo0wsQI?list=RDu15tEo0wsQI]Dawid Podsiadło, P.T. Adamczyk — Phantom Liberty[/url]
После прохождения игры у меня осталась пустота, но могу сказать следующее: игра очень стоит того. За два года моего прохождения у меня не было особых проблем; сейчас она работает плавно, иногда встречаются баги, но теперь вы можете наслаждаться всем без сбоев во время игры.

Кстати, о геймплее: в игре обширное дерево навыков, охватывающее все уровни — от боя до интеллекта персонажа. Кроме того, некоторые косметические предметы, такие как броня и кибернетические импланты, улучшают игровой процесс.

Dopo 5 anni, di cui due di pura procrastinazione, ho finalmente terminato questa meravigliosa opera. Il mese scorso ho concluso la campagna principale e, wow, quanto era complessa la situazione. Tante scelte e, con esse, diverse conseguenze. Il gioco, all'inizio, aveva molti problemi, non si può negare; era quasi ingiocabile, ma con il passare del tempo e con gli aggiornamenti, molti problemi seri sono stati risolti (ci sono ancora dei bug, ma niente a che vedere con prima).

Che dire dei personaggi? Beh, sono scritti benissimo, ognuno presenta la propria personalità attraverso il tono di voce, le espressioni facciali e, soprattutto, l'aspetto visivo, ognuno più dettagliato dell'altro.

E come si fa a non amare Johnny Silverhand? Oltre a presentarsi inizialmente come una minaccia per la vita del protagonista, si è rivelato un personaggio sfaccettato, da folle egocentrico a amico intimo, con idee filosofiche accompagnate da valori morali e con un punto di vista volto a preservare la vita del giocatore (a seconda del livello di affinità con lui). Non posso dire molto altro, poiché sarebbe considerato uno spoiler riguardo alla grande trasformazione che subisce.

NightCity è, se non il personaggio più importante, di questa storia, coinvolta in conflitti fin dall'inizio, che si tratti di corruzione, guerre tra bande e, soprattutto, la guerra tra corporazioni, nel mezzo della quale la città è andata in rovina.

[b]Phantom Liberty:[/b] questo DLC è molto speciale per me; i personaggi sono riusciti a tenermi concentrato sulla trama principale. Qui i valori morali sono esageratamente incentrati sul giocatore. Si prova empatia molto facilmente per i personaggi presentati, tra bugie e ancora bugie; non si sa di chi fidarsi. La promessa di una cura è ciò che ti trascina in questo intrigo. After finishing both the main story and Phantom Liberty, I can confidently say that Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best RPGs I have ever played.

What impressed me the most was the world of Night City. It feels alive, detailed, and immersive in a way that very few games achieve. Every district has its own personality, and simply exploring the city can lead to memorable moments.

The characters are exceptional. Panam, Judy, Johnny, Reed, and Songbird all feel like real people with their own motivations, flaws, and struggles. Their stories stayed with me long after the credits rolled.

The gameplay offers a huge amount of freedom. I played primarily as netrunner, and hacking my way through missions was incredibly satisfying. The combat, cyberware system, and character progression give you plenty of ways to create your own playstyle.

Phantom Liberty takes everything to another level. The story is tense, emotional, and full of difficult choices where there are no perfect answers. Some of the endings hit harder than any game I've played in years.

What truly elevates Cyberpunk 2077, however, is its atmosphere. The music is absolutely world-class, the visuals are stunning, and the art direction is among the best in the industry. Night City is beautiful, dangerous, and unforgettable.

Cyberpunk 2077 had a rough launch, but today it stands as one of the finest action RPGs available. If you enjoy immersive worlds, meaningful characters, and stories that make you think, this game is an easy recommendation.

10/10 – a journey I won't forget.

Sin duda recomendadísimo en 2026!

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best games that I’ve played. It had a rough start back in 2020, but they put the time and effort into fixing it up, and it is now one of the greatest story games I’ve ever played.

The story is massive and full of options, with multiple endings and dialogue choices. It’s an amazing game for people who like having choices that affect their experience.

The gameplay is also great. The gunplay feels really solid, and the same goes for the melee weapons. It never felt like a cheap game. Hacking while fighting also felt very fluid and easy, creating some really cool and cinematic moments.

The characters are well written. You genuinely feel for them and feel like you have real connections with them.

The graphics are some of the best out there, especially with ray tracing and path tracing. The soundtrack in this game is amazing. I’ve even saved a couple of tracks to my Spotify playlist.

The performance of the game varies depending on what you play it on, and it can be a bit demanding. For me, my PC ran it insanely well at 4K and 120 FPS.

The DLC is 100% worth purchasing.

Overall, this game is a 10/10 masterpiece, and it’s one of those games that I can always replay.

也许我还是不完全懂你，但至少，我和其他人不一样了，我知道你的初衷，也知道你为何会变得疯狂而又理性.....

但你......与众不同，我相信，无论所谓的公司，或者说所谓的世界许诺给你什么，你都不曾改变。

“小丫头终于成功了，自由了。”

“也有可能.....我觉得自己说什么都没有办法活下来。”
“谁知道呢。那姑娘对自己够狠心......说什么都要走到底，而我缺的恰恰就是这一点点坚持。”
那时候......我说；“至少，你能坦诚的面对。这本身也可以说是一种自由。”
你真的变了。

但.....有时候我也会觉得......你这个人确实很极端。
有时候我会觉得，我们两个人应该永远都无法成为好搭档.....至少，那时候，我这样想过。
但，现在，我觉得，我以你为荣......强尼。我们，永不消逝。

After 50+ hours, I genuinely think Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best open-world RPGs I've ever played, and honestly, it might be my favorite story-driven game period.

What surprised me the most wasn't the graphics, even though they're absolutely insane. Night City is one of the few game worlds that actually feels alive. During the day, the city is packed with people going about their lives, and at night the neon lights make everything look straight out of a sci-fi movie. Sometimes I'd find myself driving around with no objective just because I wanted to take in the atmosphere. There are very few games where simply existing in the world is enjoyable, but Cyberpunk nails it.

The story is what really sold me, though. I expected a good story, but I didn't expect to become so invested in the characters. The game somehow makes you care about the people you meet, their struggles, and the choices you make throughout the journey. There were multiple moments where I sat staring at my screen after a mission ended just thinking about what happened. The writing feels mature, emotional, and surprisingly human for a game set in a futuristic dystopia.

What I love most is that Cyberpunk isn't afraid to teach difficult lessons. Throughout the game, you're constantly reminded that life isn't fair, that power isn't always enough, and that sometimes there simply isn't a perfect ending waiting for you. Night City doesn't bend to your will just because you're the protagonist. In fact, one of the biggest themes of the game is realizing how small you can be compared to the forces controlling the world around you.

The Peralez storyline is probably the best example of this. By that point, V can become an absolute monster capable of taking down entire gangs, elite soldiers, and some of the most dangerous people in Night City. Yet when you uncover what's happening to Jefferson and Elizabeth Peralez, you're suddenly faced with something far beyond guns, cyberware, or brute force. You start pulling on a thread that leads to a conspiracy so massive and unsettling that you realize you're completely out of your depth. Then there's Mr. Blue Eyes, a character who appears briefly yet somehow manages to leave one of the biggest impressions in the entire game. The mystery surrounding him and what he represents creates this feeling that there are powers operating in the shadows that even legends like V can't truly understand. It was one of the few moments in gaming where I genuinely felt powerless, and that's exactly why it was so memorable.

The game constantly delivers moments like that. It explores identity, mortality, ambition, friendship, sacrifice, and what it really means to leave a mark on the world. It asks questions that don't always have easy answers, and that's what makes the story stick with you long after you've finished playing.

The side quests deserve a special mention because they don't feel like filler. In a lot of open-world games, side content feels like a checklist. In Cyberpunk, some side quests are so well-written that they feel like main story missions. Many of them introduce memorable characters and stories that stuck with me long after I completed them. Some of the most emotional moments I experienced weren't even part of the main story.

The lore is also incredible. The deeper you dig into Night City, the more fascinating it becomes. The corporations, gangs, politics, technology, and history all blend together to create a world that feels believable despite how futuristic it is. You can spend hours learning about the world without ever touching the main story, and you'll still find yourself discovering new details.

The freedom you have is another huge plus. Whether you're talking your way through situations, hacking everything in sight, sneaking around enemies, or charging in guns blazing, the game lets you create your own version of V. The cyberware system is one of my favorite progression systems in any RPG because every upgrade genuinely changes how you approach the game.

Now, the game isn't perfect. I've had more crashes than I would've liked, and I've run into bugs that occasionally break immersion. Sometimes NPCs behave strangely, and there are moments where the game still shows some technical roughness. But honestly, those issues never outweighed everything the game does right.

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those rare games that completely pulls you in. The combination of incredible visuals, unforgettable characters, emotional storytelling, deep lore, meaningful choices, amazing music, and thought-provoking themes made it incredibly hard to put down. There were times when I wasn't just playing the game—I felt like I was living in Night City.

For all its flaws, Cyberpunk 2077 gave me something very few games ever have: a world I couldn't stop thinking about even when I wasn't playing. The fact that a game can entertain you is impressive. The fact that it can make you reflect on life, power, identity, and the things beyond your control is something special.

Cyberpunk 2077 simply pulls you in like very few other games could. Night city feels incredibly immersive, in large thanks to Mike Pondsmith's RPG series upon which it is based, but also thanks to the masterful game design and plot. CDprojekt took a page from the great Half-Life series as there are no cutscenes in a classical sense throughout the game. You almost never see the world outside V's eyes, and that just lets you inhabit their body on a level I can confidently say is unbeatable. You don't [i] play as [/i] V, you [i] are [/i] V. Even though a great majority of dialogue options don't have particularly far reaching consequences, they offer just enough variety to truly express yourself and give V your own spin.

But immersion means nothing if the story you immerse yourself into is as bland as real life, which this is categorically not. The plot hooks are numerous and engaging with an ensemble of characters so fleshed out you begin to question game from reality. Johnny especially is such a charismatic and strong persona many would get up and follow him to Arasaka tower if it existed today. He is probably Keanu Reeve's best performance. Romance character quests are also captivating: some better, some worse, some gutwrenching and some heartwarming, but that's just how life is. Don't expect too much from your date after their personal plotline is finished, though. You get a couple fun text interactions and that's about it.

But what about gameplay? The gunplay? Pristine. The options? Numerous. Do you want to sneak around like a ninja: deadly and silent? Sure, spec into reflexes, swap some chrome and be invisible. Do you want to go in guns blazing, faster than bullets and indestructible? Of course, grab a sandy and armor up like hell. Is standing back as your enemies drop like flies from the viruses you inject into their minds more your speed? Become a netrunner. There is so so many strategies, builds, fun little quirks one can explore that no two experiences can ever be the same. It's all so incredibly satisfying but at the same time full of expression that you just have to experience it to understand.

This is where we come to the few gripes I have about the game. Number one is the bugs. If [i]this[/i] is the fixed version of the game then day one must have been pandemonium. Cars dropping from the sky, sliding through the floor, npc's getting stuck, objectives not finishing, graphical glitches and at one time a flat out crash are just some of the wonders I personally experienced. Also car handling on PC is ... bad. I imagine some of it might be better on a game pad, but most of the cars in the game are flat out impossible to control with a keyboard. They seem to drift out more at lower speeds somehow, to the point making a 90 degree turn without crashing borders on impossible (maybe a bit exaggerated but does not feel great). Bikes are slightly better but still not perfect. These mistakes are however, in the grand scheme of things, pretty insignificant.

Overall a must play.

I believe i originally preordered this game way back in 2018, before it was delayed multiple times. By the time it came out, i wasn't even too broken up over the rough state the game was in. After years of waiting, the money i had spent on it hardly felt like it had ever existed. I played the game for 10 hours and then dropped it.

Fast Forward to 2026 and i get the urge to come give it another shot. I remembered enjoying the bit of the story I did get to experience, and i knew that the gameplay and bugginess of the game had been improved to various extents.

Having now binged nearly all of the content in the base game over the course of two weeks, i can confidently say that i am satisfied with my purchase of this game eight years ago. 
While occasionally rough around the edges, i did thoroughly enjoy the combat and character progression of the game. Running mostly a blade build let me enjoy an up close, frenetic combat style that i imagine to be wholly different but equally as enjoyable as to what might be experienced from focusing more on quickhacks or on smart weapons.
I found myself doing nearly all of the side jobs the game had to offer (save for the gigs, but i occasionally still did those if i stumbled into them), and was well satisfied with more of them than i would have expected. This is really all thanks to the character writing in this game. 

By far, the standout feature of Cyberpunk is its writing. Dialogue between characters feels natural and animations in important moments are incredibly well done. I found myself really invested in the relationships between many of the main cast, and especially the relationships that V has with Johnny, Panam and Judy. 
I won't speak on the endings too much, but i think they are all very well written. Something tells me that people were not happy with some of them when the game came out, but maybe i'm just being harsh on the average gamer in 2020.

I will say, the performance in the open world can sometimes be lacking, although i will admit that i run the game on ultra settings with a 2k monitor and average above 60 fps. I will especially mention that I never had any performance hiccups during important story scenes, I never once found myself taken out of a moment because of lag. The game also has occasional small bugs, like a cop walking around inside the sidewalk or a civilian loudly and repeatedly running their car into a wall 20 feet away from a conversation you're having. Nothing serious.

Honestly, my biggest complaint with the game is the content surrounding the romantic relationships in the game, or the lack of it. [spoiler] I can only speak on the relationship with Judy, but i imagine the others are quite the same. There's a whole big mission (and honestly a decent amount of setup in the background throughout the game) of this potential relationship blossoming, and once it finally does, the only thing that comes of it is occasional text conversations that eventually dry up, and a repeatable date mission in which you have access to a few small events and a set of dialogue that never changes and is largely the same as what you would get when you called Judy before you were even in a relationship. [/spoiler]
I think it speaks greatly to this game's strengths that this is my biggest issue with it.

I know this game has largely positive reviews today, but i imagine there are still a lot of people who view the game in the light it was (often justly) received in at launch (although there were certainly unrealistic expectations surrounding the game at the time as well). I hope any of those people who may have dropped the game like i did come give it another shot some time, it's really worth it.

I think I'd give this game a 9/10. I'm very happy I came back to it. Really looking forward to the DLC next time it goes on sale :)

Особенно это касается дворов и узких улочек, через которые, на мой взгляд, можно было бы глубже рассказать о жизни простых людей.

При этом, к сюжетным персонажам у меня претензий нет: они выглядят стильно, звучат характерно и ведут себя круто.

Я видел далеко не весь побочный контент, но вот что запомнилось особенно: ужасная постановка боёв. Получаю задание - убить киберпсихопата. Думаю:"Вау, звучит интересно! В общем, это самый разочаровывающий опыт в моей жизни. Я всегда стараюсь найти в игре хоть какой-то прикол, который протащит меня до конца, но эту игру ничто не спасёт.

Title: One of the best stories and characters I've experienced in gaming
Review:
Bought this on Steam and put in ~30 hours for my first playthrough. No regrets whatsoever.
The game had a rough launch years ago, but right now in 2026 it's absolutely worth it. The world of Night City is insane — detailed, alive, and full of personality. But what really carried it for me was the story and characters.
I went full romance with Panam Palmer and honestly... I caught real feelings by the end 😂 Her storyline is fantastic, and The Star ending gave me one of the most emotional and hopeful conclusions I've had in any game. Leaving Night City with the Aldecaldos and her just hit different.
Combat feels great once you get into it, the music and atmosphere are top tier, and the choices actually matter. Yes, there are still some bugs here and there, but nothing that ruined my experience.
If you like deep single-player RPGs with strong characters, meaningful choices, and a story that sticks with you after you finish — this is it. Especially if you take your time with side quests and romances.
Would I recommend? 100%. Already missing Panam and Night City.

历经多次版本迭代打磨，《赛博朋克 2077》已然蜕变为一款名副其实的开放世界神作，夜之城用极致的赛博朋克美学，构筑出一座鲜活立体的未来都市。霓虹闪烁的高楼、阴雨连绵的街巷、贫富割裂的城区分区，沃森区的市井喧嚣、海伍德的底层挣扎、威斯布鲁克的奢靡浮华，每片区域风土人情、环境细节各有特色，光影与雨天特效将近未来的颓废繁华拉满，漫步街头便能沉浸式感受世界观魅力。
游戏剧情是最大亮点，主角 V 与强尼银手的灵魂共生故事跌宕饱满，基努・里维斯饰演的强尼塑造得有血有肉，主线层层递进，在生死与抉择中探讨人性与欲望。海量支线任务质量比肩主线，形形色色的 NPC 拥有完整人生轨迹，每个委托背后都藏着夜之城小人物的悲欢，不同选择导向迥异结局，多周目游玩仍有新鲜感。
深度的角色养成系统自由度拉满，肉体、反应、技术、智力、镇定五大属性搭配海量义体、枪械、技能，玩家能打造近战莽夫、黑客潜入、枪械射手等多种流派。改装义体改造身体，从光学义眼到螳螂臂，肉身与机械融合的设定完美契合赛博朋克内核。
DLC 往日之影更是锦上添花，谍战风格的全新地图与剧情，紧凑悬疑的故事搭配影帝级配音，斩获 TGA 最佳 DLC 实至名归。如今 BUG 大幅优化，内容充实完整，无论是欣赏世界观、沉浸剧情，还是自由探索枪战，都能获得绝佳体验。凭借独特的艺术风格与深刻的故事，《赛博朋克 2077》坐稳赛博题材游戏天花板。

Story: The main plotline of the game is simple and relatively short in its own right, but really begins to hold deeper meaning for the individual player as the world is explored beyond the main storyline. The DLC is great, the characters are great, and the small details of the world are excellent, leaving very few stones unturned when it comes to making the city feel like reality. Night City as a whole presents as a not-so-far off vision of the world in fifty to a hundred years if corporations triumph over government regulation entirely and become rulers in their own right. The average person in Night City lives uninsulated from violence, environmental ruin, and poverty, problems which have been exacerbated by the dominance of the billionaire class in America today.

From my recollection, the game ran essentially flawlessly until about the 50 hour mark, where either some game data or cache issues began to show themselves, or I simply began to interact with elements of the game that somehow hadn't been as thoroughly debugged (although that doesn't make much sense). On this system in 4K, I was able to get an average of about 70fps throughout gameplay with pathtracing on as well as DLSS and FG and all graphics settings more or less maxed out. The one persistently problematic bug I encountered was a progressive drop in performance that would occur after booting the game, with FPS falling to the low single digits and getting stuck there, possibly causing a crash altogether or just requiring a restart of the game. Sometimes this glitch reoccurred almost immediately and was typically worsened by opening the menu, making me wonder if it is caused by some sort of memory leak or something else that could progress as the game runs. I never found a fix for this problem, but rebooting my PC altogether may have helped reduce the occurrence or time to failure somewhat.

Few games in history have undergone a redemption arc quite like Cyberpunk 2077. While its initial launch was famously rocky, CD Projekt RED’s unwavering commitment to their vision—culminating in the massive 2.0 update and the brilliant Phantom Liberty expansion—has officially transformed this game into a certified masterpiece.

Night City is the undisputed star of the show. It is a towering, neon-soaked vertical labyrinth that feels genuinely alive, dangerous, and intoxicating. Walking through the crowded streets of Watson or driving through the desolate Badlands offers an unparalleled level of environmental immersion. The world-building is incredibly dense, capturing the corporate-dominated, gritty essence of classic cyberpunk lore.

It is impossible to talk about the renaissance of this game without mentioning Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, the phenomenal Studio Trigger anime series. Edgerunners didn't just capture the hearts of fans; it perfectly mirrored the game's high-stakes, tragic, and adrenaline-fueled atmosphere.

The anime injected a massive wave of fresh energy into the game, making the exploration of Night City feel even more personal. Visiting locations featured in the show, listening to "I Really Want to Stay at Your House" on the in-game radio, or equipping David Martinez’s iconic jacket adds a profound layer of emotional depth for anyone who loved the series.

With the overhauled cyberware systems, revamped skill trees, and chaotic vehicle combat introduced in recent updates, the gameplay finally matches the narrative's ambition. Combat is fast, brutal, and highly customizable. Whether you want to be a stealthy Netrunner hacking enemies from afar or a sandevistan-powered solo slicing through corporate guards with a katana, the playstyles are incredibly rewarding.

At its core, the story of V and Johnny Silverhand is a deeply moving tale about legacy, identity, and survival against all odds.

Cyberpunk 2077 is no longer just a game about promises; it is a triumphant delivery of an unforgettable sci-fi RPG. If you were waiting for the right time to lose yourself in Night City—especially if you are a fan of Cyberpunk: Edgerunners—there has never been a better time to chrome up and dive in.

[h2]  赛博朋克2077：在数字荒原中寻找人性的最后一丝微光 [/h2]

[strike] 一份迟到的测评 [/strike]

为什么现在还要聊2077？

距离《赛博朋克2077》首发已经过去数年，经历了灾难性的首发、无数次补丁、以及DLC《往日之影》的救赎，这款游戏终于呈现出它本该有的模样。但我不想再复述那些“修复了bug”“画面变好了”的老生常谈 —— 我想聊的是在这个AI写剧本、算法推荐内容的时代，“《赛博朋克2077》如何用'不完美‘打动了完美主义时代的我们”。


[h3] 夜之城：一座会呼吸的赛博地狱 [/h3]

很多开放世界游戏的城市只是“任务触发器+风景壁纸”，但夜之城不同。它的每个角落都在[b] ”叙事“ [/b]：

[b] ”垃圾堆里的芯片“ [/b]：记录着一个底层技工被公司裁员后，用最后一笔钱买了把廉价手枪，在浴室里结束生命的过程。没有任务指向这里，没有奖励，只有一段沉默的文本。
[b] ”霓虹灯下的涂鸦“ [/b]：有些写着“强尼·银手是错的”，有些写着“强尼·银手是对的” —— 这种矛盾本身就是夜之城的政治倾向。
[b] ”街头NPC的对话“ [/b]：你听到的不是随机生成的噪音，而是精心编写的“夜之城市民生存实录” —— 瘾君子在向自动售货机乞讨，两个警察在讨论怎么收黑钱更体面。

真正让我震撼的，是游戏对“赛博空间”的视觉化呈现。当你接入网络，数据流化作绚烂的光河，防火墙变成扭曲的几何怪物 —— 这不是炫技，而是一种隐喻：[i] 在这个世界，连“信息”都有了物理形态，可以被切割、被买卖、被杀戮。 [/i]


[h3] V的悲剧：我们每个人都是“备份” [/h3]

游戏最核心的设定 —— Relic芯片里的强尼·银手 —— 被很多玩家简单理解为“一个话痨老头在脑子里BB”。但往深了想，这其实是对“身份认同”最残酷的拷问：

当你的记忆可以被编辑，你的意识可以被复制，你的身体可以被改造 —— [b] “我”到底是谁？ [/b]
V是夜之城最底层的雇佣兵，强尼是已故的摇滚传奇，这两个灵魂共享一个躯体，彼此憎恨又彼此依赖。这种“共生关系”不是游戏机制，而是“对现代人精神分裂的隐喻” —— [i] 我们每个人体内都住着“想成为的自己”和“被迫成为的自己”。 [/i]

最让我头皮发麻的一个细节：在某个支线任务中，你遇到一个能把意识上传到云端的人。他说：“我死了很多次，但每次都能从备份恢复... 只是我不确定，恢复的那个还是不是我。” 这句话让我茅塞顿开。


[h3] 玩法：不是为了爽，而是为了“不自在” [/h3]

《赛博朋克2077》的战斗系统一直被诟病“不够爽”——这恰恰是它的高明之处：
但真正改变我游戏体验的，是“不杀”的玩法。游戏给了你足够多的非致命武器和潜行路线，甚至有些任务会因为你“零击杀”而解锁特殊对话。这不算圣母心，而是对赛博朋克核心精神的回归：[i] 在这个人命如草芥的世界，选择不杀人，本身就是一种反抗。 [/i]


[h3] 叙事：让玩家成为“不完美的自己” [/h3]

《赛博朋克2077》的叙事有一个被严重低估的优点：它允许你做一个“糟糕的人”。

你可以接任务然后放鸽子，NPC会打电话骂你；
你可以为了钱出卖朋友，然后看着他在酒吧里醉醺醺地诅咒你；
你可以在最终决战前，突然决定去赌场把所有钱输光 —— 游戏不会阻止你，只是会记录下这一切。

这种“不完美的自由”才是真正的角色扮演。不像某些游戏，给你一个“善良/邪恶”的二元选择，然后给你两套完全不同的剧情 —— 2077的善恶是模糊的，你的每个选择都会带来意想不到的后果，而这些后果往往不是“好”或“坏”能概括的。


[h3] 与《往日之影》：一次迟到的“补完” [/h3]

DLC《往日之影》不仅是新地图和新任务，[b] 它补全了本体缺失的灵魂 [/b]：

本体讲的是“如何在赛博世界活下去”，DLC讲的是“如何有尊严地死去”；
本体让你成为传奇，DLC让你明白传奇的代价；
本体给你选择，DLC告诉你 —— 有些选择，根本没有正确答案。

[spoiler] 尤其是新角色“所罗门·李德”，他不是一个传统意义上的“盟友”或“敌人”，而是一个[b] 被体制异化的理想主义者 [/b]。看着他为了所谓的“大局”一步步堕入深渊，你会问自己：如果我在他的位置，会做得更好吗？ [/spoiler]


[h3] 给这个“完美时代”的一记耳光 [/h3]

在2026年，我们习惯了AI生成的完美剧情、算法推荐的精准内容、社交媒体上的精致人设。而《赛博朋克2077》像一记耳光，告诉我们：
不完美才是真实的 —— 卡顿、诡异的物理引擎，反而让夜之城有了“活着的质感”；
选择没有正确答案 —— 游戏里每个任务都让你在“烂”和“更烂”之间做选择，就像现实生活；
反抗注定失败——就像强尼·银手炸掉荒坂塔，什么都没改变，但“反抗”这个行为本身，就是意义。

[h3] 最后，用游戏里一个无关紧要的细节来结束这篇测评： [/h3]

在夜之城某个偏僻的角落，有一个无人问津的自动售货机。如果你买一瓶可乐，它会用机械音说：“谢谢惠顾，祝你有美好的一天。” 但如果你连续买十瓶，它会说：“检测到重复购买行为。请确认您不是AI。请确认您还活着。”

这大概就是《赛博朋克2077》想告诉我们的：在这个万物皆可数据化的时代，唯一能证明你“还活着”的，就是那些不完美、不理性、不可预测的 —— [i] 人性。 [/i]

There are so many things I like about this game, but the biggest is that it makes me feel better about myself as a software developer. Stacked objects will randomly fling themselves around, especially tires. Traffic randomly stops or collide, and vehicles tear off for no reason. Bodies get stretched or thrown off into the far distance. It's fun to jump into a beautiful cityscape and wreak havoc, constantly being reminded that it's just a game.
For the actual game, I'd give it a B+ these five years after its launch. It's far, far too cutscene driven. The main storyline is just small side quests between long cutscenes. I constantly press 'skip forward' to advance dialog. I've completed all side jobs and quests, gotten all of the rewards from the fixers, and completed 3 of 4 game endings, but what I really remember are the early story arcs and the feeling that I didn't really know which subplot to follow (Johnny? Takemura? Panam? Evelyn? Judy? Rogue? River?).
In that way it was like Elden Ring to me. Confusing, fun, bewildering, and eventually something I'm glad I mastered. Night City is a fun place to visit, but I wouldn't want to live there.

[h1]本来这游戏我买了后玩了几个小时就放到库里吃灰了。主要是玩不懂，太复杂。又是义体选配又是加容量又是给RAM升级又是刷词条等等乱七八糟的…我还专门去b站搜视频看人家大佬讲这些个东西都是怎么选配，哪些流派选哪些义体啊等等……头开始我都是瞎弄瞎点着玩儿的，当时还不知道我现在玩的是黑客流…

后来想着买了不玩怪可惜的，就试着再玩一次，这回认认真真的。结果就越玩越投入，越玩越下劲儿。现在玩了快800个小时了。

这是我玩过时间最长的一款单机游戏，内容最丰富，景色最优美，物品最繁多的游戏了。而且彩蛋也不少，之前玩过的所有单机游戏加一起的时间都没有这一款游戏的时间长。搞懂机制后玩起来就觉得太好玩了，太有意思了，根本就停不下来。

玩主线和支线任务，还有委托任务跟ncpd任务时，不要那么囫囵吞枣的玩，要慢慢进行，很多有意思的小细节都值得去品。没事时可以去恶土还有小镇等....地方去捡东西（搜刮物质，水里、海底也有哦），没准儿还真能捡到宝贝哈哈！


PS：CDPR为什么不做第三人称视角？就是想让你身临其境。对话我一句不带跳过的，有时候甚至还回档想看看不同的角色选不同的对话，角色会有什么样的反应，这非常有趣！有时npc的对话都可能是一个支线任务的小伏笔，就连女v和强尼的拌嘴都像是老夫老妻一样经常把我逗笑。这游戏实在是太耐玩了，没有任何一款单人游戏能让我玩这么长时间的，顶天也就100个小时。而这款游戏我玩了3个周目（新游戏+mod）到现在还意犹未尽，很期待《赛博朋克2》。希望2代能把1代的坑填了，还有1代删掉的内容给补全吧。这个游戏真的很棒。单人游戏每天还好几万人在玩，真的不光是mod的功劳，游戏的品质摆在这儿呢！

*强烈建议入手DLC（往日之影），那样才算完整的赛博朋克世界。DLC比本体更好玩！

i'm conflicted on whether i just barely recommend this game or just barely advise against it. i might change my overall rating, but for now, i can't recommend it, particularly when i've had so many people tout it as the greatest game ever made.

i'll start with the things i enjoy; 

a great story with meaningful decision making.

excellent voice acting and casting. 

a wide variety of playstyles.

beautiful graphics. 

proper atmos support that scales with a home theater very well, plus a generally decent audio mix (for a video game).

and now the things i don't like; 

poor balance with difficulty scaling where enemies just get insane amounts of health while you start dying in a couple hits and don't get enough resources like ammo or upgrade materials to keep up. elden ring is a prime example of how all games should balance difficulty. make it as hard as you want, but do not use difficulty sliders. know your audience and balance accordingly. breath of the wild and tears of the kingdom are great examples of the opposite end of the difficulty spectrum, making the game very approachable to beginners and children while still being challenging. difficulty sliders are simultaneously one of the laziest forms of game design and a nightmare to program. no one wants them; just properly balance your game. this has been long proven with time, going back to some of the earliest games like mario bros, which single-digit children could beat, or a grown adult could rage at. that is perfect game balance. a difficulty slider requires devs to finely tune like 5 versions of their game instead of 1, and almost no one puts in the time to do this because it sucks and costs a ton of money. i will never comprehend how so many video games still get this wrong today.

the combat is fairly uninteresting as well. while i enjoy the talent trees, item varieties, upgrade materials and general out-of-combat RPG elements, the combat itself is pretty shallow. not that bad, just boring and not much room for skill growth. 

poor optimization as you get into higher framerates 100fps+. changing even the heaviest settings barely changes your framerate. the difference between medium-high 4k and ultra 4k + ray tracing is like 30fps average. though if you are just aiming for 60fps this game is optimized surprisingly well given the scale of the world and how good most things look.

third party CDPR launcher every time you start the game, paired with nags to log into your CDPR account for a single-player game. blegh. 

way too much unskippable crap every time you launch the game. like two minutes between game launching and gameplay, and only about 5 of those seconds are spent actually loading into the world.

the UI and general UX when using a controller is bad. so many elements just force you to use the joystick cursor, such as the horrid menus that won't properly scroll through your items, settings etc with the d-pad. the joystick mouse SUCKS. just build proper controller support. this isn't a competitive shooter where MKB matters enough to warrant neglecting controllers this much. 

the quest tracking is frustrating and inconsistent. sometimes i'll be on a main quest, then someone will call me and start another main quest, and that will override my current quest tracking. if you're not paying attention to the quest marker moving, it can have you trek like 15 minutes across the map for a completely different quest. other times the exact same scenario will happen and it WON'T override my quest tracking even though i'm only doing main quests in both scenarios. i haven't been able to figure it out but the inconsistency drives me nuts. it shouldn't be touching my quest tracker at all until i complete my current quest chain or otherwise clear my currently tracked quest. 

while i love the decision making style of storytelling, the logic behind some of it borders on nonsensical. SPOILERS, but i played blind and i wanted to get a good johnny ending, and as i am about to invade Arasaka tower, he warns me that he doesn't want me helping Corpos, which makes sense. the other option is to kill yourself, of which he also disapproves, so naturally i went with invading Arasaka tower so i could kill Adam Smasher which i figured would matter more to him, and also because killing yourself is a pretty lame ending, but nah he just brutalizes you for selling out to the Corpos, never mentions a word about you killing Adam Smasher and basically says you're dead to him. i spent the entire story trying to veer things towards a good ending with Johnny but one vague decision killed that entire plotline and gave me the bad ending. i wouldn't have minded it much if it was obvious which one he preferred, but he literally objected to both and told me earlier in the game to promise that i'd kill Adam Smasher. it was such a lame way to end my favorite aspect of the story.

and speaking of the ending, i can't tell you how much i despise rollback endings. there is nothing more insulting than beating a game then just reverting to your save from two hours ago and wiping all your loot from the final zone. Zelda games do that as well and it never stops pissing me off, but at least they have the decency to only roll you back from the final boss instead of a giant quest involving tons of loot. just implement new game+ so you can have a persistent world, and if players make mistakes on a playthrough and miss items or endings they can just run it back with NG+. rollback endings are just a lazy way to avoid having to implement a changing world, which admittedly is a ton of work, but again let's look to Elden Ring for an example of how tremendously well this works if you spend the time to flesh it out.

honestly i could say more, good and bad, but i will conclude by saying that this game certainly has a lot to enjoy, i just don't care for much of this games design philosophy.

This review won't likely sway anyone from buying the game at this point, but I thought I'd put a few thoughts down after a good chunk of time spent playing.

I do recommend it. Taken as a whole, it's a good game with fantastic storytelling, memorable characters, excellent visuals, very naturalistic animations especially in scripted sequences, and superlative world design. 

But, gameplay-wise, there's nothing I'd rate particularly highly. It has competent combat, verging on clunky at times. I most enjoyed the hacking than the gunplay. That's not to say gunning loads of goons down isn't fun, it just felt a bit disconnected to me. There are better games out there for this aspect. 

The world you inhabit looks and feels amazing, but after a while you realise that it's all window dressing. NPCs spawn in and out, cars drive away in the distance and vanish. The police, despite overhauls in various patches, are beyond stupid. They can find you easily, converging on your position in seconds if you commit a crime (show by a star rating; five is super bad) with endless waves of them crashing their vehicles through everything in an effort to stop you. This includes running down other people by the way. Anyway, if you hide and your wanted level fades out, the police immediately give up on finding you, meaning once you're no long wanted you can walk out in front of the very same police that were chasing you with impunity. Ridiculous! 

Still, as I say, it's a good game worth playing. It could have been better, but I suspect scope creep took over and depth had to take a back seat.

推荐。玩下来最大的感受是：这游戏现在值得补票，尤其是加上《往日之影》之后。

优点很明显，夜之城的氛围、音乐、美术和代入感依然是一线水平。主线和支线都不是那种纯跑腿任务，很多角色写得很有记忆点，玩到后面真的会在意他们的选择和结局。战斗系统也比想象中爽，黑客、枪械、刀剑、潜行都能玩出不同流派。

重点夸一下《往日之影》DLC。狗镇的压迫感、剧情节奏、人物塑造都很强，宋昭美和李德这条线比很多本体任务还抓人，结局也不是简单的好坏选择，而是那种选完之后会反复想的类型。个人觉得这个DLC把《赛博朋克2077》的叙事上限拉高了一档。

缺点也有。开放世界看着很大，但很多地方互动还是偏少；路人和城市生态没有想象中那么“活”。部分任务后期也会有重复感，而且载具手感、近战打击感、偶尔的小bug还是能感受到一些粗糙。

总的来说，它不是完美游戏，但绝对是很有后劲的游戏。喜欢赛博朋克题材、沉浸式剧情和角色塑造的话，值得玩，DLC强烈建议一起入。

当未来到来时，我们或许已经失去了自己
如果让我用一句话评价《赛博朋克2077》，那就是：它不是一部关于未来科技的作品，而是一部关于人类如何被未来社会吞噬的悲剧。
很多人第一次进入夜之城时，都会被那铺天盖地的霓虹灯、巨型广告牌、飞驰而过的车辆和无处不在的高科技所震撼。这里仿佛是人类文明发展的终点，一切都高度发达，一切都充满可能。
但当你真正融入这个世界之后才会发现，夜之城根本不是乌托邦，而是一座披着未来外衣的地狱。
资本彻底凌驾于国家之上，巨型企业掌握着资源、权力甚至人的生死。贫民窟与摩天大楼仅仅隔着几条街道，却像两个完全不同的世界。科技飞速发展，却没有让普通人的生活变得更幸福；义体改造越来越先进，却无法填补人们精神上的空虚。
在夜之城里，每个人都在追逐成功。
杰克想成为传奇。
强尼银手想反抗企业。
大卫·马丁内斯想证明自己。
V想活下去。
但最终，他们都没能真正赢得这场游戏。
这正是赛博朋克题材最核心的悲剧——个人在庞大系统面前的渺小与无力。
你以为自己拥有选择，但你的选择其实早已被环境所塑造；你以为自己在反抗命运，可命运不过是在换一种方式吞噬你。
而这也是《赛博朋克2077》最让我震撼的地方。
因为它并不是在讲未来。
它讲的是现在。
当我们看着夜之城中无处不在的广告时，很难不想到现实世界越来越精准的算法推荐；当企业控制媒体、信息与资源时，也会让人联想到资本对社会的巨大影响；当人们沉迷于虚拟娱乐、追逐流量和名望时，又何尝不像现实中的我们。
赛博朋克从来不是预言。
它只是把现实的问题放大了一百倍。
所以夜之城真正恐怖的地方，不是帮派火并，不是义体疯子，更不是荒坂公司的阴谋。
而是你会发现，这个世界离我们并没有那么遥远。
《赛博朋克2077》的伟大之处就在于此。
它用最华丽的未来都市，讲述了最冰冷的现实故事；用最先进的科技背景，展现了最原始的人性挣扎；用一个关于反抗的故事，告诉玩家有些东西注定无法改变。
可即便如此，人们依然会选择反抗。
因为正如强尼银手所说的那样，人无法决定世界是什么样子，但可以决定自己如何面对它。
也许这才是《赛博朋克2077》真正的内核：
在一个注定腐烂的世界里，依然努力活得像个人。
而这份微弱却顽强的反抗，恰恰就是人性最后的光芒。

This was an unforgettable experience.

Truth be told, my first playthrough of this game back during the pandemic felt like a slog. I got maybe a quarter through the game and abandoned it. Second and third playthroughs were better but I could never finish it. I came back to it in April of this, a little after my birthday after rewatching Edgerunners. Until now, I'm not sure what happened, but I got hooked instantly. 

[b] The Good: [/b]

1. Immersion. The dialogue, characters (specifically during the opening sequence), world, the corporations are believable enough to exist in the real world which helps with them being so believably distinct. They have slang, history, tech, and gear that are just believable enough to have my brain go 'yeah, that makes sense' every time someone speaks or talks about techno-babble.
2. Strong Opening. Every lifepath is strong, and the subsequent 'tutorial' phase with Jackie really helps with keeping you engaged. There are several options in these quests for roleplay and getting to know what kind of V you're going for.
3. V. V is well-written, consistent, and amazingly voice-acted (regardless of which gender you select). I won't lie and say there aren't some dialogue options where I think they might be too emotional because there are, but these are so far and few between in side missions that you just tend to forget about them after another hour of hearing them speak. They have believable goals and actions that help immerse you in the character.
4. Music. I genuinely just had to place this here. Cyberpunk would not be Cyberpunk without its music. Whether they be original songs you only hear on the radio or songs integral to the plot (specifically with Johnny), they all sound great and all fit the world.
5. Car Design. I love the sound and designs of ALL of the cars and bikes. Seriously. They're either intentionally goofy or just look cool as hell.
6. Phantom Liberty. I can't go into depth on this point, just know that if you're interested in buying this game then the DLC holds some of the best quests, side missions, unlockable gear, and characters in the whole game. It would be a shame not to play it.

[b] The Bad: [/b]
1. Bugs. Game still has bugs, some were more internal with the game wiping all autosaves and needing me to load in a manual save a few hours prior. Some were minor, like NPCs floating, repeating dialogue (which would correct itself eventually), repeating animations, etc. And some were game-breaking, some involving main quests found in the DLC which I can't explain better without spoiling a good chunk of a main story mission.
2. Driving. Some of the cars feel like you're driving with wheels made out of butter while some cars feel like you're driving a rock. Do yourself a favor and download a mod that enhances the driving experience.
3. Johnny's Friendship. No spoilers: there is a meter that tells you how close you are to a certain character and it matters very little. Spoilers: [spoiler] I absolutely DESPISE how you have to choose the "correct" dialogue options arbitrarily just to get a secret ending and how Johnny describes their relationship with V as "tumultuous" in some side quests (specifically with Kerry's) even when your friendship meter is the highest it could be. WHAT WAS THE POINT OF ADDING A METER IF YOU AREN'T EVEN GOING TO USE IT???? [/spoiler]

I first got this game back when it came out, put about 10 or so hours into it and couldn't finish it due to the bugs and my save corrupting. From what I played at the time, I thought the story was something interesting but was held back because of all the issues at the time. I uninstalled it and didn't look at it again for a long while.

I recently redownloaded this game, I've started to really love these types of games (big Deus Ex fan) and I figured it would be a good time to start again. After putting in about 40 hours, this is my review -

Gameplay - 8/10
Everything felt incredibly smooth, your stats and talents are able to be upgraded at a solid pace and goes with the game well so you're not making yourself overpowered within the first act. The upgrades you can make to your cyberware and quickhacks felt meaningful and you could definitely feel the power increase when you added in those upgrades or waited to long to upgrade. The only negative is the driving was very slippery and didn't feel very fluid. I'm on KBM so when making micro adjustments on the car or bike, it definitely moved more than I would expect it to and made those small micro-adjustments during chases or vehicle combat to avoid obstacles a bit of a pain. Bikes are definitely better than cars and you can feel it as soon as you get on a bike.

Combat - 9/10
Gunplay feels so fun and I really enjoy the fight against the AI. ADS and aiming was smooth, hip firing was relatively clean when you were in close range, and the upgrades to the scopes made ADSing much better as the game went on. The iron sights to the guns felt a little rough, but nothing that a little practice couldn't get you through. The modifications you could get to your guns were, just as I mentioned above, impactful enough to make you feel like you were actually progressing and getting stronger, as well as the option to just upgrade the one gun you were using rather than having to pick and choose between the hundreds of guns you end up getting throughout the game. Melee combat was really clean and the dashing felt very fun, doing a melee-based playthrough definitely seems like it could be a blast with all the unique upgrades and talents you can acquire

Story - 10/10
The games story is, by far, one of the best game stories in many of these cyberpunk RPG-style games. You meet some really incredible characters in the story and you can very easily get attached to them and their stories. Each of the side character storylines were well thought out and felt fun and unique, even Johnny's. The main story, while not very unique at it's core, gives a really fun take on cyberspace and pushing through to the other side of the net. Johnny's construct coming out at random points to either help or deceive you was a nice way to further change your decisions, wondering whether or not he's helping you or working towards his own motives. The endings you can get seem really fun and unique, I kept telling myself with the decisions I was making "Oh man I hope this happens with X/Y/Z, it would be a perfect ending" and by the end of the game, I got exactly the ending I was hoping for and it was definitely emotional.

Technical (graphics, quality of play, etc) - 8/10
I have a pretty decent higher mid-range PC and most of the time I had absolutely no problems with the game on mid-high settings. The environment is done up beautifully, the weather is very well done (rains way to damn much in Night City), the backgrounds and landscapes look beautiful, and they really nailed the dreary and gross feel of big city back-alleys. I did have some frame drops and lag randomly, and also when there was a LOT of entities on the screen or in the area (looking at you, parade mission!) but it smoothed out after a few minutes and never gave me much more of an issue. 

Overall - 9/10
Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is an absolutely fun and enticing game with a story that will really suck you in and have you coming back for more. I binged all 40 hours in the course of three weeks and honestly couldn't be happier with it. There's so much replayability and so many unique ways to be able to go through not only the main storyline, but the side character storylines and misc storylines that you could easily put 300-400+ hours in and have different outcomes each time. I would 100% recommend this game to others and I would say this is one of those games that you just have to play at least once in your life if you're someone who loves the story and character-building the most

[h1] Найт Сити — то, ради чего стоит умереть? [/h1]

[h2] Геймплей [/h2] 
Для меня как человека, в каком-то роде «искушённого» подобными играми с открытым миром, всё, как говорится, по стандарту. Нет ничего новаторского или как минимум прикольного, хотя можно подчеркнуть интересные взаимодействия с разного рода имплантами. Но опять же, да — с точки зрения лора это интересно, но по факту всё сводится к тем же самым показателям точности, защиты, выносливости и так далее. Не знаю, кому-то, возможно, это придётся по душе, но если снять ширму пресловутого «Киберпанка», мы всё уже это видели тысячу раз, тысячи фраз, только в другой оболочке.
Возможно, могу отдельно подчеркнуть механику метро: перемещение по городу благодаря этому типу транспорта действительно забавное, но больше 1–2 раз я им не пользовался, потому что намного проще сесть в авто и добраться до точки — это банально выйдет быстрее.

Если кратко: не хорошо и не плохо, просто нормально.

[h2] Визуал [/h2] 
Это то, ради чего стоит заходить в эту игру спустя сотни часов. Но тут очень важно получить правильный первый «экспириенс»: настоятельно рекомендую играть в эту игру на ультра-настройках графики с включенной трассировкой пути. Первые 20–30 часов я просто ездил по городу, выполняя квесты, которые попадались по дороге. Я не хотел пользоваться быстрым перемещением, потому что получал удовольствие от картинки каждую секунду, когда был в игре. Честно говоря, у меня такое было впервые, когда с точки зрения визуала игра не то что завлекала, а не отпускала до самого конца. Очевидно, что это её главный козырь.
Из минусов могу отметить визуальные баги, которые встречаются в игре даже спустя 5 лет. И да, честно говоря, я был моментами в шоке, что спустя столько времени они до сих пор встречаются. Не сказать чтобы это сильно портит опыт, потому что сам по себе визуал перекрывает всё с лихвой.

[h2] Сюжет [/h2]
Не могу сказать, что это шедевр, но написано очень сильно. Я говорю как про основную кампанию, так и про дополнение (причём, на удивление, оно, как зачастую бывает, не выглядит плохо, а держится на уровне, а иногда накал драматургии даже перевешивает основную сюжетную ветку). Лор, взаимоотношения между персонажами, сама драма и развитие писались людьми, которые знают своё дело. Повторюсь, речь не только про основную часть — побочные квесты действительно заставляют как минимум задуматься, как максимум переживать за то, что происходит на экране. Это мастерство, которого у СДПР не отнять (тем более наличие русской озвучки добавляет своего лоска событиям и персонажам).

[h2] Атмосфера [/h2] 
Тут нечего ни прибавить, ни отнять: это одна из самых атмосферных игр, которые мне посчастливилось проходить. Найт Сити днём, Найт Сити ночью, Найт Сити навсегда. Вселенная, которая живёт в своём ритме, а не крутится вокруг тебя.

[h2] Итог [/h2] 
Подводя итоги, могу сказать так: это одна из самых лучших игр в жанре (не разделяю основную игру и дополнение, потому что, как по мне, это цельная история, и изначально она так и задумывалась). Советую каждому пережить этот опыт (желательно на мощном железе, дабы вкусить все соки сего творения), но главным минусом до сих пор остаются баги и моментами оптимизация, которая иногда портит всю малину. Но с этим можно жить, поскольку в каждой игре уровня GOTY можно найти к чему придраться, поэтому это меньшее из тех зол, что в нынешней ситуации может удивить прожжённого геймера.
