Yet another mixed bag, but an interesting experience nonetheless. Some disclaimers first: I do not own the Phantom Liberty DLC, so keep in mind that my review will not touch on any of it. And I am aware that this game has been discussed to death already, so I'll make this as subjective as possible, and focus on my personal experience.

This game is the first to give me the Deus Ex feel since the original Deus Ex was released 26 years ago. Some people will eviscerate me for uttering this but Dishonored sure tried, and failed, being mostly carried by Viktor Antonov's brilliant art and design, may he rest in peace. But Cyberpunk 2077 really gave me that "you can tackle a task any way you see fit" that I relish so much (the closest being Dark Souls because building around STR, DEX, FTH and INT all feel really different from each other).
I LOVED the hacking, whether it was computers, machines, or people's brain implants. I loved that the stealth was almost always optional, only bringing you more money or a better reputation in some cases. I loved that you could disobey your missions, for example convincing someone to leave town instead of killing them, and it still counts as a win. I felt more freedom than in GTA even.
I even tried to Mirror's Edge it from roof to roof as often as I could just to see if it was viable... and it was very doable at least half of the time, it even helped in certain missions. That was great. 

This game follows a pattern that I've seen in so many open world games especially since 2017: the main quest is dogwater, sidequests are where all the fun's at. Interestingly, Cyberpunk 2077's three best quests had the exact same plot: some AI is starting to sound too human, and people do not like that (Delamain, Skippy, Brendan). Here's one piece of advice: do NOT give the talking gun to Reggie. Worst mistake of my life.

The music was great, but could it have been any different with Marcin Przybyłowicz at the helm of the audio department?

The graphics... OK, this is where things get complicated. They are all over the place.
On one hand you've got stylish art direction, and fantastic attention to detail (I remember zooming in on characters in Photo Mode and admiring how unique their belt buckles looked)... on the other hand, this game has the worst vLOD issues I've seen since Dark Souls 3 and you can constantly see models gaining and losing polygons right under your nose, which is very distracting and immersion-breaking; and on top of that the clipping is so bad that it sometimes made me feel I was playing a Nintendo 64 bargain bin game. Annoying. I guess that's a very aggressive way to optimise? I was getting around 90 FPS in 4k high settings with no DLSS and RTX off (and honestly this game has the best looking RT I have ever seen but it did tank the framerate to a cinematic mid-twenties, no thanks). There were also some weird cut corners, like all children looking like adult heads on shrunk bodies for example, or a flashback sequence taking place more than 50 years in the past where the city looks exactly the same and people dress the same as in 2077 (and use the same slang too). What the fuck?  

The game, as you know, has a Bethesdaesque amount of bugs. I saw almost constantly cars randomly falling from the sky, people half buried into the pavement, or enemy blood unexpectedly changing colour... many such cases. I've seen games with more bugs obviously... but not with a budget like that one.
The writing was also all over the place but I think that was by design. Nice characters suddenly acting like assholes and vice-versa solidifies the feeling of a morally gray society where you can't trust appearances and nothing is reliable. Although I felt like some aspects were oversimplified. Helping cops does not make your street cred go down? Come the fuck on! 

All over the place is what I'd call most of this game. The writing was globally good but there were strange incoherencies and inconsistencies, as if the writers didn't agree on a lot of things. Sometimes it felt like they were trying to make the characters appear more complex... sometimes it seemed very random and nonsensical.

There's a million errands to run so obviously they become repetitive, but also if you simply walk around and explore you'll never run out of XP, money and loot. This plethora is probably punishing for people who want to 100% the game and get all achievements, as always I'm glad I'm not one of them anymore. Also if you decide to help the cops here and there, half of the time they thank you and the other half they start shooting you and call reinforcements despite the fact you just did their job for them. That could be intentional though.

But in all honesty, what I liked the most about this game is the fashion. I spent a lot of time admiring people's style, and much more time even going to absolutely every clothing outlet, trying to curate the biggest and coolest possible wardrobe. I really locked in when it was time to create new outfits. It's what kept me excited about the game half of the time.

Oh and the combat? It's okay. The majority of weapons felt useless to me, 99% of the time I used shotguns, grenades and offensive hacking, sometimes revolvers. It was a bit chaotic, but it was fine. Using people's implants against them was definitely the best part.

I don't know if I should recommend this game or not because it's definitely an acquired taste. It's one of those games that have a lot of everything, and your brain needs to be wired for that. I personally love that but I can totally see how it can be a turn-off. There's lots of dialogue and lots of reading to do. There's also lots of gunfights, and it's during the same missions. Lots of shit to learn if you wanna really appreciate the game, but also lots of action. The pace constantly goes from slow to fast to slow to fast... it never stops being a rollercoaster. Think you can handle it? Then absolutely go for it, this game is not mind-blowing but still a pretty good time.

Once the City pulls you in, it does not let go.

I played this mainly to fill the void The Witcher 3 left in me. But now I have ended up with a second one.

Only CDPR can pull me into a world like this and make me care so much about everything and everyone in it. Even more than in The Witcher 3. I felt connected, partly due to the first-person perspective and the amount of character customization, from looks to playstyle and skills, to the decisions you make throughout the game that largely influence V and the people around them. So much so that when you face one of the many difficult decisions, are confronted with grief or loss, or end up in a romantic relationship, it feels real because you are not watching from a third-person perspective. You are really in there, getting the full experience.

All of this wouldn’t really work if it weren’t for the incredible graphics and design of Night City, which is still, seven years later, the benchmark for open-world graphics and lighting. The entire cyberpunk genre is captured in the city, the people who live there, and the dark and gritty stories they tell, while still feeling authentic and believable. If you liked the storytelling structure in The Witcher 3, you get exactly that and more in Cyberpunk. The main story pulls you through different parts of Night City and lets you meet a lot of great characters, while still giving you the freedom to branch off and explore on your own, make new connections, and experience all sorts of well-written questlines and characters. One of them being Johnny, who is constantly at your side, giving sometimes more or less helpful advice and pieces of wisdom. Over time, his relationship with V becomes one of the strongest parts of the game, constantly shifting between conflict, understanding, and genuine companionship.

Phantom Liberty adds a whole other area to the game that never feels off or disconnected from the rest, with equally great characters and stories and some of the largest and best quests in the game.

All in all, this is now, after some time of post-release development and bug fixing, the game it was always meant to be and a true successor to the success CDPR had with The Witcher. A game that not only shines bright with its looks, grand design, and intriguing gameplay, but first and foremost with great writing, characterization, and a world that feels alive and pulls you in just to toss you back out a changed person.

Игра, в которой я повзрослел.

Это максимально неполиткорректная игра, которая показывает тёмные и неудобные стороны реального мира. Город выглядит свободным, но при этом в нём чувствуется контроль. Здесь он не такой грубый, как в РФ с блокировками сайтов, цензурой книг, пропагандой, закрытием от мировых мнений. Он гораздо тоньше: через постоянные ТВ-передачи, новости и вторжение в сознание.

Уровень сложности в игре - это скорее удобство, чем челлендж. Его хочется поднимать постепенно, по мере прокачки билда. Начинал со среднего, а когда прокачался - поднял до максимального.  

Плюсы:
-Есть озвученная русская матерщина. Поначалу я её активно отвергал и даже поставил NoMat-мод. Но со временем произошло принятие. Игра стала одним из важных кусков пазла, который помог мне это осознать. Я начал разбираться и понял: христианская церковь табуировала эти слова, хотя сами по себе они не являются скверными. Скорее наоборот - их корни уходят в древний славянский мир.
-Есть ЛГБТ. Завёл роман с девушкой, играя за девушку. 
-Есть полное обнажение и секс.
-Впечатляющая графика с RTX отражениями.
-Интересная история.

Минусы:
-Это очередная игра про убийства. Я уже начал разбираться, почему они в играх настолько популярны. Дело в том, что для хорошего повествования почти всегда нужен сильный конфликт, а убийство - одна из самых ярких его форм. К тому же существует мнение, что в мире есть всего две вещи, которые сразу и без усилий приковывают наше внимание: насилие и секс. Оба эти инстинкта работают на одном уровне - они базовые, животные и крайне эффективные.
-Из наркотиков в игре алкоголь явно на первом месте. Но в игре есть и другие вещества, хотя их заметно меньше. Встречаются шутки на тему психоделиков. Единственное вещество, которое я смог получить в инвентарь и попробовать - это Black Lace («Чёрное кружево»), но в русском переводе его назвали «Чёрная дурь».  Заметно, как в русской локализации специально создаётся негативный оттенок, вместо подхода по снижению вреда. Получить его можно только через консоль. 
-Главная героиня не отражается на поверхностях. Разработчики не создали модель для этого.
-В процессе прохождения у меня завис один квест "Дорога в рай".
-Основная часть игры - это жёсткие сюжетные рельсы, где выбор влияет только на развитие диалога. По-настоящему значимые решения появляются лишь в некоторых дополнительных заданиях ближе к концу. В основном же сюжете выбор, который реально меняет историю, предлагается только в финале. После прохождения игры, она не отпускает в свободный мир, а каждый раз возвращает в точку принятия решения, создавая петлю. Из-за этого нет ощущения завершённости - вместо финала получается бесконечный цикл «отыгрывай разные концовки».

Прошёл игру первый раз на геймпаде с танковым билдом (Shotgun Build). Phantom Liberty специально не покупал, чтобы не перегружать первое впечатление. Осталось желание пройти игру ещё пару раз с другими билдами и наконец-то по-настоящему понять историю, которая с первого раза доходит лишь частично.

Необходимым модом выделю Untrack Quest Ultimate. Он позволяет убирать с навигатора маршрут до основной точки задания, чтобы спокойно ездить по городу в свободном режиме и самому ставить маркеры на нужные задания.

Cyberpunk 2077 ended up becoming one of my favorite RPGs once everything finally came together. The launch problems were rough, but underneath all that was an incredible world, great characters, and one of the most immersive cities I’ve experienced in gaming.

Night City is honestly the real main character. The city feels alive in a way very few open-world games manage to achieve. Every district has its own atmosphere, style, music, and chaos. One minute I’m walking through neon-lit streets surrounded by ads screaming at me from every direction, and the next I’m in some dark alley dealing with cyberpsychos, gangs, or people making terrible life decisions.

What really hooked me was the storytelling and characters. Almost every major character felt memorable, and a lot of the side quests honestly felt better written than main stories in other RPGs. The game constantly throws morally messy situations at you where there isn’t really a perfect outcome, which fits the whole cyberpunk setting perfectly.

The combat also became way more fun than I expected once I started unlocking better cyberware and abilities. You can play like a stealth hacker, a katana maniac, a walking tank, or a complete cyberpsycho sprinting through enemies at Mach 5 with mantis blades. By the late game I genuinely felt less like a human and more like a heavily armed software problem.

I also loved how immersive the world feels outside of combat. Driving through the city at night while the soundtrack blasts in the background just has a vibe that’s hard to explain unless you’ve played it. The atmosphere carries so much of the experience.

And then there’s Phantom Liberty, which honestly elevated the game even more for me. The expansion adds some of the best missions, characters, and spy-thriller moments in the entire game. Dogtown feels dangerous, corrupt, and completely different from the rest of Night City in the best possible way.

That said, the game still isn’t perfect. NPC behavior can still feel weird sometimes, driving physics can be questionable depending on the vehicle, and occasionally the game reminds you that the engine is holding together through pure determination and chrome-plated duct tape.

But for me, Cyberpunk 2077 became one of those games where I stopped fast traveling because I genuinely enjoyed existing in the world. Between the atmosphere, music, characters, combat, and storytelling, it’s one of the few RPGs that fully pulled me into its setting and kept me there for hundreds of hours.

Bought this game in 2026 after keeping it on my wishlist for years, and honestly, I wish I had experienced it sooner. I started with just the base version, expecting a good RPG, but what I got was something that stayed in my head long after I closed the game. The story, the atmosphere, the characters, the music — everything feels crafted with so much soul. For someone who dreams a lot and constantly thinks about life, choices, ambition, identity, and the future, this game hits differently. It doesn’t just entertain you; it gives you something to reflect on.

I’m around 40 hours in, and it still feels like I’ve barely scratched the surface of Night City. Every corner has a story, every character feels like they actually belong in this world, and even random moments somehow become memorable. I keep delaying meeting Hanako because part of me genuinely doesn’t want this journey to end yet.

Before playing, I had heard countless negative things about bugs and glitches, and that honestly kept me away from the game for a long time. But after finally playing it myself, I can confidently say that CD Projekt has put serious work into fixing and improving the experience. In my playthrough, almost everything has felt smooth and immersive.

What makes this game special to me is the freedom it gives you — not just in gameplay, but in expression. You can be reckless, emotional, calm, violent, thoughtful, selfish, human. It lets you bring your intrusive thoughts, your curiosity, and your personality into the world and just exist in it. Very few games make me feel genuinely connected to their universe, but this one did.

I’m already planning to buy the Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty expansion because I genuinely don’t want to leave this world behind anytime soon.

“Thank you, CD Projekt, for creating something that feels like more than just a game — a world that constantly makes you question what it truly means to be human. Are we more than memories and experiences stitched together over time, or are we just emotionless engrams pretending there’s a soul behind it all?”

Cyberpunk 2077

Ребят, это шедевр, про который я сейчас расскажу с минимальными спойлерами.

В начале я выбрал дитя улиц.

Мир киберпанка — это слишком красиво. То есть на твоём экране город из будущего — Найт-Сити, но также и остались места, которые выглядят как в наше время (2026).

Оценка мира: 9/10.

Баги. Багов я встретил не так много, но они были бесячие. Не могу нажать кнопку в лифте; НПС должен стоять на полу или возвышенности, но он почему‑то находится в воздухе, в обездвиженном состоянии.

Оценка количества багов: 2/10 + реп.

Боёвка. Да, я думаю, что боёвка тут самая обычная, но выглядит неплохо.

Оценка боёвки: 7/10.

Экшен. Игра построена на нём. Сколько дофамина и адреналина я ещё не получал в играх, наверное! Это рубилово просто ахирительно.

Оценка экшена: 10/10.

Оружие. Винтовки, автоматы, дробовики, пистолеты‑пулемёты — это всё обычно, но из‑за огромного количества вариаций оружия оно кажется очень крутым.

Оценка оружия: 7/10.

Ближний бой. Для ближнего боя в игре у тебя есть оружие и кулаки. Кулаками лично я пользовался очень мало, ничего толком не могу сказать про них. Оружие — катаны, мечи и др. Классно, но малоюзабельно: я их не трогал и пользовался двустволкой.

Оценка ближнего боя: 6/10.

Одежда. Просто классно! Я её менял всего два раза и не знаю, даёт ли она вообще какие‑то баффы, но Ви выглядит красиво.

Оценка одежды: 8/10.

Персонажи. Самая долгая часть обзора, наверное, но я постараюсь не сильно много написать.

Ви — главный герой: принципиальный, упрямый, боевая машина, мелкий вор, неплохой друг.

Джеки — мой пупсик! Как же я его любил, хоть он помогал мне только в начале игры. Мягких облачков, Джек!

Бестия — я даже не вдуплил толком, кто она такая, но она меня доставала.

Виктор‑док — чёткий мужик, не раз выручал.

Джонни, мать его, Сильверхенд — упрямый, настойчивый. Больше не скажу, чтобы не спойлерить.

Панам — прикольная деваха, так‑то. Помогла, я ей помог, и кенты у неё классные.

Джуди — специалист по брейндансам, очень сильно повлияла на сюжет, хороший друг.

Декстер Де Шон — вот она, мразота, из‑за которой я мучился всю игру. На его задании начинается сильное развитие сюжета.

Токэмура — типсон, который вытащил тебя со свалки и развил предконцовку сюжета. + реп.

Сабуро Арасака — я просто в ахере с гениальности этого старпера.

Ханако Арасака — «Помоги ей — поможет тебе». Концовка сюжета — она.

Ёринобу Арасака — в целом просто плохой человек и брат Ханако.

Наверное, про персонажей это всё.

Оценка персонажей: 10/10.

Сюжет. Мать его, шедевр! Не буду спойлерить, но тут всё просто на высочайшем уровне. Всё идеально.

Оценка сюжета: 10/10.

Геймплей. Просто шедеврально! Хоть он и такой простой, но так чувствуется.

Оценка геймплея: 10/10.

НПС. Да хз, что можно такого про них сказать, но норм.

Оценка НПС: 6,5/10.

Краткий итог: киберпанк — ахирительная игра, и теперь я понял, почему его все так любят.

Всем спасибо, кто прочитал!

До встречи!

Vorab: Ich habe das Spiel bereits kurz nach Veröffentlichung gespielt. Ich war damals vom Zustand des Spiels derart enttäuscht, dass ich es damals nach wenigen Stunden abgebrochen habe. Ich habe mir allerdings vorgenommen es ein weiteres Mal zu versuchen. 
Ich habe das Spiel heute abgeschlossen. Mein Fazit: Wow. Es war die richtige Entscheidung zu warten. Es handelt sich mittlerweile um ein hammer Spiel, welches ich nunmehr gerne als Vergleich zum Status Quo heranziehe. 
Denn besser geht es kaum: Die Grafik ist atemberaubend, die Story packend. Das Movement ist hervorragend, die Fahrzeugsteuerung auch gut. Das Waffensystem derart flexibel gestaltet, dass einfach für jeden etwas dabei sein muss. Selbst Mischungen von Kampfstilen sind ohne Probleme möglich. Zwar wurde das Wall-Running, welches sie in den ersten Trailern gezeigt hatten, nie eingeführt, es gibt aber ausreichend andere Mechanismen, dass man hier einen ziemlich ähnlichen Effekt erzielt. 
Zu guter letzt muss ich sagen, dass ich alle Side- und Mainquests abgeschlossen habe (NCPD-Scanner-Delikte ausgeschlossen). Vorher wollte ich das Spiel einfach nicht zu Ende bringen, und selbst dann wollte ich die abschließenden Missionen nicht machen. So gut ist dieses Spiel mittlerweile geworden. Für einen vollständigen Run habe ich 91 Stunden gebraucht - ein wirklich gutes Preis-Leistungsverhältnis.

当2077年的霓虹灯光穿透夜之城的阴雨，义体的金属冷光与人类的温热呼吸交织，CD Projekt RED用一场关于生存与救赎的叙事，将赛博朋克的内核刻进了每一段剧情肌理。这款承载无数期待的开放世界RPG，虽曾因优化争议步履蹒跚，却凭借极具张力的剧情叙述、鲜活立体的人物群像，以及对“科技与人性”的深刻叩问，成为赛博朋克文化的经典载体，历经数次更新迭代，终不负“杰出剧情游戏”的盛名。
剧情的起点，是玩家对主角V的塑造——流浪者、街头小子、公司员工，三种出身不仅决定了开局的叙事视角，更铺垫了V截然不同的性格底色与人际关系。流浪者的自由不羁、街头小子的市井圆滑、公司员工的精于算计，让每个玩家都能找到属于自己的代入感，而这种代入感，在第一人称视角的加持下被推向极致。CDPR放弃了传统第三人称的上帝视角，转而让玩家以V的双眼凝视夜之城，感受义眼扫描时的科技质感，聆听对话时的情绪波动，这种沉浸式设计，让每一次抉择都变得格外沉重。
故事的核心脉络，围绕一枚能实现永生的Relic原型芯片展开。V在一次盗窃行动中意外将芯片植入脑中，从此与数字幽灵强尼·银手绑定共生——这个曾为营救女友突袭荒坂大厦、在核爆中失踪的传奇摇滚巨星，带着对企业巨头的刻骨仇恨，与V共享一具躯体，也共享一段注定走向终点的命运。两人从最初的针锋相对、互相排斥，到后来的彼此理解、生死相依，这段羁绊成为剧情最动人的底色。强尼的桀骜不驯与内心柔软，V的野心勃勃与坚守底线，在一次次对话与抉择中逐渐丰满，他们既是彼此的枷锁，也是彼此的救赎。
夜之城从来不是单纯的背景板，而是剧情的重要参与者。这座被企业资本浇筑的超级都市，既有霓虹闪烁的繁华表象，也有底层挣扎的黑暗真相——荒坂、军用科技等巨头掌控一切，帮派割据、义体滥用、贫富悬殊成为常态，赛博精神病患者的疯狂嘶吼，诉说着科技对人性的异化。游戏通过无数支线剧情，将这座城市的肌理层层剥开：巫毒帮的黑客诡影、莫克斯帮的坚守反抗、清道夫的冷酷无情，每个势力都有自己的生存逻辑；而德拉曼的自我救赎、约书亚的信仰挣扎、朱迪与帕南的深情羁绊，更让夜之城的每一个角落都充满了人性的温度。
非线性叙事与多结局设计，让剧情拥有了无限可能。玩家的每一个选择，无论是对话中的立场倾向，还是任务中的行动方式，都将影响剧情的走向。是选择与荒坂妥协换取生机，还是与强尼并肩摧毁企业霸权；是坚守人性底线，还是沉迷义体改造沦为冰冷的机器，每一种选择都对应着不同的结局，没有绝对的对错，只有立场的差异。这种设计，不仅增强了剧情的可玩性，更让玩家在抉择中思考：当科技可以改造肉体、储存意识，当永生成为可能，人类的本质究竟是什么？
或许有人诟病其初期的优化问题，但这丝毫无法掩盖剧情叙述的光芒。CDPR用细腻的台词、精良的过场动画，将“赛博朋克”的核心命题诠释得淋漓尽致——科技是救赎也是诅咒，资本是权力也是枷锁，而人性的坚守，才是黑暗中唯一的光。V与强尼的最终告别，夜之城的霓虹依旧闪烁，那些关于野心、背叛、深情与牺牲的故事，却在玩家心中留下了难以磨灭的印记。
《赛博朋克2077》的剧情，从来不是一场简单的冒险，而是一次对人性与未来的深刻叩问。它用破碎却真挚的叙事，告诉我们：即使身处霓虹乱世，即使肉身早已被科技改造，只要守住内心的温度，便不算沦为赛博时代的傀儡。这不仅是一款游戏的剧情，更是一段关于爱与救赎、坚守与反抗的精神独白，历经时光沉淀，愈发彰显其不朽的价值。

For me, Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the greatest games ever released. The story is phenomenal and completely pulls you in from start to finish.

[b]The Pros:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Story & Cutscenes:[/b] The narrative is breathtaking. I usually tend to skip cutscenes in other games, but here I watched every single one. They are emotional, unique, and simply on another level.
[*][b]Acting & Dubbing:[/b] The acting is top-tier. If you understand Polish, you should definitely play it in that language—the voice actors did a legendary job.
[*][b]Characters:[/b] You build such a strong bond with the characters that it’s actually hard to say goodbye to them once the credits roll.
[*][b]Quests & Side Content:[/b] Every single quest is interesting and varied. There is no "filler" here; every side mission has a standout story of its own.
[*][b]Atmosphere & World:[/b] Night City is incredibly detailed. The map size is perfect—it’s not unnecessarily large but instead tightly designed so that every location feels relevant.
[*][b]Gameplay & Choices:[/b] The gameplay is super versatile. You can finish missions in many different ways and make choices that actually matter.
[*][b]Multiple Endings:[/b] The endings are brilliant. What’s great is that you don’t have to replay the entire game to see them all, as the game gives you a clear warning before you enter the final phase.
[*][b]DLC (Phantom Liberty):[/b] The DLC is absolute fire. It feels completely different from the main story and grips you immediately.
[*][b]Soundtrack:[/b] The music and the radio stations are just top-notch and fit the vibe perfectly.
[/list]

[b]The Cons:[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Post-DLC Blues:[/b] The game is so good that I’m just sad it’s over. I really hope they decide to release even more DLCs in the future.
[/list]

[b]Verdict:[/b]
A fascinating story with great gameplay and incredibly convincing characters. I will definitely play this game again. If you haven't played it yet, you are missing out on a piece of gaming history!

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of my favorite games of all time.

I've completed it three times: as a stealth assassin, a katana-focused build, and a netrunner. What impressed me the most is that each playthrough felt genuinely different. Not just because of the combat styles, but because of the choices, relationships, quest outcomes, and endings that completely changed how I experienced the story.

The first thing that makes Cyberpunk special is that your choices actually matter.

A lot of games promise meaningful decisions, but very few deliver. Cyberpunk does. The story evolves naturally based on your actions, and perhaps more importantly, the consequences make sense. You never get the feeling that the game is changing things just to prove that choices matter. Instead, characters react in believable ways, relationships develop differently, and the world feels responsive to who you decide to become.

What makes this even better is that every major ending feels justified. Whether you agree with a particular outcome or not, each path feels like a natural conclusion to the choices that led you there. By the time I reached the ending, I wasn't thinking about which ending was "best." I was thinking about which ending was right for the version of V I had created.

The story itself is phenomenal.

I spent roughly 60-80 hours completing everything I could find: the main story, side quests, gigs, exploration, and character storylines. When I finished, I wasn't ready to leave Night City. In fact, I started another playthrough and experienced the story again together with my wife because I wanted someone else to experience it too.

That's how good the writing is.

The side quests deserve special praise because they are some of the best I've ever seen in gaming. Most open-world games eventually fall into the trap of "go there, collect this, bring it back." Cyberpunk rarely does. Almost every side quest has its own story, memorable characters, difficult decisions, or unexpected twists.

Some quests stayed in my head long after I completed them. The crucifixion storyline (or Peralez) alone is more thought-provoking than entire campaigns in some other games. The game constantly presents situations that are morally complicated, uncomfortable, or emotionally challenging. Even simple gigs that start as "go eliminate this target" often turn into something far more interesting once you learn who the person is and why they're in that situation.

Many times I walked into a mission expecting a simple objective and ended up spending twenty minutes debating whether I should even pull the trigger.

That's what makes Night City feel alive.

Then there's the gameplay.

Cyberpunk gives you an incredible amount of freedom in how you approach the game. You can become a stealth-focused assassin, a walking tank, a cyber ninja slicing through enemies with katanas, a netrunner destroying entire groups without firing a shot, or something completely different. Every build opens new possibilities and changes how encounters play out.

The progression system constantly rewards experimentation. New cyberware, weapons, abilities, and playstyles keep the gameplay fresh for dozens of hours. Few RPGs manage to combine story depth and gameplay variety this well.

The result is a game where both the narrative and the gameplay are equally strong.

The biggest problem Cyberpunk created for me is that it raised my standards too high. After finishing it, I found myself comparing every other RPG to it. Other games might have a good main story, but their side quests rarely reach the same level of quality. They might have decent combat, but lack meaningful choices. They might offer choices, but fail to make them feel important.

Cyberpunk is one of the few games where the main story, side content, characters, world-building, role-playing, and gameplay all work together to create something special.

For me, it's not just a great RPG.

It's one of the best games ever made.

Геймплей: весьма вариативный. 
Ты можешь просто спокойно любоваться красотами Найт-Сити и прилегающих к нему территорий. Исследовать город (весьма интересное для меня занятие, в мире полно различных пасхалок, скрытых мест и прочего. Да и сам мир в игре многомерен), исследовать пустоши. Кому-то это может показаться скучным, мне же было интересно. Слушать разговоры пешеходов, смотреть новости, наблюдать за NPC. 
А можешь ввязаться в бой с очередными бандитскими выродками (по мере выполнения заказов порой просто волосы дыбом становились от того что вытворяли те или иные уроды и нередко хотелось выпилить их самолично, что игра даёт возможность сделать в полной мере), и тогда понеслась м*да по кочкам. Бои тут так же вариативны: можешь вырезать всех тихо, а можешь переть напролом как берсерк, расчленяя всех и каждого встречного. Благо вариантов убийства и нейтрализации супротивников игра предлагает массу. Всё это исходит из ветки и системы прокачки, которую ты выберешь. Тут вариативности тоже хватает: от тихих стелса с клинками и нетранерства, до использования пушек больших и малых калибров. В общем, выбор есть и он весьма обширный.

Как было сказано ранее: 1500+ часов о многом могут сказать. Я и сам был крайне удивлён времени, проведённому в этой игре, когда впервые взглянул на счётчик времени в Стиме. Оно летит для меня незаметно. Игра очень атмосферная и буквально погружает игрока в свой мир с самых первых его шагов.

Заключение: 
Есть такие игры, которые когда пройдёшь впервые - хочется забыть, чтоб перепройти их заново, и ощутить те самые первые эмоции. Да, не смотря на такое количество часов, проведённых в ней она по прежнему дарит эмоции, не смотря на то, что я, наверное, знаю практически всё в ней. Возможно это странно, но периодически что-то заставляет меня возвращаться в неё снова и снова. Такие игры, которые не отпускают тебя, или же хоть отпускают, но ненадолго. И Cyberpunk 2077 одна из таких немногих игр. Да, не Киберпанком единым я живу, но... Кто бы что ни говорил: для меня эта игра - Шедевр!

Ahí luego, чумбы!

Después de terminar Cyberpunk 2077 y sacar 3 finales distintos en mi primera run, puedo decir que este juego tiene muchísimo más contenido y posibilidades de las que esperaba. Incluso después de ver los créditos varias veces, sigo encontrando misiones, builds, diálogos y decisiones que cambian completamente la experiencia.
Lo mejor del juego son sus mecánicas. El combate mezcla disparos, hackeos y movilidad de una forma increíblemente divertida. Podés jugar como un netrunner que destruye enemigos sin tocar un arma, como un tanque cuerpo a cuerpo con katanas y brazos cibernéticos, o ir full sigilo. Y lo mejor es que todas las builds se sienten viables y distintas entre sí.

La ambientación de Night City es de las mejores que vi en un RPG. La ciudad está llena de detalles, personajes memorables y situaciones que hacen que quieras seguir explorando aunque ya hayas terminado la historia principal. Las misiones secundarias muchas veces tienen más calidad que historias principales de otros juegos.
Ahora, siendo crítico, el juego todavía tiene algunos problemas. La IA de NPCs y policías puede sentirse limitada en ciertos momentos, y hay bugs ocasionales o animaciones raras que te sacan un poco de la inmersión. También algunas decisiones parecen tener más impacto del que realmente terminan teniendo. Pero sinceramente, nada de eso opaca todo lo que el juego hace bien.
Después de sacar más de un final en una sola partida, la sensación que me quedó es que recién estaba empezando. Hay demasiadas formas de jugarlo, explorar builds y tomar decisiones diferentes. Pasó de ser un juego que me generó dudas y rechazo en su lanzamiento a convertirse en uno de los RPG más completos y entretenidos que jugué.  Pd: Vean el anime

I played this game on and off for 4 YEARS before seeing my first ending. It's that kind of game. There is just soooo much to do, and even when you aren't actually doing much of anything, it's plenty fun to just exist in this world. 

Without exaggeration, these people have crafted perhaps [i]the[/i] most immersive digital world to date. Aside from NPC interaction, everything genuinely feels like you are interacting with a living, breathing environment influenced by your actions. The level of detail and depth is easily my favorite thing about this game, and I often find myself falling back into the rabbit hole of videos discussing niche little elements of the world's history, geography, and iconography. Every element of this world's presentation is meticulously crafted to reflect its history, to the point where it's impossible [i]not[/i] to also occasionally feel the crushing weight of despair burdening every other inhabitant of Night City. The swaths of advertisements covering every wall, in particular, always piqued my interest. There is so much to be said about how eerily close to home this specific depiction of the cyberpunk dystopia feels.

One element of this game that I personally took issue with was its characters. While there were certainly standouts like Johny and Misty, the rest felt either severely underdeveloped or incoherent, resulting in a generally forgettable cast for me. Adam Smasher, especially, felt like he was set up as this huge presence throughout the game, but even by the end, I felt like I barely knew who he was or what he wanted. I'm not entirely sure what it was about my experience, but none of the love interest characters felt like much more than plot devices for me, with Panam in particular becoming such a conflicted mess of inconsistent motivations by the end that she ended up being the worst part of the ending experience for me. From what I hear, Judy's route seems like it would've been a bit more fleshed out and less annoying, but like wtf was Panam on at the end there?? (If you need characters, best just watch Edgerunners)

Which brings me to the ending—probably the weakest part of the story for me. In my view, this game shines most in its side missions. Heck, the only reason it took so long for me to get to the end is because I just really enjoyed driving around and solving problems for random people. Especially because a lot of those missions [i]rewarded[/i] you for being tactical (i.e., using stealth). For me, those were easily my most memorable experiences. While the main story can be exciting at times, especially at the beginning, it can get to feel sort of at odds with the type of game this is. The main thing that threw me off about the ending was how disconnected the story I was being told felt from the actual gameplay I was experiencing. By the time you get there, V is so ridiculously overpowered that tactics [i]do not[/i] matter in the slightest, so the enemy the game has been building up since the start, and still takes very seriously, just feels like a really sturdy punching bag you have to just slowly hack away at. This, combined with how ridiculous everything Panam was saying and doing, made for a very confusing, immersion-breaking experience. 

That said, Night City has a way of lodging itself deep inside your mind, to the point where a certain part of you may never truly be able to leave. If you can accept that, I think this game is very much worth your time.

Comprei em uma oferta e acredito que valeu super a pena, o jogo ainda continua tendo bugs e provavelmente isso já deve fazer parte da essência dele, mas durante toda minha gameplay não encontrei nenhum bug que fizesse eu perder meu progresso. As missões secundarias são bem interessantes, dês das que exploram mais os personagens quanto as que tocam em assuntos mais fortes, eu gostei bastante de fazer.
Falando da história principal [spoiler] tudo antes do assalto na torre Arasaka tem uma vibe diferente e obviamente isso se deve ao fato de tu não ter uma segunda personalidade na tua cabeça, que alias é simplesmente incrível, ter sempre uma pessoa falando e dando uma opinião em que tu vai fazer é interessante, sem contar que o Jhonny pode ser convincente. 之前已经给过差评了，现在50个小时游戏时间之后觉得更应该给一个完整的差评。
一、游戏算来已经卖了6年之久，经过这些更新之后有种bug不减反增的感觉，想不明白如此之久的时间内CDPR到底在干什么？在这个游戏里我已经习惯性把所有效果都归结到bug上，因为错误多到我分不清这些额外的东西里到底是应该存在还是歪打正着的bug。
二、游戏性是几乎没有的，对，整个游戏给我的感觉就像GTA的科幻世界观版，（GTA5在国内也属于是个宗教游戏，实际只有混乱的美式价值观穿插和历史虚无主义）像游戏内的通缉系统，各种抽象角色的离奇支线，经典的换汤不换药。
三、剧情可以但仅此而已，包括但不限于：强尼对于制度的破坏或者说叫革命只是形式上的破坏荒坂公司，但不敢对制度本身做出僭越，只能说是西方游戏公司的形式上地自由而事实上地不自由的人生观体现。（也就是在资本允许的范围内破环）
最后我得说，我实在是想不明白为什么这类游戏反而是最有市场的（包括我看到的各种视频网站里或论坛上这类游戏始终是最出圈的）赛博朋克社会本身就是极度的阶级斗争和资本的最大化扩张，难道所有人都喜欢这种“永远被压迫的底层群众和一层不变的病态社会”这种叙事世界观了吗？

Un action rpg che farà la storia, sia per la sua imbarazzante nascita, sia per la sua incredibile evoluzione.

Non illudetevi, i bug ci sono ancora, ma la stragrande maggioranza delle volte creeranno situazioni divertenti, non vi rovineranno l'esperienza di gioco. Ormai ho perso il conto di quante volte ho richiamato il mio veicolo e questo o è apparso dal nulla schiacciando qualche pedone oppure arriva a tutto gas ma sembra non capire dove fermarsi e continua ad andare a sbattere contro le pareti e gli altri veicoli fino a quando non esplode.

Ma al di là dei bug, [b]perché consiglio questo gioco? [/b]

1)[b]Per la sua storia estremamente cruda, estremamente punk [/b], piena di momenti belli e anche teneri, ma anche costante ti ricorda che in quel mondo la speranza e il riscatto sono solo un'illusione, per quanto ti possa riempirti di cromo.

2)[b]Per la città [/b]: ora estremamente viva, degradata e assolutamente caratteristica nella convivenza tra lusso estremo e squallore, cosa che si capisce anche solo passeggiando e ascoltando i dialoghi tra le altre persone (o vedendo da lontano uno scontro armato, molto armato, a cui poteva scegliere di partecipare o di essere spettatori).

3)[b]Per il fantastico sistema di progressione [/b]. Nel costruire il mio personaggio e nel portare avanti le missioni ho provato le stesse emozioni che provai con i primi Deus Ex. La stessa sensazione di poter davvero scegliere come risolvere i problemi, la vera libertà di bilanciare perfettamente il mio personaggio per poi ricominciare da capo con un personaggio completamente diverso.

Credo che chiunque si definisca un gamer dovrebbe almeno dare una possibilità a V e a Night City.

被低估的赛博朋克神作，经过多次更新优化，如今的2077早已褪去初期的瑕疵，成为最具沉浸感的开放世界之一。夜之城的霓虹永不熄灭，潮湿的街道、闪烁的全息广告、风格迥异的区域，每一处细节都透着赛博朋克的荒芜与繁华，走在街头仿佛真的置身于2077年的未来都市。
剧情围绕V的生存与救赎展开，Johnny银手的登场更是点睛之笔，两人从对立到羁绊，台词与配音极具感染力，每一个支线都藏着小人物的挣扎与坚守，玩完后劲十足。玩法上，枪械改装、义体搭配自由度拉满，潜行、强攻、黑客流任你选择，不同路线带来截然不同的体验。
优化后的帧率稳定，画面质感拉满，光影效果堪称顶级。它不只是一款游戏，更是一场关于自由、欲望与遗憾的赛博狂欢，无论是赛博朋克爱好者，还是开放世界玩家，都能在夜之城里找到属于自己的归宿，五星好评，值得反复回味。

Honnestly, i didn't like this game at all.

I'm a quite invested RPG player, BG3 is my fav game of all time so i might be opiniated, but my time is cyberpunk was not really a good time.
I see what the game wants to propose, i see what it wants to do, where it wants me to go, what it wants me to feels, etc. But i really feel like it's not polish well enough to have the impact it wants. I think the best exemple for that is in the begining (spoiler ahead):
[spoiler] For me, the best example of that is Jacky's death. Tbh, seing him died did not make me feel... anything? Like i see how my character feels, i see how i am suppose to feel, but from my point of view? Like, i did not know that guy, i had a single mission with him (+ the failed one but it's peanuts), i saw him for one cutscene and some small talk, but i was not really able to developp anything with him. He dies too soon, i did not get to know him before it happend. Like for exemple, Alfira death was far more impactfull in bg3 just because i was able to really connect with her in a previous scene, to share something with her. In comparison Jacky is just a random PNJ important in my character story. To give another comparison, i felt more thing with Delamain questline because we had more "shared story" as a player and PNJ (not lorewise) [/spoiler]
And sadly the game is like that with everything. 
(another spoil:) [spoiler] Evelyn Parker quest was like that too, i did not really know her more than that, and her s****** was just "empty" of emotion. TBH when i got the called, i was just a bit upset that she did that just after i saved her [/spoiler]

I feel like the quests, narratives, relationship etc are really empty. It really misses substance, impact. Some missions try to bring that with, like, no action at all, only dialogue, but even those are just a bit heavy and not really interesting. Sometimes i'm just there waiting for the discussion to finish because it lacks something. Maybe i'm too harsh because i'm used to Baldur's Gate in depth dialogue, but even with more tolerance it really feels like you have absolutly no impact in the game narratives, you are following a path, a rail, and watching a show you are not a part but just a spectator of.

Also the open world was not really interesting. I appreciate the cyberpsycho questlines but other than that... Contracts are always the same, just basic infiltration/combat sequence. Secondary quest are mostly classic and even a bit stupid sometimes, like that time i had to reload my save because my line choise during a dialogue gave me a stupid resolution to a stupid quest (the barman's wife's "affair" quest if you want to know). Combat are not really an issue, even in hard difficulty, and sneaky built are SO STUPIDLY STRONG that the game has to nerf you with "unsneakable" PNJ so you can't roll on all the games with it. The skills trees are really uneven. Some skill are really interesting and impactfull, while other feels like useless (like what are those lvl 20 shinobi skills?? I did not felt reward for my farming. Also, some skill are only oriented on ONE SPECIFIC cyber équipement or gameplay, so for a RPG it really limits what you can do with your character. Driving is AWFULL, roads feel like full of soap. Also the map really feels more like an empty grid with box to tic than like a persistant environment with events and life out of the player intervention.

So yeah, if you like RPG with a great deal of narration, i would not recommand this game. Agains maybe it's just me, but i really didn't get the thing. I hope this help my fellow RPG enjoyer, and have a nice day!

За свои 130 часов, которые я потратил на прохождение этой игры до одной из концовок основной игры + концовка из дополнения, я испытал широчайший спектр эмоций. Описать их можно парой слов будет очень сложно, но я попробую.
Геймплей в игре немного скачет. Легко перекачать персонажа до машины для убийств, но в последних миссиях сложность возрастает, что приятно для уставшего от всесилия геймера. Гоночные заезды для билда через кибердеку были легкими, хоть и заинтересовали во время квестов от Клэр. В основном игрок будет проходить доп кветы или заказы фиксеров. Однако, что там, что там, задачи могут быть однообразны: укради что-то, спаси кого-то, убей кого-то. Первоначально, даже угон машин для Эль-Капитана был интересен, спустя десяток часов стал просто еще одними метками на карте.
Графика в игре превосходная. Между квестами можно просто любоваться городом, катаясь на метро или машине/мотоцикле. Несмотря на некоторые косяки с dlss, без которого игрой не насладится на ультрах с трассировкой пути на моем компе, картинка часто радует глаз.
Звук также сделан на высоком уровне. Хоть озвучка, хоть саунддизайн, все просто ласкает уши. Особенно приятно было кататься по городу, слушая внутриигровое радио. А когда включается саундтрек, то так и хочется добавить его в свой плейлист.
А теперь самое вкусное — Сюжет. Игра очень сильна своим сюжетом. На момент первого запуска игры я знал про предыдущую игру студии(сам считаю ее шедевром, хоть лично не проходил игру), что держало планку ожиданий выше возможного, но игра пробила планку. История получилась очень захватывающей, в перестрелках адреналин бил по вискам, а в печальных или душераздирающих сценах даже могла пойти «скупая слеза». Ты проникаешься героями настолько сильно, насколько вообще позволяет экран. Сделана была неимоверная работа для этого, что заметно, но есть моменты которые рушили погружение в историю…
Несмотря на огромное количество исправлений посредством обновлений, техническое состояние игры все еще плачевно. Может оно и лучше того, как было на релизе, но все еще ошибок достаточно много. От просто сломанной анимации (не застраховани никто: ни сюжетные персонажи, ни простые нпс) до критических ошибок, из-за которых игра просто вылетала. Эти ошибки часто рушили погружение в квесты, хотя сюжету это не всегда мешало.
Если бы у меня спросил, могу ли я порекомендовать Киберпанк 2077 кому-либо, я бы сказал: 7/10, скорее да, чем нет. Перевес в положительную сторону достаточно велик, чтобы рекомендовать эту игру, но обилие багов, глюки, мешающие погружению, может отпугнуть. Однако, если игрок не будет обращать внимание на них, то он получит очень хорошую игру с потрясающим сюжетом и миром, где нет места счастливому концу. Но кто ищет, тот всегда найдет.
P.s. После прохождения лучше сделать перерыв, катаясь в той же forza horizon, или заценить инди-проекты

Nach weit über 600 Stunden auf der PlayStation 5 dachte ich eigentlich, ich hätte jede Ecke von Night City gesehen und jedes Geheimnis gelüftet. Das Spiel war dort nach Update 2.0 und Phantom Liberty bereits ein absolutes Meisterwerk. Doch der Wechsel auf den PC und das Eintauchen in das Modding des Spiels haben meine Erwartungen komplett gesprengt. Mods verändern dieses Spiel nicht nur sie heben es auf ein völlig neues Level.

Durch Grafik- und Cyberware-Mods fühlt sich die Welt noch echter und düsterer an. Anpassungen an der Wirtschaft, dem KI-Verhalten und dem Fahrverhalten der Autos eliminieren die letzten kleinen Schwachstellen des Hauptspiels. Mods, die das Fraktionssystem oder die Reaktionen der NPCs dynamischer gestalten, machen Night City spürbar unberechenbarer.

Dazu kommen völlig neue Möglichkeiten, die mir auf der Konsole komplett fehlten. Dank der Let There Be Flight-Mod fliege ich mit meinem Auto durch die Wolkenkratzer-Schluchten, was ein komplett neues vertikales Spielgefühl erzeugt. Das optische Modding von V und den Fahrzeugen ist grenzenlos, sodass ich Autos optisch komplett umbauen kann. Mod-Erweiterungen bringen zudem frische Quests und Minispiele ins Spiel, die mir nach 600 Stunden PS5 neuen Content liefern. Auch das Nutzen von voll animierten Bahnen und das Setzen in Bars via Modding erlaubt es, das Stadtleben einfach aufzusaugen.

Wer Cyberpunk 2077 nur von der Konsole kennt, hat nur die halbe Wahrheit gesehen. Das Grundspiel ist genial, aber die Modding-Community macht daraus das ultimative Sci-Fi-Rollenspiel. Nach 600 Stunden auf der PS5 fühlt sich das Spiel auf dem PC dank Mods wieder absolut frisch, aufregend und unendlich erweiterbar an. Ein absolutes Must-Have für jeden PC-Spieler!

Cyberpunk 2077 – ocena 10/10

Cyberpunk 2077 to gra, która pokazuje, jak powinien wyglądać nowoczesny RPG z otwartym światem. Night City zachwyca ogromem, klimatem i dbałością o szczegóły – każda ulica, budynek i postać sprawiają wrażenie, że żyją własnym życiem. Fabuła jest niezwykle wciągająca, pełna emocji i trudnych wyborów, a świetnie napisani bohaterowie na długo zapadają w pamięć. System walki daje dużą swobodę – można grać po cichu, korzystać z hakowania lub postawić na dynamiczne starcia. Dodatkowo rozwój postaci pozwala stworzyć własny, unikalny styl rozgrywki. Oprawa graficzna oraz muzyka tworzą wyjątkową atmosferę futurystycznego świata. Po licznych aktualizacjach gra działa znacznie lepiej i oferuje dopracowane doświadczenie. Cyberpunk 2077 to tytuł, który potrafi wciągnąć na dziesiątki godzin i pozostawia po sobie niezapomniane wrażenia. Zdecydowanie zasługuje na ocenę 10/10.

梦醒夜之城：从“传奇”到“注脚”的悲歌
对于很多玩家来说，《赛博朋克2077》是一个技术奇迹或是一个充满BUG的半成品；但对于真正沉浸其中的“V”来说，这是一场关于反抗、无力感与自我救赎的漫长洗礼。

1. 所谓“星星”：荒原上的最后一抹余晖

我的首个结局是“星星”，这或许是夜之城最温柔的谎言。当我坐在魔蝎装甲上，看着银手的吊坠掉入尘土，那不是遗忘，而是剥离。我剥离了那个疯狂的摇滚小子，剥离了霓虹灯下的尔虞我诈，试图在大地母亲的怀抱里寻找那虚无缥缈的“三个月”。

“我真的活下来了吗？”
这种挥之不去的后劲，正是《2077》剧情设计的精妙之处——它给你希望，但从未承诺永恒。

2. 宿命的死循环：无论多强，我依然是“耗材”

在GOG度过的300多个小时里，我感受到了那种最深沉的绝望：

V震天可以黑入整栋大厦，可以用螳螂刀切碎所有敌人。

底层蝼蚁在公司的财力与体制面前，个人的勇武苍白得像一张纸。

正如我所感悟的，V的经历是赛博世界悲剧的浓缩。三个出身（流浪者、街头小子、公司员工）最终都汇聚到了同一个终点——失败。在夜之城，没有所谓的“赢家”，只有“活过”和“死法”。

3. 银手的回响：从偏执狂到战友

第一周目时，银手的极端让我觉得吵闹；但当我体验过所有结局，看到公司的触角如何伸入人类的灵魂（神舆）时，才会明白他在垃圾场那句“你赢不了”是多么清醒的痛楚。

合作结局： 是最冰冷的现实，我意识到自己只是货架上的商品。

以我残躯化烈火： 则是最浪漫的自杀。既然改变不了世界，那就把自己变成一颗最亮的炸弹，在来生酒吧留下一杯以我命名的酒。

4. 玩家的告白：关于热爱与期待

从GOG的全款预购到Steam的再次补票，这种支持已经超越了消费行为，更像是一种对“艺术共鸣”的致敬。CDPR（蠢驴）虽然在宣发上摔过跤，但他们在塑造情感张力和世界观深度上，依然是业界的顶尖好手。

《往日之影》 进一步加深了这种权力的游戏与个人命运的冲突。

“猎户座”（续作） 承载着我们这些“老V”最后的愿景。

结语

夜之城没有活着的传奇，但我的V在那片霓虹荒原里真实地活过、爱过、反抗过。300小时不是游戏时长，那是我作为一名赛博浪客的第二人生。

“早安，夜之城。祝你在新的一天里，能找到回家的路。”

祝我在猎户座的群星中，再次找到那把划破长夜的利剑。

Eu tinha encostado em Cyberpunk 2077 uns 3 anos depois do lançamento, mas nunca curti muito o universo cyberpunk e nem o estilo de gameplay. Quando via vídeos, não me pegava tanto. Porém agora, quase 6 anos depois, resolvi dar uma chance… e caraca, que experiência absurda.

Absolute cinema.

Tive alguns bugs durante a gameplay, mas nada grave, carros bugados, cenários estranhos e coisas pontuais. O único problema real foram os crashes; nessa versão mais recente o jogo está bem instável em alguns momentos, e isso foi o que mais incomodou.

Agora sobre o jogo em si: valeu demais ter jogado.

A história é profunda, pesada e extremamente marcante. Ela trabalha temas como confiança, liberdade, identidade, medo da morte e, principalmente, laços humanos, e pra mim esse é o ponto mais forte da obra.

Você é o V, mas ao mesmo tempo constrói quem ele realmente é. Suas escolhas importam não só pelo final, mas pelas relações que você cria com cada personagem. Desde Takemura até um simples nômade em uma side quest qualquer, todos parecem ter vida própria.

Poucos RPGs conseguiram me passar essa sensação de que os personagens continuam existindo mesmo quando você não está olhando. Eles têm seus próprios problemas, objetivos, ambições e conflitos. Quando suas vidas se cruzam com a sua, aquilo realmente importa. Isso dá um peso emocional absurdo para a jornada.

E os finais são excelentes. Cada um carrega uma perspectiva diferente sobre tudo que você viveu até ali. Não vou listar nenhum para não estragar a experiência de quem ainda vai jogar.

Uma coisa que deixou tudo ainda melhor foi jogar pesquisando cada detalhe. Fui atrás da história das gangues, das corps, dos personagens, das regiões e até de pequenas missões secundárias. Isso mudou completamente minha experiência.

Entender o contexto de cada lugar, o motivo de certas decisões e o peso por trás de cada personagem fez tudo ficar muito mais profundo. Eu joguei praticamente com o Google Gemini do lado e também assisti vários vídeos sobre lore, e sinceramente recomendo demais fazer isso. Night City fica ainda maior quando você entende o que realmente está acontecendo ali.

Sobre a cidade e ambientação: Night City é quase perfeita.

A cidade realmente parece viva, crimes acontecendo, polícia contra gangues, NPCs discutindo, pequenas histórias secundárias e personagens vivendo seus próprios problemas. Cada região tem sua própria identidade, e as gangues têm presença e personalidade muito bem construídas.

Mas ainda existe uma sensação de “quase”. Em alguns momentos a cidade parece meio morta: faltam interiores, muitos NPCs são rasos ou repetidos, e isso quebra um pouco a imersão.

Também senti falta de um sistema mais profundo com corporações e principalmente com as gangues. Seria incrível poder construir reputação real com facções, criar rivalidades, desbloquear missões exclusivas e fazer o mundo reagir mais às suas escolhas.

Nas mecânicas, porém, o jogo entrega demais.

Você pode criar builds extremamente fortes e totalmente diferentes entre si. A árvore de habilidades permite vários estilos, stealth, hacking, força bruta, lâminas (build que usei, de samurai, OP demais), armas pesadas e por aí vai.

E o sistema de cyberwares (os famosos cromos) é uma das melhores partes. Não é só equipar itens melhores, você literalmente modifica seu corpo. Quer desacelerar o tempo? Dá. Quer virar uma máquina de combate? Dá. Quer hackear tudo sem sacar uma arma? Também dá.

Isso faz a progressão ser muito mais interessante, porque seu personagem evolui de verdade dentro daquele universo.

No geral, minha nota é 4.5/5.

O motivo de não ser um 5/5 está justamente nesse sentimento de “quase”. Cyberpunk 2077 é um quase perfeito mundo vivo.

这是一部偏剧情向的作品，如果只是想单纯的体验大世界杀杀杀、爽爽爽的快感，建议慎重考虑。

剧情的演绎绝对是殿堂级别的，人性的抉择、社会的尔虞我诈全部都被展现的淋漓尽致。每个npc都活灵活现，都有各自的人格魅力，与npc的交往真的就像在现实里与人交往，极其生动。每一个结局都引人深思，没有所谓的好结局坏结局，全部都是个人的理解。

dlc建议是必买，在超越本体发的顶级剧情的前提下，精细度至少是本体的两倍，每个委托都能选择npc的结局，完成委托后甚至能在大世界找到npc看到他们的未来，dlc为本体新增了一个结局，同时dlc也有多个结局。

中文的配音真的配的非常非常好，没有一点母语尴尬，人物的情感让配音展现的更加生动，绝对的顶级配音。

赛博风格的绝美景色、多流派战斗体验、多载具跑图、各种各样的武器、内容爆满的大世界探索，这些点甚至都只是游戏的最基本组成部分，并没有过于突出，相比于剧情和演出，这些点更像是陪衬。

扣一颗星的原因是该游戏历经多次优化，小bug依旧层出不穷，并且比较吃电脑性能，说实话前40个小时体验完全感觉不出来，但是游戏时长一旦上涨，各种各样的小bug就很难不让人注意到了，比较破坏游戏体验

Es complicado hablar de este juego. Lo amé, hice más de 110 horas en mi primera partida, completé todas las misiones que al menos yo encontré disponibles y, aun así, sigo sintiendo que es difícil definirlo.

Cyberpunk 2077 es como si te sirvieran un platillo donde el corte de carne está increíble, pero todo lo demás es un desastre, la ensalada, las guarniciones, la bebida y hasta el postre.

El mundo y la historia son lo mejor del juego, y probablemente la razón por la que me tomé tanto tiempo para terminarlo a pesar de todo lo malo. Los personajes que te acompañan durante la aventura son entrañables y muy distintos entre sí, es imposible no encariñarte con ellos y querer seguir en contacto incluso después de terminar sus respectivos arcos.

Pero el juego sigue teniendo muchísimos problemas técnicos. Yo no lo jugué de salida, y aun así la versión que juguué estaba llena de bugs. Incluso tuve que contactar al soporte porque una misión principal quedó bugeada por un error. ¿su solución? Empezar otra partida. Afortunadamente logré arreglarlo usando mods.

También es evidente que el sistema de conducción nunca terminó de funcionar del todo. Manejar se siente extraño, los choques hacen que la IA se comporte de forma absurda y varios autos deportivos parecen ir prácticamente igual de rápido que vehículos comunes. Todo lo relacionado con los autos se siente poco refinado.

El sistema de diálogos también me frustró varias veces. Odio cuando un juego te da dos opciones de respuesta, eliges una y el personaje termina diciendo algo completamente distinto a lo que aparecía escrito. Rompe muchísimo la inmersión y hace que las decisiones pierdan impacto.

El mundo está lleno de errores y detalles poco pulidos, pero incluso con todo eso, el juego me encantó. La historia, los finales y la libertad para construir tu personaje, ya sea como netrunner, usando cyberware al máximo o jugando con sigilo, hacen que realmente sientas que puedes moldear tu propia experiencia. Es un juego extremadamente imperfecto, pero también uno que logra sacar lo mejor de sí mismo cuando decides darle una oportunidad.

It's been a while since I've played this game, but I figured I'd finally leave a review for it since one's been pending for a while.

This game was honestly always a good game. It may have had a rough start due to bugs and performance issues, but the core storyline and gameplay, as well as the more interesting questlines you can follow, were always there. Then with all the QoL changes and the complete overhaul they did to the perk system, it became much more refined and enjoyable to play since you now had a variety of builds and perks you could experiment with. 

I think one of my favorite things about the game was the story and characters. Every character has an interesting and expressive personality, including your own as expressed through the voice acting (I personally prefer Male V's voice direction). Everyone feels fleshed out and like they actually have a growing relationship to you the more you interact with them. The main story itself feels very personal and high stakes, though some of that is admittedly ruined by the open world nature of the game since you can just dally along however long you want. As the meme goes, "Anything but meeting Hanako at Embers" lol. Even so, I think it manages to portray a nice drama about the meaningfulness of life, self-determination, and even hope in a world that seems determined to grind you down.

The environment is effective in portraying just how degenerate and trashy (literally, even) Night City really is, which helps in creating this sense of "contamination" and a desire to separate yourself and rise above it. 

Also, the music. The music in this game kicks ass, and I still listen to some of my favorite tracks on my Spotify every so often.

I'd say my only real complaint with the game is the lack of being able to clearly show yourself as cybernetically enhanced, such as by having clearly mechanical limbs or metallic embellishments like a Kano-style red eye. I was also never too fond of any of the romance options, but it was nice that I never felt forced to pursue any of them from what I can remember.

La verdad que ahora se puede decir que es un muy buen juego, aunque creo que nunca va a llegar a ser lo que se prometió.
Los gráficos, la música, el doblaje, los diálogos, las animaciones me parecen excelentes. Y la ambientación de Night City es espectacular y la publicidad que vemos en la ciudad es muy buena y original. Además la trama principal, me parece muy bien llevada y super interesante y los personajes que nos presentan (Jackie, Johnny, Judy, Rogue, Panam, River, Kerry, Peralez...) son muy buenos. Y la verdad que las misiones secundarias no quedan cortas, muy recomendadas hacerlas.
Y respecto al DLC Phantom Liberty, si mucho que añadir, es también muy bueno. Me molan las mejoras del Relic que añaden y los nuevos finales.

Y no he tenido muchos bug o problemas con el juego. Me crasheó una vez y un par de veces tuve que cargar un archivo de guardado anterior, pero no tuve nada muy grave que me fastidiara la experiencia.

Si que creo que hay algunos aspectos a mejorar:
- Las decisiones que tomas la verdad que no sirven para mucho salvo para el final y a lo mejor también diría que para las relaciones amorosas.
- El balanceo no me parece que esté muy bien, puedes romperte muy fácilmente y realmente el juego ya no supone un reto, aunque es divertido cargarse a todo el mundo xd.
- El Cyberware como concepto me gusta, pero quitando algunos la mayoría solo dan pasivas. Igual podría haber hecho algo más con este concepto.

En resumen, a día de hoy, el juego merece una oportunidad de ser jugado, ha mejorado y arreglado mucho, aunque no creo que vaya a ser lo que se prometió.

This game is wide as an ocean, shallow as a puddle. It's good, but people keep overrating this game. The endings fit the settings theme and it's very cinematic. The shooting is mediocre, character creation is not really that engaging, the "choices" you make don't really matter all that much, on both a micro and macro level, and EVERY single mechanic is very surface level. Jack of all traits, master of none.

It's also just a god awful RPG. Like to the point that it being described as that feels like false advertising. There's literally no "roleplaying" in this game beyond picking dialogue options. The backgrounds hardly matter beyond how you meet your character's first friend. Shooting is boring, driving is awful, the cybernetics aren't that interesting of a system. (Deus Ex and even 'Cruelty Squad' do it better! Which is embarrassing for a game that was in development for this long.)

I've tried my best to care for the characters, but I kind of just don't. You hardly get to know each other, and you don't really "work" with another beyond the individual missions. Your "friends" are not plot relevant at all, beyond Panam for Act 1 and the finale. The "ending" of the game is probably what 'saves' this game at all, as it resonates so thematically with the nihilistic world that it almost convinces you the story was actually good, and not boring meaningless filler for 80% of it. 

You are so absurdly powerful in this game - both mechanically and storywise that it kind of makes all mission "planning" a bit boring and annoying. Why even do all of this if I can just kill everything that moves? Phantom Liberty is a little bit better about this but it's still not really enough.

The themes and story is so annoyingly nihilistic, and to make it worse it comes from a pretty decently sized studio with a huge budget behind it. Oh, I'm sure a corporation would be HAPPY to promote a game where capitalism is some magical all consuming force that enslaves the planet and cannot be stopped by literally any means possible. Solutions? To capitalism? Well the writer doesn't want you to think about that, they just want you to bask in how miserable everyone is! It's individualist slop that I can't tell is out of ignorance or out of malice for the world.

The anime just saved this game's ass insanely badly. It's THE "hype moments and aura" game. If you like that, play this game. If you want an actually good story with good gameplay??

Hope that maybe the sequel will be actually good.

This game is a total dumpster fire. I cant believe how many reviews sing it any praises, beyond it looks good. Visuals are the only thing CP2077 has going for it. 
The world is shallow and derivative, with little to no reason to go anywhere or see anything in particular. Not counting the fact that when you are inspired to check something out, there is ZERO interactability. Very little to actually DO in night city, except vibe. 
The cutscenes are all drawn out, basically just Visual Novel style, except the characters are paper thin. Seriously, it's like the writers here don't even understand basic humanity, or how people interact together. 
Characters feel stiff and lifeless, without real human depth, just an edgy facade with a subtle implication of substance. Story pacing is all over the place.
 There's moments of intrigue, ruined by shitty dialogue or some ubelievably thin character aspect; cool cars scene ruined by on the rails action, generally inconsistent action will pull you out of the scene over and over in a playthrough. Not to mention the driving feels terrible. Nothing like a cool looking veneer on a slippery brick to get around NC with. When you do get somewhere with 'something to do' you're basically just killing everyone on site for the plot. Guns are weak and clunky, melee feels inorganic and unrealistic, and hacking is just not that fun, not to mention they don't reward stealth play very much, if at all, thanks to enemies being omniscient or totally blind. 

My biggest gripe with the game is one I almost never see mentioned: Almost every single story line, quest story, side quest, some characters and locations are Straight up RIPOFFS, from ACTUAL GOOD media. They ripped the name from a whole genre, confusing newbies into the scene, trying to force themselves into the discussion around the genre, when CDPR haven't even really contributed in that realm; its very disingenuous, and speaks to their philosophy as a company. Go check out any foundational cyberpunk media, and see how many tropes CP2077 straight ripped off from actual good writers and creators. Everything voodoo/AI ghost in the machine/ sentient AI using peons to escape, etc. are total 1:1 rips from William Gibson's Neuromancer trilogy. 
The only reason this game wasn't a MASSIVE flop is because braindead CONSUMERS ate up Witcher 3, and cant be honest with themselves, that this game is no anywhere near that level. 
Honestly hate this game, and I will NOT purchase anything CDPR does in the future.

Espero no ser el único en estar de acuerdo con que, el Cyberbug... ejem, quiero decir, Cyberpunk 2077, tiene una historia increíble. La mayoría de misiones secundarias no son simple relleno: le hacen un complemento brutal al lore del juego. 

El tema de los romances es un viaje. La historia de Panam, aparte de ser de las chicas más bonitas de la ciudad, se siente real. En cambio, con Kerry la cosa es diferente; aunque perfectamente podría ser el padre de V, el tipo no se queda atrás. El único problema es que su romance llega tardísimo, casi en la recta final, y es una pena porque muchos se lo van a perder si van con las prisas.

La historia de Johnny me mantuvo en un vaivén de emociones. Fue durísimo sacar el final de "El Sol" por todo lo que pasa con Rogue. Le tomé mucho cariño durante el Acto 3, y ver ese desenlace me hizo querer partirle la cara con todavía más ganas a Adam Smasher.

El único pego que le puedo poner es que el mundo abierto en ciertas zonas no se siente tan vivo más allá de generar multitudes de fondo, como pasa en el Centro Corporativo. Se nota un poco vacío en interacción fuera de las misiones, pero el juego compensa con creces en todo lo demás.

La música es una genialidad. El tema de los créditos de Phantom Liberty hizo que me pusiera a chillar de la emoción. Ese DLC es, sin duda, de lo mejorcito que se ha lanzado en los últimos años. Además, aquí es donde brilla Mr. Hands: qué hombre tan GRANDIOSO. Es el mejor fixer y, probablemente, mi personaje favorito de todo el juego.

Al final, pese a todas las duras críticas y el hate que recibió en su lanzamiento, el juego logró renacer de sus cenizas para convertirse en una maldita obra maestra.

Нещодавно пройшов основний сюжет Cyberpunk 2077, і можу сказати, що це одна з тих ігор, яка справді залишає після себе сильні емоції. Найбільше вразив сам світ Night City — він виглядає неймовірно живим, деталізованим і атмосферним. Під час проходження постійно відчувається, що ти знаходишся у величезному футуристичному місті, де за кожним кутом є своя історія.

Сюжет дуже сильний і місцями навіть змушує задуматися. Персонажі добре прописані, особливо головний герой та Джонні Сільверхенд, взаємодія з яким додає грі особливого шарму. Діалоги цікаві, а багато виборів реально змушують думати, як краще вчинити.

Окремо варто похвалити візуальну частину: графіка, освітлення, музика та загальна атмосфера просто на висоті. У деякі моменти хотілося просто зупинитися й подивитися на місто або послухати саундтрек.

Так, у гри був непростий старт, але зараз Cyberpunk 2077 — це справді якісний і захопливий проєкт, який варто пройти. Для мене це була не просто гра, а ціла пригода з сильними персонажами, важкими виборами та дуже стильним світом. Після проходження залишилося відчуття, ніби побував у чомусь великому.

Cyberpunk boiled down to bones is an upgraded version of GTA, full stop. For quests, instead of doing yoga or goofing off at a port doing nothing for hours like in GTA, you will have the most insane side quests AND get paid for it. Just to give a glimpse into what that could mean - you pick up an AI pistol off a dead guy in a shady alley and it makes you kill 50 people with it while it talks to you, you drive a creepy clown to a specific burrito vending machine (found everywhere in the city btw) only for him to kill the people standing in front of it for no reason, you eat Chinese food from a stand with a Japanese man and he calls it shit to the chef’s face, you use a light machine gun to mow down a homeless camp while they charge you, you have a street fight with a guy and take away his car in front of his pregnant girlfriend (dw tho, it makes sense and he ends up better off), the list just goes on. 

How is the game though? Overall it runs amazing and have had no major issues. One crash an hour in or something when I blew up 8 cars at the same time by accident (dropped a grenade when I went to change weapons into a car pile up). Never had an issue again. The city is beautiful, the quests are awesome, the game takes way over 100 hours to complete, the city and surrounding badlands is huge map wise (yes, you get fast travel points everywhere), the cars are fun, the clothing is awesome, the choices during conversations will require a few playthroughs (just bought the game for my main account so haven't finished the nomad one yet), the physics make sense, and the save button is the most used thing you will ever use (very very useful for going back if you screw up a convo or fight). For the story, it is a must play. 

Anything wrong with it? Yeah, nothing major but "stuff happens" sometimes. You could be on a hill trying to spawn in your car after a quest and it may explode on another car (nothing happens it's just annoying because you need to respawn it - ps it is NOT common), a quest could get stuck if you go into a cutscene and you weren't standing in the place they told you to be in (just reload last save, takes 4 seconds), people speaking can sometimes overlap (NPC 1 finishing their sentence and NPC 2 starts talking on the last word or something), loot can get stuck on bodies that you can't dispose of or loot, that kind of stuff. Most importantly, does it impact the gameplay? 100% no, it just "happens" and you reload and move on. 

Why the pos recommendation? The story and character development is worth it, full stop. Once you start, you can't put the game down because you want to complete the 270+ missions they have available. There is a LOT to do lol. 

^ With all the above said, any negatives? Yeah, this game is way too into LGBT stuff. One character that you do street races with added in randomly that they were trans for 0 reason (you can't tell at all btw, knowing the fact added nothing to the gameplay) and then they suddenly had a personality shift to get revenge on their partner's killer mid race despite the dude dying fair and square. Made 0 sense and was forced. You could also talk about this girl that has the EXACT same romance lines as if you were a woman (because she's apparently gay) and you don't find that out until the last quest where she leaves the city. The lines were double dipped and the devs were lazy there 100%. As a straight male, she just shuts you down out of left field. Last major character was this cop you did quests with. The game gives you an option to start a gay relationship with the guy, keep him as a friend, or leave entirely all in the same conversation prompt. Does the game force you to be gay or bi or whatever? Def NOT, but you will have the "option" to if you wanted it. Wish there was a feature to turn on a "straight male" mode to avoid it altogether but I guess they want night city to truly feel degenerate and without morals. "No happy endings" right? It does not impact your gameplay, it just makes it slightly annoying to see. I am totally hyperfocusing on this despite it not even being 1% of the game because it could have been perfect with an option to let you avoid all that stuff. 

Right, enough said about that. Cyberpunk is worth every dollar and you should dive right into night city choom. Thanks for reading and God bless.

We are all aware of this game's horrible launch state, but with 2.0, the Phantom Liberty DLC and subsequent updates, I believe CDPR has turned that launch disaster into what it was always meant to be, that being one of the greatest games in recent memory. Something I'd happily call this generation's New Vegas.

Pros:
- Incredible worldbuilding through lifepaths. I would recommend a new player starting with Nomad but Corpo is my favorite
- Well-written and complex characters that feel like actual people with everyone hiding at least something under the surface, no matter how insignificant they may be to the story
- Great story with a well-handled approach to many complex themes along with emotional hard-hitting moments (Especially Phantom Liberty)
- Incredible amounts of replayability, that can be owed to rewarding, deliberate and varied buildcrafting (especially on higher difficulties), satisfying gameplay, multiple endings, and of course, mod support (I have way more hours on the GOG version dw)
- Great soundtrack
- Fashion potential is off the charts, especially with mods

Cons (if I really have to nitpick):
- Some jank is still to be found if you look for it
- The open world sometimes feels a bit lifeless, but you'll be too busy doing gigs to care Lol
- The first ten levels or so are pretty slow to do, especially on harder difficulties (despite which I can still absolutely recommend them regardless)
- Some guns are straight up useless for 80% of players, which ends up diluting gunplay a lot more than it should

Despite some minor flaws, I'd still say this game has 100% earned its roses now.

Cyberpunk is a really good game. It is considered a reference on multiple fronts which combined result in a highly entertaining experience. If you get the chance, buy it and play it. 

Cyberpunk is an ambitious project in terms of scope and technical capabilities. Despite its rough start, it's undeniable this is one of the most good looking game there was when it came out, and the dimension of the project is not something that many studios would dare to tackle for an entirely new IP. I'm happy they did and we should give them credit that they took it to the end, to ensure its mostly failed launch was just a light stain on their track record.

This game was designed with realism in mind and it will pull everything out of your graphics card to make it happen. At the same time, it is still somehow flexible to be able to run on something as restricted as a steam deck. It's impressive. If you have the necessary hardware, your eyes will feast. It's a game from 2020 but still used as a tech demo reference in 2026. That's saying something. 

I feel the Cyberpunk can be best described as a linear game built on top of a massive (open?) world. Yes, you can take quests in mostly assorted order but you do feel they're all leading to the same outcome. Your decisions don't shape the world, you're just following the pre-destined path, but this path is highly entertaining. 

To be fair to the devs, open world games are tough. It's hard to get them right. Most just end up being too sprawling with little substance (looking at your Starfield) and struggle with pacing. In Cyberpunk, the devs decided to use this massive maps to sprinkle curated experiences all over the places: the quests, the gigs, the NYCP arrests, etc... All in all, making sure in every region, that there was at least something interesting happening there once.

It's not a game where the world on its own has the built-in dynamics to entertain you by itself, but CD PROJECT RED left plenty to do everywhere. I personally loved the gigs, secondary to the plot, because it provides that kind of experience you get with Hitman: "here's a constrained location and goal, there are multiple ways to fulfill the goal, go and have fun". The NYCP arrests were a bit more trash tier casual events for me. I didn't really connect with them and I failed to see their appeal. 

The world building and design this project did is amazing and they just deserve praise.

The weapon systems are interesting; the way gameplay changes based on the implants you decide to install on your character is peak. The implant and skill system is solid and built to ensure that only your imagination is the limit in deciding how you want to play this game: in your face bruiser, long range assassin, sneaky cyber-runner, a combination of the previous, etc. There are more combinations than the time you'll have to play them.  

Phantom Liberty is DLC done right. The DLC has its own review page but this doesn't subtract from the value it added to the experience, although you can't help but to feel that they are detached. The way it intertwines with the main story is superficial. To be fair, it would technically very hard to have it any other way.

Regarding music and soundtrack: I remember spending hours driving to the radios in GTA 3 and Vice City. That was no longer the case in Cyberpunk. I mostly kept the radio quiet and can't really pinpoint why. Maybe I just got old, the samples I got from the radio didn't really connect on the first listens and then I just ended up turning off the radio. Or maybe it's a sign that in general I didn't feel them appealing enough, despite the random sampling. I know there are at least 2 or 3 banger tracks, that I felt welt placed, some of them during key dialogs that really helped to shape the mood. In the places it really mattered, the score was there and provided the necessary lift. However the passive listening experience (radio) was not the best. Maybe it's just the reality of Night City of being very self-imposing with its piercing ads and obnoxious jingles.  

There was nothing I really disliked in this game. Only things that I would not mind the see changed into the next iteration of Cyberpunk 2077, if that ever ends up being a thing: 

1. V's personality was extremely bland. I picked a corpo path and the way V spoke just sounded often like a low education gangster. This dissonance between personality and background killed immersion.
2. I would like to see the design philosophy behinds the gigs more present even in the main quest. Right now everything is absolutely scripted. One way in, one way out. I feel "The Last Of Us" showed us there's is flexibility for having both. If you have level designers on your team that can develop maps like the gigs, I'm sure these can still flow into your main quest.
3. I felt sad the gigs never really tied properly with the world lore. The story is baked-in and its not reactive to decisions you took in some of these gigs. 


It's a great game. Be ready to commit some time to it :)

누구나 이 게임의 결점을 이야기할 수는 있습니다.
하지만 누구도 이토록 애정을 담아 게임을 만들 수는 없을 것입니다.

사이버펑크 2077은 분명 많은 결점을 안고 출시된 게임이었고, 지금도 완전히 지워지지 않는 아쉬움이 남아 있습니다.
그럼에도 개발진이 이 작품에 쏟아부은 사랑과 노력만큼은 단 한순간도 의심해 본 적이 없습니다.

아마 개발이 진행될수록, 개발진 스스로도 수없이 생각했을 것입니다.
‘아, 이건 이렇게 만들면 안 되는데.’
하지만 게임은 한 명의 예술가가 오롯이 자신의 고집만으로 완성할 수 있는 장르가 아닙니다.
글이나 그림, 혹은 만화는 어쩌면 가능할지도 모르겠습니다.

그러나 게임, 그리고 영화와 같은 종합예술은 다릅니다.
음악과 미술, 서사와 연출, 기술과 시스템.
수많은 요소가 얽혀 하나의 ‘아름다움’을 만들어냅니다.

사람들은 왜 예술을 만들까요.
결국 아름다움을 추구하기 위해서일 것입니다.
그리고 사람들은 그 아름다움에 감동하고, 가치를 부여하며, 즐거움을 느낍니다.

하지만 예술은, 아직 아름다울지조차 확신할 수 없는 상태에서 막대한 비용과 시간을 요구합니다.
특히 게임 같은 종합예술은 더욱 그렇습니다.

그리고 예술에 돈이 얽히는 순간, 시간이라는 가장 냉혹한 비용 역시 함께 따라옵니다.
가능성과 가치가 보이더라도, 결국 어느 순간에는 반드시 ‘완성’되어야 하니까요.

문득 그런 생각이 들었습니다.
사이버펑크 2077은 어쩌면, 우리가 쉽게 헤아릴 수 없는 수많은 사정 속에서 조금 이르게 세상에 나온 작품이 아니었을까 하고요.

물론 여기에 대한 반박도 많을 것입니다.
그리고 대부분의 반박은 결국 하나의 질문으로 귀결됩니다.

“정말 그게 최선이었나?”

사이버펑크의 주인공 V와의 여정을 끝내고 싶지 않아, 엔딩을 미룬 채 보낸 시간이 어느덧 2년.
이제는 그 질문에 답할 수 있을 것 같습니다.

적어도 결과만 놓고 본다면, 그것은 분명 그들의 최선이었다고.

그들이 상상한 사이버펑크 세계는, 그들이 할 수 있는 최선의 방식으로 이 게임 안에 구현되어 있습니다.
시간과 비용, 시대와 갈등, 그리고 수많은 고민 끝에 도달한 형태로 말입니다.

문득 영화 닥터 스트레인지의 한 장면이 떠오르기도 했습니다.
마지막 전투는 모두를 완벽하게 구해낸 싸움은 아니었지만, 적어도 그들이 도달할 수 있었던 최선의 선택이었으니까요.

최근 공개된 붉은 사막을 보며, 사이버펑크 2077의 초기 모습이 떠올랐습니다.
그래서 이렇게 뒤늦은 리뷰를 남기게 되었습니다.

오늘 저는 빈센트와 발레리와의 여정을 마무리했습니다.
그리고 새로운 세계로 떠날 준비를 하고 있습니다.

스칼리츠의 헨리, 재의 귀인, 그리고 조엘과 엘리까지.
정든 세계와 친구들에게 작별을 고하는 일은 언제나 쉽지 않네요.

그래도 앞으로 이 게임을 플레이할 사람들이, 과거의 상처와 악평만을 보고 나이트 시티로 향하는 발걸음을 멈추게 되는 것은 아쉽다고 생각했습니다.
그래서 이렇게 두서없는 글을 남기게 되었네요.

좋은 영화 한 편을 보고 극장을 나설 때처럼, 오래 마음에 남는 무언가를 느꼈습니다.

당신도 사이버시티 속에서 그 기분을 느낄 수 있으면 좋겠습니다.

긴 글 읽어주셔서 감사합니다.
