My first playthrough was incredible. It was almost bug free and actually immersive. (No DLC installed)
Graphics are ofcourse great, but some areas are just way too shiny. I don't think I should ever have to change my monitor setting just for my eyes to not fall out.

Now for the complaining part... My second playthrough with DLC installed, I encountered a bug every few hours. Among the most annoying were Sasquatch fight was completely broken (in base game it didnt happen), and the V button for vehicle call gets broken randomly. Also things like strengh execute where you throw a person is janky as hell. Kinda just breaks the whole build. Some of the other frustrating things are some of the DLC bossfights. The chimera fight was also janky. And then there is this Voodoo Boys netrunner you get locked in a room with in one quest and robots spawn all around the room and you cant prekill them or anything. Also the wanted system in this game is weird. Underwhelming I suppose. It's there to be there. I think it would make more sense if Maxtac came before 50 policemen die imo. Sometimes I even lose wanted level on accident. Another small thing I wanna complain about is how you cant interact with a lot of things. Imagine how cool it would be if you could quickhack an AV and crash it into enemies? Highjack building systems like in The Heist mission and take control of all turrets and get camera info? Another thing that had me confused for hours is how item components are straight forward for 80 hours of playing a shotgun build, and then I try netrunner build and suddenly you have to buy everything from vendors for insane cash.

Story was great, all characters are great, the ideas are there. Cyberpunk has SO much potential. So besides the things I complained about the way they are, I want to complain more about what I think could and should have been and hopefully will be.

I'm not among the people who appreciate cosmetics in games, but this is true regardless. In what world are we not getting clothes suited for fighting? We really get all these body augments just for a 25 armor combat vest to be the strongest clothing option? Also there is like ONE quest instance where the NPCs care about your clothing and it's with Johny's jacket. Just a big gaping hole where there could be something just as great as augments. And as for augments, they really are like the one big thing that should be making it great. And it is. But again, not to it's fullest potential. How come V goes 90% chrome and It's not visible on the model? Now that would be a cosmetic change I would care about, not a shirt with an image on it. Also how the game doesnt really go deep enough into the modifications. There are many cyberware modifications, yes. But what do you mean I can't have a cyberdeck and a sandevistan? They are not even in the same part of the body. You can easily get deep into this issue of how we are getting limited for no reason in this aspect. Also what do you mean the limiting factor is a cooldown? Shouldnt it be the toll on the cyberware and the body? I propose the limiting factor should be overheating. There could also be so many perks added around it. Low heat build, high heat build...
I also think there should be superheavy cyberware. Why are gorrila arms just normal metal arms? There should be super heavy cyberware options, and supportive cyberware for them. Or perks allowing them, in the super heavy tree of the strengh skill three. Imagine Gorrila arms, but double the size. anchor feet for support of superheavy artillery cyberware.
Another thing I want to complain about is how stealth, and stats work, especially the mitigation stat.
I believe, after 200 hours, that I can with confidence say, that players don't value invisible stats. Especially on Very Hard mode, Armor and mitigation are just not noticable. We don't see the bullets missing us, We don't see the armor affect the damage we receive. Also it would be great if the game showed us all stats while we're at a ripper doc clinic. Just makes sense, doesnt it? 
And for stealth... I will leave this one off the hook, since for builds without stealth, it worked as it should, and who cares about stealth in cyberpunk anyway. 

The reason I complain about the game is not because I hate it. It's because I love it. I would love to wake up in a well done futuristic world. I was a few years late to this game so I missed the car crash launch.  It actually ran really well for me, albeit on GeForce Now because the graphics were well beyond my elderly rig.  I absolutely loved the setting - Night CIty feels so alive in all of its seedy, dystopian glory - the gunplay, stealth and hacking elements of gameplay as strong and above all, the characterisation, branching storylines and worldbuilding are really compelling.

There are a few features that I would really have liked to see - like car customisation and V's origin story actually mattering beyond a few dialogue options here and there.  The biggest issue for me though is how the stories all end; I was expecting it to end GTA/Witcher 3 style so that once the main story is done you are free to just noodle around the world, find all the hidden stuff and finish the many, many side quests that feel too small to bother with because the main story is so urgent.  Unfortunately, CDPR didn't go for that and (no spoilers) whatever happens you just get teleported back to the beginning of the final section of the main quest.

It's a real shame because the game is so immersive that it feels immersion-breaking to stop and do all the trivial stuff on the way.  And the DLC doesn't correct that either.  The game is still a great game, but it would've had considerably more longevity had CDPR retained a properly open post-endgame experience.

赛博朋克2077——夜之城的视听盛宴，救赎之路与未尽的遗憾
最初借着Steam家庭共享在夜之城当了回“临时雇佣兵”，几十小时的体验让我彻底上头，最终还是没忍住补了票——毕竟这样的夜之城，值得拥有自己的存档。必须承认，《赛博朋克2077》是近年来最让我震撼的开放世界RPG之一，但它的优缺点同样鲜明，像夜之城本身一样，既光鲜又破败，既让人沉迷又让人抓狂
先说让人上头的部分。夜之城的构建堪称游戏工业的奇迹，从沃森区的霓虹招牌到市政中心的摩天大楼，从恶土的荒漠到狗镇的法外之地，每一处场景都塞满了细节——街头的涂鸦、小贩的叫卖、路人随口哼的《I Really Want to Stay at Your House》，甚至广告牌上的公司标语，都在传递“赛博朋克”的冰冷与狂热。剧情更是直击灵魂，V与强尼·银手的共生关系，从最初的互相厌恶到最后的生死与共，这种“灵魂融合”的设定让主线充满了情感张力，尤其是强尼在V脑海中逐渐“苏醒”的过程，像一场关于存在与记忆的哲学辩论，让人忍不住思考“什么是真正的自我”
战斗系统的多样性也值得称赞，无论是潜行黑客流、狙击爆头流，还是义体改造的近战狂战士，每种玩法都有独特的乐趣。超梦体验的设计更是神来之笔，在朱迪的支线里潜入他人的记忆，那种“身临其境”的眩晕感和碎片化叙事，让支线任务的深度不输主线
不过缺点也需要正视。即使经过多次更新，NPC的智能依然像个“提线木偶”——他们会重复同样的台词，对枪战视而不见，甚至在街上卡进墙里。主线结局的仓促感也很明显，尤其是“恶魔结局”里V的抉择，明明铺垫了那么多关于“生存与尊严”的讨论，最后却像被按了快进键，让人意犹未尽。另外，部分支线任务的设计略显敷衍，比如“委托：失踪人口”的重复跑腿流程，浪费了“赛博精神病”这个本可以深挖的题材
总的来说，如果你钟爱开放世界RPG、喜欢深度剧情和沉浸式体验，且能包容NPC智能和部分支线设计的短板，2077绝对值得入手，它的夜之城和强尼·银手的故事足以让你忽略部分瑕疵。但如果是追求完美细节或快节奏战斗的玩家，可能需要降低预期——它不是“赛博朋克的终极答案”，但绝对是游戏史上最具话题性的“救赎之作”

This is a tough one to rate. Trying this 5 years after release, with hardware that allows me to experience it in path traced glory on a 4K OLED monitor, I did initially enjoy the novelty of looking at those neons at night and the way light bounces off of of high resolution skin textures. 

However, the game makes me feel awfully empty, and the world while big, is barren, with very little that can be done in it that isn't a subset of repetitive actions. Combined with the dystopian setting, and the game being pretty big, playing it feels.. lonely for the lack of a better term. 

I'm a sucker for large open world games and great graphics, so on paper this was supposed to be a win. But I find myself just not enjoying playing with it, not enjoying interacting with the world in its extremely limited capacity, or the few unique characters that last beyond specific missions.

Despite 5 years passing since launch, I still fell through the ground for the game to crash hours into my playthrough. Despite those same 5 years passing, and there being some more cars, weapons, it feels like the content added is fairly mundate, adding inconsequential type of novelty. I was able to make the world a bit more interesting with mods, as 5 years allowed the community to produce quite a bit. And while the most ambitious can add some things to do, they can't address the fundamental issue of how uninterractable and barren the world feels. 

The negative rating isn't a reflection of the bugs or technical prowess of the developers, which they have demonstrated. The game looks good and generally plays at a C+ reliability level. Totally acceptable if the game was actually fun. But most of it is doing the same few things slightly differently dozens of times. The big city serves little purpose beyond providing a distance you need to drive between places where you do those things. Interesting things happen just during finite missions, and then they end, and the world is unexciting again. If something happens, it's usually a one-time scripted event where you just watch it. There is a whole lot of filler to make the city appear like a city-ish, but you can't do anything with it.
And it leads to an experience that isn't particularly fun, and it isn't as enjoyable as the other large open world games that either add interactivity, or at least introduce pleasant worlds to make up for it. I don't hate this game - I felt indifferent and slightly more negative with each hour spent in the game feeling like more and more of a waste of time on something that didn't feel fun, and I will likely not complete the story, as it feels like too much commitment to something that surprisingly doesn't spark joy.

[h2]The Review[/h2]
The graphics are absolutely [b]peak[/b]. I already completed this game once on another platform in around 60 hours, but here I am revisiting it again on PC because it’s just that freakin' good. Seeing Night City with ultra settings is a whole different experience.

The level of choice right from the start is insane—you get 3 different life paths to choose how your story begins. The customizability is [i]ultimate[/i], and the photo mode is superb; I’ve spent way too much time just taking shots of the neon streets.

[h3]Why it’s a 10/10:[/h3]

[b]The Story:[/b] This game really shows you that life is brutal and not the same for everyone. There is no "perfect" happy ending here. I was honestly devastated at the end; I had so much hope about finding a cure, but it seems like in Night City, there just isn't one. It’s a harsh, beautiful reality.

[b]The Music:[/b] 10/10 punk vibes. The soundtrack is incredible, specifically [u]"Spoiler" by Hyper[/u] and [u]"V"[/u]. Whenever those tracks hit, the atmosphere is unmatched.

[b]Interactions:[/b] 10/10. The way you interact with the world and characters makes you feel like you're actually part of the city, not just playing a game. Truly immersive.

А потом пришёл Егор Васильев и лично испортил мне прохождение своей подачей на уровне "читаю вслух договор аренды". Ви по лору - наёмник из трущоб, циник, живёт одним днём. Фанатский проект по Сталкеру делают без него - подключу связи, сук надо давить, не допущу. Ancord просто ужинал в ресторане - выйдем поговорим. При этом сам выдаёт озвучку на уровне "мне позвонили в три ночи и я вежливо делаю вид что не спал". В голосовых сообщениях фанатам у него больше эмоций чем за всю игру. Может перед записью надо было его разозлить - результат был бы другой.

Чтобы ваши сотрудники могли спокойно ужинать в ресторанах. Чтобы фанатские проекты выходили без звонков с угрозами. Чтобы Паттинсон наконец получил нормальную озвучку без чьего-то одобрения. Это не отмена - это охрана труда.

Cyberpunk 2077 on PC is almost a masterpiece.

First off, the visuals are absolutely stunning. Night City looks insane—especially on a good PC. The lighting, reflections, and overall detail make the world feel alive and immersive.

Gameplay feels just right. It’s not overly complex, but it gives you enough freedom to play how you want—stealth, aggressive, or a mix of both. It stays fun without becoming frustrating.

The story is solid. Not mind-blowing, but definitely not bad either. It keeps you engaged, and the characters and choices make it worth playing through.

One thing to note—progression can feel grindy. If you really want to level up and unlock the best upgrades, you’ll need to put in the time.

Combat? No major complaints. Gunplay feels good, skills are fun to use, and overall it’s satisfying.

Bugs still exist, but nothing too game-breaking (at least in my experience). You’ll notice them here and there.

Overall, despite a few flaws, Cyberpunk 2077 delivers a fantastic experience. If you’ve got the hardware, it’s definitely worth playing.

为了通关这个游戏，我选择了街头小子开局，也刻意选择了隐藏结局，那便是以我残躯化烈焰。
自游戏开始，便向玩家抛出了一个极具哲学性的问题，那便是“当个小人物身上插满管子老死，或者成为大人物但只有几个月可活”这个选择看似艰难，不过对我而言，我则毅然决然选择了后者。
原因很简单，每个人对人生都有不同的看法，而我则认为，如果真的能够做到让世人记住我，记住我所做的一切，我的名声响彻天下，哪怕真的只有几个月可活，也依然愿意，不为权钱和虚荣的名利，只为让世人记住：“这个世界上曾有这样一个人，他叫V，即使他明白自己的生命即将消散，即使他明白他面对的是荒板这样手眼通天的势力，他依然没有退缩。或许是为了活命，为了完成兄弟杰克的遗愿，成为真正的大人物，或许是为了向这扭曲的资本主义世界宣战，他没有选择退缩，反而是迎难而上，只身闯入塔内，向敌人发起最后的冲锋”

赛博朋克2077为我们呈现了一个技官法团社会，以及绝望且窒息的故事，自序章结束，V重获新生后，主线的整体节奏都在给人一种压倒人的“紧迫感”那便是“如果我停下脚步，面临我的将会是死亡”
同时这隐喻了一种叙事，那便是万恶的资本主义社会，同样也在不断的为底层百姓制造“紧迫感”
“考不上高中就完了，考不上大学就完了，找不到工作就完了，挣不到钱就完了，不结婚就完了，没有生儿育女就完了”一切的一切，似乎都指向了某一样东西，那便是“钱”
然而种种的“要完了”本质上不过是这扭曲的资本主义社会刻意为人们制造的普遍紧迫感，当底层劳动者开始为工作奔波，当公司白领开始为人际关系彻夜难眠，当学校的孩子开始为学业感到焦虑，一切的一切都指向他们自己那不可预知的未来。
然而可曾想过，这一桩桩一幕幕，都不过是上层的资本集团和统治阶级，联合起来精心为底层人设置好的“运行程序”其底层逻辑仍是为了让人们“服从”且一切必须都要按照“他们想要的方式进行”自此，资本集团便开始了对底层百姓的系统性剥削，他们肆无忌惮压榨着底层劳动人民的血汗，歇斯底里的榨干劳动者最后一滴鲜血，最后再像垃圾一样无情的将其丢弃。
正如强尼·银手所说：“我目睹过公司夺走农民的水源，最后是土地，也目睹过夜之城变成了一台机器，用人们崩溃的精神，破碎的梦想，以及民脂民膏来做燃料，长久以来公司控制了民生，拿走了一切，现在就连灵魂也不放过”
在这样绝望而又充满希望的世界，不断的有人向残暴的统治机器发起冲锋，也不断的有人倒下，有的人死去成为了传奇，有的人活着但放弃了理想。倘若压迫依然存在，反抗则永远不会停止。

因此，结局的那一刻，我选择了冲向“太阳”
选择了只身一人冲向荒坂塔，即使我知道这么做意味着要被太阳“焚烧殆尽”即使冒着“很可能连灰都不剩的风险”我依然选择向敌人发起堂吉诃德式的冲锋，不为金钱名利，或许只是单纯为了活命，同时也是为了向世人证明自己的决心。

只有彻底的焚烧旧秩序，世界才能迎来新生

Karalho, que jogo em! Esse Cyberpunk me impressionou demais. Eu só instalei pra dar uma olhada, sem indicação nenhuma; a única coisa que eu sabia era da fama dos bugs e, na moral, mané bug o quê... jogasso da porra! Quem ainda tem esse preconceito pelos erros do lançamento, que já arrumaram quase todos, tá perdendo muita coisa. Você aí que evita o jogo só pela fama, faz o seguinte: só testa, porque é muito foda.

Eu comecei a jogar só por jogar. Já tinha visto o anime, mas não sabia que ele era baseado no jogo. De início eu vi semelhanças, mas pensei "ah, é só o tema futurístico", mas quando vi aquele desgraçado do Adam Smasher e aquele cromo o meu o seu o nosso querido  Sandevistan, nossa, ali eu me liguei na hora. Bater de frente com a Arasaka e sentir toda a pressão daquela corporação suja é outra pegada.

Night City é absurda de bem feita, o jogo é muito bem ambientado. Não sei se é por ser em primeira pessoa, mas eu me senti na pele do V como se fosse eu mesmo ali dentro, vivendo aquela merda. As escolhas de quem seguir, em quem confiar ou desconfiar... tudo é muito foda e parece que o peso cai direto nas minhas costas. Fora as sidequests que são sensacionais, com personagens muito marcantes e bem construídos, como a Panam, o Goro Takemura, a Judy, o River Ward e o Viktor Vektor, dentre muitos outros. E falando no Viktor, eu assumo: lacrimejei vendo a mensagem final dele, o cara é um pai.

Aquele triste fim do nosso querido amigo Jackie me pegou bastante, e o relacionamento com o puto do Silverhand então? O cara começou facilmente odiável e hoje, na minha opinião, eu (V) e o Silverhand somos a melhor dupla dos jogos. Finalizei minha primeira run com 60 horas, explorei bastante, fiz muita secundária e limpei o mapa, mas depois vi que precisava da DLC pra platinar e acabei desanimando. Mas hoje finalmente comprei a Phantom Liberty e vou rejogar tudo pra platinar esse jogo de vez. Night City é um caminho sem volta e enquanto você fica na dúvida, eu já tô instalando meu próximo cromo. Prepara o Sandevistan, foda-se a porra da Arasaka e nos vemos no Afterlife!

Short comment: I started playing Cyberpunk 2077 at the end of 2025. The game is very enjoyable, however there is a lot of room for improvements. The dark world in the game is very tragic, but also a good warning for possible future.

I would honestly score the game as strong 9/10 (Modded) and 7/10 (without any mods).
Huge thank you for CDPR for making ability to create mods, as they really help with minor inconveniences that Cyberpunk 2077 has.

My take on the game details:
Gameplay: 10/10
Graphics: 9/10
Performance: 8/10
Mechanics: 7/10
Main game finish time: ~ 340h (All gigs, all ncpd, cyberpsychos, exploration, main story (Temperance) + PhantomLiberty DLC (King of Wands))

Mods I used: Skip intro, Lizzy Braindances, Enhanced Romances, change of color for arms cyberware - we can say all are cosmetic, not changing gameplay. 

Detailed description(Contains spoilers):

Very interesting dark world scenario in possible near future. Multiple warnings and truths about possible dark scenarios with usage of AI, big corporations and people just trying to survive. It is still hard to believe that our MC dies no matter what, but the whole road to death of V is very interesting. The world is corrupted, twisted and basically all residents of Night City are evil, with maybe very few exceptions(like River, seems he was one of very few that actually were not bad).

When it comes to gameplay - it is really cool. Multiple interesting aspects, details, fun interactions. Multiple options for most of gigs. Fun action gameplay with a nice scenery to it. 
Graphically the game is pretty nice, with only some drawbacks, but it is for sure one of highest standards. 
When it comes to performance, the game has hiccups on my 12GB RTX2060 dual by Palit. Of course for enjoyment of gameplay I turned off unnecessary things like DLSS, raytracing and rendered native. Nonetheless with native rendering it was working fine with around 70fps, with AI frame generation using AMD FSR it reaches target that was interesting me of 120fps at most times, however as it is with frame gen - sometimes it creates artefacts. I wish the performance would be good enough to last at 100-120fps without AI frame generation, but nowadays engines it's quite hard to achieve. 
Game mechanics are pretty interesting and very likeable, with some exceptions. I really hoped that clothes and "legendary" items would prevail, but now I can see that the system lacked a lot of options and Damage over time was not actually implemented as long-time damage over time I always seek in games. Level scaling for statistic check is quite terrible in my opinion and should never be implemented. 

Overall I enjoyed the game, had a lot of fun with it and might come back to it to finish with other endings some time, try out new builds, enjoy graphics and sing pon pon shit. This game surely is one of a kind and honestly I am glad I did not play it at launch time, as I would not enjoy it as much. A lot as I see has changed, most of it for good - maybe except for some pre 2.0 mechanics. 

Tragic story in tragic city with tragic people and tragic outcomes, crime is everywhere, AI takes over the world behind the scenes, corporations treat people like crap, government treats people like crap, it is very relatable to Real Life 2026 and this game shows a good warning on what direction might all of this take.

That's all from me, see you around, chooms!

Cyberpunk 2077 Geschichten in einer Stadt, die nie schläft 

Dieses Spiel stand lange auf meiner Liste, und endlich habe ich mich nach Night City gewagt, eine Stadt voller Neonlichter, Nachtclubs und Menschen mit ihren eigenen Geschichten. Genau das hat mich sofort eingefangen.

Ich habe mich mit einem Verschwörungstheoretiker unterhalten, der mir seine wildesten Theorien erzählt hat.
Ein Buddhist hat mit mir meditiert, und plötzlich habe ich über die Endlichkeit des Lebens nachgedacht.

Diese Mischung aus Action, verrückten Begegnungen und unerwartet tiefen Gesprächen macht das Spiel für mich so besonders.

Night City fühlt sich lebendig an, überall passiert etwas, überall gibt es Geschichten zu entdecken. Mal ist es laut und chaotisch, mal überraschend ruhig und nachdenklich.

TLDR: Play if you want to experience the power fantasy of a professional mercenary fighting for their life in a bleak dystopia, with an amazing story that has some pacing issues

In this game you play as V, a mercenary who lives in a dystopian hellhole that is Night City, whose attempt at becoming a legend lands them in a whole lot of trouble. Your job is to fix that. The story is actually really well told, and you experience it entirely from the first person perspective and they put a lot of work into making it feel as immersive as possible. The writing of characters makes them sound like actual people, the factions feel believable and the slang actually feels natural instead of tacked on.

The world, as mentioned, is pretty damn bleak. Rampant capitalism has made most people miserable and everyone tries to find a way to cope. The game does actually do a great job at hammering that point home, sometimes a bit hamfisted, but often in pretty subtle ways. The first time I realized my apartment had a mandatory adscreen in the middle of the living area it started to feel a lot less like a home, and nobody will even comment on that. And of course violence, drug abuse and sexual exploitation is everywhere. 

There is however the issue that this world is also very "set". You are not going to fix that (spoilers I guess), fine, but you are also going to have very little to no impact at all. Tons of side quests give you all sorts of decisions to make with interesting moral questions to ponder, but rarely does this have any affect but a slightly different quest reward or an angry voice call afterwards because things ended in tragedy - there are no happy endings in Night City - that it feels like a follow up was missing or you are playing an abandoned storyline. Outside of quests, if you start running people over you might trigger the police in a GTA style star system of escalations, but remain undetected for a minute and things turn back to normal. Similiarly, you can gun down a group of thugs belonging to a big gang and nobody ever will care about that, with the gang behaving just as before towards you. So this game is more about the powerfantasy of the moment to moment gameplay.

And my God is that well done. You can play all sorts of drastically different builds, like a hacker that infiltrates hideouts and triggers the grenades carried by every enemy, some shotgun wearing juggernaut that guns everything down, or a cyber ninja who parries bullets. The game lets you try everything out to find your perfect build, and if you know what you are doing your late game V is going to feel like a demigod of Night City.

Before you buy though, there is one big issue, bigger even than the non-responsive world. At the release of the game, that would have been the technical state, but nowadays CDPR managed to fix it that it runs mostly stable - still, save when possible. Now, the main issue is the pacing.

The game is structured to work with quest chains, where the main story paths, the excellent DLC story and important side stories (like the ones of Vs allies) get tons of quests, and each finished one triggers the start of the next. That works like every RPG ever. What is different that the beginning of the follow up quest often happens after a certain amount of time. So you will crash through a gang hideout, extract some data, send that to Vs friend, they will say that this will take some time to look through and they will message you once they have something. You can do something else in the meantime, and granted, you always have a full quest log, your phone constantly gets bombarded with new quests to take. The issue is if you found what you were doing really interesting and would like to continue that questline. So you wait 24 ingame hours. You wait another 24. You do another gig or five. You look up the wiki and read that the next quest step should trigger roughly 24 hours later, but at this point it has been an ingame week. This gets frustrating, because there seem to be triggers for quest updates, but they only update one quest per update, so you are at the mercy of RNGesus that you can continue the quest chain you found interesting. There also seems to be some priority with the main quest chains, which makes sense, but also means you only get to see some cool side content you would have liked to see earlier only after the main questlines have been exhausted until the point of no return. Which usually happens in the first third of my runs. A certain character is waiting a long time in the Embers, tell you that.

This issue with the quest progression triggers has no clear answer. You'll find all kinds of theories on what triggers progression online, from restarts, to specific elevators to take, to just standing still next to water for 5 minutes. The Mechanicus ain't got shit on the Cyberpunk community when it comes to esoteric tech solutions.

Still, if you can deal with the fact that some quest chains will just have an inconsistent pacing, you are rewarded with an amazing - if depressing - story, superb gameplay and overall a unique cyberpunk experience.

犹豫了很久还是想写点东西，不是吹也不是黑，就是一个普通玩家，在夜之城晃悠了几百个小时后的一点感慨，文笔一般，想到哪说到哪，老哥们随便看看就行。
 
刚发售那年我就入了，说实话那时候的体验真的一言难尽，bug满天飞，优化烂得离谱，任务设计也很空洞，很多当初吹上天的内容根本没做出来，玩了十几个小时就扔库里吃灰，那阵子跟吧里老哥一样，骂过也失望过，觉得CDPR彻底辜负了这么多年的期待，好好一个赛博朋克题材，被做成了半成品，心里挺不是滋味的。
 
后来陆陆续续更了好多次补丁，我也没怎么在意，直到2.0版本和往日之影出来，被朋友拉着回坑，才发现这游戏真的变了，彻底脱胎换骨。现在再走进夜之城，霓虹灯下的街道、沃森区的混乱、太平洲的荒芜，每一处细节都透着一股颓废又绚烂的味道，车水马龙里全是赛博朋克独有的冰冷与疯狂，不再是当初那个空有皮囊的假城市了。
 
战斗系统重做之后可玩性高了太多，义体搭配、技能流派都有了讲究，不再是无脑突突突，潜行、黑客、近战都能玩出花样，不朽武器的养成也很舒服，不用再担心等级上去武器就废了。开车手感也顺了不少，虽然还是比不上专业赛车游戏，但在夜之城的高架上飙车，听着电台里的电子乐，那种氛围感真的拉满。
 
最打动我的还是剧情，V的一生太让人唏嘘了，从一个想在夜之城闯出名头的小混混，到被芯片缠身、命不久矣的可怜人，一路挣扎一路失去，身边的人来了又走，每一个支线都藏着小人物的悲欢。强尼银手从一开始的针锋相对，到后来的互相理解，甚至有点惺惺相惜，这种人物弧光真的很戳人。还有往日之影里的亚历克斯、李德，每一个角色都有血有肉，不是单纯的工具人，他们的选择、他们的遗憾，都让这个冰冷的赛博世界多了几分人情味。
 
中文配音必须夸一句，太地道了，街边混混的骂腔、公司高层的虚伪、街头艺人的随性，没有一点违和感，比很多3A的中配都要用心，沉浸式体验直接拉满。电台音乐更是神来之笔，不同风格的电子乐、摇滚，配上夜之城的夜景，有时候我甚至不想做任务，就开着车在城里乱逛，看着霓虹闪烁，心里莫名的安静。
 
当然，即便到现在，这游戏也算不上完美，偶尔还是会碰到一些小bug，NPC的行为逻辑有时候还是很僵硬，开放世界的互动性依旧比不上一些老牌大作，很多细节依旧有缺憾。但比起首发时的一地鸡毛，CDPR真的用几年时间一点点补上了当初的承诺，这种知错就改、慢慢打磨的态度，在现在的游戏圈里已经很难得了。
 
玩到最后，其实已经不在乎什么传奇不传奇了，V拼尽全力想要活下去，想要留住身边的人，可夜之城从来不会善待任何人，这里只有资本的碾压、人性的扭曲和无尽的遗憾。每一个结局都让人心里堵得慌，没有真正的圆满，只有无奈的妥协，这大概就是赛博朋克的内核吧，光鲜亮丽的表象下，全是底层人的挣扎与绝望。
 
几百个小时下来，有过生气，有过惊艳，更多的是感慨。这不是一款完美无缺的神作，但绝对是一款值得静下心来体验的游戏，它承载了太多人的期待与失望，也完成了一场漫长的自我救赎。如果你是刚入坑的新玩家，不用在意当年的节奏，现在的2077，完全配得上你花时间去感受夜之城的一切。
 
最后想说，夜之城永远没有英雄，只有拼命活着的人。致V，致强尼，致每一个在霓虹灯下迷茫的灵魂。

Honestly, I never review games. But given the amount of hours I've spent within Night City, I feel almost obligated. I played since launch, and personally I had no bugs throughout the entire playthrough, I finished the game, that was that. I thoroughly enjoyed my time and thought that would be the end of it. Well, I was wrong. It ended up being a complete masterpiece in my book.

Graphics wise, I have - by modern standards - a dogshit pc with a 1650 (I love you really). However, how a game this beautiful, diverse, vertical and detailed runs so well on medium settings is beyond me. It ran okay on launch and has since only gotten more stable.

The soundtrack in this game is insane. I'm not really referring to the songs on the radio, though I think they're pretty damn good too, but the ambient soundtrack is brilliant. If I ever put the Spotify playlist on, all of those songs have emotional nostalgic weight attached to them, because they play at such traumatic in-game events. Also I really enjoy the combat music, gets me super hyped.

On the topic of combat, I recall when the game released some reviewers not enjoying it. While I believe in 'to each their own' I couldn't really understand it. For me the gunfights are extremely satisfying, especially handguns, with most all weapons feeling really *punchy* when you fire. Melee has seen a massive improvement since launch and is as fun as the gunfights. However, I could never let go of my quickhack deck for a melee something more melee focused like a sandevistan, as I feel you're missing out on a massive aspect of the combat by not using them (quickhacks). Anyways, combat = awesome.

Story - what can I say. Story is phenomenal. Even in instances where the choices don't necessarily matter, you really think about what you want to say carefully. I honestly think the forced first person perspective really enhances this feeling of weight and immersion that you'd lose out on with the third-person so many are clamouring for (though I think it could be cool, first person really works well). By the end of the story, when making the final few decisions, I really sat with myself to consider what I thought was morally right, and as very few games have done that, it gets top marks in my book. Also the DLC credits roll had me feeling all types of complex feelings about it. 

I think since launch the devs did some good work towards immersion. Initially there wasn't a lot you could necessarily do to engage with the world, but they've since added in some stuff like being able to go to the bar and have a drink (animated). Do I think there could be more? Absolutely. Mods fixed that for me, added loads of immersion spots, being able to lean, sit, smoke, drink anywhere. For this I simply can't rate it too highly, as if it were great already I wouldn't have sought mods to fix it.

I suppose I should go into more detail as I already mentioned it, but yes, mods are pretty great for this game. Don't get me wrong, it's not competing with a bethesda title for the types of game changing/overhauls mods, but Cyberpunk has some pretty great ones. A lot of the gameplay ones I used altered things very slightly, as I felt the gameplay was already great and I had no real desire to change anything about that, except for adding in survival aspects like eating, drinking, sleeping and nerve (which gives you tremors/ptsd). Plenty of gooner mods too (a lot actually), but I think you'll find whatever mod you would probably want (except the third person mod, that's still super janky).

The performances of all actors are all solid. The weakest performance for me is Keanu Reaves, but I've never thought he was a particularly good actor. However, he grows on you, and he for sure has some great moments and monologues. One thing I noticed on my second playthrough that I did not appreciate enough the first time I played was the body language. This is where I think third person would take away from the performances. With your little optical eyes, you can zoom in at will, and you start to notice during conversations with NPCs their body language is as good as the vocals. Honestly can't think of another game that's done it this well. Maybe RDR2? But the difference here is there's never a set cutscene. It's all first-person, all the way through, the interaction with a random NPC will be as cinematic as the most climatic moments, but it just works so well due to the performances (and the script I suppose).

Last comment is the fashion aspect. It's good. I enjoyed it. Especially when they removed the classic RPG "wear the things with the highest stats" so you end up looking ridiculous. Also it didn't make a lot of sense that in a universe with cyberwear, completely cybernetic bodies, that the real defining from gunfire is a hi-vis vest. 

Really not sure what else to say. I like the shooting, I like the soundtrack, I like the story, I like the city, I like I can enhance the whole experience with minimal mods, and photomode (which I mentioning only now) is very well done.

Cyberpunk 2077 n’est plus seulement un jeu vidéo, c’est une expérience. Une plongée brute, violente et fascinante dans un futur où tout s’achète… sauf ton humanité.

Dès les premières minutes, Night City te happe. Pas juste par sa taille ou ses graphismes, mais par son âme. Chaque rue raconte une histoire, chaque néon éclaire une vie brisée, chaque quartier a sa propre identité. On ne traverse pas la ville : on la ressent. Rarement un open world aura été aussi crédible, aussi vivant, aussi oppressant.

Mais là où le jeu frappe fort, c’est dans son écriture. Loin des récits classiques, Cyberpunk 2077 te confronte à des choix moraux complexes, sans réponses faciles. Les personnages ne sont pas là pour faire joli : ils existent, avec leurs failles, leurs ambitions, leurs douleurs. Tu t’attaches, tu doutes, tu regrettes parfois. Et ça, c’est la marque des grands RPG.

Le gameplay, lui, s’adapte à toi. Tu n’es jamais enfermé dans un style. Hacker fantôme, mercenaire brutal ou stratège méthodique : tout est possible. Cette liberté donne une vraie sensation de contrôle, et surtout, elle rend chaque partie unique.

Et puis il y a cette ambiance… cette bande-son, ce mélange de tension, de solitude et d’adrénaline permanente. Cyberpunk 2077 ne cherche pas à te divertir simplement : il te marque. Il te laisse une impression durable, presque dérangeante, comme un bon film qu’on n’oublie pas.

Oui, le jeu a connu un lancement compliqué. Mais aujourd’hui, après des années d’améliorations, il s’impose comme une œuvre complète, maîtrisée et profondément immersive. Un jeu qui a su se reconstruire pour finalement devenir ce qu’il promettait : un monument du RPG moderne.

Cyberpunk 2077, ce n’est pas juste un jeu à faire. C’est un monde à vivre.

Cyberpunk 2077 — это одна из тех игр, которые прошли длинный путь от спорного старта до по-настоящему сильного проекта.

Сейчас это атмосферное, глубокое и очень стильное приключение. Найт-Сити ощущается живым: у каждого района свой характер, музыка идеально дополняет происходящее, а визуал до сих пор выглядит впечатляюще. Сюжет — отдельный плюс: он взрослый, местами мрачный, но цепляющий. Персонажи запоминаются, а выборы действительно имеют вес.

Геймплей стал гораздо приятнее благодаря обновлениям: стрельба, прокачка и импланты дают свободу в стиле прохождения — можно идти напролом, действовать скрытно или комбинировать всё сразу.

Да, идеальной игру назвать нельзя, но в её текущем состоянии это уже цельный и качественный опыт, в который легко залипнуть на десятки часов.

Рекомендую всем, кто любит сюжетные RPG с сильной атмосферой и свободой выбора.

好玩指数：80 / 100
作为非预购但首发入手的玩家，能明显感受到 CDPR 对赛博朋克世界观的巨大野心，夜之城的开放世界充满细节，大量带碰撞体积的小模型尽显打磨诚意。可惜早期发售的糟糕体验成了挥之不去的阴影，如今仍有不少根本性问题：剧情割裂严重，除了开篇的 “交易” 剧情，主线与支线、支线之间几乎毫无关联，NPC 也多是活在自己的 “小圈子” 里，缺乏深度塑造，更像只会回复单一对话的工具人。虽有遗憾，但并非全盘否定，它本有机会比肩《巫师 3》。若有折扣值得入手，DLC “往日之影” 更是绝对的必玩之作，完美弥补了本体的诸多短板。
 
Fun Factor: 80 / 100
As a day-one player (not a pre-orderer), I can feel CDPR's massive ambition for the Cyberpunk universe. Night City is packed with intricate details, and the countless small models with collision volumes show genuine care. Unfortunately, the disastrous launch left a permanent stain, and fundamental issues still remain: the narrative is heavily segmented. Apart from the opening "deal" quest, there’s little connection between the main story and side quests, or even between different side quests. NPCs feel isolated in their own little worlds, lacking deep characterization and coming across as mere dialogue tools rather than living characters. I have roughly 80~ hours on this game, coming from PS4 before moving everything over to PC. There are only a handful of bugs, but compared to 1.8.3 to current? It's so, so much better. 

The gameplay is much smoother and runs so much better. But that's not what I want to talk about.

When I first started playing this game a couple months ago, my first impression, upon completing the game, was that it lacked in the story. Going in, I was expecting anti-consumerism and anti-capitalism/corporation themes, and they are indeed there, but not the fore front. I finished the game, complained about it to my girlfriend, then came back and played a few more times, getting a few more endings.

That's when I realized what the game is also trying to point out. Yeah, yeah, consumerism narrative or whatever, but I don't mean that, I mean V, your player.

Post prologue, V has everything ripped from them. Closest friend, they had trust taken and broken, they died and came back and now are stuck with a rockerboy terrorist in their head that's trying to take over their body.

The game has an artificial timer for this, but this is important to mention, the gameplay not forcing this timer is probably the most important to me. As you go through Night City, completing jobs, finding friends, partners, even developing your relations with Johnny, it all sets in, "you're on borrowed time, how will you spend it?"

One ending, which I can barely consider it an ending as it is very abrupt (with the player's choice), you see everyone you met, rubbed shoulders with or were acquainted. Depending on the romance option you chose, they could be furious or broken. Friends torn inside, wishing things were different. 

Another ending, just, give in. Let the corporation win and what becomes of you? You abondoned everything you loved and had. In a sense, betrayal.

This is coming from a girl who came out of a really bad drug addiction and is just getting out of frequent suicide ideation. On surface level, this game asks, "what makes you human," but digging deeper, paying attention to your playthrough, you're asked, "if you're on limited time, you die next week, what do you do? Do you pretend things are fine? Prolong your life at the expense of others and the experiences around you, or do you leave everything behind, abandon it all; leaving behind scars, damaging the people you built community with?"

This game has many problems but its story isn't one of them. This game made me change my perception of what life is. From being nihilistic, hateful, I turned the spotlight and, sure some things didn't change but, my approach to life changed. There are a lot of things I could glaze this game for, a lot of themes I could beg and beg to become a reality. But the change that did happen, within me, I accept. This is a really, really great game. 20-50 hours per save gives you everything you need to experience this game in all aspects and I could not recommend it enough.

[h2]Look at my play time. I write this review with utmost confidence and personal experience. No BS included[/h2]

[h1] TL;DR - Just play it [/h1]

I played this game not long after its original release. Bugs, crashes and all. I still enjoyed it. The story was so different from anything I had played before, and the different builds I could use drew me in deeper. After diving deep into Cyberpunk 2077 and Phantom Liberty, I can confidently say this is one of best RPG experiences created. And with it's bad release, and fantastic comeback - that should be enough for you. 

[h2] Story [/h2]
The story is nothing short of phenomenal. What starts as a tale of survival, quickly evolves into a deeply personal journey filled with moral dilemmas, unforgettable characters, and choices that genuinely matter and change the outcome of the story. The narrative grabs you early and never lets go. It’s layered, mature, and constantly evolving based on your choices. Phantom Liberty elevates this even further with a spy-thriller twist that feels intense, unpredictable, and emotionally grounded. It injects a tense espionage storyline that perfectly complements the base game’s themes of identity and control. It throws you into a horror-type scenario that keeps your heart pumping towards the end, or throws you into emotional despair. Did you, or did you not make the correct decision? Johnny Silverhand starts off as an abrasive, self-centered arse. He is loud, reckless, and seemingly impossible to trust. He constantly clashes with you, challenges your decisions, and feels more like a curse than a companion. But as the story unfolds, layers begin to peel back. You see his regrets, his failures, and the ideals buried beneath all that anger. By the end, depending on your choices, Johnny can transform into something genuinely meaningful: a loyal ally, a voice of hard-earned wisdom, and even a friend. That evolution - from intolerable to unforgettable - is one of the most compelling character arcs in the game.

Night City itself is a masterpiece. It deserves its own spotlight. The world isn’t just big - it’s feels alive for the most part. Every district tells its own story through architecture, culture, and the people who inhabit it. Every alleyway, megabuilding, and neon-lit street corner feels handcrafted with lore and purpose. The world building is insanely detailed. From corporate power struggles to street-level desperation, making it feel like a real, breathing dystopia. Not to mention the views. I pressed F12 so many damn times in this city. 

[h2] Graphics [/h2]
Visually, the game is stunning. The neon-soaked skyline, dense crowds, and dynamic lighting create a level of atmosphere that few games can match. Reflective rain-soaked streets, to the glow of holographic ads cutting through the night. The game delivers a consistently cinematic experience. Whether you’re cruising through the city at night or exploring its darker corners, it’s consistently breathtaking.

[h2] Gameplay [/h2]
Gameplay wise, the freedom is incredible. You can approach situations however you want - guns blazing, swords slashing, stealthy hacking, or something in between. The build variety is where the game truly shines: netrunners, cyber-enhanced melee monsters, precision snipers - each playstyle feels distinct and viable. Experimenting with different builds keeps the experience fresh even after dozens of hours. Don't forget about the mods, either. I sunk an extra 500+ hours with mods added alone.

[h2] Endings - where your decisions matter [/h2]
And then there are the endings. There’s no single “right” conclusion - just consequences shaped by your decisions throughout the game. None of them feel like an afterthought. Each ending feels meaningful, emotional, reinforcing the themes of identity, choice, and sacrifice.

Cyberpunk 2077, especially with Phantom Liberty, has become the game it was always meant to be - and then some. It took some time for Projekt CD RED to live up to their promises for this game, but behold true beauty as of today. Definitely in my top 3 games of all time.

I think so much discussion at release focused on what a steaming pile of trash this game's code was that it distracted from both the good and the bad. As I finally visit this game with a complete playthrough well over 5 years later, with I suppose a good chunk of the problems fixed, I can weigh in objectively having never played this game at release time.

First, this game is still horrifically buggy. People who say that the problems have been fixed are grading this on a curve versus the original release. Leaving the room where I flatlined the voodoo guy via the blackwall, I would, for example, be frozen in place while crouching and scope focused while stepping on a bit of conduit on the floor. That simple movement is still unsolved in some cases is glaring. I'm not going to go through all the bugs, just that this is still at a point that the problems are completely immersion breaking and required me to redo from saves many times.

Secondly, Keanu Reeves is a horrifically unsuited for his role here. It was a cheap and tawdry way to promote the game to cast him as Johnny. Keanu excels when he can play someone who is completely overcome by awe (The Matrix) or a stoned idiot (Bill and Ted). These are some of my favorite movies. I don't hate him as an actor. But let's face it, he should be typecasted into a very specific kind of role which is not Johnny. Keanu Reeves cannot play an emotionally stagnant revolutionary displaced decades into the future. This role is much too nuanced for him, and his voice bits come off as overread and contrived in the manner of a high school theater production. It's embarrassing. This comes off to me as cheap PR that compromises the work. Which is sad, because there are many characters here that are so well acted and could have created a timeless emotive experience that was beloved as Skyrim, but they are overshadowed by Johnny's piss-poor dialogue reading.

Anyways, the game is good enough. Play it.

[b] Cyberpunk 2077 [/b] não é só um jogo… é quase um experimento emocional disfarçado de entretenimento. Tipo assim: o pão alimenta o corpo, o aço constrói prédios… e esse jogo? Alimenta suas crises existenciais enquanto você atira em gente aleatória.

Ele te joga numa cidade tão viva que dá até a impressão de que os NPCs têm mais rotina que você. E enquanto você tenta “viver” naquele mundo, percebe que, ironicamente, tá mais presente ali do que na vida real.

A gameplay funciona bem, nada revolucionário, mas o suficiente pra você sair causando o caos com um sorriso meio suspeito no rosto. Não é o foco, mas destruir coisas nunca deixa de ser terapêutico, né?

Agora, o verdadeiro golpe vem nos personagens. Eles não parecem personagens… parecem pessoas que fariam você repensar suas decisões às 3 da manhã. Você se apega, se importa, sofre junto e quando vê, tá filosofando sobre escolhas morais num jogo onde você também pode simplesmente sair dando tiro.

No fim, Cyberpunk 2077 é tipo aquela pessoa problemática que você sabe que não é perfeita… mas mesmo assim te prende. Talvez demore um pouco pra te conquistar, mas quando consegue, já era: você já tá emocionalmente comprometido.

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the best games of all time. It’s genre-defining in both its aesthetic and its story. As an ARPG with a full capital A. it gives you an immense amount of playstyle freedom in its action. You can be a stealthy rogue hacking everything, or a ruthless tank taking hits like it’s breakfast cereal. Or everything in between. That’s where the gameplay really shines, the sheer amount of customization in how your character works. It’s an RPG that becomes an immersive sim in its depth.

This is tied together with one of the best stories in video games, especially for a game with a fully customizable main character. My V felt like a real extension of me, and I got so invested in the story because of the choices V gets put through. That's set alongside not just one of the best main characters in all of video games, but one of the best secondary leads too, Johnny Silverhand, played brilliantly by Keanu Reeves. But don't sleep on the rest of the cast either. close friends who genuinely feel like they care about V. To ambiguous fixers and morally grey but necessary allies.

The world itself is stunning. It’s one of the best-looking games out there. There is not a single shot of the skyline that looks bad. It does cost your PC some performance, it's not a light game to run, but it runs well enough, even with full path tracing. The raw graphics are made even better by the art style, which the game nails to a T. Cyberpunk's aesthetic has never looked this realized. Everything, from cars and clothes, to buildings and weapons, fits perfectly. As a total experience of walking through a cyberpunk world, nothing beats Cyberpunk 2077.

I really recommend this game. I know the launch game had heavy criticism, and a lot has changed since then. Updates have improved it massively, and the Phantom Liberty DLC is a must-play, adding an amazing side story. It's grown into a game that defines its genre, puts CDPR among the best game developers in the world, and creates a world I simply won't forget. A truly amazing game.

This is a highly overrated game, essentially sci-fi GTA but worse.

I bought this game because I read reviews and comments that described it as an open world RPG; some people commented that it is "like a science fiction Skyrim." I spent 4 hours creating my character and going through the tutorial stage; after I got into the world and saw this game for what it really is it was already too late to get a refund (denied twice). So I played it some more to give it a chance.

This game is NOT an RPG. You are a pre-determined character that is just walking through a pre-set story on rails with a few possible different game endings. In one case I rescued an annoying monk from a gang who was going to give him cyberware against his wishes. I killed the gang to rescue him, and then he insults me saying I am worse than the gang members because I killed them. I immediately tried to kill him for insulting me like that, but the game wouldn't let me! I don't think this character is tied to a later quest, the game just refused to let me kill him because the game wants to force its morality onto you. The game is constantly pushing its moral message at you, your contacts always whine about you killing criminals and scum. Some cyber-freak could kill 20 people and then I go deal with him and he attacks me and I kill him. Then, my contact cries about it and harangues me. If this was an RPG, then I would be able to kill that stupid monk and I would just do missions for a different contact that appreciated my abilities. But this is not an RPG - you don't create your own identity, you don't make a character or even pick a name. You have hit points, you get to pick your appearance and you get to pick skills from a skill tree - that is not what it means to be a role playing game.

The world is boring and repetitive. It's just a sprawling city of closed doors with nothing behind them (well, you can't even open most doors or buildings), except a few areas that are defined for the mission objectives.

O pão é feito de trigo, o aço de ferro e carbono, Cyberpunk 2077 é feito de sentimentos. É pra isso que ele é projetado, te fazer experimentar (de forma simulada é claro) satisfação, medo, esperança, raiva, ódio, duvida, frustração e por aí vai. 

Na minha humilde opinião um bom jogo de mundo aberto deve oferecer ao jogador a chance de “viver” aquele mundo, Cyberpunk faz isso bem, a cidade é bem viva, causa uma ilusão competente de coisas acontecendo ao nosso redor e de que os NPCs estão seguindo suas rotinas. A gameplay é competente também e as armas são legais de usar, apesar de não ser o foco do game, sair explodindo as coisas é tão divertido quanto seria em um bom Far Cry por exemplo.

O roteiro é bom, é bem escrito, foge do clichê. 

Porém o verdadeiro ponto alto deste jogo são os seus personagens, os desenvolvedores capricharam tanto neste aspecto que eles parecem ser mais do que apenas “bonecos de vídeo game”, é quase como se eles realmente existissem, quando você interage com eles é tudo muito convincente, é como se eles realmente tivessem personalidade, sonhos, traumas e medos. E por consequência isso faz com que você se importe com eles e com seus destinos, e pense e repense suas atitudes e decisões. 

O jogo não é perfeito, mas é um produto ímpar na indústria, com toda certeza vale a pena ser jogado, talvez algumas pessoas precisem ter um pouco de paciência até serem fisgadas pelo jogo, mas valerá o esforço.

Моё мнение мало будет отличаться от мнения большинства.

Касаемо геймплейной составляющей, на мой взгляд ей не хватает сложности в прокачке. Да, безусловно интуитивная прокачка это хорошо, но игра не 13+. Ветки прокачки там легкие. Хочешь ближнее оружие - качай эту ветку, хочешь поливать врагов из автомата, превращая их в месиво из крови и внутренностей - качай эту ветку.
Возвращаясь к DLS, хочу сказать что там слишком много уникального оружия, тебе пихают его на каждом шагу. Завершил квест на 10 минут? Держи пушку. Зашёл в подворотню? Держи ещё пушку. Теряется уникальность каждого оружия и их ценность. Для получения оружия редкости "Культовое" тебе буквально ничего не надо делать.
Вновь к теме оптимизации, а именно дорог. Если едешь достаточно быстро, то машины просто перестают рядом с тобой появляться. Если это чинится наличием более мощного железа, то это ещё более странно.
Из плюсов могу отметить ошеломительную сюжетную линию, просто верх сюжета. Персонажи раскрываются отлично посредством дополнительных квестов. Ветка Джонни стоит отдельной похвалы разработчикам. Основной сюжет так же не подводит. Разнообразие концовок от самых простых до тех, к которым путь тернист и опасен. 
По механикам. Безусловный огромный плюс. Механики нетраннера, ближника, парня с особым пистолетом Джонни. Всё на высоте. Стрелять и кромсать врагов в любым билдом крайне приятно.
Как бы я не ворчал на оптимизацию, но графика тоже ошеломительная. Чего стоит задание с парадом, одним словом - рай для глаз.
На этом всё, не забудьте навестить Ханако в Углях ;)

Cyberpunk 2077 is an ambitious and unforgettable journey into a futuristic world that pushes the boundaries of open-world storytelling. Despite having faced a rocky launch, the game has grown into something truly special thanks to constant updates, improvements, and expansions that transformed the experience into one of the most immersive RPGs of this generation.

From the very beginning, Cyberpunk 2077 impresses with its richly detailed setting: Night City. This vibrant megacity feels alive, unpredictable, and layered with stories waiting to be discovered on every corner. The world design is outstanding neon lights, towering skyscrapers, hidden back-alleys, bustling marketplaces, and diverse districts all contribute to an atmosphere that truly makes you feel like you’re living inside a cyberpunk dystopia.

The narrative is one of the game’s biggest strengths. The story is deep, emotional, and filled with intriguing characters. Every major decision you make has weight — whether it’s how you handle a mission, how you approach a conversation, or how you shape your own version of V. There are moments of humor, moments of heartbreak, and moments of sheer intensity that make the entire arc unforgettable. Characters like Jackie, Johnny Silverhand, and Panam are memorable, and their personal journeys enhance the game’s emotional impact.

Combat is dynamic, fluid, and highly customizable. Whether you prefer going in guns blazing, using stealth tactics, hacking enemies from the shadows, or crafting your own cyber-build, the game encourages different playstyles and rewards creativity. The cyberware system adds an extra layer of depth  upgrading your abilities and modding gear feels incredibly satisfying, and it gives players a real sense of progression and personalization.

Even years after release, Cyberpunk 2077 continues to impress with its visuals and performance on PC. With powerful hardware, the game looks striking  detailed character models, particle effects, lighting, reflections, and atmospheric weather all contribute to making Night City feel breathtaking and alive. Night City’s ambient soundscape and soundtrack only deepen immersion, making nighttime runs through the streets unforgettable.

Side content in Cyberpunk 2077 is also worth exploring. From small gigs to long-form quests, you’ll find a variety of stories that can surprise, entertain, and even challenge you  sometimes even more than the main storyline. There’s always something interesting around the corner, and many of the side missions feel like fully fleshed out mini-stories.

Cyberpunk 2077 is not just a game  it’s an experience. It blends narrative depth, freedom of choice, stunning world design, and intense gameplay into a package that’s bold, thought-provoking, and incredibly engaging. If you enjoy games that let you dive into a rich story, customize your playstyle, and explore a huge, detailed world at your own pace, this title delivers on all fronts. It’s a testament to how far immersive RPG design has come.

大体给到9.4，神作的守门员水平。它的优缺点分明，都让人印象深刻。
印象深刻的优点有很多：世界观庞大真实，沉浸感和生活感极强；未来风景独一无二，路径一开每一帧都是壁纸；多选择多结局玩法能活跃人的思考，剧情逻辑经得起推敲；流派搭配自由、可玩性强；dlc水平超神，拉高了整个游戏的上限。
印象深刻的缺点也不少：主线过短，主要角色塑造仓促，主要剧情些许潦草；npc人机感强，和鲜活的城市氛围形成落差；没第三人称，影子和四肢的建模也很廉价；性内容在单薄的主线下，节奏安排的很不协调。
评价归评价，真正让我记住夜之城的是一句台词：“昨天你还在阴沟里泡着，今天整个城市都在你的脚下。”这是夜之城精髓的最佳概括。要么轰轰烈烈地活着，要么轰轰烈烈地死，虽然你知道自己随时会跌落谷底，但至少有一刻，你站上了山巅。

First of all I will mention my setup as for this game that is really important and it gives more prospective, processor i7-12700K, 32GB DDR5 @6000 CL30, nvidia 5060 TI 16GB, installed on a nvme drive. The game was run on 1440p with DLSS 4.5 forced with path tracing enabled and frame generation x3 for most runs.

[h3]Positives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]Well we have to start with the visuals, this game is extremely stunning with the visuals, on the first playthrough you will spend more time looking around than actually playing the game, it really dominates visually, especially with path tracing.
    [*]Attention to detail, you are going to notice it all over the place, especially small details that you would not expect.
    [*]The audio is the next thing that is also up there, and here the top place is for the prime example on how great it comes out when you get great voice actors, not to mention that the ingame radio has awesome songs, and the battle music really fits the whole atmosphere.
    [*]RPG elements are well made and balanced, you do get a bit overpowered but it fits the game lore perfectly.
    [*]Variety of weapons to use and there is something we haven't seen in other games, netrunning abilities, it adds a unique way of playing.
    [*]Map is big, with tons of things to do and explore, with many distinguish spots that look apart from each so you can feel that now you are in the different place.
    [*]A lot of vehicles to traverse the vast map, even though you have fast travel, you can use the auto driver feature to enjoy the scenery.
    [*]Many factions that are different in their looks, talk and way they react to you, each fixed in their own block with some overlaps.
    [*]And do not let me started with how many different unique characters you are going to meet in game, many are complex characters with twists.
    [*]Keanu Reeves - do I need to say more?!
    [*]Idris Elba - not as much bonding on the screen as Johnny, but he filled the role pretty good.
    [*]Story is great, it has all you need, ups, downs, twists, comedy, annoyances, rage, culminations, etc... it is nice that some choices do matter on the story.
    [*]You want to play guns blazing?! No one is stopping you, oh you prefer stealth, go ahead it is optimized for it, netrunning it more your thing?! Well you will be able to make some superb combos. I want to say, you can play any way you like there is no limit and the game is not hindering you if you do not play a meta build.
    [*]The game is extremely well optimized for fast pace movement and slow motion.
    [*]Multiple endings, each one being different and unique in it's nature, and the main thing that was a surprise, as I cannot recall the last game that had this, once you get to the ending you get to play a bit more afterwards to have that proper feeling that you reached the end.
    [*]I feel like this needs to be mentioned, as they are one of the proper good ones, the developers are CD project RED.
    [*]Modding!!! This is done pretty good, with full support on how to get into modding, so if you want to tinker around and learn to code a bit, it can be done, but it is easier to go on Nexus mods, and just download the ones that you like the most, more than 10000 mods available. ps You do need a an account there but it is free and fast to create.
    [*]There is a character creation, it has fairly good options to create unique looks.
    [*]Great option from the developers, you can enable mature filter and it will hide certain scenes and characters will have at least underwear, this is really good as without this you would not be able to stream on youtube for example many parts of the story for example. There is also an option to remove songs from the radio that are copyrighted.
    [*]Optimized for DLSS, FSR, XeSS, choose whichever based on which video card you have, you lose a bit of quality that you will not notice unless you are looking for it hard and in return you will gain a nice boost in fps ( depends from system to system and the ingame settings you are using ).
[/list] 

[h3]Negatives:[/h3]
[list]
    [*]It still has issues, none of these are game breaking in a sense that you cannot fix all of them by either restarting the game or reloading a save game. I did get 2 game crashes as there is still a memory leak issue, happens mostly if you teleport many many times in quick successions and once when I overdid it with forcing the mod to spawn more police. Sometimes your dashing will put you through the floor, sometimes kerenzikov will not work.
    [*]Have to mention this, there is a one big inconsistency with the story that bothers me, without spoiling it, you will figure it out once you replay it.
    [*]Many choices are there as props and have no impact, which is a failure in my opinion, you force me to react but I get nothing no matter what I do.
    [*]As mentioned above, attention to detail is always a double edged sword, if you add some things and then fail to make others that are expected to be working, not work... is jus disappointing.
    [*]Even though there is plenty of weapons to play with, it felt poorly optimized for this masterpiece, simple example once you find the one iconic that fits your play style that is the only thing you will use for, in some cases, 90% of the game. Weapon modding is also simplified, compared to how cyberware was done, this felt like -lets just add this as an option. Prime example - why give me a silencer for an AR or SMG, if you cannot use it as a stealth weapon, to hear it a bit less? To have a cooler sound when you shoot?
    [*]Takedowns could have been done better to add more variety.
    [*]You do get to create your own character, visually I mean, but it felt more of just being there as an option that leads nowhere as you do not get to see yourself at all, except at the endings.
    [*]This is a personal opinion based on very hard difficulty, but it is a bit biased as the playthroughs were consecutive, the fighting becomes boring because you do become too overpowered soon, especially if you explore around, it does fit the lore. I had to give myself additional tasks to make it interesting.
    [*]Some of the mods would be better if they were part of the game to begin with, once you add some of them you do not want to play it without them anymore. This is not a negative per say but more of a notice.
[/list] 

[h1]VERDICT 9/10[/h1]

Definitely a big [b]YES[/b]on this one, and by this one I mean both the main game and the phantom liberty, the DLC is a must, it not only adds to the levels and skills, but enriches the story on it's own, you do get a great storyception there that fits perfectly with the main game.

If you want a futuristic GTA like game with a great story and awesome characters, that lets you play however you like playing without punishing you for it, this is the game for you then. The story is rich and filled with everything you would like to see, if you were watching a movie, but here you play the main protagonist. This might be a spoiler but hopefully not a big one, for me personally, I liked that there is no happy end, that is a such a great curve ball from many other games, and it fits the whole futuristic grim dystopia.

Should you get this game if you cannot run ray tracing or path tracing?
-YES, you should, the game is visually stunning even without those enabled, and yes being able to run either adds more to the visuals, but it is not that you are missing chunks of the game.

If you need videos on how the game worked, looked, how the mods fit, look and work, you can check some of the videos on my profile, be warned for spoilers as they are part of playthroughs.

Que dire de Cyberpunk 2077 ? Beaucoup d'attentes pour ce jeu. Je ne l'ai pas encore terminé mais je peux faire le bilan suivant après plus de 80h :

- L'histoire principale se perd rapidement car il y a pléthore de quêtes annexes plus ou moins qualitatives. On est très vite sollicité sur des quêtes qui peuvent vous faire perdre le fil de l'histoire. Je trouve que le jeu aurait mérité d'être un peu plus condensé avec des quêtes annexes qui s'imbriquent dans la trame principale.

- Côté technique, le jeu est en QWERTY sans option de le mettre en AZERTY, en 2026...vraiment ??!
Le jeu a beaucoup de pop-in de textures lorsque vous conduisez même avec un SSD...ça se remarque si vous êtes sensible.

- La conduite des véhicules est très chaotique. Les voitures se transforment en véritable savonnette. Prenez uniquement des motos.

- Il y a beaucoup trop de menus/sous-menus pour les armes, objets, améliorations...

- Night City manque un peu de vie. On ne peut pas rentrer partout ni interagir avec tous les personnages.

Ca n'en reste pas moins un bon jeu avec ses défauts.

5+ years on from one of the most historically disastrous launches, Cyberpunk 2077 has become an experience that captivates and immerses the player in a world where nothing truly feels impossible. Not only is Night City itself one of the most fun game worlds I've ever explored, but the characters and gameplay possibilities therein give the game a sense of personality that keeps me wanting to come back and uncover every nook and cranny of it. I finished my first playthrough of CP2077 in a week and started a new one almost immediately - that alone should speak to how captivating the world here truly feels. This is not a game you play for only 30 minutes at a time.

The game world is so immersive, in fact, that while fast travel is an option, I'd sooner jump into a car and drive from point A to point B than use a fast travel point. And I can't say the same about a lot of other open-world games I've played.

Anyway, as far as the gameplay is concerned, it's heaps of fun overall. Being on my second playthrough at the time of writing this review, I've only barely scratched the surface as far as the build options at your disposal are concerned, and I'm looking forward to experimenting with many more different builds - I'm especially eager to try out a build that's less focused on direct combat. Now that isn't to say that the combat is bad - quite the opposite, in fact. It's all sorts of satisfying, especially once you settle into a set of perks and cyberware that synergize with your weapon(s) of choice. Prime example: blades + Berserk = *chef's kiss*.

Now the game does still have some intermittent issues - NPCs are proper idiots sometimes, models and textures have trouble loading, the game might crash outright - but in my experience, game-breaking bugs have been very few and far between all things considered. CDPR definitely did their best to improve the game post-launch, and improve it they did. It's arguably the redemption arc of the decade, and they have my utmost respect for it. In the relatively short time I've actually been playing it, CP2077 has already become one of my all-time favorites, and I expect it to be no surprise why that is the case.

Cyberpunk 2077. Dieses Spiel allein ist mittlerweile eines der tiefsten, emotionalsten und atmosphärischsten Open-World-RPGs, die ich je gespielt habe.  Die Spieltiefe ist irre: Jede Entscheidung fühlt sich wichtig an, die Konsequenzen ziehen sich wirklich durch die Story und durch dein Leben in NightCity. Die Charaktere? Absolut Weltklasse. Panam hat mich emotional so hart getroffen, wie es sonst nur ganz wenige Figuren in Spielen schaffen. Judy, Kerry, River, Takemura, sogar Rogue – die haben alle Tiefe, eigene Geschichten, Schwächen und man merkt einfach: die sind echt. Dass man mit manchen von ihnen Dates haben kann, zusammen abhängt, sie in deinem Apartment trifft oder einfach nur quatscht – das hab ich in keinem anderen Spiel so intensiv und glaubwürdig erlebt.  Und dann die Grafik… NightCity bei Nacht mit Regen, Neon, Ray Tracing und Path Tracing (wenn man’s hat) ist einfach atemberaubend. Es gibt Momente, da steh ich einfach nur rum, guck mir die Skyline an und denk mir: „Das ist Kunst“.  Update 2.0+ hat das Kampfsystem, die Perks, das Fahren und die KI so massiv verbessert, dass es sich jetzt wie ein komplett anderes (und verdammt gutes) Spiel anfühlt.  Kurz gesagt: Wenn du Cyberpunk 2077 damals abgebrochen hast oder es noch nie richtig durchgespielt hast – gib dem Hauptspiel eine echte Chance. Es ist kein Hype mehr. Es ist einfach ein absolutes Meisterwerk geworden, das einem unter die Haut geht.  10/10 für mich – eines meiner absoluten Lieblingsspiele und um es in Jacky Welles Worten zu sagen: NightCity ist einfach geil!

Даааа, игра меня морально выжала, как лимон. Бывает посмотришь сильный фильм или прочтёшь сильную книгу — и еще несколько дней перевариваешь финал, новую книгу начинать нет сил и желания. Так вот, в Киберпанке со мной это случалось несколько раз за одно прохождение. Еще даже не дойдя до титров, я несколько раз "отходил" и снова возвращался, потому что местные сюжетные линии - это не просто квесты, а глубокие, самодостаточные истории, оставляющие глубокий след.


​В игре запредельный нарратив, персонажи настолько живые, что их начинаешь воспринимать как реальных знакомых. Их мотивации прописаны с невероятной точностью.
​А геройский геймплей чудесно вшит в сюжет. Ты не просто "жмакаешь на кнопки", ты развлекаешься на полную катушку, и чувствуешь себя частью этого мира.
​Это очень хорошая реализация "живого города", затягивает, по крайней мере на меня это произвело впечатление.
​Да, в игре встречаются мелкие баги, но, честно говоря, мне было на них абсолютно пофиг, даже не буду ничего про это тут писать.

​Поскольку в душе я "игровой султан" и могу позволить себе "иметь трех жен" (в плане любимых франшиз), я влюбляюсь в этот проект и ставлю его на полочку своих самых любимых игр.
 Мои мысли по поводу геймплея слишком личные, чтобы расписывать их в деталях, поэтому рекомендую всем это прожить самому.
​Это одна из лучших нарративных игр с геройским геймплеем.

标准的CDPR式剧情驱动ARPG，强大的画面表现和电台音乐，配合上科幻大片式的演出，综合的视听体验能够带给我极其愉悦的心情。前70h的游玩堪称顶级，体验到这样一个经过用心构造的开放世界场景却不罐头，能看出CDPR[strike] 制作 [/strike]和[b] 后期 [/b]上的高水准。尤其值得一提的是，光线追踪和路径追踪在本作的发挥[b] 无与伦比 [/b]。

同时缺点显而易见：“开放世界宏大却不够成熟”，“游戏的种种细节、交互、UI以及引导，相当粗糙”，“大量支线无法通过有效的串联去服务于这个世界，让我感到遗憾和阻力”。而最重要的是，剧情上吸引力不够，也是我认为2077的最大短板：不可谓不好，但缺少了动荡和转折，”扣人心弦“更是无从谈起，这也直接导致2077在第一人称下的代入感和沉浸感仍远不及巫师三。

总之，这是一部[u] 非常好的作品 [/u]，槽点不掩光芒，仍有着巨大的潜力去挖掘和提升。

Three years ago, this game was a disaster, but today, after the 2.0 update and the Phantom Liberty expansion, it is a completely different product with great mechanics and a GOAT atmosphere. If you quit because of bugs back in 2020, now is the perfect time to come back. The new skill trees finally allow for real specialization because every point you spend actually changes how you move or fight, rather than just adding a tiny damage bonus. This makes every battle satisfying, whether you use a katana or hacking. The new cyberware system also limits how much gear you can install, which forces you to plan carefully since every choice has real consequences for your stats.
Night City is immersive with its neon lights, and the new Dogtown area is even better than the original districts because it is more detailed and packed with content, so it no longer feels empty. The story in Phantom Liberty feels like a political thriller with complex characters like Solomon Reed and Songbird, making every moral choice difficult and heavy. The improved AI and new police system make the city feel alive, as it now reacts to your actions in a logical and challenging way. On the other hand, driving is still not great because cars slide too much, which is frustrating during fast chases. Also, some side activities can feel repetitive after many hours. Despite these small flaws, the graphics look amazing with path tracing, and the deep story makes this one of the best action RPGs on the market, so it is definitely worth buying the full bundle.

There are few times in my life where I play a videogame that feels like it was made for me. Like some time traveller went back in time and made this game to show me something. 

SPOILERS AHEAD [spoiler]
The moment of epiphany came when I was doing the quest to find all of Delemain's vehicles. The 2nd part of the questline. Now I thought this was going to be some random completion quest, and at one point I even got so lost inside the air ducts of the facility I needed to look up a video to get me to the next room. When I got there, I was completely expecting to just kill the splinter personalities of Delemain and fix him, after all he'd been so good to me for the whole game. Saving my life, helping me get around, rewarding me for finding his splinter personalities; and that moment when I was driving into the slums and I heard GladOS on the phone I just burst out laughing because it, apart from the absurdity, brought back memories of Portal. Delemain's questline had been so memorable and I was so glad it was the first sidequest chain I did. 

So when I went into the reactor room, Johnny stopped me right before I got to the console. "Stop you idiot, you're gonna end up killing living beings!" (not verbatum) I stopped for a moment to think, well sure they MIGHT be sentient, but if so then so is Delemain, who is dying right now. Johnny then acquainted the situation to being a cab driver asking me to kill his kids, which made me think about it. The splinter personalities were calling Delemain prime their father, and with how realistic Delemain was, I would've believed that he himself could be a sentient cyber-lifeform. This caused a mental conflict that I didnt expect from this random sidequest I chose out of the 12 other options. Johnny and I talked for abit and then left me with the option.

I couldn't pass the skill check to compress the personalities into Delemain's code, meaning my only options were to A: Reset Delemain and possibly kill 8 people, or shoot the core and... what? I didnt know what breaking the core would do. Might kill him? Might free them? Might kill them all? I had no idea. This confliction was overloading my irl brain and I started thinking erratically, worried I would make the wrong decision in the long run, till eventually I just shot it. I didnt think at all I just shot the damn thing. 

Boom, the whole room goes dark. I am now hearing demonic screeching and roars from outside of the room. My first thought was "Oh fuck what kind of demon did I just release on this world." So when I ran upstairs to see Delemain's children driving around saying that they were free, I was pleasantly surprised. I asked Johnny what he thought happened to Del, and he told me one of the car stayed. The music kicks in and I slowly walk down to the car, already mind blown by the ending timing, scene, and just aura of the whole moment. 

I walk down to the car and get in to find Delemain inside, but not exactly, more like a new copy, completely reset. This moment brought me back to a youtube audiobook I listened to a LONG time ago, "What if The Enclave Survived in Fallout 76? - Episode 3 by The Omega Initiative". That story had a similar premise involving an AI dying but giving a smaller, reborn version of himself life as he dies. Not being reborn, but a whole other lifeform created. Now I had really only played Bethesda games so I was DEF not expecting this fckin sidequest to be this good, so when the car told me to "Drive V" right as the chorus of the background song started, my jaw was left agape. Completely brain melted levels of stunned. I had to literally step away from the computer and just take a breather for a minute cuz I had NEVER seen anything like this happen for an optional, easily missable SIDEQUEST. 

I had to quickly go to work for a couple hours afterwards. When I got back I started thinking again about the story. Just how blown away I was. Skyrim, Fallout 3 and Fallout 4 never did anything like this. Then when I was in the shower, pondering the story meaning, as one does in the shower, as showers are known to give a +10 buff to intelligence and philosophy; I realized what the story meant. I have 22 hours in the game, I have only completed the Delemain quest, the Tarot card quest, and the Main tutorial up to meeting with Takemura. And yet in this moment I think I understood what the main character's story is. At least, this far in. 

Cyberpunk's main character isn't V. It isn't Johnny. It's you. The player. 
When V was shot, he died, even by the doctor's accounts. Johnny himself has already died. His soul left this realm decades ago. Instead, what happened was this being, this form, capable of life existed, at a point where no one really inhabited it. This being (the main character) held the memories, body, and emotions of V, while also accessed and interfaced with the memories and personality of Johnny. Quite literally, two dead guys in his head, not 1. V's body is dressed up with mechanical and cybernetic parts already, to the point he's practically more machine than man when it comes to the physical, so perhaps it could be like Delemain's situation.

Delemain was being bombarded by his splinter personalities, fighting for control and to be free of him.
V is being bombarded by Johnny, fighting for control and to be free of him. 
Doesn't seem that far different. So what I propose is thus,
The main character is both V and Johnny, this new being born of the death of V and generated by the memories, personality, everything of both V and Johnny. The perspective of Johnny being the one invading the mind of the main character isnt accurate, Johnny IS the main character, the same was V is, the same way Delemain's GladOS car is still Delemain, the same way Excelsior(the newborn car) is still Delemain. The story isnt about Johnny slowly eating away at V's mind and taking control. It's about YOU, the player, this new being born into this world, living with the experiences of both V and Johnny. You are both of them. You are like Excelsior. Learning to live a life as both Johnny and V. The perception of Johnny taking control is just you adapting and understanding a different side of you, same as V. 

I mean think about it, there's definitelly been times where you've meant to say something ingame and it came out WAY different than expected. A residual of V's memories, his way of speech, his personality. On the other hand, you have Johnny, slowly integrating, being understood, becoming more you the way someone growing up becomes themselves, not over forcing it, but over slowly growing and learning what you want to be. The story is about YOU, the player, given a life in the world, with the memories of V and Johnny, and the body of V, choosing what you will do. You have two tarot cards you can't get from the connected quest, I assume because they are later in the story. The Devil and Judgement. Misty explains that these cards are on your "path to discover" and are not required to complete her quest. In Cyberpunk 2077, the Judgment tarot card represents critical reflection, ultimate consequences, and finality. It symbolizes reaping what you've sown, acting as a reflection of the player's choices and the end of V's journey. The story is about YOU, and your decisions. It's about what YOU will do in this world. What life you want to make. What choices you want to make. Resetting Delemain, or shooting the core. [/spoiler]
