Today, I finished [b] Cyberpunk 2077[/b] and its expansion [b] Phantom Liberty[/b]  on PC through the [b] Cyberpunk 2077: Ultimate Edition[/b]  package on Steam, and with a multitude of QoL, aesthetic mods and very extra content from a very passionate fanbase. It finished to near total completion, and it took a total of around 143 hours according to a tracker that may or may not have glitched out, or counted some dead time in a report screen; a total of around 96 hours, according to the in-game tracker, and a total of 66 hours, according to a very untrustworthy tracker in Steam.

When I first started my trek through the dark alleyways of Night City, all I had in mind were the initial horror stories of the initial release of the game, the constant advertisement of the massive star-power involved, and a vague idea of its shooting-oriented gameplay loop. 

When the city finally spat me out, forever changed, my mind reeled with much more: how much it meant to live through such a gorgeous, gorgeous experience; the constant musings and ponderings about philosophy, morality, and identity the many, many stories put me through at every step of the way; and an aching sense of loss for the fictional lives that passed me by, fully formed that I left behind.

Cyberpunk 2077 can be thought of as an open world first person shooter with very pronounced RPG elements, with a lot of mechanics, play-styles, sprawling choices and items galore that I will probably never experience fully, because I somewhat didn't care to.

The gameplay is snappy, emergent, at times simplistic, and not always fully functional, with the driving mechanics being a particular point of contention for most; the performance of the game in my admittedly medium-range gaming laptop was spotty at best, and highly crash prone; and a lot of its world-building elements wear their inspirations on their sleeves, most times fairly derivative, sometimes cliched, and at certain points bordering on rip-offs.

Yet, even as all these elements and problems in isolation paint a grim picture, the sum of its parts reaches higher highs than most games even aspire to, all thanks to the bow that ties around this mess of a box: its earnest, painfully real story, its charming dialogue and beautifully uneven delivery that definitely borders on Lynchian, and the most well-realized player characters, supporting characters, side-characters, and even background characters that any narrative can offer.

Particular praise must be offered to the impressive integration of its DLC expansion, Phantom Liberty, which almost (due to its two amazing bookending title and credits sequences) seamlessly integrates itself into the main experience with such finesse that I cannot imagine the game as a whole without it, telling a story of its own that complements the main one, if not, fully elevate it beyond its original scope.

After every unstable crash, after every frustration with some of its mechanics, after every odd interaction, glitch and immersion-breaking groan-inducing quirk in between missions, after every exhaustive nearly futile attempt to progress side content that failed to trigger over and over again, I somehow always came back, wanting, and hungry for more, feeling like I left a little bit of myself in it every day, a little bit of my thoughts, of my choices, my hopes, dreams and doubts. The game is not perfect, as hardly anything is, it's painful, it's frictional, uneven, persistently unsatisfying, sometimes borderline hateful, but it's also tender, sweet, sincere, cool, edgy and it's so much more, but more than all of that, it's alive.

The game is not perfect, but it's mine.

故事是真的牛，尤其是强尼·银手。​ 一开始觉得这哥们就是个自大狂，烦得要死。但玩到后面，特别是那些闪回任务，看着他挣扎、失败、嘴硬心软，你跟他的关系从互相嫌弃到有点儿惺惺相惜……写得太TM真实了。最后在油管塔顶做选择的时候，我真愣那儿抽了根烟。不是那种“选A还是B”的游戏选择，而是你代入V之后，一种无奈的、彻头彻尾的悲剧感。夜之城没有活着的传奇，只有死掉的和正在死去的，这味儿对了。

但是，这游戏骨子里的“赶工感”还是能摸到。​ 夜之城看着炫，能深度交互的东西不多，大部分店门都敲不开。开车手感像在开肥皂，首发时那堆BUG修了几年才算勉强能看。技能系统2.0重做后好多了，但平衡性还是一坨，后期过于轮椅，重复性的东西太多，后期实在挺无聊的。

它不是一个完美的、革命性的神作，CDPR当年吹的牛大部分都没实现。但它是一个好故事，一个你能记住很久的故事。​ 你可能会忘记那些枪的名字，但大概率会记得和强尼在坟头抽烟，记得杰克摩托车后座上的夕阳，记得朱迪潜水时那片冰冷的湖水。

Cyberpunk is an absolute masterpiece. I am glad that CD Projekt Red took the time to fix its bad launch, improve upon the systems, and add an amazing DLC story to this game. 

Night City feels like a living entity and one of the main characters in this game. The depressing, dystopian setting is well fleshed out and has enough detail and lore to feel like a real city. As I played, the cynical part of my brain drew parallels between this world and our own making it easier to imagine what events may have lead to such a society. It is an easy world to be immersed in, also thanks to the beauty of the visuals.

The characters really make this game and the setting backs this up well. Conversations in Cyberpunk are as smooth as can be and feel like genuine conversations with real people. It's not difficult to have empathy for a lot of the characters after experiencing the world they inhabit. The visuals enhance this. In some games, no matter what dialogue is being spoken, poor facial animations make it feel like you are talking to a robot and can break immersion. Not the case here. I know that I am going to miss those deep conversations with Johnny Silverhand. 

Gameplay has a lot to offer, there are multiple valid playstyles that can make combat engaging. I fell into the generic rifle character as I do so often, but caught a glimpse of the different, more creative combat options and may do a deeper dive into them on a subsequent playthrough. I played on the "Normal" difficulty and, to be honest, it was very easy pretty much the whole way through. I think playing on the more advanced difficulties may improve the experience by encouraging further exploration into the different combat and build possibilities.

The story is well done. I was engaged and motivated throughout to keep pushing forward, which again lends to the depth of the characters involved. I would recommend playing through each of the endings, as they all seem to reveal different information and I found them interesting enough to warrant running through the final mission multiple times.

The DLC, Phantom Liberty, is absolutely this game at its best. It improves on gameplay systems like introducing a separate skill tree for the relic. Dogtown as a location, I did not find as interesting as Night City, then again its 15% of the size so it was at an unfair disadvantage. The characters, story and endings to this DLC are a must see. Some of the best moments in the game come from conversations involving the new characters and debriefing the situations you find yourself in with Johnny. After each of the endings, there is a conversation with Johnny reflecting on the outcomes and decisions you made, and these were probably my favorite moments from the game.

Overall, definitely cemented as one of my favorite games of all time. Highly recommend, I think its worth the full price tag, although now its regularly on sale for less than $30. Play this game, you will not regret it.

cyberpunk is honestly one of those games that just pulls you in and keeps you there. the world is insanely in depth and night city feels alive in a way very few games manage to achieve. everywhere you go there is detail, environmental storytelling, conversations happening around you, and little moments that make the city feel like it exists beyond the player.

the attention to detail is one of its biggest strengths. from ads playing on buildings to unique interiors, npc routines, and the sheer verticality of the city, it creates this immersive feeling that you are part of a real place. the lively spirit of the world mixed with the darker undertones of corporate control and personal struggle makes the setting hit even harder.

interactions and missions are another standout. side quests rarely feel like filler and many of them have strong narratives, memorable characters, and meaningful choices. the writing carries a lot of emotional weight and helps build connections to characters that stick with you long after the mission ends. main story moments especially land well and feel cinematic without losing player agency.

gameplay wise the build variety, cyberware system, and combat approaches give you freedom to play how you want. stealth, hacking, gunplay, melee, or hybrid setups all feel viable which adds to replay value and experimentation.

as for flaws, the biggest one is performance demand. running the game at full graphical quality can be extremely taxing and requires strong hardware to truly experience everything the visuals offer. ray tracing, crowd density, and lighting all look incredible but come at a heavy cost performance wise. outside of that though the game stands incredibly strong.

overall cyberpunk is a 10/10 type experience and easily sits in a top 10 games list. the immersive world, detailed design, strong storytelling, and memorable missions make it something special and despite hardware demands it remains one of the most impressive modern rpg experiences.

你说它是个赛博朋克城市吧，它脏乱差，霓虹灯闪得人眼花，满大街都是广告和流浪汉。但你开着车在这城市里瞎逛，听着广播里的歌，看着路边形形色色的路人，那种沉浸感真的太强了。尤其是在下雨天开着车，车灯照在湿漉漉的地面上，那氛围感直接拉满。我经常主线不推，支线不做，就光开车溜达都能溜达一两个小时。

  剧情方面，蠢驴讲故事的水平还是在线的。
主线剧情不算长，但代入感很强。特别是基努·里维斯演的强尼银手，一开始觉得这老头就是个烦人的电子幽灵，整天在你脑子里哔哔赖赖。但随着剧情推进，慢慢了解他的过去，最后竟然有点舍不得他。那种“我命不久矣”的无力感和跟强尼之间亦敌亦友的感情，确实让人上头。好几个结局都让我愣在屏幕前好久，心里空落落的。

  至于职业和玩法，现在真的丰富多了。
你可以当个黑客，站马路对面把人眼睛都给他黑瞎了；也可以当个狂暴的肌肉猛男，拿把大锤子冲进去把敌人全砸成肉酱；或者当个来去无踪的忍者，拿把武士刀玩弹反。2.0版本更新后，技能树和义体系统比以前有意思多了，怎么搭配完全看你心情。

  当然，槽点也不是没有。
比如捏脸系统还是不够自由，大街上NPC的AI有时候还是蠢蠢的，穿模这种祖传艺能也还在。

  总结一下：
如果你是个喜欢开放世界、喜欢沉浸式剧情、喜欢在赛博朋克世界里当个雇佣兵干各种脏活的人，这游戏现在绝对值得入手。别犹豫了，来夜之城，找点乐子。

Cyberpunk 2077 es el claro ejemplo de una caída exagerada… y una redención bien trabajada.

El lanzamiento fue, sin exagerar, un desastre. Bugs por todos lados, rendimiento terrible en consolas, promesas que no se cumplieron y una ola de decepción que fue proporcional a las expectativas gigantescas que CD Projekt Red había construido durante años. El hype era inmenso: un RPG revolucionario, mundo abierto ultra vivo, múltiples sistemas profundos, multijugador futuro, expansiones varias… y nada de eso llegó como se había imaginado.

El multijugador prometido nunca se materializó. Varias ideas ambiciosas quedaron en el camino. Muchas mecánicas que parecían que iban a cambiar el género terminaron siendo más tradicionales de lo esperado.

Pero aquí es donde hay que reconocer algo importante: el estudio no abandonó el juego.

Con actualizaciones constantes, parches enormes y mejoras reales en sistemas clave como la IA, el combate, las builds y el rendimiento, Cyberpunk fue transformándose poco a poco en lo que debió ser desde el principio. La expansión elevó todavía más la experiencia, mejorando narrativa, misiones y profundidad jugable.

Hoy, lejos del caos inicial, estamos frente a un RPG sólido, con una ambientación increíble, una ciudad visualmente impresionante y una historia con momentos realmente memorables. Night City tiene personalidad, estilo y una identidad muy marcada.

¿Cumplió todo lo que prometió? No.
¿Se convirtió en el juego revolucionario que se vendió en marketing? Tampoco.
¿Es hoy un muy buen juego que vale la pena jugar? Definitivamente sí.

Cyberpunk 2077 pasó de ser una decepción histórica a un título sólido que, en su estado actual, merece un 8.5/10.

No es la obra maestra que nos prometieron… pero sí es un gran juego que supo levantarse después de caer.

Essa é a quarta ou quinta vez que finalizo a história principal de Cyberpunk 2077, agora no PC e já com 100% das conquistas em outra plataforma. Escolhi o caminho Nômade, que ainda não tinha experimentado, começando nas Badlands, longe dos limites sufocantes de Night City. A experiência mudou em alguns pontos, mas uma coisa continua igual: o quanto eu amo esse jogo.

O lançamento turbulento ficou para trás. As atualizações corrigiram boa parte dos problemas e revelaram o que sempre esteve ali: um RPG ambicioso, com uma das narrativas mais densas dos videogames recentes.

A estética cyberpunk me ganha fácil, mas o que me prende é a história, de um jeito quase desconfortável. Cada escolha muda o tom das conversas e, às vezes, destinos inteiros. 

Também adoro a liberdade de construir V como eu quiser, com árvore de habilidades, implantes e hacks que permitem distrair inimigos e causar danos à distância. Só as Neurodanças não me cativam tanto: entendo a proposta, mas acho que elas quebram o ritmo.

Night City é uma metáfora sobre como o capitalismo extremo corrói tudo. Relações viram contratos, pessoas viram produtos, corpos viram plataformas de upgrade. Dividir a consciência com Johnny Silverhand, esse “fantasma digital”, é um dos pontos mais interessantes da narrativa. Mais do que salvar a própria vida, a história fala de identidade, legado e do que sobra quando as corporações controlam até a memória.

Não existe escolha totalmente limpa. Sempre há consequências.

Ainda não joguei Phantom Liberty, mas isso deve mudar em breve. E, como sempre, não consigo me despedir de Night City. Algumas histórias são impossíveis de abandonar, e Cyberpunk 2077 é uma delas.

My 90 hours on record consist of a partial playthrough a couple years ago, and then a full playthrough that I just completed in Feb 2026.  I never played this game in its original buggy state.  

The original Deus Ex is on of my favorite games of all time, and I think this is a good game too, but it doesn't wear the same mantle in my book.  It has a fun combat system, good character skill and cyberware development, an interesting story, driving, shooting, sex etc. etc.  But unfortunately it feels like so much of the good stuff is squandered.

Perthaps Cyberpunk could benefit from more focus.  I'm not sure the open world structure really works here, because most of the world is not interactive.  It's more just to establish a setting and mood.  But I think the game could've used a higher quantity and quality of specific missions, because otherwise all the cool cyberware, perks, stats, and equipment just aren't fully utilized.  I mean, most of the combat involved seems to just be with random grunts hanging out in a back alley somewhere.  So a lot of it goes to waste.  There are a bunch of things you can buy like apartments and cars and clothes, but a lot of that seems fairly useless, too.  I really was craving challenging scenarios that would force me to make full use of my build, but they were rare.  Very unfortunate...

And there are parts of this game that just DRAG.  I appreciate some good roleplaying and interesting conversations between characters, but some of that was just excessive.  I mean, if I have to press X to sit down in a chair, and then press X again to stand up one more time, I'm going to sonic shock myself to death, I swear.  There are many, MANY segments that are basically just cut scenes, but where you are required to press buttons to "do things" that are not optional.  Very irritating, and makes the idea of playing through the game again unpleasant.  Towards the end of my full playthrough, I was really feeling anxious to just be done with the whole thing already.  I was getting tired of V falling to his knees to cough up blood, and tired of him and Silverhand bickering back and forth.  I think some themes in this game are just beat to death with a hammer, and it gets fatiguing.  There is a fine line between making something feel epic, and making it feel painfully prolonged.  

But I'm glad I finished a playthrough, and I tried a couple of the different endings (because I'm definitely not playing through again).  All in all a mostly fun experience but lacks certain qualities that could've elevated it to masterpiece status, and sometimes overindulges itself to the point of being annoying.

Jugué Cyberpunk (no pienso abreviarlo) allá por el 2020, cuando no me alcanzaba para comprarlo así que lo descargué de otro lado...El tema es que lo terminé en menos de 100 horas y lo había jugado muy por encima y aún así me había encantado, por lo que años después decidí comprarlo.
Hoy en día, este juego es completamente diferente a lo que fue. Gameplay completamente renovado, talentos más complejos, transfiguración, étc. Voy a tratar de dividirlo en 4 categorías:

Gameplay: Súper dinámico y con múltiples posibilidades. El juego te deja realizar misiones de la manera que quieras siempre y cuando logres el objetivo, por lo que las opciones son muchas, y eso hace que nunca te aburras y se convierta en una entrega rejugable. De las mejores cosas que tiene el juego. Mientras que a uno le frito el cerebro sobrecargándolo con 177 terabytes de imágenes de furros, al otro le pego una piña con mis manos de titanio y con la otra mano corto con mi katana de acero vivo.

Gráficos: Está de más decir que este juego se ve hermoso, en especial de noche. Sin embargo, algo que me gustaría agregar es la optimización ampliamente mejorada que lograron. Hoy en día el juego es menos exigente de lo que fue en su salida, por lo que pude jugarlo a estables 60 FPS con unos gráficos muy buenos.

Historia: La historia principal tiene misiones muy largas, lo que compensa su poca cantidad (unas 30 aproximadamente). Sin embargo, es muy atrapante desde el principio y te deja con ganas de más. Cuenta con múltiples finales basados en tus decisiones, lo que, nuevamente, lo hace rejugable. (Y hagan cualquier cosa menos juntarse con Hanako en Ambers)

Música: No sólo cuenta con unas canciones buenísimas, si no que el DLC metió una radio nueva que se convirtió rápidamente en mi favorita. Canciones memorables, bandas como Samurai y Us Cracks con temazos, artistas ficticios como Kerry Eurodyne o Lizzy Wizzy que tienen buenas canciones, y mucho más. Tanto el soundtrack en si como las canciones son espectaculares.

Para finalizar, Cyberpunk es un juego altamente recomendado y es un MUST PLAY hoy en día. Quítense esa idea de la cabeza de que es un juego injugable lleno de bugs, porque si, vas a encontrarte algún que otro bug o glitch, pero es algo de una o dos veces, lo cuál considero que no afecta mi criterio en esta reseña.

Let me get this straight, you want me to tell you a review about this game? Whoever you are, you might as well go to the curators, because if you've come for a review on this game, you've come to the wrong place. However, if you have come for an outstanding chocolate chip cookie recipe, you've come to the right place.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt

Directions
1. Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)

2. Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.

3. Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.

4. Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.

5. Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.

For a Rocky Road Bar:
1. Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

Спустя 100ч игры решаюсь написать отзыв об одной из моих любимейших и первой полноценной купленной (после перехода на пк как платформу) игр, хотя я уверен, что не посмотрел и целую кучу оставшегося в игре контента, меня многое ждёт, но дабы не утратить свои впечатления и эмоции после игры напишу сейчас. Начну с плюсов игры, их очень много.
1. Джонни Сильверхенд. Одно большое лицо игры, честно, я думал что это будет камео или небольшой локальный прикол разработчиков, но Джонни просто колоссально меняет сюжет, Ви, тебя, как игрока и твои решения. Он способен развеселить тебя, выбесить, может понять тебя, ты можешь понять его, может подсказать, чтобы он сделал на твоём месте и ты понимаешь, что не враги друг другу, как это было в начале. Джонни - прекрасный персонаж, отчасти из за него я люблю игру всем сердцем, у него прекрасная озвучка(русская версия нравится больше оригинала), а самое главное его пиздатые фразы, какие из них стали мемами или просто разошлись по интернету? Единственное, что мы можем тут получить - это пизды, причем в плохом смысле. Сильверхенду как персонажу ставлю 10/10, лучший из лучших, он посылает нахуй всех и вся, взрывает здание арасаки и является просто пиздатым музыкантом и лучшим другом Ви после Джеки.
2. Мне очень понравилась концепция киберпсихоза и киберимплантов, нетраннинга - это та самая изюминка игры, отличающая ее от других коридорных ААА-стрелялок. Сандевистан, керезников, взрыв автомобиля или гранаты в руке, берсерк  - все это очень зашло и преукрасило динамичные и красочные перестрелки в игре. Киберпсихоз и отряд Макс-так вообще отдельная, но очень интересная тема, местный отряд киборгов от которых бежит любая банда или армия (Баргест, например).
3. Это наверное самое пиздатое, Песий город и его лидер Курт Хансен.
Сама идея оппозиции, города в городе, НИЩЕГО города в городе, куда бегут все преступники, беженцы, бомжи и просто торчки Найт-Сити это просто охуительная идея. Прекрасный визуал города, недостроенные небоскребы, хаос, тоталитаризм, вечный голос Хансена в громкоговоритель, упоминающий последние новости и правила города, рай для диктатора. К сожалению мешает любоваться красотами этого всего лишь ОПТИМИЗАЦИЯ ДОГТАУНА. Это ОГРОМНЫЙ МИНУС - в один день с лучами я могу получить стабильный ФПС, а в другой фризы и просадки(особенно рынок в песьем городе это полный пиздец), в Найт - Сити на кольце смерти такого не было, все очень стабильно.
Курт Хансен - бывший полковник армии НСША, объявивший себя правителем боевой зоны вольного города Найт Сити, очень сильный, влиятельный и умный человек, с первой встречи ты понимаешь - он читает тебя насквозь, он действительно тот антагонист, перед которым страшно, у него ебнутый взгляд и сила, сцена в казино, когда он опознает Ви как агента ФРУ просто до мурашек.
4. Саундтрек, здесь буду краток. Сделал множество скриншотов просто с названиями треков на радиостанциях, пока ехал на миссии, они ну очень кайфовые, да и игровой ост тоже пиздат, чего только стоит вступительная заставка с серьезным музлом погружающая тебя в какую то суетливую обстановку огромного города. За саундтрек ставлю также десятку.
5. ИМХО, достаточно приятная стрельба + разнообразие орудий, множество культовых вариантов( от забавного члена встанислава до кгб винтовки ноль-пять и дробовика Адама Смэшера), разные способности такие как пробивание стен у винтовки "Прорыв", Смартлинк и взрывные снаряды молота товарища порадовали. Оружие и стрельбу тут обожаю.
6. Город и Корпорации, лор игры. Полное погружение. Ты чувствуешь величественность города. Ты здесь никто, корпорации - это Боги. Тебя выебут и убьют на свалке - никто даже не вспомнит. Город давит на тебя, на твою уверенность и решения, по началу действительно чувствуешь тяжесть. Всем жителям города плевать на твое горе, ты здесь один наедине со своими целями и ты можешь умереть в любой момент(как основатель города Ричард Найт). Корпоративные войны, укрепление союза и распад США лично меня заставили заинтересоваться в лор игры, он необычный, изменён и этим устраивает. Не скажу прям, что это шедевр, но пойдет.
7. Миссии. Ты можешь участвовать в гонках, в соревнованиях по борьбе с ебучими кусками тестостерона вместо людей, будучи дохляком. Ты можешь исследовать затонувший город с любимой девушкой в гидрокостюме, а потом потрахаться, ты можешь разъебать на местном "танке" Василиске дикарей в пустоши с секси тяночкой Панам, тебя могут раздеть в переулке или трахнуть если ты женщина, ты можешь найти говорящий пистолет или автомат, можешь найти труп в холодильнике и тебе ещё и дадут пизды, если ты не успеешь его отвезти. Ну тут без комментариев, что что, а миссии в киберпанке это просто отвал башки, гта даже близком не стояла. Просто обожаю кп2077 за это.
8. Графика. Кратко: все последние технологии, трассировка лучей и пути и тд. Поэтому игра - бенчмарк. С трассировкой пути выглядит просто на отвал башки. Одна из лучших график, что я видел в играх.
9. Сюжет? Я прошел только концовку длс, к Ханако ещё не ходил, но +- знаю исходы некоторых концовок, за сюжет не скажу, дополню рецензию чуть позже.

再说游戏本身，五年前的游戏时至今日优化仍然一般，不至于浓屎一坨但也说不上多好，大地图打开帧数经常暴降，挪动视角有时也会暴降还有各种奇异卡顿，而且画面始终像是糊了一层灰，有种雾里看花的感觉，只有在每次打开拍摄模式的时候拉高对比度才得以窥见真容，暗部观感最是操了他妈，我一开始玩盗版的时候就是因为做了德拉曼支线末尾被公司里黑到死妈的路恶心一个多小时直接头晕恶心得下机卸载，入正后学聪明了先打了个手电筒的mod这才得以坚持玩了下来。驾驶手感也是死爹烂妈级别，放方向盘一扭就开始打圈，但愿你妈大批一扭也会跟着转圈圈🤣。 我承认cdpr对这座城市倾注无数心血吹毛求疵的设计确实让我大为赞叹，无论是抬头可见的高楼交通，还是地上垃圾罐头，种种看得见或看不见的细节造就了这方空前或许绝后的世界。当我放下委托专心漫步在集市道口的时候听着街边商贩叫卖以及看到霓虹灯彩炫目真的会有那么一瞬间代入进去，或许这市井乡气确实适合我。
  
 接着讲往日之影DLC，这个我个人感觉按整体来看的话还算值这个钱，不过也没有大众吹得那么神乎其神，可能是因为我先打出来的高塔结局。我一开始走的是李德线，这段玩的更是倍感恶心，跟条蛆一样被大机器人撵来撵去抓到就被剧情杀毫无还手之力，躲来躲去给我打得全程心率没下去过，你妈臭逼听到机器人噔噔声就蛆着猫起来不敢露头。结果这傻逼机器人最后死的时候还不能让我亲自下手处决它更是一拳打棉花上真他妈憋屈我真是操你妈的cdpr。我没有杀百灵鸟，我下不去手，她苦苦哀求我的时候我真的天真地希望她能活下来，于是我把她交给了迈尔斯，交给了新美国，新美国答应会治好我的病。
      
 结果出院了之后物是人非 ，我昏迷了俩年，我也丧失了改变这一切的力量，我想打电话给帕南，米契告诉我最好别联系她，话语中似乎另有深意；我打电话给朱迪，结果朱迪已经结过婚了；罗格也不待见我，不希望我拖着这副残废之躯去来生惹得人笑话；最后我决定回去找老维，见面的时候老维工作的地方已经被公司收了，穿着个不三不四的泽塔公司白皮看得我好陌生，没聊俩句来了个小鼻嘎找老维修义体，我看着那个新来的人和老维谈笑风生仿佛看到了从前的我自己，一样的年轻气盛大杀四方，但是我现在已经是废人回不到从前，老维给我诊断所有战斗义体都用不了只能回归普通人。出了老维诊所路边俩头野狗都能来踩我一脚了，还被他们给踢下楼梯，正好米斯蒂来了，她看着我跟我温柔地说：“欢迎来到平凡人的世界，V。”我难以言喻，我不甘心，我不愿就这样跟个废人一样任人踩头于是果断回档重打别的结局。
      
 这条高塔结局打完之后游戏体验过于死妈直接导致我拉低了对这个往日之影的整体评价我还是想说一句cdpr真是死妈了。
     
  回档到审判日这个任务，这次我选择了背叛李德拯救百灵鸟，一路的畅快杀敌，一路的无双清图，游戏体验比李德憋屈线好一万倍，我甚至还能动用黑墙的力量瞬杀面前所有敌人。结果在飞船前，百灵鸟跟我坦白她也骗了我，她自始至终就没有想过拯救我，她所谓的ai神经矩阵只能救一个人，那就是她自己。合着我跟头牛马似的替人办事办到最后还是一事无成，我仍旧得不到拯救。于是我把它抱起来送去飞船，这时候李德出现了，他拦住了我最后劝说了我一遍，那一瞬间我有那么一丝一毫的犹豫，毕竟一起奋战过，但是我没办法，我必须做出抉择，我必须他妈的在这俩人里二选一，于是我把李德崩了，我想看看后续发展。我当时就在想为什么没有全灭的选择，我给百灵鸟，李德，迈尔斯总统一人一炮全崩了，这些傻逼说白了没有一个是正常人，精致利己城府深、自欺欺人的愚忠、心狠手辣笑面虎，玩下来回想一遍居然只有汉兹先生最靠谱直接当场笑嘻。
      
  再次回档，我终于是站在了华子的面前，她想要让我投靠她，对她俯首称臣，我必然不愿意，我回到了米斯蒂的天台上，米斯蒂跟我说杰克以前也站在这里，站在这里跟他说他最大的梦想就是成为夜之城的传奇。我沉默良久，强尼说不如就让他跟我一起杀进荒坂塔，就跟他自己五十年前做的那样，我觉得这个比安生等死强。我回想起最开始那头三百斤黑胖问我的话，自问了一遍，我还是想成为传奇。
        
一路平推，亚当重锤也不过尔尔，我甚至刻意留了点时间跟它周旋，我觉得多少也算个大boss想给他点面子，不能死的过于草率。
         
最后，我杀到了神舆面前，奥特在我连进去的一瞬间剥离了我们，我看着神舆四周如梦似幻，奥特跟我讲有我没强尼，有他没我，这具身体只能负担一个人，又是你妈了个臭逼的抉择我真是操你妈了的cdpr。我选了我自己，奥特告诉我我只能继续活半年，我出去后这半年我活成来生的王，夜之城的传说，感觉有点理所当然以及意料之中。于是再次回档选了让强尼接管，我去到黑墙对面，看着强尼的视角。强尼在跟邻居小孩儿试音吉他的时候我听着，仿佛又回到了武侍乐队重组那一个晚上的激情澎湃，我享受着台下的万众瞩目，我张狂地拨动着琴弦，这一刻的心潮澎湃我难以忘却，迎着话筒我真的很想喊一句“我们永不消逝！”
     
  买完吉他我顺着强尼的视角去了墓地祭拜自己， 显然强尼也舍不我，自语道“我不会再走错了。“我们终是和解....慢步出骨灰龛的路上迎着夕阳，此时永不消逝的变奏适时响起，我不免心酸，我就这么平淡地落幕了。
    
 我自认为我算是沉浸式代入进整体游玩，这几天高强度推主线毫不夸张地说相当于活出了另一段的人生，我对这段人生抱憾许多，我想夸，更多的是想骂，它本应做得更好，它本应有皆大欢喜，它....或许遗憾总是贯穿始终。
      
  满分10分，本体6分 往日之影7.5分，综合评价7分，最后的最后，CDPR你死全家了，是你自己应得的。🤗

关于死亡、关于离别、关于权衡、关于情义与爱（有剧透）

赛博朋克不是我玩的第一部ARPG，却是玩法和剧情上我最喜欢的一部，尤其喜欢它沉浸式的美术风格、配乐、配音，多样的战斗系统，丰满鲜活有深度的角色形象，独具幽默或哲思意味的小短文和任务名，对话式的任务内容描述和电话短信系统很有代入感，高强度玩这部游戏的那段时间我好似短暂地脱离了现实世界的一切，真正进入了这个霓虹灯闪烁、有着电子樱花树的夜之城。

我享受游戏里v扬名立万的过程，一往无前仿佛能做到一切事情，我爱她的坚韧她的血性，钦佩她的百折不挠和理性，共情她最初如断根飘萍般的孑然一身，可能是我拖着太久没去见华子，那时我的v好像真的立于世界之巅，生杀予夺，我选择的流浪者身份则让她无所顾忌、没有牵绊而更加强大，并非命不久矣、苟延残喘。

所以v在我心里一直是来去如风的传奇形象，没有什么能够制约住她，直至必须要面对死亡和取舍，直至现实世界有珍视的人让她挂念，准确来说是让我挂念，在天台做选择时，以我之前玩类似游戏的性格，我一定会选独闯荒坂塔或是直接一死了之的选项，因为不想让任何人因我受影响、因我而牺牲，但以自杀去逃避太懦弱，我心里的v大概也不会做出这样的选择，Panam给出的如此有力如此令人安心的选择又恰好触动了我，同时也避免了跟公司做交易让johnny气得灵魂都爆炸^。一路玩下来的确是很温暖的一条线，对阿德卡多的想法也从一开始的轻蔑、觉得是在利用v赚好处，到在这个人心叵测的世界拥有了一个亲切的归属之地，尽管玩的是女v也没有让Panam和v之间的情感减少半分，反而会让我觉得这样的情义更加真心和珍贵。离开夜之城的路上，和Panam坐在车顶在星空下吹着夜风，仅剩的六个月也变得不那么惨淡和可悲了，起码当下，v依然能感知现实的一切，能在这短暂的时间拥有自由。

对于结局，我英雄主义病和骑士病爆发本来很想把身体让给johnny，并不是什么无私，是想让他带着有v的记忆一直活下去，一直记住v，对v愧疚，对v感激；当然这只是一部分，剩下一部分，我对这个一开始超级登味和大男子主义的角色在后期也产生了感情，随着剧情的推进johnny越来越能理解v，理解v的挣扎和遥不可及的理想，帮助v，到最后变成愿意为对方豁出去的那个人，所以在井口，看到甚至不为自己争取任何一句、v走到哪边就把头扭向另一边的johnny，在井里下落的过程中，我的泪水几乎是夺眶而出。

让v保留身体这个决定既有我对v的偏爱，也有对神舆之外的人的挂念，在做选择的时候突然想到，我甚至从没有机会和外面的所有人告别，对她们来说太残忍、也太不公平，尤其是Judy，v参与了她人生的诸多选择，改变了她很多轨迹，在云顶的幻想化作泡影后许诺了一个有她的远方和家，如果尚未让她知晓就蒸发于人世，又让她经历一次刻骨铭心的失去，甚至是不告而别，我无法设想这其中的痛苦，也不觉得这样的痛苦在她往后的人生能被治愈；Panam也是如此，她已经失去了部族了那么多如亲人般的存在。

赛博朋克极富魅力的一点恰恰是选择的现实性，没有客观意义上的好结局，没有两全其美，所以在做选择的时候我思考得很认真，总会权衡多方，但依然会为自己的选择给另一方带来的伤害而自责，或是因某个选择而出现掌控之外的事情而惋惜、后悔，比如动物帮的那个拳手，比如李德，比如那个狗镇新兵；然而生命也是如此，没有皆大欢喜的happy ending，关于死亡、关于离别、关于失去，一切的一切，不是争取或是不争取、不是无力、不是懦弱，遗憾就会成为遗憾，无论人生或游戏。

强尼在最后在井边对v说，“再见了，v，永远不要放弃战斗”，v再次站起了，再次面对了。

再见，永不消逝的夜之城传奇。

„Du … du bist ein guter Mensch.“

„Kannst du mit dem Sterben noch kurz warten?“

Zum zweiten Male jage ich dem Traum entgegen, endlich in die sagenumwobene Oberliga Night Citys aufzusteigen – eine Legende des Afterlife zu werden! Dieses Mal jedoch als weibliche V, natürlich bis an die Zähne bewaffnet; mit dicken Wummen, einem Cyberdeck, das selbst Bartmoss vor Neid erblassen ließe, Chrom bis zum Abwinken sowie zwei ganz sicher Lore-akkuraten, keinesfalls übertrieben großen, schlagkräftigen Argumenten zur Charismaerhöhung am Körper.

„A thing of beauty, I know“

Bereits im Prolog erhellen grelle Neonlichter die Szenerie, lassen mich deren Reflexion zusammen mit der fesselnden Geschichte immer tiefer ins Cyberpunk-Nachtleben eintauchen. Das gesamte Spiel über begleiten mich die zumeist fantastischen Licht- und Schatteneffekte, mit permanent aktiviertem Path Tracing natürlich. Selbst wenn die ein oder andere Textur von Nahem nicht den Erwartungen standhalten kann oder die Unausgegorenheit der Nvidia-Strahlen-Technologie mal wieder durchsickert, so zählt am Ende dennoch nur das Gesamtbild – und was für eines das ist!

„Will never fade away“

Night City fühlt sich gleich dreimal so belebt an wie früher, vor all diesen Patches. An dieser Stelle muss ich den geneigten Leser darauf hinweisen, dass ich „Cyberpunk 2077“ damals vorbestellt und direkt nach Veröffentlichung ruckelig, verbuggt und nicht ganz der Trailer-Grafik entsprechend durchgezockt habe. Dennoch hatte ich großen Spaß, musste für die Probleme jedoch einen Stern abziehen. Diesen gebe ich voll Wohlwollen nun zurück, mögen seine Strahlen sich in all den hübschen Glasfassaden und Pfützen auf ewig spiegeln!

„What you did to me, I know“

Abseits der Haupthandlung existiert so viel bedeutender Inhalt, sowohl kleine als auch sehr groß(artig)e Geschichten, wie schon in „The Witcher 3“. Allerdings empfinde ich eine noch etwas tiefere emotionale Bindung zu diesem Meisterwerk als zur Welt rund um V, Johnny, Judy und Co. Hier fehlt mir bei jedem der vielen Enden einfach dieses eine, dieses perfekte, dieses gewisse „Blood and Wine“-artige Abschließen, mit Augenzwinkern und echtem Happy End. Andererseits muss eine solch hochtechnologische Dystopie voller Unsicherheit, Elend, Abenteuerlust, Liebe und Arroganz dann gerade doch exakt dieses Gefühl der Unumkehrbarkeit, der Vergänglichkeit, der Leere und bittersüßen Erinnerung im Kopf der Spieler zurücklassen.

„Said what you had to say“

Schießwütig, blutlüstern und dennoch jederzeit zu einem netten Plausch bereit, cruise ich in jeder dicken Karre, die ich nur in die chromverstärkten Griffel bekomme, durch die Stadt. Dabei versuche ich, jeden Ort ohne Hilfe schon vor der jeweiligen Quest zu entdecken, an den ich mich aus dem ersten Durchgang vor Jahren noch erinnere. Ich besuche Judys Apartment, die Mox-Bar, den Plattenladen, den Totentanz-Club, das Red Dirt und natürlich die extrem gruselige Farm, welche mich fast schon retraumatisiert. All diese Orte und noch viel mehr bergen Erinnerungen, die ich nun nach und nach in den Nebenquests auffrische.

„But a thing of beauty“

Dass Johnny überall als grantiger, verbitterter, arroganter, egoistischer und dennoch zu jeder Zeit so absolut liebenswürdiger Sidekick auftaucht und zu allem etwas zu sagen hat, ist eigentlich ein sehr cleverer Erzähltrick. Auf diese Weise erschafft man sowohl einen Anker in der chaotischen Welt als auch eine Möglichkeit, das Erlebte ohne die videospieltypischen Selbstgespräche à la Lara Croft oder Geralt von Riva dennoch unterhaltsam zu erzählen und die Gedanken der beiden zu erfahren. Nach all den Updates des Spiels gibt es daneben noch so unzählige neue Textnachrichten im internen SMS-Netzwerk, die die Welt greifbarer und realistischer machen, dass ich gar nicht erst damit anfangen will.

„Will never fade away“

Meine liebsten Quests beschreibe ich aus Spoilergründen hier mal recht allgemein. Fast alle Handlungsstränge rund um die fantastisch geschriebene Judy, die ich dank weiblicher Spielfigur inzwischen endlich „näher“ kennenlernen durfte, sind auf jeden Fall in meiner Topliste dabei. Von Tauchgang bis Bordell und Snuff-Braindance ist das eine emotionale Achterbahnfahrt, die die arme Judy und V da gemeinsam durchleben. Auch die vorhin erwähnte Farm ist in der Liste mit von der Partie. Die besonders gute deutsche Synchro tut dann noch ihr Übriges, das Gesamterlebnis aller guten Quests noch eindrücklicher zu machen.

Was letztendlich bleibt, ist ein grandioses Open-World-Erlebnis voller schwerer Entscheidungen, bewegender Momente, äußerst realistischer Charaktere, actiongeladener Schusswechsel sowie einem schmauchgeschwängerten Hauch von Anarchie.

Cyberpunk 2077 is still, to this day, the best story-driven single-player game I have ever played. It perfectly matches my personal taste in every possible way — the atmosphere, the characters, the music, the worldbuilding, and especially the futuristic tech-driven setting.

Night City feels alive in a way few games ever achieved. The fusion between humans and technology, cybernetic enhancement, and the idea of identity in a digital future fascinates me deeply. While the game shows the darker consequences of such progress, the core technological vision feels incredibly believable. With today’s rapid advances in AI and brain–computer interfaces like Neuralink, it sometimes feels less like science fiction and more like a possible preview of our future.

I still remember starting the game back in 2021. That first playthrough left a lasting impression on me, and since then I’ve returned to Night City multiple times. Every playthrough reveals new emotional moments, new perspectives, and new reasons why this world stays unforgettable.

Cyberpunk 2077 became one of those rare games I never truly leave behind. Like the classic “owning GTA V on every platform” meme — that’s basically me with Cyberpunk. If a platform exists, chances are I own Cyberpunk 2077 on it. It’s more than just a game to me; it’s an experience I keep coming back to.

For me personally, Cyberpunk 2077 is simply perfect.

Five years after the launch of the game, after the big hype and an overpromising marketing campaign, followed by general disappointment reverberating through the Net once the game hit the shelves, I decided to plunge into Night City and find out for myself is it really as bad or as good as some peeps are saying. Here’s what I think.

[h2] Preem Ride, Choom, or What I Liked About [i]Cyberpunk 2077[/i][/h2]

[b]World-building and atmosphere.[/b] High tech and low lives, exactly as it says on the tin. Following the genre conventions, the world is properly harsh and grim, if not outright fatalistic. Technofeudalism, extreme social divisions and obsession with body modifications prevail throughout. You’ll be confronted with tough choices and their consequences will often burden your character’s conscience.

[b]Consistent tone. [/b] I remember being put off by the tonal inconsistency in [i]GTA IV[/i]. At one point it was a full-blown drama, and at another it introduced a character so cartoonish that they weren’t even funny. But it was a WINK, WINK parody of modern America, get it? In [i]CP77[/i], parody is still present (mostly in the in-world ads and commercials), but kind of reined in, at least for the most part. 

[b]Dialogues[/b] are usually very natural-sounding and have a nice flow.

[b]Things to do: there’s a lot. [/b] Main story mission + side quests + gigs (additional merc jobs offered by fixers in the city) + NCPD missions + DLC. It’s really fun when quests intertwine (e.g. events from one mission impact other missions or can be referenced in dialogues (and impact your choices). I also believe that side quests and gigs are often more interesting than the main story.

[b]Different ways to accomplish your goals.[/b] You need something from the building on the other side of the street. How are you going to get it? Rush in, guns blazing, slicing gonks left and right with your katana? Or maybe try to hack the back door? Or maybe go back to the street that runs above the building, jump down, and sneak in through the roof? All up to you. And again, I think that side quests and gigs offer the most freedom in that regard. Main story is more ‘cinematic’ and on-the-rails (worth mentioning that the DLC is more action-and-combat-oriented).

Last but not least: [b]Keanu Reeves[/b]. He really is breathtaking here, on top of his game. His Johnny Silverhand becomes a sarcastic, funny, and sometimes plain mean Greek chorus, commenting on your actions and choices. [b]Idris Elba[/b] shines in the DLC story. Lots of memorable characters.

[h2]You Have to Be a Gonk to Put That in the Game, or What I Didn’t Like[/h2]

[b]The world scales with your character.[/b] I hate that. You start the game and all the gangers carry tier 1 guns. Then you level up and so do they. Once a fixer rewarded me with an iconic weapon. It was waiting for me in my flat, in my personal stash. I click on the stash, and in the stash window it says ‘iconic, tier 1’. I put the weapon in my inventory, and now it’s tier 5, as I am on a much higher level myself. There was also this side quest that had three possible endings (depending on my decision). One of those required 17 intelligence (out of 20). At that moment in the game, I had 12 intelligence and 4 unspent points. No biggie, I thought. I backtracked to an earlier save, did some additional side missions, levelled up to 17 INT, and confidently came back to the same quest. Redid all of it, reached the conclusion, and now the third option required… 18 intelligence. Seriously?

[b][i]Borderlands[/i]-like itemization.[/b] You will collect lots and lots of trash. Dozens of items almost indistinguishable from one another apart from minuscule details. Gun A has 2.4 sec reloading time, Gun B has 2.3. For me, it was too much, and at the same time too little. I find clothes are even worse in this regard. You’ll find something like ‘Bulletproof hardened punk jacket’. But you’ll find ZERO information in the description about the jacket having any qualities apart from its look. Seems it has none. Lots of different designs with identical bonuses (+5/+10) or nothing at all. Shame.

In the world of [i]CP77[/i] [b]style is more important than substance[/b], or so we are told. Aesthetics is important. And yet, only the first-person perspective is available. So, you can play dress-up to your heart’s content, but you will only watch the effects in the inventory screen (TPP is available in driving sections, so you can catch a glimpse of V while they are entering the car, or getting on a bike). The choice of pubic hair or the size of your willy leaves me similarly lukewarm. It doesn’t really matter as you won’t get to see them ‘in action’ so to speak. It’s all LARP-ing, and there’s a lot of it in this game. (And no, I don’t find the photo mode the same thing as watching my character interact with the gameworld.)

[b]Driving[/b]. It can be a pain. It’s not terrible by any means, but not great either. Very much mediocre. This is partially caused by the very weak NPC AI. [i]CP77[/i] has nothing on [i]Mafia 1[/i], a game from 25 years ago. In [i]Mafia[/i], the city and the traffic were fully simulated. Cars followed traffic lights, you could even get a ticket for speeding. Not here. The shortcomings of driving in CP77 are accentuated by the autodrive function. Seems helpful but I’m not entirely sure how many times the gonk AI driver hit another car or mowed down some poor pedestrian.

[b]The open world conundrum.[/b] There’s no organic discovery of new quests. You get a map with every point of interest pin-pointed from the get-go (even if the nature of a specific quest is initially unknown) and you just hop from one spot to another. In other instances, you can get a couple of phone calls in a row form different characters, each dumping a specific task on you. Now, you can usually switch between quests, or postpone them, without any limitations, but I feel it all kind of harms the flow of the story. Compare it with [i]RDR2[/i], discovering locations bit by bit, and chance encounters on the road.

[b]Ludonarrative disonace[/b] observed in the friction between the main storyline – with its foundation in THIS VERY URGENT PROBLEM YOU NEED TO DEAL WITH RIGHT NOW – and the gameplay informed by the power fantasy of a merc making a name for themselves in Night City, levelling up, expanding operations, buying cars, renting additional flats. [i]CP77[/i] is not the first and not the last open world game guilty of it, and it’s not a terrible thing, but it’s there and you can feel it.

[b]Drive it and dump it.[/b] As the game progresses you become a proud owner of a growing number of cars and bikes. It’s a damn shame you can’t do anything with them (apart from driving, of course). I was hoping that a techie character could tinker around with vehicles. No such luck. You can’t even repair them if they get damaged. You just ‘call’ your car and it appears, all shiny and new, next to you. Often it’s just more sensible to leave the car, teleport somewhere via the teleporting station, and then call for the same car again, rather than struggle with traffic and subpar AI.

And last but not least: in the future you can install cyberware in your body, scan your surroundings, there are flying cars, cyborgs and braindances, and yet somehow… the civilisation of tomorrow lost the exquisite technology of making torches (flashlights). ‘Artistic vision’ they called it. And I say that’s just pure gonk.

[h2]Closing thoughts[/h2]

In the end my complaints stem from the fact that this game isn’t what it could have been. I wish this were the [i]CP77[/i] we got our first look on 7 years ago in [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vjF9GgrY9c0]that  trailer[/url].

Compared to that vision, even the latest version is still highly deficient. But even so, [i]Cyberpunk 2077[/i] is a massive, ambitious game with a moving story – a game most certainly worth playing.

A story that didn’t let go

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of those rare games that stops being a game somewhere along the way.
I didn’t just play as V at times, I felt like V. Every conversation, every pause, every quiet drive through Night City at night felt like it mattered. The characters aren’t written to impress you; they’re written to feel human. Flawed, contradictory, sometimes selfish, sometimes kind, exactly the way real people are.

What struck me most is how the game treats choice. Not as a power fantasy, but as responsibility. Many moments aren’t about doing the “right” thing, but about deciding what you can live with. The game trusts you with that weight, and because of that, your decisions linger long after you turn it off.

Johnny Silverhand is a perfect example. He’s loud, selfish, difficult and yet, beneath that, painfully human. Watching his relationship with V evolve, especially when neither of them chose the life they were forced into, is some of the most nuanced writing I’ve seen in a game. There’s conflict, but also respect. When it truly matters, they take care of each other in their own broken way.

For my V there’s Judy. She isn’t written as a “romance option,” but as a person - sensitive, stubborn, wounded, deeply human. Her care feels earned, not scripted. Being with her feels less like winning affection and more like sharing weight. The quiet moments with Judy, the texts, the silences, the way she processes loss they made Night City feel personal. She mattered to V deeply. Judy wanting to run away from NC with V feels so close but yet so far away, there are just few loose ends that have to be tied.

And Jackie… Saying goodbye to him never really gets easier. His absence is felt more than his presence ever was loud in El Coyote, in memories, in the version of the future that never happened. He was the heart at the beginning of the journey, and the city never quite fills the space he left behind.

Night City itself feels alive not because of scale, but because of atmosphere. I rarely used fast travel. I drove. I walked. I listened. The city breathes in neon lights, late-night music, quiet apartments, and moments of silence between missions. It’s a place that feels like it exists even when you’re not looking at it.

This game left me with a bittersweet feeling I’m still carrying. Sadness, warmth, reflection, gratitude - all at once. Very few pieces of media have ever made me think, late at night, “What would I do if I were in their place?” Cyberpunk did.
It’s not perfect. But it’s honest. And because of that, it feels like art.
Cyberpunk 2077 didn’t just entertain me.
It trusted me with a story and that’s something I won’t forget.

A Game That Truly Redeemed Itself
In my opinion, Cyberpunk 2077 will eventually be written into gaming history.
Its launch was a disaster — there’s no denying that. The technical issues, broken performance, and damaged trust were real. But what rebuilt my respect wasn’t the launch. It was what happened in the years after.

CD Projekt Red didn’t abandon the project. They didn’t take the easy way out. Instead, they kept rebuilding systems, refining mechanics, improving stability, and pushing the game toward the vision it was meant to achieve.

Now, Cyberpunk 2077 is no longer a “work in progress.” It has completed its lifecycle. It stands as a fully realized experience.

Night City feels intentional. The writing has weight. The characters leave an impact. The artistic direction is bold and distinctive.

Another thing I respect is that throughout years of public pressure and cultural debates, CDPR maintained creative independence. They focused on improving the game itself rather than constantly shifting direction to satisfy every external voice. They chose to protect the integrity of their work.

In today’s industry, studios willing to admit mistakes, invest years into fixing them, and stand firmly behind their creative vision are rare.

If there is a sequel in the future, I will choose to trust them again — and I will gladly pay for it.

Because when developers truly care about their craft, players can feel it.

Act 1 of this game is a total drag and made me put off the game. However, after picking up the game again and pushing through the lackluster beginning, the rest of the game is pretty alright. It's a fun enough game that took me a little under 90 hours to nearly 100% complete (including the DLC). 

I play games for the gameplay, and I thought this game was fun. I don't tend to do multiple runs on games like this, but I could see the variety of playstyles you could do in this game. I personally did a revolver/pistol focused build, and although it was a bit hard at first, it quickly became a cakewalk. The main things I didn't like regarding gameplay was the poorly designed bosses and the egregious lack of impact from choices both in story and the main game. Bosses are wave-dashing bullet sponges that are more annoying than entertaining, but there are only a few in the game so it doesn't matter much. The impact from choices was definitely the more annoying thing. I'd wager about 95% of the choices you make in story and sidequests don't actually affect the outcome. Most of the time nomatter what you do you will receive the same amount of money and nothing will actually change from how you approached the quest. I feel other open world RPG games like Skyrim do this better.

Story isn't a big factor on if I like a game or not, but I thought the plot was interesting here. The setup for the plot to actually start is quite bad though, and I wish they trimmed a lot more of the fat in the first act. When the story actually gets going, it ends up being enjoyable and it had me wanting to listen to extra dialogue options. However, I will say I feel like the game ends in a pretty underwhelming way both in regards to the plot and the gameplay.

TL;DR: After making your character, blitz through the first act. It's a lot of dialogue to sit through but 90% of it doesn't affect the story. From then on, have fun with the game and its open world, and don't worry about actually "finishing" since it's nothing notable imo.

Тем не менее со временем игра стала одной из моих самых любимых: я выбил все достижения и провёл в Найт‑Сити 171 час почти чистого удовольствия. Как так вышло, что разочарование превратилось в любовь?

 Изначально я думал, что Cyberpunk 2077 — это прежде всего про сюжет, но на самом деле мир и квесты понравились мне даже больше. Разнообразие билдов, видов оружия, веток прокачки и выборов по ходу игры заставляет по‑настоящему чувствовать себя героем этого виртуального мира. Ты погружаешься в целую вселенную, а Найт‑Сити затягивает так, что даже после финальных титров остаётся ощущение, будто сам побывал в шкуре Ви.

 Финал игры — это эмоциональный пик почти при любой концовке (ну, кроме той, где мы просто пускаем пулю себе в висок). Даже спустя часы после прохождения в голове остаётся куча мыслей и очень смешанные чувства. Джонни — спорный персонаж, но по ходу истории он, как и остальные, по‑живому меняется и адаптируется. Его линия с Бестией, на мой вкус, одна из лучших в игре. Финал, к сожалению, ощущается похожим во всех вариантах, даже с учётом DLC, но эмоций это всё равно не отменяет.

 Хочется отметить дополнение. В DLC снова крутые, живые персонажи, хорошо проработанная, хоть и не самая большая локация, куча квестов — как очень интересных, так и проходных. Появляются новые типы заданий вроде угонов, свежие импланты и ещё несколько печальных, но запоминающихся концовок.

 А что в итоге то?Cyberpunk 2077 для меня — шедевр и настоящий алмаз в игровой индустрии. Игра, которую когда‑то называли провалом года, в итоге выросла в почти идеальный action‑RPG и задала новые тренды во многих аспектах. Я искренне советую её каждому: такие истории, как здесь, в геймдеве встречаются единицами.

Cyberpunk 2077 entrega uma história que realmente prende. O arco do V com o Johnny Silverhand funciona muito bem, e o personagem do Keanu Reeves adiciona carisma e presença à narrativa. É uma trama cheia de figuras interessantes, conflitos pessoais fortes e momentos que dão peso às escolhas. A história é, sem dúvida, um dos pilares que sustentam o jogo.

Night City é outro grande destaque. A cidade tem personalidade própria, foi construída com atenção absurda aos detalhes e é extremamente imersiva. Andar por seus bairros, observar a arquitetura e absorver o clima geral passa uma sensação real de mundo vivo. Explorar cada canto é satisfatório, mesmo fora das missões principais.

O gameplay é sólido. O gunplay é satisfatório, os confrontos têm impacto e funcionam bem tanto em combate direto quanto em abordagens mais estratégicas. A dirigibilidade também é competente, tornando o simples ato de cruzar a cidade algo prazeroso. O stealth com hacking adiciona possibilidades interessantes, mas sem dominar a experiência. As skills são interessantes e permitem estilos diferentes de jogo, mas não chegam a ser o ponto mais forte do jogo. Os implantes acabam se destacando mais, trazendo mudanças concretas ao gameplay e se encaixando perfeitamente na proposta do universo.

As missões secundárias não chegam ao nível de The Witcher 3, mas ainda assim estão bem acima da média do gênero. No geral, o jogo passou por uma redenção clara. Eu já tinha gostado no lançamento, mas depois das atualizações e principalmente da DLC Phantom Liberty, a experiência ficou muito mais sólida. Ainda assim, o lançamento problemático nos consoles é uma mancha que provavelmente sempre vai acompanhar a CD Projekt.

S touto hrou se pojí velice osobní a důležitý příběh. Když jsem po deseti letech měnil svůj starej, rozpadající se stroj s dvoujádrovým Intel Core i-švecem, znějícím jako Černobylský reaktor za nový stroj, dlouhou dobu jsem přemýšlel, jakou hru mu dám ochutnat jako první. Po dlouhém rozvažování, stahování her, setupování atd. jsem byl nakonec přesvědčen jistým stalkerským sestřenicomilem, abych dal možnost Kyberpunči 2077 od Polského studia Kompaktní Disk Projekt Červená. Co následovalo se nyní pokusím za pomoci svého spisovatelského umu popsat, ačkoliv na některé pocity zkrátka nestačím.

Kyberpunč je, jak už sám název napovídá, zasazen do roku 2077. To je rok, kdy jsou Slizké Spolky Amerikánské ještě větší kokotporátní prdel, než v seriálu The Boys. Tyto kokotporáty válčí mezi sebou a způsobují, že si musíte platit v případě smrti Hrob Premium, bez protekce si nekoupíte ani tkaničku do bot a bez úplatku se nedostanete ani na WC. V čele těchto světospásných organizací stojí hlavně Japonský oligarcha Subaru se svým neposlušným synem a velkým mechanickým bodyguardem Adamem Drtinou, který říká na všechny lidi "Smash" a následně odmítá brát ne jako odpověď ve 150% případů. Kdo se tomuto odpornému balastu postaví?

No jedině vy jako hráč - Víčko, jemuž v cestě za dokonalou anarchií pomáhá i bývalá hvězda a hráč Těžkého Kamení a Mrtvého Kovu - Jan Stříbroruka. Spolu s ním projíždíte světem, hackujete co můžete, plníte kšefty a spolu zjišťujete, že když je někdo schopnej, tak možná celej ten svět není tak prohnilej a bez špetky radosti jak se na první pohled zdá. Když popáté začne týct kokotporátní krev, díky vašemu hackerskému umění si obludný kretén s rotačním kulometem vystřelí mozek z hlavy a to vše skončí u Cyberpunkových žen, které jsou všechny krásné, alternativní a velice dominantní maminky, člověk si až říká, že by v těchto rozbitých státech chtěl žít taky. V tomto hořkosladkém ráji jsem si liboval pět dní v kuse a často si i říkal, že jsem Honzíkovi šel v jeho plánech až moc "na ruku". Samozřejmě nemusíte mít stejný průchod jako já a může se vám líbit jiná úžasná věc co hra nabízí. Je toho víc než dost. Co už, aspoň zažijete jiný příběh a dost možná i lepší než co jsem já.

CDPR dokázali něco neuvěřitelného. Zatímco v roce 2021 si ještě člověk při projížďce Nočním Městem zpíval:

Postavy pohlaví vybral naruby,
je to prý známka Cyberpunku.
Divný voči a růžový zuby,
je to prý známka Cyberpunku.

...a chlámal se nad množstvím bugů, dnes je to umělecké dílo a jedno z nejlepších RPG na světě, které kvůli mně osobně bližšímu zasazení strčilo do kapsy i Zasírače 3. A to ani nezmiňuji skvělý špionský zážitek Dušanova Svoboda, nebo fakt že když se během příběhu a poslechu dokonalého soundtracku rozpláčete, budete na to mít absolutní právo. Dobrá práce Poláci, zase jste dokázali co západní slovanské národy v herním průmyslu dokážou :)

I jumped back into Cyberpunk 2077 and this game is wildly awesome. After all the updates, patches, and expansions, it finally feels like the open-world experience fans always hoped for.

Night City is one of the most alive, chaotic, and stylishly dystopian places I’ve ever played in. Every street corner feels like something’s going down, gangs, weird tech stuff, NPCs with attitude, and quests that actually surprise you. The world feels huge but focused, and exploring it never gets boring.

Combat is just as fun as ever. Whether you’re blasting through enemies with tech weapons, sneaking around with stealth, or straight up cyber-brawling, it all feels smooth and satisfying. The cyberware and build variety make every playthrough feel fresh, and there’s so much gear to find and craft.

The story is where it really shines. The main campaign and side gigs are packed with personality, intense moments, and characters you won’t forget. Choices actually matter — sometimes in subtle ways, sometimes in game-changing ways. The writing hits funny, dark, and emotional beats all in the same conversation.

And let’s talk about how much better the game runs now , way less buggy than launch. It finally feels polished and stable. The visuals are gorgeous too when you crank up the settings, neon everywhere, reflections popping, and the city feels alive at night.

If you’re into RPGs with freedom, style, and a little edge, this is a must-play. Cyberpunk isn’t just good now ... it’s awesome.

Киберпанк уже давно считается культовой игрой, но так было не всегда. В далеком 2020 году отвратительная оптимизация, отсутствие миллиардов обещанных фишек и баги испортили впечатления игроков. Тогда все кому не лень хейтили киберпанк, есть ощущение, что даже те, кто не играл игру. Хейт был от части заслуженный, потому что игроки почувствовали себя обманутыми, к тому же многие даже не смогли пройти нормально игру из-за тех же багов. Я лично столкнулся с багом в начале сюжета, где Джеки отказался выходить из здания мальстремовцев, из-за чего сюжет дальше не двигался. Пришлось переигрывать, ну это задание даже на высоком уровне сложности очень легкое, поэтому никакого неприятного осадочка нет.

Уже на релизе в игре было то, что никакими патчами не пофиксить. Я конечно же говорю про сюжет. Где-то через неделю после релиза я купил киберпанк в эпик геймс (мне было 14, прошу, пожалуйста, не осуждать аутиста) и я влюбился в игру с самого начала. Я не знаю, мне либо повезло, либо хз что, но тот баг, о котором я говорил, был единственным заметным багом, ломающим игру, все остальное время игра была идеальной. Это позволило мне погрузиться в мир и полноценно насладиться сюжетом. С тех пор я наиграл около 100 часов в эпик геймс и прошел игру пару раз, естественно, на разные концовки. Несмотря на нелинейность, сюжет очень последовательный, события исходят из других событий без каких-либо таймскипов, это не ломает темп, не дает заскучать, 20 часов сюжета ощущаются как 10. Хотя контента в игре намного больше чем на 20 часов. В сюжете нет глупых конфликтов, появившихся из-за недопонимания, нет даже главного антагониста как такового большую часть игры, есть только хорошо прописанная история. За персонажами и их взаимодействиями интересно следить, чего стоит только легендарный Джонни Сильверхенд. Киану Ривз оказался идеальным актером на роль Джонни, с ним Джонни получился очень харизматичным. Каждый раз при появлении Джонни ты ожидаешь какую-то забавную шутку, но получаешь только п*зды, причем скорее в плохом смысле. Простите, у меня не получается шутить так же хорошо, как у Джонни.

С релиза в игре есть и ее шикарный ост. Он в игре состоит из самых разных жанров, там вам и хард рок и поп и НУ И КАНЕШНА ЖЕ МНОЙ ОБОЖАЕМЫЙ PONPON SHI. Эти треки играют не только в особенных кат сценах, но и по радио во время езды по городу, как в гта, поэтому вы наслушаетесь их до дыр, КАК И Я НАЧАЛ ОБОЖАТЬ БОЖЕСТВЕННЫЙ PONPON SHI.
Купил шикарный музыкальный альбом, а к ней бонусом идет какая-то игра, пф.

Еще до патча 2.0 в киберпанке был шикарный геймплей, после патча он стал еще лучше. В основе своей да это просто шутер от первого лица, но все это разбавляют киберимпланты и нетраннерские механики. За счет этих механик у одних и тех же миссий появляются миллиард вариаций прохождения. Вы не просто можете пойти напролом и перестрелять всех или на стелсе обойти всех противников и добраться до нужного места, но и заранее обезвредить всех нетраннерскими способностями, киберимплантами превратить киберпанк в девил мей край и много чего еще. Прокачка в игре довольно простая, есть всего 6 параметров и у каждого свая ветка прокачки. На словах звучит страшно, но вы будете качать только то, что нужно вам, забив на ненужное.

Открытый мир интересно изучать, да и просто кататься по городу, слушая радио и PONPON SHI. Это, наверно, самая красивая карта среди игр в похожем сеттинге, я столько скриншотов наделал. Советую всем скачать мод nova lut. Этот мод убирает оригинальную цветокоррекцию, делает цвета в игре более натуральными, благодаря чему игра становится еще красивее. Редактор персонажа еще довольно неплохой, в нем даже можно настроить размер пип*ски. У женщины. В редакторе можно сделать по-настоящему «темного» эльфа или максимально girly девочку. Побочные задания не скучные, одно из таких прямо отсылает к аниме «Киберпанк Бегущие По Краю», это спин офф к игре. В нем Ви получает куртку протагониста бегущих по краю. В игре вообще много отсылок к спин оффу, [spoiler] например, можно найти дробовик Ребекки около башни Арасака, на месте, где была финальная битва в аниме. В Посмертии есть напиток под названием «Дэвид Мартинес». [/spoiler]

Ладно, аниме «Бегущие По Краю» это отдельный шедевр, заслуживающий отдельного разговора, тут не о нем.
Киберпанк 2077 игра не без минусов, моя главная претензия — это ее «нелинейность». На бумаге сюжет, конечно, нелинейный, ваши выборы даже на что-то влияют, но на практике не совсем. События действительно могут сильно поменяться в зависимости от ваших выборов, но глобально на сюжет они не особо то и влияют. Концовку вы выбираете сами в буквальном смысле. Не ваши действия влияют на концовку, а тупа финальный выбор перед самой концовкой. Не выбирать – это тоже выбор, поэтому в игре есть секретная концовка. Хорошо, что хотя бы для нее нужно сделать хоть что-то перед точкой невозврата. Кстати, о ней. Да, в игре есть точка невозврата, к которой вы можете вернуться и добить оставшиеся задания и ачивки, потому что игра заканчивается после финала, вы не сможете вернуться в открытый мир, как в гта. То есть учитывая все это, для прохождения на другую концовку вам достаточно загрузиться на точку невозврата и выбрать другой вариант в диалоге, а не перепроходить сюжет полностью. Хотя я бы не сказал, что это минус, просто в игре, где есть возможность выбора ответа в диалогах, ожидаешь увидеть реализацию, как в Detroit Become Human, а не как в геншине.
Теперь спустя столько лет киберпанк наконец-то починили. Хотел я так сказать блть, но буквально вчера у меня сломалась опять та же миссия с мальстремовцами, мне попался бессмертный милитеховец, который продолжал жить на 0 хп, хотя не стрелял больше. В этой миссии я решил скооперироваться с мальстремом против милитеха, поэтому мальстрем были моими союзниками. Перед этим бессмертным были еще двое неуязвимых, которые вполне могли стрелять в меня, но по ним урон не проходил ни из одного оружия, даже демоны на них не работали, я пробовал перегрев и замыкание. Это точно были враги, потому что в окне сканирования было написано, что они из милитеха. Мои союзники смогли их как-то убить, и я прошел дальше, тот последний бессмертный тоже не помешал успешно закончить задание, так что все вроде как норм. Эту миссию, судя по всему, геймдизайнил фанат «Неуязвимого».

Да в игре есть недостатки, но не существует идеальной игры в мире, все плюсы киберпанка перекрывают эти незначительные минусы, поэтому эту культовую игру должен пройти каждый.

赛博朋克2077的dlc往日之影的同名主题曲《往日之影》在游玩结束之后带给我了一段很长很长很长的后劲，整个dlc的体验是我近年来玩过的作品中剧情演出玩法给予我最为震撼的那一批。
一只囚鸟，一枚弃子，往日之影中的所有结局中没有真正意义上的好结局。
被心中的忠义束缚的李德，一次次想拯救身边的人，但心中的信念让他走在一条一步步麻痹自己的路上，他没有办法反抗自己，只能不断的欺骗自己自己的行为是为了身边人好，但他内心里也确实有着感情，才会去解释，对艾利克斯，才会纠结，对百灵鸟，才会故意在火箭前的桥上把枪举的稍微慢一点，对v。他对于国家的信念在赛博朋克这个崩坏的世界里是如此的可贵和难得，也为他被当做一个“弃子”埋下了伏笔。“他这样的人，即使活了下来，也只有自杀这一条路”。强尼在这个故事里也少了本体的许多轻佻，因为整个故事就是一个巨大的悲剧，他也才说出这样一句无奈的话。
将你带入这个故事的百灵鸟，是一只不断想用尖利尖锐但是弱小的喙撕破牢笼的囚鸟，她不断地设局，却让自己一步步越陷越深。李德曾说过百灵鸟精于算计却缺少大局观，但在v的视角下，百灵鸟的一切都是为了挣脱的无奈。她不断地增加着筹码，直到压上了整个自己。她无限的渴望生，渴望自由，于是她也开始不断地欺骗着身边的人，艾利克斯，李德，以及你——v，自由和生命占据了她的所有，但是内心的善促使她在昏迷前向你坦白了一切，并把最终的决定权就给了你。你会发现她并没有一开始想象中的坏，只是为了活着，生存，博得一丝希望。
往日之影最令我震撼和难以释怀的是主线，支线人物的塑造和无数的无奈以及纠结。
李德曾说过百灵鸟上了天只有死，跟着他走才能活着。你最开始以为这只是冠冕堂皇的话语，但随着你的调查，你会发现所谓的解药可能只是黑墙外的流窜ai的陷阱，百灵鸟上了月球可能真的不会如你，如她一开始想象中的那般。你发现李德是真的为了百灵鸟好，但他的忠诚却又与他的愧疚善良和对百灵鸟的情感剧烈冲突，百灵鸟的确是叛国了，叛国了就应该收到审判，李德直到百灵鸟回去之后不会有好下场，他只能欺骗自己能做些什么去改变，在航天港的楼顶，当新美国总统说出“是百灵鸟自己做的选择”后，李德试图去争辩“是你的决定还是她的决定”，但当总统反问一句之后，他心中的那些情感又被再一次的压抑。
所以我选择了送百灵鸟上天，百灵鸟可能确实会面临一些未知的危险，但她至少打破了这个牢笼，即使代价是自己的生命；李德也终于可以“静默”了，再也不用当那个被当做停火代价的“筹码”，再也不用去为一个只有自己相信的信条伤害身边的所有人，再也不用去考虑究竟该如何选择，如何权衡，去拧巴的过活
而v呢，还是那个夜之城活阎王，还是那个不变的v。狗镇的故事很精彩，何尝不当做一场幻梦呢，在一群间谍，政客，军阀，中间人的博弈中活下来，不是一件值得吹嘘的事情吗，而且，在观景台静静坐着，看着火箭升空，就像强尼说的“我们的小鸟终于自由了”，这不也是独属于夜之城的童话吗。一次能解决所有麻烦，再也无需烦恼一切问题的幻梦，终究只是一场幻梦，第二天醒来，还是要继续过活，毕竟，荒坂塔仍在那里，不是吗？
往日之影的设计密度，游玩体验丰富，文本量，演出量，以及大量的对于世界观的补充的设定，已经可以作为一部小型续作的体量。每一个支线都有独特的体验，就连最基础的偷车以及空投任务都有一定的设计，同时dlc伴随着2.0以及一系列大更新，重塑了整个2077的游戏体验，现在的2077，绝对是超一流的顶级作品

Cyberpunk 2077 hätte von Anfang an eine Legende werden können.
Die Welt, die Story und das Setting hatten das Potenzial, sich dauerhaft in die Spielegeschichte einzubrennen.

Doch der Release hat vieles davon überschattet. Technische Probleme und offensichtlicher Zeitdruck haben verhindert, dass das Spiel sein volles Potenzial direkt zeigen konnte. Ironischerweise passt das fast zu seiner eigenen Geschichte: Ein Spiel über übermächtige Konzerne, das selbst unter wirtschaftlichem Druck gelitten hat.

Fünf Jahre später sieht man jedoch, was wirklich in diesem Projekt steckt. Mit den zahlreichen Updates, großen Fixes und nicht zuletzt durch die Modding-Community ist daraus das geworden, was es ursprünglich hätte sein können: ein beeindruckendes, atmosphärisch dichtes Open-World-Erlebnis.

Heute erkennt man klar das Fundament einer echten Legende.
Ich hoffe, ein Nachfolger bekommt die Zeit und Freiheit, dieses Potenzial von Anfang an voll auszuschöpfen.

Cyberpunk 2077’yi ilk açtığım günü net hatırlıyorum. Karakter ekranında fazla vakit harcadım, sonra Night City’ye ilk defa gece indim. Arabayı sürerken camdan yansıyan neonlar, uzaktan gelen siren sesleri, kaldırımda sigara içen NPC’ler… O an “tamam” dedim, burası başka bir yer.

Bu oyun haritadan ibaret değil. Night City’nin bazı sokakları var ki özellikle gece vakti yağmur yağarken sadece yürümek istiyorsun. Görev yapmadan. Hedef kovalamadan. Sırf o atmosferi solumak için.



Bir görevden çıkıyorsun, çatışma olmuş, ortalık dağılmış. Mekâna birkaç gün sonra tekrar gidiyorsun ve hâlâ kırık camlar, sarı polis bantları duruyor. Bu küçük şeyler oyunun “yaşayan şehir” hissini güçlendiriyor.

Asansörle yukarı çıkarken şehir siluetini camdan izlemek, megabinaların içindeki o boğucu kalabalık, Badlands’e çıktığında gelen o yalnızlık hissi… Hepsi farklı ruh hali veriyor.

Arabayı sürerken radyo açıp şehir içinde amaçsız dolaştığım çok oldu. Özellikle gece sürüşleri ayrı bir his. O synth ağırlıklı parçalar çalarken şehirle uyum yakalıyorsun resmen.


Ana hikâye beni gerçekten içine çekti. Bazı görevler var, bitince 5 dakika menüye bakıp kalıyorsun. Özellikle karakterlerle kurulan bağ beklediğimden daha güçlüydü.

Johnny Silverhand mesela. Başta “tamam işte asi tip” diyorsun ama ilerledikçe karakterin altı doluyor. V ile olan diyalogları bazen gerçekten düşündürüyor. Sırf bazı konuşmalar için bile yan görevleri ağırdan aldım.

Yan görevlerin çoğu “git öldür gel” değil. Aralarında mini trajediler, ihanetler, garip dostluklar var. Bazı fixer görevleri bile ana hikâye kadar akılda kalıcı.


Ben ilk oynayışımda netrunner ağırlıklı gittim. Düşmanların sistemlerini hackleyip kavga başlamadan alanı temizlemek inanılmaz tatmin edici. Kamera zinciri kurup bütün binayı çöktürdüğüm anlar oldu.

İkinci oynayışımda blade build denedim. Sandevistan açıp zamanı yavaşlatıp 4-5 kişiyi saniyeler içinde indirmek… Gerçekten farklı bir oyun gibi hissettirdi.

Bu çeşitlilik oyunu tekrar oynanabilir yapıyor. Aynı görev bile farklı build ile tamamen başka deneyim.


Çıkış dönemindeki problemleri biliyoruz. Ama şu anki haliyle oyun çok daha stabil, dengeli ve oturmuş. Perk sisteminin yenilenmesi gerçekten oyuna nefes aldırmış; build çeşitliliği daha anlamlı ve combat çok daha akıcı hissettiriyor. Yapay zekâ da eskiye kıyasla daha tutarlı tepkiler veriyor.

Bir de şunu açıklığa kavuşturalım: Oyun uzun süre Grand Theft Auto V ile karşılaştırıldı ve bu yüzden ciddi şekilde aşağılandı. Ama herkesin bilmesi gereken bir gerçek var; eğer CD Projekt Red çıkış döneminde doğru adımları atabilseydi, Cyberpunk 2077 bugün GTA 5’i rahatlıkla mazide bırakabilecek potansiyele sahipti. Çünkü vizyon, dünya tasarımı ve anlatı derinliği açısından çok daha iddialı bir temel üzerine kurulu.

Cyberpunk 2077 kusursuz değil. NPC yapay zekâ bazen tuhaf davranabiliyor. Araç kullanımı her zaman mükemmel değil. Ama bütününe baktığında sunduğu atmosfer ve hikâye deneyimi o kusurları gölgede bırakıyor.

Bazı oyunlar vardır, bitirirsin ve uninstall edersin. Bu oyunu bitirdikten sonra şehirde bir süre daha dolaştım. Sırf o dünyadan hemen kopmak istemediğim için.

Night City soğuk, kirli ve acımasız bir yer. Ama bir şekilde insanı kendine bağlıyor.

Benim için kesinlikle oynanabilir, her kuruşuna değer bir oyundur.

/!\ Spoilers below the line /!\ (aaall the way at the bottom)

[h2] Main story [/h2]
The story took a long time to get to a point where you felt like you were actually playing a game. The first few hours, you're being railroaded until [i] the world opens up :) [/i].
Howeeeever, from that point onward the character you interact with most is the most insufferable piece of **** loser I have ever had the displeasure of meeting in any game ever. Any time I went anywhere, there was this worry in the back of my mind "what if [i] they [/i] show up again?.."
A friend tried to convince me this just meant they were a "well written character, if they manage to antagonize you this well", and that I didn't pay enough attention to get to learn the character better. I did try to get to know them though, I really did. They just kept proving again and again that they're not worth my time: if someone is toxic, I cut them out of my life. I gave this character way more chances than I would give anyone irl.

The story's pacing was out of whack. Especially near the end, everything felt like it got unnecessarily bogged down. There was one scene in particular, where you're in a flying car going up to a mega tower, and nothing is happening. The characters in the car with you do nothing. All you can look at is the bland interior of  the car or the black sheen of the ginormous tower next to you. This lasts miiinutes... Which btw, is right after you spent minutes mowing down a 'secure' complex which results in you getting a (supposedly) whole army looking for you.

Main story bosses sucked... Their main form of trying to damage me, was by running up to me and attempting melee. They all felt like a game of tag.
[i] Granted, my build was mainly sniper and basic cyberhacks; going up against speedy melees is not the most enjoyable nor exciting match-up. [/i]

[h2] The world [/h2]
The audio and visual design was great! But underused? Mismanaged?
Whenever I got to one of the main areas, I went "oooh, look at that, and this, and-wait that was all?" Every area that looks interesting when you first see it, felt bland within minutes.

For a game called "Cyberpunk" 2077, I expected the NPCs roaming the streets to look more... Cyberpunk~y? With a few exceptions, they all look like they fished one discarded piece of clothing from a rave and called it a day, at best.

[i] Also, why don't any of the cars have mirrors? [/i] I ended up driving around in a cute little car, because at least I could look directly behind me.
[i] (Yes, I know about the third person cam. No, I didn't use it. I like driving first person, thanks.) [/i]

[h2] Bugs [/h2]
The game is verified on StemaDeck: I was surprised by the amount of bugs I encountered on my Linux desktop. Just to list a few problems and oddities:
* When driving towards traffic lights, at about 25 meters in front of them, they switched from red to green or vice versa, [b] every. single. time. [/b]
* Cars floating.
* Cars appearing out of nowhere.
* Cars disappearing out of nowhere, despite my settings being set to 'far'.
* Finding occupied cars standing still in the middle of the road. When trying to cross, they somehow accelerated to full speed and hit me full on. After my character gets up, they magically disappeared, or exploded.
* MaxTac and the whole police force backing them suddenly driving off while I'm in an active gun fight with them.
* I also had this weird thing where a lot of exactly the same NPCs would be walking around. "Oh hey, theyŕe twins! Wait... Triplets? Quadruplets?? Quintuplets?! Okay, I give up..."
* Tech weapons being able to shoot through a 0.5 meter thick concrete support pillar, but bouncing off of a simple crate.
* People getting stuck inside me. (not in the fun way)
* Me getting stuck inside people. (also not in the fun way)
* There was this one side quest where I had to follow someone in a car. Although navigating the streets at high speed had been going swimmingly so far, this quest had cars spawning at max speed out of every intersection and as soon as our target was more than 25 m away, the quest failed because "we lost them"... I can see him driving right in front of my whatdoyoumean?!

[h2] Gameplay [/h2]
The cyberware mechanic was fun! Being able to equip yourself with different augments, possibly even completely changing your playstyle (e.g. by swapping to a different cyberdeck) was a nice option to have.

The combat felt very repetitive, despite me slowly gaining new skills from leveling up. This might've been down to my build and the stealth system being horrendous: I wanted to play a stealthy sniper, but:
1. There are so many cameras everywhere. Disabling them all every time got boring quickly.
2. Once I got spotted and 'in combat', it seemed like enemies know exactly where I am at all time. Unleeess, I completely leave the area...

There is one hacking minigame. Enough said.

I have no more posi-/negative to say about the gameplay. The rest of the mechanics (driving, shooting, dialogue, etc.) was what you would expect in a rpg: it's there, it works, it's nothing to write home about.

This game from the outside looking in doesn't look like anything special, but there aren't words to express just how much this title stands head and shoulders above any other GTA style open world campaign.

The storytelling alone could fill this review for enough words to make an English major blush. Me and a good few of my friends agree that there aren't many titles that have effected us emotionally like Cyberpunk has. 

The DLC Phantom Liberty is arguably more important of a purchase than the base game if that's even possible. The story is so deep and personal it will leave you watching the entirety of the credits as you are mentally taking in the experience you just capstoned. 

I'd love to tell you about the RPG mechanics of character building and how the implants open up new ways of combat, but being a netrunner is so damn fun it becomes a case of the Skyrim stealth archer build. Loading up an enemy in a room with a queue of malware just for it to spread throughout the entire building frying their cyberware is intoxicating.

The companions are so well written it will have you feeling and caring for characters on a level you didn't think was possible through a digital medium. The game touches on very human faults projected on to the exaggerated over the top backdrop of the neo-futuristic corporate hell-scape that is Night City.

If you care even an iota about storytelling in games I implore you to pick up the title and its DLC - Phantom Liberty.

TL:DR - Story is heart wrenching and probably (if not) the best story I've experienced from a game in my long history enjoying this medium. Also QuickHack-Queuing is super fun and highly recommended.

Depois de cerca de 7 horas jogando Cyberpunk 2077, ainda estou nas primeiras impressões, mas já dá para formar uma opinião inicial.

Visualmente, o jogo é impressionante. A cidade de Night City é extremamente detalhada, com uma ambientação densa e cheia de personalidade. A direção de arte é um dos pontos mais fortes — iluminação, arquitetura e estilo realmente criam aquela atmosfera futurista decadente que o jogo promete.

A história também parece interessante até agora. As missões têm boa apresentação, diálogos bem produzidos e personagens carismáticos. Dá para perceber que existe profundidade nas escolhas e nos caminhos que você pode seguir, mesmo que eu ainda não tenha avançado o suficiente para ver grandes consequências.

Por outro lado, a jogabilidade ainda parece um pouco inconsistente. O combate pode ser divertido, principalmente misturando armas, habilidades e hacking, mas às vezes a movimentação parece meio travada. A inteligência artificial dos inimigos também não é das mais impressionantes até aqui.

Em termos de desempenho, minha experiência nessas 7 horas foi relativamente estável, mas ainda notei pequenos bugs visuais e situações estranhas típicas de um mundo aberto muito ambicioso.

No geral, minha impressão inicial é positiva. O jogo claramente tem muito potencial, principalmente pela ambientação e narrativa, mas ainda estou esperando ver como ele se sustenta a longo prazo conforme a história evolui e as mecânicas ficam mais profundas.

因为鸣潮才去看的边缘行者，也是因为边缘行者才开始下载这个游戏的。看完之后好想哭，但是哭不出来，只觉得无力和空虚。露西在遇到大卫之前就想上月球逃离这个地狱一样的人间，而遇到了大卫之后她的梦想就变成想让大卫好好活着，即使把曼恩和大姐作为棋子，即使杀光所有尝试修复数据的黑客也要让他活下去。而大卫的梦想一直都是别人赋予给他的，直到遇到露西，他才意识到自己真正的梦想就是实现露西上月球的梦想。大卫经历了算计，抗过了义体金刚的反噬（这也是公司没想到的，本来只想等主角被军用科技打死或者被反噬死了之后收集数据，没想到玩脱了），就是为了救被卖回荒坂塔的露西，结果被亚当重锤杀死。即使露西登上了月球，心中也只剩下荒芜。

我不知道怎么评价边缘行者这部作品，大卫失去了家人，有了新的家人，最后逐渐失去了一切，包括自己的人性的部分让我最难受。它构建了一个纸醉金迷，资本至上，人命如同草芥的冷酷绝望世界观，即使你拥有力量，你能做到的只有逃离，融入，或者被资本彻底压垮，宛如蝼蚁的结局。而在这么冷酷世界观中，这部作品反而一直在展示爱，母亲对儿子的爱，大哥对小弟的爱，露西对大卫的爱，瑞贝卡亲眼看着大卫逐渐堕落依旧愿意陪伴他的爱。即使你失去了一切，包括人性，只要有了爱，就有意义，因为爱是最高规格的抑制剂。而我在大卫的故事结束的一年后，也要开始我在夜之城的崭新故事了

Cyberpunk 2077 is a game that has made me think long and hard about a lot of things. It's an incredible setting and a fantastically presented world. After the fixes they made to the game on release (which i had the privilege not to play), it feels smooth as butter to play, and it felt incredibly rewarding to master the game through multiple playthroughs.

To sing more praises, the phantom liberty expansion gave me a deeply rewarding story experience and an addition onto an already very fun game.

Unfortunately however, it does have its flaws, and to be frank near all of them have to do with the main story. I take issue with how the setup to the game, one where you're dying, is not at all conducive to an immersive experience if you want to go off and do side objectives. I also think that Johnny Silverhand is a misogynist who is never properly made to reckon with his actions, and particularly playing as female V, one of Johnny's quests later on (Chippin' in) feels immensely uncomfortable and violating.

Overall i'd say I'd recommend the game, but given it has flaws that are extremely difficult to ignore (given one of them literally lives inside V's head) i'd give it a 7/10 or so.
