O jogo ganha destaque no quesito gráfico, sendo um dos melhores até agora, na minha opinião. A história central e o desenvolvimento de personagens — tanto principais quanto secundários, inclusive o próprio V — estão entre os mais bem-feitos no mundo dos games. A jogabilidade é fluida e, em minha visão, atirar e explodir coisas nunca foi tão satisfatório.
Cyberpunk 2077 é, sem dúvidas, uma experiência muito boa na minha opinião, pelo menos no estado atual do game.

WARNING: If you have not played the game, [b]skip this review.[/b]

[h1] Cyberpunk 2077: An Elegy for the Parts We Leave Behind [/h1]

Playing Cyberpunk 2077 is the video game equivalent of finding a melancholic, half-remembered melody on a radio station that only broadcasts in the rain. It’s not about the hero’s journey. It’s about the erosion of the self, set against a skyline that gleams like a promise it has no intention of keeping.

For over 200 hours, Night City isn’t just a setting; it’s a state of being. It is adulthood rendered in neon and concrete: a system that asks for pieces of you in exchange for the right to keep living within it. You trade a piece of your morality for a fixer’s eddies. A piece of your loyalty for a temporary alliance. A piece of your very body for chrome that makes you stronger but feels less alive. You start with a simple goal to become a legend only to learn that a legend is just a story the city tells about people it has already consumed.

This is where the game, against all odds, achieves something profound. It is a western RPG with the soul of a bleak, philosophical novel. Its genius isn’t in the shooting (which is slick) or the driving (which is fine), but in the quiet, devastating consistency of its world. It understands that true dystopia isn’t about shackles, [b]it’s about the slow, voluntary surrender of your humanity to a logic of cold utility.[/b] Helping a suicidal cop, only to find he’s already dead. Letting a monster live because his own guilt is a more exquisite punishment than your bullet. These aren’t simple side quests as they are moral biopsies, revealing the real tumor at the heart of a dream.

The much-discussed endings are the final, masterful stroke (for me specially). There is no victory condition. There is only diagnosis. A sterile, corporate afterlife. A blaze of glory that leaves everyone you love in ashes. A hopeful exile that’s just another form of running. Each is a masterpiece of bittersweet compromise of a reality you hardly have control over. In the end, you don’t defeat Night City. You simply choose which of its scars you will wear, and which final piece of yourself you will leave on its altar.

Ultimately, this game resonates not because it lets you escape life, but because it mirrors life’s most private calculus. The exhaustion of constant negotiation. The beauty of small, defiant connections in a world that commodifies them. The understanding that growing up and living in Night City is ultimately about managing loss and despair.

It leaves you with a quiet, lingering ache, the kind that comes from saying goodbye to someone you understood too well. It is symbolically flawed, and breathtakingly human piece of art. Not because you had fun, but because for a little while, you lived in the rain, under the impossible neon, and felt it all matter...

Originally, during release and for an upsettingly long time after release, this game was a terrible, overhyped, stretched-thin, overly ambitious pile of hot garbage. The graphics were sub-par yet offensively poorly optimized, the mechanics were clunky at the best of times and completely broken and non-functional at the worst of times. The game was painful to play most of the time, and impossible to play the rest of the time. From T-posing on motorcycles, to negating all fall damage by being in the sliding post when landing. From the floor not loading in, to enemies being unkillable due to not taking any damage. The list of bugs, glitches, problems and troubles was not growing shorter, it was growing longer. With every Steam discussion and CD Project Red forum post, the list of game-breaking complications grew steadily, mercilessly longer.

But that was then. And this is now.
Today, CD Project Red has taken the proper, honorable path to redemption; rather than admitting defeat, ignoring the library of problems the game suffered from, and simply starting on a new game, hoping they'll do better next time? They listened to their player base, locked in, took the bull by the horns and refused to let the game fade into the annals of gaming history, becoming little more than another footnote in a 'Top 10 worst games of all time' Youtuber clickbait videos.

CD Project Red turned this obnoxiously bad, poorly excuse of a video game, into a redemption story worth hearing. Bugs and glitches were fixed en masse, one patch after another. Missing features(the ones able to be included without a full blown overhaul of the entire game anyway) were added rapidly and in quick succession. Graphics were radically improved, and optimized at the same time. HUD improvements, QoL additions, new vehicles, entirely new abilities and mechanics. The list CD Project Red fixed and added to the game rapidly shrank until it eventually overtook the list of issues, removing them entirely and instead began to improve the game beyond what it should be at its released state. They took the finished game and, like absolute chads, said "Nah, we can do better than that!"
It's now 2026 and this game is absolutely phenomenal! A must play for any futuristic sci-fi, punk-style RPG shooter!

几乎在游戏的每个部分都能体会到制作组的野心:无论是杰出的视觉表现，出色的世界观设计，对赛博朋克题材的演绎，都缔造出一座辉煌而又投射下阴影的霓虹之城，堪称游戏历史上最壮丽的城市地图风景线。仅仅是车辆在炸街模式下的表现与操作说明，开发者就像兴奋的阿宅打开话茬一样写了整整一页，我可以想象他们曾经想要做出怎样的游戏，又希望玩家以怎样的热情去品鉴他！然而，就像赛博朋克世界里许多戛然而止的梦想一样，曾经的愿景也在现实的重锤下化作虚影。幸好，在经历了DLC更新以后的今天，他已经是一部成熟的、值得体验的作品。
-依然是赛博朋克题材在交互流媒体艺术上最好的作品之一。第一人称的沉浸式体验与基于动捕的剧情动画带来的沉浸感足够让独特的艺术风格带来深刻的审美体验。
-堪称华丽的地图设计，游戏史上最惊艳的赛博朋克城市，让人目不暇接的美景，霓虹灯幻梦下的阴影…以及置身其中，那份如零件之于庞大机器的孤独。
-有一整个充满诚意的百科，让你体验独特而庞大的世界风貌下的方方面面。
-相比于那些同样在开放世界上受到诟病，而因为美术表现饱受赞誉的游戏——如《对马岛之魂》，CDPR依然贡献了他们在剧本上的造诣，绝大部分支线任务都有趣得多，足以支撑玩家的游戏动力。
-一个波澜壮阔的，寻求救赎、并在虚无的世界里创造自我价值的故事。比《巫师3》有更深的立意。
-适合那些对近未来科幻充满兴趣的玩家，因为有数不清的造型独特、设计华丽的武器、枪械和车辆可以收集。他们几乎每个都能满足你的幻想。
然而，就如同大卫和V对这个世界的抗争一样，这个游戏的构想本身或许就从不指向一条通途之路。城市开放世界有太高的门槛，却又诞生了太闪耀的明珠——Rockstar的《侠盗猎车》系列，几乎锚定了整个开放世界游戏的标准。每一部都市开放世界作品都不可避免地被拿来与他们比较；但无论出于工期还是工作室的体量，这都是一个不可能完成的任务。人们会觉得，当GTA系列在十几年前就做出了地铁和飞行载具以后，2077曾经承诺过的无缝地铁与浮空车却依旧只是泡沫；当前人早已经实现过的成就，对你而言依然是无法攻克的技术难题，似乎注定这部游戏在发售之后命途多舛。
遗憾的是，CDPR最终放弃了对于2077的长线投资计划，仅仅把更新局限在很小的规模以内，无论是地铁系统的妥协，还是胎死腹中的多人模式，都象征着这部作品已经敲响了晚钟。时至今日，人们依然能看到路上的npc陷入偶然的抽搐；小吃店打着不同的招牌，却卖着相同的零食；第一人称让服装变得毫无意义，武器和车辆的手感粘稠，而它们的模块化改装再也没有实现(哪怕美术设计本身非常适合这么做！)。没有浮空车，没有水上载具，捉襟见肘的生活系统，就连路边的出租车都只是冰冷的建模。这一切都让这座表面上光鲜亮丽的城市缺乏生气，让本应十分出色的沉浸体验大打折扣。在可以预见的未来内，这些都已经无法改变。
尽管如此，它依然有一个精彩的故事，一些出色的人物群像，全程配音的高水准本地化体验，有趣的角色养成系统，以及一座让人瞠目结舌的宏伟城市。如果今天人们要评价他，那么他仍然不算一个成功的开放世界；但以RPG的视角而言，也已经足够优秀。无论是对于近未来科幻充满兴趣的朋友，还是被边缘行者吸引来的粉丝们，他已足以撑得起自己的名字。

Cyberpunk 2077 turned out to be one of my favorite games. It's action-packed yet dialogue-heavy, exploring some really good and omnipresent themes with a great story and truly lets you do whatever you want. The game as a whole is really fleshed out.

Playtime: 72.8 hours (PC, M&K)

[b]Overall:  9/10[/b]

[u]Narrative: 9.5/10[/u] - This game has quite a strong story that winds all over the place and can, at times, be a bit difficult to follow. The game offers practically no introduction to the world of Cyberpunk in the beginning of the story, and lets the player figure things out on their own. The different workings of this strange (but all too real) society can be pieced together with ample notes and messages scattered around the environment, while the story takes a much more personal perspective with following an either-sex V through the crazy high stakes antics of their life. With three different beginning scenarios to choose from, each exposes the player to a different aspect of the world. A great way to start and offers fantastic replay value. Emotional moments hit nicely and always at the right time, and while there may not be too many intentional emotional moments, the pressing and existential central theme provides the player with as many as they so desire. There are also several different endings to the game depending on player decisions throughout the course of the gameplay.
The world of Cyberpunk 2077 is filled with evolutions of many problems which plague modern society today including major themes of unbridled Capitalism, tech feudalism, and hedonism. The game presents all of this in a way that doesn't feel forced or too preachy, allowing the player to write whatever conclusion they want to. The world-building is top-notch. There's no facet that the writers didn't consider and it feels very real despite oftentimes comical exaggerations. Speaking of comical, this game is funny. I say that as a statement of fact because I don't think there's any sense of humor that someone could have that wouldn't occasionally find this game funny.
Despite the many different endings, they're all tragic in their own way. I don't think I've seen that in a game with different endings, as they typically make one a 'green thumbs-up, you win' kinda vibe. I think it was a great choice considering the trials that the main character endures. I don't think this story would have hit nearly as hard if V was cured completely and there was balloons and cake.

[u]Visuals: 9/10[/u] - The game looks great. The artistic style fits really nicely with the narrative and world-building. CP2077 has a nice mix of grunge 90s and chrome futuristic aesthetics, it all works really well together. Despite this, there are some cracks. I think the world from a design standpoint is a bit too ambitious. The giant highways don't look great from a distance, and the scaling can feel a bit odd in some places. Some textures can look a bit plasticy when fully lit. As with most modern AAA games, the graphics and textures are resource-intensive with higher settings, but look great. Character models are extremely high quality and look fantastic (and have great variety), allowing for some really immersive close-up dialogue moments. Photo mode is included with full path- and ray-tracing. Great use of color throughout, leaving not a single area in the world without some glowsticks on the ground or a full-brightness LED billboard to remind you you're in Cyberpunk.
 
[u]Audio: 9/10[/u] - The score and soundtrack are really good, fits the different tones well, and does not get repetitive. This game also has a GTA-like radio available with several different stations with a variety of genres. Somehow all the songs are great. However, the radio was buggy sometimes, silencing itself, refusing to turn on. The voice acting is fantastic. Female V's voice actor in particular was just so pleasant to hear. Great emotional depth from that VA too. Very nice atmospheric noise (footsteps above you in apartments, etc). NPC chatter is plentiful and very funny if you stick around. At some points in the story all music or radio is replaced by a single track that plays out during free roam which can sometimes feel out of place.

[u]Gameplay: 8/10[/u] - At times, this game feels like a fainting and dying simulator but if you hang on that happens not as much. This game is dialogue- and cutscene-heavy, and it's also a true open world do-whatever-you-want and it doesn't lock you in unless you do so intentionally. Dialogue options are plentiful and can be fun to choose from. There are side quests, separate from Side Gigs, which are more like tertiary, minimal-story, direct combat options. Some unique gameplay mechanics are featured such as Cyberware, different upgrades to V that enhance your stats in some way or another, or offer different combat features. Quickhacks, a ranged digital attack on enemies is attainable and very effective when upgraded. The combat is fun, satisfying, and really allows the player to do whatever they want and approach any situation however they want, with more up-front combat options offered alongside stealth. The stealth is well-done and a bit forgiving and quickhacks allow for a more integrated gameplay to the stealth option. There's lots of cars in this game available to teleport to V whenever you want. Driving is mostly fun and ranges from dense city streets to empty desert roads. There's an Autodrive feature which works pretty well once you figure out how it works. My main criticism of the gameplay is the lack of background given to the player in the mission log. There's Johnny rambling of course but am I expected to remember what every mission is?

[u]Character Design: 9/10[/u] - Really great and oftentimes deeply flawed characters in this game which ties in nicely to the story and themes, of which there are many when it comes to the characters. Probably the most obvious is the struggle with the main character's identity [spoiler]after the Relic is implanted[/spoiler], but there are also major themes of unrestrained self-indulgence and the sort-of transhumanism that comes with the tech implantation culture. Most characters develop and change throughout your time in doing their missions. There are a few characters that you can become friends with and see their arcs. Panam's in particular is great. Johnny, though I hated him at first and still did a good bit throughout, is a great addition to this game and stands in contrast to the stark individualistic landscape [spoiler]as you're forced to have a partner in your head.[/spoiler] Dialogue is well-written, witty, and doesn't shy from absurdity. Background NCPs are probably the most diverse I've ever seen in a game and their chatter is well-acted and fits nicely.

[u]Environment and Level Design: 8.5/10[/u] - Night City and its surroundings are really well-built and is scaled in a way that allows a five-minute drive from one end to the other while also making each area feel distinct. The massive high-rises and projected ads juxtaposed with massive piles of garbage stretching for miles is the kind of thing that made this game feel really immersive. The game mostly successfully attempts to personalize the scale of the massive environments with elevator rides and explorable interiors to some of the mega-buildings. There are mission-specific buildings and interiors throughout. Interiors and exteriors are both really well-decorated; Night City really feels lived-in. There are many messages to read throughout the environment which expand the player's background on the world they're experiencing. 

[u]Personal Engagement: 9/10[/u]

[u]Personal Replay Value: 10/10[/u]

[u]Performance: 7/10[/u] - 2k~85 max settings with path tracing & DLSS. Several bugs in most sessions including calling cars not functioning, no music bugs, glitchy radio, others.

The gameplay itself is not particularly difficult, since the game provides a wide range of tools and options to handle different situations. However, the challenging part is managing the dialogue choices, as making the wrong decision can sometimes lead to mission failure, which is never a good outcome.

While some bugs can still be found, they are usually easy to notice and avoid. Overall, the game has clearly improved over the years, showing steady development and refinement that make the experience increasingly enjoyable.

Everything that's great about this game (graphic capability, environmental immersion, voice-acted characters, story, etc.) has already been discussed, and I recommend it overall, so I am just going to point out the one big negative that might be a dealbreaker for some players:

[b]THE DRIVING CAN SUCK![/b] In a major way. I'm not kidding—for a game that requires you to get around on wheels all the time, the car control and physics modeling feel unrefined at best and, at worst, are absolutely horrific!

The player input and physics modeling/feedback when driving are severely delayed, even if you are running at optimized FPS. At (seemingly random) times, the sense of speed and inertia are some of the worst I've experienced in any game of this caliber. It is difficult to feel like one has any consistent precision driving in this game, to the point where it may be a significant detriment to one's enjoyment of the game overall. 

In particular, some vehicles behave as if they are equipped with a four-wheel steering system that is way too aggressive and not how actual four-wheel steering works. [i]If the devs implemented this properly, it could have made the driving way cooler[/i] (imagine being able to strafe your car from side to side through traffic), but instead they [b]hamstringed many cars with it,[/b] perhaps as a balancing mechanic or as a lazy way of faking rear-wheel-drive behavior—either way, it's frustrating to deal with.

Different car makes and models omit or enhance certain characteristics, and in terms of stats there is a very wide range of vehicle capability—so in that regard, each vehicle feels unique... But only in the sense of which car is the least nonsensical. 

Some might say, "Just ride a motorcycle," to which I say, "What point is there in having 4-wheel vehicles to begin with when any motorcycle can outhandle all of them AND ram through traffic just the same!?" Don't even get me started about any in-game lore references about "drifting" or "tuning." Pure ridiculousness. Fairy tales and magic. Nonexistent in this game. 

I know this isn't a racing game. It's a single-player action RPG, so I should just STFU and enjoy it for what it is, right? Well... there are [b]a LOT of main and side missions that involve driving [/b] (without the option to use a motorcycle), in the same way a game like GTA does. Which goes back to my main point — [i] Driving around is the main transportation and exploration method in the game [/i]— [b]it's a core component of gameplay, and should have been done better! [/b]

To add a sprinkling of insult to injury, the NPC traffic is programmed to 'move out of your way,' when driving in a straight line at high speed. So guess what happens when you try to weave or do anything unpredictable? They drive RIGHT IN FRONT OF YOU! That adds absolutely nothing but frustration.  

Yes, I can drive fast in the game without crashing. Yes, I know some cars suck, and some drive properly. Yes, I can even "drift" around corners if I really want. My point is none of it feels organic. It's all clunky and primitive. It cannot be overlooked. I just wanted to make that clear. 

TL,DR: The driving physics suck, even if you like "arcade" style driving. It's like some advanced form of AI programmed traction and stability control (plus NPCs) to ruin you. Maybe that's just how driving is in the future =[

我是2021年入手的《赛博朋克2077》PS4版本。当时全世界都在骂它，bug满天飞，画面糊得像近视眼没戴眼镜。但我还是咬着牙，顶着掉帧和闪退，打完了第一个结局——荒坂公司结局。

那个结局让我沉默了很久。走出荒坂大厦的时候，V坐在那个位置上，眼神空洞，灵魂早已不在。屏幕黑了之后，我在沙发上坐了一会儿，脑子里只有一个念头：这座城市不该只给我这样的答案。

后来的事情，你们都知道了。

2024年，我终于换了PS5。重新下载PS5版本，第一次丝滑地开车穿行夜之城，我几乎想哭——不是因为感动，而是因为原来这座城市真的可以这么好看。我第一次体验到流浪者结局，V离开了夜之城，和帕南一起驶向沙漠的尽头。那是我第一次觉得，也许这座城市还可以温柔一点。

2025年，我在Steam上又买了一次。那一次我走向了荒坂塔，打出了另一个结局。每次Credits滚动的时候，我都觉得胸口有什么东西被堵住了——不是因为结局有多惨，而是因为你知道V的故事在某个地方结束了，但你的故事还在继续。

我尝试过每一个结局，除了那个隐藏的——也许我是故意留着的。像是一本舍不得看完的书，最后那几页，我还没准备好翻开。

我不知道该用什么样的词来形容夜之城。

它大得不像一座城市，更像一个活着的器官。每一条街都有故事，每一家店铺都开着门，NPC走路的样子、说话的语调、躲避车辆的速度，全都像是生活在里面，而不是被程序写出来的。开车的时候引擎声和风声混在一起，霓虹灯的光在挡风玻璃上流淌，那一刻你会觉得自己真的是V。

我很少愿意在开放世界里慢慢走路，但在夜之城，我走了无数次。

游戏的原声带也是另一层世界。有时候我只是停下车子，待在路边，什么都不做，就听着音乐和街道的底噪，感觉自己成了这座城市一部分。它让我分不清，到底是这座城在崩塌，还是我们在崩塌。

但真正把我拉进去的，是《往日之影》。

DLC主线12个小时，卖328港币——当时我觉得“波兰蠢驴又疯了”。但玩完之后，我想说：你们就保持这个疯劲，别改。支线、DLC、主线，甚至连那些不起眼的委托，都像是有人认真写过的短篇小说。

自由、反抗、资本、信任、背叛——这些大词在这座城市里都变成了活生生的人。你做的每一个选择，都会在某个角落引发回响。你以为你只是在玩游戏，但玩完之后你会开始审视自己的生活，审视自己的选择。

——这就是为什么我没办法用“好游戏”三个字来形容它。

它是我从小到大玩过所有的Story-based游戏里，最好的那个。没有之一。

不是因为它的画面、它的战斗、它的自由度——虽然这些都很好。而是因为它让我相信了一座不存在的城市，让我在意了一群不存在的人。

我依然没打那个隐藏结局。

也许有一天会打。也许不会。

我只是觉得，只要我没打完，夜之城就还在那里等我回去。

——它是我心目中永远的Top 1。

首先如果你在因为首发灾难而犹豫何时入手，那现在就是最好的入手时机，无论是游戏性，UI还是优化，现在就是最完美的版本，此后估计也不会再有这般大更新了
我很欣赏cdpr对rpg的态度，他们热衷于以无数选择取向构建起一座叙事大厦，并且这次还有分段式自动存档，让玩家可以毫无压力的探索大厦的每一处角落。你能清晰地体会到大厦内部结构的层层嵌套，几乎每一条支线都会随你选择而产生有趣的后续任务，甚至会影响主线乃至结局的进程，主线上的选择又会对支线产生变化，而这种影响又不像jrpg一般是制作组安排好的一本道，更像让你在烹饪时添几加各种香料，最终调出你想要的味道。任务解决方法也提供了很多思路，制作组也会回应你突发奇想的一些小巧思，使我游玩过程十分享受。
战斗流派更新到现在非常丰富，且切换成本极低，我在一个周目内就可以毫无压力的玩遍所有的流派和有趣的build。载具系统现在也十分全面与人性化，我做任务90%的情况都宁可不用快速传送而是自己开车过去，疾驰在夜之城中的沉浸感属实是独一份的，可惜我真的很想玩飞行载具或者像Lucy一样用单分子线荡蛛丝。并且NCPD的通缉模式真的蛮烦人的，在城区撞倒几个电线杆就要被神秘小警车和黏人小警摩群殴了，我是觉得完全可以设计低星通缉警局交罚金或坐牢之类的，追杀至死多少有点逆天了。
[h2]接下来有严重剧透[/h2]
cdpr一贯引以为豪的剧情设计在这次依旧可以给到满分，本体的确主线过于短了，当然只是说短，缺点也仅此而已，故事是完整的且优秀的。本体的故事，自始至终绕着“自我的边界”与“存在的意义”展开，V与强尼·银手的意识共生，本就是一场最极致的身心博弈——强尼不是单纯的角色，而是一种反叛的符号，是对荒坂所代表的资本体制的极致对抗，他的偏执与狂热，本质上是对“被物化的人类”的反抗，可这份反抗又走向了另一种极端：为了推倒大厦，他可以无视雪崩下的每一片雪花，为了坚守所谓的“朋克精神”，他拒绝承认个体的脆弱与求生的本能；而被relic侵蚀后V的挣扎，是每个普通人在宏大体制下的缩影，我们都在为了活下去而妥协，为了守住自我而抗争，在意识被侵蚀的日子里，每一次呼吸都是对“存在”的证明，哪怕这份证明最终指向的是无可避免的消亡。本体里的每一个选择，都不是简单的善恶抉择，而是对生命价值的不同判断：是选择成为强尼那样的反叛者，用燃烧的生命砸向冰冷的体制，还是选择做一个平凡的求生者，在夹缝中守住最后一点自我？荒坂塔的火光，不仅烧着资本的傲慢，也烧着人类对“不朽”的执念，当永生成为一种可以被购买的商品，生命的珍贵便在数据化的过程中被消解，这才是本体最刺骨的拷问——如果生命可以被复制，那所谓的永恒，究竟是实在的一抹传奇亮色，还是荒坂库里永恒存在的形式？但我在游玩过程中也时感遗憾，炸了荒坂塔又怎样呢？高塔结局中，即使没有v的干预，荒坂集团没多久也自己走上末路了，但新的公司总是存在，公司资本主义不会因为一栋大厦而崩塌，所有赛博蝼蚁所做的一切，仿佛就是这个时代下一阵微不足道的涟漪。
而往日之影，则是将这份形而上的追问拉回了现实的泥土里，把宏大的体制批判浓缩成在狗镇上演的人性修罗场，这里没有绝对的正义与邪恶，只有身不由己的选择与被体制异化的灵魂。如果说本体的对抗是个人与宏大体制的对抗，那往日之影的对抗，就是个人与被体制裹挟的个人的对抗，当庞然大物的体制最终消解为一个个具体的人，你会发现所谓的“反派”，不过是和你一样在泥潭里挣扎的人，他们的选择不是出于恶意，而是被环境所迫，被体制所驯化。这里的自由，也不再是强尼口中那种“不自由毋宁死”的极端自由，而是往日之影英文名“Phantom Liberty”所暗示的“虚幻的自由”——我们总以为自己握着选择的权利，可实际上，每一个选择都被体制、被环境、被自身的欲望所束缚，自由意志不过是人类在被控制的社会中，一种自我安慰的幻觉。百灵鸟的出现，为这场关于自由的探讨添上了最复杂的一笔，她的背叛与求生，她的挣扎与算计，让强尼的反叛符号开始有了人性的温度，也让V的选择有了更真实的重量：当你面对的不是冰冷的公司logo，而是一个个有血有肉、和你一样渴望活下去的人，你还能坚持所谓的“纯粹”吗？在狗镇，在夜之城，在这个被体制异化的世界里，没有谁的求生是原罪，也没有谁的选择是绝对的正确。
[h3] “说一千道一万，她自由了。” [/h3]
夜之城的故事始终在探讨一个核心：当科技消解了身体的边界，当体制裹挟了自由的意志，人类最珍贵的东西究竟是什么？答案藏在V与强尼的和解里，藏在狗镇每一个小人物的挣扎里，藏在每一次看似无奈却又无比坚定的选择里——那就是无论世界如何被赛博化，无论自我如何被侵蚀，人类依然拥有感知痛苦、渴望温暖、坚守本心的能力，这份能力，就是对抗一切冰冷与异化的终极力量。夜之城的霓虹永远闪烁，资本的游戏永远继续，可总有人在霓虹下坚守自我，在游戏中选择真诚，这就是赛博朋克最温柔的内核，也是人类最永恒的光芒。

[h3]TL;DR: Possibly my new favourite game. Absolutely one of the best RPGs I've ever played, and I still have a second play through with the DLC to experience. [u]Must-play[/u] if you dig games by Bethesda, Obsidian, Bioware etc.[/h3]

I've had this in my library for years and tried to pick it up multiple times, but it never hooked me. After watching Edgerunners however, I became a bit obsessed by Cyberpunk's lore and aesthetic, so decided to give it another go. [b]It's all I've played and thought about for the last three weeks[/b].
[list]
[*] Night City is beautiful and alive (even with my wooden PC running it on medium). Every character action has an animation - immersion is incredible. No matter where you go there is something interesting to see or do.
[*] The gunplay is exhilarating, melee combat is dynamic and a lot of fun, and quick hacks are probably my favourite combat/environmental feature. If like me you weren't hooked immediately, try a different playstyle and you WILL be. You can reset your attributes once per save, so play Act 1, make a save point, experiment.
[*] The main story is emotive and brilliantly written (with a lot of narrative choices offered). The voice acting and mocap are phenomenal, and the inclusion of Keanu lends it a lot of legitimacy. The side quests are some of the most fun and memorable I've had the pleasure of playing in an RPG, and I've barely scratched the surface. There's a fair amount of sex/nudity and gore, but it's done in a very tasteful way - the game treats you like an adult.
[*] The driving is a bit meh, but it does its job - literally a vehicle for showcasing the world. I rarely fast travelled.
[*] Are there bugs? Yes. Do they mar the gameplay? No. It's unreasonable to expect a game/piece of software this comprehensive to not have some bugs. I understand that on launch this game was a mess, but I literally only experienced 1 or 2 visual bugs during my first playthrough. Not at all an issue. 
[/list]
I'm only 46 hours in, so I may update my review once I've delved into more side-quests and played through the DLC. However, as someone who loves RPGs, [b]I unapologetically give this game a 10/10.[/b]

Прохожу игру в 3 раз, первые 2 были на пиратке в момент релиза. Игра за эти годы стала НОРМАЛЬНОЙ. Постараюсь без спойлеров. Игра шикарная, описывать ее плюсы я могу часами, пройти советую всем. Расскажу только о субъективных минусах.
Минусы.
1) Самый главный, лично я при прохождении постоянно думал насколько игра могла быть круче, если бы ее недоделывали в спешке и она бы вышла, например, вместе с ГТА 6. Конкретнее про тюнинг, они хотя бы завезли возможность менять цвет машин, это хоть что то, но чувство что в игре мог появится полноценный тюнинг, в котором игроки могли бы часами лепить из своих тарантасов что то непостижимое,(сеттинг идеально для этого подходит) заставляет грустить. Как и крафт различного оружия, который тоже мог бы быть. Киберпанк мог стать идеальной песочницей для создания всего на что способна фантазия, но увы.
2) Основной сюжет. Особенно в сравнении с побочными квестами, интересными и проработанными, основной сюжет выглядит бледно, достаточно классическая и предсказуемая история, с однообразными концовками.
3) Нелогичность. Киберпанк все таки не фентези, а фантастика, где всему есть научное объяснение. Приведу пример того, что больше всего меня смутило. В игре есть квест с Пиралесами, в котором оказывается, что будущему мэру промывают голову, заменяя его воспоминания, уникальной вундервафлей, которая каким то невероятным образом может дистанционно переписывать сознание человека. Мы выполняем этот квест, узнаем про эту вундервафлю и.... все. Ну реально, всем просто плевать что в этой вселенной существует такая технология. При том, что она может напрямую помочь ГГ, но нет, сюжет это все игнорирует.
И на этом все, минусов больше я не придумал, да и главный минус игры только в том, что она могла быть значительно лучше, дай разрабам время на реализацию всех задумок. Но для меня игра и так 9/10.

Cyberpunk 2077 is that gorgeous, emotionally unavailable person you date for the vibes. Mysterious, hot, a little dangerous. You have fun together. Partners in mayhem. Makes your senses explode. And later just dumps you and reminds you that's life, baby. Deal with it.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a stunning, immersive, emotionally evasive masterpiece that absolutely nails the vibes and then dodges long-term narrative responsibility like a corpo dodges taxes.

As a game? Ridiculously good.
Gunplay? Crunchy.
Build variety? Delicious.
Night City? A neon-drenched “don’t text your ex” mood board that I would absolutely move into despite the gunfire.

Driving through the city at night with the radio on makes you feel like the main character of a movie that ends badly but looks incredible while doing it.

Side quests and character stories? Genuinely fantastic. Some of the most human, grounded writing in modern games. You help people through trauma, grief, identity crises, family disasters. It’s intimate, messy, real.

And then the ending rolls up like:

“Cool emotional growth. Anyway, choose your flavor of existential shrug.”

I really thought all the relationships, gangs, and connections I built would matter more in the final stretch. You spend dozens of hours forming bonds, earning trust, changing lives. You choose a life path, you make dialog choices based on your attributes.

…and the finale goes:

“That’s nice. Please proceed to one of two narrative lanes. No, your friends cannot come.”

Is that thematically consistent with a dystopian hellscape run by megacorps? Yes.
Is it also emotionally unsatisfying? Also yes.

My ending felt:
Not heroic.
Not triumphant.
Not particularly rewarding.
Very lonely.
...yet weirdly, cathartically freeing.

Which, to be fair, is probably the most on-brand outcome possible for this world and narrative.

The game is brilliant at moments. Atmosphere. Character writing. Personal stakes.
It’s just less interested in big-picture emotional payoff where everything you did comes crashing together in the finale. Nothing really does.

So no, the story didn’t rearrange my DNA. It didn’t spiritually supplex me. But it did give me a memorable ride, some genuinely great character arcs, and a beautifully miserable city I’ll think about for a long time.

Would I replay the whole thing again? Probably not. It's a fantastic narrative action game, but a mid-at-best Roleplaying game (yeah, I know CDPR even removed any and all RPG tags from all the marketing).

Cyberpunk 2077 não foi só mais um RPG que eu joguei e segui em frente. Foi um jogo que eu realmente me envolvi, daqueles que você passa horas jogando e depois fica pensando na história, nos personagens e nas escolhas que fez.

Night City é um dos mundos mais imersivos que eu já vi em um jogo. Não só pelo visual, mas pela sensação constante de que aquele lugar é hostil, desigual e meio quebrado. Tudo ali parece funcionar contra você, e isso combina perfeitamente com a proposta do jogo. Você não é um herói salvando o mundo, você é só mais alguém tentando sobreviver nele.

Na minha primeira run eu escolhi ser nômade, e isso definiu totalmente quem o V foi pra mim. Desde o começo existe essa sensação de não pertencer, de estar sempre meio deslocado, tentando achar um lugar em meio ao caos. O romance com a Panam foi facilmente um dos pontos mais fortes da experiência. Não parece algo forçado ou jogado ali só pra ter romance. Ele cresce aos poucos, nas missões, nas conversas, nas atitudes. Dá pra sentir que existe parceria ali, confiança, cuidado.

Isso me fez criar uma ligação muito forte com o V. Não era só um personagem controlado por mim, era alguém passando por conflitos reais. A relação com o Johnny Silverhand também é absurda de boa. No começo ele é incômodo, arrogante, irritante até. Com o tempo, você começa a entender de onde vem tudo aquilo. Em vários momentos eu me peguei concordando com ele, mesmo sabendo que ele também errou muito.

A história do jogo é muito bem escrita. Ela fala de identidade, de legado, de morte e de escolhas sem resposta fácil. Nada ali é simples ou preto no branco. O jogo confia que o jogador vai entender as nuances, e isso faz muita diferença.

Também dá pra ver claramente que o pessoal que fez o jogo entende de RPGs de cyberpunk de verdade, não só da estética. Tem influência clara de Cyberpunk 2020, Blade Runner, Ghost in the Shell, Neuromancer e outras obras do gênero, mas tudo isso foi bem adaptado pro formato de videogame. Não parece cópia, parece respeito ao material original.
Na segunda run eu resolvi ir pro outro lado. Joguei como marginal, sem limite nenhum. Usei mods que me deixaram praticamente invencível, cheio de implantes, exagerado ao máximo. Um V completamente moldado pelo pior de Night City.

O combate ficou brutal, rápido e quase sem consequência. E isso muda totalmente a forma como você enxerga o jogo. Ter poder demais não deixa tudo mais divertido o tempo todo, às vezes deixa até vazio. E isso conversa muito bem com a ideia de cyberpsicose que o jogo apresenta.

Mesmo assim, o V ainda tinha sentimentos. O romance com a Judy nessa run cria um contraste muito forte. Você é praticamente um monstro andando pela cidade, mas ainda existe alguém que te conecta com o lado humano. Isso deixa tudo mais pesado, porque o conflito não é só externo, é interno também.

Os mods não estragaram a experiência. Pelo contrário, eles reforçaram o tema do jogo. Excesso de poder, ausência de limites, falta de medo. Tudo isso encaixa muito bem com o universo de Cyberpunk. Essa segunda run foi caótica, intensa e diferente da primeira, mas tão marcante quanto.
Cyberpunk 2077 pode ter tido problemas, principalmente no lançamento, mas pra mim ele acerta onde mais importa. Ele cria envolvimento, cria memória e cria vínculo com os personagens.

Não é só sobre build, armas ou implantes.
É sobre as escolhas que você fez e quem o seu V acabou se tornando.

Nota final: 11/10

Lista de mods que usei na minha segunda run - Usei o A.G.I.S., que basicamente libera uma loja virtual com todos os itens do jogo, o que me deu liberdade total pra testar armas, roupas e builds sem ficar preso a loot. Pra mobilidade e veículos, usei o Baby Driver 2.0, que deixa dirigir em Night City muito mais gostoso e menos travado.

A parte mais importante da run foi o conjunto de mods ligados a cyberware. Com o Cyberware-EX eu pude instalar muito mais implantes do que o jogo permitiria normalmente, e com o No Cyberware Cost com Edgerunner funcionando eu removi praticamente todas as penalidades. O V virou uma máquina absurda, exatamente como um marginal que passou do limite. O Cyberarm Cycle permitiu trocar braços cibernéticos em tempo real, e o CyberArms-EX adicionou variações visuais e funcionais, deixando o personagem ainda mais exagerado.

Pra combate e poder, o Forever Sandy deixou o Sandevistan quase constante, quebrando o tempo sempre que eu quisesse. Isso contribuiu muito pra sensação de invencibilidade e excesso. O Wannabe Edgerunner amarra tudo isso, simulando uma cyberpsicose leve conforme o V se enche de implantes, o que combina demais com a proposta da run.

Pra imersão, usei mods como Idle Anywhere, Immersive Bartenders e Immersive Food Vendors, que fazem Night City parecer mais viva, com interações simples que não existem no jogo base. O Metro System também ajudou muito nisso, adicionando um metrô funcional que dá mais sensação de cidade real.

Visualmente e na interface, o Limited HUD e o Preem Scanner deixaram a tela mais limpa e menos poluída, enquanto o Ultra Plus ajudou a manter um bom desempenho sem sacrificar o visual. Pequenos ajustes estéticos como o Female V’s Less Ugly Feet também entraram pra corrigir detalhes que sempre incomodaram.

Por fim, usei mods mais “fora da curva”, como o Weapon Additions – Lightsabers, que não respeita o lore, mas é simplesmente divertido, e lojas virtuais específicas como a do Sabbath7991, que facilitam acesso a armas e acessórios sem quebrar o ritmo do jogo.

PS: Sim, eu baixei um mod pro pé da V mulher ficar menos feio, aquela droga parecia uma aberração.

Math e Vinni, baixem o meu modpack pra vocês experimentarem o poder de um Cyberpsicopata.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a 2020 first person action RPG created by CD projekt Red and based on Cyberpunk, a series of pen and paper roleplaying games created by Michael Pondsmith, a man who is probably tired of saying “I told ya so.” Over the last 35 years.

Set in the fictional city of Night City, a corporate shit hole where everything is run by some sort of conglomerate or another. One of the city states that now exists in the former United States after 77 or so years of endless woopsie poopsies, Night City is the gathering ground of every important entity and person on the planet. Its a place where you can pay EMS to come in literally guns blazing and where kids cartoons tell you to not look people in the eye because they might just attack you like some sort of angry robot baboon. This is the furthest in the Cyberpunk timeline we’ve ever been, with Pondsmith’s RED being an inbetween of Cyberpunk 2020 and this one.

You play as V, a Night City Merc who comes from one of three backgrounds: Street Kid, Nomad, and Corpo. After doing your background intro, you and Jackie, your best friend, go into business of being street Mercs together, solving problems in return for Eurodollars, the dominant currency in Night City because who still pays with USDs? After a series of events, V finds himself with a construct ingrained in his cyberbrain, the construct of Johnny Silverhand, a deceased Terrorist who blew up Arasaka tower back in the distant future of 2023. Now, with Johnny’s consciousness bleeding into yours, and slowly taking over your entire body, you and your headmate set out on a journey to save both of you, or at the very least get Johnny out of your brain.

I really like this one, took me four tries, but this time I stuck with it. Mind you I’m playing this game in 2026, so a good chunk of the problems it had in 2020-2022 or so aren’t present anymore. Problems are still there, I got some bugs every now and then, but it still plays fine for me.

The game is a first person Action RPG with an emphasis on the action, stats and weapons do matter, but it isn’t like a lot of it’s contemporaries where you just shwack someone with a sword that feels like a foam bat to swing or shoot them in the head for 15 minutes until they finally drop. From what I understand, enemies don’t really level with you as much as you get better at killing them. There wasn’t really anywhere I couldn’t go early on and I wasn’t being one shotted, so I figure levels are more about what perks you pick up and how much you put into your six stats.

You can put points into muscle, reflexes, cool, tech, netrunner, and a secret, nefarious sixth option. Stats work up to 20 points, with each milestone point giving you more perks to unlock. Stuff like doing more damage with a sword if you have a sandevastan, you know that thing David had in that anime that made you buy this game? Everyone has one of those now, how time flies.
More points in muscle lets you rip open heavy doors, tech can help you bypass security, Netrunner lets you upload all three shrek movies directly into someone’s brain, etc.

Outside of your stats, there’s also cyberware, which is probably the coolest part of the game. Unlike Adam Jensen, V doesn’t really mind turning himself into a total freak show, with stuff like Gorilla Arms and legs joints that let him run like one of those cute horse girls from that anime I like. Stuff like brain implants that let you upload the Shrek movies faster, an epidermal skin graft that lets you cloak, weird, psycho shit like that.

Looking more into Cyberpunk, there’s an anti-personnel program called Brainwipe that lets you just delete someone’s Id from their cyberbrains and leaves their bodies a drooling caveman. Looking more into it, there’s also a program called Soulkiller where it still does that but also uploads their entire being into a matrix where you can just torture them for all eternity if you want.

I don’t like the Cyberpunk world, it scares me.

Like I said before, combat actually feels nice in this game. Both melee weapons and guns have a nice crunchy oomph to them and people fall apart like you just threw a baseball through a mannequin. Weapons let you shred people to pieces, with their guts and limbs going flying the more ammo you pump into them. Swords will flat out dismember or behead people and I punched a guy so hard with my gorilla arms one time that he bounced off the wall and just kept going into space.
That was probably a glitch but I’m going to pretend V can just do that.

The story is actually keeping me interested. V and Johnny play off one another really well and its just kind of funny that I have a tulpa that rides shotgun with you in your car. Everyone is voice acted pretty well and I don’t think I’ve met anyone that V can talk to on a regular basis that I don’t look.

Night City might be one of my favorite places in a video game at this point as well. Its this mix of modern and futuristic taking a lot of ques from the 2012 Dredd movie. Like, as soon as you leave the industrial and metropolitan area everything just feels like it was forgotten or thrown away by the people at large. On one side you have mega structures with probably thousands of apartments in them, and then on the other side there are literal mountains of garbage bags and thrown away appliances like fridges and flatscreen TVs.

There’s this thing in universe called a Braindance, which is basically this VR headset that lets you go through experiences, either fictional or real, that other people made. You can see people using these throughout the world and its anything from just watching a historical soccer game or playing out an elaborate roleplay fantasy all the way to first person sexual encounters and straight up snuff films.
You’d know what its like to kill someone because it would feel like you’re the one who killed the other guy, or got killed, you basically feel everything the person the shard (Think like an advanced SD card for your brain) came from.

But at the same time, when you go into the slums or the outskirts of town, you can find people in just regular-ass internet cafes or video game cafes. Its like luxury is treated like a hand me down in Night City, where the more affluent can to screw around with advanced technology, but the less fortunate are skill playing COD4 on the 360. Which is probably more true to life than you think.

Also, you can’t use the old internet, its completely swamped by a world ending eldritch super virus being held off by a virtual wall that cuts the new internet off from the old. Gamefaqs is just gone now so all those cool text walkthroughs are lost to time.

Also, yeah, you can pay a heavily armed EMS called Trauma Team to barge into gun fights and come get you guns blazing. Not you in game, but in universe.
Can you imagine just being able to call Nurse Joy with a shotgun for back up?
Night City is very much a good “Drive around” type of video game city. I really like to look at it and rarely use the fast travel unless I’m really in a hurry.

It has its technical issues still. Sometimes the graphics will just wig out, and I doubt this game plays well on anything lower than an 8gb GPU.
Michael Pondsmith is an interesting guy, and he crafted a pretty cool world with his Cyberpunk RPGs. Go check out R. Talsorian games sometimes, the website still looks like it was made in Web 1.0, its kind of fun.

Cyberpunk 2077 ist wie ein Trip in eine Zukunft, in der alles kaputt, absurd und irgendwie total logisch zugleich ist. Du denkst: „Cool, ich bin ein Cyberpunk mit Implantaten!“ – und fünf Minuten später bist du auf einem fliegenden Motorrad, während dein Auto plötzlich beschließt, dass es lieber ein Rasenmäher sein möchte, und dein NPC-Kollege tanzt synchron zu einem Werbespot, während ein Kran über deinem Kopf zusammenbricht. Willkommen in Night City.

Der Humor kommt nicht aus Dialogen – nein, der Humor kommt automatisch aus der absoluten Verrücktheit der Welt. Autos explodieren beim kleinsten Kontakt, Passanten stolpern über eigene Füße und plötzlich hat dein Lieblings-Hackerimplantat einen Bug, der dafür sorgt, dass die Drohnen anfangen, Polka zu tanzen. Du schießt auf einen Gangster und plötzlich verwandelt er sich in einen holografischen Einhorn-Clown … keine Ahnung, warum, aber es passiert.

Die Missionen sind episch, die Story ernst – aber die Welt drumherum ist Comedy pur. Ein Polizeieinsatz? Dein Auto explodiert. Ein Bosskampf? Irgendein zufälliger NPC schmeißt dir eine Leiche in den Weg. Du denkst, du spielst ernsthaft Cyberpunk – aber die Stadt lacht über dich, während sie dich in einen Automaten für schräge Side-Quests wirft.

Das Gameplay selbst ist ein Minenfeld aus absurden Möglichkeiten: Hacke einen Geldautomaten und plötzlich regnet Geld und tote Tauben, stehle ein Auto und die KI denkt, du führst eine Parade an, baue dein Implantat auf Max-Level und plötzlich sprintest du schneller als die Realität erlaubt. Alles möglich, alles Chaos, alles unglaublich witzig, wenn man es mit Humor nimmt.

Koop gibt es zwar nicht offiziell, aber stell dir vor: Du spielst mit Freunden, ihr versucht, eine Mission zu machen, und jede*r landet in einem völlig anderen Wahnsinns-Szenario. Einer fliegt auf einem Lasten-Drohnen-Hubschrauber, der andere wird von einem Müllroboter verfolgt, und du selbst stehst da und denkst: „Ich wollte einfach nur ein bisschen Cyberpunk sein.“ Aber nein, Night City hat andere Pläne.

Fazit:
Cyberpunk 2077 ist Chaos, Wahnsinn und Comedy in einem Neon-Paket. Du fluchst, du staunst, du lachst, und manchmal alles gleichzeitig. Die Stadt ist kaputt, die NPCs noch mehr – und genau das macht den absurden, unwiderstehlichen Charme aus. Wer Cyberpunk spielen will und dabei den Kopf schütteln, die Lachmuskeln trainieren und über jede verrückte Situation staunen will, findet hier sein Paradies.

Kurz gesagt: Cyberpunk 2077 = Implantate, Explosionen, fliegende Autos und total absurde Comedy – Night City liebt dich … ob du willst oder nicht.

Like the Cyberware you find in Night City, your expectations for this game need to be properly calibrated in order to get the most enjoyment out of it. What it actually is, is an action game with light RPG character progression on top of a large and beautiful albeit kind of shallow open-world.

The gunplay itself is fine, as are the skill trees.  CD Projekt Red has never blown me away with the combat of their Witcher games, and I enjoy it here in Cyberpunk more than any of the three Witcher titles but the game really struggles to make the encounters interesting.  Other than wielding a melee weapon or a ranged weapon, there is little difference between enemies and most encounters are just waves of enemies who may take cover but rarely employ any more tactics than that.

The graphics and art design are undoubtedly the best part of the game, and if you want to play something that justifies the steep price of current graphic cards, Cyberpunk will do that for you.

Phantom Liberty is undoubtedly a step in the right direction, brining more intricate quest lines and more satisfying action set-pieces.  I hope CDPR don't have to spend so much time and resource developing an engine, and can devote more time to making the world reactive and interesting in the sequel.

In my opinion this is objectively the best game ever made. Granted, it took a while to get there but there's no other action RPG out there that reaches this level of quality on the individual parts that make up for it's sum. 
In most RPG's you can easily tell where something had to give. Bethesda RPG's for instance, are overall great games but it's always very clear that the combat/gunplay isn't up to a triple A shooter level of quality. Starfield improved over Fallout 4 in that regard but they never truly got rid of that clunky feel. They also have an abundance of load screens to get the open world to work. When you play those games there's never any doubt that you're playing an open world RPG.

Cyberpunk combat reaches a quality level that's typically only found in more linear games where combat is the main focus. That goes for both the gunplay and melee combat btw. 

The same applies to the story, the branching structure, the consequences of the choices you make, it's all done to the absolute highest standard. The world building and sheer amount of dept and lore rivals that of any other big franchise out there including movie franchises like Star Wars. CD Project Red spared no expenses in creating a believable world where everything from the characters to the world they inhabit just makes perfect sense. Big tech gaining political power, the integration of tech directly into the human body. The decline of empathy, social cohesion and municipal services like even something as simple as picking up trash. It's all depicted in a truly believable way.
Added to that, the many different stories you'll find in both the main and side missions vary from hilarious to heart breaking.
All of it is also accompanied by an amazing soundtrack and top tier voice acting. (Actress Cherami Leigh as female V is absolutely amazing)

I could sing this games praises all day but I'll just leave you with this; The only reason NOT to play this game is if the sci-fi theme simply doesn't appeal to you. Some people just don't click with that and I respect that. But if that's not an issue than you really do owe it to yourself to experience this game. I've been playing games since the early 90's and I haven't seen any rpg that tops this overall experience.

It's still somewhat glitchy and buggy even on modern hardware. I've had it crash on me a few times, but it runs well enough for the most part. 

For those who are new and going in blind to how the game plays: the world and missions are similar to playing a Farcry game. The gunplay and combat has a loot/shoot system similar to borderlands or destiny, and there is a character build tree similar to Farcry or Borderlands. It has RPG elements, but it's not an RPG. More of a sandbox action game. The main missions can be a little slow paced and drawn out with excessive dialogue, and the interactions are filled with branching dialogue options that can change up how missions are completed a bit. The game really shines in the side missions. They feel endless, take a long time to get stale, and are where the real value in the game comes from. It's not a masterpiece, but I cant think of a comparable game that has released since this one that is nearly as fun. Havent played the DLC, might pick it up on a deep sale. Game is definitely worth buying on a sale, but I wouldnt pay full price.

I have waited long enough to make this review, and I mean Holy **** what a comeback. We are talking about a rushed mess with a disaster of a launch by one of gamings top studios, to what I can after over 800hrs logged between all copies I own (240 on steam alone at time of making this review) confidentally now say is one of the best RPG's of this Generation...

So let's look back quickly, year is 2020, Cyberpunk releases and it's just a horrid buggy mess. I mean to the point that Playstation pulled it from the PS4 store and refunded people, which as any playstation user can tell you, refunds can be hard to get from PSN. But instead of calling it a wash and moving on, CD Projekt RED hunkers down, radio silence, and they start to work. I'm talking patch after patch, fixing their game, shaping it into what into what it was meant to be, until it happened. UPDATE 2.0/Phantom Liberty releases, not simply just adding more content storywise and otherwise, that was not good enough, no, CDPR releases an entire overhaul of the game that not only improves the game, it changes the very way it plays, FOR THE BETTER! They fix the skill system, balance out overpowered builds, but in a way that with thought and work you can still be powerful but with the feel that no one is a perfect god like person, well at least without a little work.

Visual: Depends on you, I mean that in the best way, Night City is beautiful, and with the right specs it only gets more beautiful. This game is truly next gen and if you are into modding, you can get it looking hyper realistic where you start blurring game to IRL, all you need to do is hit up youtube and you'll see everything from realistic concrete to pores in the skin textures.

Sound: The Sounds of Night City do not disappoint, walking around the city, you will hear the chatter of the masses, horns of cars, the ads from the billboards that tower the city, right down to distant gunfire, or the hum of the neon lights, and speaking of guns, they sound loud, dangerous and deadly.

Gameplay: Gameplay is nice......depending on where you play it and your preference. PC is of course the place to play, either it be mouse/keyboard, or like myself a Xbox Series X controller. There is tons of content between the main story, side gigs, cyberpsycho gigs, NCPD Scanner gigs, random encounters, easter eggs, etc. as of Update 2.3 we have more customization with vehicles and I won't even add in Phantom Liberty whic adds more story, more side gigs and way more customization with new clothing, and new relic perks.

Price: As of early 2026, Cyberpunk 2077 goes on sale often, but honestly I would say its worth it's normal full price, my opinion, although do yourself a favour and buy the ultimate edition that comes with Phantom Liberty. Look Phantom Liberty is a diamond, don't rob yourself of that beautiful experience.

One of the best games I have ever played and spent my eddies on. I did my first playthrough after the Phantom Liberty DLC released, so luckily for me, I did not experience the game in its original buggy state. That said, I still ran into some issues. The biggest culprit was car physics and vehicle summoning in general. I saw my car fall nose first onto the road, spin on its side, crash into objects, or even explode for no real reason. It was honestly hilarious at times, but from a gameplay, mechanical and narrative perspective, this game is a pure masterpiece. I could glaze this game endlessly and write paragraphs about every single aspect of it, but I will try to keep this brief (no promises).

The gameplay is done extremely well and feels impactful once your build really comes online... I mean once you get properly chromed up. There are many different specializations and builds, and each one brings a unique way of progressing through the game and completing missi... eh I mean gigs. The game gives you full freedom to play however you want. You can run in and slice everyone apart with a katana or cybernetic arms, or take a stealth focused approach using hacking. That was my preferred playstyle, quickhacking cameras, enemies, and one tapping them with Tamayura, which is arguably one of the strongest silenced pistols in the game. This variety alone gives the game massive replay value.

Now for the story, where do I even begin. It pulled me in immediately during the 1st act. While the tutorial section felt a bit misleading and presented a different tone than the rest of the game, rest of the game exceeded all my expectations. The world, characters, and lore really spoke to me, especially since I am a big fan of futuristic sci-fi games. The story is presented as a strong and cohesive whole, with multiple branching paths that lead to different endings. It becomes a true emotional rollercoaster toward the end, both in the main story and in the DLC, because by that point you are deeply invested in its world and characters, with romance choices also playing a meaningful role in how hard everything hits emotionally. 

Since my first playthrough included the DLC, my initial ending was the Reed ending, and honestly, f*ck Songbird, you lying b*tch :D. That first ending felt incredibly empty. You end up as a nobody, stripped of your identity, while the world and the people you cared about simply move on without you. It hit harder than I expected. I eventually experienced every ending, and each one was very well written in its own way. Every ending carried its own emotional weight, especially because by that point you are so attached to V and Johnny that saying goodbye never feels easy, no matter how it ends, choom.

Before playing this game, I never really understood the appeal of Cyberpunk as a genre. But now I do and this game has sold me on the whole category.

Cyberpunk 2077 has so much variance in the quality of the game. In some ways, it is stellar and one of the best RPG's made. In others, it feels half-baked and mediocre.

The Good:
- Storytelling is excellent. Tons of great side quests with fun narratives.
- Characterisation is amazing. Judy, Panam, Kerry, River, and Johnny are all amazing with great stories and depth to their characters.
- Voice acting is phenomenal. Cherami Leigh (Fem V) and Keanu Reeves (Johnny) hit it out the park.
- Phantom Liberty is one of the best DLC's ever made. Great setting, excellent story, Songbird and Reed are the best two characters in the game. The quality of this DLC far outshines the rest of the game in my opinion.

The Mid:
- Gunplay varies from being serviceable to bad at times. It really relies on you having to try and make it fun by keeping a high mobility playstyle.
- The setting is excellent visually and in some places feels alive. But in others, it just feels hollow.
- Cyberware system has you spending a ton of resources for the most insignificant gains. Really wish it had a bit more to it.

The Bad:
- The driving is horrible. Vehicles either understeer or spin out with the slightest throttle input. The first person view in the vehicles is way too low meaning you can't see anything while driving.
- Pacing. There's some clear attempts to slow down the stories so you don't feel overwhelmed with quests, but towards the end I feel like I was just doing a mission then waiting 24 hours because I had already done everything else in the game. Got old quick.

Still, I'm happy I played it. 91 hours to 100% in the one playthrough.

[code]Cyberpunk 2077 – без преувеличения культовая игра, вышедшая в 2020 и раскрывшая свой потенциал ближе к 2025 году, после многолетних патчей и исправлений ошибок. Феникс переродился. Отдельная благодарность разработчикам за возможность поиграть на macOS с поддержкой HDR, что добавляет +100% к визуальному наслаждению.[/code]

[h3][b] Мой опыт [/b][/h3]
Я играл на macOS мужским Ви, нетранером (+ умное оружие) с предысторией кочевник. Отыгрывал роль хорошего парня: всех кого мог, щадил, кого мог, спасал. За вторым прохождением начал играть роль женского Ви корпората, Сандевистана (катанами всех режу и ножи в голову кидаю). Эта игра интересна тем, что вы можете ее перепроходить и не потерять к ней интерес ведь сюжет нелинейный, а вариативность отыгрыша огромная. Хотите мечами, махайте, хотите хакайте, а можете просто с автомата всех расстреливать. 

[b] Сеттинг 10/10 [/b]
Вселенная проработанная до мельчайших деталей. Это не игра, это иммерсионный симулятор жизни. Ты погружаешься в этот мир, который живет по своим законам, имеет огромное социальное неравенство, тоталитарное общество, где жизнь тебе не принадлежит. Если вы тоже фанаты антиутопий, то эта вселенная для вас. 

[b] Герои 10/10 [/b] 
Все персонажи легко запоминаемые и хорошо узнаваемые. Харизматичные, интересные, со своей историей. Герои в Cyberpunk не просто NPC, а личности которым есть что рассказать. Трудно поверить что они выдуманы сценаристами, а не живые люди. Ведь проводя время в Cyberpunk ты привязываешься к героям, ты видишь их мотивы, желания, цели. В каждом персонаже есть свои уникальные черты и отличия. Я слышал что образы были созданы с реальных людей и психотипов.  Это объясняет, почему ты их воспринимаешь как реальных людей.

[b] Визуал 10/10 [/b] 
Гулять по Night City да еще и с функцией HDR одно удовольствие. Я не мог спокойно протий мимо локаций не сделав селфи на внутриигровой фотомод, возле каких-нибудь неоновых вывесок или небоскребов. Благо что полиция теперь подтягивается на локацию, где ты совершил преступление, а не спавниться из пустоты из-за спины. 

[b] Сюжет 10/10 [/b] 
Он короткий и это главный его недостаток, но при этом логичный и захватывающий. Держит в напряжении до самого финала. Есть огромная вариативность и нелинейность в квестах как в сюжетных, так и в дополнительных. Даже заказы имеют разные способы решения задач: от стелса до полной мясорубке на локации. 

– СПОЙЛЕР К СЮЖЕТУ (но он очень бесит): [spoiler] Секретная концовка за Джонни, не должна быть секретной, так как по мне она является самой каноничной, когда ты сам (без таблеток и помощи, управляя самим собой, а не отдавая тело Джонни) влетаешь к корпам и всех разносишь. И самое главное никто из близких друзей не гибнет. Но почему этот вариант решили спрятать, мало того еще для достижения данной концовке НУЖНО СКАЗАТЬ ПРАВИЛЬНЫЕ СЛОВА ДЖОННИ на нефтяных вышках. А зачем тогда отношения? Зачем я добивался этих 85% процентов? Чтобы диалог на нефтяных вышках все похерил мне? Это крайне глупо![/spoiler]

[b] Транспорт 7/10 [/b] 
– Тюнинга нет
– Управляемость автомобилей посредственная
– Управляемость мотоциклами УЖАСНАЯ (поворачивать на них невозможно)
– Сцепление с дорогой среднее. Дождь или сухая погода, саванна или городской асфальт – ощущения одни и те же, разница не чувствуется.
– Где летающие автомобили?! ЭТО ЖЕ БУДЩЕЕ!
– Автопилот просто бесполезная вещь, автомобиль на нем постоянно во что-то врезается и сбрасывается

+ Почему сразу нельзя было сделать возможности стрельбы из машины?! Для этого нужно было подождать 5 лет. 
+ Прочность автомобилей улучшили и они теперь не так быстро взрываются (при наличии нужного навыка)

[b] Оружие 8/10 [/b] 
Скажем так, оно интересное первое время, а потом его становиться очень много. Повторы-повторы-повторы только с разными модификациями. Ты просто их подбираешь и потом продаешь чтобы нафармить денег. Улучшать можно только культовое оружие, которого в игре не так уж много, зато хочется найти его все. В Phantom Libery ситуация другая: культового оружия настолько много что не знаешь что с ним делать, просто забиваешь тайник этим добром и забываешь. 

Пожалуй самое интересное из оружия это демоны и скрипты. Они разнообразны и уникальны, хорошо проработаны и интересные. 

[b] Гемплейм 9/10 [/b] 
Классная и интересная вещь – киберимпланты, которые добавляют уникальность проекту и вариативность к игре из-за чего хочется пройти ее снова, но уже с другими имплантами под другую прокачку. 

Диалоги  очень живые и интересные. Голоса приятные, харизматичные и с прекрасной интонацией. Русский дубляж великолепный, вот только где озвучка для Phantom Libery?

[b] Музыка 10/10 [/b] 
Почти каждый 3 трек летит в плейлист. Жаль что нет радио в квартире в Гелине. Музыку из миссий которая играет на больших колонках нельзя послушать по радио когда едешь в машине и это обидно. 

[b] Досуг 4/10 [/b] 
Немного скучно просто кататься по городу, хоть и интересно. Кроме миссий и заказов больше ничего нет. Для разнообразия можно съездить на локации где раньше была миссия, чтобы посмотреть, произошли ли там изменения (что бывает редко). 

[b] Технический аспет 8/10 [/b] 
До пачта 2.0: баги, баги и еще раз баги
После патча 2.0: Их стало меньше, но иногда встречаются. В среднем во время каждой 5 игровой сессии происходит вылет с ошибкой. К примеру если вставать с мотоцикла, при зажатой клавиши поворота колеса в право или лево, то это 100% вылет из игры.

Встречаються локации, особенно часто в Phantom Libery где ФПС падает.

[b] 9/10 (однозначно советую всем и кажому пройти этот шедевр) [/b]

[b][h1]Cyberpunk 2077[/h1][/b]

[i]Cyberpunk 2077 to gra RPG osadzona w futurystycznym, pełnym technologii i niebezpieczeństw świecie Night City. Wcielamy się w V, najemnika, który marzy o zdobyciu sławy i zostaniu prawdziwą legendą tego miasta. Wszystko jednak komplikuje się, gdy w jego głowie znajduje się biochip zawierający cyfrową osobowość Johnny'ego Silverhanda. Od tego momentu V rozpoczyna walkę nie tylko o swoją przyszłość, ale przede wszystkim o własne życie.[/i]

[i]Podczas rozgrywki poznajemy wiele ciekawych postaci i podejmujemy decyzje, które prowadzą nas do różnych zakończeń. Jedną z najciekawszych historii jest dla mnie zdecydowanie linia fabularna związana z Panam Palmer. Jej relacja z V, historia Nomadów oraz kolejne wspólne misje były jednymi z najlepszych momentów całej gry. Zakończenie związane z Panam, które było moim drugim ukończonym zakończeniem, zdecydowanie najbardziej przypadło mi do gustu i zostawiło po sobie najlepsze emocje.[/i]

[h1][b]PLUSY:[/b][/h1]

✔️ Night City i niesamowity klimat futurystycznego miasta.
✔️ Bardzo dobra i wciągająca fabuła.
✔️ Kilka różnych zakończeń, które naprawdę różnią się od siebie.
✔️ Świetnie napisane postacie, szczególnie Panam Palmer.
✔️ Rozbudowane i ciekawe questy poboczne.
✔️ Mocne dialogi i emocjonujące momenty.
✔️ Świetna muzyka i udźwiękowienie budujące klimat.
✔️ Duża swoboda rozwoju postaci.
✔️ Różnorodne bronie, cyberwszczepy i możliwości walki.
✔️ Dużo możliwości eksploracji Night City.
✔️ Gra po licznych poprawkach działa zdecydowanie lepiej niż na premierę.
✔️ Wiele godzin świetnej rozgrywki.
✔️ Wysoka regrywalność dzięki różnym decyzjom i zakończeniom.

[h1][b]MINUSY:[/b][/h1]

❌ Niektóre elementy świata mogłyby być bardziej interaktywne.
❌ Zdarzają się drobne błędy i problemy techniczne.
❌ Nie wszystkie decyzje mają tak duży wpływ na fabułę, jak można było oczekiwać.
❌ Początek gry dla niektórych osób może być trochę wolniejszy.

[i]Cyberpunk 2077 to dla mnie jedna z tych gier, które zostają w głowie jeszcze długo po ukończeniu. Świetny klimat Night City, mocna fabuła, zapadające w pamięć postacie oraz kilka różnych zakończeń sprawiają, że ciężko przejść obok tego tytułu obojętnie. Szczególnie dobrze wspominam całą historię z Panam, która była moim zdaniem jedną z najlepszych linii fabularnych w grze.[/i]

[i]Po skończeniu gry cały czas chce się jeszcze wracać do tego świata i sprawdzać inne możliwości. Zdecydowanie [b]POLECAM[/b] każdemu, kto lubi dobre gry fabularne i klimaty science fiction.[/i]

Hoo boy. This is a ...contested game. There's a lot of history behind how this game came to be and what happened to it when it was let out into the world. So 5 years and a whole DLC later, what's my verdict? It's just not all it's hyped up to be, lads. This game's problem is that it's surface level and superficial to an embarrassing degree given how it was marketed and received. I'm going to be very harsh on this game's level of detail and freedom of expression. Why? Because in a post GTA5/RDR2/BG3 world, open world RPGs just need that level of TLC. If you don't have it, you get punished. ESPECIALLY when you say you have it, and very much do not. 

PROS:
- It's managed to keep enough of the Blade Runner/Neo-Tokyo aesthetic and grime to feel "dystopian but still pretty" in a neon-saturated red-light district kind of way, which is what the Cyberpunk genre should feel like IMO

- Melee combat and netrunner combat feels decent for the most part. The heft of the hammers and the manic katana spam has oomph, throwable knives feel good, and so do most pistols honestly

- The NCPD hustles and fixer gigs are easily the most fun I had "doing stuff" in the game. Very little railroading occurs here and you have a wide range of options to complete your objective. Full stealth is actually pretty enjoyable here.

- The lore around the NCPD/Gigs are environment-based and you can learn a fair bit about the fixers and their respective spheres of influence. 

- You can make people end it all.

CONS:
- Driving sucks harder than a joytoy on Jig-Jig Street. Whatever the hell they did to their roads and driving mechanics, so few cars handle properly it's a nightmare. You can get used to it eventually but it never really stops being a roll of the dice. 

- Guns feel like ass for the most part, especially the full auto ones. Anything above a pistol doesn't look or feel nice to use, except maybe a power shotgun. I think I stopped using assault rifles and SMGs before I was 15 hours into the game, and the various gimmicks like Tech/Smart/Unique versions of these full auto guns are still so unsatisfying. 

- TwinTone sucks and the whole owning cars system sucks, no garage sucks, why in the name of God are the color slots limited I just don't understand why this system is so bad.

Actually, forget this cons section. There's several glaring issues in this game that need their own paragraphs because we need to talk about this holistically. 

Okay, this game is railroady as all heck. You will go and do things as we say, and you will then watch this cutscene. Special mention to the 30 minute sequence following "The Heist". You've only just been introduced properly to V and his Night City shenanigans, then you're thrown into Keanu Reeves'... I dunno anarchist wet dream or something. I lost the ability to play MY character for such a long period of time that I straight up Alt-F4'd the game and afterwards sped through the explanations for what was happening. I didn't CARE about this history lesson, or introduction to Silverhand, I didn't give a single solitary fuck, and this sort of expository bullshit is a recurring feature in the game. I spent as much time avoiding main story quests as possible because of this. This extends to in quest stuff too, even if you're a netrunner build sometimes a bot will either be randomly unhackable or have a forced magic pixel of health remaining because it needs to do a story thingTM like shoot someone to create drama. 

When I said this game was superficial, I wasn't kidding. Oh you have an option to use your "Cool" or "Nomad" backstory dialogue? Yeah whatever man anyway back to the scheduled outcome and voice lines. You know how many times V said something that didn't make sense given my background/previous actions/previous dialogue? Okay, in depth explanation. Panam is a nomad and is trying to help her clan with a thing. If you, as V, have a nomad background (as I did), you can talk about her clan well before this quest and establish your shared knowledge base. Then, in the event, Panam says something to the effect of "Oh god, members of [clan] are dying!" V, nomad V, V who has discussed TWO seconds ago BY NAME this fucking clan, will go "your clan??" This is such a glaring discrepancy I just don't know what to say. There's so much stuff like this in the game. You can scan a dead body from a drone in that same quest and the game will identify it as a certain person. When Panam wonders out loud whether said person is alive, V HAS NO OPTION to say anything! You can't bring it up, you don't even get a dialogue for it. She keeps thinking they might be alive till she finds the body herself. Judy fights the Tyger Claws for control of her whore club, while you as V are completing gigs for Wakako, who has prominent influence in that gang. Can you bring this up to her or talk about the event afterwards? No, of course not. You know how I praised the lore in those NCPD hustles and fixer gigs? If you find evidence that a fixer has failed a gig previously and you are their second/third option, or if you find some interesting gossip about them on a computer in said gig, can you ask them about it? No, of course not. When you find Dakota's failed attempt to save pregnant women in the Badlands, can you commiserate over a drink? No. Am I asking for too much depth from a video game? In a world with Baldur's Gate 3 in it, I don't think so. Even if it is too big an ask, sucks to suck don't know what to tell you. 

The game breaking bugs from 5 years ago weren't plentiful in my run, but there were points where... it breaks the flow significantly when it happens. At a certain point in the DLC, I'm carrying an important character in an important moment to an important place. There is Jesus Music playing, you are princess carrying this person like the Virgin Bloody Mary. You turn the corner and... a door is closed that isn't supposed to be. Can you do anything about this? No, reload an old save and pray that works. If it doesn't? Eh I dunno. Great. 

Speaking of this DLC, okay. It's... fine. There's some extra environmental things to do in Dogtown, and the gigs and other events are of a different flavor to the rest of Night City. There's at least a couple legitimately good quests here, shout-out the "rescue two cops" gig and the "Aguilar" quest for Hands. The addition of the car stealing quests were fun for me because I like that sort of thing. Otherwise, I don't think the writing improves any. It's painfully obvious that what's going to happen won't be happy or fun for you as V.

Speaking of which, why are there so many instances in this game of "you know, that there's a bad idea, we should not do that. Anyway, here's our gonk plan for doing that really dumb thing we said is a bad idea." This is the driving force behind so much of the main story that I started wishing I was listening to Dutch tell me he had a plan again. V is stupid, most people around him are stupid, and it's not fun to be around stupid people.  

There's also a bunch of small things about the game that are unbelievably annoying. Odd lag spikes when you open the map,  that freaking "we like the pain" song, pedestrians staggering INTO the road when you drive near them, the fact that the parry counterattack is TWO hits so you might accidentally kill someone you are trying not to kill, trying to target someone in a car for hacking purposes, trying to get autodrive to not hit something 10 seconds in and shut down, single animations for takedowns, I dunno it's a list. Mods probably fix a lot of this, but the vanilla game has addressed very few of these things. 


This game sans DLC is worth maybe $15. This game with DLC is maybe worth $25. Does that seem extremely low to you? You can get better versions of this sort of game for that price, I promise. If you HAVE to have this game, consider sailing the high seas or something, I just didn't think it was worth it in the end.

1. The World (Night City) Parasite City.

Brutal: Night City is an architectural tumor. Violence awaits you at every turn: in the back alleys of Heywood, Valentino's thugs can shoot you simply for wearing the wrong color sneakers. This is a city where ads offer you a "chromed" body while you stand in a pool of your own blood
Details: Vast garbage dumps outside the city (the Wasteland) are the graveyards of history, where nomads live amid the corporate dregs. And in the center are the Arasaka skyscrapers, literally piercing the clouds, ignoring the poverty below.
Positive: But damn, it's so beautiful! When night falls and the acid rain starts, the city turns into a neon ocean. You can hop on a Yatsuji motorcycle, accelerate to 200 km/h, and just soak up the light. It's an aesthetic ecstasy you can't tear yourself away from.


2. NPC Bones in the Meat Grinder

Brutal: The world is populated by freaks. The Maelstrom gang are literally faceless people, their eyes replaced by red sensors. They feel no pain, only a thirst for blood. Ordinary people (extras) are just noise that scatters at the first shot, reminding you that in this city, you are a predator.
Details: But the story NPCs are a treasure trove. Takemura with his code of honor, Jackie Wells is your best bro, whose death you'll mourn as a true loss.
Emotions: You'll hate Adam Smasher with every fiber of your being. This hunk of metal embodies all that's evil in Night City. His presence on screen evokes visceral fear and rage.


3. Plot Death Sentence

Brutal: The plot isn't a path to glory, it's a path to the grave. You start the game as an ambitious mercenary and end it as a death row inmate with a nosebleed every five minutes. Dexter DeShawn's betrayal at the beginning of the game is Night City's first lesson: trust no one.
Details: The quests here aren't just markers. There's a mission with "Sinn" where you literally nail someone to a cross live on air for braindancing. It's wild, it's immoral, it's pure cyberpunk.
Positive: The story makes you feel alive. Every decision matters. You're not just playing, you're fighting for the right to exist just one more day.


4. Endgame - Aftertaste of Ashes

Brutal: Most endings will leave you with a hole in your chest. You can sell your soul to the Arasaka Corporation and become their property, locked away in the digital prison known as Mikoshi.
Emotions: The ending of "Afterlife," when you're flying into space to heavy rock, is the pinnacle of cool. You realize: you've achieved everything, you're at the top, but the price for it is everything you ever loved. It's honest. It's painful. It's legendary.


5. Bugs Lame implants

Fact: CD Projekt RED spent hundreds of millions of dollars fixing the game after its disastrous launch. Version 2.1 is now what the game should have been.
Brutal: NPCs used to be able to T-pose, and cars could fly into space. It's rare now, but minor interface glitches remind you that this world is held together by a shambles.
Positive: The game has become stable, the enemy AI has learned to surround you, and the police finally call in the SWAT team (Max-Tac) if you get too carried away playing the maniac.


6. The Protagonist (V) The Last Hero

Details: You're V. You can be a quiet hacker who hacks enemies through cameras, or a berserker with a "Monostring" who slices people like cabbage.
Brutal: V suffers constantly. Visual effects of brain hacking, coughing up blood—the game makes you feel his physical destruction.
Positive: The hero progression is top-notch. By the end of the game, you're a death machine that can destroy an entire Militech outpost without breaking a sweat.


7. Virus (Johnny/Relic) Your Personal Demon

Fact: Keanu Reeves is the heart of this game. His Johnny Silverhand isn't just a voice, he's a fully-fledged sidekick.
Brutal: He's an egotist, a terrorist, and an asshole. At first, he wants to kill you. In the middle, he wants to use you.
Emotions: But by the end of the game, you'll be closer than brothers. When Johnny tells you at the end, "Never stop fighting," you realize this virus has become the only one who understands you. This is the highest level of writing.


8. Love Scenes Oasis in the Desert

Brutal: In Night City, love is a commodity. But not for you.
Details: The relationship with Panam Palmer is the best romantic thread in RPG history. From campfire get-togethers to tank-fueled action, it's genuine, passionate, and honest.
Emotions: The love scenes are filmed in such a way that you feel intimacy rather than lust. These are the only moments in the game where Night City retreats, and only two people remain.


9. Music A Loud Cry of Protest

Details: The in-game radio is a masterpiece. The combat soundtrack is a shot of pure adrenaline.
Fact: The song "Never Fade Away" became the game's anthem, still sending chills down fans' spines. The music is the pulse of Night City: angry, fast, and relentless.


10. Graphics Beyond the Possible

Brutal: Your computer will suffer. Without DLSS or FSR, the game will devour all your resources.
Positive: But what you'll see is the future. Reflections in shop windows, steam from manholes, the skin textures of characters. Cyberpunk 2077 is still the most technologically advanced game on the planet. It's the benchmark that will be measured for the next five years.


Final verdict:Cyberpunk 2077 isn't just a futuristic shooting game. It's a story about humanity in a world where people are just spare parts. It's brutal, it's dirty, it's broken, but it's real. If you haven't played it yet, you've missed out on a huge chunk of gaming culture.

So, are you ready to dive into this madness? Good luck then!
