Apesar de se tratar de uma estética futurista, é impressionante como o ecossistema de Night City simboliza bem a sociedade em que vivemos, apenas de uma forma mais excêntrica.

Night City é o retrato de um lugar decadente. Por mais que repleto de prédios gigantes, eventos de entretenimento e uma população enorme e diversificada, é um local onde a desigualdade social se manifesta da forma mais brutal possível. As entidades corporativas possuem tudo: dinheiro, influência, segurança e saúde, enquanto a maior parte da população comum é negligenciada, ao passo que a criminalidade se tornou algo normal. Pessoas morrem aos montes todos os dias e as gangues tomam conta de cada pedaço da cidade, tornando o caos e o conflito rotineiros.

A história desse jogo é incrível, altamente envolvente e imersiva. Toda romantização feita acerca de um mundo tecnológico é posto em cheque: Quem de fato se beneficia com tecnologias realmente impactantes? Quais as consequências de macular a carne com implantes dos mais invasivos possíveis? Outro ponto a se destacar são os personagens, a grande maioria sendo carismáticos e marcantes.

Em termos de conteúdo, Cyberpunk realmente entrega bastante, a história principal não é tão longa, mas possui diversos finais e todos são bem aprofundados em missões próprias para cada um, o que agrega bastante conteúdo. As side quests são diversas também, entregando o dobro de conteúdo da história principal. O jogo possui muitas secundárias interessantes e bem elaboradas, mas também muitas missões repetitivas e de pouca profundidade, o que torna um pouco maçante de fazer tudo.

Graficamente o jogo é espetacular, mas a trilha sonora não me cativou muito. O mapa é bem grande e tem muitos locais e eventos para explorar além das missões. Acredito que o maior defeito do jogo tanto tecnicamente quanto de modo geral são os bugs, que aparecem bastante, alguns até que atrapalham a jogabilidade, sendo necessário recarregar o save em algumas situações.

Curti bastante também as mecânicas e a diversidade de formas de jogar, podendo focar em atuar stealth ou de modo explícito. Cada jogador pode compor a sua build com base no seu estilo de jogo, eu mesmo foquei em atributos, implantes e habilidades voltadas para stealth e hacking, que é mais o meu estilo, mas poderia ter focado em melhorias para combate armado ou combate corpo a corpo, por exemplo.

De modo geral, Cyberpunk 2077 é uma experiência extremamente divertida e marcante. A narrativa, os personagens e a construção do universo em volta de Night City me impactaram bastante. Além disso, o conteúdo, a gameplay e as mecânicas me divertiram por muitas horas. O destaque negativo fica para a alta quantidade de bugs e a repetitividade e superficialidade de muitas missões secundárias.

Cyberpunk 2077’s launch was legendary, and even then, the sheer scope and ambition of Night City blew me away. From the first moment stepping into the neon-lit streets, it was clear this was a game trying to do everything — a living, breathing cyberpunk metropolis full of characters, stories, and detail unlike anything else.

The story was gripping and cinematic, even if rough around the edges. Playing as V, every decision felt meaningful, every dialogue choice shaped your journey, and the narrative moments were genuinely memorable — especially the deeper character arcs and side quests that made Night City feel alive.

Combat and progression offered multiple playstyles — stealth, hacking, or guns blazing — and even on release, there were moments of absolute satisfaction when everything clicked. Cyberware upgrades and character builds added layers of fun, letting you experiment with your own vision of a cyberpunk mercenary.

Night City itself was stunning, ambitious, and full of life. The neon streets, towering skyscrapers, and intricate interiors made exploring feel like stepping into a real futuristic world — sometimes messy, sometimes rough, but always captivating.

Immersion et Narration
L'immersion dans Night City est tout simplement incroyable, grandement aidée par cette vue à la première personne qui ne nous quitte jamais. Pour ceux qui craignent la densité des échanges, le jeu est bien pensé : les nombreux dialogues peuvent être accélérés pour les plus impatients, sans casser le rythme.

Gameplay et Progression
Combats : Un large éventail de possibilités s'offre à nous. Entre l'arsenal varié et les nombreuses améliorations cybernétiques, chaque joueur peut trouver son style.

Difficulté : La progression est assez rapide. Même en difficulté maximale, le jeu reste globalement assez simple une fois qu'on maîtrise ses outils.

Véhicules : C’est un point plus limité. Au vu de l'univers futuriste, on aurait pu s'attendre à piloter au moins un véhicule volant, ce qui manque à l'appel.

Technique et Stabilité
Malgré une très bonne configuration, l'expérience a été ponctuée de quelques crashs assez désagréables. Côté bugs, j'en ai croisé certains (comme des ennemis qui passent à travers le sol), mais rien de rédhibitoire : passer à travers la map ne m'est arrivé qu'une seule fois en 200 heures de jeu.

Verdict
Malgré ces petits défauts techniques et la conduite uniquement terrestre, je conseille vivement de prendre le jeu. L'expérience globale en vaut largement la peine.

Cyberpunk 2077 to dla mnie przykład gry, w której fabuła gra pierwsze skrzypce i robi to absolutnie fenomenalnie. Historia V, relacja z Johnnym Silverhandem i sposób, w jaki gra porusza tematy tożsamości, wolnej woli i ceny ambicji, potrafią autentycznie wciągnąć i emocjonalnie przycisnąć. To jedna z tych opowieści, które pamięta się długo po skończeniu gry.
Ogromne brawa należą się za polski dubbing, który jest po prostu wybitny. Dialogi brzmią naturalnie, postacie mają charakter, a emocje są przekazywane z taką wiarygodnością, że granie po polsku nie jest kompromisem jest najlepszym możliwym wyborem. Dzięki temu Night City żyje, oddycha i brzmi jak prawdziwe miasto pełne różnych historii.
Na każdym kroku widać też mnogość easter eggów i świetnie napisanych dialogów. Rozmowy poboczne, krótkie scenki, ukryte odniesienia do popkultury czy drobne detale środowiskowe sprawiają, że eksploracja miasta jest nagradzająca sama w sobie. Często nawet zwykła pogadanka z losowym NPC potrafi być ciekawsza niż pełnoprawne questy w innych grach.
To produkcja, która pokazuje, jak ogromną siłę ma dobrze napisana narracja w grach wideo. Cyberpunk 2077 nie tylko opowiada historię on ją przeżywa razem z graczem. Dla mnie bez dwóch zdań: 10/10.

Cyberpunk 2077’yi 161 saat oynadım ve şunu net söyleyebilirim: Bazen ekrana bakıp “ulan adamlar ne oyun yapmış” dedim, bazen de sırf Night City’de amaçsızca dolaşmak için oyunu açtım. Çünkü Cyberpunk 2077, bütün kusurlarına rağmen, beni içine çeken nadir oyunlardan biri oldu.

Önce en bariz şeyden başlayalım: Night City. Bu şehir bir oyun haritası değil, resmen yaşayan bir organizma. Neon tabelalar, yağmur altında parlayan asfaltlar, arka sokaklarda dönen kirli işler, gökdelenlerin dibinde hayatta kalmaya çalışan NPC’ler… Bir noktadan sonra görev yapmayı bırakıp sadece yürüyorsun. Müzik kulaklıkta, kamera yavaş, şehir akıyor. 161 saatin ciddi bir kısmı “şuradan şuraya hızlı seyahat edeyim” demeyip bilerek yürümemden geliyor. Çünkü bu şehirde kaybolmak keyifli.

Hikâye tarafına gelirsek… Ana hikâye kısa denebilir ama yoğun. Özellikle karakter yazımı inanılmaz güçlü. Bazı yan görevler var ki, ana hikâyeyi sollayıp geçiyor. Seçimlerin “oyunun sonunu tamamen değiştiriyor” seviyesinde olmasa bile, duygusal etkisi çok yüksek. Bir karakterle yaşadığın kısa bir hikâye, saatler sonra bile aklında kalıyor. “Acaba farklı yapsaydım ne olurdu?” diye düşündüğüm görev sayısı az değil.
Johnny Silverhand konusuna ayrı bir parantez açmam lazım. Başta “tamam işte, bencil şerefsiz” diyorsun ama saatler geçtikçe aranızdaki ilişki garip bir şekilde derinleşiyor. Bazen nefret ediyorsun, bazen hak veriyorsun, bazen de sessizce dinliyorsun. O karakter olmasa oyun kesinlikle bu kadar akılda kalıcı olmazdı.

Oynanış beklediğimden iyi çıktı, özellikle build çeşitliliği oyunu çok taze tutuyor. İlk 30-40 saat “ben net hacker’ım” deyip sonra bir anda katanalı ninja olmam tamamen Cyberpunk 2077’nin suçu. 

Ama…  oyun kusursuz değil. Bug’lar azalmış olsa da tamamen yok olmuş değiller. Özellikle oyunda birden fazla etkileşime girmeye çalıştığım noktalarda örneğin; araç kullanırken haritaya girmeye çalıştığım zamanlar ve "N" tuşu ile fotoğraf çekimine girerken çokça kez oyun attı. Bazı noktalar hala tam stabil değil. Yeni mekan geçişlerinde anlık yüklemelerde karakter geçişlerine şahit olabiliyorsunuz.  Fakat işin ilginç yanı şu: Tüm bu eksiklere rağmen oyunu bırakmak istemedim. Çünkü gerçekten harika bir atmosfer yaratmayı başarmışlar. Her görev mükemmel değil, her sistem kusursuz değil ama ortaya çıkan bütün, beni 161 saat boyunca ekrana kilitleyecek kadar güçlüydü.

Ve sonra… -CYBERPUNK 2077 : PHANTOM LİBERTY-

Açık konuşayım: Bu genişleme paketi oyuna sonradan eklenmiş bir DLC gibi değil, sanki Cyberpunk 2077’nin olması gereken ikinci perdesiymiş gibi hissettiriyor. Öncelikle Dogtown. Night City’nin zaten karanlık olan yüzünün, daha da bozulmuş, daha da yozlaşmış hâli. Burası politik, kirli ve rahatsız edici bir yer. Şehir tasarımı daha sıkışık ama bu sıkışıklık atmosfere acayip iyi hizmet ediyor. Burada dolaşırken Night City’deki o neon romantizmi biraz kayboluyor, yerini paranoya alıyor.

Hikâye tarafı ise… işte burada CD Projekt Red resmen şov yapmış. Phantom Liberty, klasik “iyi-kötü” seçimlerinden çok, “hangisi daha az kötü?” sorusunu sorduruyor. Aldığın kararların sonuçları daha kişisel, daha sert ve daha kalıcı hissettiriyor. Oyunun sonunda ekrana bakıp birkaç saniye hiçbir şey yapmadan kaldığım anlar oldu. Çünkü verdiğim kararın doğru mu yanlış mı olduğundan emin değildim. Ve bu, bence bir rol tabanlı bir oyun için büyük başarı. Özellikle oyunun sonunda kendin için bir çıkış yolu arıyorsun. Her şey bunun üzerine kurulu; hayatta kalmak, kontrolü geri almak, kendin olmak. Ama finalde fark ediyorsun ki Night City’de kimse gerçekten kazanamıyor. Seçtiğin son ne olursa olsun, ya bir şeyleri feda ediyorsun ya da içinden bir parça eksik kalıyor. Songbird (So Mi) meselesi bunun en net örneği. Onun hikâyesinde hangi tarafı seçersen seç, kazanan yok. Yardım edersen bedeli ağır, yüz çevirirsen vicdanın rahat etmiyor. So Mi kurtuluyor mu, yoksa sadece başka bir kafese mi giriyor, emin olamıyorsun.

Ama karakterler inanılmaz yazılmış. Özellikle politik gerilim hissi çok güçlü. Casusluk teması oyuna bambaşka bir tat katıyor. Daha az kahramansın, daha çok piyon gibisin. En önemlisi de Phantom Liberty, Cyberpunk 2077’nin yıllardır taşıdığı o “yarım kalmışlık” hissini büyük ölçüde kapatıyor. Hikâye daha derli toplu, anlatım daha net, tempo daha iyi ayarlanmış.

Toparlarsam; Ben oyunu çok büyük bir keyifle oynadım. Şehrin o verdiği his, derinlik çok güçlü. Aynı zamanda karakterlerle bulunduğumuz etkileşimler, ( ki Romantik seçenekler daha geniş tutulabilirdi :) ) hikaye akışı özellikle Phantom Liberty'de çok güçlü ve beklenmedik. Bunca yılın sonunda artısıyla eksisiyle Cyberpunk oynanmaya değer bir oyun. Keyifli oyunlar ♥

An open-world game made by the Witcher devs, in a dark cyberpunk dystopia. 

A large, but not excessively vast, open-world. Instead of a huge city of boringness, there is a densely packed city with lots to do. 

Legitimately engaging main missions and side quests; you won't get any fetch quests here. Even side quest will surprise you with a twist or turn when you least expect it.

Incredible and believable voiceacting. CDPR hired high-dollar voice actors flex their acting muscles.

Guns are fun to shoot.

Some cars, like the muscle cars and sports cars, are fun to drive. The more rugged vehicles have machine guns for death races.

Cybernetics and perk trees are fun to experiment with. Reassign perks at will to change your build at any time. In terms of cybernetics, don't skip the mantis arms for maximum mayhem.

Remote quickhack enemies to short out their cyberware, or overheat them, or poison them, or remote detonate their grenades. Or use the Sandevistan cyberware to give yourself 10x speed reflexes and become the Flash with a sword and/or gun.

Load into the game and let the environmental storytelling wash over you. Read all the text logs and listen to the radio stations. Take in the context and backstory of Night City, the fall of the USA, and the rise of the New United States of America. Absorb just how rampant unchecked capitalism and corporate power run roughshod over the common man.

Play as an amoral mercenary out to save your own skin, or recognize the injustice of the system and burn it all down, or die trying.

Oh, yeah, Keanu Reeves is in this. And in the DLC expansion, Idris Elba.

Make 2026 the year you play Cyberpunk 2077, if you haven't already.

My thoughts on this aren't fresh, but in short this game will probably go down as one of my favorite RPGs of all time, and certainly my favorite for first-person RPGs. High praise for sure, but the presentation and immersion of this world alone has such draw factor for me that I felt as if I was there in Night City. My experience with this game got me to go watch the anime, check out the (included) TTRPG CP2.0.2.0. and buy and play CP:Red, and some of the music gets a listen from me outside of the game.

I am typically one to enjoy games for mechanics and developing skill at playing the game, so DOOM: Eternal, Dark Souls/Bloodborne/Elden Ring and games like it tend to be what I invest time into. But this game pulled me in from its story and characters, and was able to make me genuinely care about them more than any other game in my memory has.

At its core it is a FPS with RPG mechanics, so if you can handle yourself in an FPS you'll have no issues there. What far and above makes the game special is how it represents the world of Cyberpunk and allows you to (albeit mostly through combat) immerse yourself in it and, well, roleplay. I do wish there was more depth and options in 'social' interactions, like if you had to interact with the corps that own the chrome you buy or spend more time in areas that the unnamed NPCs travel in and out of constantly. More of the slice of life events and interactions are needed for the sequel, and on that note as someone that doesn't really engage in romance in games we desperately need things to do with our chosen partner. Just showing them around the apartment and having them stay the night is nice and all, but I was hoping we could have them drive around with us or do some kind of GTA IV date minigame to keep that immersion of living in Night City.

I also think having some semblance of a morality or infamy system would further aid in that immersion; are you a solo that specializes in key targets and you're known for clean assassinations, or are you that solo that's on the verge of cyberpsychosis that just slaughters every banger in the area when you go hunting? Are you such a feared 'runner that corps buff their security or send Netrunners after you to eliminate you? Sure, making a name for yourself is a plot point and one of the drives of V in the beginning stages of the game, but we don't really feel the effects of being one of the most capable and involved characters in the city in 2077. We don't get recognized or interacted with outside of major characters, and while those are great and well written the verisimilitude can fall apart at the edges if you stop to look outside the plot and instead at the immersive sim aspect of the game. The presentation, while in my opinion some of the best we've seen in gaming, cannot make up for the lack of world interactions.

These are things that I hope CDPR is working to include in the sequel, but what we have here is still a truly special FPS RPG experience that I wish I had experienced sooner. I think I'm due for a revisit to Night City...

Cyberpunk 2077 has come a long way and now feels like a genuinely great experience. After a rough launch, the game is much more stable and enjoyable, and it finally shows what it was meant to be.

Night City is easily one of the game’s biggest strengths. The city feels alive, dense, and full of style, and the cyberpunk atmosphere really hits. The main story is engaging, sometimes dark, sometimes emotional, and a lot of side quests are surprisingly well written, to the point where they really stick with you after you finish them.

The gameplay gives you a lot of freedom. You can focus on hacking, stealth, guns, or melee combat, and play the way you want. Character progression feels rewarding, and you really feel your character getting stronger and more efficient over time.

I played the game with mods, and honestly, it makes a huge difference. The graphics look even better, the city feels more immersive, and outfit mods add a lot of style and variety. Being able to fully customize your character and their look makes the whole experience even cooler. With mods, the game can look absolutely amazing.

From a technical point of view, the game is now in a very good state. The visuals are great, especially on a decent PC, the lighting looks fantastic, and the soundtrack fits Night City perfectly. The voice acting and sound design also do a great job at pulling you into the world.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is absolutely worth playing now. I’d definitely recommend giving it a shot and diving into Night City.

Le gameplay offre une grande liberté. Que ce soit le hacking, l’infiltration, les armes à feu ou le corps-à-corps, chacun peut jouer comme il le souhaite. La progression du personnage est gratifiante, et on ressent clairement l’évolution au fil des heures.

J’ai joué avec des mods, et honnêtement, ça change énormément l’expérience. Les graphismes sont encore plus beaux, la ville est plus immersive, et les mods de tenues ajoutent beaucoup de style et de variété. Pouvoir personnaliser son personnage à fond rend le jeu encore plus cool. Avec les mods, le rendu visuel peut vraiment être impressionnant.

Techniquement, le jeu est aujourd’hui dans un très bon état. Les graphismes sont superbes, surtout sur un bon PC, l’éclairage est réussi, et la bande-son colle parfaitement à l’ambiance de Night City. Le doublage et le sound design renforcent encore l’immersion.

Au final, Cyberpunk 2077 vaut clairement le coup aujourd’hui. Je recommande sans hésiter de se lancer et de découvrir Night City.

Cyberpunk 2077 é um jogo muito divisivo para mim. De um lado ele tem uma dos enredos mais cativantes que eu já joguei, por outro ele me deixou uma pessoa mais cética com anúncios de videogames. Depois de 5 anos eu voltei a Night City, é foi uma loucura.

No fatídico dia de 10 de Dezembro de 2020, foi lançada uma bomba atômica chamada Cyberpunk 2077, eu fugindo de spoilers não vi que essa bomba era quase injogável no PS4. Fiz minha Major Motoko Kusanari do Paraguai, encontrei meu primeiro bug quando o meu carro ficou preso em grade que apareceu do nada, esse foi o início do caos. Todo tipo de Bug possivel eu tive: bug do carro voador, bug dos npcs se desligarem, crashers, uma missão secundária não podia ser terminada porque o jogo travava, 15 FPS quando chovia, Pop-ins constantes, saves corrompidos, entre muitos outros. Depois de zerar o jogo pela primeira vez (fazendo o melhor final), eu fiquei em um dilema de esperar o jogo ficar mais estável (que ninguém sabia quando isso aconteceria) ou aceitar o fato que o Cyberpunk nunca tinha que ter sido lançado pro PS4. Eu aceitei que essa bomba nunca ficaria jogável num console de 2013, então pedi meu dinheiro de volta e esperei o dia que eu jogaria esse jogo quando ele saísse do alpha.

5 longos anos depois eu volto pro jogo que foi um evento canônico na minha vida, vamos a review.

[h3]Ambientação[/h3] - Da mistura de Los Angeles com Hong-Kong nasceu uma cidade tão terrível de se viver mais incrível em se explorar das Terras Baldias às noites coloridas da Rua Jig-Jig. Cyberpunk 2077 acertou em cheio em criar Night City, uma cidade que vende a fábula de qualquer um pode se tornar uma lenda, mas somente consome a alma de seus habitantes e transformam as lendas em produtos.
A sensação de andar pela Corpe Plaza, onde as principais Megacops ficam uma do lado da outra, dá um senso de pequinês onde parece que esses prédios vão engolir todo mundo abaixo deles.
Já as terras baldias dão uma sensação de liberdade, como se fosse possível fugir do mundo miserável de Night City.  
E Santo Domingo lembra à gente que tanto no futuro quanto no passado pobre sempre vai morar mal.


[h3]Missões[/h3] -  As Missões principais são ótimas mas poucas e não se aprofundam em outras áreas de Night City. Como outras Megacops como a Militech que tem bastante influência na Lore de Cyberpunk mas mal aparece no enredo do jogo e, sem a DLC o ato 3 de leva diretamente para missão final do jogo sem nenhum preparo e tão abrupta que realmente deu pra ver que o jogo foi rushado. Já as missões secundárias são hit or miss, ou é inacreditável como a quest do prefeito de Night City e as quest relacionadas ao Johnny e a Samurai, ou é vai lá e mate aquele cara, roube aquele item, etc. 

[h3]Personagens[/h3] - A Panam é a best girl desse jogo ([strike]fora uma certa netrunner[/strike]). Acabou… 
Brincadeiras a parte o elenco principal transborda carisma, faz o jogador se importar demais com os problemas deles. Desde a Panam com a impulsividade dela e o medo dela de ter tomar a liderança dos Aldecaldos, ou a Judy que a história dela me deixou [i]Sandevastated[/i]. O Takemura tem aspecto de conteúdo cortado, já que ele assim como a Panam e a Judy, ele tem bastante papel na história mas não tem nenhuma missão subsequente após a missão do sequestro da Hanako. Devido o relacionamento complicado com o Johnny o Kerry é muito interessante de fazer as quest dele, mas o romance dele é complicado pq ele só se interessa pelo V por causa do Johnny. Já o River e a prova do rushamento desse jogo, pq claramente o Takemura tinha que ser o romance masculino pra a Valerie, mesmo o River estando ligado as melhores quest do jogo o romance dele não convence.

Da parte dos personagens a mais surpreendente foi a conexão que eu tive com a minha V, pelo motivo da maioria dos personagens de RPGs são só uma concha para o jogador colocar a sua alma, já a Valerie me deu uma sensação que é uma personagem viva que o jogador só está vivendo uma parte da vida dela (Assim como o/a Shepard em Mass Effect). Infelizmente o jogo tem poucos diálogos relacionados a sua origem mas os poucos têm sempre me são interessantes, ver como cada V enxerga Night City dependendo da origem aprofunda bastante a personagem.

[h3]Dublagem[/h3] - Das maiores insanidades da dublagem brasileira esse jogo é a maior, só se viu um nível tão louco de localização no Chaves ou na dublagem americana de Ghost Stories. Mesmo assim a dublagem dos personagens principais são muito boas e dos personagens secundários é legal. Mas eu pessoalmente gostaria de saber quem teve a ideia que todo mundo a Rua 6 tivesse a voz do Bolsonaro, quando é apenas um npc genérico tudo bem, mas quando é um personagem que aparece na cutscene de introdução do V [i]StreetKid[/i] é difícil levar a sério a cena. Já os Aldecaldos são divisível pra mim de lado a Panam com sotaque do interior de Minas dá um charme maior pra ela (em 2020, eu fiquei completamente apaixonado pela Panam por causa desse sotaque), os outro aldecaldos são muito difíceis de entender com esse sotaque forçado, como diria um comentario que eu vi no Youtube: “A maioria dos Aldecaldos parecem querer entrar na praça é nossa, como o novo Nerson da Capitinga”.

[h3]Gameplay[/h3] - Uma coisa surpreendente foi a gameplay ser muito boa, a CD Projekt nunca foi muito boa com o combate nos The Witcher, sempre foram travados e com a câmera que mais atrapalhava do que ajudava. Já em Cyberpunk a [i]gunplay[/i] é muito divertida com cada tipo de arma tendo uma perculidade diferente, e as Builds são muito diferentes das outras. Na minha primeira campanha no PC eu fiz a minha V ser uma netrunner seguindo a escola do Rache Bartmoss, a sensação de você hackear uma câmera matar todos os inimigos com hack ou com explosivos em lugares estratégicos sem ser detectado é muito foda. Mas a Build do Sandervistan com proficiência em arma branca também é incrível.  

[h3]Gráficos e Performance[/h3] - O jogo é lindo mesmo que o meu computador não tenha condição de usar o [i]raytracing[/i]. Já a performance é estável em uma 3060 o jogo roda no alto a 60 Fps com algumas quedas no centro da cidade por causa da alta densidade de veículos e npcs, e com DLSS. 

[h3]Conclusão[/h3] - Cyberpunk 2077 é uns dos melhores jogos que eu já joguei, que eu gostaria muito de colocar no meu Top 10. Mas a sensação de ser um jogo que não atingiu o potencial completo me inibe de gostar ainda mais dele, mesmo com as melhorias que o jogo teve eu ainda não consigo sentir o jogo que me vendaram na E3 de 2018 e 2019, a marca de jogar esse jogo em 2020 ainda persiste só com o lançamento do próximo Cyberpunk eu realmente vou conseguir ver o 2077 pelo o que ele é, em vez do que ele poderia ter sido.
No final o jogo é uma experiência única que cada jogador terá, e realmente valeu a pena esperar o Cyberpunk sair do Alpha.

I don’t care what anyone says — [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] has come a long way. What started as a rough launch is now one of the most immersive, emotional, and downright beautiful open-world RPGs out there.

Night City feels alive — not just visually, but emotionally. You can walk down a random street and get lost in the atmosphere. The lighting, the music, the voices in the background — everything feels deliberate.

[b]The writing and characters?[/b] Incredible. V and Johnny Silverhand have some of the best chemistry I’ve ever seen in a game. Every major quest feels handcrafted, and even the smaller side jobs carry real emotional weight.

The [b]Phantom Liberty[/b] expansion took it all to another level. Idris Elba’s performance is top-tier, and the spy-thriller tone fits perfectly with the world’s darker side.

The gunplay and combat feel tight and weighty now. Cars actually drive properly, cops react like they should, and performance on PC is smooth. CDPR really pulled it together — it’s not just “fixed,” it’s reborn.

[hr]
[b]Pros:[/b]
[+] Deep, emotional storytelling
[+] Fantastic performances
[+] One of the most detailed open worlds ever made
[+] Great combat, driving, and stealth systems (post 2.0)
[+] Top-tier music and atmosphere

[b]Cons:[/b]
[–] Still the occasional bug or jank moment
[–] You’ll wish there was even more

[hr]
[b]Verdict:[/b]
Cyberpunk 2077 went from “what could’ve been” to “what games should strive to be.”
If you skipped it at launch — now’s the time.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a beautifully violent machine that finally runs like it should’ve at launch. If you’re the type that needs a game to respect your time, your immersion, and your standards… this one can, now—but only if you come in with the right mindset: treat it like a city you’re surviving, not a checklist you’re completing.

Night City is the main character. The lighting, sound, density, the way streets feel alive—this game has that rare “I’m inside it” aura. And the story? It hits harder than people admit. The pacing, the characters, the moral gray, the “you’re not special, you’re just stubborn” energy—Cyberpunk understands that power isn’t given, it’s taken… and usually it costs you something. That’s my lane.

Gameplay-wise, it’s an operator sandbox. You can build V into a problem-solving weapon: stealth ghost, loud psycho, hacker puppeteer, blade-demon, gunslinger—whatever fits your ego. The best part is when your build starts clicking and you’re no longer reacting… you’re routing the entire fight. Walk in, scan, isolate targets, break the room, leave. More heat, less foam.

Is it perfect? No. Sometimes the open world still shows seams. AI can be inconsistent. A few systems feel like they’re one patch away from greatness. But the core experience—story + atmosphere + build freedom + combat flow—is strong enough that I stopped nitpicking and started living in it. That’s the real test.

Who I recommend this to:

People who like games that reward planning, efficiency, and build mastery

Anyone who wants a single-player world that feels like a real place

Players who enjoy being the calm, surgical menace in the room

Who should pass:

If you need flawless NPC AI or ultra-reactive sandbox sim behavior

If you hate dialogue/story and only want nonstop action

Verdict: Cyberpunk 2077 is the comeback story people argued about for years. Now it’s simply a high-tier RPG with a top-tier city. If you play like an operator and build with intent, Night City will pay you back.

★★★★☆ (4.5/5)

A more detailed review below (with possible hints at spoilers, non-censored):

Pros:
+ Decent map design
+ Decent worldbuilding
+ Tons of quests, main and side, plus all side hustles
+ Several interesting characters, each different in their own ways.
+ Main story was decent. However, it lacked substance in the middle. The prologue and most endings stand out. The rest of it was...fine. But nothing outstanding imo.
+ Phantom Liberty was way better written than main story. The pacing, the variety of missions, the endings, the main theme..."The Killing Moon" was genuinely one of the best video game missions I've ever played. And there was humor in just perfect amounts.
+ While the gameplay is rather simplistic, it was also highly addictive. Great variety in firearms and melee weapons, plus all quickhacks.
+ A good character creator
+ Good voice acting all-around
+ Decent soundtrack and radio stations
+ Keanu Reeves delivers excellently as Johnny Silverhand. Good and memorable character, without which the story just wouldn't be the same.
+ Idris Elba delivers excellently as Solomon Reed. Just as memorable as Johnny.
+ Romance options for both male and female V are decent
+ SO MUCH CLOTHING OPTIONS
+ The game very much instills some darn good existential dread into you in several ways. Johnny's story, the main story and Phantom liberty BOTH, Jefferson's quest...
+ The endings offer decent variety and stay true to the theme of cyberpunk. Yet despite this, one does leave you with hope.
+ Judy. Not gonna elaborate. And Jackie (sadge).
+ Pretty graphics with decent optimization options
+ All personal apartments are surprisingly stylish in their own ways. Although there could've been more customization options
+ Decent cyberware customization
+ Simple but decent crafting system
+ Role-playing aspect is well implemented. You can very much be positive/open-minded, or straight-up asshole. Perfect.
+ With all the worldbuilding, characters, graphics, missions and slang, the game's pretty darn immersive, even if NPCs kill the immersion too often.
+ Decent character skill tree which lets you tailor your own gameplay and combat experience together with cyberware.
+ Street Kid lifepath fits V's voice acting and character like a glove. Genuinely think this was the way the game was meant to be played. Adds to immersion.
+ Decent humor all-around. You take too long to reply to Takemura, and he asks if you've got "what they call ADD". 

Cons:
- Some characters from the main story were pure missed potential. Seriously, come on. Especially from the prologue. Dex, Evelyn, Jackie, T-Bug, Stout. Takemura, Yorinobu and Smasher, too. This is my biggest gripe with the game. Let's throw Rogue in there, too; she could've had at least a bit more prominent role.
- While Phantom Liberty was a step-up from the main story in terms of depth and pacing, the main story could've used this more, too. Yes, CDPR learned their lessons, but having finished Phantom Liberty I now feel like the main story can't never quite reach the same level. The whole ACT2 of main story was pretty meh. Side missions and character quests filled the void, yes, but I'd expect more from the main storyline itself.
- Alright, I already mentioned Yorinobu. But seriously, he was the lamest antagonist ever. He's like someone you just acknowledge, but actually has practically zero role in the story. Same goes for Smasher; dude just exists and offers one lame-ass boss fight. Lol.
- "The Tower" ending could've used more work. Seriously, way more. It's like CDPR deliberately wanted to give you a middle finger for your choices. The sour taste it left me with was worse than any other game has. Thankfully it's only one of the endings. There's certain plot and character details it doesn't take into account at all and undermines all your achievements so far.
- You can't use Gorilla Arms with polished nails. Come one, they're like the coolest melee weapon, contending with Mantis Blades, but I had to resort to the latter just because of this.
- Muamar's haircut. As Johnny puts it, "El Clowno"
- NPCs drive like idiots. They also jump in front of your car if you're about to drive past very close.
- NCPD is ridiculously incompetent and will start a firefight with you out of any possible excuse, even if you're just taking down thugs that're killing and mugging pedestrians. There's no arrest or jail mechanic, and escaping the cops becomes ridiculously easy with even half-decent cyberware and guns.
- Having "Nocturne OP55N1" read on my screen half of the playtime was pretty annoying
- Bugs. I know the game was one massive bug itself when it came out, but 5 years later, it's still buggy. NPCs disappearing under the floor in the middle of combat or getting stuck in surfaces in ragdoll mode. V's figure clipping through clothes in equipment menu. NPCs bouncing over obstacles on the street.
- Game crashed several times from simply accessing main menu or entering a new area. At least the crashing didn't lock me from completing any mission.
- The one and only hacking minigame gets tiring fast. Variety needed.
- All computers in the world are of similar design. Really pushes back on the immersion, especially if you want to read every single conversation and file there is.
- NCPD Scanner side hustles are a decent idea, but they get very tiring VERY fast. There's several tens of them, all practically just of similar design. Variety needed. On the positive side, some of them reward you with firearm blueprints or other higher-grade stuff.
- Most areas in all Fixer side gigs are of rather one and only design and become a repetitive experience over time.
- Most cars and motorcycles seem damn useless to own. You'll get by with what you have by default. And fast travel is more useful anyways.
- Kinda was hoping for a longer questline for Claire
- SAMURAI is painted as a legendary band, but their music is genuinely underwhelming and very generic-sounding
- Map was too small, especially dogtown.
- You can't remove damage/firemode mods from firearms

 * The game runs smooth and looks incredible. If you have been holding off because you are worried about glitches you are doing yourself a disservice.
 * While some people complain that the city feels like a sandbox with no depth I found it completely immersive. The atmosphere is unmatched.
Story and Content
 * The writing is top tier. Some reviews say the dialogue is cringe or the choices do not matter but I disagree completely. The story paths feel heavy and the emotional beats actually land.
 * There is a ton of side content to dive into. If you ever feel like you are burning yourself out on the main story mode you can just go get lost in the side gigs and character quests for hours.
 * Unlike what some critics say about the world being empty there is actually plenty to do if you bother to look beyond the main quest markers

Cyberpunk 2077 est, selon moi, un jeu très solide sur le fond, mais beaucoup plus discutable sur la forme.

Profil : actuellement +20h de jeu et niveau 20-25.
Je suis l'opposé du mec qui rush le jeu en un temps record. 

D’un côté, l’intrigue est réellement prenante. L’histoire principale, les quêtes et l’univers cyberpunk sont extrêmement intéressants et bien construits. Night City a une vraie identité, et tout ce qui touche aux fonctionnalités du jeu — hacking, combats, styles de jeu, personnalisations — est riche et varié. On sent clairement le potentiel et l’ambition derrière le projet.

Mais là où le jeu déçoit, c’est sur des aspects pourtant essentiels pour un open world moderne.

❌ Points négatifs

- Une physique et une technique datées
La physique et la modélisation font franchement vieilles, au point de rappeler des jeux sortis autour de 2012. À ce niveau-là, GTA V (sorti en 2013) est largement au-dessus, ce qui est décevant pour un jeu aussi récent et ambitieux. Pour un open world cyberpunk, Cyberpunk 2077 a clairement manqué le coche.

- Un gameplay rigide et une liberté limitée
Les déplacements du personnage manquent de souplesse, et la liberté d’exploration est parfois artificiellement bridée. Certaines zones sont inaccessibles en véhicule (moto, voiture) sans réelle justification logique : ce n’est ni un problème d’espace ni de cohérence, mais juste un blocage imposé. Or, l’essence même d’un open world, c’est de pouvoir faire ce qu’on veut.

- Des PNJ peu crédibles
Les PNJ sont très basiques : peu d’activités, comportements répétitifs, une IA peu intelligente et peu cohérente. On peut même croiser plusieurs fois les mêmes personnages dans un même quartier, ce qui nuit fortement à l’immersion et donne un vrai sentiment de manque de diversité.

- Des bugs visuels et des détails absents
Il arrive de voir des voitures apparaître brusquement en tournant la caméra, parfois même superposées les unes aux autres, créant un chaos visuel peu naturel.
De plus, malgré la réputation graphique du jeu et la mise en avant du ray tracing, le personnage joueur n’a aucun reflet sur les miroirs, les vitres ou les flaques d’eau. C’est étonnant pour un jeu qui prétend accorder autant d’importance aux détails.

- Un système de tutoriel très mal expliqué
C’est un gros point noir du jeu. le didacticiel reste extrêmement pauvre. Les rares explications concernent surtout le combat, tandis que le reste des mécaniques est peu ou pas expliqué. Certaines fonctionnalités importantes, comme le crafting, manquent cruellement de clarté, au point de ne toujours pas être comprises après de nombreuses heures de jeu. Les explications sont soit absentes, soit trop superficielles, ce qui donne l’impression que le joueur doit tout deviner par lui-même.

Je tiens à rappeler que Red dead redemption 2 et God of war sont sorti 2 ans plus tôt que cyberpunk2077.

✅ Points positifs

+ Univers cyberpunk très réussi et immersif

+ Histoire et intrigue vraiment captivantes

+ Systèmes de gameplay riches (hacking, combat, styles de jeu)

+ Ambiance et direction artistique marquées

Conclusion::
Cyberpunk 2077 est un jeu ambitieux avec un univers et une histoire de grande qualité, mais il est freiné par une technique datée, un gameplay rigide, une IA peu crédible et un manque cruel d’explications sur ses propres systèmes. L’expérience reste intéressante et prenante, mais elle laisse constamment le sentiment que le jeu aurait pu — et dû — aller beaucoup plus loin. Je continue d'espérer des améliorations constantes du jeu et je vais même mettre le pouce bleu pour motiver les devs à continuer de travailler sur le projet.


Update +50h : plus j'y joue et plus nombreux sont les bugs/crash comptabilisés. C'est assez fréquent et nuisible à la longue, dommage pour un "open world". J'ai rien à dire sur l'histoire, mon avis global ne change pas, juste qu'au début j'en étais à "quelque bug" mais là ça devient un euphémisme. Le jeu, ne serait-ce que sans bug, serait très bon.

Durante mucho tiempo estuve indeciso entre comprar este juego o seguir dejándolo pasar. Sinceramente, aunque es bien sabido que se arregló después del desastre que fue su lanzamiento, en mí todavía quedaban esos rezagos de un juego “mal hecho” y el temor de invertir tiempo en algo que no estuviera a la altura.

Pero creo que no sorprende a nadie decir que Cyberpunk 2077 es, en realidad, un juego maravilloso, incluso en 2026, cuando por fin lo terminé. Lo que más me atrapó fue su capacidad de meterte en Night City: una ciudad que se siente viva, densa y con una identidad muy marcada. El diseño de distritos, la estética, los letreros, los NPCs, la música ambiental y esa vibra futurista decadente logran que muchas veces quieras caminar sin objetivo solo para ver qué encuentras. Es de esos mundos donde constantemente te distraes, pero en el buen sentido.

La historia de V está muy bien llevada: tiene momentos íntimos, decisiones que pesan, y un tono que mezcla muy bien la ambición, la tragedia y la supervivencia. Además, la forma en la que el juego maneja la identidad, el control, la pérdida y lo que significa “ser tú” dentro de un mundo tan agresivo, hace que varias misiones se sientan más personales que “solo una quest más”. Y aunque hay personajes que claramente brillan más que otros, el elenco principal tiene carisma y deja huella. Hay diálogos que se sienten auténticos y misiones secundarias que podrían ser historia principal en otros juegos, tanto por escritura como por impacto.

A nivel jugable, me gustó mucho la libertad para armar tu estilo. Puedes jugarlo como shooter, como sigilo, como hacker, como un híbrido, o simplemente como un personaje ultra agresivo que entra a romper todo. El sistema de talentos y progresión permite experimentar, y la variedad de builds hace que realmente sientas que “tu V” no es igual al de los demás. También se agradece que el loot y el equipamiento tengan sentido dentro de la fantasía del juego: implantes, mejoras, armas con personalidad, y opciones para adaptarte a tu manera de jugar.

En cuanto a lo técnico, se nota muchísimo la evolución respecto a lo que fue en su lanzamiento. La experiencia hoy se siente sólida, estable y disfrutable. No es perfecto, pero en general ya no se siente como un juego “a medias”; se siente como el producto que debió ser desde el inicio: pulido, ambicioso y con una visión clara.

Ahora, mi único “pero” (y es bastante importante) es la dificultad. Aun jugando en la más complicada, no se siente realmente desafiante. Tal vez durante la primera hora, cuando no tienes buen equipamiento ni armas y estás limitado, pero eventualmente el juego se vuelve muy fácil en todos los sentidos. Llega un punto en el que tu personaje escala tanto, y tus herramientas son tan fuertes, que los combates dejan de requerir estrategia y se convierten en rutina. Esto le quita tensión a varias misiones que, por narrativa, deberían sentirse peligrosas o “al límite”. Me habría encantado que el juego castigara más errores, que los enemigos fueran más inteligentes o que existiera una curva de dificultad más agresiva para mantener esa sensación de riesgo constante.

Aun con eso, la experiencia general fue excelente. Es un juego que, cuando te atrapa, te consume: por su ambientación, por su historia, por su estilo y por esa sensación de estar viviendo algo único en un mundo crudo y espectacular. Terminarlo deja esa mezcla de satisfacción y vacío que dejan las buenas historias, cuando sabes que ya no vas a volver a vivirlo por primera vez.

En fin, estoy feliz de haber jugado esta obra. Si alguien todavía tiene dudas por lo que pasó al inicio, entiendo perfectamente el miedo… pero a estas alturas, Cyberpunk 2077 es una experiencia que vale mucho la pena.

上高中时就在小黑盒上入了《赛博朋克：2077》，直到上大学解锁了人生第一台电脑才有机会玩到，先说结论：目前经过5年来多次优化版本的《赛博朋克：2077》绝对算的上是一款顶级3A,它基本满足了所有我对赛博朋克风格的游戏的幻想，绝对值得购买。
        谈到这款游戏，就不得不说到夜之城，它简直是赛博朋克社会的完美标本，2077以这座罪恶都市为载体，用极致的美学与锋利叙事照见现实，给玩家带来了深刻的体验。以荒坂为代表的科技巨头控制了国家的经济与军事命脉，牢牢的把控着底层人的生活；沃森区、威斯布鲁克的灯红酒绿与纸醉金迷；太平洲的贫民窟污水横流，帮派的林立割据与底层人的挣扎，令现实世界的我甚至也感到窒息，这一切恰是阶级固化的真实写照。
        除了庞大的世界观外，2077的人物塑造与叙事也极具张力，V与强尼的意识共生、三种出身与多结局的叙事玩法以及大大小小的支线都令人眼前一亮。同时中文的配音也是顶级，各种国粹疯狂输出。唯一的遗憾就是V的结局，无论怎么选择核心都是难逃一死，当然了，不影响它是一款优秀的开饭世界赛博朋克风3A大作。

I got the game at launch and even if it was buggy and very rough around the edges, you could feel the love that was put into it simply from the world that CDPR created and the depth of the characters throughout the story.

Fast forward many years later and it finally got the time it needed to become what it was meant to be from the start; a masterpiece like no other.

It's a dark yet colorful world where you find yourself stopping to explore every little details as if you were really there. Night city is immersive, as tall as it is wide, full of life and secrets to discover.

This game hooks you fast and it does it before you even have time to realise what's happening. There is one downside to it though. Once you go through the main story and DLC, you might feel a void no other game will fill for a while. It's one of those games you wish you could erase your memory just to live it for the first time again.

It's in my top 3 games of all time and I'm glad it finally got the love it deserved.

Jogo muito bom, acabei de terminar a historia principal. Porem o Cyberpunk é aquele famoso jogo que foi claramente negligenciado pela empresa e foi feito as pressas com bastante coisas cortadas. Eu diria que o Cyberpunk é um jogo que não foi tão aproveitado assim e é um jogo que você espera ter muito conteúdo mas pelo menos a historia principal não. Meio que a historia principal se transforma o "tutorial do jogo" e o resto do jogo que é de verdade. 

Um exemplo disso é o dialogo, você pode escolher muitos diálogos mas a maioria não muda tanto a historia, maior parte só muda a narrativa. As habilidades, cybernética, sistema de hack e etc não são tão aproveitados assim durante a historia do jogo, além que pra mim pelo menos achei o stealth do jogo muito fácil, e mesma assim se você não quiser jogar em stealth dá pra sair matando geral com a arma no jogo por que é bem fácil matar os cara. Não ironicamente único boss que eu achei difícil do jogo foi o primeiro, por que é quando você tá aprendendo as mecânica do jogo mas o resto, é bem fácil de matar, eu matei o ultimo boss acho que nem deu 20 min sem morrer nenhuma vez, isso jogando na dificuldade normal. 

Eu comecei o jogo no marginal, depois vou querer zerar de novo com as outras categorias, e agora quero fazer as missão secundaria para eu realmente aproveitar esse jogo. Pelo menos no Reddit dizem que algumas missão secundaria do jogo são melhores que a historia principal, que ainda dá pra fazer bastante coisas além dos finais alternativos (fiz só 2 até agora) e ainda tem bastante coisas para fazer. E pelo que eu entendi, Cyberpunk é aquele clássico jogo que não se joga somente a missão principal, uma coisa muito parecida com muitos jogos RPG como o Skyrim por exemplo, e que se você quer jogar o jogo de verdade você tem que fazer as outras coisas do jogo como os serviços e as missão secundaria para aproveitar de verdade. 

Eu recomendo Cyberpunk pra quem quer começar jogar jogo RPG e ter uma experiencia de como funciona RPG sem precisar praticamente estudar o jogo antes, e sem precisar fazer 40 task com 200 diálogos chatos mitológicos pra ler antes de acontece algo foda de verdade.[i](apesar do Cyberpunk ter um pouco disso pelo menos nele [b]para mim[/b] dá pra tankar essas partes chatas.) i just finished my first playthrough of cyberpunk 2077 and WOW did i have fun! this game is a first for me in a lot of ways-- my first game where fps is a major component, my first triple A game, my first 3d game with multiple endings, my first game where i truly enjoyed being violent... wowza!! so, admittedly, i might be a little biased cause for a lot of things, i have no experience with previously and so naturally cyberpunk 2077 is what my brain registers as the 'best option' 

i really, really loved this game. and im honestly glad i chose to play it now considering the current political climate of the world because i feel like it, embarrassingly enough, pushed me into educating myself more of what's ongoing between governments and corporations. sighhh

for things i really liked: i thought the cast was sooo good. panam, misty, viktor, rogue, judy, kerry etc etc... theyre all so good!!! everyone felt really fleshed out, though admittedly i do have some complaints about the romanceable characters, but i think Everyone is aware of the issues with river so i digress. panam and kerry in particular really stood out to me, as we help them go through a journey of finding themselves in a world where they feel lost and empty... [spoiler]aiding panam in finding her place back with her family and pushing kerry into realizing he has the power to be his own person and legend if he simply stops waiting for the shadow to keep encompassing him and intentionally steps out into the sun himself[/spoiler]. yay!
i also really loved johnny and v's relationship. sometimes johnny's acting felt a bit wooden, but ignoring that, i LOVED the way their relationship progressed throughout the story! the scene where he says he [spoiler]regrets having the samurai concert because v is more important than him rehashing good moments with some of the people who used to be the most important to him is so... awee... johnny!![/spoiler]
and the worldbuilding!! yes!!! i think that is the main point everyone will bring up when speaking of the positives of cyberpunk. its just SO GOOD
also, the colours!!!!! it blew my mind when i realized that [spoiler]the afterlife lights basically blanketing all the people within in green is like the same exact colour as johnny sees the world... rogue may not love johnny romantically, but he was a portion of her life that she can only ever look back on fondly despite all the hard times. ugh, you are so amazing rogue!! i was trying to think of reasons as to why johnny's colour is green, and the first idea that popped up in my head was maybe it had to do with the colour of money? i know eurodollars arent exactly the brightest green, but in the real world money is typically that colour. it's pretty interesting that the man so vehemently against corpos and the way capitalism views human beings as code and data sees the world in green. perhaps it is symbolism of how he sees the world as it is, and still chooses to spin whatever ideal and perspective he can cause he refuses to follow the norm? he doesnt care if green = prosperity and social status, green is his colour now... maybe? i havent thought much of it since i only finished playing like 2 hours ago. but yeah! lots to think about ^_^[/spoiler]
also i really enjoyed (what i personally interpreted to be) the main themes of cyberpunk 2077 but LOL i think itd be pretty stupid to just basically spoil the message of the game here so

anyways, for some things that I Didnt Like As Much: ahhghhhhb some of the acting felt kinda bad... the voices sometimes would not come off emotional enough and sometimes when V (i played female V) would act tough it DID NOT FEEL TOUGH AT ALL!!! T_T 
sometimes the dialogue felt a little lame??? sometimes
i wished there was more cohesion with the quests and the personal status of V. also, just johnny in general.... i know!! i know!! i said that his relationship with V is one of my favourite parts of cyberpunk, and it truly is!! but at the same time, he just kind of felt like a dissapointing character? like he's built up as this cool, terrorist (i am aware that those are two conflicting adjectives okay) dude that hates corpos and YEAH sometimes he is but at other times he is just so lame?? at one point when you choose to [spoiler]help judy and the joytoys to take over clouds in response to the abuse the joytoys there experience, johnny says something like "are you really going to help these whores?" and its like...???? his whole character is being against major corporations (i am aware cloud isnt a MAJOR CORPORATION but it is still a well-known establishment that doesnt see its workers as people and only transactions for money) and he just.. doesnt care? huh? especially after seeing what happened to evelyn and how much of a POS woodman is? i think that specific line really hurts the character the game set him up to be[/spoiler]. despite being so anti-oppression, he only shows concern at specific times which is in my opinion pretty weak writing considering he's supposed to be THE anti-corpo guy T_T i get that hes a jerk who doesnt actually care for the individual, thats the whole point of his character-- but i feel like the game is too.. A Stunning Redemption — Night City Finally Lives

I came in skeptical after the launch drama, and I’m leaving stunned. Cyberpunk 2077 is now the definitive open-world RPG it always promised to be: Night City is vivid and dangerous, the characters are raw and unforgettable, and the gameplay—after the 2.0 overhaul and Phantom Liberty—lets you play the game you want, not the one the bugs forced on you. Every mission feels purposeful, every street corner hides a story, and the choices actually carry weight.

Why I keep playing

Worldbuilding: Night City is immersive on a level few games reach; districts, NPCs, and ambient storytelling reward exploration.

Characters and writing: Johnny, Judy, Panam, and others are complex, memorable, and emotionally resonant.

Gameplay variety: Stealth, hacking, gunplay, and cyberware builds all feel meaningful and fun.

Presentation: The soundtrack, art direction, and atmosphere combine into a cinematic experience.

Minor gripes

Occasional AI oddities and rare bugs still pop up, but they never break the experience.

Some systems could use more polish for endgame balance.

Verdict  
If you love story-driven RPGs and atmospheric worlds, this is a must-play. It’s a remarkable comeback—ambitious, stylish, and deeply human. Buy it, dive in, and let Night City get under your skin. Recommended.

I hated this game when it first came out. Back then, I was trying to run it on an old laptop with a GTX 1650, and it was a total disaster. The optimization for older mobile cards was non-existent low FPS, blurry textures, and constant stuttering. It left such a bad taste in my mouth that I just uninstalled it and moved on, thinking it was a lost cause.

Fast forward to now: I finally upgraded my rig to an RTX 50-series card, and my mind is officially blown. Playing this with everything cranked to Ultra and DLSS Frame Gen enabled is a completely different world. And honestly, the ending really got to me. It was genuinely emotional, and I was actually happy to see the story conclude the way it did, it felt earned and meaningful after everything the game puts you through.

The one annoying thing?

It’s 2026 and we still don’t have a proper AZERTY keyboard preset :/ Having to manually remap every single key just or just switch to an english preset on my windows settings just because I’m on a French layout is such a chore for a AAA title. It’s a small detail, but it’s a constant reminder that we’re still an afterthought for the UI team.

Bottom line: If you have the hardware to push it, Cyberpunk is a masterpiece. Just don’t bother trying to play it on an old GTX laptop save yourself the heartbreak and wait until you have a decent RTX card

I played this at launch on base PS4 and it was a hilarious, aborted disaster. Lacked 60% of what was advertised, couldn't run on low, and was mechanically a 5/10 RPG with 6/10 shooting mechanics. But even then, there were a few bones of a decent game. The story had potential and the world, when it was loading properly, was beautifully immersive and masterfully realized.

Now, a few years on, this feels like the game I thought I was buying. Total overhauls to combat, progression, performance, graphical fidelity, and character customization. Massive, sweeping additions to the world and systems. Tens more hours of story content. And the single greatest city ever rendered in interactive media. It still suffers a bit from the common issues of being developed for wide appeal on a bloated budget, but this game is one of the easiest to recommend that I've ever played. It has something for everyone, and for most, it has more than any other game will offer you at the price point. 

The Side Jobs stand out as really exceptional content and the new endings included with Phantom Liberty are some of the most emotive scenes I can remember playing in a 30-year career of playing games. I would still buy this on sale because games are expensive and the world is falling apart around us, but this is a must-play game and a generation-defining classic.

This game has come a LONG way from the broken mess of a launch it had back in 2020.

CDPR have spent the last few years fixing and improving upon everything that players had taken issue with during its initial release, bringing it from a 5/10 to a solid 8 or 9.

Let's start with the changes. The combat and progression mechanics were given a massive overhaul, now making it much easier to naviagte the skill tree and properly build your V to the way you like them. In regards to combat, the gun-play and melee are far less clunky than they were on release, allowing you to engage with enemies in however way you see as efficient or fun. Quick-hacks are especially fun to use in combat.

Mission layouts. While a lot of the side quests from the 2020 release are still there with the very basic "option A or option B" solutions, the Phantom Liberty expansion brings with it far more engaging main and side quests with solutions that can range from grey to even darker shades of grey on the moral compass. More often than not you find yourself having to pick what you feel is the lesser evil and for a dystopian cyberpunk universe it fits perfectly.

The main story is still the same as it was at launch - only with feck all bugs. V is thrust into a life or death race against time as the artificial soul of Johnny Silverhand (Keanu Reeves) is slowly taking over your mind and body - not by his own choice, mind you - and so V must find any way to remove Silverhand and regain control. When it comes to the main story, unlike the pre-PL side quests, your choices DO have an affect on the plot overall. Not just in how it ends but in how you persue relationships.

Then there's Phantom Liberty where V has been contacted by the mysterious Songbird to help thwart a plot to kill the president of the NUSA with the help of Solomon Reed (Idris Elba). But not all is as it seems as you delve into a labrynth of twists and turns that will have you questioning not only your own morality but the morality of every character you come across in that expansion. Who to trust, who to keep at a distance, facing the consequences of your choices - be they good or bad - and a very strong replay value as there are a variety of ways the expansion can end.

In the end Cyberpunk 2077 has become the game it was supposed to be at launch, and - if you're looking for a good cyberpunk sci-fi RPG to sink your teeth into - is well worth adding to your library to experience Night City in full.

在绚烂的废墟中重生：《赛博朋克2077》与它的夜之城

当清晨第一缕人造阳光穿透摩天楼的缝隙，洒在“来生”酒吧门口时，V正站在全息广告牌的闪烁光影中，思考着如何花掉昨晚赚来的最后一点欧元。这不是现实，却比许多人的现实更加真实——《赛博朋克2077》构建的夜之城，一个既令人向往又让人恐惧的数字乌托邦。

夜之城：赛博朋克美学的终极呈现

踏入夜之城的那一刻，视觉冲击是压倒性的。高耸入云的摩天楼如同金属森林，全息广告投射出永不熄灭的欲望，浮空车在高架轨道间无声穿梭，而在地面，贫民窟的霓虹灯在潮湿的街道上投下病态的光芒。这种极端垂直的社会结构不仅是美学选择，更是对资本主义晚期城市分层的直白隐喻：顶层是公司精英的空中花园，底层是挣扎求生的无名之辈。

CD Projekt Red打造的这个虚构加州大都会，其灵感直接源于威廉·吉布森、菲利普·K·迪克等赛博朋克文学先驱的作品，却以21世纪的游戏语言进行了重新诠释。在这里，科技没有带来普遍福祉，反而加剧了不平等；人体改造不是增强人类，而是模糊了人与机器的界限。夜之城是一个自相矛盾的存在——它既是技术的奇迹，又是人性的坟墓。

V的故事：身份危机的赛博格寓言

玩家扮演的V，无论选择哪种出身——街头小子、公司职员或流浪者——最终都将卷入一场关于身份与存在的危机。当叛逆摇滚明星强尼·银手的意识芯片意外植入V的大脑，两个灵魂开始共享一具身体，游戏提出了赛博朋克的核心问题：在意识可以数字化、身体可以组件化的世界里，“我”究竟是谁？

V与强尼的关系构成了游戏最动人的叙事线索。最初是宿主与入侵者的对抗，逐渐演变为某种奇特的共生，最终成为超越友谊的联结。这种双重意识体验在游戏机制中得到巧妙体现：强尼会不时“接管”V的身体，提供对过去事件的另一种视角；玩家则在对话选项中平衡两个性格的反应。这种设计不仅推动剧情，更让玩家亲身经历身份解构与重构的过程。

玩法与选择：非线性叙事的实验场

《赛博朋克2077》继承了《巫师》系列选择与后果的传统，并将其复杂程度推向新高。游戏提供了三种基本职业路径——黑客、技师和战士——但真正的自由在于这些路径的无缝融合。你可以用黑客技能让敌人的武器失效，用技术能力破解安全系统，或是纯粹依靠火力杀出一条血路。

任务设计的多路径解决方案体现了真正的角色扮演精神。以游戏早期的“抢劫”任务为例，玩家可以选择正面突击，利用黑客技能从后门潜入，通过对话技巧骗过守卫，或是完全避开战斗。这些选择不仅影响即时结果，更会以微妙方式改变后续游戏世界：你饶恕的敌人可能成为日后的盟友，你偷取的数据可能解锁隐藏剧情线。

争议与重生：从灾难到文化现象

2020年12月，《赛博朋克2077》以近乎灾难的方式发布。主机版性能崩溃，BUG如影随形，承诺的许多功能缺失。游戏成了过度营销和开发压力的典型案例，CD Projekt Red的声誉一夜之间跌入谷底。

然而，接下来的故事出人意料。通过长达两年的持续更新、修复和免费内容补充，特别是2023年的“自由幻局”扩展包和2.0大更新，游戏逐渐实现了最初的承诺。社区模组制作者的创意贡献，如改善AI、增加自定义选项、修复小问题等，也形成了开发者与玩家共同修复游戏的独特景观。

这种转变本身就带有赛博朋克色彩：一个破碎的系统通过集体努力和自我修正，最终实现了某种形式的救赎。今天的《赛博朋克2077》不仅是一款游戏，更是一个关于艺术创作、商业压力与玩家期望的复杂寓言。

赛博朋克精神的数字载体

《赛博朋克2077》最终的成功不在于它完美实现了什么，而在于它敢于尝试什么。它试图在一个互动媒介中捕捉赛博朋克文学的精神内核：对技术乌托邦主义的批判，对身份流动性的探索，对社会边缘者的关注。

在夜之城的某个角落，你会找到一个 graffiti：“这里的灯光永远不会熄灭，但大多数人也永远无法真正醒来。”这或许是对我们数字时代最贴切的隐喻。我们生活在技术奇迹中，却常常陷入数字疏离；我们比任何时候都更加连接，却比任何时候都更加孤独。

《赛博朋克2077》邀请我们进入这个矛盾的世界，不是为了提供答案，而是为了让我们提出正确的问题：当身体成为可自定义的商品，人性价值何在？当记忆可以数字化存储，真实体验意义何在？当社会被公司完全控制，个体自由何在？

这些问题没有简单答案，但提问的过程本身已经是一种抵抗——正如所有伟大的赛博朋克作品所提醒我们的：在最黑暗的系统深处，人性的火花仍然在闪烁，等待着被点燃。夜之城可能是个没有英雄的地方，但每个在它的街道上寻找意义的玩家，都在以自己的方式成为那个火花。

Quando iniciei minha primeira gameplay fui de forma despretensiosa, muito devido a uma pessoa que insistiu muito para que eu jogasse. 
Após a introdução do game fiquei com aquela impressão de: "caraca o que foi tudo isso, que louco!".
Após múltiplas missões, uma mais insana que a outra eu finalizei a primeira vez, e vou ser sincero, nunca me senti dessa forma, eu fiquei triste mas não soube explicar, um luto literário em conjunto com uma epifania, uma sensação de que perdi algo muito importante e ao mesmo tempo uma visão de que devo rever algumas coisas na vida, como estou focando ou deixando de focar certas coisas importantes, foi tão impactante que eu fiquei semanas refletindo sobre tudo que passei durante minha gameplay.
Claro que após zerei os outros finais, mas, ainda sim considerei o meu primeiro final o verdadeiro, principalmente por eu ter seguido firmemente as ideias que o V desenvolve como personagem, ser uma lenda, dedo no cu e brotaria, mas é aquilo que o próprio jogo indaga, ninguém é feliz em nightcity e o quanto você está disposto a sacrificar para alcançar o seu objetivo?
O meu V sacrificou tudo, e esse foi um dos pontos que mais me pegou.
Por fim super recomendo o game, ele é aquele tipo de jogo que tem personalidade, você sente alma em cada pedacinho do jogo, é o tipo de jogo que ao invés de te dar respostas ao final, ele virará para você e te fará uma pergunta direta: "Valeu a pena?"
E sendo sincero essa pergunta vem como um soco no estômago...
Por fim, super recomendo e provavelmente irei zerar mais algumas vezes até vir o próximo em meados de 2030.

Obs. Fechei o phantom liberty também, e que espetáculo de DLC, praticamente outro jogo se for parar para pensar, também recomendo quem ficou com aquela sensação de quero mais após zerar!

We all know how this game started out, back on launch day. There's video compilations of it, hours of glitches and endless optimization issues and bugs.

These days it's pretty much stable and the best thing I can say about it all is that the game is a victim of its own ambition. It's actually pretty great. It's got good combat, it's got a decent skill tree, it's got good level scaling, good difficulty, fun options, interesting setting stuff, interesting story, whatever. It's moddable, it's versatile, it can look pretty, it can look like a potato. It's all great.

But you know, sometimes it can break and remind you that it's ultimately extremely janky. Quests break, cars decide to spawn 100 feet in the air, pedestrians decide to dive head-first into your car like it's an olympic event and they're going for gold. It's all good, it's fine. It's jank. It's okay.

It's not a perfect game. Goodness no. It doesn't work if you install it on a hard drive. Some of the main characters are insufferable. Some of the missions are cookie-cutter. There's entire bits of the game that got ripped out and never got replaced because of balance issues. The enemy AI is very exploitable, sometimes it's too overpowered, sometimes you dunk on them, it's all fine. It's all good, it sucks, it's great. Whatever.

The science fiction setting is great. Mike Pondsmith didn't really know what he made, some big conglomerate decided to expand on his setting with love and care, and the best thing is that he didn't get in their way. He vetoed some stupid things, he allowed some other things, he enthusiastically went with the best things, he's on a radio station, there's an anime. It's great, it's a good setting. I kind of want to run a campaign in it, on the tabletop version, give or take house rules because the actual tabletop game is also jank.

But you know what? I've sunk 350 hours and 4 playthroughs into it. It's a good game. Well worth the money. Phantom Liberty made me do the big think. It's pretty good.

Hoje, especialmente depois das grandes atualizações e da DLC Phantom Liberty, dá pra dizer sem exagero: o jogo finalmente se tornou aquilo que prometeu.

O maior acerto do Cyberpunk é a imersão em Night City. A cidade é viva, densa, cheia de histórias pequenas acontecendo nos cantos mais inesperados. Não é só cenário bonito, é um lugar que te engole. Os personagens são muito bem escritos, com diálogos naturais e escolhas que realmente pesam. Dá pra sentir que as relações importam, principalmente com Johnny Silverhand, que deixa de ser só um “passageiro irritante” e vira um dos personagens mais importantes na vida do nosso protagonista V.

Sobre a DLC Phantom Liberty é, sem exagero, o melhor conteúdo que Cyberpunk 2077 já recebeu. Dá pra sentir que a CD Projekt Red colocou tudo o que aprendeu ao longo dos anos aqui,
A história tem um clima forte de thriller político e espionagemm, A cidade Dogtown é suja, opressora e cheia de tensão.
Os personagens são excelentes, com destaque para a Songbird, que carrega o peso emocional da DLC, e o Solomon Reed.
No geral, Phantom Liberty é a prova definitiva de que Cyberpunk 2077 encontrou sua identidade. É madura, triste, intensa e inesquecível. Uma DLC que não só expande o jogo, mas redefine como ele será lembrado.

Prima di giocarlo su PC, l’avevo giocato e platinato su PS5 quando uscì, prima delle patch correttive o di qualsiasi aggiornamento, e mi piacque davvero moltissimo. Certo, non è il gioco che ci aspettavamo: diverse promesse sono venute a mancare, ma per me questo titolo rimarrà sempre nel cuore. La storia è scritta davvero bene, così come i personaggi, che per me rappresentano il cuore pulsante del gioco. Personaggi che sembrano vivi quanto la città stessa, anche se in maniera più superficiale.

Cyberpunk 2077 non mi ha mai annoiato, non l’ho mai trovato frustrante, e mi ha saputo coinvolgere in un modo che pochi altri giochi riescono a fare. Ogni missione, anche quelle secondarie, aveva qualcosa da raccontare, qualcosa di unico, e l’atmosfera di questa città alla Blade Runner è così viva e immersiva che spesso mi sono fermato solo per osservarla, rapito da un mondo tanto straordinario quanto inquietante (si, inquietante!).

Non c’entra nulla, ma consiglio la lettura di Il Neuromante di William Gibson, libro da cui Cyberpunk 2077 prende sicuramente molta ispirazione.

Заключается это в диалогах (местами умопомрачительными), в его репликах (уже ставшие платиновыми) даже когда мы не в сюжетном задании и моментах, когда он появляется в виде голограммы. То есть:
- Наблюдать за его историей интересно 
- Всё взаимодействие с ним интересно 
- Остальные персонажи на его фоне НЕ интересны
Неплохо синхронизировано это с Ви (За которого мы играем), но опять же главный герой здесь по натуре не он. Сильный, харизматичный персонаж затмевает игровую куклу, то есть наемника Ви.
Квесты дополнительные местами бывают занимающими, но в основной массе это принеси, подай, убей, лей лей не жалей. Неплохо передан дух этой вселенной киберпанской, где уже практически у каждого вставлены импланты, брекеты и дилдо. Можно отметить неплохую картинку и внушительного уровня графику.
Где-то на сотом обновлении разработчики догадались добавить очевидные решения, например, можно сбросить ветку прокачки в игре с уклоном на RPG. Кстати о прокачке, хотелось бы уточнить у игроков. Кто либо играл в вариации "взломщика-хакера". На мой взгляд это скучно и уныло и без того медленный темп я разбавил билдом киберсамурая с катаной. Может что-то ещё забыл из таких положительных моментов.

Если же говорить о слабых сторонах либо противоречивых, то конечно же ЛИЧНО мне бы хотелось коридорный шутер с элементами RPG (раз уже у CD Projekt RED из любой игры получается Ведьмак). Так как открытый мир здесь пустейший, никакой глубины у него нет. Какие-то магазинчики с едой, чтобы восстановить хп. Просто ходить и убивать, бить полицейских или бандитов на улице? Про систему розыска и полицейских в принципе лучше не говорить, поберегу свои нервы. NPC могут на некоторые вещи не реагировать, либо реагировать самым тупым образом. Есть конечно прикольная ветка про киберпсихов (монстры из Ведьмака), но зачем он нужен то, открытый мир такой? "Аряяяя это не ГТА"! А нах вы вообще лезете в эту стезю? На пользу игре бы пошел условный коридор и нормальный качественный шутан, упор на стрельбу в основе своей. А не на смену курток и кроссовок и выбор размера полового члена (ыыыыы выберу самый большой) в меню создания персонажа. В сухом остатке RPG дрочильня, где нужно каждые 10 минут менять оружие, потому что у того на 10 единиц урона больше и вапщета оно "Легендарное". На этом фоне я удалял игру 3-4 раза и осилил полное прохождение только с 5-того. Всё давал игре шанс и не понимал, почему им так нравится исследовать этот невероятный Найт-Сити. По итогу открытый мир примерно на уровне Mafia II (2010). То есть можно ездить на машине куда-то и зачем-то...
Транспорт конечно отдельная история. Весь транспорт в игре управляется просто абсурдно, ну вы возьмите какие-нибудь заготовки не знаю. Почему так плохо сделана простейшая езда, неужели нет лекал по которым можно скопировать езду и физику автомобиля. Единственный автомобиль, который не вызывает чувства апатии и желания повеситься во время езды это Porsche 911 (930) Джонни Сильверхенда. Видимо производитель настоял на том, чтобы он управлялся как надо и не готов получать удар по имиджу. Поэтому в основном я передвигался через быстрые точки и пешком в комбинации с двойным прыжком (имплантом).

Придраться ли к таким вещам, что после стрельбы по колесам они не спускают? Придраться ли к физике окружающего мира и разрушаемости? Или вы что все деньги Киану отдали? Зато есть голые и возможность ходить в кибердрочильню. Смешно смотреть, что люди недовольны багами и производительностью, но их в целом устраивает всё остальное и особенно им нравится дрочить пункты на карте с надписью "NCPD" или покупать машины (!) в игре с самым худшим управлением за всю историю.

Слышал, что высоко оценивают сюжетное дополнение. Не играл в него и не углублялся, но вот есть ощущения, что там тоже сюжетка тащит. Это новая история и может ради неё и стоит брать DLC.

Из-за затраченных денег на эту игру, из-за сильной, нарочитой рекламной кампании и конечно же хайпа эта игра не заслуживает такого ценника. То есть ожидание - реальность. Моё мнение, что игра возложенные на неё надежды не оправдала.

Pros

• Impressive graphics if you have the rig to run it. 
• The skill-trees are fun to explore and play around with.
• Voice acting is pretty good.
• Brain dance mechanic is cool.
• When the main story finally gets rolling, it gets semi-interesting.

Cons

• The first 6-7 hours is a tutorial. An interactive movie where not one choice is made by the player. This is just a lengthy prologue. 32% of the players fall off before The Heist is over, according to statistics.
• Is it impossible to program mirrors in games anymore? All the mirrors are black! Making the excessive character-customization almost moot.
• The dialogue sometimes feels hackneyed, with technical "future"-jargon shoehorned in. Seems a bit ham-fisted and cringe-inducing. But this probably stems from the 1988 pen-and-paper game.
• The hacking/breach-minigames are boring. Was this the best they could come up with?
• Where is the emergent gameplay? Most of the time, I feel like V is on rails.
• RedLauncher - We don't need this bloatware 
• Putting skill points into Body and going guns blazing makes the game super easy, even on Hard. Inhalers, grenades and even health itself regenerate super quickly. 
• Still not completely bug-free after all these years. I've also had multiple crashes.


Conclusion: Night City feels empty despite its size. It's mostly set dressing and not something the player can interact with in a meaningful way. There is no emergent gameplay here, only traversing from quest marker to quest marker, going through the motions. In contrast to another CDPR-game, The Witcher 3, Cyberpunk 2077 feels vapid behind all the fancy, shiny graphics. 

Score: 6.5 out of 10.

Okay, yeah — Cyberpunk 2077’s launch was a dumpster fire. Bugs? Crashes? V popping out of the map? You’ve heard the horror stories. But here’s the thing: if you can look past that (or just play post-patch), this game is insane. Like, in the best way.

Night City isn’t just a city. It’s a living, breathing nightmare I actually wanted to explore. Every street corner, every neon-lit alley, every little side job feels meaningful. And the characters… God, the characters. Johnny Silverhand is an absolute menace and heartbreaker. Panam, Judy, Kerry, Rogue, Misty — they hit different. You care about them, which is rare for an open-world game.

Gameplay-wise, it’s a little wild. Late-game V can slice through anyone like butter (and yes, I felt like a legend doing it), but that’s kind of the point: you’re supposed to be that unstoppable nightmare in Night City. Most of the tension comes from choices and relationships, not just health bars.

Honestly, the story is brutal, raw, and surprisingly human. You’ll laugh, you’ll rage, you’ll probably cry a little (don’t judge me). If you can survive the early technical headaches, it’s absolutely worth it.

проведя в игре более ста часов и пережив все возможные финалы, включая историю из phantom liberty, я могу сказать одно: это игра, которую нужно прожить, а не просто пройти

атмосфера найт сити - это главный герой. город давит безысходностью, марит неоновым блеском и затягивает в свой ритм. здесь хочется просто находиться: бродить по ночным улицам, слушать переговоры нпс. музыка (просто рай для ушей) и визуал работают в идеальном симбиозе, не выпуская вас из этого хрупкого, жестокого мира

сюжет ведёт от одной сильной эмоции к другой, плавно переплетаясь с побочными историям. многие из второстепенных заданий - это не просто "вопросики" на карте, а полноценные мини-истории, которые раскрывают город и персонажей с новых сторон. они естественно вплетаются в историю, делая её ещё более насыщенней (кроме некоторых исключений, по типу "ви осталось жить пару недель" и "чтобы игуана выросла надо 90 дней")

особое место занимают отношения ви и джонни сильверхенда. это одна из самых сложных и пронзительных связей между персонажами. вы начинаете с ненависти, страха, приходите к вынужденному союзу, а заканчиваете чем-то, что сложно назвать простой дружбой. это история о двух потерянных душах в одной голове, которые берут разные качества друг у друга, и финал этой истории оставляет после себя тихую, щемящую пустоту

дополнение phantom liberty лишь усиливает всё вышесказанное. догтаун - это найт сити в концентрированном виде: грязнее, опаснее и циничнее. новая сюжетная линия - идеальный шпионский триллер (типично для идриса эльбы), где каждый выбор имеет вес, а новый финал переворачивает с ног на голову представления о жертве и спасении (осознание джонни - тому пример)

геймплей даёт свободу. стрельба, хакерство, стелс, ближний бой - нет ощущения загнанности в один стиль. древо прокачки позволяет улучшать сильные стороны, игнорируя неинтересное. да, это не эталонный шутер, но механики отполированы и работают как часы

в итоге, cyberpunk 2077 сегодня - это тот редкий случай, когда игра через годы патчей и дополнений стала тем, чем должна была стать с самого начала. это не просто игра, это пережитый опыт. история о том, как в погоне за статусом легенды можно найти гораздо более важное - кусочки самого себя, разбросанные по неоновым улицам бесконечно живого и бесконечно мёртвого города. 10 из 10 однозначно

Verdict: A visually stunning, narrative-driven RPG that has matured into the experience it always had the potential to be.

Cyberpunk 2077 excels most in atmosphere and storytelling. Night City feels alive—not because every NPC is interactive, but because the world sells its tone consistently. The lighting, sound design, and environmental storytelling do much of the narrative heavy lifting, and it works.

Character writing is a standout. Side quests often rival the main story in emotional weight, and player choices feel grounded rather than artificially “good vs evil.” The game does a strong job of letting moments breathe instead of rushing players from objective to objective.

Gameplay-wise, the RPG systems offer flexibility rather than rigidity. Builds are viable across multiple playstyles—stealth, hacking, gunplay, or hybrids—and recent updates have made combat feel more responsive and cohesive. Progression feels meaningful, especially when perks and cyberware start to synergize.

Performance and stability have improved significantly compared to launch. While minor bugs still surface occasionally, they are far less intrusive and rarely break immersion.

What Works Well

Strong narrative and character writing

One of the most immersive open worlds in recent years

Flexible and rewarding build customization

Excellent art direction and sound design

What Needs Improvement

Some open-world activities still feel shallow

NPC AI can be inconsistent

Certain systems feel underutilized given the world’s scope

Final Thoughts:
Cyberpunk 2077 is now a fully realized RPG that succeeds where it matters most—story, atmosphere, and player agency. It’s not perfect, but it delivers a memorable experience that lingers long after the credits roll.

My assessment is based on the combined experience of the base game and Phantom Liberty. On its own, the base game feels closer to a strong but imperfect entry. With the expansion included, it becomes something far more compelling.

The world of Cyberpunk is dense, stylish, and full of life. Night City feels active and layered, even if much of its depth remains in the background rather than fully explorable. The game promised extraordinary systemic immersion, and while it delivers a visually and atmospherically rich setting, it does not always fulfill the full scope of that ambition.

Combat and character progression become genuinely enjoyable once builds begin to take shape, though the gameplay loop can grow repetitive. Many side activities fall into familiar patterns such as eliminating targets or retrieving vehicles, and they rarely evolve beyond that structure.

Phantom Liberty shifts the tone into a focused spy-thriller, and this is where the experience truly shines. The writing feels tighter, the pacing more deliberate, and the overall polish closer to what the game initially aimed to be. It is phenomenal and worth playing even on its own merits.

Taken together, it becomes a strong narrative-driven RPG with a captivating setting and memorable moments. Anyone who values ambitious worldbuilding and story should experience it, especially with the expansion included.
