Это не живой город, это скринсейвер за 60 долларов.

2. Биполярное расстройство сценария
Здесь мы наблюдаем эталонный *лудонарративный диссонанс*. Сюжет истошно вопит: «Ты умираешь! Чип выжигает твой мозг! Жить осталось две недели!». Что делает игра? Вываливает на вас сотню мусорных заказов: «Ви, найди сбежавшее такси», «Ви, укради ноутбук», «Ви, купи эту ржавую развалюху».
Герой, который в катсценах харкает кровью и теряет сознание, в геймплее бодро скачет по крышам и работает мальчиком на побегушках у каждого городского сумасшедшего. Драматизм ситуации разбивается о структуру открытого мира, как лицо мотоциклиста об асфальт.

3. Хроника объявленной смерти (Сюжет)
Сюжет игры... это затянувшаяся предсмертная записка. Вы не спасаете мир, вы даже себя спасти толком не можете. Всю игру вы занимаетесь паллиативной помощью самому себе.
Вам в голову подселяют Джонни Сильверхенда — самовлюбленного террориста-нарцисса с замашками пубертатного подростка. И игра через «стокгольмский синдром» заставляет вас с ним дружить. В итоге у вас есть выбор из трех стульев: продать душу корпорации, тихо сдохнуть в космосе или уехать в закат, зная, что все равно скоро умрешь. Здесь нет катарсиса, только разные оттенки безысходности. После титров хочется не радоваться победе, а принять душ и записаться к психотерапевту.

4. Иллюзия выбора и ролевая импотенция
Вам обещали глубокую РПГ? Забудьте. Ваш выбор предыстории влияет ровно на 15 минут вступления. В итоге вы всегда превращаетесь в одного и того же уличного наемника с манерами гопника. Вариативность диалогов в 90% случаев сводится к трем кнопкам:
1. Да (саркастично).
2. Да (агрессивно).
3. Да (спросить про деньги).
Это не отыгрыш роли, это иллюзия свободы в тюремном коридоре.

5. Симулятор клоуна-барахольщика
Экономика и лут перекочевали из дешевых корейских ММО. Вы  легенда Найт-Сити, киберпсих с военными имплантами. Почему вас убивает с двух ударов бомж с бейсбольной битой? Потому что его майка-алкоголичка 50-го уровня, а ваш титановый бронежилет  5-го.
Чтобы выжить, вам придется надевать на героя розовые шорты, противогаз и ковбойскую шляпу, потому что у них статы выше. Вы выглядите не как киберпанк, а как сумасшедший, ограбивший секонд-хенд под ЛСД.

6. Искусственный Идиот
Враги в этой игре обладают тактической смекалкой тостера. Весь «челлендж» строится на том, что они просто губки для пуль. Полиция  отдельный вид испанского стыда. Стражи порядка материализуются у вас за спиной из воздуха, но стоит завернуть за угол  и они забывают о вашем существовании, как золотые рыбки.

Johnny Silverhand is a big part of what makes this game so compelling. When you first meet him, he seem to just be an angry guy, mad at the world, and looking to cause some damage. But as the story progresses, and you learn more and more about this character, the deeper and more complex he becomes. The role is played by Keanu Reeves and honestly, I think it is some of his best work. 

But the true magic of Night City is in the details.

The voice acting is quite good. There are many interesting characters in Night City, and I liked them all. Everyone felt very real. The voice acting is not limited to a small cast of characters. Many of the people you will meet, have things to say. Even random gang members, and people you walk past on the street will be having conversations you can listen in on. 

There are people everywhere of all shapes and sizes in all sorts of different outfits. Most are simply walking. But others will be having conversations, or spray painting the walls, or shooting at each other in the street. The sheer variety in what you will see and hear is truly impressive.

The side jobs and other optional content also do their part to add to the depth and complexity of Night City. Every job big or small has a story to tell. Everything you see or do adds to the depth and complexity of the world. 

The game isn't perfect. It does have bugs. It is somewhat demanding on your hardware. When I first played it I tried installing it on a standard HDD, and soon found that I needed to transfer it to my SSD to help with stability. Even so, it does glitch now and then, and it crashes occasionally, but honestly, it's not that bad. The game auto-saves frequently so that when anything does go wrong, you won't lose much.

Cyberpunk 2077 es un juego que hay que valorar con matices. No es la obra revolucionaria que prometía ser en su lanzamiento, pero tras parches, mejoras y reequilibrados, se ha convertido en una experiencia sólida y muy disfrutable.

Night City es, sin duda, uno de los mundos abiertos más impactantes visual y atmosféricamente que se han hecho. La ambientación, la música y el diseño artístico están a un nivel altísimo, y consiguen que el universo cyberpunk se sienta creíble, decadente y vivo. La narrativa principal y varias misiones secundarias destacan mucho, con personajes bien escritos y momentos que se quedan contigo.

Jugablemente ha mejorado bastante, pero sigue teniendo altibajos. El gunplay y los builds funcionan bien, aunque el equilibrio no siempre es perfecto y algunos sistemas prometen más profundidad de la que realmente ofrecen. Hay libertad, pero no tanta como el juego insinúa en sus primeras horas.

El mayor problema es que todavía se notan restos de ambición no cumplida: decisiones con impacto limitado, sistemas que parecen recortados y una IA que, aunque funcional, no está a la altura de un RPG de referencia. No rompe la experiencia, pero sí recuerda constantemente lo que podría haber sido.

Aun así, cuando Cyberpunk 2077 acierta, lo hace muy fuerte. Es un juego que recompensa la exploración, la inmersión y tomárselo con calma. No es perfecto, ni lo será, pero hoy por hoy es una experiencia muy recomendable para quien busque una buena historia en un mundo con mucha personalidad.

+ main quest is good and the Johnny Silverhand -stuff works very well

Cyberpunk 2077 is an absolute BEHEMOTH of a game, and before GTA6 is probably the most hype I've ever seen behind a game. Even to this day people rave about how amazing it is, and whilst I definitely think it's really great I do think some of it is exaggerated.

I certainly didn't expect this game to suck me in and keep me entertained for as long as it did; I put around 80 hours into this, doing pretty much every side quest, gig and NCPD scanner mission that I could find. There is an absolutely crazy amount of stuff to do in this game, and it does feel very smooth to play (more on gameplay specifics a bit later.) I was constantly floored by how many side missions would pop up with a new, well written character that I would then hear from again in like 10 hours of gameplay later to continue their story, or simply want to ring me to tell me what they've been up to since. A LOT of the characters in this game are really memorable, interesting, and very visually distinct! The main plot of this game is cool, but I do wish this game had an easy to access glossary of some kind, as terms and names of companies, characters, and even concepts would come up that I wouldn't fully understand/remember (BIG game with lots to do between story missions) as it would just help me stay up to speed with exactly who everyone involved is, because there are a lot of moving pieces at points.

There are two really glaring problems for me in this game that I think stop it from being a true top marks masterpiece, and that is the main characters and the immersion/polish. I know it's been over 5 years and the team has been hard at work, but this city is so buggy pretty much all the time, ESPECIALLY when you're driving around. After about 20 or so hours, this stopped bothering me as much because I started just accepting that Night City is more of a "setting" than a full immersive world, but it was still a bit of a bummer especially to start with. My MAIN problem and it's a big one is our two main characters: V and Johnny FUCKING Silverhand.

I hate Johnny Silverhand. He's definitely the archetype of character that I dislike anyway, but I think the main issue is with Keanu Reeves' performance, which unfortunately is absolutely dreadful; there is a reason that Reeves' has only really found big praise in his roles where he doesn't say that many lines, and that is because the way he delivers lines sounds like he's reading English for the first time in his life. It's not fully on Johnny though; I played through as female V and I also thought her performance was really lacking. Not the delivery itself for the most part, but the actual voice that Cherami Leigh is putting on just sounds so fake; it makes V sound like a character who's trying to seem cool rather than one who actually is cool.

The driving in this game is also kinda ass? This may not actually be the game's fault, as I played exclusively with a keyboard&mouse, which are infamous for being bad for driving/racing games, but I thought I would mention I started my playthrough trying to drive everywhere, but after my 50th accident because an NPC just threw themselves into the road I gave up and started fast travelling everywhere.

ANYWAY, enough about the negatives, here's the stuff I liked:

Gameplay: holy crap the shooting in this feels fantastic! I was expecting it to feel a little wonky because of how it's RPG-afied, but this is not the case at all! I ran a very offensive shoot em up style of character, but the options for stealth always felt good whenever I'd go for that route in the early game, and I noticed tons of weapons and equipment which would allow for this playstyle, same for a hacking/"netrunner" playstyle, which I've heard from friends is a really fun way to play too! Lots of my playthrough was just going to places and shooting guys, and it felt great! It felt like Borderlands but without the tedium of picking up weapons that feel like waterguns in terms of strength.

Side characters: loved so many of these guys, omg, and some of the quests associated with them are crazy. Finding River's nephew?? Jefferson Peralez and his desire to become the mayor??? No spoilers but like, these were side missions and they've stuck with me; I really wasn't expecting where some of these went, and a lot of the characters are really likable! The side quests are also kicked up a notch in the DLC; ALL of them have like, 2+ outcomes it feels like they really wanted to make the DLC feel unique, and they succeeded in that really well I'd say.

World: I know I said it's not always that immersive, but the way CDPR brought Night City to life on the screen is to be commended. Walking around the city and looking up at this crazy dizzying architecture really does feel like a beautifully realised near future metropolis. If you just want to admire the sights, Night City is good for that for sure.

In conclusion, this game is definitely superb, even if I think you need to squint your eyes sometimes. Somewhat overrated in some ways, but still has excellent strengths that it consistently keeps at the forefront throughout its extremely long and entertaining runtime.(9/10)

It's more of a cinematic experience than a proper game.

✔ immersive sim in unique world
✔ lots of content, including setpieces and optional side quests
✔ action-based combat gives the feeling of power later on, at least with melee build

? very cinematic experience
? heavily scripted. There were times I wanted to just kill an NPC, but I was not allowed. It seems to be slightly better in minor side quests, where I could do it, finishing the gig faster
? stats barely matter, very action-based
? huge, beautiful, but gameplay-shallow world (no reason to explore other than the sights). I am really tired of open-world games like this personally
? linear story, except for endings
? good story and well-characterized characters, although both aren't that deep

✘ played on recommended difficulty as a melee blade wielder and it's far too easy. In fact the most difficult encounter of my 40h+ was in the tutorial (not an exaggeration, it was the only time I had to parry melee attacks)
✘ why are there so many repeated models?! In my first hour I had 3 of the same 'unique-looking' NPCs standing at one table and then a few more a few meters further away, in main quest location. Many such cases! I noticed it all the time at bars and cafes in the game. I don't get this, since the character generator is so customizable...
✘ items do not really matter, the stats part of RPG feels fake
✘ AI is bare bones and I think it shouldn't be acceptable any longer for enemies to barely move and just shoot at you in games of this scope. Where are the enemies that can match or outmatch my mostly-organic V? Where is their double jump or even single well-used jump?
✘ economy is based on exponentially more expensive tiers of the same augmentations with minor boosts, there are no other meaningful money sinks and I stopped picking most stuff up quite early
✘ constant forced suspension of disbelief (e.g. barely any changes in 50 years, not just in tech, but also on the product, fashion and celebrity side in a world with such high level of murder, no less!)

I could recommend it for what it is as an experience, a sim, but not what it could have been as an RPG. Currently it sits at "Very Positive" and I think it's too high, hence my choice.

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the few games that truly makes the player feel like they are living inside its world rather than simply playing through it. Even in 2026, Night City remains one of the most immersive settings ever created in gaming. From the neon-soaked streets of Japantown to the dangerous atmosphere of Dogtown, the game constantly feels alive, detailed, and believable.

The story starts strong and gradually evolves into something much deeper. As V grows stronger and begins defeating enemies that once seemed impossible, the player can genuinely feel the increasing influence and reputation of the character within Night City. However, despite the power fantasy, Cyberpunk 2077 never forgets its darker themes. Every ending carries sadness in some form, and there is no truly perfect outcome. The Sun ending stood out the most to me because V finally becomes free and leaves behind the city that caused so much suffering in the first place. At the same time, Reed’s ending is probably the most realistic and hopeful one because V is finally given a chance to survive.

The characters are another major strength. Johnny Silverhand initially comes across as irritating and difficult to tolerate, but over time he becomes far more human and even starts feeling like a genuine companion helping V through daily struggles. Jackie is also unforgettable despite his limited time in the story, leaving a lasting emotional impact very early in the game.

One of the most satisfying moments in Cyberpunk 2077 is fighting Adam Smasher. Watching V, despite being weakened by the Relic, overpower one of the most feared figures in Night City makes the battle incredibly rewarding.

Gameplay variety also gives the game excellent replay value. Different lifepaths, builds, and choices make each playthrough feel fresh, which is why replaying the game multiple times still remains enjoyable.

The game is not without flaws. Even years after launch, bugs still exist. I encountered issues such as frozen calls, missions failing to progress, and even losing around three hours of progress because of a required reload. Thankfully, these problems were not enough to ruin the overall experience.

Cyberpunk 2077 is ultimately a story about survival, identity, and becoming a legend while slowly dying from within. Despite its imperfections, it remains one of the most memorable and immersive RPG experiences available today.

Cyberpunk 2077 n’est plus une promesse brisée :
c’est un grand RPG, exigeant émotionnellement, techniquement solide, et profondément marquant.

Cyberpunk2077 y su género no es un juego que vaya del salvar al mundo, no cambias y derrumbas un sistema cruel y explotador, simplemente intentas salvarte tu, y a los que puedas ayudar. Esto es algo que para mí ha sido un soplo de aire fresco. El juego base es excepcionalmente bueno; puede que en su salida fuese un desastre, pero ha día de hoy se han redimido totalmente con la calidad del producto que venden. 

Este juego te va a hacer llorar, puesto que en Night City, como dice Johnny Silverhand, ¿Finales felices, para gente como nosotros? Gente equivocada, ciudad equivocada. No hay finales felices, pero si finales esperanzadores. recomiendo enormemente que la primera run sea sin entrar en el DLC, aunque lo tengas comprado, tomarse el tiempo de explorar todo NC, completar los chanchullos secundarios y misiones que vayan saliendo, por que tomarse su tiempo es algo positivo (al fin y al cabo, nosotros lo tenemos, no V). 

El título es una disertación detallada de las consecuencias del capitalismo sin ninguna restricción y de cómo afecta a las personas; o tomas una vida corta y legendaria, o una larga y tranquila, ambas son incompatibles. La familia es la que una escoge, y en Night City, es difícil hacerlo, puesto que más personas están interesadas en los eddies que en no pisar a quien se tiene al lado. 

uno debe decidir cómo va a operar en La Ciudad de los Sueños, si va a pisar quien tiene al lado para tener lo que necesita, o si en cambio va a intentar ayudarlos sin esperar nada a cambio. En este mundo, no eres un héroe que salva el mundo y vive feliz al final, solo cambias el micro, a quienes te importan, y eso es todo lo que puedes hacer. 

He llorado mucho con este juego y no me cuesta admitirlo, si hubiese un botón de super recomendarlo le daría sin dudarlo. Ahora solo tocará esperar a Cyberpunk 2079 (u Orión, como lo andan llamando).

10 HOURS IN:
It is actually *very* hard to make a seamless transition into it. I enjoy first person shooters, I was dying to start shooting enemies and levelling up, and gaining skills. But that's slow going. I don't mind story-focused games. But I did get overwhelmed, quite quickly in the first few hours.

Because of the amount of *things* the game asks you to do that are not second nature, and either are not in a lot of the games I've played. Scan this, find this, then this, and then that. Click this button, then this one, then that! I had to take multiple breaks away from this game as it consumes a lot of brain power. You can't play this game mindlessly in the first 10 hours (I bet you can't do it at any point). Makes me wonder when you complete the game, can you just free-roam and wander and max out everything? 

It asks you to constantly do something, unless maybe you ignore *all* of the main quests and do side quests? But yeah, first ten hours, rough. Gave me a headache. 

For a game that looks stunning, there are definitely areas they could have thrown more money at. The AI cars... absolutely trash. Having to AVOID AI vehicles that don't even react to the traffic lights in the game... can we fly? I know I saw a flying car somewhere in some footage of this game...

You cannot even *enjoy* driving down these streets. In car camera POV made me nauseous, so that was a no go. I prefer running to a location or mission point if it's less than 500m. The character creation ...really wish the graphics and options were a lot more...finessed, and a lot more...rich. 

Give yourself patience for this game. Ten hours in does not a review make. But it definiftly shows what only 10 hours has garnered in opinion.

As of this update now, I have 14 hours. And I am FINALLY getting the hang of the mechanics of the game. OH MY GOD, there's AUTODRIVE?! LIFE SAVER!

Thankfully the game has several quick save slots, so make sure you F5 frequently

One downside that I mentioned before, are the several bugs, not everything is perfect, and often you'll need to restart the game completely to get things working. A few of the NCPD mini-objectives suffer from this bug. Also, if you're familiar with Bethesda games, then you're familiar with Crash-To-Desktop (CTDs) errors. Rating: ✪✪✪✪✪ (5/5)

Overall impression:
Cyberpunk 2077 isn’t just a game — it’s a full‑fledged cyberpunk experience that stays with you long after you put down the controller. After all the hype and controversy surrounding its release, I finally dared to dive into Night City — and I didn’t regret a single moment.

What I especially liked:

World and atmosphere. The neon‑lit metropolis with its rainy streets and stark contrast between luxury and poverty feels incredibly alive. Each district has its own distinct character, and environmental details (holographic ads, street chatter, graffiti) create a convincing vision of a futuristic city.

Story and characters. V’s journey is not a generic action tale but a multi‑layered drama with moral choices and complex characters. Johnny Silverhand (voiced by Keanu Reeves) is one of the most charismatic companions in recent gaming history. The dialogue is sharp and witty, and the endings genuinely reflect your decisions.

Freedom of play. You can be a stealthy netrunner, a brutal berserker, or a cunning sniper — the character progression and playstyle are entirely up to you. Missions often offer multiple approaches, and side quests can be even more engaging than the main story.

Visuals and sound. Even years later, the game looks stunning (especially with ray tracing). The soundtrack is a perfect blend of synthwave, electronic, and rock music that enhances the atmosphere perfectly.

Drawbacks (objectively):

At launch, the game suffered from technical issues, but the situation has improved significantly after numerous patches. On PC at max settings, you might still encounter minor bugs (e.g., NPC animations), but they’re not game‑breaking.

Some mechanics (like driving) could have been more polished, and while the open world is beautiful, it sometimes feels a bit “empty” compared to other RPGs.

Conclusion:
Cyberpunk 2077 is an ambitious project that lives up to its promises. Yes, it’s not perfect, but its atmosphere, storytelling, and world‑building make it one of the best titles in the genre. If you’re a fan of cyberpunk, choice‑driven RPGs, or compelling narratives, this game is a must‑play.

Recommendation:
Play on PC with a good graphics card (for ray tracing) or on a next‑gen console. Definitely check out mods — they further enhance the game’s potential.

Time played: 30+ hours (and I’m eager to return).

Overall really enjoyed this game. I'll give a more detailed account of my experience below but for the quick readers: visually interesting, great music, cool characters many of whom I came to care for, interesting story, large open world city to explore and I think there's a good chance I'll play it again. 

Not as good as Witcher 3 and not even remotely close to as good as RDR2. But still had a lot of fun and can recommend this game.

Now to the details. Cyberpunk is a cross between GTA and Bladerunner. Many times as I was cruising around Night City I felt like I was playing a Vice City reboot. I mean that in a positive way as that's the only GTA game I ever liked.

Night City is a happening place! Colorful characters everywhere. Lots of eye candy. Even has it's own lingo. Plenty of missions/quests to keep you busy to the point it can be a little daunting at first.

Driving is very sensitive. You'll get the hang of it but you might steer into some street poles in the beginning. 

The graphics are pretty impressive not gonna lie. Is it worth spending 600 bucks on a GPU for? Well, that's for you to decide. Personally I'd take RDR2 graphics any day over this. But they're very good.

There's a lot of fetch style quests but also there's a whole rogue concept that makes even those seem kinda fun. There are romantic options, at least I think there are as I picked my boo early and stuck with her.

The downsides of this game are you need a beast of a system to play it. Hefty GPU beyond the means of ordinary people who just like to game in their free time, especially if you want the full VRAM experience.

As a result there may be crashes. There are also glitches like your car starts with the pedal to the metal and you can't break, or the car just floats and the background goes white. Manageable though.

I'm not a big fps guy and there's a lot of that in this game. I'm an adventure gamer/RPG guy. I need a good story and lovable characters. I found enough of that in this game to make it interesting to play the whole way through.

Big game (I spent about 150 hours but I'm a slow poke completionist) and many different interactions you can have based on your choices. 

If your computer has the chops to play Cyberpunk and you don't mind flashing lights in a game, definitely give it a try. I think you'll have a real preem time!

因为故事里的每一个人，都在用灵魂在抵抗失去。
可这座城，却是永远填不满的空虚。故事太短暂，短暂到我都还来不及思考，到底什么结局才配得上这一路的失去。怎么看，代价都太高了。

我知道游戏本身还有诸多的遗憾，但如果你看到我的评论，请一定毫不犹豫的走进这座城。
这不是一个关于如何走上巅峰的故事，这是关于一些人，一些心碎的故事。
也是一个人，一个用生命对抗消逝的人。

Cyberpunk 2077 passou por uma redenção absurda. Hoje, sem muita discussão, dá pra dizer que é o jogo que prometeu ser. Está longe de ser perfeito, mas faz muito bem aquilo que se propõe a entregar.

História, personagens e ambientação se encaixam de um jeito muito natural pra formar o que é Night City. E ela não é só mais uma cidade genérica de mundo aberto. Night City é viva, opressiva, linda e, ao mesmo tempo, desconfortável. Ela não está ali só como cenário, ela faz parte da experiência.

Os personagens são tão bem construídos que é impossível não se importar com eles. E quando eu digo se importar, não é só gostar. Você sente raiva de alguns, ódio de outros, frustração, empatia… mas ninguém é indiferente. Todo mundo deixa alguma marca.

O fator rejogável é quase infinito. Cada escolha, cada origem, cada abordagem muda a forma como a história se desenrola. Mesmo rejogando várias vezes, você sempre acaba com um V diferente, vivendo a mesma Night City sob outra perspectiva.

Alguns podem dizer que o jogo é incompleto ou imperfeito. E tudo bem. Mas não dá pra dizer que ele não tem identidade. E, às vezes, isso é o que mais importa.

Everything from the open world exploration to cybernetic builds to combat is incredible, no complaints. Plenty of stuff to do, great quests both main story and side-story, progression feels just right in pace. Even just getting around is fun, the dash and double jump open up a lot of parkour and getting around enemies in unusual ways.
Some bugs, like enemies being unlootable or getting softlocked clipping out of bounds or getting stuck behind a locked door an enemy opened, but infrequent enough that I don't mind.

My only real complaint is that the stat system is incredibly biased towards Body and Technical, having by far the most gameplay-affecting stat checks and being the two skills capable of opening locked doors, on top of having incredible perks like Adrenaline and in-combat regen and healing item and cybernetic/stat buffs, making these two skills universally good across the board regardless of playstyle. Meanwhile, Cool and Reflexes have extremely limited impact in dialogue and utility, and are less versatile in combat, making it hard to justify leveling either past 9.

[b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] - це справжній фенікс від світу ігор. Фенікс, котрий повстав з попелу,  щоб палати яскраво і довести всім, що його ще зарано списувати з рахунків. 

Здається, що навіть люди, які не дуже сильно цікавляться іграми, чули історії про фатальний старт довгоочікуваної гри від авторів Відьмака. Проте CD Project RED не опустили руки і взялися як лагодити гру, яка їм була далеко не байдужа, так і повертати втрачений кредит довіри геймерів. 

Праця була тривалою, але принесла плоди. Зараз [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] сміливо можна назвати однією з найкращих ігор останньої декади і 35 мільйонів проданих копій зайвий раз це доводять. Хоча й сьогодні можна почути тези, що гра досі зламана, але це не так. Гра чудово працює, добре оптимізована і не містить жодних критичних багів, окрім зовсім дрібних, які не впливають на геймплей і є хіба косметичними чи навіть кумедними. Загалом, це вже норма для сучасних ігор з відкритим світом. Дрібні баги є всюди в подібних проєктах. 

А що по самій грі. [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] це дуже атмосферний та неймовірно красивий проєкт з хорошим сюжетом, шикарними персонажами, якісними діалогами з відмінним озвучуванням, цікавими квестами та чудовою бойовою системою, доповненою розгалуженою прокачкою та варіативністю білдів, які урізноманітнять проходження квестів. Шляхів і способів виконання задачі зазвичай є декілька і все залежить від вашої прокачки, встановлених імплантів і креативності. Гра в цьому плані доволі імерсивна і чимось мені навіть нагадала Dishonored. Також в грі дуже крутий транспорт з хорошою фізикою, яка спочатку може здатися незручною, проте з часом звикаєш. Вона справді дарує відчуття, що ти їдеш не в пластиковій коробці, а на кількох тоннах сталі, особливо коли чуєш соковитий гуркіт двигунів тутешніх авто. 

Проте справжньою перлиною [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] є місто. Найт-Сіті сміливо можна назвати одним з найкращих, найбільших і найкрасивіших міст, які ми бачили в іграх. Завдяки чудовому дизайну, візуалу та роботі зі звуком і освітленням, Найт-Сіті відчувається справді живим. Часом можна просто зупинитися посеред вулиці, вслухатися в навколишні звуки і почути як це місто дихає. Я б навіть сказав, що головним героєм гри є саме Найт-Сіті. Місто, в якому народжуються легенди. 

Також CD Project RED вкотре довели, що як ніхто вміють робити сюжетні DLC. Доповнення [b]Phantom Liberty[/b] втягне вас у заплутану історію з нелегким вибором і десятком годин нового контенту. 

І, що надзвичайно круто, в [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] присутня офіційна повна текстова локалізація українською мовою, за що окремий респект і подяка CD Project RED та всім причетним до створення перекладу. 

В підсумку, це чудова гра яка варта вашої уваги та ваших грошей. [b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] подарує вам цікаву історію, живих персонажів та десятки, а то й сотні годин контенту, проведених на вулицях та околицях Найт-Сіті. В місті, яке виглядає футуристично та брутально, та все ж залишається домівкою для звичайних людей з їхніми звичайними проблемами, історіями та травмами, які завжди актуальні. Хоч за вікном 2077 рік, 2027, чи будь-який інший.

Oyunu ilk çıktığı zaman değil, günümüzde oynadığım için şanslıyım sanırım. Bahsedilen birçok bug temizlenmiş, fakat hâlâ ana hikâyede ilerlemeyi engelleyen bir iki bug ile karşılaştım. Geçmiş save’e dönerek ilerleyebildim.
Bu oyun, ilk başta pazarladıkları gibi bir RPG değil. İyi karakter özelleştirmesine sahip, başarılı bir aksiyon oyunu. Hele ki en iyi RPG deneyimi hiç değil. Bunun sebebi, oyunda yalnızca eski bir paralı asker olabilmemiz. Oynadığınız karakter, hangi seçimi yaparsanız yapın aşağı yukarı aynı çizgide ilerliyor. Seçimlerinizin tek etkili olduğu bir sekans var ve bu da final üzerinde seçim yapabilmenizi sağlıyor.

DLC’ye gelirsek, RPG deneyimi ana oyuna göre daha fazla ve hikâye olarak daha çok hoşuma gitti diyebilirim. Tek canımı sıkan nokta ise DLC’nin ana oyuna ek bir devam hikâyesi olarak sunulmaması. Oyunu bitirip DLC’ye geçtiğinizde, sanki ana hikayede yaptığınız her şey hiç olmamış gibi tekrar aynı amaç için savaşıyorsunuz.

Sonuç olarak, Cyberpunk 2077 derin bir RPG deneyimi sunmuyor. Ancak açık dünyasıyla ve aksiyon-macera öğeleriyle türünün en başarılı örneklerinden biri.

Что ж, спустя долгое время, решил дать шанс этой игре. Изначально брал еще в 2020 году, надеялся, что моя 1060 на ноуте потянет, но чуда не случилось. И вот наконец, заимев норм железо решил посмотреть, так ли страшен волк как его малюют.

Что понравилось:

Живой мир, постоянно происходит что-то интересное. Один момент: оставил машину парковки одного из зданий и пошел по заданию, и слышу что-то пикает, ну думаю какой-нибудь робот, а потом резкий взрыв, ничего не понял, решил вернуться к машине, думал мою кто-то взорвал, а потом смотрю на парковке чела подорвали в машине, видимо какого-то корпа. Это прям очень сильно улыбнуло.

Персонажи. Персонажи в этой игре очень яркие и харизматичные. Очень понравилась озвучка многих персонажей, особенно Джонни Сильверхэнда от Киану.

Открытый мир, атмосфера киберпанка. Очень нравилось ездить самому по улицам города, редко пользовался фасттревелами. Тут и небоскребы, и сельская местность с домиками и пустоши, где ничего нет.

Система прокачки. Ну, в целом нормальная, не скажу что прям какой-то огрызок, но и ничего выдающегося, качаешься под свой стиль игры, и этого достаточно.

Сюжет. Сюжет достаточно интересный и затягивает, что хочется узнать что там дальше.

Разнообразный автопарк. Очень много разных видов авто.

Что не понравилось:

Русская озвучка. Это просто какое-то убожество, я не знаю. Настолько безэмоциональная и переполненная матом там где он не нужен. Не выдержал 30 минут и переключил на английскую. Сюда же отнесу и перевод: в один моментах персонажи говорят "Nice" а в субтитрах выводят "з@eбиcь". Настолько "профессионалы" переводили, что просто отвращение вызывает перевод. Поэтому рекомендую играть ТОЛЬКО с английской озвучкой.

Отсутствие вменяемого тюнинга для авто. Смена хрустального покрытия, ну давайте будем честны, просто затычка.

Боевка. Ужасно скучная боевка. Именно поэтому я не люблю шутеры с циферками. Потому что стелсить не имеет смысла, так как оружие не ваншотит никого кроме слабых врагов, а выпендривать и ползать всех  оглушать вблизи 30 минут тоже не в радость. Собственно и открытый бой это тоже губки по впитыванию урона. На начальных уровнях можно долго ковырять, потом с более менее нормальным оружием становится повеселее.

Концовки. Вообще не зашла ни одна концовка. Все концовки (а их там 5(!) без учета ДЛС) по итогу сводятся к двум выборам, что меня очень разочаровало. Нет нормальной концовки переходящей в эндгейм.

По Phantom Liberty:

Сюжет ДЛС мне понравился меньше, чем основной игры, но последняя миссия была очень крутая. И опять же вообще не понравилась ни одна концовка. 

Но не смотря на все минусы, игра мне понравилась.

I held off for a long time before getting started on this game. When I finally did, nearly 90 hours flew by in a flash. I finished the main story and the more important side quests, now I'm going through the DLC, and finally I'll clean up the map of smaller side quests for achievements. CDPR set the bar high for themselves, and ultimately the project turned out to be brilliant, but not perfect. Subjectively speaking, it's a masterpiece. It's worth highlighting elements of the game such as:
• the open world (as far as Night City allows),
• the cyberpunk vibe,
• a mature, emotional storyline with clear moral choices,
• distinctive and well-written characters,
• the character development system – extensive perk trees, cyberware and character builds,
• side missions – often story-driven, non-linear, and significant to the game world,
• themes – it touches on serious issues: identity, transhumanism, freedom, death, corporate power.
The Phantom Liberty expansion is on par with the main game in terms of quality. New location, new missions, new characters.

I can't name too many downsides, but one major one is bugs. Yes, compared to the early stages of the game, there are far fewer of them, but they are still there.

Despite everything, the game deserves huge applause, and I would put a big “MUST PLAY” sign next to its name – if anyone is still hesitating.

Bit late to the party with this review, but holy hell... what a GREAT game this turned out to be. It may have taken years of bug fixes, patches, content additions, and overhauls, but we got here eventually.

Whilst I never personally experienced any major bugs or issues when the game intially launched, there was definitely still a LOT missing from the game - and I don't even mean cut content. Police literally spawned on the player when committing crimes, NPCs appeared and disappeared at the end of each street, cars were fully on rails with zero pathfinding AI in the event of collisions or obstacles. It was rough. The game almost felt more like an amusement park rather than an actual game.

5 years later though, and I am pleased to say that this is no longer the case. Night City FEELS alive now, and it looks better than ever before. I genuinely believe that NC is the best metropolitan location out of any game to date. The city is just so incredibly detailed, vibrant, beautiful, and grimy, all at once, and it's quite easy to just pick a random direction, start walking, and be entertained for hours.

Then comes the writing. My god, this game has premium-tier world-building, story, and characters which, to be fair, is on par for CDPR. It genuinely is in a league of its own. The characters are so well written, each with their own personalities, fears, ambitions, and flaws, that it's sometimes easy to forget that none of these people actually exist beyond pixels on a screen. And don't even get me started on the enormous amount of subtle world-building littered throughout the map in almost every nook and cranny. The devs truly did bring the Cyberpunk universe to life in the best possible way.

If there was ever one single example to argue video games as an art form, then this would most certainly be it.

Then there's the other thing; Phantom Liberty. 

Now, I gotta say, it's very rare to come across an expansion pack which rivals the quality and depth of a main story, let alone exceeds it, but Phantom Liberty absolutely blows it outta the park. The storyline in this DLC was such a wild ride from start to finish and I did not expect to get as invested as I did. It'll also come as no surprise that Idris Elba absolutely kills his role, on par with Keanu Reeves' in the main game, and is supported by similarly outstanding performances from the rest of the cast. I freakin' loved this DLC man, and the ending hit SO damn hard (Reed path, of course).

Long story short, Cyberpunk 2077 is now in the best state it's ever been in and, in my opinion, a definitive must-play for just-about anyone who enjoys solid story-driven experiences.

If you haven't jumped into **Cyberpunk 2077** yet—or if you tried at launch and bounced—stop everything and play it *now*. In 2026, this game isn't just redeemed; it's a towering achievement in open-world RPGs, delivering **outstanding gameplay**, **incredible immersion**, and rock-solid performance that makes Night City feel like a living, breathing metropolis you could get lost in forever.

Let's start with the **gameplay**, which is nothing short of phenomenal. CD Projekt RED has refined every system to perfection through years of updates. Combat is a fluid blend of gunplay, melee, hacking, and cyberware abilities—whether you're quickhacking a squad of Maelstrom goons into oblivion or chaining dash-dodges in a high-octane shootout, it all feels responsive and empowering. Build variety is insane: go stealthy netrunner, tanky gorilla arms brute, or blade-running katana samurai. Driving handles like a dream across the sprawling districts, and side gigs keep the action fresh with meaningful choices that ripple through the world. It's the kind of loop that had me pulling 100+ hour playthroughs without a hint of fatigue.

Immersion? Holy chrome, it's on another level. Night City is a dystopian marvel—neon-drenched streets buzzing with NPCs who react to your chaos, dynamic weather that turns the sprawl into a cyberpunk fever dream, and a soundtrack that hits like a Sandevistan overclock. The main story grips you with Keanu Reeves' iconic Johnny Silverhand and a cast of unforgettable fixers, romancables, and gangers. Add the **Phantom Liberty** DLC, and you've got spy-thriller perfection with Idris Elba stealing scenes. Path tracing on PC elevates it to photorealistic bliss, making every rain-slicked alley and corpo tower feel hyper-real.

And crucially, launch woes are ancient history—patches 2.0+, DLSS 3.5/FSR 3, and frame gen make it buttery smooth even at 4K ultra with ray tracing. My mid-range RTX 5060 setup hovers at 80-100 FPS without a stutter in sight. Consoles hold up beautifully too, no more frame drops or pop-in. It's optimized for current-gen hardware like never before.

**Cyberpunk 2077** is essential gaming. Grab the Ultimate Edition on sale—it's cheaper than a single Night City eddie and delivers a lifetime of replayability. CDPR turned a diamond in the rough into the shiniest choom in the sprawl. V deserves your chrome.

霓虹灯下的沉沦与救赎——《赛博朋克2077》&《赛博朋克：边缘行者》联合评测

 
当夜之城的霓虹第一次刺破屏幕，当大卫·马丁内斯的身影倒在荒坂塔的阴影里，《赛博朋克2077》与它的衍生动画《赛博朋克：边缘行者》共同构筑了一个充满矛盾与张力的赛博世界。它们并非简单的“游戏+动画”的附属关系，而是互为表里的精神载体，将“赛博朋克”这个早已被反复书写的题材，演绎出了新的深度与温度。
 
一、 《赛博朋克2077》：从“半成品”到夜之城的终极形态
 
2020年的《赛博朋克2077》，注定是游戏史上绕不开的“争议之作”。发售初期的优化灾难、内容缺失、BUG泛滥，让这款承载了无数玩家期待的大作，一度沦为业界笑柄。但CD Projekt RED用三年时间，以近乎偏执的态度完成了一场“救赎之旅”——2.0版本的全面革新与DLC《往日之影》的惊艳登场，彻底重塑了夜之城的灵魂。
 
如今的夜之城，不再是一个徒有其表的霓虹牢笼，而是一个充满细节与活力的开放世界。玩家扮演的“V”，不再是一个割裂的任务执行者，而是一个真正扎根于街头的“赛博浪客”。2.0版本重构的技能系统、战斗机制与警察体系，让每一次街头火拼都充满策略性；载具追逐战的手感优化，让荒坂工业园的狂飙突进有了电影级的爽快感。而《往日之影》则补全了游戏最核心的剧情短板，狗镇的灰色地带、与所罗门·李德的周旋、以及最终关于“灵魂”与“生存”的抉择，将V与强尼·银手的羁绊推向了新的高潮。
 
更重要的是，夜之城的“烟火气”终于被点燃。沃森区的贫民窟里，小贩在雨夜里叫卖着劣质合成肉；威斯特布鲁克的霓虹灯下，富人们在豪华会所里挥霍着生命；太平洲的海滩边，流浪者们在篝火旁讲述着关于自由的传说。这些细节，让夜之城不再是一个冰冷的游戏地图，而是一个真实的、令人窒息的“人间地狱”——在这里，科技高度发达，人性却极度匮乏；阶层壁垒坚不可摧，梦想不过是廉价的商品。
 
二、 《赛博朋克：边缘行者》：一场献给玩家的“悲剧情书”
 
如果说《赛博朋克2077》是一幅宏大的“夜之城浮世绘”，那么《赛博朋克：边缘行者》就是一把精准的“手术刀”，剖开了这座城市最隐秘的伤口。这部由扳机社（Trigger）制作的原创动画，没有试图去讲一个“拯救世界”的宏大故事，而是聚焦于一个名叫大卫·马丁内斯的底层少年，用他短暂而炽热的一生，诠释了“赛博朋克”最核心的命题：当科技成为压迫的工具，人性是否还能残存？
 
大卫的故事，是夜之城无数底层人的缩影。贫民窟的出身、母亲的惨死、被权贵践踏的尊严，让他别无选择地走上了“赛博精神病”的道路。军用科技的“斯安威斯坦”，既是他逆袭的资本，也是他毁灭的诅咒。在这条不归路上，他遇到了一群志同道合的“边缘行者”——渴望自由的露西、火爆直率的丽贝卡、沉稳可靠的多莉欧……这群被世界抛弃的人，在彼此的身上找到了一丝温暖。
 
扳机社用极具冲击力的画风，将夜之城的疯狂与浪漫展现得淋漓尽致。高速移动的战斗画面、赛博义体过载时的畸变特效、霓虹灯光与雨水交织的赛博美学，每一个帧都充满了张力。而动画最动人的，是它的“悲剧内核”。大卫最终的结局，从他戴上“斯安威斯坦”的那一刻起就已注定——在夜之城，底层人的反抗，不过是蚍蜉撼树；所谓的“逆袭”，不过是一场加速死亡的狂欢。
 
但《边缘行者》的伟大之处在于，它让这场悲剧充满了“浪漫主义”的光芒。大卫与露西的爱情，没有狗血的误会与拖沓的纠缠，只有两个孤独灵魂的相互救赎。即使知道前路是深渊，大卫依然选择为了露西的梦想，冲向荒坂塔的顶端；即使知道大卫终将被义体吞噬，露西依然选择陪他走完最后一程。这份在霓虹灯下绽放的爱情，成为了夜之城最黑暗的底色里，一抹最耀眼的亮色。
 
三、 互为表里：一场世界观的完美共振
 
《赛博朋克2077》与《赛博朋克：边缘行者》的联动，是游戏与动画领域的一次“教科书级”的合作。它们并非简单的“彩蛋互嵌”，而是真正做到了世界观的深度融合。
 
动画里的元素，在游戏中得到了完美的呼应。玩家可以在夜之城找到大卫的母校、丽贝卡的枪店、甚至可以穿上大卫的标志性夹克，重温那些令人心碎的场景。而游戏里的“赛博精神病”支线任务，也在动画中得到了更直观的诠释——那些被义体吞噬理智的“疯子”，曾经也是一个个有血有肉的人。
 
更重要的是，两者的精神内核高度统一。无论是V还是大卫，他们都是夜之城的“边缘人”，都在为了生存与梦想而挣扎。他们的故事，都在拷问同一个问题：在一个异化的世界里，如何保持人性的完整？ V的选择，是与强尼·银手和解，在毁灭之前，为自己活一次；大卫的选择，是燃烧自己的生命，为露西点亮通往月球的道路。他们的结局或许是悲剧，但他们的反抗，却让夜之城的霓虹，多了一丝人性的温度。
 
四、 总结：霓虹永不熄灭，传奇永不落幕
 
《赛博朋克2077》与《赛博朋克：边缘行者》，共同构成了一个完整的“夜之城宇宙”。它们或许并不完美——游戏的开放世界依然存在重复度过高的问题，动画的剧情节奏也略显仓促——但它们却用最真诚的态度，讲述了一个关于“反抗”与“救赎”的故事。
 
夜之城依然是那个冰冷的牢笼，但V和大卫的故事，却让我们看到了希望。在这个科技碾压人性的世界里，总有一些东西，是义体无法替代的；总有一些梦想，是金钱无法衡量的；总有一些爱情，是死亡无法阻隔的。
 
当霓虹再次亮起，当引擎的轰鸣声再次响起，总有新的浪客，会踏上夜之城的街头。而V和大卫的故事，将永远在这座城市里回荡，成为永不熄灭的传奇。

Cyberpunk 2077 is an outstanding, brutal, and highly entertaining game.
I’ve already completed it around four times on other platforms, and when I saw it on sale on Steam, I simply couldn’t resist buying it again.

It’s the kind of game you never get tired of. There’s a huge amount of content to explore, from main missions to side quests, gigs, and random events that constantly pull you back into Night City. The characters are incredibly well written, with strong personalities and memorable stories, making every interaction feel meaningful.

As a proper RPG, your choices truly matter. Decisions—big or small—have real consequences that affect the story, relationships with other characters, and even the endings, which gives the game great replay value.

Night City itself feels alive and immersive. The atmosphere, visuals, and sound design do an amazing job of making you feel like part of a futuristic, chaotic world. Driving is fun and satisfying, with some truly awesome vehicles. Personally, I prefer using a motorcycle over a car, since the streets are often narrow and traffic can make driving cars a bit tedious if you’re not role-playing. That said, if you embrace the realism, the driving system feels well thought out and fits perfectly within the game’s world.

Overall, Cyberpunk 2077 is a unique experience, full of style, depth, and freedom. A must-play for fans of RPGs, immersive storytelling, and futuristic settings.

先说结论，不推荐。网上很多人吹捧这款游戏，但是我认为有部分原因是它的美术风格比较少见，如果自己不玩，看视频过剧情其实还行。但是自己玩的话，就要面对很多问题。
1，主线非常短，支线加起来也不够长，还混杂了一大部分实际流程一样的任务，例如去哪里偷东西，杀人。尽管说会有文本信息来说明不同的任务背景，但是初期可能会认真看，去思索关联。到了后面，永远不变形式的文本背景，会耗尽玩家的兴趣。这时候对于玩家而言就是重复劳动了。（所以我认为这是观感不错，实际游玩枯燥的游戏，作为观众看别人解读文本信息，都是不一样的内容，不会去不停的重复任务本身的重复性，但是作为玩家，文本阅读占小部分，大部分时间是自己操作人物，重复的任务模板就极大的破环了玩家的耐心。）尤其我还是一个希望把地图上的任务清完的“强迫症”，玩到后面，感觉已经完全没有耐心了。而且从网上的评价来说，都提到加上dlc之后才算是完整的作品，我是买了《往日之影》，但是我打完原版主线的星星结局之后，dlc只游玩了一部分内容，发现我已经感受不到剧情的魅力，从能看完对话到不停按y键，我心里想的仅仅是打完结局而已。因为原版内容短暂的剧情，千篇一律的任务，我接着玩下去的心情已经没了。每次打开之前，心里反而不是兴奋，是不得不工作的无聊感。所以dlc买了之后，浅尝辄止，卸掉了游戏。因此，对于任何希望玩得比较有乐趣的人，我不建议你去刷任务，什么赛博精神病，偷车。这些玩多了会让你对游戏失去兴趣。只要体验一下就行。（在卸载之前，我已经刷完了赛博精神病和日本街那个中间人的所有任务，其他中间人也刷了一半。）
2，说是开放世界，我玩起来觉得很空，设定是在拥挤而繁华的城市，但是大部分地区都不过是个背景板，给我的而感觉就是空。有一个我很无语的就是，在面对路人时有“交谈”的选项，结果当你满怀期待的按下去之后，不过是npc机械的说两句话。至于城市，到处都是进不去的门，各个街区，划分什么日本街，唐人街，除了装修风格稍微改一下，文字变一种，就像是复制的一样。
3，有不少莫名奇妙的设定，不知道是做不完了还是怎么样，地铁几乎没有存在感，和传送点定位冲突，自己的房子，几乎除了和伴侣进行重复的剧情外没什么用。睡觉跳过时间，在外面也可以跳过。房子的特点太少了。
（关于第一点，同样是开放世界，大镖客2，我从头到尾都看着剧情打完了，每一章节都有其特点，所以网上很多不同时间点的分享存档，但是对于赛博朋克，你在不同剧情点变化很小，自始自终都是一个地图，就像在一个罐子里以不同的姿势跳，但是跳不出去，很容易枯燥。大镖客2地图大得多，所以有能力做出剧情地点的改变。所以不同的章节能够给人新意）

Cyberpunk 2077
Score: 9.5/10
Review (contains spoilers)

Cyberpunk’s greatest strength for me is its incredibly detailed open world. Night City feels like a place shaped by years of passion. Every aspect of the city, from its history and architecture to its fashion, advertisements, and even its slang, feels deliberate and engaging to explore.

The gameplay focuses mainly on combat. While mechanically simple, it never became boring thanks to how fluid it feels. The different weapon types all play distinctly, and quickhacking was by far the most enjoyable system for me. It allowed for creative combinations and more thoughtful approaches to encounters instead of relying purely on gunplay or melee combat.

The story is where my feelings become mixed. On one hand, you play a mercenary who grows more powerful every day, becoming nearly untouchable by the mid-game. On the other, the narrative tells the story of someone slowly deteriorating and losing themselves. In the open world, you feel like the merc, unstoppable and in control. The moment you enter a main mission, however, you are suddenly coughing, collapsing, and barely able to stand. Both stories are strong on their own, but they clash when combined.

The pacing suffers because of this. The plot constantly emphasizes urgency, yet the game encourages you to spend dozens of hours on side content. On my first playthrough, I rushed the main story because it felt urgent, only to later realize I had skipped large portions of content clearly meant for early-game V. By the time I reached the point of no return, I had lost immersion. I found myself forcing reasons for why V would take on side gigs instead of focusing on their far more personal and pressing situation.
V also feels somewhat disconnected from the world. Night City is brutal and exhausting, yet V moves through it effortlessly, completing multiple gigs a day without showing any real fatigue. Consumables and downtime feel largely pointless because V never shows signs of wear or vulnerability outside of scripted moments. Dialogue options are somewhat limited, though this did not bother me too much since the major choices still felt meaningful. That said, I would have liked more skill or background-based dialogue, as those moments added a lot of personality to V.

The side characters are a strong point. They feel like real people with their own goals rather than tools for the player’s story. Johnny, in particular, stands out. The idea of a terrorist living in your head and gradually influencing your decisions is compelling, and his presence adds a lot of depth to the narrative.

Overall, I really enjoyed what Cyberpunk 2077 had to offer. It often felt like I was playing two different games at once. Both are excellent in their own right, but they clash when combined. If the tension between V’s personal story and the open-world design had been handled better, this would have been an easy 10 out of 10.

Время в игре: почти 74 часа (из них 50 — езда по городу на новой тачке, 20 — перекачка кибернетики в тишине, 4 — вялое удивление: «А, тут ещё и сюжет есть?»)

Всем привет. Я — живой памятник парадоксу. Я — тот, кто прошёл «Киберпанк 2077» дважды. Первый раз — на пиратке, в те тёмные времена, когда Сандевистон был лишь призрачной надеждой в патчах, а игра была коллекцией красивых багов в форме города. Я прошёл, убил всех, кого надо, посмотрел концовку и… стёр память. Словно плохой ромаш.

И вот я вернулся. Чистый, с официальной копией, с обновлениями, с исправленным ИИ полиции и прочей магией. Я вошёл в Найт-Сити с мыслью: «Теперь-то я пройду всё как надо. Вникну в историю, открою каждую ветку диалога, почувствую всю боль и поэзию этого мира». Я был готов к путешествию души Виасада в кибернетическом аду.

Акт 1: Травма прошлого. Или «Кровь, кости и единственная ясная память».
Из всего того первого, скомканного прохождения в голове засела одна кат-сцена. Одна. «Кровь и кости». Тот самый подпольный чемпионат по боям без правил. Я помнил катарсис. Помнил, как бился в клетке не на жизнь, а на смерть, выжимая из своего тогда ещё кривого билда всю ярость. И вот я снова здесь. Моё новое «я» смотрит на этого нового Ви. И я принимаю единственно верное решение.

Я бросаю все силы в ближний бой. Мои кулаки становятся легендой. Я качаю тело в сталь, реакторы — в мышцы, а нервную систему — в прибор ночного видения для поиска новых жертв. Я не стал наёмником. Я стал чемпионом. Тем, кого нанимают не для стрельбы, а для демонстрации того, что происходит, когда 200 кг бионизированной ярости врезается в толпу гопников на скорости грузовика. Сюжет? Джонни Сильверхэнд? Сорян, ребят, у меня сейчас спарринг. Я готовлюсь к реваншу.

Акт 2: Великое бегство от сюжета. Или синдром «потом, обязательно потом».
А потом случилось странное. Я стал миллионером. Не метафорически. На моём счету в игре лежали миллионы евродолларов. И у этих миллионов была одна, чистая, кристальная цель: личный транспорт.

Я заболел. Я просыпался в своей квартире в Мегазидании, открывал карту и видел не точки заданий, а иконки машин. Каждая — вызов. Каждая — новая краска для коллекции. Я забыл дорогу к Виктору. Я знал дорогу к каждому дилеру, к каждой тупиковой аллее, где по контракту стоит уникальная тачка. У меня их больше 30. Тридцать. Я купил всё: от ржавой колымаги «макасины» до гиперкара, который стоит как маленькая квартира. Я крашу их, тюнингаю… и ставлю в гараж. Потому что завтра нужно купить следующую. Сюжет звонит мне на связь? «Джонни, я сейчас очень занят, у меня сделка по квадре на набережной. Перезвоню. Возможно».

Акт 3: Киборг-трансценденция. Или «Сюжет умер. Да здравствуют импланты».
А на что тратить деньги, когда все машины куплены? Правильно. На себя. Моё тело — не храм. Это стартап, поглощающий венчурные инвестиции. Я превратил Ви в ходячий арсенал «Мильной Техники». Каждый визит к рипдоку — это новая ипотека на новый имплант. «О, скидка на эпидермальную броню? Беру две!». «Мозговой имплант, позволяющий замедлять время при уклонении? Да это же must-have!». Я трачу сотни тысяч, чтобы мой персонаж мог на полсекунды дольше прыгать или на 5% быстрее перезаряжаться. Я оптимизирую билд, в котором уже давно нет достойных противников, потому что все второстепенные миссии и «грехи» я давно зачистил. В тишине. Без отвлекающих звонков от раздражённого рокера-призрака в голове.

Эпилог: Я купил игру, чтобы сбежать из неё.
И вот я сижу. На моём счету — миллионы. В гараже — весь автопарк Найт-Сити. В теле — вся нанотехнологическая мощь, которую можно купить за деньги. Я стою на крыше своей квартиры, смотрю на неоновый ад и понимаю, что я не дошёл даже до середины сюжета. Я игнорирую звонки Такэмуры. Я отмахиваюсь от видений Джонни. У меня всё есть. Я — король побочного контента. Я — титан финансового успеха в мире, где главный герой должен умирать.

Я не прохожу «Киберпанк». Я живу в его песочнице. И это самый дорогой, самый красиво проработанный, самый нелепый кризис среднего возраста в истории видеоигр. Я купил игру за её историю, а играю в её бессмысленный, прекрасный симулятор капитализма и кастомизации. Я не хочу спасать душу. Я хочу купить ещё один спойлер для машины, которой никогда не буду ездить.

Итог: Игра теперь — огонь. Но осторожно: она может незаметно подменить ваш эпичный квест на спасение на эпичный квест по сбору достижений в меню статистики. Вы можете стать самым могущественным, богатым и технологически продвинутым человеком в Найт-Сити, который забыл, зачем он сюда пришёл. А зачем, если можно просто купить ещё одну тачку и прокачать ещё один слот для кибердеки? Нет, серьёзно, я спрашиваю. Мне нужно понять, у меня ещё 10 побочных квестов горят. И дилер написал про новую партию байков.

Acredito que Cyberpunk 2077 terá um efeito no futuro como Blade Runner (1982) teve anos depois. 
Muitos críticos da época acharam o ritmo do filme lento e a história complexa, focando excessivamente no visual e menos na narrativa. O filme encontrou seu público e aclamação com o tempo, especialmente após o lançamento da "Versão do Diretor" em 1992 e, posteriormente, o "Final Cut" em 2007. A sua estética cyberpunk influenciou todo o cinema de ficção científica que veio depois, consolidando-o como um clássico cult. 

O cineasta Ridley Scott expôs sua avaliação para o culto tardio a ‘Blade Runner’ (1982) após o filme dirigido por ele fracassar nas bilheterias na época de seu lançamento. Com orçamento de US$ 30 milhões, o longa protagonizado por Harrison Ford fez ‘apenas’ US$ 41 milhões em vendas de ingressos ao redor do planeta. Apesar do desinteresse do público quando o filme chegou aos cinemas, a ficção científica acabou se tornando um clássico contemporâneo.

“Houve um ou dois fanáticos que gostaram bastante quando saiu”, relatou Scott. “Estava sem a narração, tinha um pouco de [música do grego] Vangellis, um pouco de [trilha sonora do compositor] Jerry Goldsmith, e saiu e isso reacendeu a coisa toda. Essa é a loucura de Hollywood”.

Parece que minha Análise está apenas retratando o filme de Ridley Scott e não estou falando nada sobre o jogo, não é? Mas vai fazer sentido.
Lembro o Hype gigantesco com esse jogo ao ser anunciado. Um mundo aberto de Cyberpunk? Gráficos incríveis, jogabilidade incrível, Keanu Reeves! O astro de cinema de ficcção científica (Matrix!!!) tudo a ver, tudo para ser perfeito... E então veio enfim o tão aguardado lançamento. 
E foi uma bomba, em um dos piores sentidos da expressão. Cheio de Bugs, e quebra de expectativas nas promessas que o público aguardava.
Todos perderam o interesse progressivamente... Eu diria que o jogo caiu em um ostracismo. E a empresa sofreu. 
E o que mais me faz pensar disso tudo é sobre a mensagem que o jogo passa ao decorrer da sua história, dentre esse futuro distópico apresentado, as grandes corporações e a exploração de trabalho toma conta daquele futuro.
Será que já não tá tomando conta? que não tomou conta do processo de Cyberpunk 2077? Sei que houve vários adiamentos. Mas se sabiam que o jogo ainda não estava totalmente finalizado, porque apressaram? Ganância de dinheiro?

É irônico pensar nisso tudo com o que a crítica que o jogo apresenta. Acaba que isso escondeu a grande pérola que a história desse jogo traz, desde a sua história principal, que particularmente achei genial. Uma alma consciente digitalizada dentro de uma pessoa, tal como um vírus corroendo por dentro. E você acaba tendo que lidar com essa personalidade, que nada menos é Johnny Silverhand (Keanu Reeves).
E as histórias secundárias, que na maioria do tempo de gameplay soava até mais impactante com o que tava acontecendo em primeiro plano.
Acho que o jogo ainda não tá totalmente perfeito, ou que não foi concebido de uma forma perfeita. Esse monte de informações sendo jogado na cara do jogador logo de início é assustador. Você se pega olhando pro mapa e vê aquele monte de informação e fica transtornado. Mas talvez essa seja a intenção. Mostrar que o futuro tá longe de ser perfeito e que informação é o que mais vamos ter. Cabendo a nós mesmos filtrar tudo aquilo.

E pra finalizar, acredito que em um futuro bem próximo, Cyberpunk 2077 será cultuado assim como Blade Runner foi.

Cyberpunk 2077 feels very familiar in terms of its gameplay like I'm playing Far Cry and/or Outer Worlds. This isn't a real RPG and more of an Action RPG. Mainly because more than 95% of the game's dialogue choices have no impact on the world. Especially the blue text dialogue options. Your choices only matter during main jobs to open up specific side jobs and that one scene and Main Job. Even in Side Jobs, Gigs, and NCPD jobs your choices really doesn't matter. It is better than Fallout 4 but almost close to Fallout New Vegas in terms of a RPG. I wanted to say because you're not playing a character with a background you can craft, but it is half true. You're playing as V, a merc, and always will be V, a merc. As a ARPG Shooter, it is great. But as a RPG (that it was originally advertised and promised), it sucks at it. Compared to Witcher 3's quality, experience, and writing, CP77 falls behind.

Beside that, good and bad things about the game. All my issues with the game is mostly gameplay related and there are nitpicks. Can't remove/replace weapon mods. Can't respect more than 1 time when Witcher 3 lets you respect unlimited amount. Can't Dash/Dodge while scanning. Can't switch to another weapon while carrying a body. Can't use consumables during combat and common consumables are useless. A button to sell all alcohol would be QoL and Perks/feature/Cyberware that auto use consumables and buff/make them useful would be good. Not a looter shooter game, but you'll be running around scavenging for crafting materials, Health upgrades, and Cyberware Capacity upgrades. Swimming mechanic is nearly never used in base game. There are still so many bugs and glitches, but doesn't make the game unplayable. They're REALLY annoying that requires looking up a fix or restarting the game. They just ruin the experience. No wall running (cut content). Taking fall damage near an neutral enemy cause them to aggro. There are still A LOT of cut contents and features even after all the patches. Cyberware/Grenade are slotted on the same button. Can't use Quickhack/Cyberdeck and use OS Cyberware at the same time. No dual wielding pistols, melee weapons, or sword/pistol. Análise – Cyberpunk 2077 (291 horas | 100% Conquistas)

Depois de 291 horas, múltiplas builds, finais diferentes e todas as conquistas desbloqueadas, posso dizer com tranquilidade: Cyberpunk 2077 não é mais o jogo que nasceu em 2020 — é o jogo que ele sempre prometeu ser.

Night City é, sem exagero, um dos mundos mais imersivos já criados. Não apenas pelo visual absurdo ou pela trilha sonora impecável, mas pela atmosfera: a cidade respira decadência, ambição, solidão e excesso. Caminhar sem objetivo, ouvir conversas aleatórias, observar a arquitetura e os contrastes sociais já é uma experiência por si só.

A narrativa é um dos maiores trunfos. V, Johnny Silverhand e os personagens secundários são escritos com profundidade rara. As histórias não seguem o padrão maniqueísta de “bem versus mal”; aqui tudo é cinza, desconfortável e humano. Algumas side quests são melhores do que a campanha principal de muitos jogos AAA.

O sistema de RPG evoluiu muito ao longo do tempo. Builds são variadas, viáveis e recompensadoras — seja jogando como netrunner furtivo, solo agressivo ou um híbrido caótico. O combate hoje é fluido, satisfatório e, acima de tudo, divertido. Cada estilo realmente muda a forma como o jogo é vivido.

Tecnicamente, o jogo está polido. Bugs ainda existem (como em qualquer mundo aberto gigantesco), mas nada que quebre a experiência. O desempenho é sólido, os sistemas funcionam e a sensação é de um produto finalmente finalizado.

E um destaque especial para quem gosta de rock: a trilha sonora não é apenas barulho de fundo. As músicas dialogam diretamente com o universo do jogo, e até as letras carregam identidade, atitude e crítica social. Muitas faixas funcionam quase como extensões narrativas de Night City — agressivas, melancólicas ou revoltadas na medida certa. É o tipo de soundtrack que você procura fora do jogo depois de desligar o PC.

Platiná-lo não foi uma obrigação mecânica, mas uma consequência natural de querer continuar em Night City. Poucos jogos me fizeram permanecer tanto tempo sem sentir desgaste. Cyberpunk não é perfeito — e talvez nunca precise ser —, mas é marcante.

Se você se afastou por causa do lançamento conturbado, este é o momento de voltar.
Se nunca jogou, jogue.
Night City merece ser vivida.

It's rare that an open-world game keeps me captive at the keyboard for more than two-to-three hours these days. That shared, when a game can set you on a quest in the late afternoon, push you into the wee hours of the following morning, and be the source of regret for having to get off before completing the tangent quests I was sidetracked by... the feeling is welcomingly magical.

I'm going to try and summarize and condense my experience with the game, forgive the breezy analogies and touches. TL;DR, this is a great game. Easily top 3 games I have ever played.

In the beginning, I felt like I was playing a first-person GTA based in the future. That holds true for the first few missions until you start unlocking perks that adapt and define your playstyle. I leaned into a 'one-shot, one kill. no one saw me, no alarms were raised' playstyle and loved it. This didn't work against 'bosses' so I adopted a DoT hacker backup plan; it's hard to hit me when your cyberware (implanted tech) is overheating, while giving me wallhacks and amping incoming damage. By endgame, I was weaving both styles together to clear outposts and bases before anyone realized I was onsite.

The story is great. Some characters you're going to love. Others you're going to hate. If you take your time, you can uncover the 'why' each character is the way they are. The depth of the world is deep and I appreciate the time and effort that went into putting the player near the core of events. When you complete a mission and are told "good job but, it could have been better" it pushes you to operate within the parameters you don't need to abide by. If you do, the acknowledgement of you abiding by their preference is a reward on its own. The details grab and engage you.

If you like good games, Cyberpunk is top tier.

I didn't know much about this game when I got it other than it had an awful launch when I started playing it and thanks god I gave it a chance when I first played it in 2025. It is literally the reason I decided to upgrade my gaming PC setup to experience it as you are supposed to — and I couldn't even be more glad I did.

The game is absolutely gorgeous and it's definitely one of the most immersive games I have ever played. I have always been skeptical when it came to first person camera games, but this game proved me wrong and made me really embrace this kind of cameras and everything it brings to the table. The attention to detail is also outstanding, and I found myself reading every shard or piece of information every chance I could, both in main quests and secondary quests, which all had an intriguing story in some way or another.

The writing in this game is fantastic, the characters are very complex and fleshed out and a lot of them will stay with you forever. I love that the game makes you question your own decisions over and over throughout the game — specially in the Phantom Liberty DLC, and how the choices you make are reflected in the story in different ways. Another aspect I love about this game is the plethora of customization options and the ease you have as a player to choose how to approach quests along, which also gives it a fantastic replayability value.

I think everybody should visit Night City at least once in their lives and that this game is a must play for everybody that likes a good story, very well written characters, and attention to every detail in a game.

Holy fucking shit, what a journey…
When I started the game, I didn’t expect this emotional masterpiece.

What I found kind of disappointing in parts of the base game was that a lot of missions and boss fights felt really repetitive. But with Phantom Liberty, that completely turned around. You can feel the extra love, creativity, and effort that went into it.

This world practically screams critique of capitalism. I haven’t felt it so strongly in any other medium. Of course, that’s not just the game, it’s also Mike Pondsmith’s ideas.

The world and the characters, beyond the story, are what really make the game. I haven’t experienced another medium that hit me emotionally like Cyberpunk did.

Crazy how easily Johnny Silverhand becomes Keanu Reeves’ best role ever. Absolutely convincing character, and you grow to love him more and more, even though he’s kind of an asshole at first.

I’ve played all the endings, and each one fucked me up in its own way. [spoiler] Because you get so attached to the characters, you want a happy ending, but you only get it partly, since all endings leave what happens next open. [/spoiler]

[spoiler] What hit me the hardest were Judy’s voicemails during the credits. In almost every ending, all you can do is empathize with her and wish her something better… [/spoiler]

And when I played my favorite ending for the last time and realized I had actually finished the game, I had to start crying, because I was so emotionally connected to this world and its characters. 
Thank you for this experience.

Comprei Cyberpunk 2077 achando que seria um hacker futurista. Virei um entregador de encomendas que erra curvas, atropela NPCs e vive tomando choque em painéis elétricos soltos. O verdadeiro cyberware era a gente consertando o jogo junto com a CD Projekt RED.

Mas falando sério (ou quase):

Já passei mais tempo customizando o visual do meu V do que o meu próprio rosto na vida real.

O Keanu Reeves no meu ouvido é melhor que 90% dos meus contatos no WhatsApp.

Toda missão secundária é uma sessão de terapia com um toque de tiroteio.

Dirijo tão mal que a polícia de Night City me multa só por existir.

Hoje, depois de updates, o jogo tá mais estável que meu emocional. A cidade é linda, a história gruda igual cola de obra e os fãs que zoavam viraram fãs que choram com o final.

Recomendo? Sim, se você tem paciência para:

Aceitar que seu personagem ainda pode voar sem avião.

Amar uma cidade que te odeia de volta.

Rir de bugs que viram features (ex: NPC dando tchau com o pé).

Conclusão: Night City não é um lugar, é um relacionamento abusivo que a gente ama.

 10/10 se você curte futuros distópicos, tiros, drama e motos voadoras que caem da ponte.

Análise escrita após 150h de jogo e 3 PCs chorando.

《赛博朋克2077》：瑕不掩瑜的未来狂想
在游戏的浩瀚宇宙中，《赛博朋克2077》无疑是一颗备受瞩目的星辰。它带着玩家们穿梭于2077年的夜之城，在科技高度发达却又充满矛盾与混乱的世界里展开冒险。尽管这款游戏存在一些bug，但总体而言，它依然是一款不可多得的好游戏。
初入《赛博朋克2077》的世界，夜之城的繁华与喧嚣扑面而来。霓虹灯闪烁的街道、高耸入云的摩天大楼、街头巷尾的帮派斗争，每一处细节都构建出一个极具未来感的城市。玩家扮演的主角V，为了自己的生存与梦想，在这个充满危险与机遇的城市中摸爬滚打。在游戏过程中，确实会遇到一些bug，比如偶尔的卡顿、穿模现象，甚至某些任务的触发异常。这些问题在一定程度上影响了游戏的流畅体验，让玩家在投入剧情时突然被拉回现实。
然而，这些bug并不能掩盖《赛博朋克2077》的闪光点。从剧情设计来看，它有着极其丰富和深刻的故事线。玩家的每一个选择都可能影响剧情的走向和角色的命运。在与各种人物的交互中，能感受到人性的复杂与多面。比如与强尼·银手的合作与对抗，强尼这个角色充满了叛逆与理想主义，他的故事与主角V的经历相互交织，让玩家在游戏中不断思考自我、人性以及科技与社会的关系。这种深度的剧情体验，就如同阅读一本精彩的科幻小说，让人沉浸其中，欲罢不能。
游戏的玩法也十分丰富多样。战斗系统结合了射击、潜行、黑客等多种元素，玩家可以根据自己的喜好和角色的发展方向来选择不同的战斗方式。在探索夜之城的过程中，还能发现各种隐藏的任务和秘密，每一次探索都可能带来新的惊喜。这种开放世界的设计，给予玩家极大的自由，让玩家真正成为夜之城的一部分。
从更宏观的角度来看，《赛博朋克2077》也反映了许多现实社会的问题。在这个赛博朋克的世界里，科技虽然高度发达，但贫富差距巨大，社会阶层固化严重。富人们享受着高科技带来的一切便利，而穷人则在底层挣扎求生。这让我们联想到现实生活中科技发展带来的利弊，以及如何平衡社会发展与公平正义的问题。这不仅是一款游戏，更是一面镜子，让我们反思现实。
尽管《赛博朋克2077》存在一些瑕疵，但它的优点远远超过了这些小问题。它以独特的视角和丰富的内容，为玩家呈现了一个充满想象力的未来世界。在未来的游戏体验中，我们可以带着从《赛博朋克2077》中获得的思考，更加深入地感受游戏所传达的情感和意义。同时，也期待游戏开发者能够不断优化游戏，解决那些存在的bug，让这个精彩的世界更加完美。《赛博朋克2077》就像一颗未经打磨的宝石，虽然表面有一些瑕疵，但依然散发着璀璨的光芒，值得每一位游戏爱好者去探索和品味。

赛博朋克 2077》绝对是一款值得玩家反复品味的佳作，它以其卓越的故事内容和令人惊叹的沉浸体验，在众多游戏中脱颖而出。
踏入夜之城的那一刻，我就被这个充满赛博风格的世界深深吸引。鳞次栉比的高楼大厦、五彩斑斓的霓虹灯光、空中穿梭的飞行载具，每一处细节都构建出一个生动且真实的未来都市。这个世界不是冷冰冰的设定，而是有着自己的呼吸和心跳。街头巷尾的各种人物、他们的对话与故事，都在无声中丰富着这个世界的血肉，让人真切地感受到夜之城的繁华与腐朽、希望与绝望并存。
游戏的剧情更是一大亮点。主角 V 的故事充满了未知与惊喜，从一个籍籍无名的小人物逐渐卷入夜之城的权力纷争，每一次的选择都像是在人生的十字路口做抉择，而这些选择又会切实地影响到剧情的走向和最终结局。这种高度的自由度让玩家真正成为了故事的创作者，每一次游戏经历都是独一无二的。而且剧情中的角色塑造极为丰满，他们有着各自的性格、动机和过去，与 V 之间产生的情感纠葛也十分动人，让人忍不住全身心地投入到他们的故事中，为他们的命运担忧、欢喜。
在沉浸感方面，《赛博朋克 2077》堪称典范。音效设计十分出色，无论是街头的嘈杂声、载具行驶的轰鸣声，还是各种高科技设备发出的电子音效，都仿佛将玩家直接带到了夜之城的现场。画面表现也相当惊艳，细腻的建模和精美的光影效果，让每一个场景都极具视觉冲击力。再加上出色的配乐，与游戏的氛围完美契合，进一步加深了玩家的代入感。

Cyberpunk 2077 - это просто охрененная игра. Cyberpunk - это одна из тех игр про которые сложно нормально рассказать, потому что слов тупо не хватает. Мне в ней нравится вообще всё.  Да, вообще. Но если по-честному, то половина успеха - это охринительный сеттинг.

Найт-Сити - это не просто город для заданий. Это атмосфера давящая, красивая, грязная, стильная. Ты просто едешь по улице, играет музыка, вокруг неон, реклама, люди — и уже ловишь эмоции. Даже если ничего не делать, просто находиться в этом мире приятно.

Я не знаю, как выразить ту тучу эмоций, которые испытал за неоднократные прохождения с начала на пиратке потом на лицензии. История цепляет, персонажи запоминаются, моменты реально остаются в голове. После некоторых концовок просто сидишь и смотришь в экран, потому что нужно время переварить.

Да, на релизе всё было так себе. Но они реально всё допатчили, перепатчили и довели игру до состояния конфетки. Сейчас Cyberpunk - это пример того, как нужно исправлять свои ошибки, а не забивать на игру после провала.

В итоге это не просто «игра про будущее», а сильный, эмоциональный опыт, в который хочется возвращаться. И каждый раз он всё равно цепляет.

[h1]Найт-Сити: красивый город, в котором тяжело жить[/h1]

[b]Cyberpunk 2077[/b] — это игра, которая одновременно нравится и утомляет. Она может быть очень атмосферной, стильной и эмоциональной, но при этом не всегда удобной и стабильной. Даже сейчас Найт-Сити ощущается как город, который живёт по своим правилам и не особо подстраивается под игрока.

[h2]Картинка и производительность[/h2]

На моей RTX 5060 игра выглядит отлично. Неон, ночной город, освещение — иногда просто останавливаешься и смотришь по сторонам.
Но 8 ГБ видеопамяти дают о себе знать. С включёнными лучами первое время всё работает нормально, но спустя какое-то время начинаются просадки FPS и ощущение, будто управление становится менее отзывчивым.

Я пробовал разные конфигурации настроек: менял пресеты, включал и выключал RTX, экспериментировал с DLSS и другими параметрами. Это помогает на старте, но проблему полностью не решает — через какое-то время просадки всё равно появляются. Честно говоря, я даже не до конца понимаю, в чём именно причина: возможно, дело в видеопамяти, а возможно, у меня есть какие-то проблемы с железом или его настройками. В итоге приходится выбирать: либо RTX на средних настройках, либо ультра без лучей.

При этом даже без RTX игра выглядит очень достойно, особенно ночью.

[h2]Технические моменты[/h2]

Иногда игра всё ещё ведёт себя странно. Бывает, что [b]машины исчезают прямо перед тобой на дороге[/b], но ты всё равно в них врезаешься.
Иногда [b]предметы окружения на несколько секунд становятся невидимыми[/b], а затем появляются обратно. Пару раз я также застревал в текстурах зданий.

Такое происходит редко и не ломает игру полностью, но выбивает из погружения и показывает, что [b]Cyberpunk 2077 до сих пор не идеален технически[/b].

[h2]Геймплей и бои[/h2]

Я играл через силу: катана, оружие и импланты. Поначалу это весело и эффектно, но со временем становится слишком просто.

[b]Большинство врагов почти не оказывают сопротивления.[/b] Даже на высокой сложности они быстро перестают быть угрозой, и бои теряют напряжение.
Выделяется разве что Адам Смешер, но и он сложен не из-за механик или тактики, а просто потому, что у него много здоровья. Это скорее затянутый бой, чем реально сложный.

Вождение тоже спорное: есть машины, которые управляются приятно, но большая часть ощущается не очень уверенно.

[h2]Сюжет и персонажи[/h2]

Сюжет в целом [b]просто хороший[/b]. Он не делает ничего революционного, но нормально держит интерес до самого конца.

[b]Многие персонажи[/b], включая героев побочных заданий, запоминаются. У них есть характер, и они не ощущаются пустыми. Побочные квесты хорошо дополняют основную историю, но не пытаются быть важнее неё.

Джонни Сильверхенд — яркий и харизматичный персонаж, хотя отношения с ним иногда развиваются слишком резко.
Пролог показался слабым: он короткий, и ключевые события не успевают по-настоящему зацепить эмоционально, тем более что часть из них была известна ещё до релиза.

[h2]Саундтрек[/h2]

Музыка в игре — [b]одна из её сильнейших сторон[/b]. Она отлично передаёт атмосферу Найт-Сити и часто пробирает до мурашек.

Многие треки я переслушиваю отдельно от игры, и они всё равно вызывают те же эмоции. Саундтрек отлично работает сам по себе и легко возвращает в этот мир даже тогда, когда игра давно закрыта.

[h2]Концовки[/h2]

Я открыл все концовки, и они оставляют тяжёлое впечатление. В игре нет по-настоящему счастливого финала. Какой бы путь ты ни выбрал, ощущение потерь остаётся.

Это грустно, но честно. Cyberpunk 2077 не обещает счастливый исход и не пытается угодить игроку.

[h2]Итог[/h2]

Cyberpunk 2077 — игра не идеальная, но запоминающаяся. У неё есть технические проблемы и спорный баланс, но атмосфера, музыка и общее настроение перекрывают многое.

[h1]Cyberpunk 2077 Review[/h1]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1091500/Cyberpunk_2077/
[h2]Spoilers ahead[/h2]

I wish I could give it a neutral/medium rating. I completed all achievements, spent 70 hours in the game, and basically binged it without breaks.

I’m not a fanboy, so you won’t see me blindly praise it as a 12/10. There are major parts of the game that are just… bad, especially compared to what it’s being praised for.

[h2]Negatives[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Bugs and glitches:[/b]

Six hours in, my character got stuck on a fence. Literally stuck. I couldn’t move, jump, or crouch—only rotate the camera. The fence wasn’t anything special and even had the climbing animation. Stuck.

Police cars would, without provocation, aggressively follow or crash into me. If you don’t touch anything, nothing happens. Accelerate even slightly and suddenly a police officer will hunt you down.

NPCs who say they will call you sometimes refuse to call. I leveled up nearly ten times, cleared almost all Cyberpsychos, completed side content, and Rogue still wouldn’t call. Sleeping manually and trying forum tricks didn’t help. I had to reload an older save to avoid missing an alternate questline tied to an ending.

Cutscenes cannot be skipped. No matter how many times you play or how familiar you are, you must watch them all with their slow mannerisms and quirks. Around 75% of a replay is spent listening to Dex, Jackie, or Arasaka people. Only certain dialogues can be advanced, not cutscenes.

[b]Loot:[/b] Loot becomes irrelevant six hours in. I found a good pistol, sniper, and shotgun, and didn’t swap them until reaching Dogtown, where I replaced them with iconic weapons. Loot doesn’t matter.

[b]Story urgency:[/b] Inconsistent. During main missions, V will cough blood, faint, or be distressed, but two minutes later you can party with the Nomads, help Judy, raid NCPD scanner locations, kill Psychos, or play concerts with Johnny. Either the urgency should matter or it shouldn’t. Ignore side content and the game ends quickly. After the Hanako Parade mission, the story is basically over.

[*][b]Phantom Liberty:[/b] Same issue. After a point, So Mi contacts you, and you spend days infiltrating Dogtown, assisting the President, and playing Agent. You’re supposed to be barely alive, constantly repaired by nanobots, yet expected to act normally. Breaks immersion.

[*][b]Repetitive gameplay (Ubisoft style):[/b] NCPD Scanners, Cyberpsychos, Gigs, and carjackings follow the same patterns. Open the map, run 150–350 meters, kill NPCs, loot, repeat. Phantom Liberty missions are slightly better, but the base game is basically:
[code]see NPC → shoot NPC → loot → done[/code]
Speed, double jump, and dashes make this even faster. It’s boring and offers little challenge or strategy.

[*][b]Carjacking missions:[/b] Absurdly repetitive. Every mission:
[quote]“V! I KNEW I PICKED THE RIGHT MERC FOR THE JOB! V! V! I KNEW I PICKED THE RIGHT MERC! THE RIGHT MERC! V! THE RIGHT MERC! V!”[/quote]
Even the Arasaka Truck mission has the same line in the middle of action. It becomes ridiculous and breaks any tension.

[*][b]Empty city:[/b] Beautiful but hauntingly empty. Graphics and copy-pasted NPCs do not make an open world feel alive. NPCs barely interact, repeat a few lines endlessly, and most buildings are non-interactable. Invisible boundaries punish you with fake fall damage, even when climbing or jumping.

For comparison, older open worlds like Morrowind (over twenty-five years old) let you freely climb, jump, and explore almost anything. Cyberpunk cannot handle that level of openness.

[*][b]NPCs and world design:[/b] Hollow. Most repeat the same lines for 70 hours. The world feels static rather than dynamic.
[/list]

[h2]Positives[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Story:[/b] Engaging overall, though somewhat generic and predictable. Phantom Liberty missions are stronger than the base game.

[*][b]Character writing:[/b] Johnny is deep, multi-layered, and stays true to his core principles. Different endings highlight his character variety.

[*][b]Character mirrors:[/b] So Mi mirrors V, Reed mirrors Johnny. Interactions are excellent. Voice acting is strong: Minji Chang as So Mi, Idris Elba as Reed, Keanu Reeves as Johnny.

[*][b]Takemura:[/b] Well-written and consistent.

[*][b]Romances:[/b] Fine but limited in depth.

[*][b]Minigames:[/b] Mostly retro-style. Some reward outfits or apartment items.
[/list]
