Cyberpunk 2077 is a fantastic story and I loved every moment of it.

The story of this game is you are V. A merc in Night City who wants to climb the ranks and become a legend and after a job doesn't go as planned you end up with the construct of old Night City legend and terrorist Johnny Silverhand. 
So now the goal is to get Johnny out of your head before he completely takes over your body. 
Its not that complicated of a story but i think that its characters and the relationships you build along the way is what makes the story so good.
Johnny is stuck in your head and can only appear and talk to you and i love that more often than not during situations and conversations with people Johnny will just appear out of nowhere to comment (usually with a lot of profanity) on the situation. Not only that but i also love characters like Jackie, Panam and Judy. Would also mention Claire as well but she ended up hating me in my playthrough so fuck her.

Now this game is an RPG and although V isn't necessarily a self insert character and they have their own personality and goals. They are a great character you play as and you choose their decisions so you get the feeling of a character you can project yourself onto. 

And of course you level up different attributes of V the way you want and how you play. If you prefer going in with brute strength then go for it. If you prefer to keep your distance and stealth your way through situations or Hack the systems to reach your goal then go for it or if you prefer guns blazing then go for it.

As for the world of Cyberpunk. its absolutely gorgeous. I love Night city and all of its neon lights and there are tons to do. you can stop crime, stop a cyber-psycho, go to a bar and drink, every now and then the character you romanced will trigger a mission called 'I Really Wanna Stay at your House' which is just a date at your apartment and its sweet, you can get new guns or cyber-ware and you can even hire a Joy Toy.
There is always something to do.

Now there are multiple endings depending on your choices. Including a secret ending if you have a good enough relationship with Johnny and you wait 5 minutes at the ending choices. 
To get a good enough relationship with Johnny you have to have done specific missions, choose specific dialogue options and don't kiss his ass and just agree with him constantly. You have to call him out every now and then so he respects you.

Overall Cyberpunk 2077 is amazing and even after finishing the main story i am back and playing more to do all the side missions, explore and just enjoy myself.

Maior representação do mundo real.
Por que?
Pois em Night City sua vida e jornada, aquilo pelo o que passou e as dificuldades que você enfrentou não significa nada. Você tem "edinhos"? Pois bem... Isso é o que importa.
Nada de tchuns (amigos) a longo prazo, se eles não morrem você morre, nada que você faça vai mudar o fato que ou você morre atrás de dinheiro, ou tentando ser alguém importante. Mas no final tudo se trata de apenas uma coisa; sobrevivência, tal qual o mundo real.

Os grandes prédios, as luzes neon e os carros altamente futuristas, e elementos no qual faz esse jogo parecer tão marcante, nada mais é para tentar mascaras os traços do mundo em que vivemos com a desculpa de um mundo novo e cyber-futurista. Assim como na atualidade, a busca incessante por edinhos e o contexto em que você está inserido molda seu personagem e aqueles ao seu redor assim destacando a filosofia central de Rousseau (O homem nasce bom, a sociedade o corrompe). Mas em Night City quando a corrupção começa? Provavelmente bem cedo, assim como na vida real.

"Os fins justificam os meios". Você ja escutou essa frase certo? Geralmente atribuída a Maquiavel mesmo que ele não tenha criado essa frase, ela tem como principal entendimento a prática de que, não importa aquilo que você faz contanto que o indivíduo central conquiste seus objetivos. Parece algo meio individualista e egoísta não é? Bem... Tenho a certeza que você já conheceu alguém assim. Pois os elementos centrais do jogo está ao redor de todos aqueles que respiram e daqueles que já passaram por essa terra.

My fav memory from the game is spending 45 minutes walking around a single block looking for a hidden entrance and parkouring over the skyscrapers because the mission marker was 3 meters above my head and I refused to believe the only way up is the main staircase like some kind of a pleb.
You learn a lot about physics when your most optimal route is straight up/down.

Cyberpunk is a master of immersion. 
I wanted to simply try out the game for 5 minutes before sleep, just to see what it's like, but I was greeted by an inner voice: No sleep for you buddy! It's Night City Night.

Very few games nowadays can get me engaged this fast from the get-go. 
The scariest part about the game is not the Arasaka or the vivid dystopian future - It's the fact that during the time I played it completely replaced my socializing needs - this just hints at how well thought out player-game interaction is, and the first person angle amplifies the visceral experience.
The city truly feels alive. Every single NPC has a name and a tragic backstory, which means I'm constantly delaying missions just to stand there like an idiot and eavesdrop on their local gossip. 

Cyberpunk 2077 has kickstarted its artstyle revival. It has done what Blade Runner did, just as good if not better. The sheer density of visual information is overwhelming, but in a positive way and I guarantee there is not going to be a 10 minute period where you won't experience sensory overload. You could probably not even pay attention to the game's story and still have fun just beholding the buildings, cars, flying vehicles, futuristic fashion and listening to music.

Cyberpunk's music direction choices were a bullseye hit. 
The music is tied to the game's world identity. It has a very wide array of genres - from simple beep boop rap to futuristic black metal to the renowned classics of jazz - I was really surprised to hear Charles Mingus while driving around in my Caliburn and it further reassured my enthusiasm towards that game. The atmospheric side of the soundtrack (not the songs you listen when driving like a maniac but rather the stuff that plays when there's a story breakthrough) beautifully emphasize the story reception and emotions. 

I found the combat way more enjoyable than Witcher 3. 
The game really incentivized you to develop your equipment based on your desired playstyle. 
You can dash around like an idiot with a katana, you can go full berserker with an LMG, you can go full stealth with a suppresed pistol+knife, and the best part of it is it affects the story of the missions. Your playstyle is not dictated by just one aspect like a weapon choice. It stems from multiple aspects like: implants, tech tree and weapon mods. The tech tree might be intimidating but the levelling tempo is balanced out to mitigate this. 
The only issue I have with all this customization is the constant pressure to scavenge. I’ve developed this twitch where I cannot leave a dumpster or a dead enemy unlooted.

It's a shame Cyberpunk had such a bad launch, because it is definitely in the top 3 of story games that I've finished, I'd consider it a Magnum Opus. I'd even say this is a greater Magnum Opus than Da Vinci's Mona Lisa, Homer's Odyssey, Beethoven's Symphonies and Michelangelo's David. Why? Because it blends all kinds of art into a one medium, and it delivers it on a very high level. While all those other artists were limited to marble or oil or words, CDPR was working in the medium of neglect of my personal life and I enjoyed every second of it.

My only complaint would be how separated the DLC feels from the main game - I recommend NOT halting the main storyline for the sake of the DLC, finish it and then just load THAT savefile.

It is a must play.

8.5/10  Great game.  

Grand Theft Auto in the dystopian future.  Gameplay, combat, Night City, the Badlands, the graphics...chef's kiss.  11/10.  Never seen anything like it.  You truly feel the dirt and despair of the environment.  The overall story, Kenau Reeves guest staring, the 1st person view making you truly feel like you're 'V', even if it's voice acted.  

The RPG elements are all there, and while different, I feel it works, as there are multiple RPG elements to take advantage of.  

The sound is hit or miss.  Some decent radio tunes, the background music can be good at times, but the background music can be beyond migraine-inducing too.  I've had to turn it off and go on YouTube and have Stealth Music from Irving Heat playing just so I can have some decent background music that isn't the radio when I'm running (or sneaking) around Night City.  

The dialogue is sophmorish at best.  Sweet Baby Inc. got their mitts into CD Projekt Red, which is now a publicly traded company.  Meaning their focus is not about Art, Story, or Character Depth anymore, it's about maximizing player base and profit while minimizing cost.  Meaning CDPR tried to appeal to 15 year olds and 50 year olds, and everyone in between, all at the same time.  Meaning the story and dialogue are dumbed-down.  There is also a lot of unnecessary cursing.  I love cursing.  A lot.  But this was too much even for me.  It's a sign of insecurity in the writers.  Also, desiring fame and wanting to be "the most famous mercenary in Night City," is another sign of insecurity.  The main focus is to heal yourself from the Relic, but also be famous?  It doesn't make sense.  

The story even contradicts itself at times.  In the same conversation, not only can dialogue be repeated (not a glitch, actual dialogue with a few words changed around), but attitudes and priorities can suddenly change.  It's hard to explain, but it's not a mature storyline.  The voice acting is also hit or miss.  Female 'V' is great, and most of the other characters are great.  Idris Elba as Solomon Reed is the best voice acted character in the game.  But some of the random NPCs are absolutely atrocious.  

I wish I could give this game a 10/10.  The environment is like nothing I've ever seen before.  Driving in the different cars to so many different places is...resplendent.  8-D  You know what really stuck with me?  The pedestrian railings in Japantown (and elsewhere).  The cold, hard, steel with no humanity or life in them.  Even leaning on them is painful.  And the concrete railings near V's apartment.  And the vending machines with cheap food and drink literally everywhere.  It really brings the Dystopia home.  

But the story...the dialogue.  It's beyond childish at times.  I couldn't even do some of the side-quests because SEVERAL of them were, "My partner is cheating on me; find out who with."  :| .....  I'll pass.  But overall, most of the quests are pretty good, if some of them are quite short and shallow.  

There are subtle nods to how torturous development was for the main team at CDPR.  So many hidden easter eggs.  The glitter waterfall at the top of the tower in Dogtown (the talent falling into smoke and ash, because everyone is leaving; it won't be the same CDPR that makes Witcher 4), the sad face Reed always has, talking to a little girl and she says, "I'm a princess and you're not, la la la, la la la la..."  I've done research, and those were the kinds of managers the team had to deal with...I'm not even going to go into the initial disastrous first launch, and then charging us for a DLC that should have been in the main game to begin with.  Even the name is a message, 'Phantom Liberty."  Like Metal Gear Solid 5.  The Phantom Pain...  

Anyway, play it, enjoy it.  Just know it could have been so much better.  A decent overall story, and the game itself is very fun, but in my opinion, no mod can fix the dialogue.  And while a great game, I will probably never return to replay it, even with mods.

Well then… I never thought I'd say this, and I never thought it would be this sad, but goodbye, Night City.

This was a pretty long journey, stretched out over years. And you know what? I just didn't want to finish the game, because I knew it would end…

A game I once used just to test my PC's performance became my favorite game. I fell in love with it fast. And that love started the moment I heard the radio in the car. "Never Fade Away" was playing. To say that the energy of that song impressed me would be an understatement. Back then, I hadn't heard anything that emotional in a long time. I genuinely love the game's soundtrack — it's high-quality and perfectly fitting, and the band Samurai is something else entirely. I never thought I'd love a fictional band.

And then Johnny appeared. At first — like a splinter, like noise in your head, like a foreign voice that's annoying and keeps pushing in where it's not welcome. But the further you go into the story, the more you realize he's not just a hologram with a rockstar attitude and an ego the size of Night City. He's a reflection, a mistake, pain and protest all at once. His past, his anger, his regrets slowly intertwine with V's story, and at some point you catch yourself no longer knowing where he ends and you begin. The story doesn't try to be "comfortable" or heroic — it presses on you, doubts, asks uncomfortable questions about identity, choice, and the price you pay for living. And that's exactly why it hits so hard.

And then you stand at the edge of the story, looking at this city — cruel, beautiful, fake, and alive at the same time — and you understand that this goodbye is real. Not to a game, but to something bigger: to time lived through, emotions, a state of mind. Cyberpunk 2077 is not a perfect game, but it's honest in its feelings. It leaves a void after the final credits and that very silence where you just want to sit and think.

Goodbye, Night City. Thank you for the noise, the pain, the music, and the moments that won't fade away.

Never fade away.

Cyberpunk 2077 é um excelente jogo. Mas, melhor do que o jogo em si, é o universo que ele habita. Toda a distopia futurista tecnológica, para quem tem o mínimo de abertura ao tema, é muito bem explorada e aproveitada para criar uma atmosfera única e uma ambientação extremamente imersiva.

Em comparação a outras mídias, os jogos possuem uma vantagem considerável quando o assunto é imersão. Você não vivencia Night City apenas como espectador: você faz parte da cidade e da história. É você quem toma cada uma das decisões que impactam o futuro e o destino de inúmeros personagens ao longo da gameplay. Nesse quesito, devo admitir, nunca joguei algo tão prazeroso.

Estar na pele de V é uma experiência única, profundamente imersiva e bastante satisfatória do começo ao fim. O melhor é que toda a sua integração ao universo do jogo acontece de forma orgânica: você não se sente confuso com conceitos novos, nem com as gírias que Night City apresenta (a dúvida sobre “o que é um Tchum?” não dura muito tempo). Aliás, falando em localização, que trabalho incrível. A dublagem é de altíssima qualidade, e termos como “clandesclínica” ou “medicânico” dão um charme muito especial, convenhamos.

Cyberpunk 2077, como um bom RPG, oferece uma quantidade gigantesca de conteúdo adicional. Muitas sequências de quests secundárias são — várias vezes — ainda mais envolventes e interessantes do que a própria história principal. É muito comum você se engajar em histórias paralelas e acabar esquecendo, nem que seja por um instante, que seu V está à beira da morte, em uma corrida contra o tempo.

Gosto bastante de como todas as quests são integradas por meio de contatos, “cacos” de conversas e mensagens. Novamente, tudo acontece de forma muito natural. Com um pouco de atenção, dá para perceber como uma quest leva à outra e como, aos poucos, seu V vai se desenvolvendo, criando laços e ficando mais forte.

Sabemos da polêmica que envolveu o lançamento do jogo; felizmente, não tive contato com Cyberpunk 2077 nessa época. É de conhecimento público a enorme volta por cima que o jogo deu, apesar dos problemas iniciais, e nem preciso me estender sobre isso aqui. Se você ainda tem a imagem de que Cyberpunk é um jogo cheio de bugs, mal otimizado e com problemas de compatibilidade, pode esquecer. Tudo foi consertado. Claro, vez ou outra algo estranho pode acontecer, mas nada realmente relevante.

Certamente, se eu fosse fazer um review completo abordando cada aspecto desse jogo, precisaria escrever mais do que seria possível. Por isso, encerro dizendo apenas que Cyberpunk 2077 foi uma das experiências mais satisfatórias que já tive com um videogame em toda a minha vida.

I really wanted to like Cyberpunk 2077, but I just can’t get into it. Despite its scale and presentation, the game feels shallow at nearly every level. Night City looks impressive at a glance, but it plays like an empty theme park rather than a place people actually live. There’s spectacle everywhere, yet very little sense of routine, history, or everyday life. It’s loud, dense, and busy — but rarely believable.

Many of the systems the game presents as important feel undercooked or pointless. Hacking, for example, is framed as a core mechanic, yet it rarely feels meaningful or necessary. Dialogue options are plentiful, but they often amount to cosmetic flavor rather than real choice. I rarely felt that my decisions mattered or that the game respected my time or agency.

Even visually, the game doesn’t hold up as well as its reputation suggests. There’s a huge amount of visual noise — neon lights, fog, particle effects — but when you slow down and actually look, many textures feel flat or unfinished. Surfaces lack detail, environments rely heavily on lighting to mask simplicity, and the world often feels like a façade held together by post-processing. Night City looks striking from a distance, but up close it can feel oddly hollow, as if pieces are missing.

The overall tone is relentlessly vulgar, graphic, and grotesque in a way that feels juvenile rather than purposeful. Instead of using excess to say something meaningful, the game leans on shock for its own sake. It comes across less like thoughtful cyberpunk and more like something designed to impress teenagers with how edgy it is. This constant attempt to provoke ends up undercutting any moments that might have carried real weight.

The main story doesn’t help. It feels like something you endure rather than something you want to engage with. Cyberpunk 2077 borrows heavily from better works — Blade Runner, Akira, Deus Ex, RoboCop, SiN, Watch Dogs — but it imitates their aesthetics without understanding what gave them substance. It has the vibes, but none of the insight, restraint, or thematic depth that made those stories endure.

Spending time in the character creator or customizing your appearance also feels pointless when every narrative outcome leads to V’s death. Compared to a game like Red Dead Redemption 2, where Arthur Morgan’s story is about redemption and meaning, V’s story feels like it’s about nothing at all. You invest time, effort, and attention into a character whose arc ultimately goes nowhere.

In the end, Cyberpunk 2077 is a game that wants very badly to feel important, deep, and transgressive, but rarely earns any of those things. Beneath the neon and noise is a hollow experience — impressive on the surface, but shallow, unfocused, and ultimately unsatisfying.

🌃 Cyberpunk 2077: La Redención Definitiva en Night City

Cyberpunk 2077 ya no es el juego que se lanzó en 2020; es la prueba de que la perseverancia puede convertir un inicio accidentado en una obra maestra generacional. Hoy por hoy, es el RPG de acción en primera persona más inmersivo, visualmente impactante y emocionalmente desgarrador que puedes encontrar en Steam. Bienvenidos a Night City, la ciudad que te lo promete todo y termina por devorarte.

🌆 Night City: El Personaje Principal
Ningún otro mundo abierto se siente tan denso y vertical como Night City. No es solo un mapa; es un organismo vivo de metal, neón y decadencia.

Diseño Urbano: Desde los rascacielos corporativos de City Center hasta los suburbios polvorientos de Santo Domingo, cada distrito tiene su propia alma, arquitectura y peligros.

Atmósfera: Pasear por sus calles bajo la lluvia ácida mientras escuchas la radio es una experiencia sensorial inigualable. La iluminación con Path Tracing establece el nuevo estándar gráfico de la industria.

🔌 Jugabilidad: El Cyberware y el Estilo de Combate
Tras el rediseño total del sistema de habilidades (Update 2.0+), el combate es dinámico y extremadamente satisfactorio.

Libertad de Build: Puedes ser un Netrunner que fríe los cerebros de sus enemigos desde las sombras, un Samurái con katana que desvía balas, o un Solo pesado con brazos de gorila que atraviesa paredes.

Cyberware: La gestión de tus implantes ahora tiene un límite de capacidad, lo que añade una capa táctica de RPG real. Instalarse un Sandevistan para ralentizar el tiempo y ver cómo las balas se detienen es, sencillamente, épico.

🎭 Una Narrativa que se Queda Contigo
La historia de V y Johnny Silverhand (interpretado magistralmente por Keanu Reeves) es un viaje filosófico sobre la identidad y la mortalidad.

Decisiones con Peso: El juego no te juzga, pero te hace vivir con las consecuencias. Los finales son crudos, humanos y dejan un vacío emocional que pocos juegos logran.

Phantom Liberty: La expansión añade una capa de thriller de espionaje que eleva el juego a la perfección, introduciendo personajes inolvidables como Solomon Reed (Idris Elba).

🏆 Veredicto Final

Cyberpunk 2077 es la redención hecha videojuego. Es una carta de amor al género ciberpunk que logra capturar tanto el brillo del neón como la suciedad de la calle. Es un viaje obligatorio para cualquier amante de los buenos RPGs y de las historias que te hacen pensar mucho después de que aparecen los créditos.

Puntuación: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (10 / 10) — Despierta, Samurai. Tenemos una ciudad que quemar.

I don't know why I can write a review for this game considering I don't own it on PC, but I will.

As someone who has played this game for ~75 hours on console and got a Platinum trophy, I can 100% recommend this game to basically everyone. It's no longer what it was when it first released and presumably hasn't been the same for quite some time now, CDPR really proved that a game with a horrible launch is fixable.

Night City, as a location, is the perfect embodiment of the future we are heading into. Corporations own everything, cities are very much vertical and people comoddify themselves. I don't know about you, but some of these trends are already slowly happening. Now, if we ignore the dark and gritty things happening within the city and just purely focus on THE city, I would say it is definitely one of the coolest locations I've seen in a game. It's hard to explain, but there is this certain vibe when you drive through the city (more specifically areas like Heywood, City Center, Westbrook, etc.) that I personally don't get in, e.g, GTA V.

The storyline is pretty good but also fairly short. The main point of it is that after something [b]very bad[/b] happens, you don't have much time to live. CDPR thought that because that is the main point of the game, the player needs to finish the main storyline as soon as possible. Problem? It's already short! You finish a main quest and the game throws another one directly at you and before you know it, you're already 50% done with the game with less than 10 hours in it and barely any side content done!

Not only that, the game is fairly easy, which isn't necessarily a problem. First game I ever played where the devs recommend you to play on hard instead of normal, but honestly in this game, "hard" just means "normal" and "very hard" means "hard".

I can't speak for the Phantom Liberty DLC as I haven't played it (yet), but according to others it is supposed to be pretty good too.

This game came out incomplete and, though a lot of bugs have been fixed, it doesn't deliver what was promised. The story is middling, the gameplay repetitive with some neat gimmicks that get old quick, and the world just isn't fleshed out.

Some characters and moments stand out but most of the time characters are just telling you things or leading you by the hand and you're expected to play along. All the fluff makes the actual good moments of the game come across as disjointed.

It's not a bad game, it's just mediocre made by a company whose last title was one of the greats. The story and characters suffer from the same writing problems the late-game of the Witcher 3 had, except here it seems most of the game was written with that way. 

The world-building is also terrible and seems like an after-thought, Night-City feels more like Toon Town with all the characters disappearing and reappearing constantly to give you basic missions, nearly all of which seem like they exist completely separate from one another. Most of what you know about the world will be from reading data-logs lying around or people straight up explaining things to you as if you were born yesterday (this wasn't how it was done in the Witcher where you saw things play out and pieced it together yourself).

If I was feeling mean I would say it's a tackier, edgier dystopian GTA that takes itself too seriously - but Cyberpunk has a bit more going on than that, I would only recommend it if you;
A- Really like cyberpunk settings in general (will make up for the lack of set-up this game has).
B- Want to 'tell your own story' Todd Howard style by killing the same mobs of enemies while glitchy techno music plays in the background (the combat can be fun - for a while).
C- Have more money than you know what to do with and want to use this game to benchmark your PC's performance.

This is probably one of the best games I have ever played, if not the best. Writing this after completing my first playthorugh as thoroughly as humanly possible at 350 hrs  (I can't get enough of this game and already have future playthroughs planned). The gameplay, variety of playstyles and builds, story, characters, music, dialogue, voice acting (played as female V), its all just so so well crafted with love and passion. Night City is probably one of the most dense, lived in, and beautful game worlds that just oozes with personality. Not a single quest or interaction in the game felt like a waste of time or like padded content, there were always unique interactions, lore tidbits and new experiences to be found. I liked how seemingly insignificant dialogue choices/order of quests affected the world and unlocked certain interactions/consequences that I would only find out about days later, making the playthrough truly unique. One thing that could have been expanded upon was the romance options, by which I mean both the variety of encounters as well more interactions outside the main quests, as having the same 2 lines available for every hang out felt repetive and lacked depth (its a wonderful feature, just needed to be fleshed out more). Apart from that, my only other complaint/nitpick would be that we needed a lot more clothing options, as a lot of times it felt like a clothing option would be great on its own, but making an outfit based around it was very difficult, be it due to color variations, or lacking style options to match with, and also because there were so many npcs dressed better than what was possible for V lol. CDPR also outdid themselves with Phantom Liberty, absolute wild ride that was. Anyone looking to get into the game should most definitely get the dlc as well.

All in all, the game is a 10/10 masterpiece and probably one of the best pieces of art out there. This is the kinda thing everyone should experience once in their life. Happy gaming fellow chooms!

แต่ถ้าคุณเข้ามาเล่นโดยผ่านเกม RPG ยอดเยี่ยมหลายเกมมาก ๆ อย่าง The Witcher 3, Kingdom come, Skyrim คุณจะค้นพบว่า Content ส่วนใหญ่ของเกมนี้ค่อนข้าง "กลวง" เมื่อเทียบกับเกมข้างต้นที่กล่าวมา เนื้อหาประเภท Side gig ที่ให้ทำสะสมตามพื้นที่ต่าง ๆ นำเสนอไม่ค่อยดีนัก เหมือนทำมาเพื่อให้เรามีกิจกรรมทำจำนวนมาก ซึ่งการเล่นโดยหวังเก็บให้ครบเป็นอะไรที่ไม่สนุกเอาซะเลย ให้บรรยากาศเหมือนทำ Side quest ในเกม Skyrim ซึ่งนั่นเป็นเกมหลัก 10 ปีมาแล้ว แม้ว่าจะมี Side quest ที่สนุก หรือเนื้อเรื่องกินใจอยู่บ้าง แต่ Content ที่คุณภาพประมาณนั้นนับว่ามีสัดส่วนน้อยมาก ๆ เมื่อเทียบกับเควสให้ทำไปเรื่อย

Takes way too much time. I usually skip dialogue but not in this. I am hooked for this. World is love letter for Cyberpunk Genre. You take Metropolis, Bladerunner, Neuromancer, Ghost In the Shell and Akira.  Then add bit Matrix and Johnny Mnemonic as spice, bake it in game form and this is what you get.

I launched the game just to try it out and ended up spending almost 1000 minutes in a single session. Time completely disappears, there is always something new to do, and you keep telling yourself “just a little more”.

The romance storylines are done really well, a solid 10/10 for me. The characters feel alive, with real personalities and emotions. Panam’s storyline especially stood out. It’s written deeply and honestly, and you genuinely get attached to her.

What impressed me the most is the level of immersion. At any moment you can simply call a character, talk to them, or send a message. It may seem like a small thing, but details like this make the world feel alive. Sometimes I caught myself forgetting that this was a game at all.

Night City pulls you in with its atmosphere, music, and visuals. I often wanted to explore the city even without quests, just driving around, listening to the radio, and taking it all in. Combat and build variety give you the freedom to play the way you want.

Сюжет хоть до безобразия простой и клишированный но стоит отдать должное его постановке. Важные сюжетные диалоги и катсцены вылизаны практически идеально. Периодически удивляет многое: локация, проработка света, текстур, общее настроение, музыка, амбиенты. Но так только в важных моментах но и то не во всех. Стоит от них отойти в сторону побочек или просто открытого мира то там всё очень плохо В итоге про сюжет могу сказать что как минимум один раз пройти норм и глянуть что там по концовкам. Второе и последующие прохождения рассматривать нет ни малейшего желания даже с учетом что в начале есть различные варианты предысторий которые в самом деле хоть немного но всё же влияют на сюжет и прохождение в чём я изначально сомневался.

Побочных миссий много. Даже очень. Какие то попроще вида убей/спаси/укради/взломай по стелсу, какие то сюжетно подвязаны и фактически нужны но не необходимы для прохождения игры и довольно большие миссии даже с какой то да вариативностью. И даже тут не без проблем. Я точно знаю что наверняка не прошел их все но это точно не зависело от меня. Часть миссий просто висят на карте, часть дают как фактическое продолжения другого квеста в том числе и сюжетного а часть дают просто потому что. Буквально. Гайд по получению такого квеста буквально "уйди в угол карты и стой афк 10 минут реального времени если не помогло уйди в квартиру Ви и поспи 48 часов. Если не помогло - повторить".
Знаков вопросов на карте чуть больше чем дофига и они сильно упрощены геймплейно (вот тебе пачка врагов на локации убери их всех) и в качестве награды лут с врагов и записка с лором чаще связанная с той или иной побочной миссией.

Визуально игра удивляет. Как в хорошем так и в плохом смысле. Иногда это какая либо высококачественная модель с ультра реалистичной текстурой а иногда коробка в три полигона и ультра плохой текстурой и главное такое не скрыто где то в стороне и ещё найти надо а может попасться на глаза посреди обычной миссии. Да что там. Графические недоработки и баги могут попасться даже в титрах.

Геймплейно всё тоже по простому. Либо стелс либо бой при этом вариаций через бой немного больше и начиная играть через стелс я всё же начал всех вырезать т.к это всё таки веселее. Иммерсивность в таком случае работает через двери. Чтобы пройти на локацию и сделать миссию надо открыть одну из дверей. Одна с проверкой на силу и скорее всего автоматически начнёт бой, вторая с проверкой на технику или интеллект и ты будешь находится за спиной у всех врагов с укрытиями. Если такую проверку пройти не можешь то рядом есть открытое окно в которое можно зайти. Всё.
На вашу общую силу больше влияет ваш уровень и оружие/навыки на взлом. Навыки и дополнительные статы в большинстве ни на что не влияют. Я всей этой прокачкой занялся только в конце игры и что с этой прокачкой что без неё шибко большой разницы не обнаружил. Общий перекач вносит большее влияние.

[h1]A successful dystopian adventure[/h1]

This game does the cyberpunk genre justice. You move through a city driven by corruption and greed, ruled by wealthy mega-corporations. The dystopia feels real because it builds on experiences we recognize from our own time, just without regulation or control. The whole city is packed with ads on every corner: weapons, gambling, sex.

The top earners in the corporations act and think just as morally questionable as the criminal organizations underground, which gives the hopeless dystopian vibe a lot of credibility. Everything is loud, flashy, and broken in one way or another. It’s a world where nobody cares about you and you shouldn’t expect any empathy. People are exploited and used for maximum profit.

The setting is very coherent, and the characters feel believable in their actions and attitudes regarding the reality they live in. The gameplay is solid, but it’s a real shame that a game with such a strong focus on customization doesn’t offer a third-person view. The soundtrack is phenomenal and adds a lot to the atmosphere.

Many side quests can be approached in different ways depending on V’s abilities, and some side characters have surprisingly deep storylines that can really hit you. And Night City doesn’t hand out happy endings out of goodwill.

Driving doesn’t feel particularly satisfying, but on foot the game plays quite well. There are also lots of small details you can discover while exploring that have little or nothing to do with the main story, yet contribute a ton to the setting and overall atmosphere.

Personally, I’d say the final product still falls a bit short of the expectations that were built up, but the purchase was absolutely worth it.

2020年赛博朋克2077首发，那时我还是个大二的穷学生。考完期末最后一科，迫不及待回到寝室，根据哥们给我的盗版网站，下载了2077。没办法，298的首发价对于那时的我太过于昂贵。
大学最不缺的就是时间，每天陪伴我的就是2077与笔记本嗡嗡响不停的散热声。因为配置和盗版，游戏经常会出现过热闪退甚至存档损坏，记得当时打出的是和罗格一起打荒坂塔的结局。2077在当时可谓是被骂得惨烈，但对我来说倒是无感，唯一眼馋的就是博主们发的那些高画质游戏视频，跟我笔记本上显示的马赛克贴图简直天差地别。
一转眼五年过去了，五年后的今天，我被公司裁员，多年的感情止步于此，失去了目标和方向。在家浏览steam时刚好遇到2077打折，刚好自己配了3060ti的台式，于是毫不犹豫入了手，就当宴请过往的自己。在此期间我入手了dlc，看完了边缘行者，在网上补全了2077的世界观，知道了摩根黑手、奥特、红蜘蛛、荒坂、军用科技等背景资料。这几天我像是着了魔一样，每天陪伴我的除了外卖就是机箱散热的嗡嗡声。2.3版本和1.0版本简直就是两个游戏，没想到竟然有了地铁和自动驾驶，没想到dlc做得竟然比本体都精彩，更没想到2077治好了我多年的电子杨威。现在回想，所谓电子杨威，是因为自己将过多的时间和精力放在了现实，于是过去喜欢玩游戏的你被判为“不务正业”，但真的没必要。
在最后我送百灵鸟去了月球，和帕南一起离开的夜之城，打通关我长舒一口气，瘫坐在椅子上。感谢cdpr给了我一个新的世界，能让我从现实世界中抽出身，有那么一个虚拟世界的避风港。
我想每一个人都是v，因为每一个人都会走到生命的尽头。如果代入v的视角，最后的六个月你会干什么，还会焦虑眼下的事情么。
在奔三的年纪，才从游戏中学会着眼于当下，至少我没背负房贷车贷，父母和自己身体还算健康，这就够了。
结束了夜之城的旅程，我也要回到地球online对线了，想起了游戏初始黑胖“耶稣”所说“你是选择名扬天下还是无名小卒？”
我认清了现实，我只是一个普通平凡希望能快乐幸福过完一生的小卒。
以上是自己的一点点感想，祝各位v震天在夜之城玩的愉快。

「大事なのは、どう記憶されるか。誰が覚えているのか。」

2023年に購入していたのですが、現実逃避として今年の11月中旬頃から遊び始めました。本編をクリアした直後、ちょうど本作がまさかの5周年を迎えており、そこに何か運命的なものを感じたので、このレビューを書くことにしました。
これまで色々なゲームをプレイしてきましたが、これほどまでに自分を主人公に感情移入できるゲームは、これまで見たことがありません。
おそらく、今後数年間はこれほど没入させてくれる作品は出ないと思いますし、仮に出るとしたら、それは続編だと思います。（続編早く出てほしい！！）

このゲームは、自分なりに一言で表すなら、「自分が主人公」の映画です。
ミッションによってはアクション映画にもなり、ミステリー映画にもなり、時にはコメディ映画にもなります。世界観の作り込みも非常に優れており、VRなら本当にナイトシティという都市で生きていると感じられるかもしれません。

このゲームは、システムや演出など各方面で非常によくできています。とはいえ、そうした要素についてはすでに多くの人が絶賛しており、私が改めて語らなくても、文章力のある方々がもっと上手く伝えていると思います。私にとって何より良かったのは、主人公であるVに強く感情移入できる点、いわゆるロールプレイが成立している点でした。「自分がVだったら、この状況でこう言う、こういう行動を取る」。そうした選択を自然に考えさせてくれる点において、このゲームは非常に優れていると言わざるを得ません。没入感のある世界観と、その世界の一人の人間として生きている感覚が、本当に素晴らしかったです。

少しネタバレになりますが、生きるために様々なミッションをこなし、その結果としてどうしても悲劇的な結末へ向かっていく。しかし、それでも最後の道を自分で選べるという点が、個人的には非常によかったです。

「みんな幸せになれる・・・ハッピーエンドはないのかよ？」

　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　「この街で。俺たちみたいのに？そりゃ夢を見すぎだぜ、V」

　　　
　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　　「少なくとも選択する権利は手にできた。意志と努力の賜物だ」

V（わたし）は生きるために手を汚してきました。だからこそ、最後に全員が幸せになるようなハッピーエンドでは、さすがにご都合主義すぎるのではないかと思います。

もともと自分はビターエンドが好きなので、エンディングについても非常に満足しています。

個人的な感想として、このゲームはメインストーリーだけを追うとやや短く感じるため、一番おすすめしたいプレイスタイルは、ゆっくり遊ぶことです。
色々なミッションをこなし、街を観光し、道端のNPCの会話に立ち止まって耳を傾ける。そうした遊び方が、このゲームの魅力を最大限に引き出してくれると思います。「そろそろメインストーリーを進めるか」と感じたときに、少しだけ物語を進める。そんなペースがちょうどいいでしょう。

レビューはこれで一区切りついたところですし、私はこれからドッグタウンへ向かう予定なので、今回のレビューはここまでにしたいと思います。

Absolutely masterful.  Whatever issues may have plagued this game on launch - as of 2025 (going into 2026) - software here is spotless.  The story and [i]game[/i] underneath shine as brightly as I imagine was intended from the get-go.

I didn't rightly [i]know[/i] what I was getting into here.  I have no prior experience with CDPR games, so the writing took me by surprise.  If I had to expect anything, it would have been another Skyrim - a long list of checkboxes to tick and a rote, tired gameplay loop that gets boring as quickly as you reach the end of it, padded out by bullet sponge enemies or simply making you [i]walk farther.[/i]  A bunch of faceless, soulless PG-13 robots that exist to push you along to the next theme park ride.  But that's not at all what we've got here, not by a long shot.

I look at this, look at the hours I've put in here, in what feels like such a small amount of time, and I do not consider one minute of that time wasted.  Of course, there were issues, but they were so infrequent that experiencing the issues themselves stood out to me.  The fact that any occurred at all made me realize how seldom they happened.  There is no 'filler' here.  Everything that exists does so for a purpose, and of the time spent just going from A to B, there was always something fun to do in between, whether that was some kind of side-thing, or just the movement itself.  Everything was done fantastically.  Of the issues I had throughout my time with this game, all of them were either forgotten or resolved themselves before the end.

Truly the only issue that hasn't been fixed is that there isn't [i]more[/i] to some of the narratives, but nothing feels like it got the MGSV treatment.  Nothing here is half-finished or cut short, the game's lore doesn't just exist stuffed away in audio or text logs - though there are plenty of the latter if you like reading.  Some things just end on a cliffhanger.  Things you're never meant to know, maybe.

This game isn't the kind you can make a sequel to, I don't think.  At least not for another decade or so, give or take some kind of narrative epiphany.

The story was written by people who understand how people speak, and did not pull punches for the sake of pleasing either the player themselves or the PC in-universe.  There [i]are[/i] cases where you have to make decisions and you cannot do everything you can possibly want in one playthrough.  There are decisions with consequences that will affect how you play, and more importantly, how you [i]feel[/i].  You can savescum of course, but the only one you're cheating is yourself.  Robbing yourself of the experience you've just invested hours into seeing through.  This is not a game for the guy who wants to save everyone.  There's no all-seeing god looking over you to lower your score at the end for killing people instead of knocking them out.  There's just you, the world, and your conscience.

The topics covered in this game's story, among other things it holds, have always been extremely interesting to me in particular.  There are so many parallels here to things I've personally dealt with in my life, things I've already had to consider, problems I've solved or thought I had solved, now staring me right back in the face, in a way that seems as real as any sort of digital "reality C" can possibly ever be.  It may as well be real, with how it f-cks with my head.  I guess that's just art, isn't it?

This game made me change as a person, for the better.  Sounds dramatic, but that's the truth.  Through all the sci-fi bullsh-t, I see bits of myself in this thing.  I have walked away with new, perception-altering experiences tucked away somewhere in my brain, to inform my behavior down the line, am I to ever find my way into these situations again.

Maybe now I'll put together what being alive means.  I've got the pieces right in front of me - Disco, NITW, and the rest from my time in meatspace.  Maybe this was the last one.

Night City merita ogni secondo del vostro tempo
Dopo quasi 20 ore di gioco, posso dire con certezza che Cyberpunk 2077 è diventato il capolavoro che tutti speravamo fosse al lancio. Se siete stati indecisi fino ad ora, questo è il momento perfetto per entrarci.

Perché vale la pena giocarci oggi:
Immersione Totale: Night City è visivamente mozzafiato. Passeggiare per i vicoli di Watson o guidare nelle Badlands offre un'atmosfera che nessun altro open-world riesce a replicare.

Gameplay Solidissimo: Il feeling del combattimento (che sia stealth, hacking o scontro a fuoco aperto) è fluido e soddisfacente. La build del personaggio si sente davvero "tua".

Phantom Liberty è la ciliegina sulla torta: Anche se sono ancora nel pieno dell'esperienza, il DLC aggiunge uno spessore narrativo e una tensione da spy-thriller che eleva tutto il pacchetto. Dogtown è un'area densa e incredibilmente dettagliata.

Narrazione d'impatto: Le missioni non sono mai banali. Ogni scelta sembra pesare e i personaggi (Johnny Silverhand in primis) restano impressi.

In sintesi
Nonostante l'inizio travagliato della sua storia, oggi il gioco è pulito, profondo e onesto con il giocatore. È un'esperienza che ti spinge a riflettere sul futuro e sul valore della verità in un mondo che cerca di corromperla.

Voto: 10/10 - Un acquisto obbligatorio per chi ama i GDR e le grandi storie.

I'm frankly not sure how this game receives acclaim now despite it still being somewhat of a mess. Granted, most of the large issues such as crashes (Most of the time) or overall surface presentation have been resolved in due part to patches. However, I question whether or not this approach to game design is going to work out for studios when they can't even out develop a game from a decade ago or more. There are multiple arguments or conversations to be had about why the game shipped in such a state for the initial release, but it doesn't help everything has to be reworked and tacked on due to poor planning. Such additions don't feel natural personally and very awkward during a playthrough. 

I can at least praise the concept/art/music aspects of the game or even the general plot of the story, but interest just falls off for the story/gameplay so quickly after Act I. There's not really any captivating characters to keep interest for me personally besides Jackie and Johnny, but [spoiler] Jackie ceases to be after Act I [/spoiler] and Johnny is not well written or acted in my opinion. The spam of characters/quests contacting you as well doesn't do the game any justice either. It would at least hold up in some regard if it played like an RPG which might separate it from the mundane gameplay, but a lot of times you are forced into doing whatever the scenario wants you to do. 

An example would be getting into Clouds at the start of Act II looking for Evelyn. You can't bypass the receptionist in any way besides jacking in and creating a profile, despite there being another sole choice for the intellect skill right below it stating that's not safe. In almost any other RPG, there'd be bribe, intimidate, persuade, maybe flirt, or even just blow their brains out choices, but that doesn't exist here and barely is present in other missions. What's more ironic is that later a mission comes up where having somebody access your character's system proves to be fatal as a result of there being no choice to deny them doing so. Contrast this to Deus Ex: Human Revolution from 2011 where even just updating your character's system/augmentations due to a recall proves to be a problem later on in the story and the term RPG for this game become laughable.  

In short, while presentation is here, the gameplay and depth of an RPG isn't. You have a overall cool surface level world to shoot and drive in, but no place to really to immerse or build yourself in as your V. I've picked up this game three times now to try and really love it, but it's just not there. Would recommend any other RPG, even if some like New Vegas need a literal 20 mods just to tape the engine back together so it'll work.

Le système d'infiltration est similaire, les armes sont en terme de gameplay très basique (Et ce même si certains fusils ou certains révolvers sont juste des bonbons à utiliser) et la manière de se battre est semblable à beaucoup de shooter. Ne vous attendez pas à une révolution là dessus. Par contre c'est peut-être classique et vous aurez l'impression de déjà savoir jouer mais ça fait largement le travail.

Niveau visuel je ne peux m'empêcher d'être un peu déçu. Je vais être franc. Quand on me dit Cyberpunk, je m'attends à du lourd. Du chrome qui sort du dos de manière agressive, des implants rafistolés en vrac placé à la va vite sur la main d'un mec, des cyborgs dont l'humanité est à peine visible dans le regard... Du bon gros Gumn en terme de variété de corps. ( Ou Alita Battle Angel si vous ne connaissez pas le manga.) Malheureusement c'est pas le cas. Bien que le chrome et le métal est présent, il est très discret la plupart du temps. Je peux compter sur les doigts d'une main les personnages avec un charadesign vraiment surprenant dans le sens Cyberpunk du terme comme Adam Smasher ou le Maëlstrom (Qui reste assez basique globalement, je parle surtout des yeux.). Je voulais que le DLC en ajoute, il l'a fait. Pas de grand chose mais il l'a fait. 
Ensuite pour ce qui est de la ville... C'est juste une ville quoi. Encore une fois, y'a rien de surabusé. On nous parle de bätiment ou de structure de fou mais on en voit pas spécialement. Après qu'on me fasse pas dire ce que je n'ai pas dit, c'est beau. Y'a des intérieurs superbes et des zones qui ont un vrai charme mais je sais pas... Je me dis que j'attendais une expérience Cyberpunk plus forte que ça et que ça a largement biaisé mon jugement la dessus.

Niveau musique c'est très varié, il y en a pour tous les goûts. Le seul reproche que j'aurais à lui faire, c'est que je suis pas le public et qu'elle reste au final hyper discrète. Y'a aucun moment où je me suis dit qu'elle était indispensable quand je la remarquais.

Quand à l'histoire, je vous laisse découvrir. Que ce soit l'histoire du jeu de base ou celle du DLC, je trouve que les deux valent le coût d'être vécu. Et les fins me laissent un arrière goût d'insatisfaction... Rah. Voyez par vous même.

Pour les chasseurs de succès: Le jeu est très simple à faire au complet. Faites juste gaffe dans certaines missions, ce sera mon seul conseil. Par contre soyez prévenu, ce jeu possède à mon sens le pire type de succès: les succès "Différentes fins". Pourquoi? Parce qu'elles retirent toute la saveur de chacune des fins. Si il y avait juste "Terminer le jeu", y'aurait aucun soucis. Mais comme chaque fin est censé être émotionnellement forte, le fait de les faire pour ce genre de succès retire tout l'intérêt que tu y portes. Vous gâchez pas l'expérience. Jouez-y d'abord par plaisir.

Pour conclure, c'est un bon jeu. Faites le, ne serait-ce que comme introduction à l'univers ou l'esthétique Cyberpunk. Il est parfait pour ça. J'ai prit du plaisir à le faire et à le compléter mais ce n'est pas l'ovni que l'on m'a présenté. Je ne pense pas me refaire une partie. Une seule aussi complète suffira bien.

Cyberpunk 2077 — это игра с огромным потенциалом, которая прошла путь от разочарования к одному из самых атмосферных RPG последних лет.

Найт-Сити — живой, красивый и детально проработанный город. Исследовать его интересно даже без квестов: атмосфера, музыка, неон и общий стиль цепляют с первых минут. Сюжет и побочные задания написаны на высоком уровне, персонажи запоминаются, а история часто поднимает взрослые и сложные темы.

Боёвка и прокачка дают свободу выбора: можно играть через стелс, хакерство или чистый экшен. После крупных патчей и обновлений игра стала заметно стабильнее и приятнее.

Минусы всё же остались: мир не всегда реагирует так глубоко, как хотелось бы, а на старте игра подорвала доверие многих игроков. Но в текущем состоянии это уже совсем другой Cyberpunk.

Итог: сейчас Cyberpunk 2077 — это качественная сюжетная RPG с мощной атмосферой.
Определённо стоит попробовать, особенно в обновлённой версии.



Review in English

Cyberpunk 2077 is a game with huge potential that went from disappointment to one of the most atmospheric RPGs in recent years.

Night City is a vibrant, beautiful, and highly detailed world. Exploring it is enjoyable even without quests — the atmosphere, music, neon lights, and overall style are captivating. The main story and side quests are well-written, with memorable characters and mature themes.

Combat and progression offer a lot of freedom: you can focus on stealth, hacking, or pure action. After major patches and updates, the game has become far more stable and enjoyable.

Some issues remain: the world doesn’t always react as deeply as expected, and the rough launch damaged trust for many players. Still, in its current state, Cyberpunk 2077 feels like a completely different game.

Final verdict: Cyberpunk 2077 is now a strong, story-driven RPG with an incredible atmosphere.
Definitely worth playing, especially in its updated form.

В этой игре Ви разговаривает так будто я нахожусь в теле "подростка пытающегося быть крутым" и не только Ви, буквально каждый персонаж, разговаривают крутыми фразочками и я не знаю как дела обстоят в оригинальной озвучке, но конкретно в русской локализации все плохо, особенно с матами. Диалоги в которых нету выбора, игра позиционирует себя как РПГ,  но она абсолютно линейная и какой бы ты ответ не выбрал, все в конечном итоге сводится к одному единому выбору, по моему опыту выбор присуствует только в тех же романах, где ты банально можешь его завалить или в той же концовке и точно также выбор стилей игры абсолютно не имеет никакого значения, разве что прибавит разных вариантов ответа в диалогах, которые точно также ни на что не повлияют в будущем, а в остальном отличаться будет только началом игры, и я абсолютно непонимаю в чем смысл внедрения данного прикола.

Кастомизация персонажа максимально деревянная и как бы ты не пытался сделать красивого или намеренно уродливого персонажа в конечном итоге они будут выглядеть практически идентично друг другу, потому что ползунков изменения внешности банально нету, ты лепишь себе персонажа по готовым шаблонам, а сколько красивых слов было по поводу реалистичности всего этого. Графон и баги

Я не знаю, может я что-то где-то забыл включить, но у меня были дикие проблемы с дальностью прорисовки и я не нашел настройку, которая отвечает конкретно за нее, а в интернете единственным решением было скачать мод фикс на эту тему, в игре иногда просто все появлялось перед твоим лицом.
Самый смешной баг, который я встречал в этой игре, это когда я взял машину перехватом управления и въехал в рандомного типа и я видимо так неудачно в него въехал, что текстура его штанин растянулась почти на весь экран вплоть до того, что у меня начали проседать кадры, а машина в свою очередь просто взлетела в небеса.

Мир абсолютно кажется пустым и не живым. Из случайных событий разве, что можно встретить нападение шайки банд на машине и это максимум. Every time I turn down an alleyway I haven't explored, I find something new to do. 

The story progresses at a rate that gives you a chance to relish in a feeling or a mood, but still moves along fast enough that you can spend an hour each evening and feel like you accomplished something.

Just buy it if you haven't tried it, and if you like it as much as I did, there's an expansion that added almost an entirely new main story worth of content. 

I am pleased with CDPR and the efforts they took to fix the game, and I am VERY excited for a sequel.

Cyberpunk 2077 - игра, которая сначала упала, а потом встала и сказала: «Ну что, по новой?»

Cyberpunk 2077 - это та самая игра, которая даже спустя 5 лет остаётся эталонным бенчмарком для теста ПК. Если хочешь проверить видеокарту, процессор, охлаждение и собственные нервы - Night City к твоим услугам.

Графика здесь до сих пор одна из лучших в индустрии: свет, неон, тени, дождь - всё выглядит так, что хочется просто стоять и смотреть, забыв про сюжет.

А сюжет, между прочим, тут очень даже есть. Интересный, мрачный, местами философский и неожиданно человечный.

Персонажи живые, эмоциональные, отлично озвученные - к ним реально привязываешься. 

Город при этом ощущается не декорацией, а живым организмом, который дышит, шумит и живёт своей жизнью.

Сайд-квестов - вагон и маленькая тележка, и что особенно приятно - они не «принеси-подай», а зачастую ничуть не хуже основного сюжета.

Системы прокачки и механики дают кучу вариативности: хочешь быть тихим нетраннером, хочешь - киберберсерком, хочешь - стильным ганслингером. И всё это реально играется по-разному.

Да, на релизе было больно. Очень.
Баги, косяки, мемы - интернет всё помнит.

Но огромный респект CD Projekt Red за то, что они не бросили игру на полпути, а дожали проект до состояния, в котором не стыдно. Исправили, дополнили, отполировали - и сделали то, что должны были сделать изначально.

Итог простой:

Сегодня Cyberpunk 2077 - это культовая игра, прошедшая путь от провала до уважения.

Это большой, красивый, насыщенный и запоминающийся опыт, в который теперь можно (и нужно) играть без боли и разочарования.

Night City всё-таки заслужил второй шанс. И, чёрт возьми, он его оправдал.

两年前打完了本体全成就，那时候还是大一，玩游戏总有一种执念，觉得必须把地图上的问号清空，必须打出一个所有人都在的完美结局，才算没白玩。

现在是2025年底，大四快结束了。这两年的经历让我对很多事情的看法有了改变，不再那么执着于所谓的“完美”。再次站在维克托诊所的天台上，面对最后的抉择时，我忽然明白，在“夜之城”这座烂到骨子里的城市，根本不存在皆大欢喜的童话。夜之城没有活着的传奇，与其把V在乎的人拖进泥潭来换取虚假的圆满，不如由他自己去面对这一切。

通关后的感觉很复杂，并不全是爽快。在这个结局里，V似乎赢了一切——站在了夜之城的顶端，成为了“来生”真正的传奇；却又似乎失去了一切，辉煌背后只剩下最后六个月的生命倒计时。

但这恰恰是这个结局最让我触动的地方：它很纯粹。

之所以选择这条最难的路，不是为了证明V有多强，仅仅是因为不想再看到朋友流血。[b] “以我残躯化烈火” [/b]——V选择践行这句话，并不是为了毁灭，而是为了守护。为了保护罗格、帕南等等，不让她们卷入必死的战斗，V必须独自背负所有的风险。这是一个关于“承诺”的故事——对自己，也对身边的人。

那一刻，V带着强尼——这个曾经想杀V、如今却最懂他的混蛋，完成了最后一次演出。我们没有把身体拱手让人，也没有拉任何人垫背。

虽然V的时间所剩无几，但在太空中看向窗外的那一刻，我觉得V活得最像自己，也最像强尼。没有妥协，没有牵挂。

这或许不是最圆满的结局，但对于V来说，这是最体面、也是最好的告别。

Lo tenía precomprado y cuando salió me desilusionó como a todo el mundo, por eso lo abandoné sin terminar. Pero pasó el tiempo y fui viendo que los desarrolladores lo iban transformando de vergüenza a obra maestra y este año volví aprovechando mi compu nueva, ya que Cyberpunk 2077 sigue siendo un juego modelo para probar la performance de la última tecnología de NVIDIA.

La sorpresa que me llevé al entrar a Night City y ver que el ambiente ahora sí era completamente inmersivo y pulido hasta el más mínimo detalle, fue mucho más grande de lo que me esperaba. El humor afilado de cada publicidad y diálogo random seguía ahí, pero esta vez daba placer colgarse mirándolos, caminando por mercaditos llenos de humo y ruidos que hacen que casi huelas el ambiente. Las cucarachas en el suelo cuando te sentás en un chiriniguito a comer un bocado, el tránsito que ahora sí funciona bien... todo el ambiente me pareció excelente.

Por último, el RPG y la historia me engancharon desde el principio, cosa que la primera vez no me había pasado. La historia realmente es muy buena, las intervenciones de Johnny no son simplemente porque pudieron contratar a alguien famoso y le dieron unas líneas para que aparezca acá o allá. Mis prejuicios con el juego desaparecieron porque realmente está todo bien hecho. Llegué a la última misión sin ganas de que se termine, hice GIGs y maté psychokillers por todos lados, disfruté muchísimo del mundo y del juego completo. Las misiones de la main quest line y su final(es) están buenísimos, son fuertes, bien guionados y conmovedores. Me quedan recuerdos inolvidables de este juego como hacía rato no me pasaba con open world RPGs así que felicito a los desarrolladores que supieron sacar a esta joya del barro en el que se les había caído en el lanzamiento.

Cyberpunk 2077 has some strong dialogue and a handful of genuinely memorable moments, but overall I think it’s overrated. Even ignoring the disastrous launch and judging the game as it exists now, it still feels subpar when compared to other big narrative-driven open-world games like Grand Theft Auto V or Red Dead Redemption 2. Which it tried to compete with, so I think it's fair to compare them to these rather than the Witcher. I wouldn't really say this game is much of an RPG it's more so an action game.

I finished the main story and felt surprisingly little. RDR2’s ending hit me emotionally in a way this game never did, and I don’t think that’s just personal taste - it’s about buildup, character weight, and payoff. Cyberpunk has interesting ideas, but it rarely commits to them long enough to make them land.

I like Johnny Silverhand. He’s easily the strongest character in the game, and his arc is conceptually solid. What I appreciated most is that the story allows V to help Johnny finish his war with Arasaka, but still ultimately choose autonomy and survival. Johnny isn’t meant to “win” by replacing V - he’s a ghost, a consequence, almost like a demon bargain that has to end. Letting Johnny go isn’t betrayal that works I think it’s resolution a logical conclusion.

The problem is that very few other characters reach that level. A lot of the cast feels one-dimensional or forgettable, and many storylines reset emotionally instead of building momentum. The endings are philosophically interesting, but they’re emotionally distant. They feel like statements rather than conclusions, which makes it hard to care even when the ideas are sound. A lot of dialogue is very boring and there's only a few speeches that I would consider good writing.

The combat and gameplay also work against the narrative. Moment-to-moment combat is stylish and fun, at first but the systems are shallow and lose novelty fast. Builds become overpowered quickly, enemy AI rarely adapts, and the game leans heavily into power fantasy. This directly clashes with the story constantly telling you that V is dying, hunted, and disposable. Mechanically, you feel unstoppable; narratively, you’re supposed to feel desperate. That disconnect undermines tension and makes the stakes feel artificial.

The open world looks incredible, but it’s largely a visual sandbox rather than a systemic one. Gigs and side content are repetitive, enemy encounters lack identity, and there’s very little emergent gameplay to make Night City feel alive beyond its aesthetics. Compared to other cinematic open-world games, it feels flat and overly gamey. This game simply just has a bland jank nature to it.

The game constantly tells you it reminds you it’s a dog-eat-dog world where the system always wins, but it rarely makes that feel personal outside of Johnny. Choosing survival over martyrdom makes sense in this setting, yet the narrative doesn’t give that choice the emotional weight it deserves. It feels more like an intellectual exercise than a lived-in tragedy.

I like the setting and the genre, but the game didn’t live up to what it promised to be. It’s not worth full price in my view, and despite flashes of quality, it feels bland and underwhelming as a complete story experience. If others love it, that’s fine - it just didn’t deliver the cinematic, emotionally impactful narrative I was hoping for.

Base game verdict: Extremely mid - Johnny is the only redeeming factor and the aesthetics everything else is hollow cardboard.
DLC verdict: Even more mid with less freedom - bad writing disguised as everyone is manipulating you.

tl;dr, a solid 9/10, I would definitely recommend playing this game, ESPECIALLY PHANTOM LIBERTY.

Few things to point out:
Gameplay was good, movement/combat and was very smooth and enjoyable. Mind you, I was playing at the hardest difficulty. And at highest difficulty the game felt like it had a challenge. The game didn't let me run around like crazy without getting killed. And the killing part was pretty often. 
The dark sci-fi corpo dystopian setting was very ejoyable. What was only a dream some time ago, or a CGI movie, now is in a video game, that can be played. Also happy to see it in a AAA game setting/format. 
The OST is 10/10. Phantom Liberty probably pushes that to 11/10. 
Can't say a lot about the story. I cared enought to play it until the end. I think star power did add up a little bit (*ahem* Keanu). Phantom Liberty did feel a bit more interesting.

So why it's a 9/10 ? Well I can point out two things:
1. I mostly enjoyed V. I played a female V, and I do think she fits better (ESPECIALLY IN PHANTOM LIVERTY). Male V feels a bit generic. But the main issue was that she was consistently cocky while speaking with others. I mean sure, it's her character, but at some point it became unatural and unfitting.
2. I'm very dissapointed that after 5 years this game still has enough bugs that can be encountered while casually playing the game. Since I enjoyed the game and the game improved a lot since launch, I will assume that the game's engine is at fault. (It's probably the reason why the next Cyberpunk game will be on Ureal Engine...)

If you are somewhat interested in the game, here's my advice. Play the game on max difficulty. Do some side missions/activities and continue on with the story. If it gets boring or whatever, play until you can switch over to Phantom Liberty and continue with it.

After following this game's hype train from its 2013 trailer to launch, I really wish I could give this game a mixed review. Unless you've been completely offline for half a decade, you'll know that this game's debut was one of the most controversial and damaging game launches seen up to that date. Fast forward 5 years and you'll see many praising this game as "one of the greatest comebacks ever bro!" thanks to constant patches that were necessary to keep CDPR's reputation from sinking to the ocean floor, and an excellent anime launched nearly two years after the base game. I would never call Cyberpunk a "bad game" by any means, it's just if you ever stop to look at it in context, you'll see the broken promises, lost potential, the voids left behind by story rewrites, and an ultimately hollow feeling world.

Since Cyberpunk 2077's identity at launch became more known for its bugs than anything else, other pressing issues were quickly eclipsed behind NPCs walking through walls, cops spawning out of thin air to punish your crimes, and enemies t-posing while using the sandevistan. However gamebreaking (and hilarious), because the bugs and glitches that held the publicity spotlight were getting fixed, people began to forget the fact that the game was a mere shell of what was promised over the course of the 2010s.

I would say that this is especially true after the anime, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners, came out in 2022 and pumped new life and a new fanbase into the game. Most everyone who jumped in after watching the pop-culture phenomenon anime got to experience a completely different game than those at launch. Many new and returning players quickly began to praise it as a complete comeback akin to No Man's Sky. Ironically, Cyberpunk completely swept the "Labor of Love" award from No Man's Sky that year at the Steam Awards based on its newfound popularity, which I, and many others at the time, would say was mainly thanks to the popularity boost by the anime. However, many players who had been playing since launch were rather confused by CDPR winning the award, since all they were doing as "Labor" was fixing bugs and reversing asinine gameplay choices that should have been ironed out before delivery. They weren't even adding content to the game at that point. Effectively, Studio Trigger carried the corpse of Cyberpunk across the finish line, and CDPR got a crown for it. 

I wholeheartedly believe that CDPR does not catch enough flak for their broken promises and false advertising leading up to the game's launch. This game continues to advertise itself as an RPG, and the actual commercial advertising leading up to the game's launch promised a deep RPG experience akin to the tabletop game. Each of the unique lifepaths you chose for your V were going to have vastly different consequences on the gameplay depending on what you chose. Instead all you got is a flavorful 20 minute section at the beginning of the game according to your lifepath before your character flows into the same overarching story regardless of choice. 

Fallout 4 style branching dialogue runs the show with "Yes" (Corpo) "Yes" (Nice) "Yes" (Snarky) "No" (Mean) that ultimately changes nothing for the most part. Sometimes dialogue options can lead to extra bonuses if you choose the lifepath option, such as calming a hacker down with the Corpo option to where she gives you some extra eddies, but that's about it. The only time your choices will actually have an impact on the game is during the end. You will choose your ending and that's it, that's pretty much all the agency that you have. Outside of that, the story of your V will be the same as anyone else's. Even the way you build your character with upgrade points does not really matter since you are granted enough points to build an effective jack-of-all trades. And you can always just respec your character if you feel like your build does not benefit you. If you look at Cyberpunk as an action game with a couple RPG elements, it's a fantastic at what it does, but going off what it was advertised as: Cyberpunk a completely lackluster RPG.

One of the more nitpicky issues I have with Cyberpunk is the game's style and fashion. You might be ready to say "But Woomy, Cyberpunk is all about style over substance!" and I would completely agree with you. I would actually argue that base game Cyberpunk has a completely lacking in style for a cyberpunk setting, especially for something that takes place in the flavorful and stylish Cyberpunk universe itself. The base game's clothing options look more like what would be depicted by a stereotypical millennial in San Francisco who thought that mashing the styles of bandits from Borderlands with the fashion choices of the average level 1000 in GTA online would make for the perfect depiction of Cyberpunk's available style and fashion. During your gameplay, you'll find plenty of cheetah print fedoras, leather pants, rusty respirators, and worn out looking military surplus clothes, but nothing that really screams "high-tech, low-life" or "cyberpunk". If you want to argue with me "Well the chaotic nature of Cyberpunk is its style!" please just look at the ads leading up to the game's launch, and then look at the database of clothing options offered in the game. Simply just look at the stylistic differences between the style of the 2013 announcement trailer VS what was delivered in the base game in 2020. Beyond that, the styles that CDPR advertised in their "Style vs Substance" advertisement made before the game's launch are not even offered in the base game, making it another complete false promise. You can see them start to get touched upon in the game's DLC, Phantom Liberty, but even there, the list is cut too short for what should have been. It's rather pitiful variety for a game that takes place in a universe that's about people desperate to look, feel, and be unique in a world wrought with nihilistic consumerism. You can still tell that the game's amount and variety of clothing options were designed to fill the game's loot pool when it was running off of the horrid armor/clothing stats system that hindered the game at launch by forcing people to run around in underwear and netrunner headsets for the sake of stats. Now, the stats are gone, but the lacking fashion choices remain.

Ultimately, I would say Cyberpunk did not even begin to shine until its DLC, Phantom Liberty, came out. It could be said that wherever Cyberpunk fell flat in polish, character agency, style, and story, Phantom Liberty addressed it and fixed it within its own complete package and amazing self-contained story. It honestly feels jarring going from Phantom Liberty and back to the comparatively unpolished base game. Ultimately, Phantom Liberty left me wanting more, even when I knew I could not ever have more.

All in all, if you are going to buy Cyberpunk, please remember that it is ultimately not an RPG where your choices matter. It's an action game with a few RPG elements and a solid story that lacks polish literally everywhere besides the beginning, and the end. It's one of those games where if you ever stop to really look at it, you can still see and feel so much of the lost potential and broken promises around every corner. I can recommend the game with what it currently offers, but I can only recommend it if it's on sale alongside Phantom Liberty, as I feel like that is the real Cyberpunk 2077 experience.

Compré el Cyberpunk 2077 apenas salió en 2020, luego de haber estado más de 10 años esperando su lanzamiento. Pensé que, de tanto hype que tenía, me iba a decepcionar, pero al final, no lo hizo. Tampoco me decepcionó el early del juego, donde fue muy criticado por bugs y errores que tenía, haciendo que varios usuarios dejen de jugarlo, pero yo lo disfruté totalmente.

Hoy, volví a jugarlo para probar el DLC, y es imposible no notar lo pulido, sólido y maduro que está. La diferencia es notable en rendimiento, estabilidad y sensación general de juego. Si en su momento de lanzamiento, con todos esos problemas, ya me parecía un juegazo, hoy en día me parece una obra maestra. Cyberpunk 2077 hoy es la versión que siempre debió ser y una experiencia prácticamente obligatoria para cualquier fan del género.

Cyberpunk 2077 es un juego que hoy finalmente muestra la visión que CD Projekt siempre quiso entregar. Night City es, sin exagerar, uno de los mundos abiertos más impresionantes y atmosféricos jamás creados. Desde el primer momento, la ciudad te envuelve con su identidad distópica: luces de neón, arquitectura futurista, contrastes sociales y una estética cyberpunk muy marcada.

La dirección de arte y la composición de color son increíbles. Cada distrito tiene personalidad propia, y caminar por la ciudad de noche, bajo la lluvia y rodeado de carteles luminosos, es una experiencia visual única. Se nota el enorme trabajo artístico en los escenarios, interiores, vestimentas y diseño de personajes.

La historia principal es sólida, madura y muy bien narrada, con buenos diálogos y personajes totalmente memorables. Las misiones secundarias están muy bien escritas y, en muchos casos, son tan interesantes como la trama principal, aportando profundidad al mundo y a sus habitantes. 

En cuanto al gameplay, el juego ofrece una gran variedad de estilos de juego y la banda sonora es otro de sus puntos más altos, acompañando perfectamente cada situación de la trama.

Único punto negativo que remarcaría sería el de que una vez que elijamos nuestro final, no nos vuelva a aparecer la misión previa de "Hanako en el Ember" y tengamos la posibilidad de seguir nuestro camino haciendo misiones secundarias o finalizarla ahí dependiendo lo que hayamos elegido.

Si con sus errores iniciales lo recomendaba, hoy en día, si o si tenés que probar este deleite visual.

This game quickly rose to the top of my list of all time favourites. Great story and characters, engaging and fun gameplay, awesome soundtrack

Story:
Probably the best story in a RPG open-world game. A lot of twist and turns, engaging. None of the take this go there type of quest, each quest is waiting to suprise you in every turn. Some of the best character written as well, each of them feels unique and almsot actually alive. Hands down best endings in a RPG, none of them feels out of place, all of them logically make sense and feel like its something a real human can choose. And the Phantom Liberty DLC is what every DLC in a RPG should be like.

World:
Developers did a wonderful job crafting the world of cyberpunk, I will say it is the most immersive experience I personally have ever played in a -first/third person RPG. From the colour palet, intricate use of light and shadows between streets, to the ambient sounds, cyberpunk is a world that truly draw you in (or make you feel uncomfortable cause of how horrible life in NC is). 

Balance/different play-style:
The game used to be quite unbalanced, meaning certain play-style is significantly more rewarding than others in every difficulty. With the patches given with Phantom Liberty, I can say the skill tree is quite balanced, meaning you can use every play-style in every difficulty and be effective. Granted in the hardest difficulty there are certain play-styles that are easier to be effective, but other ways of playing works too. So you won't feel like you have to choose a particular way to play the game just because that is easier.

Bugs:
Like any game, this game has bugs. None of them game breaking. The npc T-posing and vehicles spawn out of nowhere bugs from the early days are gone. 

Mods:
There are so many mods, you don't need any of them to make the game playable, but there are some very good mods that can cater to the kind of experience you prefer in cyberpunk, and make the game even more immersive than it already is. I personaly recommend the Nova city mods, make the lighting in the game much more realistic and in turn, makes NC's different districts looks even more distinct than it already is.

Cyerpunk had a rough start, as we all know. It released as a shell of empty promises and ambitions that the developers had for the game but couldn't or wouldn't be able to implement in time for release.

CDPR redeemed themselves over the years by fixing this game, and righting the ship. Right now, it is a masterpiece, with an incredibly good story and realized near future dystopian world that is straight out of the genre bests like Blade Runner, The Matrix and Akira. It wears it's influences on it's sleeve but it stands on it's own.

I truly think it might be CDPR's best game now, even after the rocky start. Phantom Liberty injected such life into this game, as well as the 2.0 (and subsequent) updates that overhauled the game systems, RPG elements and progression to be just flat out better. 

The best thing about this game is the story has meaningful choices to make. It has a somewhat open-ended world but a strong, character driven narrative that doesn't pull it's punches. There are consequences to your actions and several endings that reflect that, and your relationships with certain characters can definitely change depending on what you decide to do. I love this and I wish more games had meaningful story moments like this.

Gameplay has been so much improved from it's release that it doesn't even resemble it's original build. Everything is just so much more fun and streamlined (for the better) now in the latest updates that I feel like different builds and playstyles really stand out. 

I highly recommend it to everyone, except I strongly suggest you have a decent computer to run this. This game is playable on older hardware but you're doing yourself a disservice by not being able to use Ray Tracing and some newer gen tech (like Frame Generation) to take advantage of how great this game can look and play. I upgraded in the middle of my third playthrough and was blown away at what I was missing out on.

Don't be a gonk, play Cyberpunk.

Antes de jogar o jogo, eu estava esperando que ele fosse como um GTA, porém num universo Cyberpunk. Eu não sabia oque me esperava depois de joga esse jogo e eu posso falar com confiança, esse é um dos MELHORES JOGOS QUE JÁ JOGUEI NA MINHA VIDA.

Os personagens importantes da história não só existem e estão lá pra quando você precisar falar com eles, você interage com e fala, eles te mandam mensagens, reagem as coisas que você faz no seu tempo livre, eles vivem uma vida, teve momentos durante minha gameplay que eu senti que estava traindo minha namorada nas missões que você se aproxima de um dos parceiros românticos do game de tão imersivo que é(sim, era a Panam). A dublagem só faz esse aspecto ficar mais claro, jogar o jogo dublado é essencial para se sentir dentro da história.

Gameplay é fluída, divertida, mecânicas são diferentes, cada build que você faz é uma experiência diferente, eu no inicio achava que era pra buildar um atributo pra usar um tipo de arma e outro pra outra, mas jogando melhor o jogo percebi que independente da arma ou estilo de jogo que você tiver, você vai se divertir com as mecânicas. Minha nota final é 5/5, com as optimações e atualizações de conteúdo o game ficou perfeito, caso tenha comprado durante a época de lançamento e se arrependeu, eu recomendo fortemente dar uma chance para Cyberpunk 2077.

I preordered this game in 2018, I played 2 hours on release day, then stopped until 2025 to play and finish it. I learned two lessons from that, never preorder any game again, it is worthless, and the second lesson is to wait and give the devs time to fix the mess they created.

The game still looks good after 5 years, I barely had any bugs and nothing mission breaking. This is a good testament to the devs not stopping until they turned it into the vision they had in mind.

Idea wise, it borrows a lot from Deus Ex but makes it more action oriented and open world. You can use several playstyles, from sneaking to going mental and killing everything that moves using all kinds of firearms or melee weapons. While the game is not groundbreaking, the gameplay is fun, especially if you try to approach each encounter differently.

Some side missions are better than the main missions, even funnier, there is a lot to explore but the city, while looking good, is not very distinctive between the different regions, it mostly feels the same. Missions are very straightforward and the map, while you can filter it, has too many things going on. I am not sure we needed all those repetitive activities. They are also very easy to follow, which kills actual exploration, all you have to do is go from point A to point B.

Some characters are awesome and Panam tops this list easily, Johnny is also great, Male V not so much, but overall the characters, voice acting, and soundtrack are very good, and the graphics are still looking great even 5 years after release.

I was very happy playing this game, I just wish it was this good on release day, and I also expected more innovation and exploration. It is a good game, but it feels closer to a popcorn movie than to a masterpiece.

Recommended for people who love open world action games, this game is fun.
