I’ve been watching Cyberpunk 2077 from a distance for nearly five years, following its patches and improvements without playing it. In 2025, I’m finally jumping in so this review reflects the game as it exists today, not the problems at launch.

At its best, Cyberpunk 2077 shines in its hand-crafted spaces and curated missions. Clubs, bars, and districts like Japantown or Corpo Plaza feel dense, intentional, and visually exceptional. When the game narrows its focus to authored content, it works extremely well.

Where it still struggles is the open world. Traversal is slow and unrewarding, vehicle handling is painful, and the game compensates by flooding the map with fast-travel points which is a clear admission that moving through Night City isn’t very fun. The streets between major locations often feel like filler rather than meaningful gameplay space.

Random encounters like NCPD alerts, cyberpsycho sightings, and gang activity all lack depth and consequence. Over time, they blur together, encouraging a blunt “kill-on-sight” playstyle rather than supporting role-playing. 

That said, the game is absolutely still worth playing and buying. I’ve been borderline obsessed with it for the last two weeks, which hasn’t happened to me with a game in a long time. The cyberpunk aesthetic, lore, and curiosity about Night City carried me deep into the experience. The game also works surprisingly well as a “turn your brain off and go loud” RPG. I’ve been playing my character like a full cyberpsycho no stealth, killing everyone on sight and it feels oddly aligned with how the game is designed.

I can easily see myself replaying it later with a stealth-focused build to explore a different side of the systems. Even with its flaws, Cyberpunk 2077 in 2025 is a compelling, addictive game especially if the world and genre already speak to you.

2. Открытый мир.
Большой открытый мир - это то, что я люблю в играх. Здесь мир ощущается живым: в нём постоянно что-то происходит, множество локаций, переулков, подвалов и т. д.

3. Персонажи.
Тут много харизматичных и интересных персонажей. Я бы сказал настоящих личностей. Их истории очень увлекательны, выстраивать с ними отношения тоже интересно (не только любовные). В общем и целом, следить за их жизнью "занятие увлекательное".

Что мне не понравилось:

1. Игровой мир.
Несмотря на то, что в достоинствах я указал открытый мир как сильную сторону игры, его наполненность вызывает вопросы. Начиная от глупейших мобов и полицейских, заканчивая постоянно одними и теми же диалогами у NPC, которые не меняются от слова совсем. Причём одни и те же диалоги между NPC можно встретить в разных частях карты.

2. Обилие игрового контента.
Я человек простой - тратить на игры сотни часов желания не имею. В данной игре очень много разного контента, и его нужно изучать: как прокачивать персонажа, что дают те или иные модули / способности / импланты (а их очень много).
Много мусора в виде различных предметов. Непонятно, насколько нужен тебе тот или иной предмет. Я просто копил почти всё, в итоге ловил перевес, складировал это в тайник и к концу игры оказалось, что 90% этого просто мусор)))

Это я молчу в целом про вселенную киберпанка. Её историю и развитие мне пришлось изучать через ютуб. А читать миллион записок с вырванным из контекста содержанием у меня не было ни времени, ни желания.

3. Отсутствие катсцен.
Тут скажу коротко - в игре мало динамичных и красивых катсцен. Очень мало. По сравнению с Ведьмаком их тут кот наплакал.

4. Скудность оружия, неочевидный крафт предметов, слабая механика взаимодействия с автомобилями.
Объединяю всё это в один пункт. До сих пор не очень понимаю, в чём смысл крафта собственного оружия. Почему такой малый его выбор? Рукопашная боёвка - это вообще нечто кривое. Управление автомобилями слишком аркадное, с упором на заносы. То есть разработчики решили не заморачиваться и сделали просто слишком резкое управление вместо адекватного.

Вывод:

Первое своё прохождение я начал за корпората, а закончил кочевником Альдекальдо.
Я не знаю, как так вышло… Никогда не симпатизировал этим бомжам, а в итоге с ними и уехал в закат. Стрём.

Вероятно, буду проходить и на другие концовки. Игру рекомендую как минимум на одно прохождение. Всё-таки это один из шедевров игровой индустрии.

# 赛博朋克2077：用三年打磨，铸就赛博朋克标杆之作
从首发争议到如今Steam“压倒性好评”，《赛博朋克2077》用持续不断的更新与打磨，完成了一场教科书级别的逆袭，成为无可替代的赛博朋克题材天花板。它不仅构建了一个沉浸感拉满的未来都市，更在叙事、玩法与美学上实现了三重突破，让每个踏入夜之城的玩家都能找到属于自己的雇佣兵传奇。

## 沉浸式夜之城：细节拉满的赛博乌托邦
夜之城绝对是游戏最亮眼的核心，50平方千米的开放世界里藏满惊喜。七大区域风格迥异，从沃森区的霓虹小巷到恶土的荒凉戈壁，每座建筑都独一无二，低空飞行的浮空车、闪烁的全息广告与街头改造人的义体纹路交织，构成了极具冲击力的赛博美学。

这里的细节足以让玩家沉浸其中：扫描模式下能读取每个NPC的背景故事，随机触发的街头冲突、帮派火拼让城市充满活力，2.0版本新增的地铁系统更让通勤变成一场风景漫游。中文配音全程在线，街头的嘈杂人声、电子乐与环境音完美融合，走在街头仿佛真的置身2077年的未来都市。

## 深度叙事与角色：有血有肉的赛博羁绊
CDPR的叙事功力在本作中展现得淋漓尽致。主角V为追寻永生植入体卷入阴谋，与银手强尼的灵魂碰撞贯穿始终，每一次对话选择都影响着剧情走向与最终结局。主线剧情紧凑有力，杰克的牺牲、与帕南的游牧冒险、朱迪的“脑舞”抗争等桥段情感饱满，支线任务更是惊喜不断，每个角色都有自己的故事与挣扎，让人共情不已。

游戏的多结局设计堪称点睛之笔，不同选择导向的结局或释然、或伤感、或悲壮，搭配全语音台词与电影化过场，带来堪比科幻大片的沉浸体验。这种“你的选择定义故事”的设定，让每个玩家的夜之城之旅都独一无二。

## 革新玩法：自由定制的战斗盛宴
2.0版本的更新让游戏玩法脱胎换骨。重制的技能树更加聚焦，五大属性搭配猎头、黑客、忍者等五大技能，支持玩家打造专属战斗风格——无论是用螳螂刀近战收割的“快刀流”，还是远程黑入敌人系统的“黑客流”，或是驾驶载具激战的“车战流”，都能获得极致爽感。

义体系统更是充满创意，从手掌的智能武器瞄准到身体的二次跳跃，从狂暴技能到闪电鞭，十几种义体自由组合，让角色成长充满可能性。车辆战斗的加入让街头追逐更具张力，可远程黑入敌方车辆、触发挂载武器，高速激战中尽显赛博魅力。此外，街头声望系统、不朽武器升级、塔罗牌收集等玩法，进一步丰富了游戏内容，让探索充满乐趣。

## 持续进化：诚意满满的开发者态度
最让人动容的是CDPR的坚持与诚意。从首发的优化问题到如今的稳定流畅，历经1.5、2.0版本更新与DLC《往日之影》的补充，游戏不仅修复了大量BUG，更全方位革新了战斗、技能、AI等核心系统。《往日之影》销量超500万份，TGA最佳持续运营游戏奖的荣誉，正是对这份诚意的最好认可。

如今的《赛博朋克2077》早已不是当年的“半成品”，它用三年时间证明了优秀作品的潜力——无论是赛博朋克题材爱好者、开放世界探索者，还是RPG玩法发烧友，都能在夜之城中找到属于自己的乐趣。

Completing Cyberpunk was a powerful experience. I want to share my thoughts while the emotions are still fresh.
First of all, Night City is not just a set; it’s a living organism. And the characters make it live. Jackie Wells has become a real bro for me. His attachment to his mother and sincere love for Misty make his image human and worldly. His vitality, ambition and sincerity caught on without trying to appear as someone else. His loss is felt acutely, not just the death of a loyal friend, but the loss of a sense of security. The city suddenly becomes empty when the only person who believed in you without any hidden motives disappears.

Special thanks to the developers for Judy. Stunningly written character with a solid character, behind whose external harshness hides an aching soul. Her strong independence and anarchist spirit combine with an inability to cope with emotional problems and a tendency towards self-destruction. Despair, sabotage and emotional problems seem very real, not just a perfect option of romance, which makes her journey more impressive. Great empathy caused the similarity of this character with me, forcing to self-reflection. Not just an admiration for the character, but a chance to better understand yourself. It serves as a kind of mirror reflecting my inner conflicts, fears and desires. It shows that you can be both strong and vulnerable, idealistic and realistic, that you can fight injustice while seeking inner peace. Her story is a reminder that even in the darkest world you can find light and hope, and it’s normal to open, even if it’s scary.

The ending of Arasaka is remembered for a long time, dark and psychologically difficult. In exchange for the promise of life you give up your freedom and dignity. In this ending you understand that for Arasaka you are not a hero or even an ally, but a valuable asset or just a lab rat. Friends from a past life either distance themselves, or look at you with pity.
The space station scene where V endlessly solving the Rubik’s Cube is a brilliant way to convey mental decay. You repeat it again and again, but it does not bring satisfaction. It is a symbol that the V's mind is damaged, and Arasaka simply calibrates the remnants of your personality. When V in rage or despair disassembles the cube and finds a red devil inside, this is the moment of truth. It’s the realization that there is nothing human inside you anymore, only corporate code. You survived, but the price of this life was so high that life itself lost its meaning.

One of the drawbacks for me is the lack of a canonical end. I appreciate when there is a clear conclusion in the narrative, where everything is wrapped up and understood. Not when you have the option to select a favorable outcome for yourself. It's preferable to have one clear conclusion. Even if it leads to disappointment.

“首发灾难”“Bug 不断”“半成品”这些标签，曾让我几度对《赛博朋克2077》望而却步。

但如今，在经历了所有结局、达成全成就，并完成了大部分支线之后，我可以很明确地说：如果你愿意真正沉入夜之城，这款游戏值得一试。

其实，达成全成就已经是几个月前的事了。之所以现在才写下这段评论，是因为几个月过去后，我依然忘不掉它带给我的那种独特体验。

如果要用两个词概括《赛博朋克2077》的主题，我会选择“自我”与“抗争”。V 原本只是夜之城中一个微不足道的人，却因为 Relic 芯片，被迫卷入一场关于生命、意识与身份的挣扎。这个故事真正打动我的地方，并不只是“如何活下去”，而是在一切都逐渐失控时，V 仍然要回答一个问题：我到底是谁？我又该以怎样的方式走到最后？

比起战斗带来的爽快感，我更忘不掉的是 CDPR 对人物的塑造。不只是主线角色，许多支线人物也有自己的立场、执念、软弱和选择。竹村偶尔流露出的幽默，瑞弗身上的正直，帕南的冲动与真诚，朱迪的敏感与坚持，都让我觉得他们不是单纯的任务 NPC，而是真正在夜之城中生活、受伤、挣扎过的人。也正因为如此，和他们相处时，我常常会被带入他们的情绪之中。

《赛博朋克2077》的几个结局也各有震撼之处。它们并没有简单地告诉玩家什么是“最好的选择”，而是让每一条路都带着代价、遗憾和余味。不同结局中的 V，像是在用不同方式回应同一个问题：在这座吞噬一切的城市里，人究竟能不能为自己争取到一点真正属于自己的东西？

最后不得不提的是音乐。直到现在，我依然会听《I Really Want to Stay at Your House》《Afterlife》等原声。经历完整个夜之城的故事后，这些旋律不再只是好听的配乐，而像是某种记忆开关。每次响起时，我都会想起那些街道、霓虹、选择、告别，以及 V 一路走到最后的身影。

对我来说，《赛博朋克2077》早已值回票价。几个月过去后，我记住的不是某一场枪战或某一次升级，而是这座城市留下的情绪、人物和余味。这也正是它最打动我的地方。

Why It’s Actually Incredible Now:

Builds matter. Random perks = sad V. Plan ahead.
Driving is better than launch but still… let’s say “stylish chaos.”
Bugs are mostly gone, but Night City still believes in character.

Pro Tips for New Runners:
Don’t rush the main story. Side quests are where the soul lives.
Read shards and messages — the worldbuilding is hidden everywhere.
Invest in cyberware early. Flesh is temporary, chrome is forever.

Emotional damage is unavoidable. Save often.

Final Verdict:
Cyberpunk 2077 went from cautionary tale to redemption arc done right. It’s immersive, stylish, emotional, and genuinely memorable. Not perfect — but bold, ambitious, and finally delivering on its promise.

You won’t just beat this game.
You’ll remember it.

星星结局就是和帕南打上荒坂，最后穿过边境离开夜之城，太阳结局和节制结局可以通过罗格，隐藏的结局，和帕南结局解锁，把身体留给强尼就是节制结局，印象最深的就是去v的墓地道别，熟悉的neverfadeaway响起，最后说出“我不会忘，我什么都不会忘”坐上大巴离开，太阳结局选择把身体留给自己，成为来生传奇，隐藏结局是要和强尼好感度达到一定程度，选对对话并且在终章沉默五分钟，就会解锁以残躯化烈火，单枪匹马冲上荒坂塔，最后选择太阳或者节制，这几个结局都相对来说比较好，算是好结局，至少是站着活下来了

总结，好游戏，剧情玩法无可挑剔，每个任务设计都很有新意，史低打折放心入，没有首发一堆bug，还有很多攻略参考，可以说是入手最佳时机了

I played this in 2024, 4 years after release, and only remember a bug in the prologue where npcs were stuck t-posing in a cutscene montage. Hopefully this game served as a lesson to CDPR. Surely they made serious internal changes to their marketing team because what it is now is a great game in its own right, thanks to the developers who had to clean up their mess (also shoutout to Mike Pondsmith).

The combat is the most fun I've had in a long time. Enemy camps offer versatility (long sightlines for sniping, hacking opportunities, secret stealth routes) and I often changed combat methods during fights. The grind for clearing out locations did not feel tedious at all. The rpg elements include character creation and combat playstyle. The only choices you make are how you want to deal side quests and the ending for the main story. Another thing is, the game has an awkward rhythm since the prologue is lengthy and the main questline is very short comparatively.

I'm not always invested in videogame plots, but V's story ended up working for me emotionally. There are also a handful of memorable side quests where the stories fit perfectly in the bleak cyberpunk setting, my favorite being Sinnerman. The DLC doubles down and gives an even more bitter story with Songbird and Reed.

As for negatives, I would've liked having some more compelling side characters (Misty and Panem were all I cared about in the main game). Keanu's voice acting was ok, Grimes should not have been allowed to voice anything. There are a bunch of megacorps established the Cyberpunk 2077 universe but this game mainly features only one, Arasaka. There was a side quest that seemed like it was starting a plotline dealing with another megacorp called Militech but it went nowhere, which was disappointing.

 If they had advertised this as the mostly-linear immersive action adventure game it is, Cyberpunk 2077's memory would have been far better than what it is currently known for.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a neon-soaked, morally ambiguous playground where you can customize your implants, drive ridiculously fast cars, and somehow survive a city that seems determined to kill you in at least three creative ways per minute.

If you enjoy open-world RPGs, absurd cybernetic enhancements, and a city that refuses to play nice, Cyberpunk 2077 delivers a wild, unforgettable experience.

Highly recommended. Upgrade everything, survive the chaos, and maybe don’t anger the mechs.

这是我玩过最爽的开放世界3A游戏，没有之一。整个游戏的画风很有未来科技感且和现实生活的城市没有太大的割裂感，给人的感觉就像是2077年的美国某个洲真的就是这样的。
夜之城的构建真的很不错，整个城市就像是活的一样。要说有什么不完美的地方，只能说城市还是不够大！还是不够大！还是不够大！真的就是没玩爽。
游戏里的各大派系都很有特点，主线剧情里面都会接触到，当然都会被V震天做掉几个。主线剧情的丰富程度还是很不错的，游戏里面有很多的文件会补充，2077的世界观非常的精彩，全流程下来我感觉波兰蠢驴还是阉割了很多剧情，而且我认为这些最终没呈现出来的剧情也是相当精彩，比如公司战争，军用科技的那一部分剧情。
我是女V开局，我认为这个游戏的中配真的太神了，非常有灵性，非常大胆，这才是优秀的配音，伟大的配音，给每一位角色包括npc都注入了独一无二的灵魂。一百多个小时结束，真的意难平，没有完美的结局，每个结局都让我心里不好受，总感觉缺些什么，主角V真的算得上是传奇中的传奇，我有太多的话想分享了，无法通过冰冷的键盘说清楚我内心的感受。
传奇主角V的故事我认为基本上是完结了，V小姐/V先生短暂而传奇的一生已经深深刻进了夜之城的故事里，这座城市会永远记得V。强尼银手的存在让全流程的剧情锦上添花，因为各种各样的巧合，V和强尼也算是互相拯救，V弥补了强尼当年的种种遗憾，给了强尼第二次生命；强尼给V诉说着50年前的传奇故事，关键的relic芯片给V带来了各种痛苦同时也挡下了致命的一枪，给了V第二次生命。
往日之影dlc的剧情更是神中神中神，把这个游戏拉到了传奇3A的高度，我三次游玩都选择帮助宋昭美上月球，因为某种程度上，小宋和V一样，为了活下去没得选择，这也是无论她骗我多少次我都会选择把她送上月球。向往自由的鸟儿值得广阔无垠的天空，V没得选，宋也没得选，既然只能二活一，我选择帮人帮到底。虽然我知道就算宋昭美上了月球也会有其他的麻烦，但是我更不希望她落到新美国，落到迈尔斯手里。李德其实也算是好人，但是对新美国的愚忠让我不得不在送鸟上月球的路上也送他一程，李德的死我觉得也算是让他解脱了，很多时候大家都身不由己，都没得选。
心中还有千言万语无法诉说，只能说非常非常期待续作的到来，希望cdpr续作能好好打磨，我愿意等到2030年！

"Night City always wins"

That's what I was told before starting this game for the first time. I didn't think much of it but after advancing through the main story I began to understand what this actually means. Sure you can be the main character, a legend of the Afterlife, Corpo scum or just a regular guy trying to stay alive but no matter what you do, this city will put you to your knees in the end. 

Cyberpunk 2077 is much more than just a game, it is something that you can be part of. You can be stranded in the middle of the badlands with no human in sight but then you spot a car off the road and decide to look what has happened, upon arrival you see a NCPD officer covering up his tracks after killing someone they weren't meant to off. Upon getting too close you get shot and have to make a decision. It's you or them! After helping yourself with staying alive you can uncover the whole situation. The officer just wanted to feed her family and the payout for the gig was too good to pass on. You look down on the ground, her lifeless body right infront of you and you start to realize that this city doesn't need you. It breathes and goes on no matter if you're there or not.

I just can't help myself getting immersed in these kind of situations. Daily biz that shows you the dreadful reality of your life in this city. Barganing with someone you are meant to flatline just for them to tell you that they were screwed over by some corpos and it's not their fault, really let's you think about what you're doing.
In other games i just get the quest, fulfill the requests, maybe listen to the dialouge as to why this was sooo important to the quest giver and then move on.
In Cyberpunk 2077 I indulge in the jobs and gigs given to me. Letting a fixer only have a few gigs available and unlocking more once you earned their trust and proven your worth really lets you feel like you have a connection to the other characters, They aren't just NPCs, they are your Employer, your fellow merc and sometimes your choom.

Never have I ever felt so much about an NPC dying as I did in this game. It felt real in a way. You learned so much about them over the course of the story that it really hits you when they are suddenly gone and you can see the pain in their buddies faces. The first time I finished an ending and the credits rolled I just sat there and thought about everything that had just happened. For the first time in a game I intentionally let the credits finish rolling and didn't even try to skip them. The calls of all your chooms and fixers, after you completed the main quest hit right where they need to and I started to really feel sorry for all of them. Because no matter what fun you had with them, no matter how close your were and how deeply you cared about them, in the end "Night City always wins"

This is not supposed to be a review, it is a love letter to the creators and the characters in the story they created. With almost 300 hours on a single save i have yet to experience everything this game has to offer and i'm looking forward to the sudden thought of wanting to indulge in this world again.

It was a preem experience and no matter what Night city throws at you, I always strive to be a Legend again!

Ich habe nun etwa 320 Stunden in diesem Game, spiele es seit knapp drei Monaten und um ehrlich zu sein, zocke ich zur Zeit fast gar nichts anderes mehr. Rückblickend kann man wohl sagen, dass es gut war, so lange zu warten, bis Cyberpunk 2077 alle Updates rausgebracht hat, denn weiß ich nicht, ob ich beim Launch so viel Geduld gehabt hätte – soll ja richtig schlimm gewesen sein. 
Wo fange ich am Besten bei diesen Review an? Vielleicht mit dem, was mich von Beginn an in das Game gesogen hat: die Spielwelt. Night City ist mehr als nur eine Stadt, die als Hintergrund für die Handlung dient, sondern eine eigene kleine Welt, in der sich verschiedene Stories abspielen. Sie sieht mit ihren Neonlichtern, den hohen Gebäuden und den verschiedenen Stadtteilen nicht nur großartig aus, sondern durch die zahlreichen NPC's, die durch die Straßen gehen, laufen und fahren extrem lebendig wirkt. An jeder Ecke passiert etwas, man erlebt brutale Drive-by's oder wird sogar selbst Ziel von einem. Zeitweise bin ich einfach nur durch die Gegend gelaufen oder gefahren und habe die Welt auf mich wirken lassen. 
Doch wir haben nicht nur das beeindruckende Stadtbild, sondern auch das umliegende Gebiet, welches zwar nicht mehr ganz so belebt ist wie die Stadt, aber mit der Wüste und den Bergen am Horizont einen Kontrast zu dieser darstellt. Wie in der Stadt ist das Leben auch hier für die Bewohner hart, aber auf eine ganz andere Weise und für nicht Wenige auch wesentlich freier. Auch im Umland zu Night City gibt es eine Menge zu entdecken.

Kommen wir zu Story. Der Einstieg mit den verschiedenen Backgrounds zeigt uns schon einmal die verschiedenen Lebenswege, die man in der Welt von Cyberpunk einschlagen kann. Da haben wir das Straßenkind, dass zwischen den Megagebäuden der Stadt aufgewachsen ist und früh lernen musste, dass man entweder als Legende unsterblich wirst, oder einer von vielen lebt, an den sich nach ihrem Tod niemand mehr erinnern wird.
Der Konzerner zeigt uns das genau Gegenteil des Straßenkindes, denn aufgewachsen mit den Annehmlichkeiten, die das Leben in dieser Zeit zu bieten hat, mussten sich die meisten Konzerner nie Gedanken machen, wie sie an ihre nächste Mahlzeit kommen. Das bedeutet jedoch keinesfalls, dass es leichter für diese Menschen war, denn in der Welt der Konzerne geht es ähnlich erbarmungslos zu, wie auf den Straßen der Stadt. Jeder um Dich herum könnte Dir jederzeit in den Rücken fallen, um sich auf der Karriereleiter nach oben zu bringen.
Die Nomaden, die in den Badlands um Night City leben, versuchen sich von den Zwängen der Zivilisation zu befreien und leben ihren Begriff von Freiheit. Nomaden lassen sich von niemandem außerhalb ihres Clans etwas sagen, gehen ihren eigenen Weg und halten sich normalerweise aus den Belangen der Städter heraus. Natürlich haben aber auch sie mit für sie alltäglichen Problemen zu kämpfen, da sie zum Beispiel nicht lange an einem Ort bleiben können, da es früher oder später zu Problemen führt. Entweder durch rivalisierende Clans, Badland-Bewohnern, die keine Nomaden in ihrer Nähe haben wollen, oder durch Konzerntruppen, weil wieder einmal ein Militärkonvoi überfallen wurde. Schnell merkt man, dass die vermeintliche Freiheit auch nur eine Illusion ist, denn auch Nomaden brauchen Geld oder Ressourcen um zu überleben.

Wie beim ersten Dragon Age hat jeder Background eine eigene Einführung in das Spiel, doch im weiteren Verlauf ändert der Lebensweg nur einige Dialog-Optionen, oder wie die Menschen in Deiner Umgebung auf Dich reagieren. Trotzdem hat es hier oder da auch Vorteile und kann Dir aus gewissen Situation helfen. Die Hauptstory, zu der nun auch Phantom Liberty gehört, ist alleine wegen dem Setting relativ unverbraucht und hat mich relativ schnell in ihren Bann gezogen, was zum einen an den teilweise tollen Charakteren lag, aber auch an der Präsentation. Phantom Liberty zum Beispiel ist ein Agenten-Thriller, der viel aus bekannten Agenten-Filmen übernimmt, inklusive Besuch in einem Casino und ist fantastisch erzählt. Aber auch der Rest der Geschichte nimmt einen mit auf eine emotionale Reise und bringt euch mit einem Sidekick zusammen, bei dem man nicht weiß, ob man ihn hassen oder lieben soll. Keanu Reeves aka Johnny Silverhand ist einfach mega stark und interessant. Aber auch Judy, Vik, Jackie, Rogue und Co sind liebevoll ausgearbeitete Charaktere, von denen einige wie Judy, Panam und River ihre eigene Storyline mitbringen.
Aber auch die Nebenmissionen und Aufträge sind teilweise sehr gut ausgearbeitet, sind oft direkt oder indirekt mit anderen Stories verbunden, so dass man sich tatsächlich in einer zusammenhängenden Welt befindet. Mehr möchte ich nicht auf die Story eingehen, da man sie selber erleben sollte. Vor allem da es auch mehrere Enden gibt.

Was gibt’s noch zu sagen? Technik, Grafik, Gameplay sind auf einem guten bis sehr guten Niveau, das Cyberware-System ist richtig nice und joa, auch hier gibt es nichts zu meckern. Ach ja: Sound und Musik ist richtig stark, mit ein paar richtig guten Songs wie Delicate Weapon, Night City, I really want to stay at your house, Circus Minimus, uvm.

Abschließend bleibt mir nur zu sagen, dass Cyberpunk 2077 ohne Frage eines der besten Games ist, dass ich jemals spielen durfte und ich hoffe sehr, dass wir bald eine Fortsetzung erleben dürfen.

I feel it has to be said - the game ‘Cyberpunk 2077’ is this era’s very own ‘The Wire’.
I realise this may seem a strange thing to say at first, as ‘The Wire’ was a different medium, a television series, set in the real world, at the same approximate dates as it was made, while Cyberpunk 2077 is a CRPG set, not only in a sci-fi future, but an actual parallel timeline to our own.  But this is where the big, important differences stop.
When the HBO television series ‘The Wire’ came out, it blew audiences away with the depth, scope, breadth, and sheer profoundness, in storytelling, quality of acting, use of the tools of the medium, and, if that wasn’t enough, people’s very perceptions of what the limits of the medium used to tell the story were.  The rules of how deep a story could go, how big it could be, how relevant and important to our time and society something made within such a medium could get.
So, when I compare it to Cyberpunk 2077 on those criteria, I cannot find two examples closer.  This game took the very concept of a story told via computerised gameplay, and utterly revolutionised how deep, important, and relevant to our current social issues that story could be.  It blew players, including myself away, as we found ourselves submerged in a world so utterly real and compelling, with such complex characters, deep, rabbithole subplots, perfect voice acting, and mind-blowing atmosphere, that there was no way of leaving that place the same as when we went in.  And it did so with the kind of brilliant, intelligent, and engaging gameplay that perfectly completes anything achieved in this medium.
If you haven’t tried this game, whether you’re interested in the medium as a whole or not, you should play this game.  It is too important to miss.
Tell your friends, tell your neighbours, tell your family, tell your Gran, who constantly complains about ‘young people’ and ‘violent video games’ and ‘millenials being a problem’ for whatever reason.  Whoever misses this game is missing the most profound commentary on our society out there.

A Grand Theft Auto, Blade Runner, DeusEx, The Matrix, Ghost in the Shell, Shadow Warrior, mashup; that's the feeling I have while playing Cyberpunk.  It's futuristic nature and grand scale add to the allure.  With all the shiny glitz and pomp the story and music really drive the addiction for me.  The arc, takes you where you've never been, introduces you to people who become as close to family as you can have in a game, and all that, pulls you in and won't let go.  

The skill tree is unique.  It's the way in the game to build your character meaningfully and level up.  The interesting aspect of it is, you can't balance across all skills, you have to focus on specifics.  That makes all the difference.  Handguns in this game are wild, but paired with your own cyber implants, it goes wild.  Smart weapons are fun, hacking them is funner!  

Night City is vast.  It's fun to explore.  While exploring, the radio creates an ambiance that's almost soothing.  I rarely find myself fast traveling anywhere as a result.

This game has been reviewed many many times, so it's impossible to add anything unique here.  I will say however, whether this game intentionally did this or not, it instills a sense of loneliness.  Everywhere you go in the game, you're surrounded by people but usually alone.  When you connect with another in the story-line, they always leave or die.  Again, I don't know if this was intentional, but it's a feeling that follows you everywhere in the game, and it adds weight to everything you do, every decision you make, and every happy, or otherwise, event.

This game still has bugs, and they are often noticeable, but for all it's flaws, after having played for some time, I personally feel as though this has created an entirely new genre of game-play that will be mimicked for many years to come.

А потом магия ломается. Ты вдруг понимаешь, что город — это просто красивая картонка. Зайди за угол от сюжетного квеста — и всё, пустота, мертвые болванчики ходят туда-сюда чисто для массовки.

Сюжет и Джонни Сильверхенд тащат на себе вообще всё, тут без вопросов. Диалоги крутые, личные квесты персов сделаны с душой. Но основная ветка... почему она такая короткая и рваная? Тебе всю дорогу орут "Ви, ты умираешь, счет на дни!", а игра тут же вываливает тонну заказов в духе "съезди убей бандитов". Темп истории ломается напрочь.

Геймплей — ну, обычный шутер. РПГ-элементы прикрутили чисто чтоб было. Про физику машин даже говорить не хочется — на байках еще куда ни шло, но авто ездят как утюги на льду.

В общем, сейчас игра работает нормально, багов стало меньше, но осадочек никуда не делся. Это хорошая история с крутыми персонажами в потрясающих декорациях. Но как полноценная RPG в живом мегаполисе — увы, недотянули

Night City doesn’t welcome you.
It tolerates you — briefly.

You arrive as V, thinking you’ll make it big.
Money, chrome, reputation.
Night City hears that and immediately schedules your emotional collapse.

Every street is neon, every alley is danger, and every NPC looks like they know something you don’t.
The city breathes, glitches, lies, and somehow still feels alive enough to judge you.

Then there’s Judy.
Quiet, emotional, and carrying more unresolved feelings than the entire city combined.
Her story isn’t loud — it just sits with you, heavy, reminding you that Night City doesn’t just break bodies, it breaks hearts too.

Combat is chaos with style.
Guns blazing, hacks flying, mantis blades out — all while your minimap politely suggests routes you will absolutely ignore.
When things go wrong, they go wrong fast… and usually in slow motion.

And of course, Johnny Silverhand.
A walking midlife crisis with a guitar and too many opinions.
He lives in your head, insults your choices, and somehow becomes the most honest voice in the room.

The story isn’t about saving the world.
It’s about surviving it — long enough to decide who you actually are in a city that wants you replaceable.

• Installed chrome → Lost a piece of myself.
• Trusted Night City → Night City laughed.
• Still chasing legends → Because quitting isn’t an option here.

Cyberpunk 2077 is style + identity + emotional damage.
If you love this game… congratulations, Night City already owns a part of you.

It’s the end of 2025. Most of my friends played this game by this point, and all of them sung serenades for it. “The DLC just made this game goated.” And so, I thought it’s finally time for me to give it a try. Here are my thoughts…

The game is beautiful. The city is finally living and breathing, and works mostly like clockwork. By the point I got to the DLC though, I started experiencing some major stuttering when many NPCs were present on screen, but I’m happy to write this off as suboptimal hardware. Interestingly, the stutters continued even outside of the DLC area, where they previously didn’t occur — not sure why this is. Otherwise, I had just 2–3 crashes over the playthrough. Considering how disastrous the technical state was at launch — a massive improvement. Other impressive things include: the ambience, atmosphere, sound design, environment, and everything else having to do with the world. Outstanding.

Story — wouldn’t call it amazing 10/10 content, but it’s solid enough. What’s noteworthy is that the overarching narrative didn’t stand out nearly as much as some little moments and details, either in main or side missions. These really shined through (e.g. Kerry’s reaction to you playing guitar at his house — my God, that was so cool). This is what really helped with immersion and with keeping my interest — even if I didn’t care much about the story at times, I was still curious about certain interactions characters might have with each other.

Speaking of characters — the writing is, again, mostly solid. 
For me there was a caveat — I didn’t really manage to connect with the majority of them. I did say I enjoyed interactions between characters, but I don't mean the characters themselves. That is with exception of Jackie, having started as Corpo, Reed, and, surprisingly, Brendan (what the hell right?). Many of the characters I didn't hate, but that's not a great achievement. Johnny especially — I was mostly annoyed with him at all stages of the game, which sucks, because he’s the foremost character. The legendary Johnny Silverhand, no more than an angsty teenager. Songbird likewise — the game kept telling me I should care for her... but I just failed to. Judy's quest I straight up skipped — the point of her character flew over my head entirely. Think I maybe understand what the writers were going for: it’s supposed to be a city where everyone’s out for themselves, so you aren’t necessarily meant to like most of the people in it. It’s similar to the show Euphoria in this sense (although on a lesser scale), and there, this point is also by design. If so, I can live with this, even if it's not my cup of tea.

Keep in mind — THIS (all the above) is what you are going to be playing the game for. It’s not GTA, it’s not Skyrim/Fallout, or any of the other AAA RPGs. More notes on why I found it so — below.

Gameplay — I haven’t played with the “magic” system, which I heard was fun, but still — on normal difficulty you are literally just cruising through everything. I’d suggest playing on harder difficulty, but there isn’t an enemy variety to speak of to justify making them bullet sponges. If you’re satisfied with the combat, then maybe that’s OK; personally, I wasn’t entirely.

Here comes the sad part — I really thought that, as my friends suggested, post-DLC, all or most of the initially promised features/fixes would be added. No. From minor things like wall-running, which still isn’t there, to major stuff like police AI still being dumb as hell, driving sucking ass, plentiful and engaging side content like in Witcher 3 being sadly absent, to name a few. For the latter point here, I mean specifically quests such as the meditating monk (either single mission or very short questlines) — there weren’t many such quests, and most of them were a chore to complete. Gigs I also found less entertaining than contracts in the Witcher. I have to stress that this isn't just me being salty about the broken promises. These genuinely felt like core parts of the game were seriously undercooked, even after 5 years of updates.

All of this breaks immersion significantly, but could be forgiven if gameplay and narrative were in tune. Witcher had the same problem, by the way. However, in Witcher it was borderline negligible; here it’s way worse. The game starts, they say you’re on a timer. Mentally, you want to get the important stuff out of the way and then return to side content. Then the game just ends upon completing the final mission — you need to reload a save afterwards. As such, you need to complete every side objective within the span and context of the main story.

So you’re telling me that I have two weeks left to live, and then I can just wait half a year in my room for certain events to take place, finish the story, and then perish at the exact moment it's convenient for the plot?

I have to say that CDPR makes great games, but this is the greatest sin they commit many times — gameplay and narrative just don’t mesh with each other. This also ties into a previous comment — this isn’t a sandbox RPG into which you could/should sink 1000s of hours, The game ends where it ends. However, many design and marketing choices point to it being such. This created an uncomfortable dissonance in my mind as a player.

TLDR:
Didn’t mean for the review to get this long, but I’ll leave it at this: Cyberpunk has its good moments, and it has its bad moments.

To compare it to a movie again (sadly, that’s the best analogy I can muster for now) — if it was a 2-hour-long one, I’d say, “I’m glad I watched it,” and wouldn’t return to it in the future. Here I can say exactly the same thing… but it was 120 hours long.

It’s good, but I don’t think it’s good enough for what it's trying to be.

玩了六周目《赛博朋克2077》，从最早那个跌跌撞撞的夜之城，再到往日之影完整的故事线，现在闭着眼都能摸清每条暗巷，我发现这游戏最让人着迷的，从来不是打打杀杀或者一身神装。它像你脑子里一个甩不掉的损友，不停地问你：当努力都是白费劲，当谁都不能信，当你自己都不完全是自己——人，到底是个什么东西？

说到努力，刚进夜之城那会儿，我还是个公司狗。我和V想得一样：只要够拼，就能从无名小卒混到名扬天下。接最危险的活儿，装最猛的义体，以为这样就能把命运攥在自己手里。可玩到后来，味道就变了。你爬得越高，越能看清那张早就织好的大网——公司、体制、还有那该死的命运。V折腾到最后，连自己的身体都守不住。这感觉太熟悉了，就像我们拼命加班、内卷，以为这样就能接近“成功”，但那目标像海市蜃楼，你追，它就跑。最讽刺的是，你所有的“变强”，最后可能只是为了在一个注定的悲剧里，多演几分钟。但这种“明知道可能没用，还是不服”的劲儿，恰恰是人最闪光的地方。就像帕南带着族人在恶土上求活，就像朱迪想为死去的人讨个说法——反抗本身，就成了意义。

这时候，脑子里那个声音就响起来了：“妈的，全是狗屁！”没错，强尼·银手。他就像焊在你神经里的一个错误，一个活生生的叛逆符号。最开始你觉得他就是个自私的混蛋，满嘴脏话，只想用你的身体去完成他五十年前没炸完的“事业”。但慢慢地，你发现这个数字幽灵戳破了很多虚伪。他嘲笑V为公司卖命是“打工打到脑浆都成公司的”，他看透了夜之城所有光鲜亮丽背后的腐烂。他本身就是“努力”的反面教材——他当年那么努力地反抗荒坂塔，结果呢？成了芯片里的一段数据，一个被困在别人脑子里的囚徒。可他偏偏又是最不肯认输的那个。他的存在本身就是个质问：如果结局都是完蛋，你是选择跪着适应，还是选择他妈站着，朝着该死的老天比个中指再死？

这就引出了那个最要命的问题：在夜之城，什么才算“人”？胳膊腿能换，眼睛能换，记忆能像超梦一样被编辑。当你脑子里还住进另一个人的灵魂，每天跟你吵架、争抢控制权，“你”到底是谁？我操控的V，做的决定有多少是自己的，又有多少是被强尼那个摇滚混球影响的？玩到朱迪的支线更难受，她深爱的艾芙琳只剩下一堆破碎的数字残影，那还是原来那个人吗？

强尼和V的纠缠，把这个问题推到了极致。你们从互相憎恶、争夺，到后来竟然能坐下喝一杯（哪怕是在意识里），甚至产生某种诡异的理解和……友情。这个过程就像把你的人格撕开又糅合。到最后，选择把身体让给他，还是坚持做自己，已经分不清是高尚还是自私。这为《往日之影》里更棘手的困境，铺好了路。

狗镇那摊子烂事——百灵鸟、李德、迈尔斯总统——直接把“背叛”这个词扔进了高温熔炉，烤得你良心滋滋作响。而经历过强尼洗礼的V，看他们的眼光都不一样了。

百灵鸟骗了你，利用你去月球。她就像个更绝望、更脆弱的“版本”的挣扎者。但你知道她被黑墙外的AI侵蚀，是个非人非鬼的怪物，她的背叛是困兽最后的嘶吼。选择帮她，有点像理解了强尼那种“哪怕毁灭世界也要自由”的疯劲，但代价可能是未知的灾难。

李德呢？这个老特工就像走了另一条路的强尼。强尼选择向外炸毁一切，李德选择留在系统内，相信能从内部改变点什么。结果，他的“忠诚”让他背叛了像女儿一样的百灵鸟，也背叛了自己心里那点柔软。他像个穿着风衣的悲剧，你恨他冷酷，又可怜他被自己的信念折磨。帮他，感觉就像背叛了强尼教给你的那种“绝不妥协”的反叛精神。

迈尔斯总统则是顶层的“背叛艺术家”，她的理由永远是国家利益、更大福祉。牺牲百灵鸟？必要之恶。利用李德？棋子的本分。在她那里，背叛是门冷冰冰的管理学。

夹在中间，你发现每个选择都像在背叛另一些人，甚至背叛一部分的自己。帮百灵鸟，背叛了李德的托付和可能的“大局”；交还百灵鸟，又背叛了对她作为一个“人”（哪怕不完全是了）的承诺。DLC最狠的就是，它让你看透每个人的无奈，然后告诉你：看透了，也没好路走。这种滋味，强尼早就尝过——他背叛了奥特，背叛了当年的队友，他比谁都清楚背叛的灼痛。

玩了这么多个周目，试遍了所有结局，我算是明白了夜之城最真实的规则：这里没有完美答案。成为传奇然后陨落？把身体让给强尼看他替你活？和奥特去数字彼岸？送百灵鸟上天还是让她重回牢笼？每一个结局都伴随着深深的缺憾和失去。强尼银手早就看穿了这一点，所以他用愤怒和破坏来回应这个荒谬的世界。

但恰恰是这种“不完美”，让每一次选择都有了千钧重量。就像强尼，明知是徒劳，五十年前还是要炸荒坂塔；明知会消失，最后还是可能把生的机会留给你。这游戏不是教人变冷漠，它是在逼问你：在一个一切都在崩塌、连自己都可能靠不住的世界里，你还要不要坚持去定义属于自己的“对”与“错”？当努力没有回报，当信任换来背叛，你还要不要当个有温度、会疼痛的“人”，而不是一个只会计算的机器？

夜之城的霓虹照不亮所有的黑暗，但也许，正是这片黑暗里，我们每一次听从内心（哪怕心里吵翻了天）的选择，我们为某个理念、某个人、甚至只为一口不服的气而做的抗争，才是这座腐烂巨塔里，唯一真实的人性微光。它弱，但吹不灭。强尼银手用他愤怒的一生证明了这一点，V用他短暂而绚烂的余生重复了这一点。这大概就是夜之城，在六百个小时之后，留给我的东西——不是通关的成就，而是一面镜子，照见我们自己在现实废墟中的那点固执、那点脆弱，和那点永不熄灭的，关于何为“活着”的追问。

For almost 7 years, I waited for this game. My excitement started from the early trailers, gameplay demos, all the way to the iconic trailer with Keanu Reeves. It launched in 2020 in a terrible performance state, which made me hold off on buying it back then. But I was confident that after waiting nearly 5 more years, with countless fixes, updates, and patches, the Cyberpunk 2077 I had been longing for would finally be playable smooth, without major issues, and with minimal bugs.

We start by choosing our life path: Nomad, Streetkid, or Corpo. Honestly, I was curious about all three, but I preferred Nomad because it felt the most unique to me. Then we head to Night City to become a higher class, more intimidating mercenary. As for the story, I have zero complaints. I loved the flow from beginning to end: plenty of plot twists, jokes, and sharp satire woven throughout. The only disappointment was that the three life paths only differ in the prologue. I had hoped for much deeper differences, something that would encourage multiple playthroughs. Still, I absolutely loved the story that puts you in the shoes of a dying mercenary constantly accompanied by Johnny Silverhand. The missions offer multiple approaches usually stealth or direct combat, like most games. What really stands out (classic CDPR strength) is the dialogue feels like a movie. A single conversation can easily last 30–60 minutes, deepening both the story and the Cyberpunk world itself. The portrayal of massive corporations with overwhelming power is excellent make you really feel like an ordinary citizen who can’t possibly stand up to what the corpos control.

The world itself is absolute cinema. Night City feels incredibly real and beautiful. Every detail is there: huge corporations, restaurants, brothels, bars, gangs, prisons, and countless small touches scattered everywhere. Weather cycles are varied and gorgeous, like morning, afternoon, night, rain, thick Blade Runner style fog everything is rendered stunningly.

Unfortunately, activities are limited to main quests and side quests. The good news is there are tons of side quests, and they’re very varied not just “kill this, kill that.” Some are silly, some are heavy on dialogue and uncovering secrets. The main story missions are delivered brilliantly; everything is told in detail and clearly if you pay attention to the conversations. Dialogue choices feel meaningful (though there aren’t tons of them), and they do affect the story. Skipping side content has consequences, including on the endings. What I missed was small, low stakes activities to slow down the pace things like eating at restaurants or doing silly random stuff. Because everything is tied to quests, the pace stays fast the whole time, which can make you tired more easily.

V’s cyberware, weapons, and skill trees are great. I love how detailed the cyberware system is you can build exactly what you want, and it has a huge impact on both combat and stealth. The skill tree influences gameplay too, though the options for truly changing how you play are somewhat limited. Weapon variety isn’t massive, but the rarity tiers and four main categories give each gun a distinct feel like rifles, SMGs, melee weapons, and ones integrated with your cyberware. Early game combat and stealth felt pretty rough, but once you upgrade, combat becomes extremely satisfying and deadly while still feeling well-balanced against enemies. The only letdown is the stealth takedown animations—they’re bad and there’s basically only one type.

Graphics don’t need much explanation: this is one of the most beautiful games I’ve ever played. The immersive, terrifying future city is depicted gorgeously. From the lavish, neon reflected heart of Night City to districts like Kabuki and Santo Domingo with their own distinct vibes, to the rundown, chaotic outskirts everything is portrayed incredibly well.

Vehicles were awful at launch, driving felt terrible. But once you progress, earn money, and buy proper cars or bikes, driving becomes enjoyable. My only complaint is that navigation would be better with arrows on the road rather than just the minimap it’s hard to drive while constantly glancing up.

Overall, I’m extremely satisfied with Cyberpunk 2077 after waiting 7 years for it. The story, gameplay, world, and atmosphere are all fantastic. I’m glad I waited longer so I could play a mostly fixed version without bugs or major issues, I sank almost 70 hours into it, often playing 4 hours a day and losing track of time. I love all the little details: fast travel via metro, clothing and weapon shops, driving around listening to the radio stations (many songs are original and all of them are great). My only regrets are that the main story feels shorter compared to a heavy narrative game like The Witcher 3, and so much content was clearly cut, things like the nano wire hacking, wall climbing with mantis blades, and many features shown in early demos that never made it to the final game. It really feels like the rushed launch prevented the game from reaching its full potential. Still, I’m not fully satisfied yet. I’m still hungry for more Cyberpunk content, which is why I’m so excited to play the Phantom Liberty DLC.

I’m also currently finishing the prequel anime series, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners.

And I’m already incredibly excited for the sequel, that I hope it brings tons of surprises and all the content they couldn’t include in this one.

I played this game at release for about 10 hours and was really disappointed. I uninstalled and never played it again until now. What I just played ends up somewhere on my top 20 all time! I can't believe how good this game ended up being. 

The main quest is good, That's all a main quest needs to do. it doesn't shit the bed and ruin everything else. The side content blew my mind. I couldn't believe how engaged I was in the writing behind a tiny NCPD scanner quest on occasion; quests that would feel like radiant, automatically-generated content in other (lesser) games. Gigs seemed like mini-quests as well and yet they were really well written and I can't think of a single one right now that I didn't like. 

The real stars of this game are: 1.Night City itself and 2. The characters. Graphics are never a primary focus for me, but in this case, they really bring the world to life. This is definitely the best looking game I've ever played. I never skipped a single ride in the passengers seat because I just wanted to look out the window and take in the city. There are games with an art style that I appreciate more, but I'd have to really think about it to give anything more credit than this. 

I have a lot of problems with the game. They just get overshadowed by the things I loved. First and foremost, the atrocious release can never fully be forgiven. We've all heard all of those arguments. I don't need to rehash them here. But it was messed up. I don't feel cheated all these years later anymore, but imagine if I bought it on the previous gen consoles. Next, I think this game is horrible at teaching you how everything works. I think the dialogue is great except when they are trying to be cool. Johnny's dialogue has a lot of stuff that just feels silly. I'm not talking about writing generally, I'm talking about style and syntax here. There's also conceptual complexity in the stories background that leaves me a little bewildered. I didn't enjoy the combat until I got a decent sandestivan (sp?). I wish I could have forgone netrunning earlier and just player with slow-mo start to finish. I loved the cars but I felt like all that effort was kinda wasted by the end of my time with the game. There was not enough to do with your car collection. The last one might be a bit controversial, I felt like Phantom Liberty was a step down in quality for me. The whole James Bond spy thriller thing was great, breathtaking even at times. But it still felt like a modest downgrade with regard to the universal themes, genre tropes, atmosphere of the base game. 

I finished a near complete playthrough. I got all of the endings, all missions (that I know of), all gigs, almost every NCPD scanner blip etc. and it never got old. I am even now sad to uninstall the game. I'm really going to miss this place and these people. I haven't felt that since Fallout: New Vegas. I'm not exaggerating when I say, I'm 100% confidant that I could start the game over right now and play it to completion and my opinions wouldn't change. I'm 150 hours in (lots of AFK has my playtime way higher but the in-game timer says 160). That's mental. 

I love it! I'll definitely come back in a few years. This is something special folks. It really challenges my capacity to stay mad at CDPR. Hmm...still won't buy their next release when it comes out though. They have to do a bit more penance for me.

История Ви и Джонни Сильверхэнда, по настоящему лучшая сюжетная история что я видел в видеоиграх, даже моя любимая Mafia 1, не так меня тронула как Cyberpunk. 

Вкратце сюжет: Действия происходят в 2077-ом Году. Наёмник Ви в огромном мегаполисе Найт-Сити всегда мечтал стать верхушкой криминального мира. И со своим другом Джеки под предводительством фиксера Декстора Дешона Фиксер - во вселеной Киберпанка человек дающий заказ на выполнение наёмникам, проще говоря наниматель, чаще всего именно крупные фиксеры после выполнения заказа просто пускают пулю в затылок ребятам которых и наняли, просто используют их, а потом бросают их трупы на свалку. Задание заключается в том чтобы выкрасть из отельного номера основателя многомиллиардной корпорации Arasaka секретную разработку некого чипа которую еще нигде не показывали, но стоит она триллионы долларов. На задании конечно-же все идет не так, товарища Ви убивают, а он из безысходности вставляет этот чип в порт в голове, то есть как имплант. Позже фиксер конечно-же застреливает Ви, но он чудом спасается благодаря этому чипу. Ведь на него загружено сознание умершего еще 40 лет назад террориста и легенды Рок-н-Рола, лидера легендарной группы SAMURAI Джонни Сильверхэнда, если вынуть чип после выстрела в голову, Ви тут-же умрет, если не вынуть, сознание чип перезапишет сознание Ви на сознание Джонни в течение 2-ух недель и Ви исчезнет как будто его никогда и не было, а контроль над телом получит Джонни, то есть считай вернется из мертвых в новом теле. Вот тебе и задачка, 2 недели, и всю игру Ви четно пытается найти способ выжить и не потерять при этом контроль над  телом. А Джонни в свою очередь постоянно мешает этому, ведь кто откажется вернуться в реальность спустя 40 лет заключения в цифровой тюрьме на каком-то там чипе? Это буквально искусственно созданное раздвоение личности. 

В игре нет хорошей концовки, самое лучшее что может сделать Ви, это отдать контроль Джонни, ведь так он спасет хоть кого-то, все остальные концовки ведут у неминуемой смерти обоих. Ви обрек себя на медленную смерть, простой жаждой к известности среди обычных преступников.

Cyberpunk 2077 is by and far the greatest action R?PG that I have played, and is one of the best games in this genre on offer.

One of the cardinal sins that RPG's commit is the "statification" of growth. Instead of being give new abilities and ways to interact with the world, you instead receive a +% modifier to damage. While of course modifiers like this are important, RPG's very often fail to meet breakpoints with these stat changes, i.e. "With this sniper crit buff, can I now one shot enemies whereas once I could not, or does this just either a) not do enough to kill an enemy in one shot, or b) increase the damage that I did which was already one-shotting enemies?

Cyberpunk initially launched with this sort of Bethesda-esque "perk points make numbers go up" style of perks, however, with the release of Phantom Liberty, they made one of the most masterful perk systems that exists in video games. Each perk sink first gives stat bonuses, and then at the end gives a new ability. It could be a cool finishing move, the ability to block bullets with a sword, being able to sneak-sprint - all of these make the player feel rewarded with something cool for investing in a tree. What's more, it makes different playthroughs feel very unique, as investing in different trees dramatically affects the way that V is able to defeat enemies and interact with the world. Every RPG that you know would be dramatically improved by adopting the style of character growth that Cyberpunk has made for itself.

The fidelity to the genre and the tabletop game is also phenomenal. The world is gritty, sad, and bleak, but the moments where life is definitively placed in your hands feels like fire - so much inevitability is all around the story, but in spite of that, in extraordinary circumstances, V can take the reins of life and become a legend. 

I cannot recommend this game enough. If you like any aspect of what Cyberpunk is, you'll be better for having played it.

整体游玩下来的体验还算不错，唯一值得吐槽的就是车辆驾驶的手感不太舒服。而且在2025年9月11日的2.31版本更新后，自动驾驶的设定/系统有点鸡肋（个人认为）。问题出现在前往任务点的线路上，但凡遇到需要在狭窄的道路拐弯时，就会撞到建筑物上（或者是出现其他情况，例如遇到大量车辆、人群的时候，又或者是驶过大片的人行道等等），继而停止自动驾驶。这个时候对于想要解放双手（也可以说是懒，想休息一会）的玩家来说：不太友好。

另外，在游玩的过程中，可以看出制作团队在制作游戏到发售的整个过程中，出于各方面的压力，导致曾经想要加入到本体游戏中的各种内容都阉割了，个人感觉比较惋惜。在剧情方面，制作团队推出了DLC《往日之影》来弥补本体游戏的缺陷。而玩法方面，也随着后续的补丁更新，有了一些新的内容以及优化。

Vom Sorgenkind zum immersivsten Erlebnis, das ich je hatte:

Zuerst einmal: Ja, wir wissen alle, wie der Start war. Ich habe lange gebraucht, um zu diesem Spiel zu finden. Aber nachdem ich es vor Patch 2.0 schon gut fand, bin ich nach meinem zweiten Durchgang (jetzt mit Patch 2.x und Phantom Liberty) absolut sprachlos.

Nur eine kleine Warnung vorweg, falls hier minimale Spoiler auftauchen.

[b]Die Welt lebt (und atmet):[/b]
Was mich beim zweiten Durchspielen umgehauen hat, ist die Zeit, die man sich für die Inszenierung nehmen kann. Es sind die kleinen Dinge: Ich stehe im Fahrstuhl und schaue Nachrichten, beobachte Leute bei Unterhaltungen oder höre im Radio, dass irgendwo der Strom ausgefallen ist – und realisiere grinsend: "Ups, das war ja ich." Diese Art von Immersion, dieses "Hereinziehen" in die Welt, habe ich so noch in keinem anderen Spiel erlebt.

[b]Quests mit Herz:[/b]
Natürlich gibt es die typischen 08/15-Aufgaben. Aber dazwischen finden sich Perlen, die so großartig inszeniert sind. Ein Beispiel: Man wird später einfach mal zum Dank zum Essen eingeladen, obwohl die eigentliche Quest längst vorbei ist. Dass Entwickler noch Dinge "drumherum" bauen, nur für das Gefühl, ist heutzutage selten.

[b]Gameplay & Technik:[/b]
Technisch ist das Spiel zwar schon ein paar Jahre alt, fordert den PC aber immer noch ordentlich. Mit hohen Einstellungen und etwas KI-Upscaling sieht es aber schlicht fantastisch aus. Spielerisch klebe ich leider zu sehr an meinem Netrunner-Build (ich liebe den Kram einfach). Das Potenzial des Kampfsystems habe ich sicher noch nicht ausgereizt – da muss ich meine eigene "Eingefahrenheit" wohl noch überwinden.

[b]Phantom Liberty DLC:[/b]
Ich bin noch nicht durch, aber als Fan von "Die Klapperschlange" (Escape from New York) feiere ich den Stil von Dogtown extrem. Es gab da eine Szene auf einer Party... eigentlich wollte ich nur mit einem Kollegen quatschen, aber dann zeigt eine Tänzerin eine Performance mit Lasershow auf der Bühne. Ich stand da, hatte Gänsehaut und war hypnotisiert, mir dem Gedanken "Was passiert hier gerade". Genau solche Momente meine ich.

Fazit:
Es geht hier nicht nur um Storytelling. Es geht darum, völlig in einer Welt zu versinken. Klare Empfehlung.

毫无疑问，2077的首发可以用灾难性来形容，当时自己还是预购的gog版本，然而由于预售跳票、半成品的首发版本、极其难用的gog平台以及那时自己的硬件条件限制，自己只玩了很短很短的时间就弃了坑。正式开始游玩2077的时候还是额外在steam上购买了一份，版本号也已经到了1.63版本。随即而来的便是2.0游戏框架玩法大改以及大型资料片《往日之影》的发售。以今天的眼光来看，现如今的2077虽然还有多多少少的bug、主线剧情阉割、画饼遥遥无期等一系列问题，但在这个现如今游戏内玩法框架已经成熟、且有高质量资料片兜底的版本，2077也算得上一款值得体验的良作。

[h3]游戏背景：脱胎于桌游的近未来赛博世界[/h3]

与CDPR的成名作《巫师/猎魔人》系列一样，2077也有着自己的背景来源，不过与前者脱胎于《猎魔人》系列小说不同，2077的故事发源于《赛博朋克》相关系列桌游：《赛博朋克2013》、《赛博朋克2020》与《赛博朋克：红(RED)》。除了1988年发行的初代《赛博朋克2013》因年代过于久远而基本绝版外，其余两部桌游规则书均可或多或少在国外相关论坛中查阅到相应的影印版甚至是实体版拍卖渠道（当然，实体版的代价也是相当高昂），而《赛博朋克2077》游戏本身的故事背景与世界观也参照了2020与RED这两部规则书中的内容。正因如此，2077拥有非常庞大的世界观作为铺垫，从军用科技、荒坂、康陶、生物技术等巨企，到美联邦的分裂与新美国的崛起、旧网崩溃、夜之城的起源与荒坂塔核爆等大事件，玩家所看到的、存在于npc口中传述的故事或者隐藏在路边芯片中的一条条背景信息，都有规则书中的内容为其背书。这些丰富的背景信息使得游戏整体的世界观趋于自洽，也为游戏本身的剧情发展奠定了一个良好的基础。作为一款带有rpg与开放世界元素的游戏，与只通过游戏内剧情与关键人物互动来交代世界观等背景信息的方式相比，这类隐藏在整个世界中，而又有充分背景资料的世界观表现方式无疑更能增加玩家们的代入感。
正如游戏名称所属，2077是一款纯粹的未来/近未来的科幻风格游戏，而同时由于为了更好的融入原设定书所描述的背景信息，游戏中或多或少会存在一些在今天的我们看来很不可思议，甚至是落后与愚昧的体现：可能你会见到落后的充满西部风格的单动左轮手枪与高精尖技术制造的电磁动能狙击枪共同出现在帮派据点中，可能路面上奔跑的汽车所使用的燃料在现代化学的视角来看几乎是子虚乌有，可能巨企建立的能够“容纳你的灵魂”的计算机所用硬件基本与当代家用微机相当，甚至你会见到打扮与言行非常“多元化”、即含有部分lgbt要素的npc......然而，这一切在今天的我们看来很无法理解的现象，在游戏的背景设定之下又拥有着自己特殊的合理性：旧网崩溃导致的技术失衡、科技发展方向的过度歪曲、生活质量的巨大差异与特殊文化的全球性冲击......游戏用一个个荒谬的设定，反向勾勒出了一个真实的赛博世界。当然也不得不承认，这样的设计从某种角度也变相对玩家提出了筛选，虽然从概率角度来讲发生的可能性非常低，但我也确实在社区中见到过因为过度抵触游戏世界观而被迫提前弃坑的玩家。不过当你充分了解到游戏的故事背景，这些在现实生活中的不合理设定反而会在游戏中为你提供最大程度的代入感与沉浸感。

[h3]玩法与任务设计：完善且多样的战斗体系及流派、味道尚可的成长系统与开放世界[/h3]

2077的战斗系统其实已经不用多说什么。时至今日，经历了首发版本的半成品、1.6版本的数值失衡、2.0版本后的多次战斗系统调整，目前版本的2077在战斗玩法上已经可以说是达到了一个趋近完美平衡点。围绕黑客、时停、狂暴三种操作系统、五大属性技能树与资料片加入的relic技能树，搭配上从武士刀链锯剑飞刀等近战武器到西部左轮突击步枪乃至拉栓大狙与电磁动能武器等花样百出的枪械，目前游戏内有一定强度、适合大多数玩家的流派已经多达十余种，如果算上并不大众或者只适合高玩的个人diy流派，那么这个数字肯能还会进一步增加至几十种。除了传统黑客、时停刀剑、狂暴钝器、肉体霰弹等轮椅流派外，诸如近战黑客、狂暴飞刀、时停西部牛仔左轮、半伤龟壳流乃至围绕克伦奇科夫与装殖减缩进行构筑的无操作系统纯枪械流等新型流派也在不断开发。这也是为什么2077作为一款纯粹的单机游戏，自己仍然体验了四百余小时的原因。背景、剧情以及隐藏在开放世界中的彩蛋固然是一方面，但毕竟游戏没有new game+，缺少了花样繁多的战斗系统与个人流派，单靠剧情彩蛋本身可能并不会使一个没有ng+的游戏进行多周目体验——毕竟彩蛋可以从单一存档sl来进行发掘。
2077的成长系统算是比较标准的rpg角色成长体系了。除上文提到过的义体品质与属性技能外，游戏内主角的成长要素还包括角色等级、街头声望（类似于世界等级）、装备品质与配件、天赋技能等。自2.0战斗系统大改后，游戏删除了武器装备方面类似《巫师3》的等级机制，通过击杀掉落或拾取而新获得的武器装备不再随角色当前等级而具有固定等级，取而代之的则是随街头声望而固定的装备品质与随机的孔位、配件。这一改动极大方便了强迫症进行收集工作，也一定程度上避免了前期获得的不朽在后期因数值过于落后而不得不退居二线。然而改良后的成长系统增加了一个令自己深恶痛绝的机制——义体副词条。由于2.0后版本整体数值收缩，只靠义体、装备本身的属性以及天赋虽然可以应付最高难度下部分任务与几场boss战，不过由于数值的差异整体战斗下来会比较考验操作，而义体副词条则弥补了这部分数值差异，虽然单一副词条提供的加成微不足道，但积少成多，如果刷单一词条综合下来的总加成能达到百分之几十甚至上百。然而刷副词条的过程又是极端痛苦的，虽然有cet控制台指令可以通过退出义体升级界面来达到速刷的目的，但总体下来这部分内容与刷5++多孔武器相比还是相当浪费时间，个人很不适应。
当然，作为一款含有开放世界元素的游戏，2077的夜之城大世界中也确实包含大量的ncpd事件，即俗称的“罐头”，不过在自己看来，2077中的大世界罐头属于个人最能接受的一类方式。2077的ncpd事件没有任何形式的解密，同样是大世界中的“？”，与《霍格沃茨之遗》中包含的重复解密、《巫师3》史凯利格海洋中大量在后期没有多大价值的素材相比，2077的罐头只有纯粹的战斗爽，以及用于补充剧情及世界观的芯片。如果不只是为了打全成就，这些ncpd事件可以成为玩家前期重要的经济来源、后期的零件来源、流派的试验场、世界观的补充说明，这部分虽然还是罐头内容，但吃起来也还算比较香的。

[h3]故事发展：阉割的主线、优质的支线与更上一层楼的资料片剧情[/h3]

2077本体的主线剧情实际上占比并不高，如果自始至终不顾结局选择只单独完成本体主线，那最终用时可能只有三十余小时。而且令自己很不满的是，主线开篇部分对于详细剧情的描绘很少，从出身相关的序章任务后便直接跳转到了主线，中间大量与杰克一起，认识熟悉老维、威尔斯太太、米斯蒂等重要人物，并且在夜之城初步立足的剧情全部被cg代替。个人认为这一做法非常毁坏玩家的代入感，删去序章到当前主线中间的剧情很容易造成玩家难以对后续发生的剧情产生共情（比如杰克的去世后一些玩家认为v和其他人物的感情非常突兀）。我曾经听到过一种传言，发售时cdpr为了赶工期刻意删去了尚未完成的前期剧情内容，虽然这一说法的真实性很值得商榷，但开篇部分大量cg的完成度似乎从某个角度印证了这一点。虽然自己对2077蕴含的精神内核非常有兴趣，但在体验所有剧情内容后，回过头来看一个开篇阉割的主线实在是给人一种不好的印象。
与主线相对，2077的支线可谓是相当丰富，从四条与主线结局息息相关的“个人线”、强尼与罗格的“旧日线”外，从对主线剧情内容的补充、对世界观的拓展，到对夜之城本土帮派的行动、对“劳苦大众”的帮助或者惩戒，再到单纯的彩蛋或者联动......且不提玩法上可能存在部分雷同的中间人委托与ncpd事件（事实上，这部分内容确实是世界观的强力补充以及针对主线剧情人物结局的填坑），只考虑在列表中标记为支线的任务，2077支线剧情的可发掘内容也至少达到了与主线持平甚至超越的水准。其中有v身边人物的互动、与帮派结社的交涉、对人性发人深省的思考、以及令人忍俊不禁或细思极恐的彩蛋。虽然不得不承认支线也有罪与罚这样强行输出价值观的难绷任务，但整体上看支线剧情的水准还是足够的。
至于资料片的剧情，我只能说如果当初本体剧情能做到这种程度那么也不会遭到那么多人吐槽。首先资料片开局的表现力就远超本体的阉割开局一大截，坠毁的飞机拖着火光从眼前冲来，伴随着v从高台上跌落，《往日之影》的标题随之显现，这一幕在我心中的印象随时间的推移甚至已经超越了单挑荒坂塔的“以我残躯化烈火”。而资料片的剧情部分围绕新美国与狗镇本土权力争夺两条剧情线，结合资料片附带的支线任务，整体叙述框架呈现出双线并举、环环相扣的网格状，同时也没有过多叙述的啰嗦与强行输出价值观的引人不适。这么一看也难怪资料片在很大程度上挽救了本体的口碑。

[h3]人物塑造：充满矛盾的内核与五光十色下的众生百态[/h3]

对于2077主要人物蕴含的精神内核，有人说是底层人们针对公司狗决不妥协的反抗，有人说是在钢铁森林下对自由的向往，但在我看来，游戏中人物体现最多的还是内心中的矛盾与冲突。v，一名初出茅庐的佣兵，在绀碧大厦一役后便陷入了生命的倒计时，而v原本的传奇梦与自己对活下去的渴望在此时此刻便开始了冲突。在与银手相熟后，v内心的矛盾点又增加了一份对银手的的看法。太阳、星星、节制乃至高塔，不同结局在我看来可以说是矛盾冲突的不同缓解方案，但在夜之城这么一座“逐梦之城”、乃至整个世界的大背景下，正所谓“夜之城没有活着的传奇”，这一矛盾永远无法真正解决。至于强尼·银手，有人说他是恐怖分子，有人说他是一代巨星与革命者，但在我看来，他也是一个充满矛盾冲突的综合体。一方面，他在生前多次公开表达对公司的不满以至于与公司爆发冲突，最终参与了核爆荒坂塔的行动，但另一方面，他又在v的记忆里篡改过去的真相，把摩根·黑手与晒衣驼乃的功劳揽在自己身上，试图掩盖自己面对亚当·重锤时的无力与脆弱。而随着剧情的推进，强尼也在逐步与自己的过去和解，从一个一味通过破坏的方式试图毁灭公司的摇滚小子逐渐转变为了一个懂得思考、学会站在他人角度、与v同甘共苦的斗士。虽然剧情里一些场合中强尼的表现很不讨喜，但通关后再回味，强尼在剧情中的成长以及与v之间一步步走向互相理解反而为这个人物增加了一分独特的魅力。
除了v与强尼这两位主角外，游戏中有名有姓的重要人物还有很多，视v如己出的老维、一心成为传奇的挚友杰克、慈眉善目的威尔斯太太、忠诚但可惜是愚忠的竹村、英姿飒爽的罗格、为了自由不惜一切的百灵鸟、沉稳但无主见的李德......他们与无数无名的角色一起，共同构成了夜之城的众生百态。也许是行走在路上的一句吐槽，也许是“无意”撞车后对方的咒骂，也许是酒吧中粗放的大声谈笑，也许是市中心高档商店中的彬彬有礼，有名与无名的角色一起，为夜之城这个游戏中世界增添了一份生机与活力。自己几百小时开了六次新存档固然有一部分因素是被战斗爽吸引，但不可否认的是，夜之城中众生百态增添的一份代入感也是很重要的因素。任务与委托之外的闲来无事，开着超跑在环城高速上闲逛，或者漫步在大街小巷去感受市井之中的另类繁华，那一份“游戏中的真实”也带来了别样的体验。

[h3]本地化：良莠不一的翻译与瑕不掩瑜的优秀中配[/h3]

2077的本土化分为翻译与配音两方面，其中翻译部分的问题是比较大的。我理解翻译对于接地气的追求，但翻译要讲究信、达、雅兼备，如果为了追求所谓接地气连最基本的准确都做不到，那么这种翻译方法无疑是相当失败的。无论是本体剧情中剧情选项翻译不明确、引发玩家判断错误导致走向了不想选的剧情，插管任务中把工程师关于强尼手枪去向的语句含义完全翻译为反义，还是资料片中把老船长的话翻译为“爸爸”、特定语境下的百灵鸟依然按照原本翻译为“百灵婊”，这些为了所谓接地气而曲解原意、带给玩家错误判断的翻译方法个人看来非常不妥当。关于这一点需要求证的玩家可以打上双语字幕mod来验证翻译的正确与否。而与之相对的，中配这部分自己就非常满意，虽然可能是因为盲配的原因导致剧情中偶尔会出现文本与配音出现些许差别，但总体上还是不影响游玩的。

[h3]总评[/h3]

我有大量理由去黑2077：首发跳票、半成品、画饼不填、bug反复、非pc端优化爆炸等，确实cdpr这番操作某种程度来讲也算开了预售半成品、事后以更新方式补救的坏头。然而，今日的2077依然成为了我最喜欢的单机游戏之一，究其原因可能是游戏战斗爽的玩法，可能是漫步于夜之城中的沉浸感。但思来想去，最终我还是把原因归结于2077给了我一个关于赛博朋克世界真实状况的假设。曾经我以为的赛博朋克世界，是充满了高科技，人人只要拥有武力就可高高在上、睥睨他人性命的混乱世界，也一度对那种世界充满了向往。但在反复品尝本作后，我才意识到了一个事实：你我这样的普通人倘若到了夜之城的世界中，或许大概率也只能成为最底层的百姓，也就是游戏中被v、帮派、犯罪分子、公司武装随手杀掉的芸芸众生。而赛博朋克世界的真相或许对部分人来说可以是乌托邦，但对于大多数人来说，那样的世界或许只能是一片吃人不吐骨头的黑暗罢了。

전체적인 미션들은 위쳐3에서도 보여줬던 CDPR 특유의 선택지 고민을 사이버 펑크 세계관에서 해볼 수 있도록 메인 미션과 사이드 미션들이 구성되어 있었습니다. 덕분에 나이트 시티라는 이 사이버 펑크 세계관에 더 빠져들 수 있었고, 이 세계관에서만 볼 수 있는 참신한 사건과 경험들을 겪어 볼 수 있어서 정말 좋았습니다. 전체적인 스토리도 깔끔했던 것 같긴한데, 뭐랄까 저는 개인적으로 초반 플레이어와 조니 실버핸드의 관계가 어떻게 진행되고 있는지를 잘 파악할 수 없었습니다. 자세한 내용은 스포일러라 말할 순 없지만, 간단하게 말하자면 조니의 말을 듣는게 맞는지 아니면 내 생각대로 하는게 맞는지 잘 판단하기기 어려웠습니다. 물론 게임을 끝까지 플레이하고 나서는 어렴풋이 이해가 되었지만, 플레이 초반에는 둘의 관계가 무엇인지 따라가기가 좀 버거웠습니다.
이러한 메인 미션과 사이드 미션을 제외하고는 나머지 보조 임무들은 주로 반복적인 형태를 띄고 있습니다. 대부분의 보조 임무들이 해당 지역의 픽서에게 의뢰를 받고 해당 지역으로 이동해서 조사하거나 죽이거나 둘 중 하나이기 때문에, 저는 보조 임무만 집중적으로 하다가 지루해질 때 쯤 다시 메인 미션을 하러 가는 방식을 선택했습니다. 그럼에도 불구하고 모든 보조 임무에서 픽서가 홀로콜을 통해 미션 브리핑을 하는 더빙의 퀄리티와 모든 임무들에 대해서 텍스트를 통해 충분히 개연성을 부여해주었기 때문에 저기 옆동네 유비소프트식 맵 밝히기보다는 훨씬 더 정성이 들어가 있다는 생각이 듭니다. 
엔딩에 대해서 말해보자면, 다양한 엔딩들과 각각의 분기점들도 납득이 가는 것들이라 게임 막바지에는 게임 자체에서 제공하는 엔딩 직전 시점으로 돌아가는 기능을 통해 제가 볼 수 있는 엔딩들을 모두 다 볼 수 있어서 좋았습니다. 각각의 엔딩마다 납득도 되고 의미가 있는 내용을 담고 있어서 보는 재미가 있었습니다. 나중에 사평을 플레이할 생각이 있으시다면 제 생각에는 우선 본편 엔딩을 먼저 보고 싶으신 만큼 다 본 다음에 팬텀 리버티로 해금되는 엔딩을 보는 것을 추천드립니다. 본편만으로 볼 수 있는 엔딩들은 엔딩 이후에 V가 엔딩에 직결되는 미션을 하기 전으로 자동으로 돌아와 지는데, 팬텀 리버티로 해금되는 엔딩을 본 다음에는 그렇지 않더라고요. 물론 저의 개인적인 경험이라서 잘못된 정보일 수는 있겠지만, 본편 엔딩과 팬텀 리버티 엔딩 내용 자체만 비교하더라도 이런 순서로 보는게 맞다고 생각하긴 합니다.
이에 더해서 또 좋았던 부분은 아무래도 사이버 펑크라는 세계관 자체가 아닐까 싶습니다. 나이트 시티라는 거대한 도시 안에서 사이버 펑크에 존재할 것 같은 거의 모든 모습을 담아내고 있기 때문에 판자촌부터 시작해서 거대 빌딩들이 즐비한 도시까지 사이버 펑크라는 하나의 세계관을 이보다 더 잘 보여주는 도시가 과연 있을까 싶을 정도로 도시 구역마다 개성도 뚜렷하고 비주얼도 화려해서 차를 타고 의뢰를 하러 이곳저곳으로 돌아다니는 맛이 좋았습니다. 여기에 더해서 임플란트라는 개념과 총기 그리고 NPC들의 살벌한 외형까지 하나부터 열까지 세세하게 구성되어있다는 점에서도 정성이 돋보여서 플레이하는 동안 이 세계관에 더 쉽게 몰입할 수 있었던 것 같습니다.
저번의 발표를 통해서 CDPR에서 사이버펑크 2도 개발하고 있는 것 같은데, 부디 이번에는 회복된 평판을 다시 떨어뜨리지 않는 멋있고 재밌는 게임으로 잘 나왔으면 좋겠습니다.

Estamos falando do jogo da minha vida, aquele jogo que me fez amar o gênero Cyberpunk, que fez eu conhecer diversas obras que hoje são minhas preferidas também, como Akira e Cowboy Bebop (eu sei esse último é muito ligado ao space western, porém tem muitos elementos de Cyberpunk, as óticas são parecidas). Desde o primeiro momento que eu toquei nesse jogo foi sensacional, a ideia de ser uma ex marginal e agora ser um mercenário querendo alcançar o topo, na visão de V fiz muitas escolhas, algumas com peso na história, outras não. Mas no resumo de tudo é uma história impecável, com um baita ponto forte sem os personagens, a forma como o Jhonny Silverhand se torna mais o V e a gente se tornando mais o Jhonny, com ambos se entendendo e se importando um com o outro. Também a relação entre o V e Panam, Juddy e até o River Wand são tão profundas, por que a gente vê como em meio a tanto caos que é Night City, é incrível como facilmente o V toma as dores das pessoas que por muito acabou de conhecer e não sabe nada, e isso resultando com você ser retribuido, todos te ajudando na buscar de uma cura que provavelmente nem existe, mas que querem acreditar, pois se tiver uma chance, eles precisam buscar.

No fim do tudo, é um jogo que divide opiniões. Tem quem goste e tem quem odeie. Sendo sincero, a maioria das pessoas que não gostam dessa obra, estão apegados a uma visão distorcida do que foi o lançamento desse jogo, porém tenho certeza que se a maioria dar uma chance sem ligar para essas questões, vai ver que esse jogo é sensacional, não atoa é meu jogo top 1. E olha que só estou citando o jogo base, a Dlc é outra maravilha a parte, Idris Elba fez um papel impecável. 
Então se hoje você está com dúvida se joga ou não Cyberpunk. Eu diria que você deveria ao menos dar uma chance, a profundidade que esse jogo entrega é surreal. Você vai entrar no jogo com uma visão, e sair com outra totalmente diferente, a forma de ver o mundo muda. Mas antes de jogar sempre se lembre, Night City não tem final feliz...
Simplesmente fantástico.

I had heard that the bugs with this game were fixed, but that was not the case for me. Visual glitches where people, objects, and cars clip into each other or suddenly respawn are extremely frequent. Dead bodies are especially glitch-prone, although at least they're sometimes funny. I had one outright freeze requiring a force kill and restart.

The many NPCs roaming the world are very stiff, and their interactions unnatural. This applies to cars driving as well. The world does not feel rich and full of things to find as you explore, it feels hollow. Ultimately it is not immersive and comes off as a mediocre video game, not a living world.

The gameplay is pretty standard fare FPS stuff. Moving around just feels too janky for melee combat to be satisfying, despite their focus on making it a viable strategy. Jumping over things and leaping toward enemies just doesn't work very well. The only interesting thing here is the hacking aspect, which they did do a good job with.

The menus, which you will need to be interacting with all the time, are a pain on controller. They seem to have simply taken the mouse-based menus and done a poor job of adapting them for a controller. Often you'll need to be simply navigating the menu by controlling a virtual mouse pointer with your thumbstick. This was very surprising and disappointing, making good controller-based menus is table stakes for a game this big.

The story is the only interesting thing about this game, but it moves far too slowly. After an awesome intro, it slows to a crawl and gets way more boring, just dangling the promise of something interesting in front of you to keep you going, while drip feeding little hints of what cool thing might be in the future.

All in all, a game that is much too big for its own good. It's spread very thin.

CD Projekt Red совершили невозможное: заставили меня ненавидеть, затем терпеть, потом уважать и, в итоге, любить этого циничного, язвительного, сломленного рок-звезду-террориста, который поселился в моей голове. Это не просто «напарник в голове». Это самая сложная, многогранная и пронзительная связь между персонажами, которую я когда-либо видел в играх. Диалоги с ним — от перепалок до исповедальных разговоров в которых герои уходят в бесконечный самоанализ и проговаривание своих собственных ошибок. Финал этой истории оставил в моей душе пустоту, как после прощания с реальным человеком. Отдельный респект русской озвучке Джонни которая ничуть ни хуже оригинала(хоть и Киану Ривз вне конкуренции).
Основная сюжетная линия и без того была невероятна, но «Phantom Liberty» — это квантовый скачок. Догтаун — это Найт-Сити в миниатюре: ещё грязнее, ещё опаснее, ещё безысходнее. История с Соломоном Ридом и Сойкой — это триллер уровня лучших шпионских фильмов, где каждый выбор давит грузом ответственности. А новый финал... Он перевернул с ног на голову всё, что я думал о жертве и спасении. Это была та самая «ещё одна миссия», которая изменила всё.
ИТОГ:
За 167 часов Найт-Сити стал мне домом. Со всеми его язвами, неоновым блеском и потерянными душами. Cyberpunk 2077 с «Phantom Liberty» — это больше, чем игра. Это пережитый жизненный опыт, трагическая и прекрасная история о человеке, который в погоне за легендой нашёл нечто большее — себя, пусть и ненадолго. И того рокера-призрака, который навсегда останется не просто чипом в моей голове, а частью моей памяти.

Cyberpunk 2077 is the only game where you buy a $3,000 cybernetic eye just to still miss every shot, crash your car into a vending machine, and get emotionally manipulated by an NPC who looks better than you ever will.

Night City is alive. Too alive. Every pedestrian has a full backstory, a trauma, and a reason to walk directly into your car at 200 km/h.

The graphics? Insane. My GPU aged 5 years in 10 minutes. Ray tracing so realistic I could see my own bad life decisions reflected in puddles.

The story hits hard. One minute you’re saving the city, the next you’re questioning free will, capitalism, and why Keanu Reeves lives rent-free in your brain telling you to commit crimes.

Bugs? Sure. Sometimes NPCs T-pose to assert dominance. Cars spawn inside other cars. But honestly… that just makes it more cyberpunk.

Cyberpunk 2077 isn’t just a game.
It’s a beautiful, glitchy, existential crisis simulator where style matters more than morals and everyone needs therapy.

메인 스토리라인만을 진행했음을 밝히며 이 게임의 엔딩분기가 해당 엔딩들과 연관된 서브퀘스트를 완료했는지에 따라 갈리고 메인 스토리만을 진행한다면 어떤 선택지도 없이 베드엔딩으로 진행한다는 걸 이 게임은 안내하지 않았다.
어떤 지식도 없는 상태에서 플레이하기 좋아하는 유저가 위와같은 시스템을 모르는 상황에서 고급 택시 ai의 심부름이나 누군가의 의뢰 같은 서브 퀘스트를 시한부 주인공의 생존이라는 게임의 메인 퀘스트보다 우선하지 않으면 이 게임은 그것을 처벌하는것이다. 

메인스토리의 내용들은 결국 '기업을 위해 증언을 해주면 어딘가에 접근할 권한을 준다'는 계약과 그곳에서 '그 권한으로 누군가를 그곳에 대려간 후 아무튼 고쳐줘'를 해본다는게 엔드게임인것과 그 엔드게임에 다다르기까지 견뎌야 하는 퀘스트간의 빈약한 핍진성을 참아내며 최종장에 다다르니 게임 분위기를 포함한 주변 등장인물이 어떻게 니 친구를 죽인 기업의 개가 되는 '선택'을 할수 있냐며 끈임없이 힐난한다.
의뢰를 맡긴 주체가가 약속을 지키지 않을것 같다고 미션을 중지하면 퀘스트의 내용이 '돌아가서 ~의 의뢰를 수락하라'로 이어지는 만큼 어떤 선택도 개입되지 않는 선형적 플레이임을 다시 한번 강조할때, 뜬금없는 이런 반응들은 당혹감과 지금까지 전혀 선택한게 없었는데 도대체 어디서 분기가 있었는가 하는 스트레스와 불쾌함을 느끼게 했다.
그러나 이 불쾌감은 위에서 어거지로 참고 견뎌낸 쓰레기 같은 스토리로 진행하지도 않는것에서 큰 혼란과 분노로 바뀌었다. 
내 증언이 도대체 의미가 있나하는 의심과 실제로도 좆도 쓸모없었음은 뒤로 하더라도 거기서 끝났어야 했는데 갑자기 어물쩡 현재 권력자를 제압해라, 우당탕탕 보스전, 그래 잘했어 이제 우리가 고쳐줄게 하며 엔딩으로 급전개 한다. 이미 내가 이해한 스토리 전개와 전혀 맞지않아 도대체 이게 뭔 상황인가 하는 혼란속에서 조니와의 마지막 대화로 이 게임의 인상은 돌이킬수 없을 정도로 망가졌다.

이 조니라는 캐릭터는 엔딩분기를 만들지 않는다면 플레이 내내 조현병 환자와 같이 다니는것과 같을정도로 혼란스럽다. 처음 내 뇌에 침범해 본인이 내 자아를 대체하는 과정인데도 재키급으로 친근하게 말붙이는건 차치 하더라도 갑자기 본인이 사라져 주겠다는 둥 본인의 과거가 나와 겹쳐보인다는둥 뜬금없이 친밀도를 쌓더니 본인을 전적으로 믿으셔야 한다며 몸 좀 빌려주라고 빌드업을 하지않나 메인스토리가 강요하는 선형적 과정 과정마다 내 '선택'을 비난하고 종국에는 갑자기 본인과 내가 동화된걸 정말 몰랐냐며 사실은 내가 지우?려고 하는 본인의 인격이 이 거지같은 도시의 삶에서 유일하게 남음 인간성이 었다는 씹소리를 내 얼굴에 싸지르고 사라진다.
엔딩 분기가 여러가지, 즉 선택이 존재함을 안 이후에서야 어렴풋이 그의 조현병적 행보가 그 선택들이 존재함을 전재함로 한다는것을 이해 할수있었으나 역시 그 선택의 기회를 얻는 방식에는 굉장히 큰 불만이 생길 수 밖에 없었다. 내가 뒤져가는데 왜 심부름이나 해야하는건지, 차라리 페르소나 시리즈의 커뮤 달성도가 더 납득이 될 정도였다. 똑같이 전혀 진엔딩의 조건으로 유추할 수는 없으나 최소한 커뮤는 게임의 분위기나 메세지에 직접적으로 맞닿아있기라도 했으니 말이다.
그 이후에는 내가 생존을 위해 한 선택들이 사실은 고작 몇개월 수명을 연장시킨것 뿐이며 결국은 너도 사이버 감옥에 수감돼 니가 강탈할 몸이 생기기를 기다리는 '악마'이고 너 때문에 최악의 독재자가 새몸을 얻어 더욱 그의 치세를 공고히 할것이라며 끝까지 내 선택에 침을 뱉는다.

게임의 선악구도 역시 유치하다. 기업은 무조건 나쁜것 기업 나빠를 외치는 편은 무조건 좋은편. 너 왜 기업편들어 실망이다. 하하 날봐 내 아들몸을 빼았았어 나 엄청 나쁘지? 하고 굳이 뉴스에 나와 쳐 떠느는둥  발화들이 다 이딴 수준이다.
선택과 결과라는 플롯이 흥미로우려면 모든 선택들이 각자의 매력을 갖고있고 결과들은 납득이 되는 수준안에서 놀라움을 줘야 한다는 내 사견으로, 그리고 그 사견에 바탕이된 전작 위쳐3에서 보여준 놀라울 정도의 짜임새를 보여준 회사에서 이런 '너가 무조건 나빴어' 하는 유치함을 베드엔딩에 심어놓았다는것이 너무나도 아쉽고 불쾌했다. 특히, 그런 비정함을 묵묵하게 그려내는것이 사이버 펑크의 멋진점임을 생각할때 더욱 그렇다.

This isn't a power fantasy. It's not supposed to make you feel like a badass hero who saves the city. If you went in expecting that, you fundamentally misunderstood what the game is trying to do. CP2077 is a 60+ hour meditation on what it feels like to literally lose yourself in a world that was built to grind you into paste.

**Your body is not your own.**

The first-person perspective isn't just a design choice. It's the entire point. You're locked inside V's skull, and from minute one, that body is a problem you're trying to solve. On one hand, you're installing chrome; turning yourself into a modular meat machine, subject to market logic. You're not "upgrading." You're commodifying your own flesh. On the other hand, the Relic is killing you from the inside. Your body is simultaneously a DIY project and a terminal diagnosis. You are, at all times, a dying animal trying to pretend you're a immortal god.

**Night City is not a playground.**

The open world isn't freedom. It's a cage designed to look like freedom. Every icon on that map? That's not content. That's a shift. You're doing gig work. Literally. The game takes the structure of a modern open-world game (all those map markers, all those side hustles) and reveals it for what it actually is: late-capitalist piecework. You are a precarious laborer in a precarious world, and the "choice" you have is which fixer to bleed for today. The constant flood of calls, ads, and notifications aren't immersion-breaking; they're the point. You're never alone. You're always being sold to, called on, managed.

And yet you're not alone in another way, too. You meet people. Judy, Panam, Takemura. You form actual connections. You have conversations in dim apartments and on rooftops at dawn. You fall in love, maybe. You find a community. But here's the trap: those connections can't save you. They can't change the structure. The system doesn't care that you have people who love you. The Relic is still killing you. The gigs still come. The city still runs on your body. You're surrounded by genuine human connection in a world built to atomize and consume you, and that makes the alienation worse, not better. You're lonely *and* not lonely at the same time, and neither state offers escape.

**Johnny Silverhand is the ghost of a dead revolution.**

The Relic isn't just a plot device. It's a hostile takeover of your consciousness by a failed radical. Johnny represents every angry kid who thought you could burn it all down and start over. He tried. He lost. And now he's a tumor in your brain, forcing you to reckon with the fact that all the old ways of fighting back are dead. He's the political unconscious of the setting; the corpse of 20th-century rebellion haunting a 21st-century graveyard. The conflict between V and Johnny isn't a buddy comedy. It's two incompatible ideologies fighting a war on the battlefield of a single, dying brain.

**"Becoming a legend" means destroying yourself.**

The game keeps telling you to become a legend of Night City, and everyone acts like that's the goal. But look at what that actually means. Johnny's a legend. He's dead, and he lost. David Martinez from Edgerunners? Legend. Dead. Legends in Night City aren't people who won. They're people who burned so bright they couldn't be ignored on their way out. The game is offering you a choice between surviving as a nobody or dying as somebody. And here's the kicker: the survival endings feel hollow. The "good" endings are the ones where you go out swinging. This isn't about accumulation or victory. It's about sovereign self-destruction; choosing the terms of your own end in a world that wants to choose them for you.

**The combat system is a lie you tell yourself.**

And here's where it gets really interesting. The gameplay loop lets you become an absolute monster. Sandevistan time-dilation, gorilla arms, mantis blades, reflex tuning; you can build V into a one-person apocalypse. The combat feels incredible. You feel unstoppable. And that is the *point* of the dissonance.

The game lets you feel like a god in a body that's rotting from the inside. Every upgrade, every perk, every piece of chrome makes you better at solving problems that don't matter. You're getting stronger in a system that's already killed you. It's the perfect mirror of consumer culture: here, have this power, this product, this upgrade. Ignore that it changes nothing about the structure that's killing you. The progression system is a coping mechanism. You're playing a power fantasy inside a tragedy, and the tragedy wins.

But then, and this is crucial, the game lets you *use* that power for something that matters. The "blaze of glory" ending is where all that mechanical mastery finally means something. You've spent 60 hours building the perfect killing machine, and now you get to spend it all on one last, doomed, beautiful act of defiance. The gameplay power isn't there to let you win. It's there so you can choose *how* you lose. That's what makes it a legend. Not that you survived. That you got to decide what your death looked like.

Cyberpunk 2077 is not here to make you feel good. It's here to make you feel *something*; specifically, what it's like to be a person in a world that has mechanized, monetized, and moduleized every aspect of existence, including your own body and mind. It's a game about trying to find meaning in a system designed to extract value and then discard you.

🌃 **Cyberpunk 2077 – neonowy sen o wolności i upadku**

Cyberpunk 2077 to gra, która od pierwszych chwil wrzuca cię w świat skąpany w neonach, przemocy i technologii, gdzie człowieczeństwo jest towarem, a marzenia mają cenę. Night City żyje własnym rytmem – głośnym, brudnym i hipnotyzującym – i bardzo szybko wciąga bez reszty.

Rozgrywka łączy strzelanie, skradanie i elementy RPG w dość elastyczny sposób. Możesz być cybernetycznym najemnikiem idącym na rympał albo cichym hakerem, który łamie systemy, zanim ktoś zdąży się zorientować. System rozwoju postaci i cyberwszczepów daje sporo swobody, a zmiana buildów realnie wpływa na styl gry.

Największą siłą Cyberpunka jest klimat i narracja. Fabuła, relacje z postaciami i poboczne wątki często potrafią zaskoczyć dojrzałością i emocjonalnym ciężarem. Night City to nie tylko mapa – to miasto pełne małych historii, moralnych wyborów i poczucia, że świat nie kręci się wokół ciebie.

Oprawa audiowizualna robi ogromne wrażenie: detale miasta, oświetlenie, muzyka i design świata tworzą spójną, intensywną wizję przyszłości. Jednocześnie gra nie ucieka od swojej nierówności – zdarzają się powtarzalne aktywności, a miejscami tempo rozgrywki potrafi siąść.

Mimo swoich problemów Cyberpunk 2077 to doświadczenie, które zostaje w głowie na długo. To opowieść o ambicji, tożsamości i cenie, jaką płaci się za życie w świecie bez zasad.

⭐ **Ocena: 8,5/10** – wciągająca, stylowa i pełna charakteru podróż po mieście, które potrafi zachwycić równie mocno, co przytłoczyć. Jeśli dasz mu czas, Night City odwdzięczy się klimatem nie do podrobienia.

[h3]Я долго думал, можно ли вообще сейчас писать про Cyberpunk
и не выглядеть как человек, который только что вышел из комы.[/h3]
Оказалось — можно, но аккуратно.

Игра сейчас, внезапно, работает.
Не идеально, не «вау»,
но без постоянного ощущения,
что вот сейчас что-то обязательно сломается.
Хотя… иногда всё-таки ломается. Но редко. Ну почти.

У меня не NASA-комп,
и Cyberpunk на нём не делает вид,
что ему срочно нужен RTX 9090.
Настройки покрутил,
картинку сделал нормальную,
и да — играть можно.
Даже с кастомизацией,
а не «шапка и шорты на весь Найт-Сити».

Сам город всё ещё странный.
Вроде живой, шумный,
а потом ловишь себя на мысли,
что половина NPC просто существует для галочки.
Но при этом гулять по улицам всё равно хочется,
потому что неон, реклама и ощущение,
что ты тут вообще лишний.

Стрельба — окей.
Не эталон, но стрелять приятно.
Стелс живёт своей жизнью:
иногда ты ниндзя,
иногда — «а откуда он меня увидел вообще?».
Ближний бой… есть. Скажем так.

Сюжет внезапно цепляет.
Не всегда, не везде,
но в какие-то моменты
ты реально сидишь и слушаешь диалоги,
а не думаешь, что бы включить на втором мониторе.
Побочные квесты местами вообще лучше основного.

Персонажи — сильная сторона.
Некоторые появляются ненадолго,
а потом ты ловишь себя на мысли,
что они запомнились больше,
чем главные герои из других игр.

Да, это всё ещё Cyberpunk.
Анимации иногда чудят,
оптимизация может внезапно обидеться,
и где-то в глубине души
ты всё равно ждёшь подвоха.
Но это уже не та игра,
которую хочется удалить через два часа.

Самое главное — в неё нормально играть.
Не терпеть, не уговаривать себя,
а просто заходить и залипать.
А потом смотреть на часы
и думать: «ну ладно, ещё один квест».

Если ты дропнул игру на релизе
или просто отложил «на потом» —
сейчас это наконец-то
адекватная RPG,
а не исторический экспонат.

👍 Рекомендую.
Без фанатизма,
но уже без стыда.

I really wish there was a way to write informal reviews for games, without having to recommend them or recommend against them. Because that what this game would get from me.

Now, don't get decieved by Steam saying, I'd only have 5 hours in this game, because I don't. I've been playing this game since Version 1.1, if not 1.0, and finished the entire game, including the DLC. In total, I have around 100 hours, most of that on GOG.

But to my opinion on the game. Do I enjoy it? Yes, I do. Is it amazing, has barely any bugs now and runs great? Absolutely not.

It's a good game. It's unique, does things no other game does and I enjoy it because of that. It's far from amazing, though, and still doesn't even remotely live up to the promises CDPR made before release. But it doesn't need to, it's fine as it is. You can do stupid builds (I built a nearly invincable V, that does way more damage than he should) and I love it for that. It has a ton of completely useless, yet very interesting features, which I'm really a fan of.

It does have a ton of bugs. Some funny, like cars randomly exploding, losing all doors and wheels or NPCs casually walking over things they shouldn't be able to walk over (like cars or walls), but some are really annoying or even game breaking. I'm pretty sure there's also a memory leak somewhere in there, which I ran into a few days ago. Additionally, the game has a few issues with the AMD GPU driver ever since CDPR released the 2.3 update, leading to a ton of micro stuttering and issues with path tracing. That's annoying as heck, and if you enable path tracing even game breaking. What doesn't help is, that the FSR 3 implementation is probably the worst out of any game. It's horrible. FSR 2 is fine (FSR 2 is just old), but FSR 3 is not. So on a Steam Deck, if FSR 2 is too low quality for you, then I'd recommend getting Decky and installing Optiscaler through that, making it possible to use the leaked (by AMD themselves) version of FSR 4. And weirdly enough, on my PC, I feel like the game had less issues on version 1.1 than since 2.0. Despite my PC getting a lot more powerful and the game getting a lot of updates since then. Or perhaps the game has more issues on more powerful PCs?

The performance is... Fine. It's not bad, especially on lower end hardware (like the Steam Deck) the game runs actually surprisingly well, but on higher end hardware the game seems to not scale as well as I would expect. The DLC also has some performance issues, meaning it will struggle on lower end devices, like the Steam Deck and the Switch 2, even though the main game runs fine.

I really hope, that Cyberpunk 2077 2 (or whatever they'll call it) will have less bugs and better performance. And that they'll bring AMD FSR Redstone to both this game and it's sequel.
