I'm shocked it actually runs alright on my lower tier hardware (i7-7700k 4.20ghz & RTX 2070). I get my 30fps at 4K max settings (DLSS on Performance Plus mode, Ray Traced Reflections & Shadows off). The story starts off very confusing at the beginning but after playing for five hours, things start to make a little bit of sense. I've already heard multiple NPCs repeat their dialogue at the entrance of the apartment, which is very disappointing, because I've only visited the apartment a couple of times. The driving/car handling is extremely rough, and the auto-pilot feature doesn't work. The gun play isn't my favorite either (on Xbox Controller), the recoil is insane, and everyone is heavily armored, so picture every gunfight being like Apex Legends. This pushes you towards a stealth approach which works 60% of the time. The hacking is incredibly tedious, imagine Watch Dogs 2 times ten and on steroids. The game does look pretty, though! 

I guess coming from playing a lot of Rockstar Games' titles, the world and writing here feels mediocre for the genre. Not entirely terrible, but if Red Dead Redemption 2 is Alfred Hitchcock, Cyberpunk 2077 has felt like a bad Hallmark Movie up to this point. It's just not consumable when you have experienced greatness beforehand. You'd only be able to like it, if it was the first open world game you played.

I will update this review once I finish the game, because it's entirely possible the story just needs time to marinate and evolve into something greater. From what I've read, this is supposed to be an all-time great, but I have yet to see what all of the hype is about.

Update: 13 hours in, Keanu Reeves has come in to save the story. The writing seems to be getting a little better too. Maybe there is hope after all.

Update 2.0: 20 hours in, the game's story has completely hit a brick wall and I don't even feel motivated enough to finish it. The story telling is just so bad and predictable. You may get one good mission here or there, but first you have to complete ten monotonous ones to get to it. I can't recommend this game. The only stuff that it has going for it are a couple good voice actors and the visuals, everything else feels super unfinished and not very well thought out. I'd say, it's a $20 game at best. I spent double that and feel disappointed with my purchase.

Eu só joguei CP após as correções de DLC, então tive a melhor experiência possível de jogo.

Cyberpunk é a minha estética favorita.

Este é o segundo melhor jogo que já joguei e, na imersão e diversão que me traz, é um mundo completo a se explorar, juntamente com mods que fazem a experiência ficar ainda melhor.

É incrível ver a história de V e como houve o desenrolar dela, onde realmente há consequência de tudo e onde Night City não perdoa ninguém, assim como é nas grandes metrópoles, onde há dor, ignorância e um local onde sempre vai haver alguém pisando em você.

A história de redenção do Johnny, onde ele ainda continua sendo um imbecil, mas um imbecil um pouco melhor, é muito boa de acompanhar, onde pela primeira vez ele tem um amigo e o peso das decisões que você faz e o quanto isso vai moldar a sua experiência e o seu V.

Phantom Liberty foi onde definitivamente me apaixonei por este jogo, é surreal. A SongBird e o Reed são, de longe, os melhores personagens, exceto pelo V e Johnny, e o peso que essa trama traz pra esse jogo é incrível; você decidir a melhor forma que vai ter da trama da Song e o peso que isso vai te fazer sentir, só TLOU 2 me fez sentir.

Foi o meu terceiro jogo platinado e o que eu mais me diverti fazendo; ver todas as outras escolhas e situações que eu poderia ter feito foi muito divertido.

CP tem seus problemas, mas a construção de história, cidade e gameplay fazem com que estes problemas se tornem muito menores.

É uma pena que eles não tiveram tempo de realizar tudo que gostariam pra esse jogo, porque definitivamente eles sabem como fazer uma história.

Sem contar na animação de Edgerunners, que é muito boa.

CP é incrível e um dos jogos da minha vida.

I picked up Cyberpunk again years after release, expecting a decent comeback story. What I got instead was one of the best open-world RPG experiences I’ve played in a long time. With all the updates and reworks, the game finally feels like the version we should’ve had from the start—alive, stylish, and actually worth losing hours to.

Night City finally lives up to the hype. The city is dense and chaotic, the gunplay and cyberware builds feel incredibly fun to experiment with, and the story hits way harder when everything around it actually works. Side quests aren’t filler, they’re actual stories that pull you into the city’s mess. Half the time I ignored the main mission just because the random jobs were too good to walk away from.

It’s crazy how much replay value there is once you understand how different builds change the game. Hacking everything, going full “street samurai,” or running a tech sharpshooter build changes not just combat, but how you approach missions, exploration, and even gear.

Is it perfect now? No game ever is. But it’s genuinely great. The atmosphere, characters, music, and world all come together in a way that sticks with you after you log out, and that’s rare.

Pros

Night City actually feels alive and worth exploring

Builds and combat are insanely fun now

Side quests feel like real stories, not chores

Great writing, characters, and soundtrack

Massive improvement compared to launch

Cons
– You’ll want extra playthroughs just to try new builds (not really a con)
– Expect to lose weekends without noticing

Final Verdict:
After 100 hours, Cyberpunk 2077 has finally become the game it was meant to be. If you skipped it at launch or dropped it early, it’s absolutely worth playing now. Highly recommend.

I remember when this game first came out. I remember the night before when I pre-ordered it. I remember the night before I couldn't sleep because I was so excited about it. I feel like most gamers shared the same experience. 

The morning of December the 9th, I awoke to overwhelmingly negative reviews. Why? Because CD Projekt RED had fumbled. Fumbled harder than almost any other company in the history of video games. Their product was a complete disaster, burning from the inside out. A year passes, minor patches are put in place, but nothing significant. Most people have moved on, thinking that the game will never be in a great state....

But then they come out swinging. Cyberpunk 2077 explodes into probably one of the best games ever made. A massive open world, hundreds of DIVERSE quests and even more side activities, the most colorful cast of characters to probably ever grace a monitor, and more guns, cyberware, and skills than anyone would know what to do with. An overnight success that took a year to get it to that state. 

And they weren't finished. They hit us with Phantom Liberty, a DLC so packed with stuff that it basically feels like a completely new game (think Blood and Wine for The Witcher 3). A completely new story, new characters and new gear. And I'm still working on finishing this up as I type this, but I just had to write this review to tell everyone how much I love this game. 

To this day, I don't think there's a single greater comeback in the history of video games. The fact that CDPR actually cared about this and wanted to fix it is still crazy to me, because there are so many devs that, at that point, would shutter the game and try to bury all of the negative press. But I think that's why so many have respect for CDPR. Not because they're talented. Not because the worlds they create are amazing. Not because their characters (no matter how fantastical) are still somewhat relatable. But it's because they care about the games they make, and the people who play them. 

And don't get me wrong. This game isn't perfect. No game will ever be 100% bug free, but CDPR has done a great, great, great job with their patches and hotfixes. I really think the only bug I've seen more than once is NPCs somehow randomly getting teleported through the roof of my car and getting stuck, but only when I get out and start shooting at people. Strange bug, but not terrible by any means. 

Anyway:

Now, with another Cyberpunk game in the works (fingers crossed for a 2027-ish release), I hope that CDPR has learned from their past fumble and grows this series into something bigger than they ever realized it could be. I think we all know they have the talent and capability to do it. 

Thank you, CDPR,  for giving us such an incredible experience (even if it took a while to get it there!)

Dieses Spiel ist etwas ganz besonderes. Insbesondere für Erwachsene. Ich will darauf hinaus, das in diesem Spiel ohne jeden Filter gesprochen wird. Gewalt, Sex, Flüche wie auch immer. Zusammen mit einer wirklich interessanten und Skill abhängen Anzahl an Antworten die man in verschiedenen Situationen geben kann, einer Open Map die man völlig frei erkunden kann. Drei verschiedenen Herkünften, der Wahl ob man männlich oder weibliche oder gemischte Charaktäre spielen will. Wer es mag kann seinen Charakter völlig nackt sehen und erleben. Es gibt auch ein paar Sexszenen die nicht alles zeigen aber fast.
Blut spritzt, Gedärme fliegen (wenn man das will). Man kann sich entscheiden ob man mit extremer Beschleunigung mittels Sandevistan (oder Berserker) auf Nahkampf skilled und auch da gibt es es ne Menge Auswahl. Es gibt Waffen die man immer weiter aufrüsten kann. Es gibt zahlreiche Fahrzeuge die sich komplett unterschiedlich fahren. Diese gibt es mit einer, zwei oder auch ohne Waffen. Einige Fahrzeuge sind Gratis und müssen gefunden oder freigespielt werden, die meisten kann man aber kaufen. Wobei auch hier Preis und Verfügbarkeit davon abhängen ob man für einen NPC Autos klaut. Und hier geht es mal auf Zeit, mal das die unversehrt ankommen und mal wird man unterwegs von Horden von Gegner versucht daran zu hindern das Auto zu klauen. Und wehe man tötet einen Zivilisten oder noch schlimmer einen Polizisten. Dann gibt es Ärger vom ganzen Polizeiapparat. Je mehr man sich gegen die Polizei wehrt desto krasser fahren die auf. Die Erweiterung Phantom Liberty ist ein echter Goldschatz und bringt echt super coolen und neuen Content.

Das beste an dem Spiel ist, das es einer echten Welt (in ferner Zukunft) so nahe kommt wie kein anderes das ich kenne. Das Licht, die vielen verschiedenen NPCs, die Vielen verschiedenen Questreihen und Aufträge, und auch die möglichen Beziehungen machen es einfach unglaublich fesselnd. Ja ihr habt richtig gehört. Man und Frau können mit insgesamt jeweils mindestens zwei NPC´s eine feste Beziehung eingehen. Dabei gibt es hetero und und homosexuelle Optionen und auch was dazwischen. Man kann das Geschlecht und die Stimme jeweils frei kombinieren.

Und es gibt eine Vielzahl verschiedener Enden. Mir persönlich fehlt eine Option mit der man seinen Charakter für immer weiter spielen kann, oder wie im Netflix Anime im Team spielen kann.

Und ich würde mir wünschen die zwischenmenschlichen Beziehungen und Freundschaften vertiefen zu können. Ist man einmal mit einem Partner zusammen, kann man sich in einer Wohnung treffen (man kann mehrere Wohnungen kaufen) und dort zusammen kuscheln (harmlos auf der Couch) ein paar Sekunden zusammen duschen und schlafen gehen (vollkommen harmlos). Und es gibt nur eine fest definierte Anzahl an 3-4 Fragen bei jedem Treffen. Das ist echt mau.

Daher verstehe ich nicht wieso Cyberpunk 2077 nicht noch ein paar Content updates bekommt bevor die neue Version vermutlich 2030 frühestens rauskommt. Vermutlich zusammen mit GTA6 :-) Kleiner Scherz.

Also um es nochmal klar zu machen, Auch wenn es bei einigen Leuten immer wieder mal zu abstürzen kommt, dieses Spiel ist einfach eine Klasse für sich. Ich hatte keine Ahnung wie sehr ich das Spiel mögen würde, sonst hätte ich es nicht erst vor ein paar Monaten gekauft. Allerdings ist mit dem letzten Updaten vor kurzem erst der automatische Fahrmodus eingeführt worden und mit dem letzten Update so korrigiert worden das er relativ gut funktioniert. Bevor man die Schnellreisepunkte freigespielt hat, kostet es sonst ewig Zeit irgendwo hinzutuckern ohne den Auto Mode.

Wieso das nicht von Anfang an schon in der Alpha Version eingebaut wurde ist mir ein Rätsel. Gerade sowas nervt die Leute doch maßlos. 

Also wer es noch nicht hat und einige Wochen Tag und Nacht durchzocken will ohne das es auch nur ansatzweise langweilige wird, der sollte das Spiel kaufen.

Ich bin bereits beim 5ten Mal Ich habe es normal schwer und extrem gespielt und mit dem richtigen Skill (ich meist mit Cyberdeck als Netrunner) aber auch jetzt zuletzt mit einem Sandevistan wird man schnell zu einem Gott der völlig OP ist meistens und dennoch immer wieder herausfordernde Bossgegner besiegen muss.

394个小时，我通关了《赛博朋克2077》。
这不是我第一款3A，甚至在发售前，我都没有过多期待只知道它出自波兰蠢驴。第一次打开这游戏，还是借别人的电脑，连账号都是朋友共享的。

谢谢朋友们，谢谢你们。

57个成就，断断续续，从2020年走到现在。
我很幸运，初次进入夜之城就没遇上什么严重的BUG，于是那些记忆，大多都是明亮的。
我也幸运地遇到了黑梦BUG那段全黑夹杂闪噪的体验，居然是限定版本的超强带入感玩法。

我还记得第一次见到杰克，觉得这大个子真不错。
直到雨夜，他将芯片递给我，生命随之流逝。那时我心里难过，却还未懂得什么叫失去。
后来几年，我在现实里工作、创业，和人周旋、计算。一次次重新打开游戏，重新开档，一次次回到那个时刻。
看着这个热血又粗糙的大个子，流着血，在最后一点光熄灭前，把未来托付给我。
他说：为了我，收下吧。
这一次，我终于感觉到了痛。


然后，强尼·银手出现了。
整个游戏流程，我都在防着他。我觉得他就是个自大、激进、讨人厌的2b，所以他说什么，我偏要反着来，就不给他抽烟。

可玩到最后，我竟然有点舍不得这个吊毛。
他有一种该死的真诚。
随着一次次重新开始，我对他越来越温柔，也渐渐看见他嚣张背后，那些不同的棱面。

我整个游戏过程真切地为V揪心。我如此迫切地想拯救他的生命，看着他挣扎、选择，替他回应每一句对话。
我手中的V，和现实中的我并不一样，他总是先为朋友付出。因此，他拥有了帕南与阿德卡多家族，拥有了家；他拯救了那个光头警察，他杀死了百灵鸟，也放走了百灵鸟；朱迪一同潜入水底，知晓了她的过往，也理解了她的离开。
还有老维、威尔斯太太、米斯蒂……还有那么多人。
我想在生命的最后的六个月，V依然是被爱包围着的。
我想救他，不仅是他有珍贵的梦想，也是因为这些朋友。

可那时，因为现实的原因，我没有充足的时间玩他。

几年间，我在工作与成长中，也逐渐看清自己性格里也有一团火。
所以再次打开2077，我忽然明白，自己或许真的被那个摇滚小子浸染了V与他，早已在意识中交织，共享着同一簇不灭的火。

无论是选择节制走向新人生的强尼，还是随奥特离去的强尼，
我都相信，我们还会再见。
我永远不会忘记他最后那句：

“再见了，V，永远不要放弃战斗。”

394个小时，57个成就，以及这个被夜之城改变了一部分的我。
我不会忘记他们。
在某个意义上，我就是V。

所以

永远不要放弃战斗，我。

[i][b]Almost no game cuts this deep.[/b][/i]
[i]If you’re the kind of player who lives for good storytelling, breathtaking atmosphere, diabolical combat mechanics, the freedom to craft insanely creative builds, and a city that feels painfully real, Cyberpunk 2077 will hit you harder than anything else on the market.[/i]

[hr][/hr]
Cyberpunk 2077 is, to me, one of the most influential, meaningful, and fruitful experiences I have ever played. This game will [i]never fade away[/i] from me or my life. There are many personal reasons behind why I speak about it with such certainty. It is by no means a perfect game, but it is perhaps the most soulful and emotionally hard-hitting game I have ever gone through.

Bogged down by negative reception and a myriad of bugs during its release and early months, I was there, I heard all of it. I decided to try the game anyway, through the ways of the pirates, and I was pleasantly surprised that the experience on my computer was decent. I’ve always had a habit of not trusting the general public’s narrative about anything, and no opinion or commentary convinces me until I experience it myself. By then, I was already captivated by its world, Night City, the characters, the atmosphere, everything. This genre has been my niche for some time, so I understand there may be bias involved.

Nevertheless, I’ve always felt this game never truly reached its potential. That’s a controversial statement, especially after all my praise, but here’s why: I believe CDPR had to shave off large portions of its original vision to cope with hardware limitations. In Phantom Liberty, we finally see them hold nothing back, and I can confidently say it is more engaging than the core game. But that itself is a strong compliment. Cyberpunk 2077’s core gameplay is what made me a fan of this franchise and genre in the first place, and Phantom Liberty felt like a letter to fans, old and new, enough to seal my trust in CDPR.

I bought the Ultimate Edition recently with my hard-earned money, and I believe that’s what you should get. Don’t miss a single crumb of it. It feels right to start my recommendation by praising what Cyberpunk is, instead of immediately comparing it. Still, I want to say this: no matter how many times I play any of the Grand Theft Auto games, GTA will always remain a sandbox for acting out your wildest “what ifs.” Everything GTA lacks exists here, and it’s done beautifully. Sure, Cyberpunk 2077 lacks several mechanics and milestones GTA established, but that never stopped me from preferring Cyberpunk over it and always will.

There’s a lot more I could say, but I’ll end it here. Buy this game. You will not regret it.

Cyberpunk 2077: A Masterpiece of Redemption


Note: I am writing this review after completing the game 100% with all achievements unlocked, playing on Version 2.1 at Level 60. This is based on the final, most complete experience of the game.

Cyberpunk 2077 wasn't just a game for me; it was an experience I lived through. It taught me valuable life lessons, and I truly connected with characters like V, Johnny, and Joshua. Through Panam, I experienced the true meaning of love and loyalty.

The game starts with an incredible hook, setting the pace and showing you exactly what it takes to become a "Legend of Night City." Our journey begins with Jackie Wells, a deeply lovable character whose impact resonates throughout the entire story.

The gameplay in this game was full of excitement and charm! The freedom to choose your build, the variety of cyberware, and the ability to upgrade your character according to your personal playstyle made it truly engaging and fun.

The side quests and side characters in this game are remarkably deep and thought-provoking. For instance, the personal quest of the killer, Joshua Stephenson, left a profound impact on me—it was so emotional that it actually moved me to tears. Then there’s Jefferson Peralez, a man unaware he’s being brainwashed, leaving his fate in our hands. Other standouts include Claire, driven by revenge for her husband, and Brendan, the AI whose sentience is tragically wiped by a "routine" update. These stories truly made me reflect on life.

Regarding the romances, the game features four main paths: Kerry, River, Panam, and Judy. River Ward’s detective arc involving the serial killer "Peter Pan" was gripping. However, my relationship with Panam Palmer was the highlight of the game for me—simply unforgettable. Judy and Kerry also had fascinating storylines.

As for the leads, V is a powerful and charismatic protagonist, and the "Deuteragonist" Johnny Silverhand—brought to life by Keanu Reeves—is absolutely phenomenal.

The open world felt truly alive to me. I loved the "reactivity"; if you helped someone during a Gig, you might run into them later at a bar. Hearing the citizens talk about their daily lives added a layer of immersion that kept me hooked on Night City.

The Phantom Liberty expansion is easily one of the best DLCs ever made. It’s a gripping spy-thriller set in Dogtown with two powerhouse characters: Songbird and Solomon Reed. Their story was incredibly moving and was perhaps my favorite part of the entire experience. Even Mr. Hands' Gigs felt more refined and narratively deep compared to other fixers.

When it comes to the endings, the game offers eight paths, all echoing the famous mantra: "There are no happy endings in Night City." I loved how the achievement system encourages you to experience every ending to see the full picture.

Completing 100% of the achievements was a joy. It didn't feel like a chore; it felt like living in Night City.
My only minor critique is that the main story felt a bit short. I wish it had been longer. However, the depth of the side quests and the DLC more than make up for it.

Final Verdict: Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the greatest games I’ve ever played and easily sits in my Top 10. It had a disappointing launch, but its redemption is nothing short of glorious.

My Ratings:
* Story: 9.5/10
* Engagement/Fun Factor: 10/10
* Protagonist: 9/10
* Deuteragonist (Johnny Silverhand): 10/10
* Side Characters: 9.5/10
* Gameplay: 9.5/10
* Open World: 9.3/10
* 100% Achievement Difficulty: 4/10
* Overall Score: 9.7/10

Cyberpunk 2077 
Hoje é praticamente outro jogo, e isso fica ainda mais claro quando você escolhe começar como Corpo, o caminho corporativo.

A sensação inicial já é totalmente diferente: você não nasce nas ruas, não vem da pobreza. Você começa lá em cima, dentro das máquinas frias da corporação, cercado de poder, ambição e aquela arrogância elegante típica de Night City. É um começo que combina política, traição e aquele clima de escritório futurista onde todo mundo sorri enquanto te apunhala pelas costas.

Você tentou jogar no lançamento e, sinceramente, naquela época era difícil gostar: bugs, quedas de FPS, performance quebrada demais. Mas agora? O jogo foi praticamente reconstruído. Muitas falhas sumiram, a otimização melhorou e dá até prazer ver a cidade brilhar sem travar.

O que mais impressiona é como a história funciona bem para o Corpo. V tem um passado pesado, cheio de escolhas que deixam marcas na personalidade. O roteiro é mais afiado, mais dramático, mais humano. A narrativa faz você sentir que está sempre no limite entre controle e colapso — perfeito para alguém que já viu o poder por dentro.

E os gráficos, hoje, são outro nível. Night City fica absurdamente viva. As luzes de neon, a chuva no asfalto, os reflexos… tudo cria um clima que não existe em nenhum outro jogo. É aquele tipo de estética que dá satisfação só de caminhar pela cidade.

Resumindo a você, cara interlocutor:
Depois de tantos ajustes, Cyberpunk 2077 finalmente entrega aquilo que prometeu. Um universo denso, estiloso e imersivo. Uma história que prende. E um visual que realmente deixa você feliz de estar ali dentro. É quase como se o jogo tivesse renascido — e, dessa vez, vale cada minuto.

I played this game on PC.
I held off so long on playing this game because of it's sloppy launch, I remember it too well, it was so bad that it had to be taken off stores and refunded to customers. Few games, even bad ones, achieve that kind of failure, but Cyberpunk did, one of the most highly anticipated games at the time, but as years passed, I heard updates had been pushed, glitches fixed and even people celebrating the game's newfound success. Especially once the anime released to critical acclaim, I finally caved and purchased it so I could experience it for myself.
One thing should be clear, Cyberpunk 2077 is still unfortunately quite buggy, animations break, T-Poses randomly occur and NPCs lips arent synced way too often, at least for my playthrough. It took barely 10 minutes to get my first major glitch and it was not reassuring, but from what I can tell, the game has come a long way. Between the occasional glitch is a fine game with an exciting story and equally incredible world. Night City is beautiful and this universe created by Mike Pondsmith is nothing short of impressive. The story is so enticing with the "ghost" of Johnny Silverhand corrupting your mind, maybe you'll become enemies, maybe you'll become friends. It's an anti-capitalist epic that I can honestly say deserves it's praise. The RPG elements are expertly implemented and feel very approachable and easy to comprehend. This isn't GTA, but if thats what youre looking for, I dont think youll be disappointed. I cant wait for whats next in this franchise. 8.5/10

This is the best open world game ever. Period. (yes, I have played RDR2 and GTA5, but the range of things you can do in CP2077 far exceeds that in those games. (RDR2 has its own charm with realistic immersion though)
CP2077 is more than just a game, it is an experience. I keep coming back to Night city to do some random gig and explore something new. You could spend hundreds of hours customising your character, trying out different builds (cyberware, perks, weapons, etc) but what really fascinates me about this game is its immersive storyline and lore - While the initial lifepath (i.e. your character's backstory - nomad/street kid/corpo) does not seem to affect the story much, every choice you do make has a consequence and you wouldn't realise it until much later. Definitely do try out the different endings. Also, there's tons of mods to make graphic upgrades/gameplay changes/new or alternative missions/cool customisations for your character and companions.

Highly recommend getting it with the Phantom Liberty DLC - especially if on sale. I got both at full price and do not regret it one bit now. Yes, initially the game was broken/had weird bugs, but the devs have clearly made an effort to turn it around into a smooth and polished game. It has some jankiness, but its fun to watch when something weird happens now.

Cyberpunk 2077 is one of the rare games that’s truly worth every cent.

Cyberpunk 2077 — это уже легенда.

Не игра, а полноценный культурный феномен. Пройти мимо неё было невозможно, и мой путь в Найт-Сити — лучшее тому доказательство.

Это одна из тех редких игр, которая врезается в память навсегда. Неистовый дух Найт-Сити, его неоновая меланхолия, истории живущих на краю людей — Ви, Джонни, Джуди, Панам... Это не просто сюжет, это пережитый опыт. Каждый перепроход открывал новые детали, пласты скрытого смысла и альтернативные пути. Игру хочется исследовать до дна, и она щедро награждает за это.

Моё знакомство с миром началось... скажем так, в эпоху большого хаоса на релизе. Я прошел игру вдоль и поперек, видя все её трансформации — от сырого алмаза до огранённого бриллианта после патчей и дополнения «Фантомная свобода». Я вложил в Найт-Сити сотни часов, прожил десятки жизней, и мне стало понятно: столько эмоций, труда и страсти команды CD Projekt RED обязано быть оплачено.

Juegardo. No se como fue cuando salio, lo jugue en 2024 y es de lo mejor que hay en este estilo de juego.

Las secundarias y la construccion del mundo no se acercan al Witcher 3, pero esta por encima de todo lo demas del mercado, es un mundo vivo con lore por todos lados.

La jugabilidad, muy dinamica para un RPG en 1era persona, mucha posibilidad con los estilos de juego y las builds que te puedes armar. En lo personal jugue netrunner, y creo que esta totalmente roto, la mision final lo hice solo en muy dificil y casi que no gaste balas. Muy roto el netrunner, creo que equivaldria a un mago en un soulslike.

Musica, meh, tiene sus temaikenes pero no creo que sea lo destacado. Acompaña bien cuando te agarras a los tiros, pero fuera de eso yo viajo con la radio apagada.

Personajes: perdon, PERSONAJES. No destaca tanto en la construccion de cada personaje individualmente, sino la contruccion que se le da a la relacion de V con cada personaje. Una alternativa a lo comun en este genero. Aca no crecen los personajes, crecen las relaciones con el protagonista. Para mi una maravilla como se aborda.

En resumen, te gustan los rpg en 1era persona? top 3 en el genero; te gustan los mundos abiertos para perderte en las calles y rutas? este juego es para vos (paseito en el caliburn, piloto automatico, un lujo); te gusta agarrarte a tiros y andar volando por los aires? compra y no lo pienses mas.

Город - просто сумасшедший. Ночной ДатоСити живёт своей жизнью: неон, реклама, мусорные переулки, небоскрёбы корпораций - всё выглядит настолько атмосферно, что иногда просто садился на мотоцикл и катался без цели, слушая радио и смотря на закаты над городом.
Сюжет и персонажи - отдельный кайф. Основная линия цепляет, а многие побочные квесты сделаны на уровне отдельных мини-историй, которые запоминаются не хуже главного сюжета. Некоторые выборы реально заставляли задуматься, а концовка(и) оставили послевкусие ещё на несколько дней.
Боевка и прокачка тоже порадовали: можно играть по-разному - вломиться в лоб с дробовиками, тихо взламывать всех через кибердек или делать что-то среднее. Оружие ощущается приятно, ближний бой тоже не заброшен, а импланты позволяют собрать свой уникальный билд.
Да, у игры была сложная история на старте, но сейчас это уже совершенно другой уровень. Видно, что проект довели до ума, и ты просто получаешь удовольствие от мира и истории, а не борешься с багами.
Итог: мощная атмосфера, сильный сюжет, запоминающиеся персонажи и один из самых проработанных городов в играх. Night City однозначно стоит того, чтобы в него вернуться и потеряться там ещё не на один десяток часов. Рекомендую 🌃✨

You remember the hype for this game, right? They announced it back when dinosaurs were still filling out job applications. By the time it actually came out, my toaster had more processing power than the original consoles it launched on. They promised a revolutionary future, a living breathing world, meaningful choices, next-gen immersion, advanced AI, deep role-playing… and what I got was a radioactive dumpster fire wrapped in LED lights and marketed as art.

This thing was delayed so many times I thought it needed a therapist, a life coach, and a priest. They built it up like it was gonna cure depression, fix the economy, and make your dad finally come back with the milk. Instead, it showed up stuttering, glitching, naked from the waist down, and asking for 60 dollars plus tax.

You boot up the game and the first thing it does is look at your console and go, “Good luck.” The frame rate drops so hard it looks like a PowerPoint presentation made by someone having a stroke. Characters are popping in and out of existence like ghosts on a day pass from the afterlife. Half the NPCs don’t have faces. The other half have the same face copy-pasted like some cursed clone army made by a drunk intern.

You walk down the street and it’s supposed to be this bustling futuristic city, but half the people are walking straight into walls like their brains are powered by expired batteries. Some of them are squatting in mid-air. Some are T-posing like they’re asserting dominance on the laws of physics. I saw a guy having a conversation with a vending machine and honestly, he was the sanest character in the entire game.

The police system? Oh my god. You steal a candy bar and suddenly a cop teleports right behind you like a perverted guardian angel. No chase, no logic, no warning, they just materialize out of nowhere like you summoned the Wizard of Law Enforcement. You could be on top of a building, floating in space, inside a locked bathroom stall, and the cops will still appear behind you like “Hello there, criminal.” What is this, Cyberpunk or a jumpscare simulator?

Driving is a circus act. The cars handle like you’re trying to steer a drunk cow on an ice rink covered in butter. You tap the wheel and suddenly you’re spinning like a malfunctioning Beyblade straight into a hotdog stand, five pedestrians, and the last bit of hope you had left. The car physics make Mario Kart feel like a military driving simulator. This isn’t driving, it’s a scientific experiment in suffering.

And the bugs. Cars falling from the sky. Characters clipping into walls. Guns flying out of your hands like they gained free will. NPCs standing on chairs, in chairs, becoming chairs. I saw a dude T-posing while sitting down, which shouldn’t even be possible unless the universe itself hit Alt+F4.

The dialogue plays from characters whose mouths aren’t moving. Voices are coming from behind you while the person is in front of you making unblinking eye contact like a cursed department store mannequin. Relationships trigger out of nowhere. Quests break. Missions lock themselves. The game doesn’t just have bugs, it has a thriving ecosystem, complete with a food chain and regional variants.

The launch was so bad that even Sony said, “No.” That’s like a dumpster telling you that you’re too gross to be thrown in it. This wasn’t a game launch. This was a digital crime scene. This thing should’ve shipped with police tape and a therapist.

It wasn’t “Press X to start,” it was “Press X to lower expectations.”

And the marketing, oh the marketing. They sold it like a futuristic paradise. What we got was a broken funhouse run by malfunctioning robots on their last AAA batteries.

But then, after years of patches, updates, fixes, and probably some dark ritual performed under a full moon, the game actually became good. Now it runs well. Now the world feels alive. Now the characters hit harder. Now the story is solid. Now it’s actually what was promised.

But that doesn’t erase the fact that at launch this thing was about as useful as a screen door on a submarine.

You don’t get a medal for fixing the house after you already burned it down and charged people for the ashes.

At launch, Cyberpunk 2077 wasn’t an RPG. It wasn’t an action game. It wasn’t even software. It was a glitch museum that you paid to walk through.

Now it’s a great game. Then it was a digital insult, a technological prank, a betrayal compressed into an executable file.

Cyberpunk 2077: from absolute disaster to genuine masterpiece, but it took years, and the emotional stability of half the gaming population, to get there.

It wasn’t just broken. It was bugged to hell, back to hell, then trapped in an infinite loading screen while your console cried for mercy.

Да некоторые достижения получаются путём вылизывания карты до блеска , но я начал делать подобные ачивки с Уестбрука , потом прошёлся по центру и так далее постоянно увеличивая размер зачищения локаций . Нравилось ли мне это делать ? Ну вряд ли , но ачивки того стоили . Что качается самой приятной части игры , а именно сюжета : вкусно , но мало . Всего 15~18 часов чистого сюжета без побочки и особого фарма . Но благодаря побочным квестам сюжет и раскрывается , ведь именно они влияют на конец игры , что круто . В целом , сюжет киберпанка просто офигенный  , блестящая история и такая же блестящая реализация , мне очень понравилось . В ведьмаке 3 , были квесты , по типу собирания игральных карт , здесь есть подобное , но не надо искать гайды в инете , чтобы их найти , достаточно просто на карте включить спец указатель и всё , иди собирай , радуйся , лутай ачивку и тд. ( к слову я на другом аккаунте , где у меня ведьмак , так до сих пор и не получил ачивку за карты по Гвинту ). Графика данного шедевра просто зашкаливает , помню был случай , когда играл в неё часов 5 подряд , сделал перерыв , лёг на кровать , зашёл в ютуб с телефона и на первый попавшийся шортс подумал , что это момент из киберпанка , а там просто чел паркурил по зданиям покрашенным в такие же желтые , голубые  , зеленые цвета ( короче  , графика - круть) . Теперь поговорим о нашем напарнике , который является неотъемлемой частью сюжета ( Внимание дальше спойлеры! ) 
Наш напарник - Джонни Сильверхэнд , мне кажется это один из лучших напарников вообще за всю историю игроделания . Данный экземпляр тебя и разозлит ,  и преободрит ,и развеселит , и на**й пошлёт , в общем настоящий кент . Да и в целом Джонни как персонаж намного больше раскрыт чем Ви . Ви это просто рандомный чумба , которому уж так не повезло в жизни , что он умирает . А Джонни не просто хрен с улицы , он рок звезда , мятежник и настоящий террорист , у которого не получилось . Я считаю , что роль Джонни у Киану можно смело сравнивать с ролями Уика или Нео , ведь везде Ривз играет на совесть . 
Джонни Сильверхрена разобрали , теперь что касается вообще рискованной идеи от СД связанной с видом от первого лица , я считаю , что это было правильное решение , но полное отсутствие 3 лица персонажа ( кроме транспорта ) это уже не очень. Но это пожалуй почти единственное до чего можно докопаться . 
Баги - *барабанная дробь* ихххх... есть , да баги есть , но их мало, те что есть они никак не ломают игру  , а иногда делают её забавной . Например , в одном квесте пробегаю я по комнате полной противников , расстреливаю их всех , захожу в лифт и каким-то образом за мной заходит противник , я его убиваю и он ( так как я опускаюсь вниз на лифте ) поднимается вверх и застревает сверху . Или уже в дополнении , когда я зашёл в церковь и прошёл к стойке , я увидел чумбу , парящего в воздухе , там рядом была коробка или стол и я думаю он должен был быть по идеи на этом предмете , но чумба решил полетать в церкви ( это было очень угарно ) . 
Кстати , что касается дополнения - оно офигенно , просто нет слов , русских слов , а английских там навалом . Жаль конечно , что нет русской локализации , но мне , как человеку проходившему рдр 2 и не один раз это не помешало , было даже прикольно вслушиваться в слова персонажей и проверять текстовый перевод на некоторые неточности . Сама локация длс маленькая по размеру локации , но захватывающая с головой . Сюжет длс на равне с сюжетом основной игры ( кста по продолжатель он не сильно и меньше ) есть новые механики  и в общем это именно то длс , которое можно представить в данной игре .

Игра затянула и сейчас у меня ощущение , что хочется ещё , а нет , все 57 ачивок собраны , все концовки пройдены , осталась парочка доп заданий , которые ничуть не привлекают . Every quest has two or five ways it can end, the characters feel human and morally complex with how they act, how they react, their backgrounds, and branch into your story that makes them more than a side quest. The voice actors did phenomenal jobs conveying personality and emotion, more so than any other game I can think of that I’ve played in the past three years. You will sympathize with them, empathize, and relate to these npcs who feel like fully realized people, and with Johnny, especially Johnny, how he constantly challenges you and comments on your decisions, and opens up is such a surreal and oddly natural experience, especially with how some of them show their character growth. 
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3590308079 
Moving on to Night City itself, I adored it. It’s loud, it’s futuristic, and it’s as beautiful as it is rotten with all its trash spilling out from between buildings and overflowing garbage bins. Also, somehow, it’s completely walkable with a WORKING public transportation system, an honest to god metro transit I spent way too much time in. (I’ve never personally lived in a state where it was possible to Not Own A Car.) and I adored its towering buildings and districted areas. It’s absolutely such a treat, you can find a ton of food stalls, shops, places where npcs linger around, bits of environmental storytelling like homeless camps, crime scenes, crashed cars with data messages, a guy who died via vending machine, religious groups doing public speeches. You never know when you’re gonna get pulled into a side quest or what you find exploring random forgotten corners.
https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3615855273 
It's weird that I’ve gotten this far without talking about how much I hated Cyberpunk the first 50 or so hours I played it. I love RPGs, I love happy endings, but Cyberpunk is genuinely and truly a game about compromises, lose-lose situations, and letting you pick what bittersweet poison you will drink next. NPCs will meet or choose terrible fates without you being able to do a single thing about it, and you have to accept it. Night City is legitimately a terrible place to live and it shows that in every questline. Some quests are timed, and the game doesn’t tell you, and there were a few times I felt like I was actively being punished for exploring the open world instead of following the storyline. NPCs will call you, they will ask for help, and despite best efforts, quest lines pile up and can get seriously complicated if you don’t resolve them and let them linger. How you spend your time in Night City is almost as important as exploring it – this is a warning. It took me a long time to appreciate the value of a story without a happy ending, but in the end, I’m really glad I strayed out of my comfort zone and stuck with it.

Update: I’ve decided that I cannot finish this game. In the later half of the game every mission seems to boil down to “follow NPC, wait for NPC”. The characters are insufferable and the writing is cliche ridden. The ham fisted attempts at trying to be deep, or topical, or comment on true social issues is mind numbing. The world, the writing, the characters, the philosophy all seem like they were ripped from the pages of a 14 year olds diary.

I played Cyberpunk 2077 on a Legion Go S, and it performed better than I expected. I am not real a fan of cyberpunk as a genre; the aesthetic rarely appeals to me. The fetishization of Japanese culture, the machismo, and the overtly sexualized presentation of the world have always felt odd, and I am not entirely sure who this specific brand of sci-fi is meant to click with.

That said, the game’s dialogue is often intriguing. The main plot is a fairly straightforward mix of espionage and revenge, but thankfully it avoids drowning itself in unnecessary world-building or heavy-handed exposition. The narrative moves along cleanly, and the writing is stronger than I anticipated.

Character progression is varied, and I can see the potential for many interesting builds. But, with only one meaningful respec opportunity, experimenting feels limited. While Incan see some builds that would definitely be worth trying, the overall experience doesn’t really justify a full second playthrough.

There are plenty of side missions and characters to interact with, but they ultimately feel hollow. This is a broader issue I have with open-world design: the main story is framed as urgent and consequential, yet the world asks you to take detours into activities that feel tonally disconnected like lecturing a police officer about mental health or joining a shooting competition without any narrative weight.

I suppose I would recommend it. It’s a fair game. I don’t regret playing it, but I probably won’t feel compelled to return for another go ‘round.

Как изменится эмуляция вашего сознания, от 8 часовой подачи тяжелых веществ? Вопросы идиотские, а по игре есть что сказать? 
Основной сюжет отличный, но сам мир показан слабовато. Игра вне строго заскриптованных квестов быстро становится абсолютно пластиковой. Второстепенные задания косвенно затрагивают интересные идеи которые уникальны для сэттинга киберпанка, и тут же отшучиваются: "Ой блин, бывшая девушка захромировалась и хочет меня убить.", "Ой блин! Мои гениталии закоротили, отвези меня к доктору!". Игра специально сводит данные проблемы в шутку. В самом сюжете отлично всё, дорогие локации, музыка, модели, постановка, часто, кроме самого сценария. А ещё там куча алкоголя, веществ, сисек и мата, йоооу мама я такой взрослый уже, я реально панк!!! 
Разработчики взяли в цель массовость а не глубину, не мрак а юмор, не идеи а пафос.

Геймплей в целом понравился, бой реализован отлично, множество разных возможностей повеселиться, стелс, касты, сама стрельба достаточно приятная, особенно приятно когда не стреляешь по хп в коротких сценах с Сильверхендом. 
Вне боя и сюжета - вообще забей. Свободное перемещение это смазанные маслом покрышки на машинах, на спидометре 100 миль в час, ощущаются дай бог как 40 км в час. Перемещение вне транспорта быстро превращается в спам двойного прыжка и дэша, что ощущается приятно и одновременно максимально выбивает из погружения в игру. Зачистка карты которая заставляет тебя всё больше и больше обращать внимание на пластиковость и плоскость мира и нивелирует дороговизну сюжетных сцен и полученного погружения. Сам город прекрасный, в котором сделаны переходы, вторые этажи, выступы, трубы, но они не были созданы для игрока, местами забраться туда можно и ощущалось это приятно, хоть и немного сломано.  
Видно где у ребят закончились сроки и деньги, видно что на мир денег не хватило и это не починить никакими патчами. В игре явно не хватает кор-функционала для нпс, для противников и приятной физики машин. Чем больше углубляешься тем больше видишь этот огромный, потерянный потенциал, который где-то там утонул в адской истории разработки данного проекта. 

Крч, сюжет классный, дорогущий, проработанный, дофаминовый, но достаточно поверхностный, массовый. Побочные задания ещё более массовые, может быть я где-то и пропустил бриллиант, но сил моих нет. Вне сюжета, порой играющий альбомы The Uncanny Valley/I Am The Night и воспоминания про просмотренный киберпанк до этого, заставляли меня чувствовать интерес к геймплею больше чем это делала сама игра.

Cyberpunk 2077 is most certainly a contender for my top five games of all time, easily. Now i wasnt someone who was following the development cycle of this game before it was released. but i did pre order and i was excited to get my hands on it and see what it was all about, as it peaked my interest for sure with its themes alone. now when cyberpunk released i had a really good computer for that time, so i got a near glitchless, bugless first experience. I know this was not the case for many people, and i wont excuse the game being pushed out faster then it shouldve been. I truly think they shouldve held off on releasing the game and i hope they learned their lesson and wont do that again. but now that a lot of time has passed, weve gotten lots of updates and content drops for free, and a great paid dlc with a whole new story basically. This leaves cyberpunk in a great spot and i think anyone who hasnt given this game a shot because of that bad launch, should absolutely play this game now. we know they are going to make a sequel and they are producing another season of the cyberpunk show. theres a lot to look forward to here. Cyberpunk also features insane graphics, they are pushing the industry to its full potential. especially with mods, i have quickly glanced at screenshots from this game sometimes and thought it was real life photos. also the music in this game is so amazing. they have produced so much music that fits the setting of this world its incredible. just driving around with the radio on, passing by crowded parks of people and tall as the eye can see skyscrapers is so immersive. you can really get lost in this game with its visuals and audio . i love how the music in this game supplements the visuals of night city so well. theres songs in all sorts of different genres that help add some real depth into this crazy universe. it really helps with the world building when the music compliments the visuals the way they do in cyberpunk. a cold dark night, police lockdowns, psychos going crazy, gangs in military level wars over turf. super soldier like police forces fighting back. its dark and really embodies that dystopian feeling the game set out to showcase. the environments really help paint the picture of a decaying social norms. it blends these themes of oppression and hopelessness, depression and pervasion.  And with Cyberpunk being an open world, first person shooter RPG, there is so much you can do build wise. so many different ways to play and complete the tasks you set out to achieve. I think this game will easily be one of those games we all back at in ten years and really appreciate what this game is. Games like this are becoming increasingly rare and hard to come by.

Cyberpunk 2077 is the game that’s practically drowning in character work. The writing is messy, human, morally grey in all the ways good sci-fi should be. It doesn’t give you the traditional “good hero versus evil villain” setup other games cling to. Everyone is compromised, everyone’s broken, and that’s exactly what makes Night City feel alive instead of like another power-fantasy sandbox.
It scratches the same itch as Blade Runner: neon, rain, and an existential crisis simmering under every conversation. You’re not saving the world-you’re navigating it, and it pushes back.
And the DLC? That ending absolutely wrecked me. Phantom Liberty sticks the landing with an emotional punch you don’t see coming. I didn’t expect to get attached to Johnny the way I did, but there I was, ugly-crying.
The game isn't built for people who wants black-and-white storytelling. It’s built for people who can sit with the grey and still call it beautiful.

Oubliez tout ce que vous avez entendu sur la sortie en 2020. Aujourd'hui, Cyberpunk 2077 est le RPG d'action ultime. Night City n'est pas juste une carte, c'est un personnage à part entière.

Cocher la case appropriée :

☐ Public : ☐ Les enfants ☑ Les ados ☑ Les adultes (C'est mature, sombre et viscéral) ☐ Tout le monde

☐ Graphismes : ☐ Pixel art ☐ Acceptables ☐ Beaux ☑ Le nouveau standard de l'industrie (Surtout avec le Path Tracing, c'est une démo technologique jouable)

☐ Histoire : ☐ Oubliable ☐ Sympa ☐ Très bonne ☑ Incroyable (L'écriture est phénoménale, vos choix comptent, et la fin vous marquera)

☐ Bande-son : ☐ Aucune ☐ Générique ☑ Bonne ☑ Masterclass (La radio, les musiques de combat, Samurai... tout est parfait)

☐ Gameplay : ☐ Ennuyeux ☐ Répétitif ☑ Fun ☑ Jouissif (Que vous jouiez Katana/Sandevistan, Netrunner ou Bourrin au fusil à pompe, tout fonctionne)

☐ Bugs : ☐ Injouable ☐ Beaucoup ☑ Quelques-uns (Comme dans tout open world massif) ☐ Aucun

Points forts :

Night City est la ville la plus immersive jamais créée.

Les personnages (Judy, Panam, Johnny Silverhand) sont inoubliables.

Le système de combat refait (2.1) est ultra dynamique.

L'extension Phantom Liberty est un indispensable.

Points faibles :

Une fois fini, on ressent un grand vide.

Il faut un bon PC pour en profiter à fond (RTX on).

Conclusion : Ce jeu est une expérience. Il vous happe, vous brise le cœur et vous laisse en redemander. Un chef-d'œuvre absolu de la science-fiction. Réveillez-vous, Samouraï.

Night City es, sin exagerar, una de las ciudades más vivas y detalladas que vi en un videojuego. Cada calle, cada rincón, cada personaje tiene vida propia. Te perdés caminando, escuchando conversaciones, mirando luces de neón… y cuando la historia te agarra, no te suelta más.

La trama principal es atrapante, llena de momentos intensos y personajes memorables —V y Johnny Silverhand se te quedan grabados. Las misiones secundarias, lejos de ser “relleno”, tienen historias profundas y humanas que te hacen sentir parte de ese mundo.

El apartado visual, la música y la ambientación son una locura. Todo transmite ese espíritu cyberpunk: rebelde, melancólico y lleno de estilo.

Después de todas las mejoras y expansiones, Cyberpunk 2077 es exactamente lo que prometía ser: una experiencia inmersiva, emotiva y visualmente impresionante.

Cyberpunk 2077 has been one of the most memorable gaming experiences for me in recent years. It is not just a game, but a complete immersion into the world of the future, where style, atmosphere, and drama merge into one. After completing it, I can confidently say that it is one of the best games I have ever played.

The main character, V, quickly evokes an emotional connection: customisation and variability of choices make her journey unique. Her development — from a mercenary to a key figure in the events of Night City — is presented so convincingly that you start to genuinely root for her.

Johnny Silverhand is another strong point of the game. Keanu Reeves' charisma adds depth to the character: rebellious, cynical, but with a human core. His tense and emotional relationship with V creates one of the best duos I've encountered in games.

The gameplay offers considerable variety: levelling up, abilities and cyber implants allow you to create your own style — from a quiet netrunner to an aggressive cyber ninja. This blends perfectly with the lively, atmospheric open world.

Night City impresses with its detail and atmosphere. Just driving through the streets is a pleasure, and the soundtrack makes you want to catch the rhythm of every scene. Some tracks you'll want to listen to even outside of the game.

The main story is a dynamic and deep journey where choices really matter. But even the side quests often shine just as brightly: strong characters and emotional mini-dramas make them unforgettable.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a unique experience where everything works in unison: the plot, the world, the characters, the music, and the gameplay. The game leaves you with vivid emotions and a strong desire to return to Night City again. I definitely recommend it to anyone looking for something stylish, deep, and captivating.

The number of traffic jams that just happen is ridiculous when the city streets are mostly empty but then suddenly traffic jam and good luck trying to get your vehicle around cars just sitting there. Missions are basically go here, talk to that guy, go over there, do something. [h1][b]Cyberpunk 2077: Não acredito em finais felizes.[/b][/h1]

[h1]Visão Geral:[/h1]
Booooom dia, Night City... Acreditava que esse jogo era uma bomba pelo começo caótico que teve no lançamento, mas atualmente isso está longe de ser verdade. Explorar a cidade que nunca dorme e ouvir a história de cada personagem traz a mesma sensação de jogar Skyrim em 2015. Cada side quest é interessante e andar pela cidade é fascinante. É um dos poucos jogos que facilmente entrou no meu Top 3.

[h1]Exploração e Mundo:[/h1]
O que dizer de [b]Night City[/b]? A grande cidade que é palco da nossa vida, uma cidade que promete fama e dinheiro, algo que atrai muitos dispostos a arriscar tudo para alcançar o topo. Porém, uma das coisas que aprendi nesse lugar é que finais felizes não existem por aqui. Bem, o que poderíamos esperar de um lugar controlado por corporações corruptas, diversas gangues super violentas e sonhos não realizados?

A construção de mundo desse jogo é incrível. Desde o primeiro passo dentro do coração da grande cidade, você se encanta (ou desespera) com a visão que tem: prédios gigantescos por causa da concentração da população, diversas propagandas chamativas em quase todo lugar que olha e, claro, também vemos a parte ruim, desde as gangues com diversas modificações corporais até o lixeiro que são as zonas mais pobres da cidade. Uma construção Cyberpunk muito bem feita e moldada, visualmente impecável.

A essência da exploração segue a fórmula básica, muito similar aos RPGs da [b]Bethesda[/b]. Temos um mundo aberto e livre para explorar, literalmente podendo ir para quase qualquer lugar que queira. Junto a isso temos a missão principal, que é uma boa ideia ignorar até ter feito outras coisas, e as muitas missões secundárias, que são muito ricas de conteúdo e história, muitas delas me fazem refletir até hoje. Junto a isso, temos itens raros espalhados pelo mapa e alguns colecionáveis.

A sensação é parecida com Skyrim: um mundo com um milhão de missões secundárias que te fazem facilmente esquecer a principal, e que você nem sabe onde foi que pegou ou quem te mandou, mas essa é a diversão. Essa parte do jogo não te prender a nada possibilita uma [b]rejogabilidade[/b] interessante, podendo seguir a mesma ideia de começar um novo save, ir para onde quiser e construir a build que tiver interesse, focando apenas nas missões que deseja.

Junto a tudo isso, temos as sub-regiões dentro de Night City. Umas mais pobres, outras mais ricas, mas o interessante mesmo é a mudança visual entre elas, os fornecedores de missões ([b]Canais[/b]) que têm personalidade diferente em cada local e, obviamente, a gangue diferente que comanda aquela parte da cidade. Lembre-se de atirar em todos os [b]Rapineiros[/b] que passarem pela sua tela.

[h1]Sistema e Progressão:[/h1]
Existem vários pontos de variação de mecânica aqui, sendo a principal delas o [b]Cromo[/b], a alma desse universo em partes. Estamos falando das modificações corporais: trocar o braço simples de carne e osso por uma [b]Lâmina Louva-a-Deus[/b] que corta inimigo igual papel é uma coisa sensacional. No geral, podemos equipar vários implantes cibernéticos no nosso personagem, cada um com seu buff extra, passiva específica e às vezes habilidades ativas, porém temos um limite do quanto podemos equipar (podemos evoluir isso com nível e outros itens, além de uma passiva roubada que aumenta muito o seu limite).

Outra evolução passiva que temos é a árvore de habilidades. No jogo temos 5 árvores, cada uma vindo de um atributo e focada em um estilo de gameplay diferente, desde bônus de danos de armas específicas (SMG, pistolas, snipers...) até coisas mais específicas como habilidades atreladas a hacking ([b]Trilha-Rede[/b]) ou pulos extras para ataques pesados, etc.

Falando em armas, creio que tenha uma variedade boa, principalmente de [b]armas icônicas[/b], que geralmente só podem ser pegas em momentos específicos e têm algo de especial nelas. Mas isso ainda não tira o brilho das armas normais, que podem ser equipadas a bel-prazer, com miras ou itens de upgrade com bônus. Algo extra que gostei são as [b]armas inteligentes[/b]: armas que geralmente são menos fortes em questão de dano, mas têm tiros teleguiados (joguei bastante com elas usando builds de Trilha-Rede).

No geral é um RPG que dá para se divertir bastante variando as builds e armas, principalmente se focar em algo específico. É possível criar um save novo e ir direto para as missões que vão dar os itens da build que deseja seguir, sem enrolação e com facilidade.

[h1]Enredo:[/h1]
A verdadeira parte onde esse jogo brilha. É incrível como esse jogo conseguiu me cativar desde o começo, com as três rotas que você pode escolher (Nômade, Marginal ou Corporativo), a parte onde realmente viramos um mercenário tentando virar uma lenda junto ao nosso parceiro, até o momento que você termina o prólogo e entende que não existe final feliz aqui.

O que mais me encantou, na verdade, foram as [b]missões secundárias[/b]. Achava que seriam sem graça e chatas, mas nunca estive tão errado na minha vida. Muitas delas são incríveis, com história envolvente e com personagens cheios de carisma, até hoje não esqueço do CyberPsicopatas que só queria salvar a filha das garras dos Garra de Tigre.

Estou evitando dar spoiler, mas algo muito presente também (e que repeti algumas vezes acima) é que essa cidade realmente quer te devorar. A realidade é simplesmente assombrosa: toda missão tu vês alguém tentando vencer e perdendo de forma miserável, sonhos sendo destruídos e algumas poucas vitórias. Essa temática mais sombria e a falta de esperança deixam o jogo mais sério, com mais peso e senso de realidade.

[h1]Conclusão:[/h1]
[quote]"É impossível vencer em Night City"[/quote]

Viver como um mercenário em Night City é uma experiência muito agradável em questão de gameplay e muito triste em questão de história. Temos um mundo aberto livre para explorar e fazermos as missões que queremos e quando queremos, junto à variedade de armas (algumas icônicas são incríveis e com lore), além dos mil implantes cibernéticos para virarmos uma máquina de guerra.

Por outro lado, a história só me deixou feliz umas três vezes. Que mundo cruel é esse, kk. O jogo tem o prazer de te mostrar a realidade sombria de onde você vive e como tudo funciona: todas as lendas estão mortas e você não é especial.

Se o tema lhe agrada, gosta de RPG e quer algo mais sério em questão de história, não pense duas vezes: espere uma promoção e compre isso junto à DLC [b]Phantom Liberty[/b]. Tente salvar a Songbird.

[quote]"Um final feliz? Não nesta cidade, não para pessoas como nós."[/quote]

Review: The Redemption Arc is Real – Night City in 2025 is a Masterpiece

If you've been holding off on Cyberpunk 2077 because of the launch horror stories from years ago, stop waiting. In 2025, this isn't just a "fixed" game; it is genuinely one of the most immersive, emotionally resonant open-world RPGs ever made on PC.

THE REDEMPTION
CD Projekt Red didn't just patch the bugs; they rebuilt the game's skeleton. The 2.0 overhaul changed everything, but the subsequent updates (2.1 and the recent 2.2) added the soul that was missing. Riding the NCART metro system while listening to the portable radio, customizing vehicle paint jobs on the fly with CrystalCoat, or just having Johnny spontaneously hop in the passenger seat during a long drive makes Night City feel alive in a way it never did before.

PHANTOM LIBERTY (THE EXPANSION)
Phantom Liberty isn't just "DLC"; it's a tight, paranoid spy thriller that fits perfectly into the middle of the main story. Dogtown is dense, vertical, and absolutely dripping with atmosphere. The narrative shifts from the base game's "fight for survival" to a complex web of espionage, loyalty, and betrayal.

Without spoiling anything: Idris Elba (Solomon Reed) and the character Songbird deliver performances that rival cinema. As someone who values narrative depth, the choices here are agonizing. There are no "good" outcomes, only choices you have to live with—which feels perfectly cyberpunk.

GAMEPLAY & BUILD DIVERSITY
The new skill tree (introduced in 2.0 and refined since) finally lets you roleplay effectively.

Want to be a cyber-ninja deflecting bullets with a katana? You can.

Want to be a Netrunner god who causes cars to explode with a glance? You can.

The vehicle combat is actually fun now, and the police system finally punishes you logically rather than spawning cops behind your back.

PC PERFORMANCE & VISUALS
On a modern rig, this is the visual benchmark for the decade. Path Tracing (overdrive mode) transforms the city into something photorealistic. The neon reflections in puddles, the steam rising from vents, the way light diffuses through fog—it’s breathtaking. Performance is stable now, and the glitches are virtually nonexistent compared to launch.

THE VERDICT
Cyberpunk 2077 in 2025 is the game we were promised, and then some. It’s a tragic, beautiful, adrenaline-fueled experience that will leave you staring at the credits feeling completely empty (in the best way possible).

10/10 - A preem experience. See you in the major leagues, choom.

In October of 2012 a trailer dropped, CD Projekt Red were going to do Cyberpunk 2077. What followed in January 2013 was a video of Mike Pondsmith, the author of the Cyberpunk pen and paper RPG, regaling us with his vision of his setting, thus starting the hype for one of the most anticipated games in the following years. The game released in December of 2020, but 8 years of expectations met a cold harsh reality, not unlike that of Night City.

So where does the game stand 5 years later post release, after numerous larger updates and a full DLC? Is it worth your time to play through it?

Yes, but with several caveats.

Cyberpunk 2077 is a first person action RPG shooter, featuring a dystopian near future, Night City, where corporations hold the power, and everyone else struggles to get by. Enter V, the titular character, a cyber punk that gets dealt a bad hand during a heist and who then struggles to come out alive on the other side of it.

The game's story is clearly its high point, even though it threads familiar ground and it’s all something we’ve seen before. In fact I’d go so far as to say it's basically the plot of a Johnny Mnemonic and Strange Days mashup, the main plot features elements of both movies, the only thing missing is the dolphin, and I admit I was fully expecting it at some point. Add a sprinkle of the 13th floor mixed in, and you can basically sum up the entirety of the storyline.

The game is very narrative heavy, full of very long dialog heavy scenes, which is not necessarily negative, but the gameplay is kinda poor, as the vehicle for this narration.

The main story clashes against the seemingly open world approach to the rest of the game. The story has a great sense of urgency, but the gameplay doesn’t, as V is slowly dying from the biochip he klepted, which is ridiculous  for a game which also tries to serve up a freeform open world game.
This narrative disconnect, or "Ludonarrative dissonance" can easily take you out of the overall immersion.

This isn’t helped by the gameplay outside the main story threads being somewhat on the weaker side.
You have this sizable cityscape to explore, but where's the emergent gameplay? Everything in Night City is static scripted placements, just sitting there waiting for you to roll by. The city lacks dynamic gameplay.

The overall story threads sees you as a mercenary working up through a reputation mechanic called Street Cred, but ultimately this serves little purpose other than to gate a handful of missions, as a pseudo leveling restriction.
Many of these side quests / tasks barely have any differences between them.
They are frequently presented by the in universe quest givers called Fixers, each offering a series of side content that leads nowhere. With no tie in with the Street Cred mechanic or the overall narrative, they exist in a pocket.

The city police, the NCPD, is the most inept and chaotic, you can walk into a bar and just blast every ganger to bits and they don't respond, but god forbid you run over a pedestrian, because Auto-Drive is designed by a gonk-brain, they’ll be on your case instantly.
They also constantly need you to clean up boringly trivial “flash points” throughout the city, which ranges from five different variants of “shoot these NPCs”.
Variants of “shoot this gonk” should have been a part of the dynamism that's missing. We had a MMORPG some 25 odd years ago that had the right idea, Anarchy Online, and its mission generator. Night City could have used something similar, it would also tie in well with the mercenary approach.

Given the repetitiveness of the side content, by the time you’re through with them, most of the mechanics and the storytelling have long overstayed their welcome. The side content is reminiscent of Ubisoft design philosophy, repetitive spam.

Then there’s the non-combat aspects, you can rent new apartments, but the story treats your original apartment as the only one. No one rides motorbikes in the city. There aren't even real vendors for vehicle purchases, it’s just a lazy catalogue terminal.

There’s ripper docs, a big part of the universe, as they are the ones that offer installation of cyberware, but they all offer identical services and availability.
The clothing stores offer a random, at the time of visit, assortment, for a first person perspective game. You almost never see your character outside of Photo Mode. On top of that with a random selection you cannot get any specific fits.
Consumable vendors, if you’re lucky they have what you want, sell in quantities of 2-4 items.
The in-universe setting is 2077, everything is online and connected, yet the gameplay design is so dated it’s still using walk-in vendors.

Many of these features feel like half baked after thoughts and an aging design philosophy.

Speaking of half baked, there’s the progression systems, it’s an RPG after all.
The main progression system is incredibly dull, the same old trite banality, on top of weird level-adjacent perks and skills, that are wholly disjointed and create an overall awkward experience. You have an assortment of Attributes, which limits what perks you can choose which affects various weapons, side adjacent you have a progression system that’s influenced by your actions, giving minor stat boosts and more perk points.

The cyberware has seemingly random stats, you can upgrade iconic weapons, but not regular ones, you can slot in mods in weapons, but not take them out, 

Add to that yet another disjointed system in the expansion.

Overall it’s just a large mess of systems and ideas that don't fit together.

The combat isn’t worth writing much about, it is really basic and the AI is relatively trivial. The game also strongarms in a not-magic spells system, which is rather silly, because the devs couldn’t design the real netrunner experience or let it be handled by NPCs, so now we have techno-mages hacking people remotely with not-spells.

The game features a selection of radio stations, many of which are not very classical cyberpunky / techno / punky / dark ambient, they feel too contemporary. There’s also a dire lack of ambient music throughout the game. A game which is ripe for Blade Runner-esque scenes and grand ambient sci-fi themes.

The expansion is a spy thriller, one we've watched 100s of times in movies and tv series, one cliche after another, it is Escape from New York mixed with Ghost In the Shell story beats. An entirely standalone compartmentalized experience, with very little in common with the core game. It feels like the usual quick buck AAA expansions we used to get for games 15 years ago, it does nothing for the main game experience.
It also didn't need yet another high profile actor. Add to that, that Songbirds story is just a carbon copy of V's. You can do without the expansion.

Overall they could have done so much more with the game, this game was ripe with potential, The biggest crime this game does is that it's a solo experience, you never get the team, where are the NPC companions joining you on missions? Where's the crew, so many side quest characters are obvious choices for joining up with V as his merc crew.

You should treat the game like a tv show, that’s how the game presents itself, as a lengthy tv show, full of filler episodes and a bit of a core story, like the old 23 episodes format.
The game oozes atmosphere, but that's really all it has going for it. We're so starved for a good cyberpunk experience that even this middling experience is welcome.

It’s very telling that only 36% have completed the main storyline, despite the games seemingly popularity. Perhaps further emphasized by how most of the playerbase is playing dress up with mods and treating it like The Sims.

Cyberpunk 2077 hatte ohne Frage einen äußerst schwierigen Start. Ich denke, da würden mir viele zustimmen: Der Launch war geprägt von zahlreichen Bugs und technischen Problemen, die das Spielerlebnis stark beeinträchtigten. Doch trotz dieser Anfangsschwierigkeiten hat es das Spiel geschafft, sich über Wasser zu halten – und nicht nur das. Über die Jahre wurde es so stark verbessert, dass man heute kaum noch etwas von den damaligen Problemen merkt. Die meisten Bugs sind verschwunden, und das Spielgefühl ist nun beeindruckend rund.

Was Cyberpunk 2077 heute ausmacht, ist ein unglaublich gutes Gesamtpaket. Die Spielmechaniken sind hervorragend umgesetzt – ob Ablenkungen, Hacking oder natürlich das berühmte Sandevistan, das man schon aus dem Anime kennt. Alles fühlt sich dynamisch, gut durchdacht und einzigartig an.

Besonders hervorheben muss man das Storytelling. Die Geschichte ist extrem gut geschrieben, emotional, intensiv und nimmt einen komplett mit. Man merkt an jeder Ecke, wie viel Herzblut die Entwickler in dieses Projekt gesteckt haben. Nicht nur die Hauptmissionen überzeugen, sondern auch die Nebenquests, die oft genauso hochwertig, tiefgründig und spannend sind wie die Main Story.

Für mich persönlich übertrifft Cyberpunk 2077 sogar GTA V – eine gewagte Aussage, aber das ist meine Meinung. Das Spiel hat mich so gefesselt, dass ich nach dem Kauf praktisch eine ganze Woche nur noch vor dem Bildschirm hing. Die Story hat mich einfach komplett in ihren Bann gezogen.

Manchmal wünsche ich mir, ich könnte meinen Kopf gegen die Wand schlagen, nur um das Spiel, den Soundtrack, das Gameplay und die ganze Atmosphäre zu vergessen – einfach damit ich alles noch einmal völlig frisch erleben kann.

Im Großen und Ganzen: 100 von 100 Punkten.

I just finished my third playthrough of the game. I did one after the other, choosing a different life path for each. It is truly a captivating game. The details, the immersion. It is truly a masterpiece. 

The only downside I see, especially for somebody jumpy like me, is the ability to miss story-missions. On my first playthrough I missed out on the entire Kerry questline, because I got the key to the container and jumped off the Ebunike before Rogue had started her dialogue. This marked the mission as failed and blocked me from ever meeting Kerry. Sometimes NPCs take long breaks while talking. Remember this, if you play the game. Take your time, wait for everybody to finish before moving on to another part of the map. 

One change I would wish for, would be more dialogue options. I run past Claire in the Afterlife and get shouted at for not engaging in conversation. Adding a "sorry, talk later" dialogue option would really increase the immersion in my oppinion. Especially since Claires "Hey, we're not done here" call can be repeated indefinitely, if you just walk out, wait three seconds, and walk past her again. 

Other than these minute details: masterpiece, must buy!

The most heartbreaking game I've ever played. I'm a sucker for redemption arcs and Johnny's is one of my absolute favorites. Doesn't mash it in your face that he's sorry but makes it very clear you matter more to him than anything else. The game had me bawling my eyes out more than I care to admit, and it's easy to understand why when you see and recognize the immense love and care that CDPR has put into making 2077 truly special. Every major character feels like an actual living person with goals, aspirations, and personalities, with their own unique interests and responses to how you choose to talk and act with them. You can try your best to help people but after all is said and done, Cyberpunk leaves you realizing just how bleak and punishing Night City, as well as our seemingly destined future is. Even the "happy" endings will leave you with a pit in your stomach, but at least some of them were caused by you choosing your own fate. Though, in the end, you'll wind up affecting others' lives as well as their own fates no matter how hard you try to distance yourself, because you never realize just how many people care for you. There truly are no happy endings in Night City.

There is no other game like Cyberpunk 2077 and i say it surely. Had probably one of the rockiest launches ever, which in my opinion was the reason it didn't even get nominated for Game of the Year in 2020. Since then CDPR kept updating and updating the game, even giving us a surprise on September after previously stating they were done and looking at the next one. The immersion and the feeling this game has is out of this world. Its a big thing for me that it really made me install a mod that lets me sit everywhere the f i want. Its the feeling. No other game i've played made me this invested in exploring its world or its lore outside of whats in front of you. This is pretty much the only game as well that is this horny but somehow makes it feel earned and right. The gameplay at times can be a bit clanky but you walk past this just because of the general feeling it gives. Raw shooting and stuff is not what the game was made for. However the seer depth and the ways you can go through the missions are top notch. Want to be a complete junky that runs around cutting peeps in half? Put on a Sandy and go for it. Wanna be a bully that finishes a fight without even pulling out a gun? Put on a cyberdeck and go for it as well (istg, the audio of using the blackwall gives me the chills every damn time). Recommended although if you are looking for a pure RPG experience look elsewhere.
Pros:
1. Fun and varied combat which all seem to be viable. Between the 5 Skill trees (each are further divided into 3 sub trees), 3 Classes? of guns (tech- shoots through cover, power- bounces off surfaces, smart- auto locks enemies so you don't have to aim much) further divided into multiple types of guns (snipers, rifles, Ars, pistols, revolvers, shotguns, LMGs, etc), Swords, hammers, throwing knives, multiple types of nades, the cyberware system. You can mix and match these to create one of the most diverse combat systems I have seen.

2. Night City and Dogtown are gorgeous, vast as well as densely packed. Dogtown especially is also vertically expansive. I had a fun time using the double jump cyberware to get on top of a building to keep sniping Barghest, which brings me to the AI.

3. Now, I play CP2077 with lots of mods (800+, I might have issues) but even without the AI is pretty good. They take cover, lob nades at you very accurately,  if they have a sandy they will rush you. Melee types also have handguns so if you think you will get into an unreachable spot to cheese them they will start shooting at you. The AI pathfinding is also great. The Barghest were somehow navigating through linked surfaces to reach where I had simply double jumped my way to.

4. Story is pretty good and somewhat unique.  Voice acting is great. I won't say much here in case I spoil anything but Core Story is pretty good and uses the First person perspective to its advantage. The story NPCs are very well done except one.

Cons:
1. Most of the choices ultimately don't matter. Not in the way they did in games like Witcher 3, Me or Baldur's Gate 3. They mostly change the flavor of your beverage but you are still drinking coke and won't be able to switch to tea or coffee if you want. There are exceptions with the final mission being a big one but again compared to some of the better RPGs out there not great.
2. Driving is not good, mods somewhat fix them.
3. Generic NPCs don't react much compared to something like GTA V.
4. Iconic weapons make weapon mods redundant as you will 99% not be using only iconics by end game.
5. There are still bugs and glitches which we need mods to fix.
6. Inventory management is needlessly cumbersome, which again mods do a better job at. But why is this one aspect which no RPG can seem to get right. Atleast, the ones I have played.
7. A few things that even very old games had like you can loot the clothes of enemies or NPCs, your actual physical body changing with in game actions, etc. would have been a nice touch for role-playing. Compared to how out there some NPCs can look, V is a bit bland without mods. Also, dynamic gang wars (GTA SA had it back in 2004) would have been nice considering how many factions there are in night city in sometimes very close quarters.
8. Unless H10's elevator is actually used as a loading screen, it sucks and will almost always make you fast travel.

Cyberpunk 2077 — це потужна й амбітна рольова гра від CD Projekt RED, яка пропонує гравцеві зануритися у химерно прекрасний і водночас гнітючий світ майбутнього. Найт-Сіті постає перед нами як мегаполіс, що блищить неоном, але приховує тіньові коридори криміналу, цифрових залежностей і корпоративної тиранії. Саме цей контраст — розкіш і занепад — створює унікальну атмосферу, яка є однією з найсильніших сторін гри.

Сюжет вибудуваний довкола боротьби за власну ідентичність у світі, де людське тіло й свідомість стають товаром. Головний герой/героїня Ві переживає особистісну драму, пов’язану з інтеграцією цифрової свідомості Джонні Сілверхенда, і ця лінія додає грі філософської глибини. Особливо вражає те, як гра поєднує екшен із моральними виборами, що справді впливають на фінал.

Візуально проєкт захоплює: архітектура, світлотінь, дизайн районів і NPC створюють живу екосистему міста. Саундтрек — це окрема історія, адже він точно передає ритм урбаністичної антиутопії: жорсткий, електронний, нервовий.

Попри гучний реліз і проблеми зі стабільністю на старих платформах, наразі гра значно вдосконалена: сюжетні лінії доповнені, механіки відшліфовані, а DLC Phantom Liberty зміцнило репутацію проєкту як однієї з найякісніших RPG останніх років.

Cyberpunk 2077 — це не просто гра про майбутнє. Це історія про людину в світі, де технології здатні як підняти, так і знищити. Вона вражає масштабом, атмосферою та емоційністю й залишає після себе довгий післясмак роздумів про свободу, контроль і ціну мрій.

Да, игра не без шероховатостей. Встречаются мелкие баги, но после всех патчей это уже не то, что было на старте. Сейчас это шлифованный алмаз, в котором можно с головой потеряться на сотни часов.

Итог: Если вы откладывали «Киберпанк 2077» из-за старого скандала - самое время вернуться. Это одна из самых атмосферных и глубоких RPG за последние годы. Двести часов пролетели как один вечер. Настоятельно рекомендую.
